metadata.description: Lists the number of officers in the Army and Navy by rank at the end of 1904, giving totals for each service.

metadata.title: Salary
metadata.caption: per annum, Yen
metadata.description: Lists the annual salaries of Japanese officials by rank (Shin-nin and Choku-nin), showing the pay attached to each post and the extra allowances for certain governors.

metadata.title: Diplomatic and Consular Service
metadata.description: Gives the salary and allowance scales for diplomatic and consular posts, with allowances varying by the country where the officer serves.

metadata.title: Officials of the Imperial Household Dep't
metadata.description: Lists the salaries of the principal officials of the Imperial Household Department, showing the pay scale at the top of the household administration.

metadata.title: Judges and Public Procurators
metadata.caption: Salary per annum
metadata.description: Gives the annual salaries of judges and public procurators across the Court of Cassation, Appeal Courts and District Courts, by rank and place.

metadata.title: University Professors
metadata.description: Shows the salary ranges paid to university presidents, professors and assistant professors, plus the extra emolument for holding a chair.

metadata.title: Naval Officers
metadata.description: Lists the salary scale for naval officers from Admiral down to Commander.

metadata.title: Naval Officers' Salaries (Continued)
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a list of naval officers' salaries by rank, giving the pay figures for the junior grades.

metadata.title: Military Officers
metadata.description: Shows the pay of military officers by rank, split into service-with-the-colors salary, salary for commissions, and the total.

metadata.title: Military and Naval Attaches at Embassy and Legation
metadata.description: Lists the salaries paid to military and naval attachés at embassies and legations, by rank and by the countries concerned.

metadata.title: Residency-General in Korea
metadata.description: Gives the salaries, bonuses and allowances of officials of the Residency-General in Korea, with a note on the allowances permitted to residents and senior civil servants.

metadata.title: [Prefectures, Area and Number of Administrative Divisions]
metadata.description: Prefectures, Hokkaido and the dominions are listed with their area and the number of counties, cities, towns and villages in each, as compiled from the returns at the end of 1904.

metadata.title: [Prefectures: Area and Administrative Divisions]
metadata.description: The table lists each prefecture's area in square ri together with its number of gun, cities, towns and villages, illustrating the local administrative divisions described beside it.

metadata.title: [Returns for 1903 of Members, Electors and Eligible Persons by Prefecture]
metadata.description: The text explains local assemblies and the franchise, and this table gives the 1903 returns of members, electors and eligible persons for each prefecture.

metadata.title: Local Administrative Jurisdiction
metadata.description: The table lists each prefecture's administrative division against the historical province(s) it corresponds to and the name of its governor.

metadata.title: [Prefectures, Provinces and Governors]
metadata.description: Lists each prefecture with its historical province(s) and its governor, showing the administrative and historical divisions of Japan in 1904.

metadata.title: Principal Cities and Their Mayors
metadata.description: Gives the population at the end of 1903 and the mayor's name for the two largest cities, Tokyo and Osaka.

metadata.title: [Principal Cities: Population and Mayors]
metadata.description: A list of the principal cities of Japan with their population at the end of 1903 and the names of their mayors, given under the local administration heading.

metadata.title: Great Britain
metadata.caption: Kōjimachi-ku Goban-cho. (Teleph. "Bancho" 59.)
metadata.description: Lists the British embassy staff in Tokyo by post, with the embassy's address and telegraphic address given above the list.

metadata.title: U. S. A.
metadata.caption: Akasaka-ku Enokisaka-machi. (Teleph. "Shimbashi" 144.)
metadata.description: Lists the United States embassy staff in Tokyo by post, with the embassy's address and telephone number given above the list.

metadata.title: Germany
metadata.caption: Kōjimachi-ku Nagata-cho. (Teleph. "Shimbashi" 1658.)
metadata.description: Lists the German embassy staff in Tokyo by post, with the embassy's address and telephone number given above the list.

metadata.title: France
metadata.caption: Kōjimachi-ku Iida-machi Itchome. (Teleph. "Bancho" 291.)
metadata.description: Gives the French legation's address and telephone number together with the names of its ambassador and staff posts.

metadata.title: Argentine
metadata.caption: Tsukiji.
metadata.description: Shows the Argentine legation's location in Tsukiji and the name of its chargé d'affaires.

metadata.title: Austro-Hungary
metadata.caption: Kōjimachi-ku Kioi-cho. (Teleph. "Bancho" 1308.)
metadata.description: Gives the Austro-Hungarian legation's address, telephone number and principal staff members.

metadata.title: Belgium
metadata.caption: Kōjimachi-ku Ura-kasumigaseki. (Teleph. "Shimbashi" 3180.)
metadata.description: Gives the Belgian legation's address, telephone number and its minister and attaché.

metadata.title: Brazil
metadata.caption: Akasaka-ku Aoi-cho. (Teleph. "Shimbashi" 3931.)
metadata.description: Gives the Brazilian legation's address, telephone number and its senior staff.

metadata.title: China
metadata.caption: Kōjimachi-ku Nagata-cho. (Teleph. "Shimbashi" 808.)
metadata.description: Gives the Chinese legation's address, telephone number and its minister and second secretary.

metadata.title: [Consular Representatives of Foreign Powers in Japan]
metadata.description: Lists the foreign consular and diplomatic officers stationed at each Japanese treaty port, grouped by the country they represent.

metadata.title: [Embassy Staff]
metadata.description: Lists the members of the Japanese diplomatic staff at the top of the page, continuing the staff list from the previous page.

metadata.title: Consulates-General
metadata.description: Names the Japanese consul-generals and acting heads at the Consulates-General in the British Empire.

metadata.title: Consulates
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese consulates in Britain's dominions and Asia-Pacific ports, with their consuls or honorary consuls.

metadata.title: Embassy at Washington
metadata.description: Gives the Japanese embassy staff at Washington, listing the ambassador, secretaries and attachés.

metadata.title: Consulates-General
metadata.description: Names the Japanese consul-generals in New York and Honolulu.

metadata.title: Consulates
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese consulates in American cities and Manila with their consuls or honorary consuls.

metadata.title: Consulates
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese consulates in France and the officers in charge of each, several of them honorary.

metadata.title: Embassy at Berlin
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese embassy staff in Berlin, giving the post held and the holder's name.

metadata.title: Consulates
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese consulates in Germany and the honorary officers in charge of them.

metadata.title: Legation at Vienna
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese legation staff in Vienna, including the minister, expected to take up the post.

metadata.title: Consulates
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese consulates in Trieste and Vienna and their honorary officers.

metadata.title: Legation at Brussels
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese legation staff in Brussels, giving the minister and the secretaries.

metadata.title: Consulates
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese consulates in Belgium at Antwerp and Brussels and the officers in charge.

metadata.title: Legation at Peking
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese legation staff at Peking, China, by post and holder.

metadata.title: Consulates-General
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese consuls-general in major Chinese cities and their names.

metadata.title: Consulates
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese consulates in Chinese treaty ports and the officials in charge of each.

metadata.title: Consulate at Copenhagen
metadata.description: Names the honorary Japanese consul at Copenhagen, the only Japanese post listed for Denmark.

metadata.title: Legation at the Hague
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese legation staff at The Hague, Holland, by post and holder.

metadata.title: Consulates in Holland
metadata.description: Names the honorary Japanese consuls at Amsterdam and Rotterdam.

metadata.title: Legation at Rome
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese legation staff at Rome, Italy, by post and holder.

metadata.title: Legation at Mexico
metadata.description: Gives the staff of the Japanese Legation at Mexico, from Minister down to the Third Secretary.

metadata.title: Legation at Bangkok
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese Legation staff at Bangkok, Siam, with the minister and second secretary.

metadata.title: Legation in St. Petersburg
metadata.description: Lists the staff of the Japanese Legation at St. Petersburg, including the minister and military and naval attachés.

metadata.title: Consulate at Odessa
metadata.description: Names the Japanese consul at Odessa, the only Russian consular post listed here.

metadata.title: Legation at Madrid
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese Legation staff at Madrid, with the minister and the first interpreter post, which has no name printed.

metadata.title: Legation at Stockholm
metadata.description: Lists the staff of the Japanese Legation at Stockholm, with the minister and two secretaries.

metadata.title: Consulate at Stockholm
metadata.description: Names the honorary consul at Stockholm for the Japanese consulate there.

metadata.title: Consulates
metadata.description: Lists the honorary consuls at Lima and Buenos Ayres under the miscellaneous heading Others.

metadata.title: Successive Japanese Ministers Accredited
metadata.caption: (From opening of the country)
metadata.description: Lists the successive Japanese ministers accredited to Austro-Hungary, France, Germany and Great Britain since the opening of the country, with appointment and relief dates.

metadata.title: [Japanese Diplomatic Representatives Abroad: Italy, Russia and U.S.A.]
metadata.description: The page lists Japanese envoys and ministers sent to Italy, Russia and the United States, with their rank, dates of appointment and of departure or recall.

metadata.title: Obituary
metadata.caption: (July '05—June '06)
metadata.description: A list of prominent Japanese people who died between July 1905 and June 1906, giving each person's name, profession or position, and date of death.

metadata.title: Gross Area
metadata.description: Gives the gross area of land in Japan proper, excluding Formosa and Saghalien, divided between Crown and private holdings and other categories.

metadata.title: Arable Land
metadata.description: Shows how the arable land of Japan proper, about 15.7 per cent of its whole area, is classified into paddy fields, upland fields and others.

metadata.title: Margin of Reclamation
metadata.description: Compares whole area, land inclined under 15 degrees, land under tillage and unreclaimed gentle land by region, showing the remaining margin for reclamation.

metadata.title: Forests and Wild Land Converted
metadata.description: Shows the area of forest and wild land converted each year from 1900 to 1904, by use category, with five-year totals.

metadata.title: Farming Population
metadata.description: Gives the number of farming families in 1903 and their share of all householders, excluding three or four prefectures that had not reported.

metadata.title: [Farms Tilled by Owners and Tenants]
metadata.description: Breaks down farms by whether they are tilled by owners or tenants, by paddy-field and upland type, with area and percentage.

metadata.title: [Taxable Land Area and Value]
metadata.description: Compares the area and officially assessed value of taxable land for 1901 to 1905, following the July 1905 total of 13,942,108 cho valued at 1,406,440,222 yen.

metadata.title: Rate per Tsubo for Urban Dwelling-Land
metadata.description: The Treasury's 1906 investigation of dwelling-land gives the official value, annual rent and market value per tsubo of urban dwelling-land for each prefecture and the national average.

metadata.title: Rate per Tsubo for Rural Dwelling-Land
metadata.description: The same 1906 Treasury investigation gives the official value, annual rent and market value per tsubo of rural dwelling-land for each prefecture and the national average.

metadata.title: Official and Market Value of Medium Farm per Tan
metadata.description: Shows official and market values of medium farm land per tan for paddy and upland fields from 1887 to 1904, based on Mr. M. Saito's research.

metadata.title: Yield per Tan of Medium Farm
metadata.description: Gives the yield per tan of medium farm in rice and in yen of crops for paddy and upland fields over the same years.

metadata.title: Public Burdens per Tan of Medium Farm
metadata.description: Lists the national and local taxes and rates borne per tan of medium farm, for paddy and upland fields, showing the rising burden after the Emergency Taxation.

metadata.title: Tenant Rate per Tan of Medium Farm
metadata.description: Gives the tenant rate per tan of medium farm, in rice and in money, for paddy and upland fields over the same period.

metadata.title: Burdens in Per Cent. per 100 of Yield
metadata.description: Shows public burdens on land as a percentage of yield for paddy-fields and upland farms, with averages, for the years 1887 to 1904.

metadata.title: Tenant Rate in Per Cent. per 100 of Market Price of Land
metadata.description: Gives the tenant rate for paddy-fields and upland farms as a percentage of the market price of land, for 1887 to 1904.

metadata.title: [Tenant Rate Net of Public Burdens Paid by Land-owners]
metadata.description: Shows the foregoing tenant ratios after public burdens paid by land-owners are deducted from the sums received from tenants, which greatly reduces them.

metadata.title: Share of Land-owners per 100 of Gross Yield per Tan of Paddy-field
metadata.description: Compares gross yield and tenant rate per tan of paddy-field in koku, with the resulting tenant share of gross yield per 100, for 1887 to 1904.

metadata.title: [Average Value of Yield During the 18 Years Ending '04]
metadata.description: Gives the average value of yield per tan for rice-paddy and upland farm, and the overall average, over the 18 years ending 1904.

metadata.title: [Comparative Yen Figures by Country]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Compares a per-unit yen figure for several Western countries and their average with Japan, illustrating the relative productive position discussed under the productive power heading.

metadata.title: [Average Yield per Tan of Paddy-Fields]
metadata.description: Shows the average paddy-field yield per tan over three periods of the seventeen years ending 1903, indicating that productive power remained roughly stationary.

metadata.title: Ratio of Increase, Crop of '87 Taken as Standard.
metadata.description: Indexes the yearly crop yield from 1887 to 1904 against the 1887 crop taken as 100, showing how productive power changed over time.

metadata.title: Increase of Tillage Area in Old Japan.
metadata.description: Compares the growth of paddy-field, upland and total tillage area in old Japan between the 1884–93 and 1894–1905 averages, showing that upland farms expanded faster.

metadata.title: [Transfers of Ownership of Arable Land, 1902–1904]
metadata.description: Gives the number of land transfer returns recorded by the Department of Finance for each of the last three years, showing the rate of transfer of arable land through petty subdivision.

metadata.title: Ratio of One-Crop and Two-Crop Farms
metadata.description: The official 1903 returns show the division of paddy-fields between one-crop and two-crop land, by area and percentage of the total.

metadata.title: Cattle and Horses for Farm-Work
metadata.description: Cattle and horses used for farm-work are shown as a share of the total number of each kind of animal, which exceeds 80 per cent.

metadata.title: Human Labor and Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.description: Land tilled with cattle or horse labor (1st kind) is compared with land tilled exclusively by hands (2nd kind), by paddy-fields and upland farms.

metadata.title: Commencement
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of places and cho area of land improvement projects sanctioned, work sanctioned and work completed from 1900 to 1905, with expenses.

metadata.title: Consumption
metadata.caption: (in 000 yen)
metadata.description: Gives the approximate volume of manure consumption as investigated at the end of 1905, broken down by type of manure.

metadata.title: Home Production and Imports
metadata.description: Compares the value of imported manure with home production and the combined total for 1902 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Artificial Fertilizer Output in Tokyo, Osaka, Hyogo and Other Places, 1903 and 1904]
metadata.description: Shows the recent striking growth of the artificial fertilizer industry, giving output by quantity and value in the main centres for 1903 and 1904.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.description: Gives the rice area, total production, and yield per tan for 1900–1905 together with a normal yield figure, showing annual variation in the staple crop.

metadata.title: Exports and Imports of Rice
metadata.description: Shows Japan's rice exports and imports, by quantity and value, for 1900–1905, indicating the shifting trade balance in rice.

metadata.title: Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat
metadata.description: Lists the annual harvests of barley, naked barley and wheat, with their combined total, for 1900–1905.

metadata.title: Oats
metadata.description: Gives the cultivated area, harvest and value of oats from 1902 to 1905, noting that oat cultivation, mainly in Hokkaido, was expanding rapidly.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.description: Shows annual output of several miscellaneous grains in koku for 1900 to 1904, part of the agricultural statistics on crops.

metadata.title: Beans, Sweet Potatoes and Potatoes
metadata.description: Gives yearly production of soja beans, red beans, sweet potatoes and potatoes from 1900 to 1904, reported in koku and kwan.

metadata.title: Leaf Indigo and Leaf Tobacco
metadata.description: Lists the yearly quantities of leaf indigo and leaf tobacco produced from 1900 to 1904, in kwan.

metadata.title: Fibers
metadata.description: Records the acreage and output of cotton and hemp fibers for 1901 to 1904.

metadata.title: Raw Silk
metadata.description: Presents the mulberry tree area and the number of households engaged in sericulture for 1900 to 1904, as background to raw silk production.

metadata.title: Cocoons
metadata.description: Gives the annual total cocoon production for 1900 to 1904, broken down into cocoons, double cocoons, pierced cocoons and waste cocoons.

metadata.title: Cocoons Classified by Season
metadata.description: Splits the cocoon crop of 1900 to 1904 by season, showing spring, summer and autumn cocoon quantities in koku.

metadata.title: Production of Raw Silk, and Waste Silk
metadata.description: Shows average raw and waste silk output for 1886 to 1889 and yearly output from 1889 to 1904, in kwan, with totals.

metadata.title: Exports of Raw Silk
metadata.description: Lists the quantity and value of raw silk exported from the average of 1886 to 1890 through 1905.

metadata.title: Where Exported (Raw Silk)
metadata.description: Shows the quantity of raw silk exported to the United States in each year from 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Trade by Countries (continued from previous page)]
metadata.description: A continuation table giving figures by country, including France, Italy, England, Canada and Russia, with totals; its column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Imports (from China)
metadata.description: Shows annual imports of ordinary and wild silk cocoons from China, by quantity and value, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Raw Silk Production (1904)
metadata.description: Lists the six leading prefectures for raw silk production in 1904, with families engaged and value of production.

metadata.title: Applications to the House
metadata.description: Records the number of silk examinations at the Yokohama Silk Conditioning House and the applications received from Japanese and foreign clients, 1896 to 1905.

metadata.title: The Examinations Classified
metadata.description: Shows the yearly examinations from 1896 to 1905 classified by gross weight, net weight, quality, softening allowance and total, introducing the discussion of the examination results.

metadata.title: Percentage of Moisture
metadata.description: Gives the ten-year average, maximum and minimum percentage of moisture found in the net weight examinations.

metadata.title: Percentage of Moisture Allowance
metadata.description: Gives the ten-year average, maximum and minimum percentage of moisture allowance accompanying the net weight examinations.

metadata.title: [Average Breakage Record, 1896–1905]
metadata.description: Shows, for each year from 1896 to 1905, how many examined cases fell into each quality grade (fine, medium, full, extra full) in breakage tests.

metadata.title: [Filament Size Averages, 1896–1905]
metadata.description: Shows the ten-year average of filament size variation for fine, medium and full grades, with the difference between extremes, from 1896 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Extra Full Size Filament Data, 1904 and 1905]
metadata.description: Gives the extra full size filament data for 1904 and 1905, which were returned separately because that grade was only recorded in those two years.

metadata.title: [Knots Recorded by Grade, 1896–1905]
metadata.description: Lists the average number of nodes and knots found in each filament grade over the ten years, following the examination of cases in 1905.

metadata.title: [Strength and Elasticity of Filament]
metadata.description: Shows the average strength and elasticity of filament over the ten years since conditioning business began, for a 9.0 denier filament.

metadata.title: [Untitled Numeric Columns]
metadata.description: A block of unlabelled figures printed at the top of the page, apparently the continuation of a numeric table from the previous page whose headings are not shown.

metadata.title: [Direct Export of Raw Silk by Japanese Merchants, 1900–1905]
metadata.description: Shows the number of raw silk bales exported directly by the three Japanese firms (Kiito Gomei, Mitsui Bussan, Doshinkaisha) and their share of total volume, 1900–1905.

metadata.title: Japanese and Foreign Exporters of Raw Silk
metadata.description: Lists the principal exporters of raw silk and the quantities each shipped to America and Europe from 1st July 1905 to 1st March 1906.

metadata.title: [Silk Shipments by Firms (Continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a table of silk shipments by firm, with the column headings on the previous page; the totals close the list of shipping firms.

metadata.title: Area Under Tea Plant and Number of Tea-Manufacturers
metadata.description: Shows the area planted with tea and the number of tea-manufactories in Japan for each year from 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Tea
metadata.description: Gives the annual output of tea in kwan by kind (green grades, black and oolong) and a total, for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1904)
metadata.description: Lists the six leading tea-producing districts in 1904 with the number of families engaged in tea and the value of production.

metadata.title: Exports of Tea
metadata.description: Shows Japan's tea export quantities and values from the 1886–1890 average through 1905, indicating the trade's scale over time.

metadata.title: Destinations of Green Tea Exported
metadata.description: Gives the countries receiving Japanese green tea exports each year from 1900 to 1904, with totals, showing the main export markets.

metadata.title: Destination of Black Tea Exported
metadata.description: Shows the destinations of Japanese black tea exports from 1899 to 1904, mainly to the United States, Siberia and other countries.

metadata.title: [Stallions Kept by Breed, 1897–1905]
metadata.description: Shows the number of stallions of each breed kept by the Government from 1897 to 1905, with totals, as part of the account of horse breeding.

metadata.title: [Horses at Two Studs and Nine Depots, 1904]
metadata.description: Gives the number of horses kept in 1904 at the two Government Studs and nine Depots for breeding, by native, imported and cross-bred stock.

metadata.title: Average Prices (Yen) of 2 Year Colts
metadata.description: Average prices of two-year colts, comparing cross-bred and pure native animals, to show the contrast in value of colts from foreign stallions and native mares.

metadata.title: Cattle Imported for Breeding
metadata.description: Numbers of cattle of foreign breeds imported each year for breeding, by breed and by bulls and cows, showing the scale of imports from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: No. of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Number of cattle in Japan from 1900 to 1904, divided into native, cross-bred and foreign animals, with totals.

metadata.title: Horses
metadata.description: Number of horses in Japan from 1900 to 1904, divided into native, cross-bred and foreign horses, with totals.

metadata.title: Birthrates and Deathrates of Cattle and Horses
metadata.description: Birth and death rates of cattle and horses in Japan from 1900 to 1904, giving the number of births and deaths of each animal per year.

metadata.title: Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of sheep, goats and swine in Japan from 1900 to 1904, illustrating livestock numbers in the agricultural section.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Records the numbers of cattle and calves, horses, sheep and pigs slaughtered in Japan each year from 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: [Fruit Output by Kind]
metadata.description: The figures give the official returns of fruit output by kind, which the page says are the only reliable figures available so far, with the rest of the country still missing.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.caption: (Relative percentage)
metadata.description: Gives the relative percentage of Japan proper's sedimentary and igneous strata by geological period, with subtotals and a total of 100, as a background to the chapter on mines.

metadata.title: Output of Gold and Silver
metadata.description: Gives the yearly national output of gold and silver in momme from 1895 to 1904, showing the growth of Japan's precious metal production over the decade.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Gold and Silver Mines (1905)
metadata.description: Lists the principal gold and silver mines in Japan in 1905 with their location and the gold and silver output of each mine in momme.

metadata.title: [Gold Output by Mines]
metadata.description: The gold output by mine, with a total, listed for the year, followed by the text comparing this year's gold output with earlier years.

metadata.title: Output of Copper and Its Exports
metadata.description: Copper production and exports for each year from 1895 to 1904, with exports shown as a percentage of production.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Copper Mines in 1904
metadata.description: Ore output and copper products of the four principal copper mines, all in Akita prefecture, for 1904.

metadata.title: [Output of Principal Copper Mines (continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a list of mines with two figure columns for each mine, whose headings are on the previous page.

metadata.title: Output of Iron and its Imports
metadata.description: Shows Japan's annual iron products output and the quantities of iron and steel imported from 1895 to 1904.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Iron Mines in 1904
metadata.description: Gives the 1904 output and production of two principal iron mines in Iwate Prefecture.

metadata.title: Output of Antimony and Manganese
metadata.description: Shows annual antimony and manganese output in kin from 1895 to 1904.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Manganese Mines in 1904
metadata.description: Lists the acreage and product output of the principal manganese mines in 1904, showing the scale of each mine's production.

metadata.title: Demand and Supply of Coal
metadata.caption: (in 000 Ton.)
metadata.description: Gives the annual national coal supply (output and imports) and demand (consumption and exports) from 1895 to 1904, showing how supply and demand grew over the decade.

metadata.title: [Coal Output by Districts, Estimate 1906 Compared with 1905]
metadata.description: Shows the estimated 1906 coal output of the principal coal districts against 1905 actual output and the increase, as the text introduces the latest returns and current-year estimates.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Coal Mines in 1904
metadata.description: Lists the area and metric-ton output of the principal coal mines in 1904, completing the survey of the coal industry on this page.

metadata.title: [Coal Mines of Fukuoka Prefecture]
metadata.description: A list of Fukuoka coal mines with two printed figures for each, continuing the mining statistics before the consumption index table.

metadata.title: Relative Ratio of Consumption of Coal
metadata.caption: (Index number)
metadata.description: Index numbers showing how coal consumption rose from 1894 to 1904 for ships, railways, factories and salt production, with a total.

metadata.title: Output of Sulphur and its Exports
metadata.description: Annual sulphur production and export quantities in kin from 1895 to 1904, showing how output and exports changed over the decade.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Sulphur Mines in 1904
metadata.description: Output and production figures for the principal sulphur mine of 1904, listed at the end of the sulphur section.

metadata.title: [Oil Wells Figures (Continued From Previous Page)]
metadata.description: Lists oil-producing wells by locality with two figures per well, continuing the list of wells that opens this page.

metadata.title: Output of Petroleum and its Imports
metadata.description: Shows yearly Japanese petroleum output and the quantity and value of petroleum imports from 1895 to 1904.

metadata.title: [Petroleum Fields in Niigata Prefecture]
metadata.description: Gives the area in tsubo and annual output in koku for each petroleum field in Niigata Prefecture.

metadata.title: Mine-Employees
metadata.caption: (At the end of June.)
metadata.description: Reports the number of mine employees at the end of June each year from 1897 to 1900, by mine type and alluvial diggers.

metadata.title: [Mines and Mining Statistics, Continued]
metadata.description: A continuation of a mines statistics table from the previous page, giving yearly figures for 1901 to 1904; its column headings do not appear on this page.

metadata.title: Accident in the Mines
metadata.description: Lists the number of mine accidents and the resulting deaths, severe injuries, other injuries and totals year by year from 1895 to 1904.

metadata.title: Fishing-Boats
metadata.description: Shows the number of fishing-boats by region in 1904, split between boats over 30 feet and those under 30 feet, to illustrate that most boats are small open-boats.

metadata.title: Accidents to Fishing-Boats and Casualties to Fishermen
metadata.description: Shows the number of fishing boats lost by each type of accident in 1904 and the resulting killed, wounded and missing fishermen.

metadata.title: The Value of Catches and of Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of fish catches and of marine products from 1900 to 1904, showing the trend over five years.

metadata.title: Returns for 1904 Distributed by Main Divisions of the Country
metadata.description: Distributes the 1904 catches and marine products among the four main divisions of Japan, as the text introduces.

metadata.title: Principal Kinds of Fish of Commercial Value for 1904
metadata.description: Lists the principal fish kinds by commercial value in 1904, with their yen values.

metadata.title: Principal Kinds of Manufactured Marine Products
metadata.description: Lists the principal manufactured marine products, such as dried squid and herring for manure, with their values.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Marine Production
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures by value of marine production in 1904, shown as two side-by-side lists of districts and their values in yen.

metadata.title: [Aquiculture Output by Kind, 1903–1904]
metadata.description: Gives the value of aquiculture products by kind for 1903 and 1904, showing totals and the share of each type of culture.

metadata.title: [Pelagic Fishery Returns, 1902–1904]
metadata.description: Reports the number of junks, sailing-ships and steamships in pelagic fishing and their crews, with total catch value, for the two latest fiscal years.

metadata.title: [Bounty Granted to Whaling Vessels, Years Ending March 1900–1905]
