metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign instructors by nationality at government institutions from 1900-1 to 1904-5, with the total and annual salary amounts.

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age.
metadata.description: The table gives the number of children of school age by sex, showing those under compulsory attendance receiving or not receiving the prescribed course, those not yet obliged, and the percentage attending school for 1900-5.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows monthly salary maxima, minima and averages for regular and special teachers in ordinary and higher public elementary schools, 1900-1 to 1903-4, illustrating teachers' pay.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.description: Gives the number of kindergartens, their conductors and total infants enrolled for each school year from 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.description: The page introduces the Kyoto and Tokyo blind and dumb schools, then gives annual statistics on their instructors, pupils, training-course pupils and graduates for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Higher Normal School Statistics]
metadata.description: Gives the staff, student, graduate and admission figures of the Tokyo Higher Normal School by course, with totals for five successive years.

metadata.title: The Hiroshima Higher Normal School
metadata.description: Gives the staff, pupil numbers and admissions for each course of the Hiroshima Higher Normal School, with yearly totals for 1902-3 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: [Special Institutes for the Training of Teachers: Courses, Instructors, Pupils, Graduates and Admissions]
metadata.description: Table giving the courses of the special institutes for training teachers, with instructors, pupils, graduates and admissions for each course and for each year from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Normal Schools: Applicants for Admission and Those Admitted to the Regular Course]
metadata.description: Shows, for each school year, how many applicants sought admission to the regular normal school course, how many were admitted, and the resulting percentage.

metadata.title: [Students and Graduates Classified by Sex]
metadata.description: Shows students and graduates of the schools split by sex for five school years, introduced by the statement that they are classified as to sexes as follows.

metadata.title: [Middle School Applicants and Enrolment]
metadata.description: Gives the number of applicants for admission to public middle schools, those enrolled, and the enrolment ratio, since applicants far exceed available places.

metadata.title: [Public and Private Schools, Instructors, Pupils and Graduates]
metadata.description: Compares public and private middle schools by number, instructors, pupils and graduates for five years, introduced as showing the relative numbers of public and private schools.

metadata.title: [Girls' Higher Schools: Schools, Instructors, Pupils, Graduates and Admissions]
metadata.description: Shows the number of girls' higher schools, their instructors, pupils, graduates, applicants and admissions by public and private management for 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.description: Shows instructors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolment for the seven government high schools and their yearly totals, 1900-1 to 1904-5, as statistics on education.

metadata.title: [Ages of Students Enrolled in 1904]
metadata.description: The ages of those enrolled in 1904 in each college are given as maximum, minimum and average, to show the age range of the student body.

metadata.title: Statistics Relating to the Imperial University of Tokyo
metadata.description: Shows professors, students, graduates and admissions for the Imperial University of Tokyo's faculties and for each year from 1900-1 to 1904-5, illustrating the university's growth.

metadata.title: [Ages of Students Enrolled During the Year]
metadata.description: Shows the maximum, minimum and average ages of students enrolled during the year at each college, as introduced by the preceding text on terms and ages.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.description: Gives the number of professors, lecturers, students, graduates, applicants and matriculants for each college of the university, with yearly totals for 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: Professions of the Graduates
metadata.description: Shows how graduates of the Imperial Universities were distributed by profession or condition in life, broken down by faculty, with Tokyo and Kyoto figures stacked in each cell.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.description: The table gives instructor, student, graduate, applicant and enrolment figures for the government medical special schools, with yearly totals from 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: [Students and Instructors at the Tokyo Fine Art School, 1904-5]
metadata.description: The table gives the instructors, students, applicants and enrolment of the Tokyo Fine Art School by course for the year, with five-year totals beneath, illustrating the school described in the text below.

metadata.title: [Statistics of the Tokyo Academy of Music]
metadata.description: The table gives the numbers of instructors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolled pupils at the Tokyo Academy of Music by course, with yearly totals for five years.

metadata.title: [Private Schools and Universities Teaching Law, Medicine, Theology and Other Subjects]
metadata.description: The list names the private schools and universities of higher learning in Japan, giving each one's locality, founding year and subjects taught, with a note on the staffing of the leading institutions.

metadata.title: [Nautical School Students and Graduates, 1900-1 to 1904-5]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly numbers of navigation and engineering students and graduates at the Nautical School, the only collegiate navigation institution in Japan, for five academic years.

metadata.title: [Higher Agricultural School Statistics, 1900-1 to 1904-5]
metadata.description: Shows instructors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolments of a higher institution for five school years, placed before the Morioka school description.

metadata.title: Morioka Higher School of Agriculture and Forestry
metadata.description: Gives the instructors, students, applicants and admissions of the Morioka school, which was founded in 1903 with agriculture, forestry and veterinary courses.

metadata.title: Tokyo Higher Commercial School
metadata.description: Gives staff, student numbers, graduates, applicants and enrolments of the Tokyo Higher Commercial School over five school years.

metadata.title: Kobe Higher Commercial School
metadata.description: Shows instructors, students, applicants and admissions of the Kobe Higher Commercial School, established in March 1903, for two school years.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Higher Technical School — Enrolment and Graduates]
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for instructors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolments at the Tokyo Higher Technical School, following the description of its courses and admission rules.

metadata.title: [Apprentices' School Affiliated to the Tokyo Higher Technical School — Enrolment and Graduates]
metadata.description: Shows instructors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolments at the apprentices' school attached to the Tokyo Higher Technical School for five school years.

metadata.title: [Kyoto Higher Technical School — Instructors, Students and Admissions]
metadata.description: Gives instructors, students, applicants and admitted pupils at the Kyoto Higher Technical School, which opened in September 1902, for three school years.

metadata.title: [Fishery Institute: Applicants and Admissions by Course]
metadata.description: Gives the number of applicants and of those admitted to each course of the Fishery Institute for 1903 to 1905, showing demand against places available.

metadata.title: [Institutes for Training Teachers: Instructors, Students, Graduates and Admissions]
metadata.description: Summarises instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admissions at the three Government teacher-training institutes for several school years, describing their size and intake.

metadata.title: Public and Private Technical Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of public and private technical schools, with their instructors, pupils and graduates, for each school year from 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of miscellaneous schools, with their instructors, pupils and graduates, for each school year from 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students (15 to 25 Years Old) in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Shows the physical condition of male students aged 15 to 25 examined in government institutions, by constitution and eyesight, for 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: Health of Female Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Shows the health of female students in government institutions over five school years, by constitution and eyesight, for comparison across years.

metadata.title: Measurement of Students of Both Sexes in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Gives average stature, weight and chest measurements by age for male and female students in government institutions, comparing 1904-5 with 1903-4.

metadata.title: [Physical Examination of Pupils by Kind of School]
metadata.description: Shows the physical condition (constitution and eyesight) of school pupils examined, by kind of school, for 1904-5 with totals for earlier years.

metadata.title: [Physical Examination of Girl Pupils by Kind of School]
metadata.description: Shows the same physical examination figures for girl pupils by kind of school, with yearly totals, following the boys' data.

metadata.title: [Imperial Library Volumes, Days Open and Visitors]
metadata.description: Shows the Imperial Library's holdings of Japanese, Chinese and European volumes, days open and visitor numbers for five years, illustrating its size after the move to its new building.

metadata.title: [University Libraries Volumes]
metadata.description: Compares the number of Japanese and Chinese, European and total volumes held by the Tokyo and Kyoto Imperial Universities in 1904-5 and 1903-4, supporting the remark that Tokyo's library surpasses the rest.

metadata.title: [Libraries, Volumes, Days Open and Visitors]
metadata.description: Statistics of libraries over five years, showing the number of libraries, volumes, days open, visitors and average daily visitors, illustrating growth in public library use in Japan.

metadata.title: License for Secondary Schools
metadata.description: Figures for licenses granted to secondary school teachers over the last five years, split between those granted without examination and those granted on examination.

metadata.title: License for Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of licences granted to elementary school teachers, without examination and on examination, with totals, for each school year from 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: Medical License
metadata.description: Gives the number of candidates for medical, dental and pharmacy licences in 1903-4 and 1904-5 and how many of them passed the examination.

metadata.title: [Educational Stock Fund and Loans to Civic Corporations]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly balance of the Educational Stock Fund and the loans it granted to civic corporations for primary education purposes, from 1899-1900 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: [Education Fund Receipts, Disbursements and Amount Carried Over]
metadata.description: Shows the education fund's receipts, disbursements and balance carried forward to the next account for five fiscal years, 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: For Teachers of Primary Schools and Primary Technical Schools
metadata.description: Gives the pension fund for primary school teachers, its receipts, and the pensions paid to retired teachers and families of deceased teachers, with recipient numbers.

metadata.title: For Teachers of Secondary Schools
metadata.description: Gives the secondary school teachers' pension fund income and the amounts and recipient numbers of pensions granted for five years.

metadata.title: Outlays and Receipt of Public Schools
metadata.description: The table gives the outlays of public schools by kind of school for the fiscal years 1900-1 to 1904-5, showing the expenditure trend across primary, middle, technical and other schools.

metadata.title: Public School Property
metadata.description: The table gives the public school property figures for 1901-2 to 1904-5: school grounds, buildings, their values, and the total school stock property.

metadata.title: University and Preparatory Stage (Altogether Five Years)
metadata.description: Shows the estimated yearly and total school expenses a family must bear for the university and preparatory stage of education, to illustrate how costly schooling had become.

metadata.title: Intermediate Stage (Five Years)
metadata.description: Gives the estimated costs of the five-year intermediate stage of schooling, showing the expense of each charge and the total, to compare with other education levels.

metadata.title: Elementary Stage (Six Years)
metadata.description: Lists the monthly charges for the six-year elementary stage, showing how much a family pays each month, to show that elementary schooling was comparatively affordable.

metadata.title: [Number of Publications by Year, 1900–1903]
metadata.description: The table gives yearly totals of original works, translations and overall publications from 1900 to 1903, background to the text on the kinds of books published in 1903.

metadata.title: Resume of Statistics of Christian Missions in Japan (1904)
metadata.description: Following a discussion of Christian union in Japan, this table gives the 1904 statistics of Protestant, Roman Catholic and Russian Orthodox missions, including churches, membership, schools and property values.

metadata.title: Relief Fund
metadata.caption: (yen.)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly state of the prefectural Relief Fund, including local apportionments, proceeds, State aids, disbursements and the balance remaining, for four years.

metadata.title: [State Relief Paupers, Amounts Paid and Foundlings, 1899-1903]
metadata.description: Gives the number of paupers supported at State expense, the State's payments, foundlings and total expenses for each year from 1899 to 1903, as outlays for paupers.

metadata.title: [Offences Committed by Inmates of the Home]
metadata.description: The page lists the offences recorded against the charges of the Home, broken down by type and by number of prior offences, with totals.

metadata.title: How Far the Work Has Born Fruit May Be Seen From These Figures
metadata.description: The Home reports the outcome of its work by counting its male and female inmates by their present status, from protection to self-support, death, desertion, or disappearance.

metadata.title: Principal Charity Institutions Existing in Japan
metadata.description: Beyond the Home's own figures, the text lists the other principal charity institutions in Japan with their religious affiliation and location.

metadata.title: [Settled Account for 1904]
metadata.description: The page gives the settled account of the society for 1904, showing the standing, special and current funds with their receipts, disbursements and carried-forward balances in yen.

metadata.title: [Charity and Relief Expenditure Account (Continued)]
metadata.description: The continued expenditure account of the society for the year, closing with the sum carried to the next account.

metadata.title: [Society's Inventory at End of 1904]
metadata.description: The society's inventory at the end of 1904, totalling Y. 10,137,513, broken down by category of holding.

metadata.title: [Members of the Society Returned in October 1905]
metadata.description: The membership of the society returned in October 1905, totalling 1,103,721, distributed by class of member.

metadata.title: The Society's Work in the Late War
metadata.caption: (from beginning to end Nov. '05.)
metadata.description: The society's medical corps work during the Russo-Japanese War, counted from its beginning to the end of November 1905.

metadata.title: Relief Disbursements
metadata.caption: Yen
metadata.description: This table shows how the society's relief disbursements were spent, divided between home, the front, ships and miscellaneous items.

metadata.title: [Receipts and Disbursements of Head Office, Branches and Hospital]
metadata.description: This table gives the receipts and disbursements of the society's head office, its branches and its hospital, following the 1906 estimates.

metadata.title: Patents
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of patent applications filed and patents granted at the Japanese Office since the law was enforced, from 1885 to 1905.

metadata.title: Designs
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of design applications and design registrations at the Japanese Office since the law was enforced, from 1889 to 1905.

metadata.title: Trade-Marks
metadata.description: Yearly trade-mark applications and registrations from 1900 to 1905, with a grand total, continuing the record of the preceding table.

metadata.title: Applications by Foreigners
metadata.description: Number of patent, design and trade-mark applications filed by foreigners at the Japanese Office, and the numbers granted or registered, from November 1896 to December 1904, by country.

metadata.title: Revenue of the Patent Office
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: The annual revenue collected by the Patent Office from 1886 onward, showing how fee income grew with the number of applications.

metadata.title: [Letter Postage Rates by Distance Zone]
metadata.description: Gives the postage rates for letters by weight band, for mail within the Interior, to Formosa, and to Korea or China; the text notes interior rates in Korea or China match Japan's.

metadata.title: Money Orders Fees
metadata.description: Lists the fee charged on ordinary money orders according to the sum remitted, up to the 50 yen maximum.

metadata.title: Telegraphic Money Orders Fees
metadata.description: Lists the fee charged on telegraphic money orders according to the sum remitted, up to the 50 yen maximum.

metadata.title: Foreign Parcels
metadata.description: A list of the cheapest foreign parcel post routes and maximum rates in yen from Japan to each European, Indian and other destination, with rate notes where a single figure does not apply.

metadata.title: [Postal Rates to Foreign Countries by Route]
metadata.description: Lists the postal rates for letters sent from Japan to various foreign countries, by route and carrier, with the charge for each weight step.

metadata.title: Number of Post and Telegraph Offices
metadata.description: Gives the yearly growth of post and telegraph offices and the average area and population each office served, from 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Number of Post and Telegraph Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Shows how the number of Japanese post and telegraph offices stationed abroad increased year by year from 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Ordinary Mail Matter Transmitted
metadata.description: Records the total volume of ordinary mail handled and the letter share, with per capita averages, for 1894 and 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: [Post-cards and Newspapers]
metadata.description: Shows post-card and newspaper/magazine volumes by fiscal year with per-capita averages, illustrating the growth of postal communication in Japan.

metadata.title: Parcel Post
metadata.description: Gives the total number of parcels handled by the parcel post by fiscal year, with the average per 100 of population.

metadata.title: Mail Matter and Parcels Dealt With at Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Lists mail matter and parcels transmitted and delivered by Japanese post offices stationed abroad, by fiscal year.

metadata.title: Foreign Mail Matters and Parcels Dealt With
metadata.caption: (Exclusive of these dealt with by Offices stationed abroad.) (in thousand.)
metadata.description: Shows foreign mail matters and parcels transmitted and arrived by fiscal year, excluding those handled by offices stationed abroad.

metadata.title: Mail Matters Exchanged with Principal Countries in 1904 Fiscal Year
metadata.caption: (in thousand.)
metadata.description: Shows the volume of mail transmitted and received with Asian, European and American countries in the 1904 fiscal year, illustrating the postal exchange of Japan with principal countries.

metadata.title: Postal Savings Deposits at Home
metadata.description: Shows the growth of postal savings deposits within Japan from 1894 onward, with depositor numbers and amounts, noting the marked increase after the late war.

metadata.title: Savings Deposits at Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Shows savings deposits held at Japanese offices stationed abroad from 1894 to 1904, with number of depositors, amounts and average deposit per depositor.

metadata.title: International Rates
metadata.description: The page lists the telegram charges in sen from Japan to places abroad, all routed via Shanghai, for the reader's reference.

metadata.title: [Telegraph Rates to Korean Stations]
metadata.description: Gives the telegram charge from the Korean stations, routed via Fusan, showing the rate per station in yen.

metadata.title: [Telegraph Rates to Manila, Europe, Australia and Other Places by Route]
metadata.description: Lists telegram charges from Japan to places in Asia, Europe and Australia, by the alternative routes available for each destination.

metadata.title: [Telegraph Rates to America and Honolulu by Route]
metadata.description: Shows telegram charges from Japan to American destinations and Honolulu, by the Shanghai, Manila or Ogasawara routes.

metadata.title: Extension of Telegraph
metadata.description: Shows how the telegraph network grew from 1894 to 1904, measured by aerial wires in ri and submarine cables in knots at each fiscal year end.

metadata.title: Number of Domestic Telegrams Transacted
metadata.description: Gives yearly domestic telegram volumes and messages per hundred people, alongside foreign telegrams transmitted and arrived, from 1894 to 1904.

metadata.title: Number of Telegrams Transacted by Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Records telegrams sent and received through Japanese offices stationed overseas for each fiscal year from 1894 to 1904.

metadata.title: Foreign Telegrams in 1904
metadata.description: Breaks down the foreign telegrams of 1904 by region, showing Asia as a whole and its countries China, Korea and India.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Subscribers
metadata.caption: At end of fiscal year.
metadata.description: Gives the number of telephone subscribers at the end of each fiscal year from 1894 to 1904, showing the growth of the telephone service.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Apparatus
metadata.caption: At end of fiscal year.
metadata.description: Lists the number of exchange, ordinary subscriber and automatic telephone apparatus installed at the end of each fiscal year from 1894 to 1904.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Receipts
metadata.caption: (in thousand yen.)
metadata.description: Shows the receipts of the post, telegraph and telephone services by category for selected fiscal years from 1894 to 1904.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Service Expense
metadata.caption: (in thousand yen.)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly expenses of the post and telegraph service by branch, from 1894 and 1900 to 1904, in thousand yen.

metadata.title: Telegraphic Revenue Classified
metadata.description: Breaks down telegraphic revenue for 1894 and 1900 to 1904 into home service (domestic and foreign) and offices stationed abroad, in yen.

metadata.title: Number of Registered Steamers Classified According to Tonnage
metadata.description: The table shows how the number of registered Japanese steamers grew from 1893 to 1906, broken down by tonnage class, illustrating the expansion of mercantile marine described in the chapter.

metadata.title: Steamships, Sailing Vessels and Junks
metadata.caption: (in thousand ton or koku.)
metadata.description: Shows the number and gross tonnage of steamers, sailing vessels and Japanese junks at the end of each year, illustrating the growth of the merchant fleet.

metadata.title: Built at Home
metadata.description: Records the shipbuilding returns for ships built in Japan from 1900 to 1905, showing shipyards and steamers and sailing vessels built.

metadata.title: Purchased Abroad
metadata.description: Shows the number and tonnage of steamers and sailing ships purchased abroad by Japan, by year, from 1870–1899 and then annually 1895–1905.

metadata.title: Ships Built in Compliance with the Law
metadata.description: Lists the gross tonnage and indicated horsepower of steamers built by Japanese builders in conformity with the bounty law, year by year from 1897 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Steamers Built in Compliance with the Law Classified by Tonnage and Horse-Power]
metadata.description: Breaks down the 53 steamers built under the law by gross tonnage and by indicated horse-power class, with totals for each classification.

metadata.title: [Leading Dry-Docks]
metadata.description: The table lists the leading dry-docks of Japan with their lengths, entrance widths and depths over sill, as stated in the section on docks and yards.

metadata.title: [Steamers Under Construction Under the Bounty Provisions]
metadata.description: The list gives the steamers now under construction in conformity with the bounty provisions, with their orderers, builders and tonnages, totalling fourteen vessels.

metadata.title: [Subsidy Granted to Steamship Lines This Year]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: The subsidy granted this year to Japanese steamship lines, by route, is set out as an account following the explanation of the bounty regulations.

metadata.title: Ships Classified According to Service
metadata.description: Shows the number, total tonnage and average tonnage of Japanese steamers, divided between regular and irregular service, illustrating the growth of the carrying trade.

metadata.title: Regular Service Ships Classified by Routes
metadata.description: Summarises the number, total tonnage and average tonnage of regular service ships grouped by the three trade routes, with a grand total.

metadata.title: Foreign Lines
metadata.description: Lists the regular foreign shipping lines by name, route, number of ships, tonnage and operator, with a total, as a companion to the note on the Bangkok line.

metadata.title: China Lines
metadata.description: Lists the regular steamship services to China ports, with the number of ships, tonnage and the company operating each route, ending with a total.

metadata.title: Vladivostock Lines
metadata.description: Gives the Vladivostock shipping routes with ship numbers, tonnage and operating lines, followed by totals for this service and the grand total of all lines listed.

metadata.title: Coasting Trade
metadata.description: Shows the coasting trade routes for Formosa, Japan proper and Hokkaido, and Karafuto, giving ships, tonnage and operators, with subtotals and a grand total.

metadata.title: Ships on Regular Service Classified by Ownership.
metadata.description: Lists the ships on regular service held by each owner, with their number and aggregate tonnage, giving the total fleet of regular steamers.

metadata.title: Ships on Irregular Service Classified by Ownership.
metadata.caption: These are in greater part owned by members of the Shippers' Union formed by small steamship companies and a portion of individual ship-owners.
metadata.description: Shows irregular-service ships split between the Shippers' Union and other owners, with their number, aggregate tonnage and average tonnage.

metadata.title: Seamen of Higher Grade
metadata.caption: The number of licensed captains and mates in 1903 (Dec.), 1904 (Dec.) and 1905 (Oct.) was as follows, showing the rate of increase since the outbreak of the Russo-Japanese War.
metadata.description: Gives the number of licensed captains and mates of each class in 1903, 1904 and 1905, showing how their numbers rose after the Russo-Japanese War.

metadata.title: Shipwrecks
metadata.description: Records the yearly number of steamer and sailing-ship/junk wrecks, with destroyed, damaged and missing vessels and totals, for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: No. of Lives Lost and Injured
metadata.description: Shows deaths, injuries, missing persons and lives rescued in shipwrecks for each year, as a companion to the wreck statistics.

metadata.title: No. of Pilots
metadata.description: Lists the number of Japanese, foreign and total licensed pilots for 1900 to 1904, explained by the rules of the 1899 Pilotage Law.

metadata.title: Captured Vessels
metadata.description: The page lists the 64 vessels Japan captured in the late war, classified by the flag they had flown, with a note on the Russian steamers sunk at Port Arthur.

metadata.title: [Mercantile Marine Statistics, 1893-1905]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly vessels, tonnage, capital, receipts, expenditures and profits of a shipping company from 1893 to 1905, with the account year ending 30th September.

metadata.title: The Osaka Shosen Kaisha (Osaka Merchant Steamship Company)
metadata.description: Gives the fleet size, tonnage, capital, receipts, expenditures and profits of the Osaka Shosen Kaisha from 1893 to 1905, under a heading naming the company.

metadata.title: [Shipping Company Vessels, Capital, Receipts, Expenditures and Profits, 1903-1905]
metadata.description: Gives the fleet and financial figures for a shipping company whose entry (the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha shipping department, described just above) closes this page, for 1903 to 1905.

metadata.title: Mileage Open to Traffic
metadata.description: Shows the growth of state and private railway mileage open to traffic at the end of each fiscal year from 1899 to 1904, opening the chapter on railways.

metadata.title: State Railways in 1904-5
metadata.description: Gives, for each state railway line, its open mileage, construction expense, rolling stock and average construction cost per mile in 1904-5.

metadata.title: [Mileage, Construction Expenses and Rolling Stock of Lines]
metadata.description: Shows mileage, construction cost, locomotives, cars and wagons of each state railway line, with average construction cost per mile, explained by the remark on line dates and leasing.

metadata.title: Table II
metadata.description: Gives net profit, daily average receipts, expenses and profit per mile, and profit per 100 yen of construction expense for each line.

metadata.title: Average Account per Day and per Mile
metadata.description: Shows the average daily and per-mile receipts, expenses and profit of railways for 1902 to 1904, giving the financial performance of the lines.

metadata.title: Private Railway Companies: Mileage, Cost of Construction and Rolling Stock
metadata.description: Lists the private railway companies with their open mileage, construction cost, locomotives, carriages, wagons and average construction cost per mile, as of the 1904-5 period.

metadata.title: [Railway Lines: Total Profit, Receipts, Expenses and Profit per Mile per Day]
metadata.description: The table gives each private railway line's total profit alongside its receipts, expenses and profit per mile per day, plus profit per 100 yen of construction cost, for comparison of company performance.

metadata.title: [Railway Companies]
metadata.description: A table of railway companies listing, for each, the year it opened, its capital, its president or general manager, and the locality of its head office.

metadata.title: Volume of Passenger and Freight Service
metadata.description: Shows the yearly volume of passenger traffic and freight tonnage carried by state and private railways, from 1874 to 1904.

metadata.title: Net Profit of State and Private Railways
metadata.caption: Net Profit (in Yen 1000.)
metadata.description: Gives net profit of state and private railways in thousand yen, and profit per 100 yen of construction cost, for selected years from 1895 to 1904.

metadata.title: Railway Casualties
metadata.description: Lists deaths and injuries among railway staff, passengers and others in railway accidents, 1899 to 1904, with totals.

metadata.title: Lines to be Nationalized
metadata.description: The table lists the private railway lines to be nationalized, giving each line's paid-up capital, cost of construction, purchasing price, loans, reserves and bonds to be issued, as set out in the nationalization scheme.

metadata.title: Redemption of the Railway Nationalization Loan.
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: The page describes the nationalization purchase and its revised redemption plan, and this table sets out the year-by-year cost, profit, interest, and balance of the railway nationalization loan.

metadata.title: Passenger and Goods Tariff on the Government and Other Railways
metadata.caption: Passenger Tariff Rates per Mile
metadata.description: The page closes its account of the Seoul-Fusan railway purchase and railway materials with the passenger fare scale per mile for Government and Nippon lines by class and distance.

metadata.title: Goods Tariff Rate per Mile per Ton
metadata.description: Gives the goods freight tariff per mile per ton for each railway group, by goods kind, treasures and terminal rate, in rin.

metadata.title: Luggage and Parcels
metadata.description: Lists the free luggage allowance by class and the delivery charge for luggage on the main railway lines.

metadata.title: [Parcel Rates by Weight and Distance]
metadata.description: Gives the parcel rate charged by weight for each distance band, with an additional charge for every extra 5 kin.

metadata.title: Special Car-Load Rates on Government Lines
metadata.caption: (per Ton per Mile.)
metadata.description: Shows special car-load freight rates per ton per mile on government railway lines for several commodities, by distance band, as a reference for shippers.

metadata.title: [Rates on Raw Cocoons and Dried Cocoons]
metadata.description: Gives the ordinary consignment and car-load freight rates for raw and dried cocoons, continuing the special rate listing for government lines.

metadata.title: [Electric Railway Companies in Tokyo]
metadata.caption: (Capital in 1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Lists the three electric railway companies operating in Tokyo, with service opening year, mileage at December 1905 and capital.

metadata.title: [Mileage of Remaining Electric Railway Companies, End of 1905]
metadata.description: Lists the remaining eight electric railway companies outside Tokyo, with the mileage returned at the end of 1905, following the note on combining companies.

metadata.title: Courts of Law and Judiciary Force
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of courts, judges, procurators and barristers at the end of each year from 1897 to 1903, illustrating the growth of the legal and judicial establishment.

metadata.title: Prisons and Prisoners
metadata.description: Gives the number of prisons and the male, female and total prisoner counts for each year from 1898 to 1903.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Court of Cassation
metadata.description: Records the civil cases in hand and the cases disposed of at the Court of Cassation each year from 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases of the Court of Cassation
metadata.description: Shows the number of cases brought before the Court of Cassation by subject matter, with yearly totals, for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Court of Cassation
metadata.description: Breaks down cases involving foreign parties at the Court of Cassation by nationality of appellant and outcome, for 1903 with earlier years for comparison.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Five Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Gives the civil cases handled by the five Appeal Courts each year from 1899 to 1903, split between appeals from District and Local Courts, as cases in hand and cases disposed of.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Shows the nature of civil cases decided at the Appeal Courts for 1899 to 1903, broken down by category such as land, money, rice and documents.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Lists the nationality of parties in aliens' cases appealed from the District Courts, with case numbers and how each case was disposed of, for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Gives the same breakdown of aliens' cases appealed from the Local Courts, showing the number of cases and their disposal for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the District Courts
metadata.description: Summarises the number of civil cases handled by the district courts each year from 1899 to 1903, including cases disposed of, cases remaining, and new cases per 10,000 population.

metadata.title: [Civil Cases Affecting Aliens at the District Courts]
metadata.description: Shows, under the civil cases table, how many cases involving aliens were brought and disposed of in 1903, with comparative figures for 1899 to 1902 by nationality of party.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the District Courts
metadata.description: Breaks down the district court civil cases by nature of case, such as personal, land, money and general matters, for each year from 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Appeals Made to the Local Courts
metadata.description: Gives the number of appeals made to the local courts each year from 1899 to 1903, with cases disposed of broken down by the nature of the case.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Local Courts
metadata.description: Shows yearly civil case loads at Japan's local courts, with cases disposed of, remaining and new cases per 1,000 population, 1899–1903.

metadata.title: [Civil Cases Affecting Aliens at the Local Courts]
metadata.description: Breaks down the civil cases affecting aliens by nationality of the party, giving case numbers and cases disposed of for 1899–1903.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the Local Courts
metadata.description: Classifies the local court civil cases by subject matter (land, buildings and ships, money, rice, things, documents, general) with yearly totals, 1899–1903.

metadata.title: Law Suits on Money Matters of the First Instance Classified
metadata.description: Groups first-instance money lawsuits by the sum in dispute, from under Y. 500 up to Y. 10,000, with total cases and total money amounts, 1899–1903.

metadata.title: Cases of Conciliation Dealt with at the District Courts
metadata.description: Shows the number of conciliation cases handled at district courts from 1899 to 1903 and their outcomes: settled, failed, withdrawn or rejected, and cases left pending.

metadata.title: Nature of Conciliation Cases
metadata.description: Breaks down the conciliation cases of each year by the nature of the dispute, such as personal, land, money, rice and documents, with yearly totals.

metadata.title: Cases of Insolvency and No. of Persons Affected. Cases of Rehabilitation of Civil Rights.
metadata.description: Gives insolvency case numbers, debtors, creditors and amount of credit, plus rehabilitation of civil rights cases sanctioned or rejected, for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Criminal Defendants
metadata.description: Shows the number of male, female and total criminal defendants convicted each year from 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: [Persons Found Not Guilty by Sex]
metadata.description: Shows the number of accused persons found not guilty each year from 1899 to 1903, split into male, female and total, as a companion to the sentences table.

metadata.title: Sentences Carried Out
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of sentences actually carried out from 1899 to 1903 by type of punishment, showing the decline in total sentences over the period.

metadata.title: Major Criminal Cases
metadata.caption: No. of Major Criminal Cases and No. of Accused.
metadata.description: Lists the total number of major criminal cases and the number of persons accused in them for each year from 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Nature of Accusations and No. of Conviction (in 1903)
metadata.description: Breaks down the accusations in major criminal cases in 1903 by offence, showing how many accused were convicted, acquitted or otherwise disposed of.

metadata.title: [Accusations and Results by Year]
metadata.description: Gives the same case results for the four preceding years, 1899 to 1902, for comparison with the 1903 figures.

metadata.title: [Aliens as Accused]
metadata.description: Lists the sentences passed on foreign nationals accused of crimes in Japan from 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Causes of Murders Classified (Sentence in Presence of Accused.)
metadata.description: Breaks down the causes of murder cases from 1899 to 1903, with a male and female split for 1903, and the number of murders actually carried out.

metadata.title: Literacy or Illiteracy of Accused
metadata.description: Shows the literacy and illiteracy of accused persons in major crimes and murder cases, by sex, for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: No. of Accused per 100,000 Population
metadata.description: Gives the rate of accused persons per 100,000 of population for each year from 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Personal Condition of Accused Charged with Major Crimes
metadata.caption: (Cases sentenced in presence of accused.)
metadata.description: Breaks down accused persons charged with major crimes by age and by marital and consort status for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Cases of Minor Crimes and No. of Persons Accused
metadata.description: Shows yearly totals of minor criminal cases, persons accused, and judgments delivered in the accused's presence, with rates per 1000 population, for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Nature of Accusation of Minor Criminal Defendants and No. of Conviction
metadata.caption: (in 1903.)
metadata.description: Breaks down 1903 minor criminal defendants by nature of accusation into convictions, acquittals or rejections and others, with yearly totals for 1899 to 1902 below.

metadata.title: Aliens Accused of Minor Crimes
metadata.caption: Of the total number of cases of minor crimes those committed by aliens were:—
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of minor-crime cases involving aliens, broken down by conviction, acquittal or rejection, other outcomes, and total, from 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: No. of Commissions by Defendants Accused of Major or Minor Crimes
metadata.caption: (Judgment declared in presence of accused.)
metadata.description: Counts defendants by sex and by the number of times they were tried, from first trial to seventh or later, showing how many were tried repeatedly each year.

metadata.title: Violation of Administration Rules
metadata.description: Gives yearly counts of violations of administration rules, including cases, offenders and convictions, with notes on summary judgments and cases involving aliens.

metadata.title: Offenders Charged with Police Offence and Conviction
metadata.description: Shows yearly counts of offenders detained, fined, acquitted or rejected under police offence charges, giving the totals for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Appeals to the Court of Cassation and Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Reports the appeals received, cases dealt with, non-suited or cancelled cases and cases left in hand by the Court of Cassation and the Appeal Courts for 1903 with earlier years.

metadata.title: Appeals to Appeal Courts and District Courts
metadata.description: Gives yearly appeals to the Appeal Courts and District Courts, with cases dealt with, non-suited or cancelled, and cases remaining, for 1899 to 1903.

metadata.title: Police Offices and Police Force
metadata.description: Lists the number of police offices, police officers and men, and population per officer in Japan from 1897 to 1903.

metadata.title: Suicides
metadata.description: Annual suicide totals for 1897 to 1902, broken down by male and female, showing the trend in self-inflicted deaths over these years.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Number of fire cases and houses destroyed or damaged each year from 1897 to 1903, indicating the scale of fire losses.

metadata.title: Hospitals, Doctors and Mid-wives
metadata.description: Numbers of hospitals, doctors and mid-wives at the end of selected years, showing the growth of medical facilities and personnel in Japan.

metadata.title: Epidemic Diseases and Mortality
metadata.description: Cases and deaths from dysentery, cholera, plague and other epidemic diseases from 1898 to 1904, with mortality per 100 cases for each year.

metadata.title: Total Casualties During the Late War
metadata.description: Gives the number of Japanese Army deaths from all causes during the late war, by division, distinguishing deaths from wounds and from disease and accidents.

metadata.title: Total Casualties During the Late War
metadata.description: Shows Japanese Navy casualties during the late war by rank category, split into those killed or died from wounds, those wounded, and the totals.

metadata.title: Revenues
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Formosa's revenues by fiscal year, split into ordinary revenue, subsidies from the central government, and other receipts, illustrating the success of colonial finance.

metadata.title: Chief Items of Ordinary Revenues
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Breaks down the principal components of Formosa's ordinary revenue (land tax, customs, and public undertaking receipts) for the years 1898 to 1901.

metadata.title: [Revenue Figures, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: Continuation of a financial table for Formosa whose header lies on the previous page; it shows yearly figures from 1902 to 1906, with 1905 and 1906 partly estimated.

metadata.title: Expenditures
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: This table gives Formosa's government expenditures in thousands of yen by category for each fiscal year from 1898, with 1905 and 1906 shown as estimates.

metadata.title: List of Governor-Generals
metadata.description: This list names the Governors-General of Formosa with their dates of appointment and release, from 1895 to 1906.

metadata.title: Population
metadata.description: This table reports the population of Formosa by sex, total and number of families for 1900 to 1903 and October 1905, distinguishing Japanese residents from natives.

metadata.title: Area of Tillage Land
metadata.description: Shows the area of cultivated tillage land at the end of 1902 and 1903, split between rice-paddy and upland field, as a basis for the agricultural statistics that follow.

metadata.title: Agricultural Products
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the yearly output of principal agricultural products, from rice and tea to sweet-potato, jute and indigo, for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the quantity and value of raw and cured marine products caught and processed in Japan from 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Mineral Products
metadata.description: Records annual output of gold, gold dust, coal and sulphur in Japan for 1900 to 1904, as the mineral counterpart to the agricultural and marine figures.

metadata.title: Textile Fabrics
metadata.description: Shows the number of textile weaving works, looms, value of output and persons employed in Formosa's textile industry for 1900 to 1902.

metadata.title: Camphor, etc.
metadata.description: Gives yearly quantities of camphor and camphor oil produced in Formosa from 1900 to 1904, reported in kin.

metadata.title: Amount of Opium Manufactured
metadata.description: Lists the quantity of opium manufactured in Formosa by fiscal year from 1900 to 1903, given in momme.

metadata.title: Opium-Smokers
metadata.description: Shows the number of opium smokers by sex and their proportion per 100 population in Formosa from 1901 to 1903.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Presents Formosa's foreign trade values, with exports, imports and totals in thousands of yen, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Trade with Japan Proper
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of exports and imports of trade with Japan Proper from 1900 to 1905, with the balance of trade for each year.

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Exported
metadata.caption: Value (Y. 1,000).
metadata.description: Gives the value in thousand yen of the principal commodities Japan exported, namely black tea, rice, sugar, camphor, turmeric and flax, hemp and jute, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Imported
metadata.caption: Value (Y. 1,000).
metadata.description: Gives the value in thousand yen of the principal commodities Japan imported, including opium, petroleum, flour, hogs, Chinese cotton tissues and cotton satins, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: No. of Schools
metadata.description: Reports the number of schools, teachers, and students and pupils at the end of each year from 1901 to 1903 under the education section.

metadata.title: Schools Classified (at end of 1903)
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools in Formosa at the end of 1903, classified as State, Communal and Private, with three unlabelled figures per type.

metadata.title: Railway
metadata.description: Gives the growth of Formosa's railway from 1900 to October 1905, covering mileage open, rolling stock and receipts.

metadata.title: Temperature
metadata.description: Monthly mean temperatures at six Korean stations, based on meteorological records kept at Japanese or other consulates, given to illustrate Korea's climate.

metadata.title: Rainfalls
metadata.description: Monthly and total rainfall in millimetres at four Korean stations, shown to describe the seasonal distribution of precipitation in Korea.

metadata.title: No. of Days of Rainfalls and Snowfalls
metadata.description: Number of days with rain or snow at five Korean stations, given as a continuation of the meteorological observations; the table is cut off at the page foot.

metadata.title: [Monthly Figures (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a monthly table from the previous page, with figures for March to December and yearly totals; its column headings are not shown on this page.

metadata.title: Expenditure of State
metadata.caption: (Estimate for Current year)
metadata.description: Shows the estimated ordinary and extraordinary state expenditure by department for the current year under the Korean government.

metadata.title: [Principal Court Revenue Items]
metadata.description: Lists the principal revenue items of the Court, given as the main sources of its income in the year described in the accompanying text.

metadata.title: Japanese Residents in the Japanese Settlements, Korea
metadata.caption: (in June 1906)
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese households and residents living in each of the Japanese settlements in Korea as of June 1906.

metadata.title: Volume of Trade
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of Japan's imports and exports through the Korean settlements' trade for 1902 to 1905, in yen.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Breaks down Korean-settlement exports by commodity for 1902 to 1905, in thousands of yen, with totals for each year.

metadata.title: Imports
metadata.description: Shows Korea's imports by category for 1902 to 1905, with totals and re-exported foreign goods, giving the overall trade volume.

metadata.title: Export and Import of Specie and Bullions
metadata.description: Gives the yearly export, import and balance figures for gold and bullion, indicating the specie flows for 1902 to 1905.

metadata.title: Trade with Different Countries
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Compares Korea's trade with Japan, China, Britain, the United States, Russia and Belgium by imports and exports for each year from 1902 to 1905.

metadata.title: Customs Receipts
metadata.description: Lists Korea's customs receipts from import and export duties and tonnage dues, with yearly totals, for 1902 to 1905.

metadata.title: Japanese Official Disbursements in Korea
metadata.caption: Approximate figures, yen.
metadata.description: Lists the approximate yen amounts the Japanese Government disbursed in Korea on various undertakings, with the total of the principal outlays.

metadata.title: Harvest
metadata.caption: (per tan, this unit holding good for other statistics)
metadata.description: Shows the experimental cotton harvest per tan at several places, comparing seed and ginned cotton of the Upland and Korean varieties, as part of the cotton cultivation experiments.

metadata.title: Rate of Ginned Cotton and Staples
metadata.description: Compares the ginning rate, staple length and staple size of Upland and Korean cotton, which underlie the valuation of the two varieties that follows.

metadata.title: [Value of 100 Kin of Ginned Cotton by Variety]
metadata.description: Gives the value of 100 kin of ginned cotton for each variety, derived from the assumed price of Y. 25 and the differing rates, as the basis for the receipts per tan.

metadata.title: [Ginned Cotton Yield and Value of Upland and Korean Cotton, With and Without Manure]
metadata.description: Comparing the ginned cotton yield and value of Upland and Korean cotton under different manuring methods, showing the superiority of Upland cotton and the gains from fertilising.

metadata.title: [Annual Gold Output in Korea, 1902–1905]
metadata.description: The gold-mining section gives the yearly output of gold in Korea, which reaches about 5 million yen a year, as evidence of Korea's trade balance.

metadata.title: Cost of Engineering Work etc.
metadata.description: Lists the estimated engineering and repair costs in yen for the South Manchurian Railway, the line transferred from Russia to Japan in 1906.

metadata.title: [Government Capital Allocation for Manchurian Works]
metadata.description: The first items of the Government's capital plan for Manchurian railway and mining works, with their yen amounts and a total of 100,000,000 yen.

metadata.title: Valuation of the Government Property
metadata.description: Gives the valuation in yen of the Government property in South Manchuria, itemised by railway, coal-mines and stations, with the total.

metadata.title: Estimate of Investment and Profit of South Manchurian System
metadata.description: Estimates, year by year for ten years, of the aggregate investment, net profit in yen and rate of profit in per cent for the South Manchurian Railway system.

metadata.title: Construction and Working Expenses of the Tairen-Chungchun Section
metadata.description: Shows the yearly construction and working expenses of the Tairen-Chungchun section, split into reconstruction, doubling, rolling stock and a total for the first year.

metadata.title: [Instalments of Capital, Continued]
metadata.description: A continuation of an instalment schedule whose upper rows fall on the previous page; only the 6th to 8th instalments and the totals are printed here.

metadata.title: Gross Earnings and Operating Expenses of the Above Lines.
metadata.description: Gross earnings, operating expenses and net profits of the railway lines listed above, year by year over ten years, as a projection of the enterprise's results.

metadata.title: Capital to Be Invested in the Exploitation of Fushun and Yentai Mines
metadata.caption: Capital to be invested.
metadata.description: Planned capital outlay for the Fushun and Yentai mines by year, with the accumulated totals shown in the final column.

metadata.title: Mines
metadata.description: Projected yearly gross earnings, disbursements and net profit of the Fushun and Yentai mines, shown alongside the capital plan for the same enterprise.

metadata.title: [Gross Earnings, Operating Expenses and Net Profit by Year]
metadata.description: Yearly gross earnings, operating expenses and net profit of the enterprise, shown with losses in early years turning to profit by the eighth year, alongside a note on its share subscription.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Chien-kin-sai Coal by Grade]
metadata.description: Proximate analysis of the three grades of Chien-kin-sai coal, given to show that the quality of this large deposit is excellent.

metadata.title: Estimates for the Island of Karafuto for the Fiscal Year
metadata.description: The page gives the estimated expenditures and revenues of the island of Karafuto for the fiscal year, showing that the budget totals about 495,000 yen.

metadata.title: [Catch by Japanese Fishermen in Karafuto, to Beginning of September]
metadata.description: Listing the catch by Japanese fishermen in Karafuto reported to the Department of Agriculture and Commerce up to the beginning of September, showing fishery as the most important industry there.

metadata.title: [Disposal of Fishing Grounds in Karafuto, 1906]
metadata.description: Summarising how fishing grounds were disposed of in 1906, by priority of right, tender, or reservation, with rent, average figures and number of companies.

metadata.title: Weights, Measures and Moneys
metadata.description: A comparison of Japanese units of length, area, capacity, weight and money with their English equivalents, given to help readers convert figures.

metadata.title: [Area of Japan by Districts]
metadata.description: The area table gives the square ri of Japan's main islands and island groups, with a total, to show how the country's territory is distributed.

metadata.title: [Principal Mountain Peaks Above 8,000 Feet]
metadata.description: This list gives the principal mountain peaks above 8,000 feet, illustrating the mountainous character of the country's terrain.

metadata.title: [Principal Mineral Springs of Japan]
metadata.description: Introducing the mineral springs, the page lists the principal hot and cold springs with their location, distance from the nearest convenient place, quality of water and temperature.

metadata.title: [Principal Rivers of Japan]
metadata.description: A list of the fifteen longest rivers of Japan with their lengths in ri, given in the physical geography section beside the notes on lakes, plains and coasts.

metadata.title: [Coast-Line of Principal Islands]
metadata.description: Gives the total coast-line length in ri of the principal islands and the surface area per ri of coast-line, showing how well each island's coast is indented.

metadata.title: Opened In
metadata.description: A list of Japanese and Formosan ports with the years they were opened to foreign trade, grouped by island or region, shown with leader dots in the original.

metadata.title: Monthly Average Temperature in Japan
metadata.description: Monthly average temperatures in degrees Celsius for nine Japanese observatories, with record highs and lows, shown to illustrate the climate of different regions.

metadata.title: Average Monthly Rainfalls and Snowfalls in Japan from Beginning of Observation to 1905
metadata.description: The table gives average monthly and yearly rainfall and snowfall at eight observation stations, with days of precipitation per year, illustrating the heavy precipitation described in the text.

metadata.title: [Disastrous Seismic Calamities Recorded in the Pre-Tokugawa Period]
metadata.description: The page opens a survey of Japanese earthquakes by listing the most disastrous seismic calamities recorded before the Tokugawa period, with dates and places.

metadata.title: [Principal Calamities During the Tokugawa Period]
metadata.description: Listing the major earthquakes and tidal-wave disasters of the Tokugawa period, with dates, places, houses destroyed and deaths, to show the scale of past calamities.

metadata.title: [Severe Earthquakes in Recent Times]
metadata.description: Recent severe earthquakes, with dates, places, houses destroyed, and persons killed and injured, presented as evidence of the seismic risk in Japan.

metadata.title: Movement of Population
metadata.description: Shows the male, female and total population of Japan for each year from 1900 to 1904, illustrating the population growth described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Population Density and Population per Family by Region]
metadata.description: Gives the average population per square ri and per family for each region of Japan proper as of the end of 1904, according to the compiled returns.

metadata.title: Distribution of Population in Rural and Urban Districts
metadata.description: Classifies the rural and urban districts by population grade, giving the number of city, town and village units and the totals for the years 1895 to 1898.

metadata.title: [Cities by Population Grade, 1894, and Rate per 100 Population, 1894–1903]
metadata.description: Shows how the population of cities was distributed by size grade, with the number of cities in 1894 and the percentage of total population in each grade for 1894–1903.

metadata.title: Population by Ages and Sexes
metadata.description: Gives the population of Japan in 1903 by five-year age groups and sex, with each age group's share per 100 of population for 1903 and earlier years.

metadata.title: Marriages and Divorces
metadata.description: Lists the yearly number of marriages and divorces from 1899 to 1903, with the rate of each per 1000 population.

metadata.title: Married or Unmarried, by Age
metadata.description: The table breaks the population down by five-year age groups, showing married and unmarried persons by sex, the totals, and the number of males per 100 females.

metadata.title: Birth-Rates
metadata.caption: (Exclu. Still-Births)
metadata.description: Gives birth-rates for 1899 to 1903, showing male, female and total births, births per 100 people, sex ratio at birth and still-births.

metadata.title: Births Classified
metadata.description: Classifies births for 1899 to 1903 by legitimacy, comparing sex ratios of males to females and illegitimacy rates per 100 legitimate births.

metadata.title: Death-Rates
metadata.description: Gives death counts for 1899 to 1903 by sex and total, with deaths per 100 people and the male mortality relative to females.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified
metadata.description: Lists the principal causes of death in 1903 with their numbers, with the remaining deaths grouped as other causes to reach the total.

metadata.title: Stature
metadata.caption: Per cent.
metadata.description: Army surgeon's examination of conscripts over eleven years, showing the percentage in each height band and the number of men examined, to show the Japanese growing taller.

metadata.title: Population by Social Rank (at End of 1903)
metadata.description: Breakdown of the population by social rank (peers, shizoku, heimin) at the end of 1903, giving heads of family and male and female totals.

metadata.title: Number of Passports Issued to Japanese Going Abroad
metadata.description: Annual numbers of passports issued to Japanese travelling abroad, split by males, females and total, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Foreigners Residing in Japan
metadata.description: Number of foreign residents in Japan at the end of each year from 1902 to 1905, split by males, females and total.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Japan, by Nationality (at end of 1905)
metadata.description: Lists the nationalities of foreigners numbering 100 or more in Japan at the end of 1905, with male, female and total counts.

metadata.title: Foreign Countries and Places Where Over 100 Japanese Are Living (at end of 1905)
metadata.description: Shows where over 100 Japanese were living abroad at the end of 1905, by country and place, with male, female and total figures and 1904 comparison.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Japan by Districts
metadata.description: Official returns giving the number of foreign residents in Japan by prefecture or district at the end of 1905, with the 1904 figures for comparison.

metadata.title: [Population Figures by Prefecture, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuation of a prefectural table whose opening rows and column headings appear on the previous page; the column headings are not visible here.

metadata.title: Foreign Visitors to Japan
metadata.caption: (in 1906)
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign arrivals in Japan by nationality for 1904 to 1906, illustrating the 1906 total of 25,353 foreigners and the rise over the previous year.

metadata.title: [Golden Kite Decorations Conferred for the China Trouble of 1900]
metadata.description: Lists the number of Golden Kite decorations, by grade, conferred for services in the China trouble of 1900, as an illustration of the order's distribution.

metadata.title: Holders of the Grand Order
metadata.description: Names the living recipients of the Grand Order of Merit and Grand Cordon of the Chrysanthemum, listed by their rank or office.

metadata.title: [Number of Peers by Grade, 1884–1901]
metadata.description: Shows how the number of Peers in each of the five grades, and in total, changed in selected years from 1884 to 1901.

metadata.title: [Continuation of Table of Yearly Figures, 1902–1905]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a multi-column yearly statistical table whose headings appear on the previous page, giving figures for 1902 to 1905.

metadata.title: Precedence at Court According to Rank
metadata.description: The page lists how the imperial princes holding the Grand Order rank in the court precedence, with their military ranks given beside each name.

metadata.title: [Imperial Court Personages and Their Positions]
metadata.description: This list gives the princes, nobles and officials of the Imperial Court with their titles and posts, as a reference for readers of the Year Book.

metadata.title: Member of the Present Cabinet
metadata.description: A short list naming the two principal members of the newly formed Saionji Cabinet, set after the text describing its composition.

metadata.title: [Membership of the House of Peers by Date]
metadata.description: Shows how the membership of the House of Peers changed at successive dates from 1894 to 1905, as the House's statistics are given.

metadata.title: [Composition of the House of Peers at the Last Mentioned Date]
metadata.description: Breaks down the House of Peers by rank and category of member at the latest date given, with the total at the foot.

metadata.title: [Groups or Coteries in the House of Peers]
metadata.description: Lists the informal groups or coteries into which members of the House of Peers are grouped, with the number of members in each.

metadata.title: [House of Representatives Sessions, Dates and Presiding Officers]
metadata.description: Lists each House of Representatives session with its opening and closing dates and the Speaker and Vice-Speaker, marking dissolutions and elections.

metadata.title: The Composition of the House
metadata.description: Gives the party-colour classification of the present House of Representatives, with the number of members in each party and the total.

metadata.title: Number of Franchise-Holders
metadata.description: The table gives the number of franchise-holders from 1890 to 1904, with holders per member of the House and per 1,000 population, accompanying the discussion of the electoral system.

metadata.caption: (Existing at the end 1904.)

metadata.description: Lists the annual allowances paid to military and naval attachés by rank, with the countries of each embassy or legation grouped by pay level.

metadata.description: Shows the number of recipients and total amounts of pensions, annuities to families of deceased officers, and grand totals, by Civil Service, Army and Navy, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: One Time Grant of Money
metadata.description: Gives the number of recipients and total amounts of one-time grants of money to Civil Service, Army and Navy personnel for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Administrative Divisions of Prefectures]

metadata.title: [Returns for 1903 of Members, Electors and Those Eligible by Prefecture]
metadata.description: Returns for 1903 showing the number of members, electors and those eligible to serve in the local assemblies of ten prefectures, as introduced in the text on local government.

metadata.title: [Figures by Prefecture, Local Administration]
metadata.description: Lists each prefecture with three figures, followed by national totals, showing the local administrative units of Japan; the column headings are not printed on this page.

metadata.title: Local Administrative Jurisdiction
metadata.description: Matches each prefecture with its historical province and its governor, showing the administrative jurisdiction arrangement of the prefectures.

metadata.title: Principal Cities and Their Mayors

metadata.title: [Principal Cities: Population and Mayors]
metadata.description: Lists the principal cities of Japan with their population figures and the names of their mayors, part of the local administration section.

metadata.title: Emigrants of Hokkaido
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of emigrant families, males, females and total emigrants leaving for Hokkaido from 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: Italy

metadata.description: Lists the staff of the Italian Embassy in Tokyo, with its address and telephone number, as one of the foreign embassy entries.

metadata.title: U. S. A.

metadata.description: Lists the staff of the American Embassy in Tokyo, with its address and telephone number, as one of the foreign embassy entries.

metadata.title: Embassy at Rome

metadata.title: Consulates in the United States

metadata.title: Legation at Brussels

metadata.title: Holland — Consulates

metadata.title: Russia — Legation in St. Petersburg

metadata.title: Spain — Legation at Madrid
metadata.description: Lists the minister and interpreter of the Japanese legation at Madrid in Spain.

metadata.title: U. S. of America

metadata.title: General Statistics of Education

metadata.title: Expenditure for the Department of Education (1906–'7)

metadata.description: The table sets out the weekly hours and subject content of each school year in the ordinary elementary school curriculum, as described in the adjoining text on course grades.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Higher Elementary Schools
metadata.description: The table sets out the weekly teaching hours for each subject across the four school years of the higher elementary schools, showing the official curriculum of the period.

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age
metadata.description: Shows the number of school-age children by sex, split into those under and not under compulsory attendance, and the share actually attending school, for 1900-1 to 1905-6.

metadata.title: Male and Female Teachers (Including Foreigners)
metadata.description: Gives the number of male and female teachers, government or communal and private, including foreigners, in each school year from 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows monthly salaries of male and female teachers in ordinary and higher public elementary schools, by teacher grade, for 1900-1 to 1904-5.

metadata.title: [Applicants for Admission to Public Middle Schools]
metadata.description: Gives the number of applicants for admission to public middle schools, the number enrolled, and the percentage enrolled, for 1904-5 and 1905-6.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Pupils, 1899–1904]
metadata.description: A continuation of an earlier statistical table giving yearly figures from 1899 to 1904, with the column headings lost in the scan.

metadata.title: The Curriculum of the Middle School
metadata.description: Shows the weekly teaching hours for each subject in each of the five years of the middle school course.

metadata.title: The Relative Numbers of Public and Private Schools, Number of Pupils, etc, May Be Seen from the Following
metadata.description: Compares public and private schools for 1900–1906 by number of schools, instructors, pupils and graduates, with branch schools and foreign instructors noted.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Girls' Higher Schools
metadata.description: The curriculum table sets out the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each of the four years of the girls' higher schools course.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Girls' Higher Schools, 1900-1 to 1905-6]
metadata.description: The statistics table gives, year by year from 1900-1 to 1905-6, the number of girls' higher schools, their instructors, pupils, graduates, applicants and admissions, public and private.

metadata.description: The page describes the high school system and sets out the weekly hour allocations for each year of the first section's preparatory course, leading to university entry.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the 2nd Section of the High School
metadata.description: The page gives the weekly hours per subject for each of the three years of the second section of the high school curriculum, set out in the same format as the first section.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Third Section of the High School Preparatory to the College of Medicine
metadata.description: Gives the weekly hours per subject and year-total across three years of the Third Section preparatory course for the College of Medicine.

metadata.title: [Instructors, Students and Graduates of the Seven High Schools]
metadata.description: Shows the instructors, students, graduates, and admission figures for the seven government high schools, with yearly totals from 1900-1 to 1905-6 below.

metadata.title: [Ages of Those Enrolled in 1905]
metadata.description: Shows the maximum, minimum and average ages of students enrolled in each college in 1905, supporting the discussion of enrolment ages in the text.

metadata.title: Statistics Relating to the Imperial University of Tokyo
metadata.description: Gives the staff, student and pupil numbers, graduates, applicants and matriculants for each college of the Imperial University of Tokyo.

metadata.title: [Ages of Students Enrolled During the Year]
metadata.description: The ages of students enrolled during the year are given for each college, showing maximum, minimum and average ages in years and months.

metadata.title: [Professors, Students, Graduates and Applicants by College]
metadata.description: The table gives, for each college of the Imperial University and by year, the numbers of professors, students, graduates, applicants and matriculants, showing the growth of enrolment.

metadata.caption: The graduates of the Imperial Universities classified according to their condition in life make the following record.
metadata.description: The table classifies Imperial University graduates by their condition in life, separately for Tokyo (upper figures) and Kyoto (lower figures), by faculty.

metadata.title: Applicants for Admission to the Regular Course of Normal Schools
metadata.description: Shows, for each school year, how many applicants sought admission to the regular normal school course, how many were admitted, and the resulting admission percentage.

metadata.title: Students and Graduates Classified as to Sexes
metadata.description: Breaks down normal school students and graduates by sex for each school year, from 1900-1 to 1905-6.

metadata.description: The table gives the instructors, students, graduates and admissions of the Hiroshima Higher Normal School by course, with yearly totals from 1900-1 to 1905-6, as described in the school's account beside it.

metadata.title: [Main Course and Preparatory Course: Instructors, Pupils, Graduates and Admissions]
metadata.description: The table gives the instructors, pupils, graduates and admissions of the school's main courses and preparatory course, with yearly totals for 1902-6.

metadata.title: [Higher Normal School for Females: Courses, Instructors, Pupils and Admissions]
metadata.description: The table shows the courses of the Higher Normal School for Females with instructors, pupils, graduates and admissions for each year from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens, Conductors and Infants, 1900-1 to 1905-6]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly number of kindergartens, their conductors and the total infants enrolled from 1900-1 to 1905-6, illustrating the growth of kindergarten education described in the text.

metadata.description: The page introduces the annual statistics of the blind and deaf schools, showing instructors, pupils and graduates, including training-course pupils, for 1900-1 to 1905-6.

metadata.description: The table gives, for each government medical school and for each year from 1900 to 1906, the instructors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolments of the special medical schools.

metadata.description: The page gives enrolment, graduate, applicant and instructor figures for the Tokyo Foreign Language School, by course for the current year and by academic year from 1900–1 to 1905–6.

metadata.title: Public and Private Schools of Higher Grade
metadata.description: The page lists public and private institutions of collegiate standing, giving each school's name, locality, founding year and subjects taught, as examples of higher-grade schools.

metadata.title: [Students and Graduates of the Nautical School]
metadata.description: Shows the number of navigation and engineering students and graduates at the Nautical School for three recent years, as the school's collegiate role is described.

metadata.title: [Sapporo Agricultural College Statistics, 1900–1906]
metadata.description: Statistics of instructors, students, graduates and admissions at Sapporo Agricultural College for six school years, described in the text above.

metadata.title: [Morioka Higher School of Agriculture and Forestry Statistics, 1903–1906]
metadata.description: Staff, student numbers and admission figures for the Morioka agricultural and forestry school over three years, following its description in the text.

metadata.description: Enrolment and examination statistics for the institution described just before this point, covering six school years from 1900-1 to 1905-6.

metadata.description: Statistics of instructors, students, applicants and admissions at the Kobe Higher Commercial School for the three school years 1903-4 to 1905-6.

metadata.description: Instructors, students, graduates and admissions at the Tokyo Higher Technical School over six school years from 1900-1 to 1905-6.

metadata.description: Enrolment and admission figures for the Kyoto Higher Technical School, opened in 1902, for its first four school years.

metadata.description: Yearly statistics of the three Government institutes for training technical teachers, covering instructors, students, graduates and admissions for 1900-1 to 1905-6.
