metadata.description: Gives the physical constitution and eyesight condition of male students examined in government institutions in each school year from 1900–1 to 1905–6.

metadata.title: Health of Female Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Gives the physical constitution and eyesight condition of female students examined in government institutions in each school year from 1900–1 to 1905–6.

metadata.description: Gives average stature, weight and chest measurements of male and female students aged 15 to 25 in government institutions, with upper and lower figures for two successive years.

metadata.description: Shows the physical condition and eyesight of pupils examined in elementary, middle and normal schools, introduced after noting pupil numbers and health returns for recent years.

metadata.description: Shows the growth of libraries over six years, with their number, volumes, days open, visitors and average daily visitors, illustrating expanding public library use in Japan.

metadata.description: Shows contributions paid into the pension fund for secondary school teachers and the pensions granted to retired teachers and their families, with recipient numbers, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.description: The table gives the area, value and money held as school property across four school years, showing how public school grounds, buildings and equipment were valued and changed over time.

metadata.title: Elementary Stage (Six Years.)
metadata.description: Shows the estimated monthly school expenses for an elementary pupil, illustrating that schooling is affordable mainly to wealthier families and creating need for aid to poor students.

metadata.description: Shows the subsequent careers of the 386 graduates of the Japan Woman's University up to 1906, explaining the low status of women's higher education.

metadata.title: [Ryugakusei Sent Abroad by the Department of Education, 1903-1905]
metadata.description: Lists the number of ryugakusei, government-selected students sent abroad by the Department of Education in recent years, by destination, for 1903 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Students Abroad by Countries of Study, 1903–1905]
metadata.description: Shows the number of students abroad in 1903–1905 by the countries where they studied, with yearly totals, to illustrate the scale of overseas education.

metadata.title: Resume of Statistics of Christian Missions in Japan (19 5)
metadata.description: Summarises the number of churches, preaching places and missionaries of the Protestant, Roman Catholic and Russian Orthodox missions in Japan, placed after the discussion of the union movement.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Protestant, Roman Orthodox Church and Russian Christian Missions in Japan]
metadata.description: This table compares the size, membership, schools, medical work and property of the Protestant, Roman Orthodox and Russian Christian missions in Japan.

metadata.description: Shows how the 5,209 ex-convicts cared for by the homes were classified by their outcome, illustrating the results of the reform-home system.

metadata.title: Courts of Law and Judiciary Force
metadata.description: Shows the number of courts of law, judges, procurators, barristers and sheriffs at the end of each year from 1900 to 1904, illustrating the growth of the judicial establishment.

metadata.title: Prisons and Prisoners
metadata.description: Gives the number of prisons and the male, female and total prisoner populations at year end for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.description: Shows the number of cases heard by the Court of Cassation each year from 1900 to 1904, broken down by the nature of the case.

metadata.description: Lists the aliens-related cases before the Court of Cassation from 1900 to 1904, by nationality of parties and their outcome.

metadata.caption: There was no case of this nature in 1904

metadata.description: Shows the civil cases in which aliens were involved, by nationality of the party, with cases and cases disposed of for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.description: Breaks down the district court civil cases by their nature (personal, land, buildings and ships, money, rice, things, documents, general) for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.description: Reports appeals made to the local courts, cases disposed of, and the nature of cases disposed of by category, for the years 1900 to 1904.

metadata.description: Breaks down the civil cases at local courts by the nature of the claim (land, buildings and ships, money, rice, things, documents, general) for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.caption: (in 1904.)
metadata.description: Breaks down the minor criminal defendants of 1904 by nature of accusation into convictions, acquittals or rejections and others, with totals by judgment type and sex, and yearly totals for 1900 to 1903.

metadata.title: Aliens Accused of Minor Crimes
metadata.description: Shows the number of minor crimes committed by aliens over 1900–1904, broken down into convictions, acquittals or rejections, others and totals.

metadata.title: No. of Commissions by Defendants Accused of Major or Minor Crimes
metadata.caption: (Judgment declared in presence of accused.)
metadata.description: Gives the number of commissions by defendants accused of major or minor crimes, by sex and by how many times they had been judged, for 1900–1904.

metadata.title: Violation of Administration Rules
metadata.description: Lists cases, offenders and convictions under administration rules for 1900–1904, with notes on summary judgments and cases involving aliens.

metadata.title: Offenders Charged with Police Offence and Conviction
metadata.description: Shows the number of offenders charged with police offences by outcome (detained, fined, acquitted or rejected, others) and totals for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Appeals to the Court of Cassation and Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Gives the number of appeals to the Court of Cassation and the appeal courts, with cases dealt with, non-suited or cancelled, and cases remaining, for 1904 by court and for 1900 to 1903.

metadata.title: Appeals to Appeal Courts and District Courts
metadata.description: Reports appeals to appeal courts and district courts for 1900 to 1904, showing cases dealt with, non-suited or cancelled, and cases still pending.

metadata.title: Police Offices and Police Force
metadata.description: Lists the number of police offices, police officers and men, and population per police officer for each year from 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Suicides
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of male, female and total suicides from 1900 to 1904, with the ratio per 10,000 of population.

metadata.title: Acts of Suicides
metadata.description: Breaks down the suicides of 1900 to 1904 by method (hanging, drowning, edged tools, fire arms, poisons, others), by sex, with totals.

metadata.title: Cases of Suicides of Over 200 Classified
metadata.description: Shows suicides of over 200 cases, classified by assigned motive (mental derangement, long illness, poverty, love or jealousy, remorse, domestic discord), by sex, for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Sufferers From Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.description: Shows the number of people suffering from robbery, larceny, peculation and fraud in each year from 1900 to 1904, with the rate per 1000 population.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Gives the number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, total burnt area, and average house and area loss per fire for 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Hospitals, Doctors and Mid-Wives
metadata.description: Lists the number of hospitals, doctors (total and per 1000 population) and mid-wives at the end of each year from 1900 to 1904.

metadata.title: Epidemic Diseases and Mortality
metadata.description: Shows cases and deaths from enteric fever, dysentery, diphtheria, cholera, pest and other epidemics for 1901 to 1905, with mortality per 100 cases.

metadata.title: Living Painters Classified According to Special Lines
metadata.chapter: Arts and Crafts of Modern Japan
metadata.chapter_raw: Arts and Crafts of Modern Japan
metadata.caption: (T.=Tokyo. K.=Kyoto.)
metadata.description: The author notes that Western-style painters are now numerous and groups them by specialty, starting with living landscape painters and where each works, Tokyo or Kyoto.

metadata.title: [Japanese Style Painters (Continued)]
metadata.chapter: Arts and Crafts of Modern Japan
metadata.description: Continuation of the list of Japanese-style painters, grouped by school, with each painter's school abbreviation given in parentheses.

metadata.title: Flowers and Birds and Animals
metadata.chapter: Arts and Crafts of Modern Japan
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese painters honoured under the flowers, birds and animals category, with their schools or home towns.

metadata.title: Manners and Customs and Human Figures (Not Portraits)
metadata.chapter: Arts and Crafts of Modern Japan
metadata.description: Lists painters of manners, customs and human figures, excluding portraits, arranged in two columns by school.

metadata.title: Historic Pictures
metadata.chapter: Arts and Crafts of Modern Japan
metadata.description: Names the painters of historic pictures, with their school abbreviations.

metadata.title: Cartoons
metadata.chapter: Arts and Crafts of Modern Japan
metadata.description: Names the cartoonists, with their school abbreviations, arranged in two columns.

metadata.title: Lady Painters
metadata.chapter: Arts and Crafts of Modern Japan
metadata.description: Names the female painters, with their school abbreviations, in two columns.

metadata.title: [Gross Area of Land in Japan Proper]
metadata.description: Gives the distribution of the gross land area of Japan proper, excluding Formosa and Sakhalin, between Crown and government land, private land, and unclassed areas.

metadata.title: [Arable Land Classified by Type]
metadata.description: Shows the classification of the arable land of Japan proper into paddy fields, upland fields and others, with the total arable area in cho.

metadata.title: [Land Available for Reclamation by Region]
metadata.description: Compares whole area, gentle slopes, land under tillage and unreclaimed gently sloping land by region, to show the margin left for reclamation.

metadata.title: Forests and Wild Land Converted
metadata.description: Shows the area of forests and wild land converted to arable land, dwelling-lots and other uses each year from 1900 to 1904, with totals.

metadata.title: Farming Population
metadata.description: Gives the number of families and their percentage share of the total in the farming population for 1903 and 1904, distinguishing full-time farmers from those combining farming with other occupations.

metadata.title: Farms Tilled by Owners and Tenants
metadata.description: Compares the area of farms tilled by owners and by tenants, paddy-fields and upland farms, in 1903 and 1904, with their percentage shares.

metadata.title: [Area and Value of Dwelling-Land, 1901-1906]
metadata.description: Shows the area and value of dwelling-land from 1901 to 1906, given at the head of the section on the Treasury's revised official value, market value and rent investigations.

metadata.title: Rate per "Tsubo" for Urban Dwelling-Land
metadata.description: Gives the official value, annual rent and market value per tsubo of urban dwelling-land in the principal prefectures and the national average, from the Treasury investigations of 1906.

metadata.title: Rate per "Tsubo" for Rural Dwelling-Land
metadata.description: Gives the official value, annual rent and market value per tsubo of rural dwelling-land in the principal prefectures and the national average, from the same Treasury investigations.

metadata.title: [Average Yield per Tan of Paddy-fields]
metadata.description: Shows the average yield per tan of paddy-fields over three seventeen-year-period spans, illustrating that productive power has stayed roughly stationary.

metadata.title: Ratio of Increase, Crop of '87 Taken as Standard
metadata.description: Gives an index of yearly crop productivity for selected years, with the 1887 crop set at 100 as the base for comparison.

metadata.title: Increase of Tillage Area in Old Japan
metadata.description: Compares the average tillage area of paddy-fields, upland farms and the total in two periods, with the rate of increase, to show growth in cultivated land.

metadata.title: [Transfers of Arable Land Ownership by Year]
metadata.description: Lists the number of land ownership transfer returns for the last three years, showing the rapid subdivision of farming plots.

metadata.title: Ratio of One-Crop and Two-Crop Farms
metadata.description: Official returns give the approximate ratio of one-crop and two-crop paddy-fields in 1903 and 1904, in cho and per cent.

metadata.title: Cattle and Horses for Farm-Work
metadata.description: Shows the number of cattle and horses used for farm-work in 1903 and 1904, with each animal's percentage share.

metadata.title: Human Labor and Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.description: Gives the approximate area of land tilled with cattle or horse labor (1st kind) versus by hands alone (2nd kind), for 1903 and 1904.

metadata.title: [Land Improvement Projects, 1900–1906]
metadata.description: The table gives yearly figures for land improvement projects sanctioned, begun and completed, with expenditure, from 1900 to June 1906, supporting the point about expanding rice cultivation.

metadata.title: Consumption
metadata.caption: (in 000 yen.)
metadata.description: The table shows the estimated value of manure consumed, by kind, as investigated at the end of 1905.

metadata.title: Home Production and Imports
metadata.description: The table compares the value of imported manure with home-produced manure, and their total, for 1902 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Artificial Fertilizer Output by Places, 1903–1905]
metadata.description: The table gives the returns of the artificial fertilizer industry by place for 1903 to 1905, showing its rapid growth after 1902.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.description: Gives the rice area, total production and yield per tan for 1900–1906 with a normal-yield average, showing the year-by-year variation in the staple crop.

metadata.title: Export and Import of Rice
metadata.description: Shows the yearly quantities and values of rice exported and imported by Japan from 1900 to 1906, indicating the shift from net export to heavy net import.

metadata.title: Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat
metadata.description: Gives annual production in koku of barley, naked barley and wheat, with their combined total, for 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: Oats
metadata.description: Shows the cultivated area, harvest and value of oats from 1902 to 1905, a crop mainly grown in Hokkaido where cultivation was advancing rapidly.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.description: Output of minor grains (millet, buckwheat, Italian millet, sarva millet) for 1900–1905, presented as part of the agricultural statistics of Japan.

metadata.title: Beans, Sweet Potatoes and Potatoes
metadata.description: Yearly output of soja beans, red beans, sweet potatoes and potatoes from 1900 to 1905, listed under the agricultural returns for minor crops.

metadata.title: Leaf Indigo and Leaf Tobacco
metadata.description: Output of indigo and leaf tobacco in kwan for 1900 to 1905, giving the yearly production of these two industrial crops.

metadata.title: Fibers
metadata.description: Acreage and output of cotton and hemp fibres from 1901 to 1905, showing the trend in these fibre crops.

metadata.title: Other Minor Crops
metadata.description: Area and output of pea, beans, pea-nut and maize, the remaining minor crops listed at the close of the agricultural statistics.

metadata.title: [Areas and Output of Miscellaneous Crops and Products]
metadata.description: This table gives the cultivated area and output of various miscellaneous crops and products, showing the scale of each non-cereal crop industry in Japan.

metadata.title: Raw Silk
metadata.description: This table shows the area under mulberry trees and the number of households engaged in sericulture, the basis of raw silk production, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Cocoons
metadata.description: This table gives annual cocoon production broken down into total output, sound cocoons, double cocoons, pierced cocoons and waste for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Cocoons Classified by Season
metadata.description: This table splits annual cocoon output into spring, summer and autumn crops for 1900 to 1905, showing the seasonal pattern of silk production.

metadata.title: Production of Raw Silk, and Waste Silk
metadata.description: Gives annual output of raw silk and waste silk in kwan, with totals, for 1900 to 1905, showing the scale of Japan's silk production.

metadata.title: Export of Raw Silk
metadata.description: Shows yearly quantity and value of raw silk exported, alongside the highest price of Shinshu filature silk, from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: Where Exported (Raw Silk)
metadata.description: Breaks down raw silk exports by destination country for 1901 to 1906, showing France, Italy and the U.S.A. as the main buyers.

metadata.title: Export of Waste Silk
metadata.description: Gives the quantity in piculs and value in yen of waste silk exported in 1905 and 1906, noting that most went to France and Italy.

metadata.title: Import (from China)
metadata.description: Records imports of ordinary and wild silkworm cocoons from China by quantity and value for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Raw Silk Production (1905)
metadata.description: Shows the leading prefectures for raw silk production in 1905, giving the number of families engaged in sericulture and the value of output in yen for each district.

metadata.title: Japanese and Foreign Exporters of Raw Silk
metadata.description: Gives the July-June raw silk export volumes in bales, including shares going to Europe and the United States and the proportion shipped by Japanese firms, illustrating the growing direct export role of Japanese merchants.

metadata.title: Area Under Tea Plant and Number of Manufacturers
metadata.description: Shows the area planted under tea and the number of tea-manufacturing establishments from 1900 to 1905, documenting the growth of the tea industry.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Tea
metadata.description: Shows the annual output of tea by grade and type in Japan from 1901 to 1905, with totals, giving the scale and mix of domestic production.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1905)
metadata.description: Lists the leading tea-producing prefectures in 1905 with the number of families engaged in tea and the value of production.

metadata.title: Export of Teas
metadata.description: Gives the yearly quantity and value of tea exported from Japan from 1900 to 1906, following the discussion of foreign market prospects.

metadata.title: Destinations of Green Tea Exported
metadata.description: Breaks down Japanese green tea exports by destination country (U.S.A., Canada, China, others) for 1900 to 1906, showing where the green tea trade went.

metadata.title: Destination of Black Tea Exported
metadata.description: The table gives the annual export of Japanese black tea in kin, broken down by destination (U.S.A., Siberia, others) for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Foreign Horses Imported by the Government, 1900–1906]
metadata.description: Foreign stallions and other horses imported by the government after 1894-95 at the Horse Investigation Commission's urging, shown by breed and year.

metadata.title: [Number of Horses Kept at Studs and Depots in 1905]
metadata.description: The page lists the horses kept for breeding at the two studs and nine depots in 1905, with the total printed beneath.

metadata.title: Average Prices of 2 Year Colts
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Shows the rising average prices of two-year-old colts, cross-bred versus pure native, as evidence that government horse-breeding encouragement raised market prices.

metadata.title: Cattle Imported for Breeding
metadata.caption: Kind of Breed
metadata.description: Lists the number of bulls and cows of each European breed imported for cattle breeding in successive years, showing the shift toward dairy breeds the authorities favoured.

metadata.title: No. of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of cattle in Japan, by native, cross-bred and foreign breeds with totals, from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Horses
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of horses in Japan by native, cross-bred and foreign breeds with totals, 1900 to 1905, as a companion to the cattle figures.

metadata.title: Birthrates and Deathrates of Cattle and Horses
metadata.description: Records the yearly births and deaths among cattle and horses in Japan, showing livestock reproduction and mortality from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Lists the yearly numbers of sheep, goats and swine in Japan from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Reports the yearly number of animals slaughtered in Japan (cattle and calves, horses, sheep and goats, swine) from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Number of Households Keeping Poultry, (1905)
metadata.description: Gives the number of households keeping barn fowl and ducks in 1905, with the number of birds and the value of eggs, illustrating the minor scale of poultry farming.

metadata.title: Leading Poultry Districts in 1905
metadata.description: Lists the twenty-one leading prefectures for poultry in 1905, showing households, fowl and ducks, and the value of eggs produced.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Dairy in 1905.
metadata.description: Shows the leading prefectures for dairy farming in 1905, with the number of dairy establishments, milk cows and milk output in koku and yen.

metadata.title: Fruits in 1905.
metadata.description: Gives the number of fruit trees and the yield for each main fruit kind in Japan in 1905.

metadata.title: Outputs of Principal Fruit Districts
metadata.description: Lists the principal prefectures producing each fruit kind and their outputs, introduced by the sentence 'The outputs of principal fruit districts are shown below'.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.caption: Relative percentage
metadata.description: The page gives the relative percentage of Japan proper's sedimentary and igneous strata, introducing the chapter's account of metal veins and non-metallic deposits.

metadata.title: Output of Gold and Silver
metadata.description: Gives the yearly national output of gold and silver in momme from 1895 to 1906, showing the trend in the country's precious metal production.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Gold and Silver Mines (1905 and 1906)
metadata.description: Lists the principal gold and silver mines by name, prefecture and output in momme for 1905 and 1906 (1906 figures estimated), supporting the national totals above.

metadata.title: [Gold and Silver Output by Mines, 1905–1906]
metadata.description: Gives the gold and silver output of each mine in 1905 and 1906, showing the producing mines and the national totals used in the discussion of the year's mining output.

metadata.title: Output of Copper and Its Export
metadata.description: Shows Japan's copper production and exports for 1900 to 1906, with exports as a percentage of production, illustrating the trade in copper output.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Copper Mines in '05
metadata.caption: (Over 100,000 kin)
metadata.description: Lists the principal copper mines, their prefectures and their ore and product output for 1905, restricted to mines producing over 100,000 kin.

metadata.title: Output of Iron and Its Import
metadata.description: Gives yearly iron products in kwan and the quantities of iron and steel imported in kin from 1900 to 1906, showing the growth of domestic output and imports.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Iron Mines in 1905
metadata.description: Lists the output and production of the two principal iron mines in Iwate Prefecture for 1905.

metadata.title: Output of Antimony and Manganese
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of antimony and manganese in kin from 1900 to 1906, the 1906 figure being an estimate.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Manganese Mines in 1905
metadata.description: Gives the area in tsubo and the manganese products in kin of the principal manganese mines in 1905.

metadata.title: Demand and Supply of Coal
metadata.caption: (in 000 Metric Ton.)
metadata.description: Compares coal supply (output and imports) with demand (consumption and exports) in metric tons from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: [Latest Returns for Principal Coal Districts]
metadata.description: Gives the estimated 1906 coal output of the Hokkaidō and Jōban districts against 1905, with the increase, as the text introduces the latest returns.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Coal Mines in 1905
metadata.caption: (Over 100,000 in metric tons)
metadata.description: Lists the principal coal mines producing over 100,000 metric tons in 1905, with their location, area in tsubo and output.

metadata.title: Relative Ratio of Consumption of Coal
metadata.caption: (Index number.)
metadata.description: Gives an index of coal consumption by use (ships, railways, factories, salt production) and in total for 1900 to 1902.

metadata.title: Output of Sulphur and Its Export
metadata.description: Shows yearly sulphur output and exports from 1900 to 1906, giving the production and export trend for the industry.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Sulphur Mines in 1905
metadata.caption: (Over 500,000 kin)
metadata.description: Lists the principal sulphur mines of 1905 that produced over 500,000 kin, with their output and production.

metadata.title: Output of Petroleum and Its Import
metadata.description: Gives petroleum output in koku and imports by quantity and value for each year from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Petroleum Mines in 1905
metadata.caption: (Over 50,00 Koku)
metadata.description: Lists the principal petroleum mines of 1905 with their location, working area and output, concluding the petroleum section.

metadata.title: Mine-Employees
metadata.caption: (At the end of June)
metadata.description: Shows the number of employees in metal, coal, non-metal and alluvial mines at the end of June each year from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Accident in the Mines
metadata.description: Gives the number of mine accidents each year from 1900 to 1906 with deaths, severe injuries, other injuries and totals.

metadata.title: [Fishing Boats by Length and Main Division]
metadata.description: Shows the number of fishing boats in each main division of the country, split by length, and states the estimated cost of new boats in 1905.

metadata.title: Accidents to Fishing-Boats and Casualties to Fishermen
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1905 fishing-boat accidents by cause, giving the number of boats lost and the resulting crew killed, wounded, missing and total.

metadata.title: The Value of Catches and of Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of fish catches and marine products from 1900 to 1905, showing the trend over the period.

metadata.title: [Catches and Marine Products by Main Division, 1905]
metadata.description: Distributes the 1905 values of catches and marine products among the main divisions of the country, as introduced by the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Principal Kinds of Marine Products Caught]
metadata.caption: (Value in yen)
metadata.description: Lists the chief kinds of fish and the yen value of each caught, introducing the page's discussion of marine products.

metadata.title: [Principal Kinds of Manufactured Marine Products]
metadata.caption: Value
metadata.description: Gives the values of the principal manufactured marine products, such as dried squid, prawns, bonito, sardine and herring.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Marine Production
metadata.caption: (1905). Value in yen
metadata.description: Ranks the leading prefectural districts by the value of their marine production in 1905.

metadata.title: Crucian
metadata.description: Shows the value of aquaculture output by species, such as oysters, carp, eel and porphyra, for 1903 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Pelagic Sea Returns, July 1902 to June 1906]
metadata.description: The pelagic sea returns for the last four available years show junk, sailing-ship and steamship catches and the total catch value, illustrating the scale of marine harvest outside the bounty system.

metadata.title: [Bounty Granted to Pelagic Fishery, Years Ending March 1900 to 1905]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of ships engaged in pelagic fishing and the Treasury bounty paid for tonnage, crew and in total, showing the amount of bounty granted over six years.

metadata.title: Pelagic Fishery on Korean Coast (1905)
metadata.description: The table lists the number of ships, crew and yields of each kind of pelagic fishing on the Korean coast in 1905, illustrating the scale of Japanese whaling and fishing there described in the text.

metadata.title: [Salt Production, 1900-1905]
metadata.description: Summary figures for salt fields, furnaces, production, value and average price in Japan over 1900-1905, introducing the salt industry section.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Salt Production in 1905.
metadata.description: Lists the seven leading salt-producing districts in 1905 with their salt field area, production and value, showing where most Japanese salt was made.

metadata.title: Area of Forests
metadata.caption: (At end March, 1906).
metadata.description: Gives the area of Japan's forests by ownership at the end of March 1906, split into protection and utilization forests, showing the forests cover about 59 per cent of the country.

metadata.title: [Prefectural Figures Continued From Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top of the page lists further prefectural figures in two columns, continuing a list begun on the previous page.

metadata.title: [Forest Yield for the 1905–1906 Year]
metadata.description: Shows the forest yield of timbers and fuels by quantity and value for the 1905–1906 year, excluding Hokkaido, Formosa and other outlying places.

metadata.title: [Financial Yield of Forests by Kind of Forest, 1905]
metadata.description: Gives the financial yield of forests for 1905 by ownership class, with timber and faggots values, areas utilized and yield per cho, excluding Hokkaido and other outlying places.

metadata.title: [Forestry Receipts, Expenses and Balance, 1900-1906]
metadata.description: Shows annual receipts, expenses and resulting balance of State forest administration, illustrating that the profit margin was comparatively small.

metadata.title: Forest Products in Foreign Trade
metadata.caption: (in 1000 yen.)
metadata.description: Lists the principal forest products figuring in Japan's export and import trade by year, in thousand yen, showing rising timber and export values.

metadata.title: [Progress of State Forest Adjustment Work]
metadata.description: The table tabulates the progress so far made on State forest adjustment up to 1904, the estimates for 1905 and 1906, and the prospective work after 1907.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Camphor Twigs and Fallen Leaves]
metadata.description: Results of a chemical analysis at the Agricultural College in Tokyo showing water and camphor content of twigs and leaves, from hydrated and dehydrated materials.

metadata.title: [Proportion of Camphor Used in Various Products]
metadata.description: Shows the approximate share of camphor consumed by each product, with celluloid taking the largest proportion of the total.

metadata.title: Budget for 1907-8 Year
metadata.caption: (in, 000 yen)
metadata.description: Gives the estimated expenditure voted by the 23rd Diet session for the current financial year, split between ordinary and extraordinary expenditure and the supplementary budget.

metadata.title: The Ordinary Budget
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Compares the current year's ordinary budget revenue and expenditure with the preceding year, showing the amounts for each year and the increase or decrease.

metadata.title: Items of Ordinary and Extraordinary Revenues
metadata.caption: Ordinary Revenues (in Y. 1,000).
metadata.description: This table lists the items of ordinary revenue for 1907-8 against 1906-7, with the increase or decrease, showing where the national income came from in each year.

metadata.title: Extraordinary Revenues
metadata.caption: (in 000 yen)
metadata.description: Shows the extraordinary government revenue items, with two unlabelled comparison years and the increase or decrease between them, leading to the total of ordinary and extraordinary revenues.

metadata.title: Ordinary Expenditures
metadata.description: Lists the ordinary expenditure of each government department for 1907-8 against 1906-7, with the difference and the overall total.

metadata.title: Extraordinary Expenditures
metadata.description: Lists extraordinary expenditure by department with two comparison columns and the difference, showing where the extraordinary spending changed most.

metadata.title: [Extraordinary Expenditures by Department, Continued]
metadata.description: Continues the government expenditure statement, listing the remaining extraordinary expenditure items by department and the overall ordinary and extraordinary totals.

metadata.title: Special Account Funds Existing During 1904-5 Fiscal Years
metadata.caption: (1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Lists the special account funds in existence during fiscal years 1903-4 and 1904-5, in round thousand-yen figures, with their totals.

metadata.title: Consolidated and Working Funds
metadata.description: Shows the consolidated and working funds for the two fiscal years, with their total and the grand total of all special and working funds.

metadata.title: General Features of National Debts (Existing at the End of Mar., 1907)
metadata.description: The table lists Japan's national debt loans outstanding at the end of March 1907, by internal and foreign loan, with rates, issue years, redemption dates and amounts.

metadata.title: National Debts Existing at the End of Each Year
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Shows the year-by-year movement of Japan's national debt from 1871 to 1906, including issues, redemptions, outstanding amounts and debt per head of population.

metadata.title: Annual State Revenue and Expenditure Pertaining to the General Account
metadata.caption: (1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Gives state revenue and expenditure under the general account for the fiscal years 1893 to 1907, with estimates for 1905 onward, showing the budget balance over time.

metadata.title: Sources of Revenues (1)
metadata.caption: (1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese government's annual revenue from taxes, stamp receipts and public undertakings and state property, 1893–1907, with estimates for 1905–1907.

metadata.title: Sources of Revenues (2)
metadata.caption: (1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Continues the revenue breakdown, listing loans, the transferred Chinese indemnity and miscellaneous receipts for the same years, 1893–1907.

metadata.title: Proceeds from Principal Taxes and Duties (1)
metadata.caption: (1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Gives the proceeds of the principal taxes and duties (land, income and business taxes) for 1893–1907, with estimates for 1905–1907.

metadata.title: Proceeds from Principal Taxes and Duties (2)
metadata.description: Shows yearly receipts from taxes on liquor, customs duties and sugar excise from 1893 to 1907, continuing the principal taxes and duties series.

metadata.title: Proceeds from Principal State Undertakings and Properties
metadata.caption: (1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Lists receipts from the post and telegraph service, the tobacco monopoly and the railways by year from 1893 to 1907, as state undertakings and properties.

metadata.title: Proceeds from the War Taxes
metadata.description: Compares estimated and actual receipts from each War Tax for the fiscal year April 1905 to March 1906, which exceeded the estimates by over 3½ per cent.

metadata.title: [Estimated and Actual Receipts from Taxes and Monopolies]
metadata.description: Shows estimated versus actual state receipts from the listed taxes and the salt monopoly, with totals, for the financial year reported.

metadata.title: Appropriations for the Departments of State (1)
metadata.caption: (1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Gives annual state appropriations to the Civil List, Foreign Affairs, Home Affairs and Finance departments from 1893 to 1907, with estimates marked for later years.

metadata.title: Appropriations for the Departments of State (2)
metadata.description: Continues the state appropriations by year, here for the Army, Navy, Justice and Education departments from 1893 to 1907.

metadata.title: Appropriations for the Departments of State (3)
metadata.description: Summarises appropriations for the Agriculture and Commerce and Communication departments, with yearly totals, for selected years from 1893 to 1903.

metadata.title: [Appropriations for Agriculture and Commerce, Communication and Other Services]
metadata.description: Shows annual appropriations for agriculture, commerce and communication, with a note explaining changes in appropriations for justice, army and navy.

metadata.title: Percentage of Ordinary State Expenditure Allowed to Different Services
metadata.description: Gives the share of ordinary state expenditure allotted to military, debt, administration and total services for each year from 1893 to 1906 and the average.

metadata.title: State Monopolies — Japan Proper, 1906-7 Estimates
metadata.description: Lists the estimated receipts, outlay and purchasing expenses of the salt, camphor and tobacco monopolies in Japan proper for 1906-7.

metadata.title: Land Tax
metadata.description: Shows the national land tax rates by land category, giving the normal rate, war-time surcharge and combined total in percent.

metadata.title: Local and Subordinate Land Taxes
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Lists the yields of the subordinate local, urban and rural land tax scales, with their total, which the text says were added to the national tax.

metadata.title: Income Tax — 1st Kind: Income of Juridical Persons
metadata.description: Gives the normal and war-tax rates of the first kind of income tax, applied to companies and to other juridical persons by income bracket.

metadata.title: Income Tax — 2nd Kind
metadata.description: States the normal rate of the second kind of income tax, which applies to income from bonds and shares.

metadata.title: 3rd Kind (Income of Other Descriptions)
metadata.description: The page gives the normal income tax rates and corresponding war tax percentages for the third kind of income, showing how rates rise with income bands.

metadata.title: [Business Tax Data of Assessment and Rate of Assessment]
metadata.description: The page lists the data used for assessing business tax under each of four kinds of business and the corresponding normal rate of assessment.

metadata.title: [Business Tax Rates by Kind]
metadata.description: Lists the national business tax rates for the 5th to 10th kinds, each charged on capital, proceeds, contract amount, rent, or commission, and on persons, followed by the war tax surcharges.

metadata.title: Registration Fees
metadata.description: Gives the registration fee rates for immovables, corporations, trade establishments and professional registration, noting the rates are based on value and include war taxation.

metadata.title: [Fees for Copyright, Patent Right, Designs, Trade-marks and Mining]
metadata.description: These are the government fee schedules for registering copyright, patent rights, designs, trade-marks and mining rights, listed by type of transaction.

metadata.title: [Medicine Selling Tax Rates]
metadata.description: This list gives the rates of the medicine selling tax: the compounding and selling charge, the license per kind, and the stamp duty on medicine.

metadata.title: Sugar Excise
metadata.description: Lists the sugar excise duty rates per picul for each of the four sugar classes.

metadata.title: Woollen and Silk Textiles or Mixtures
metadata.description: Gives the tax rate on woollen and on silk textiles or their mixtures, each set as a share of value.

metadata.title: Kerosene Oil
metadata.description: States the tax rate on kerosene oil, given per gallon.

metadata.title: Prefectural Finance
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1000).
metadata.description: Shows prefectural revenue and expenditure for selected years from 1893 to 1902, illustrating local government finances under the existing regulations.

metadata.title: [Prefectural Revenue and Expenditure, 1903–1907]
metadata.description: Shows prefectural revenue and expenditure over 1903 to 1907, with later years estimated, illustrating the prefectural budget position before the discussion of prefectural revenue sources.

metadata.title: [Estimated Prefectural Revenue from Ordinary Sources, 1906–7]
metadata.description: The text states that the ordinary sources of prefectural revenue were estimated to yield these amounts for 1906–7, with the total shown at the foot.

metadata.title: Contributions and Aids from the Treasury to Local Finances
metadata.description: Lists the amounts the Treasury gave to local finances as contributions and aids for 1905 to 1907, given in yen.

metadata.title: Finance of Municipal Corporations (Cities)
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1000)
metadata.description: Gives revenue and expenditure of Japanese city municipal corporations for selected years from 1893 to 1904, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Finance of Towns and Villages
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives revenue and expenditure of towns and villages for selected years from 1893 to 1904, in thousands of yen, following the city figures.

metadata.title: Total of Prefectural, Municipal, Town and Village Revenue and Expenditure
metadata.description: Shows combined revenue and expenditure of prefectural, municipal, town and village finances from 1893 to 1904, as background to the discussion of local loans.

metadata.title: Local Loans Existing at the End on Each Year
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1000)
metadata.description: Gives the year-by-year amounts of local loans outstanding at each year end, broken down by prefectures, counties, cities, towns, associations and short-term loans.

metadata.title: [Local Loans Existing in November 1905 by Class]
metadata.description: Following the Home Office investigation, it lists the debts outstanding in November 1905 for prefectures and counties in yen.

metadata.title: [Local Debts by Rate of Interest]
metadata.description: Shows how the local debts were distributed across the interest rate bands, as the text introduces with the statement that the rates were returned as follows.

metadata.title: Classification of Local Loans
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1000)
metadata.description: Gives the annual amount of local loans from 1893 to 1905 classified by purpose, showing how the total borrowing was spent on each category.

metadata.title: Financial Resources of Japan at the Close of 1904
metadata.description: Lists Japan's financial resources by category at the close of 1904, from lands and buildings to warships, totalling to a grand total after deducting foreign loans, as part of an inquiry summary.

metadata.title: [Estimated Increase of Financial Resources from the Close of 1904 to the Middle of 1906]
metadata.caption: Mil. of Y.
metadata.description: Gives the estimated growth of Japan's financial resources over roughly one and a half years after 1904, net of foreign loans, and the Taiwan figure for comparison.

metadata.title: [Financial Resources of Japan, Middle of 1906 (Continued)]
metadata.caption: (Mil. of Y.)
metadata.description: A continuation list giving the components of Japan's financial resources in 1906, with the grand total, which excludes several state undertakings for lack of returns.

metadata.title: [Gross Amount of Taxation and Individual Burden in 1906]
metadata.description: Official 1906 research giving gross receipts from national, prefectural, municipal and rural taxes and the resulting per capita individual tax burden in Japan.

metadata.title: [Taxation and Per Capita Burden Compared with European Countries and the U.S.A.]
metadata.description: A comparison of national taxes and per capita burden in several Western countries, used to show that Japanese taxation per capita is not light relative to wealth and exports.

metadata.title: [Comparative Volume of Exports]
metadata.description: Comparing Japan's export volume with other countries, this table lists exports in 100-yen units and taxes per 100 yen of exports for each country, based on 1902 returns.

metadata.title: Japanese Stocks in Foreign Hands
metadata.description: Based on investigations around March 1906, this table lists the Japanese government bonds and municipal stocks that had passed into foreign hands, with amounts in yen and a total.

metadata.title: [Loans Floated Since the Conclusion of Peace]
metadata.description: The table lists the loans raised by companies and municipalities since the peace, excluding Government bonds, with their amounts, interest rates, net proceeds and actual interest.

metadata.title: [Government and Osaka City Bonds for Reference]
metadata.description: The page gives the Government and Osaka City bonds issued earlier, offered for reference alongside the recent loans listed above.

metadata.title: Receipt by Japan
metadata.description: Shows the sources of money received by Japan from foreign shipping, tourists, and government and legation transactions, with a total, as an account of international receipts.

metadata.title: Disbursements by Japan
metadata.description: Lists the payments Japan made abroad, such as overseas travel, shipping, and government expenditure, with a total, paired with the receipts table above.

metadata.title: [War Disbursements by Japan, Army and Navy]
metadata.description: Gives the war disbursements of the Army and Navy from the outset of the war to March 1907, with the combined total.

metadata.title: [Receipts to the War Fund]
metadata.description: Lists the sources of funds that financed the war, such as loans, general and special account appropriations and miscellaneous receipts, with a total, and notes the timing of final accounts.

metadata.title: Progress of Industrial Investment
metadata.description: The table shows yearly growth from 1896 to 1905 in number of companies, capital, reserves and profits of organized industrial enterprises, illustrating the investment progress discussed in the text.

metadata.title: [Industrial Companies with Paid-Up Capital of Y. 500,000 and Above, 1905]
metadata.description: Lists the forty kinds of industrial companies with paid-up capital of Y. 500,000 or more, with their number and paid-up capital, for 1905.

metadata.title: Distribution of Industries
metadata.description: Lists leading prefectures containing companies each with over Y. 3,000,000 paid up capital in 1905, giving the number of such companies and their paid up capital.

metadata.title: Factories and Its Employees
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of factories, separated by motive power, and the male, female and total operatives employed, from 1893 to 1905.

metadata.title: Motive Powers in 1905
metadata.caption: Note:—For 1905 kinds of motive powers are as follows:—
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1905 factory motive power by kind, giving the number of engines and horsepower for steam, gas, petroleum, water wheels, dynamos and motors.

metadata.title: Kind of Factories
metadata.description: This page lists the number of factories by industry group, split by whether they were run by motors, with daily average employees, giving totals for Japan's factory sector.

metadata.title: Weaving Establishments, Operatives and Value of Production (1895 to 1905)
metadata.description: Gives yearly totals for Japan's weaving industry from 1895 to 1905: number of weaving houses, looms, operatives and value of production.

metadata.title: Leading Weaving Districts (1)
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures for weaving, with weaving houses, machine and hand looms, total looms and operators, as a first part of a fuller district list.

metadata.title: Leading Weaving Districts. (2)
metadata.caption: Value (in Y. 1,000).
metadata.description: Shows the value of silk, mixed, cotton, hempen and woollen fabrics produced in each leading weaving prefecture, continuing the regional survey of textile output.

metadata.title: Production (Value).
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000).
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of silk, mixed, cotton, hemp and woollen fabric production from 1895 to 1905, showing the trend of the textile industry.

metadata.title: [Spinners Union Returns for June 1906]
metadata.description: The Spinners Union returns for June 1906 give the number of companies, paid-up capital, and spindles in the cotton spinning industry, showing the sector's scale after its recent growth.

metadata.title: [Cotton Piece Goods Looms, Output and Yarn Consumption by Half-Year]
metadata.description: The cotton piece goods industry, especially shirtings and T-cloth, is shown growing over 1903–1905 through looms in operation, output, yarn consumed and waste yarn.

metadata.title: [Cotton Yarn Consumption at Home, Exports and Imports by Half-Year]
metadata.description: Consumption at home, exports and imports of cotton yarn are given by half-year for 1903 to 1905, illustrating the trade behind the piece goods industry's growth.

metadata.title: Cotton Spinning Mills and Production
metadata.description: Number of cotton spinning mills, capital, spindles, yarn output, hands and working hours are compared for 1895 and 1896.

metadata.title: [Cotton Spinning Statistics, 1897–1905]
metadata.description: A continuing multi-year series of cotton spinning figures for 1897 to 1905, whose column headings appear on the preceding page.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Cotton Spinning. (1905)
metadata.description: Shows, for each leading cotton spinning district in 1905, the number of factories, capital, spindles, operatives and yarn output.

metadata.title: Leading Cotton Spinning Companies. (1905)
metadata.description: Lists the leading cotton spinning companies in 1905 with their capital, spindles, half-yearly profit per spindle, dividends and head office locations.

metadata.title: [Cotton Spinning Companies]
metadata.description: A list of cotton spinning companies with their figures and locations, continued from the previous page, forming part of the industry survey.

metadata.title: Export and Import of Cotton Yarns (Quantity)
metadata.caption: (Quantity)
metadata.description: Shows annual export and import quantities of cotton yarns for 1896–1905, presented in two side-by-side blocks.

metadata.title: Ceramics
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the value of ceramic production and exports in yen for 1896–1905, shown in two side-by-side blocks.

metadata.title: Leading Ceramic Districts
metadata.caption: (1905) (Above 150,000 yen)
metadata.description: Lists the leading ceramic-producing prefectures in 1905, with families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Value of Lacquer Ware Production and Its Export
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of lacquer ware production and exports from 1896 to 1905, presented as two side-by-side blocks to illustrate the trade's development.

metadata.title: Leading Lacquer Ware Districts (1905)
metadata.description: Lists the twelve leading lacquer ware districts in 1905 with the number of families engaged, employees, and value of output.

metadata.title: Production and Export of Match
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly production and export of matches from 1895 to 1905, with quantities in thousands of gross and values in thousands.

metadata.title: Leading Districts for Match Industry
metadata.description: Shows the number of families, employees and value of the match industry in the six leading districts in 1905.

metadata.title: Value of Wax and Refined-Wax Products
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for families engaged and the value of wax and refined-wax products from 1895 to 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Wax Districts
metadata.description: Lists the leading wax-producing districts in 1905 with families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Mats and Matting
metadata.description: Shows families engaged, employees and value of floor mats and fancy export matting produced from 1899 to 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Mat and Matting Districts
metadata.caption: (of above Y. 200,000 in the year ending June, 1905)
metadata.description: Shows the leading prefectures for mat and matting manufacture, with families, employees, and values of floor mats and export fancy matting for the year ending June 1905.

metadata.title: Plaits of Straw and Wood Shaving
metadata.description: Gives yearly totals for the straw and wood shaving plait industry from 1899 to 1905, covering workshops, employees, and value.

metadata.title: Leading Straw-Plaits and Wood Shaving-Plaits Districts
metadata.caption: (of above Y. 200,000 in 1905.)
metadata.description: Lists the leading districts for straw-plait and wood shaving-plait production in 1905, by workshops, employees and value of each plait type.

metadata.title: Vegetable Oils
metadata.description: Shows families engaged, employees and value of the vegetable oil industry for the years 1896 to 1899.

metadata.title: [Vegetable Oils Industry, 1900–1905]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of families engaged, employees and value of the vegetable oils industry from 1900 to 1905, continuing the industry statistics.

metadata.title: Leading Vegetable Oils Districts
metadata.caption: (Places which produced above Y. 250,000 in 1905).
metadata.description: Lists the prefectures whose vegetable oil output exceeded Y. 250,000 in 1905, with their families, employees and value.

metadata.title: Japanese Paper
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for the Japanese paper industry from 1896 to 1905: families engaged, employees (not reported for 1896–1898) and value.

metadata.title: Japanese Paper Districts
metadata.caption: (Places which produced above Y. 300,000 in 1905).
metadata.description: Lists the prefectures whose Japanese paper output exceeded Y. 300,000 in 1905, with their families, employees and value in yen.

metadata.title: [Prefectural Statistics of Paper Manufacture]
metadata.description: This continuation table lists prefectures with families engaged, employees and value of paper manufacture, carried over from the preceding page's account of the industry.

metadata.title: European Paper
metadata.description: This table gives the yearly development of the European paper industry from 1895 to 1905, covering factories, capital, machinery, horse power, employees and output.

metadata.title: Leading European Paper Manufacturing Companies
metadata.caption: (Places mhica produced above Y. 500,000 in 1905)
metadata.description: This table lists the leading European paper manufacturing companies, with their capital, machines, horse power, employees and output, limited to those producing above Y. 500,000 in 1905.

metadata.title: Production and Import of European Paper
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: This table sets the value of European paper production against the total value of imports for each year from 1896 to 1905.

metadata.title: Production of Sugar in Japan
metadata.caption: (in thousand kin)
metadata.description: Summarises Japan's domestic sugar output for 1903-1905 by manufactories, sugar, molasses, syrup and candy sugar.

metadata.title: Import of Sugar
metadata.description: Shows the value in yen of brown, refined and total sugar imports into Japan for 1896-1905.

metadata.title: Export of Sugar from Formosa
metadata.caption: (in thousand kin)
metadata.description: Gives sugar exported from Formosa in 1895-1905, split into white and brown sugar sent to Japan proper, to other countries, and in total.

metadata.title: Demand and Supply of Sugar.
metadata.description: Shows the yearly sugar consumption in Japan from 1900 to 1904, split into home production with Formosan sugar and imports, plus per-capita consumption.

metadata.title: Sugar Production of Formosa.
metadata.description: Gives the output of brown and white sugar in Formosa for 1904 and 1905, with the combined total, as a source of Japan's sugar supply.

metadata.title: Formosan Sugar Import to Japan Proper.
metadata.description: Lists the Formosan sugar imported into Japan proper in 1904 and 1905 by sugar grade and port of entry, with totals.

metadata.title: Indigo (Japanese.)
metadata.description: Shows the number of families, employees and value of the Japanese indigo industry from 1899 to 1905, showing a decline in later years.

metadata.title: [Indigo Production in Tokushima, 1905]
metadata.description: Introduced by the statement that most of the 1905 indigo production came from Tokushima, this gives that prefecture's families, employees and value.

metadata.title: Peppermint
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of families, employees and the value of crude peppermint, menthol crystal and oil produced from 1899 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Peppermint Production in Kanagawa, 1905]
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1905 peppermint production, which came mostly from Kanagawa, by factories, employees and the value of menthol crystal and oil.

metadata.title: Leather
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of families, employees and total value of leather production from 1899 to 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Leathers Districts in 1905
metadata.caption: (Places producing above Y. 100,000).
metadata.description: Lists the leading leather-producing districts in 1905, with families, employees and leather values by type and in total.

metadata.title: Leading Manufacturing Districts of Crude-Camphor and Oil. (1904)
metadata.description: Compares the leading crude-camphor and camphor-oil manufacturing districts in 1904 by factories, furnaces, licences, employees and price.

metadata.title: Leading Clocks Districts (in 1905)
metadata.description: Shows the number of factories, employees and value of output of the clock industry in the leading districts in 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Glass Districts (in 1905)
metadata.description: Shows the number of factories, employees and value of output of the glass industry in the leading districts in 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Brushes Districts (in 1905)
metadata.description: Shows the number of factories or workshops, employees and value of output of the brush industry in the leading districts in 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Button Districts (in 1905)
metadata.description: Shows the number of factories, employees and value of output of the button industry in the leading districts in 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Hosiery Districts (in 1905)
metadata.description: Shows the number of families engaged, employees and value of output of the hosiery industry in the leading districts in 1905.

metadata.title: Bricks and Tiles in 1905
metadata.description: Statistics of the brick and tile industry in 1905, showing factories, employees and values by district, with bricks split by fire-proof and ordinary types.

metadata.title: Milling Districts in 1905 (by Machine.)
metadata.description: Milling statistics for 1905 for machine-operated mills by prefecture, listing factories, employees, output and value.

metadata.title: Canned Articles in 1905 (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Canned food production in 1905 for Tokyo, Kyoto and Aichi, giving factories, employees and values by beef, fish and other products.

metadata.title: [Prefectural Figures, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: Continuation of a prefectural table listing six western and Kyushu prefectures and their totals, the column headings of which appear on the preceding page.

metadata.title: Artificial Manure (in 1905)
metadata.description: Shows the number of artificial manure factories, employees, and animal and mineral output and value by district in 1905.

metadata.title: Leading Silk Handkerchief Districts (1905)
metadata.description: Lists the number of workshops, employees by sex, and quantity and value of silk handkerchiefs produced in the leading districts in 1905.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Industries (in 1905)
metadata.description: Lists factories, employees, output and value of miscellaneous industries such as bamboo wares, fans, cement and soaps in 1905.

metadata.title: Factories Conducted by Government (1905)
metadata.description: Lists the government-run factories, arsenals, shipyards and works in 1905, giving engines, horsepower, employees, daily wages by sex and coal consumed.

metadata.title: Number of Banks (Feb. 1907)
metadata.description: Shows the number of banks of each class in Japan in February 1907 with their authorized capital, giving the national banking picture after the old system ended.

metadata.title: Foreign Banks in Japan (Feb. 1907)
metadata.description: Lists the number and authorized capital of foreign banks operating in Japan in February 1907, by class of bank.

metadata.title: Liabilities
metadata.description: The Bank of Japan's half-year statement for 1906 is set out here, listing its liabilities in yen to show how its funds were held.

metadata.title: Assets
metadata.description: The same half-year statement continues with the Bank's assets in yen, showing its loans, discounts and deposits.

metadata.title: Profit and Loss Account
metadata.description: The bank's profit and loss account for the half-year, showing debit items (expenses, dividend, reserve and balance carried forward) and credit items balancing to the same total.

metadata.title: Assets
metadata.description: The asset side of the same balance sheet, listing cash, bank deposits, bullion, bonds, loans and property, balancing the liabilities total.

metadata.title: Account
metadata.description: The profit and appropriation account of the bank, showing reserves, the dividend paid and the balance carried forward.

metadata.title: Liabilities
metadata.description: The balance sheet of the Industrial Bank of Japan, listing its liabilities (capital, reserves, debentures, deposits and profit) to illustrate the Bank's financial position.

metadata.title: Assets
metadata.description: The balance sheet of the Industrial Bank of Japan, listing its assets (cash, loans, bonds and uncalled capital) to show the Bank's holdings, matching the liabilities total.

metadata.title: Account
metadata.description: This table shows how the Hypothec Bank of Japan's profit for the period was appropriated among reserve, dividend, bonus and carried-forward balance.

metadata.title: Liabilities
metadata.description: This table gives the liabilities of the Hypothec Bank of Japan in yen, including debentures, capital, reserve and profits, with the total.

metadata.title: Account
metadata.description: Lists how the year's profits were applied, covering the dividend, reserves, bonus and the balance carried forward.

metadata.title: Liabilities
metadata.caption: (Exiting on 31st Dec. '06)
metadata.description: A balance sheet of the bank showing its liabilities as at 31 December 1906, with the total matching the assets total.

metadata.title: Assets
metadata.description: The bank's assets as at 31 December 1906, set against the liabilities, with the same total.

metadata.title: Accounts
metadata.description: The distribution of the bank's net profit for the half year, showing dividend, reserve, bonus and the balance carried forward.

metadata.title: Liabilities
metadata.caption: (31st Dec., '07)
metadata.description: Shows the liabilities side of the Hokkaido bank's balance sheet at the end of 1907, with capital, reserves, deposits and net profit.

metadata.title: Assets
metadata.description: Shows the asset side of the bank's balance sheet, listing unpaid capital, loans, bonds, property and cash, which balances the liabilities total.

metadata.title: Account
metadata.description: Shows how the bank's current half-year net profit was distributed between dividend, reserve and balance carried forward.

metadata.title: Ordinary Banks.
metadata.caption: (At end of 1906.) (in 000 yen.)
metadata.description: Lists the leading ordinary banks in Tokyo, Osaka and Yokohama at the end of 1906, giving paid-up capital, reserve fund, deposits, loans and dividend for each bank.

metadata.title: Survey of Banking Business: The Bank of Japan
metadata.caption: (In thousand yen.)
metadata.description: The page gives annual figures for the Bank of Japan's capital, reserves, deposits, advances, net profits and dividends from 1895 to 1906, as a survey of its banking business.

metadata.title: The Yokohama Specie Bank
metadata.caption: (In thousand yen.)
metadata.description: This table gives the same yearly banking figures for the Yokohama Specie Bank from 1895 to 1906, set beneath the Bank of Japan survey for comparison.

metadata.title: Ordinary Banks
metadata.caption: (In thousand yen.)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly position of ordinary banks from 1895 to 1906: number, capital, reserve, deposits, loans and bills discounted, showing growth of banking business.

metadata.title: Savings Banks
metadata.caption: (In thousand yen.)
metadata.description: Shows savings bank statistics from 1895 to 1906: number of banks, capital, reserves, deposits, loans and bills discounted, with ordinary banks' savings business shown separately.

metadata.title: Comparative Table of Bank Rate
metadata.caption: (Bank of Japan)
metadata.description: Shows the Bank of Japan's highest and lowest loan and bill discount rates and deposit interest for each year 1897–1906, giving the context for Japanese banking rates.

metadata.title: Comparative Table of Tokyo Market Rate
metadata.description: Gives the average Tokyo market rates for loans, discounts, current account and fixed deposit interest for 1897–1906, showing money-market conditions in the Tokyo banking world.

metadata.title: Amount of Bills Cleared at Various Clearing-Houses in Japan
metadata.caption: (In thousand yen.)
metadata.description: Shows the amount of bills cleared at Osaka and other Japanese clearing-houses by year, from 1895 to 1906, illustrating the scale of the Osaka clearing-house in the national system.

metadata.title: Fineness of the Coins
metadata.description: Summarises the regulation fineness of the gold, silver, nickel and copper coins introduced under the 1897 currency reform.

metadata.title: Amount of Coins in Circulation
metadata.description: Shows the yearly amount of gold, silver, subsidiary, nickel and copper coins in circulation at year-end, from 1895 to 1906.

metadata.title: Volume of Paper Currency in Circulation
metadata.caption: (In thousand yen.)
metadata.description: Gives the volume of government paper money, national bank notes, convertible bank notes and their total in circulation at year-end, 1895 to 1906.

metadata.title: Volume of Specie Reserves
metadata.description: Shows the gold and silver coin reserves held at the end of each year, with the total and the coin, paper money and bank notes in circulation, from 1895 to 1906.

metadata.title: Amount of Coins Turned out by the Mint
metadata.caption: (In thousand yen)
metadata.description: Lists the coins struck by the Japanese Mint each fiscal year by metal, with totals, from the opening of the Mint through 1906, with asterisked old gold coin face values.

metadata.title: [New Enterprises Launched or Expanded, October 1905 to March 1907]
metadata.description: Shows the new companies and expansions of existing companies in banking, spinning and electricity that the Bank of Japan recorded from October 1905 to March 1907, in thousand yen.

metadata.title: [New Capital and Expansion of Companies by Nature of Project]
metadata.description: Compares new company capital and expansion of existing companies across industries, contrasting the period after the Japan-China war with the later investment boom.

metadata.title: Total Number of Companies
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of companies with their authorized and paid-up capital, illustrating the growth of corporations from 1896 to 1905.

metadata.title: Companies Established by Foreigners
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Shows the number and capital of companies established by foreigners at each year-end from 1901 to 1904, with the unknown-capital counts marked by asterisks.

metadata.title: Number and Capital of Companies Classified by Nature of Enterprise
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Shows yearly counts and paid-up capital of companies in Japan from 1896 to 1905, split by agricultural, industrial, commercial and transportation enterprise, with totals.

metadata.title: Life Insurance Business
metadata.description: Shows the growth of life insurance companies in Japan from 1881 to 1904, covering number of companies, capital, reserves, premiums and payments.

metadata.title: [New Contracts and Number of Assured at End of Year in Life Insurance]
metadata.description: Gives the new life insurance contracts made each year and the number of assured persons and policy amounts at year end, 1881 to 1904.

metadata.title: Fire Insurance
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Summarises the fire insurance companies in Japan for selected years from 1895 to 1904, with capital, reserves, insured amounts, receipts and expenses.

metadata.title: Marine Insurance
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for Japan's marine insurance companies, covering capital, reserves, insurance amounts, receipts and expenses, from 1895 to 1904.

metadata.title: Carriage Insurance
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Shows carriage insurance business from 1900 to 1904, with the figures for companies whose carriage insurance was only a subordinate line marked by an asterisk.

metadata.title: Leading Life Insurance Companies in 1905-6
metadata.caption: Capital Paid-up (¥ in 1,000); Liability Reserve (¥ in 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the twelve leading Japanese life insurance companies in 1905-6 with their paid-up capital, reserves, premium amounts and dividend rates.

metadata.title: Leading Foreign Fire & Transport Ins. Cos. in Japan
metadata.description: The table lists leading foreign fire and transport insurance companies operating in Japan, with the deposit each lodged with the Government and the amount of premium recorded.

metadata.title: Chambers of Commerce at Principal Districts
metadata.description: Lists the number of members, electors by voting qualification, and expenses of chambers of commerce in the principal Japanese commercial districts in 1905.

metadata.title: Tokyo Mercantile Agency
metadata.caption: (Established 1896)
metadata.description: Shows yearly subscriber numbers, inquiries received and replies given by the Tokyo Mercantile Agency from 1901 to 1906.

metadata.title: Osaka Mercantile Agency
metadata.caption: (Established 1901.)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly subscriber numbers and communication counts of the Osaka Mercantile Agency from 1901 to 1906, by type of communication.

metadata.title: Number, Capital, Etc. of Exchanges
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows the number, authorized and paid-up capital, reserves, deposits and profit of Japan's exchanges from 1900 to 1905, introduced as the exchanges section.

metadata.title: Amount of Bonds and Shares Transacted at the Stock Exchanges
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of bonds and the number of shares traded on the stock exchanges from 1900 to 1905, illustrating growth in exchange business.

metadata.title: Amount of Merchandise Transacted at the Merchandise Exchanges
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the yearly amounts of various commodities such as iron, sugar, cotton and silk traded on the merchandise exchanges from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Amount of Merchandise Transacted at the Merchandise Exchanges (continued)
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Continues the merchandise exchange figures, giving yearly transactions in textile fabrics, salt and manure from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Amount of Rice Transacted at the Rice Exchanges
metadata.description: Shows the yearly volume of rice traded at the rice exchanges from 1900 to 1905, with the average price per koku, illustrating the home grain market.

metadata.title: Margin Money of Popular Shares
metadata.description: Lists the existing margin money rates for some of the most popular shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, as described in the accompanying text.

metadata.title: [Dues Rates on Shares and Bonds]
metadata.description: Lists the dues charged by various companies and securities on the Tokyo exchanges, showing the fee rate per unit against each name.

metadata.title: [Exchange Dues and Brokerage on Jiki, Nobe and Teiki]
metadata.description: Shows the exchange dues, brokerage and total charge in sen for three kinds of transaction, Jiki, Nobe and Teiki, per shares and per Y. 100 of debentures.

metadata.title: Jiki
metadata.description: Gives the dues, brokerage and total per share by price bracket in yen for the Jiki transactions.

metadata.title: Teiki
metadata.description: Gives the dues, brokerage and total per share by price bracket in yen for the Teiki transactions.

metadata.title: [Brokerage Charges Table (Continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a brokerage fee schedule by transaction value, showing rates for each yen bracket, which the surrounding text on brokers explains.

metadata.title: No. of Shares, etc. Transacted in 1905 and 1906
metadata.description: Monthly number of shares transacted on the Tokyo and Osaka stock exchanges in 1905 and 1906, shown to illustrate the volume of trading in each year.

metadata.title: Annual Average Quotations of Leading Shares
metadata.description: Average annual share prices of three leading companies, Hokkaido Colliery, Nippon Yusen Kaisha and the Tokyo Stock Exchange, from 1895 to 1903.

metadata.title: Monthly Quotations of Leading Shares
metadata.caption: Yen 50
metadata.description: Monthly highest and lowest quotations of Japan Railway Company and Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Company shares for 1905 and 1906, given in yen per share.

metadata.title: Tokyo Gas Company
metadata.caption: Yen 50
metadata.description: Monthly highest and lowest share prices of Tokyo Gas Company stock for 1905 and 1906, printed beneath the Nippon Yusen Kaisha table as a comparison of home-market movements.

metadata.title: Tokyo Stock Exchange
metadata.caption: Yen 50
metadata.description: Monthly highest and lowest prices of Tokyo Stock Exchange listings in 1905 and 1906, given to show the market's monthly price range during those two years.

metadata.title: [Gross and Paid Up Capital of Warehouses]
metadata.description: Shows the gross and paid up capital of the four leading warehouses in Japan, introducing the state of the warehousing business.

metadata.title: Dividends Declared During The Last 14 Terms
metadata.description: Lists the dividend percentages declared half-yearly by the four warehouse companies over the last fourteen terms, from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: [Four Companies' Inventory As Reported In The Last Term]
metadata.description: Gives the liabilities and assets of the four warehouse companies as reported in the last term, showing their financial position.

metadata.title: Comparative Table of Wages
metadata.description: A summary index of wage levels by occupational group and in general average for 1900 to 1905, placed before the detailed wage tables to show the overall trend.

metadata.title: Wages
metadata.caption: (m.=males; f.=females; y.c.=yearly contract; m.c=monthly contract; d.w=daily wages.)
metadata.description: Detailed daily and monthly wage rates in sen for many trades and occupations, grouped by industry, for 1901 to 1905, giving the detail behind the comparative index.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous
metadata.description: Shows the wages paid to various classes of workers from 1901 to 1905, given in sen, as part of the home trade and price survey.

metadata.title: Comparative Table of Price of Commodities
metadata.description: Indexes of commodity prices by category, with a general average, for the years 1900 to 1905, showing the trend in living costs.

metadata.title: Domestic Exhibitions
metadata.description: Summarises the results of the first five national Domestic Exhibitions held from 1877 to 1903, covering area, exhibitors, sales, visitors, proceeds and expenses.

metadata.title: [Japan's Exhibits at World Fairs, 1893–1903]
metadata.description: Summarises Japan's participation in the Chicago, Paris and St. Louis world fairs, giving the size of its section, exhibit numbers, values, sales and expenses, following the text on Japan's early exhibition history.

metadata.title: [Prize Winners in Art and Craft Exhibitions]
metadata.description: The page lists prize-winning artists and craftsmen with their residence and exhibit, including the Grand Prizes and Gold Medals awarded at the St. Louis World's Fair.

metadata.title: [Craftsmen and Artists, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: A continuation list of artists and craftsmen with their localities and fields of work, part of the Home Trade survey of notable producers.

metadata.title: [Ainu Population in Hokkaido, 1872–1905]
metadata.description: The Ainu population figures for Hokkaido from 1872 to 1905, given to support the article's claim that the Ainu numbers are increasing rather than decreasing.

metadata.title: Export and Import of Commodities
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: The page shows the yearly value of Japan's exports, imports and total foreign trade from 1871 to 1906, illustrating the growth of foreign trade since the treaty ports opened.

metadata.title: Exports and Imports of Specie and Bullion
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: This short table gives the exports and imports of specie and bullion for two years, 1875 and 1885, following the commodity trade figures.

metadata.title: Monthly Trade Returns in 1906
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the monthly value of Japan's commodity exports, imports and balance of trade for 1906, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Specie and Bullion
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows monthly exports and imports of specie and bullion in early 1906, in thousands of yen, with the net balance.

metadata.title: [Monthly Exports and Imports]
metadata.description: Shows month-by-month exports and imports for the latter part of the year, with the balance of trade for each month and a yearly total.

metadata.title: Trade Returns of Leading Ports (1905 and 1906)
