metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Compares the export and import values of the leading treaty ports for 1905 and 1906, showing where Japan's foreign trade was concentrated.

metadata.title: Exports of Specie and Bullion
metadata.description: Gives the export of specie and bullion from Japan by destination for 1903 to 1906, with yearly totals, under the specie and bullion section.

metadata.title: Imports
metadata.description: Shows the value of imports by country of origin, with the four year columns whose headings are not printed on this page; it precedes the monthly import and export figures.

metadata.title: Monthly Import of Merchandise
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Gives the monthly value of merchandise imports for 1902 to 1906, with annual totals, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Monthly Export of Merchandise
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Lists monthly merchandise export values in thousands of yen for five years, the year headings for this table not appearing on this page, following the monthly import table.

metadata.title: [Monthly Figures for October to December, 1902–1906]
metadata.description: This fragment continues a table of monthly figures from the top of the page, giving the October to December totals and annual totals for 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: Monthly Export and Import of Specie and Bullion
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: The page gives monthly figures for Japan's export and import of specie and bullion over 1904 to 1906, with yearly totals, showing the flow of gold and silver in each month.

metadata.title: Relative Shares of Asia, Europe, America and Australia in the Trade of Japan
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's foreign trade with Asia, Europe, America and Australia at intervals from 1874 to 1906, as a basis for the discussion of principal exports.

metadata.title: Annual Export of Staple Commodities
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's yearly export values of major staple commodities from 1890 to 1906, given as a long-run trade record.

metadata.title: Exports to Various Countries
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Lists Japan's exports by destination country, grouped under Asia and Europe, for 1902 to 1906, with Asian totals shown.

metadata.title: Annual Import of Staple Commodities
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Annual figures for the main imported staple goods, such as raw cotton, yarn, tissues, sugar, rice and iron, accompany the discussion of principal imports.

metadata.title: Imports from Various Countries
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's imports from each foreign country and region for 1902 to 1906, grouped by Asia, Europe, America and other countries, with regional totals.

metadata.title: [Continuation of Foreign Trade Table: Hawaii, Other Countries, Unknown and Grand Total]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a foreign trade figures table whose column headings appear on the previous page; the rows show Hawaii, other countries, unknown and grand totals.

metadata.title: Steam-Vessels That Entered From and Cleared to Foreign Countries
metadata.caption: (Tons is thousand.)
metadata.description: This table gives the tonnage of steam vessels entering from and clearing to foreign countries by nationality, year by year from 1895 to 1906, showing the growth of shipping.

metadata.title: New Import Tariff Schedulm
metadata.caption: (Official Translation). Import Tariff
metadata.description: The page reproduces the official English translation of the new import tariff schedule, listing articles in groups with their units and duty rates in yen or percentage.

metadata.title: Import Duty Schedule: Seeds, Beverages and Comestibles
metadata.description: This page lists the Japanese import duty rates on seeds, vegetables, fruits, tea, coffee, cocoa and spices, given per 100 kin or ad valorem.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Schedule: Flours, Biscuits, Sauce, Vinegar and Meat]
metadata.description: A schedule of import duty rates on foodstuffs, listing each article with its unit of assessment and rate, showing the tariff applied to these goods.

metadata.title: [Customs Tariff Rates on Foods, Sugar, Alcoholic Liquors and Alcohol]
metadata.description: This page lists customs duty rates by article for foods, sugar, confectionery, alcoholic liquors and alcohol, under the tariff's Group system, showing unit and yen rate for each item.

metadata.title: [Import Duties on Alcoholic Liquors, Skins, Hides, Hair and Leather]
metadata.description: This Japanese customs tariff list gives the import duty rates in yen, or ad valorem percentages, for alcoholic liquors, furs, hides, leather and hair under their tariff numbers.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Schedule: Furs, Feathers, Bones, Horns, Tortoise-shells and Sponges]
metadata.description: This import tariff schedule lists the duty rates on animal skins, hairs, horns, shells and similar articles, showing the unit of each rate and the rate itself.

metadata.title: Group VII. Drugs, Chemicals, Medicines and Medicinal Preparations
metadata.description: This section of the import tariff schedule gives the duty rates for drugs, chemicals and medicinal products under Group VII.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Rates on Drugs, Chemicals and Related Goods]
metadata.description: A list of import duty items on drugs, chemicals and related goods, giving each article's unit of charge and its rate, shown here as a tariff reference.

metadata.title: [Foreign Trade Items 127–159: Drugs, Chemicals and Essential Oils]
metadata.description: A schedule of duty-rated foreign trade items, numbered 127 to 159, listing drugs, chemicals and medicines with their units and values, leading into the Group VIII oils section.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Schedule: Oils, Fats and Waxes]
metadata.description: This page of the import tariff schedule lists duty rates for vegetable, animal and mineral oils, fats and waxes, with units and rates per item.

metadata.title: [Group IX: Dyes, Pigments and Paints — Tariff Rates]
metadata.description: This page lists the import duty rates for Group IX dyes, pigments and paints, giving each article's unit of quantity and its rate under the tariff.

metadata.title: [Customs Tariff Schedule: Paints, Inks and Yarns]
metadata.description: The page lists customs duty rates for paints, inks, dyes and textile yarns and threads, by item number, unit and rate, as part of the tariff schedule.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Schedule, Items 227–256]
metadata.description: A customs tariff schedule listing import duty items 227–256 with their units and rates, covering silk, cordage and textile fabrics, which the Year Book reproduces as part of the foreign trade section.

metadata.title: [Customs Tariff Schedule of Woollen and Silk Textiles]
metadata.description: A customs tariff schedule listing duties on woollen and silk textile items by item number, unit of measure and rate, continuing from the previous page.

metadata.title: [Import Duties on Textiles and Related Goods]
metadata.description: This page lists customs duty rates on textile goods such as blankets, carpets, curtains, nets and tapes, giving the unit of measure and the rate for each item.

metadata.title: [Customs Tariff Schedule, Items 329-343]
metadata.description: A customs tariff schedule listing duty rates for paper goods and printed matter, with units of charge, as part of the import tariff classification.

metadata.title: [Customs Tariff Schedule, Items 344-346 (Ores and Minerals)]
metadata.description: A customs tariff schedule giving duty rates for metallic ores, precious stones and stones under Group XIV, Ores and Minerals.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Rates on Raw Mineral Materials and Metals]
metadata.description: A customs tariff schedule listing import duty bases and rates for raw mineral materials (Nos. 347–363) and then for metals such as platinum and iron and steel (Group XV).

metadata.title: [Import Duties on Iron, Steel and Other Metals]
metadata.description: A list of import duty rates on iron, steel and non-ferrous metals (spiegeleisen, copper, lead, tin, zinc, nickel), giving the unit and rate for each item in the tariff schedule.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Schedule for Iron, Metal and Hardware Articles]
metadata.description: A list of customs duties on iron and metal goods such as nails, screws, locks, tools and chains, giving the unit and rate for each article under the tariff numbers.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Schedule, Items 398–411]
metadata.description: A customs tariff schedule listing import duty rates, by unit or ad valorem percentage, for metal manufactures and earthenware, porcelain and glass goods.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Schedule: Glass Manufactures, Vehicles, Vessels, Instruments and Machinery]
metadata.description: A customs tariff schedule listing import duty rates by item number for glass manufactures and for vehicles, vessels, instruments and machinery, showing units and rates of duty.

metadata.title: [Import Duties on Boilers and Machinery]
metadata.description: Customs tariff rates for boilers and machinery, listed by tariff item number, showing the unit of valuation and the rate of duty for each article.

metadata.title: Group XIX. Miscellaneous Articles
metadata.description: Customs tariff rates for miscellaneous articles in Group XIX, including copra, tan bark, rattans, bamboos, cork, woods, charcoal and pulp, with units and duty rates.

metadata.title: [Tariff Rates on Articles Nos. 471–485]
metadata.description: This page lists the import duty rates on articles numbered 471 to 485 in the tariff schedule, giving the unit of quantity and the rate for each item.

metadata.title: [Customs Tariff Rates on Caoutchouc, Celluloid and Miscellaneous Manufactures]
metadata.description: The page lists customs duty rates for rubber, celluloid, abrasive, cement, leather, wood and cane manufactures, with units and ad valorem or specific rates.

metadata.title: [Customs Tariff Schedule, Items 508 to 525: Lamps, Walking Sticks, Umbrellas, Photographic Films, Toys and Tobacco]
metadata.description: This page lists customs tariff items 508 to 525, giving the unit of assessment and the rate of duty for lamps, umbrellas, photographic films, toys, soaps and tobacco.

metadata.title: [Schedule of Import Duties, Items 526 to 538]
metadata.description: A customs tariff schedule listing import duty rates on items 526 to 538, giving each article's basis of duty (by weight or ad valorem) and its rate.

metadata.title: Under Control of Brigade Headquarters at Yokosuka
metadata.description: Lists the units placed under the Brigade Headquarters at Yokosuka, giving each station, its troop strength, and whether it has horses.

metadata.title: Under Control of Brigade Headquarters at Shimonoseki
metadata.description: Lists the units placed under the Brigade Headquarters at Shimonoseki, giving each station, its troop strength, and whether it has horses.

metadata.title: Field Artillery Brigades and Their Stations
metadata.description: Shows how the three newly reorganized field artillery brigades and their constituent regiments are to be distributed across their stations.

metadata.title: Military Expenditure for 1906–7
metadata.description: The page closes the army section with the national military expenditure for 1906–7, split into ordinary and extraordinary items, showing the grand total.

metadata.title: List of Full Generals on Active Service
metadata.description: The list names the full generals on active service with the date each received his appointment, following the notes on the Supreme Military Council and Supreme Council of War.

metadata.title: Distribution of the Standing Army
metadata.description: The table gives the distribution of the standing army by division, brigade, regiment and garrison locality, shown on this page as the continuation of the army organisation description.

metadata.title: [Garrison Distribution by Town, Army and Navy]
metadata.description: A rotated table of army and navy garrison entries by town, with divisional numbers (11th to 18th Divisions) listed beneath each town, showing where units were stationed.

metadata.title: General Staff Office
metadata.description: Lists the principal officers of the General Staff Office, giving each post with the rank and name of its holder.

metadata.title: Military Inspection Board
metadata.description: Shows the chief and section heads of the Military Inspection Board, with each officer's rank and name.

metadata.title: List of Divisional Commanders
metadata.description: Lists the commander of each division of the army, including the Imperial Body Guards, with rank and name.

metadata.title: List of Brigade Commanders
metadata.description: Lists the commander of each infantry brigade, with the division to which each brigade belongs, rank and name.

metadata.title: Commanders of Forts
metadata.description: Names the commanders of the coastal and harbour fortifications such as Tokyo Bay, Hiroshima Bay, Maizuru, Shimonoseki, Saseho and Tsushima.

metadata.title: Appropriations for the Navy (1907-8)
metadata.description: Shows the government's naval appropriations for 1907-8, split into ordinary and extraordinary expenses, to illustrate the scale of funding for the Imperial Navy.

metadata.title: [Outlays of the Three Naval Programmes]
metadata.description: Shows how the outlay for the 3rd naval programme, the Emergency Outlay and the Fleet maintenance fund is divided among ship construction, weapons, buildings and repairs.

metadata.title: [Naval Cadet Academy Admissions and Applicants, 1894–1906]
metadata.description: The text describes the Naval Cadet Academy and gives yearly admission, examination and applicant numbers since the Japan-China War.

metadata.title: [Naval Engineering School Admissions and Applicants, 1894–1897]
metadata.description: The Naval Engineering School, a collateral institution at Yokosuka, is shown with yearly admission, examination and applicant figures for 1894 to 1897.

metadata.title: Volunteer and Conscription Service
metadata.description: Gives yearly numbers of conscripts, volunteers and their total in the Navy, explaining that conscription supplements the volunteer service.

metadata.title: Officers and Bluejackets on Active Service
metadata.caption: (Compiled at the end of the year.)
metadata.description: Lists the strength of officers, warrant officers, bluejackets and cadets in the Navy at the end of each year, with totals, to show the growth of the service.

metadata.title: Admirals on Active Service
metadata.description: Lists the admirals on active service in the navy with the month and year each was appointed to that rank.

metadata.title: Naval Department
metadata.description: Names the holders of the principal posts in the Naval Department of the Ministry at the time.

metadata.title: Naval Staff Board and Admiralties
metadata.description: Gives the chiefs of the Naval Staff Board and the commanders and key staff of the Yokosuka, Kure and Sasebo Admiralties.

metadata.title: Battleships.
metadata.caption: Those in Commission or Launched.
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese battleships in commission or launched, giving each ship's displacement, launch year and nominal speed.

metadata.title: Armored Cruisers
metadata.description: Lists the armored cruisers of the Japanese navy with their tonnage, year of construction and speed, with a total for the class.

metadata.title: Protected Cruisers
metadata.description: Lists the protected cruisers of the Japanese navy with tonnage, year of construction and speed, with a class total.

metadata.title: Armored Coast Defence Ships
metadata.description: Lists the four armored coast defence ships of the Japanese navy with tonnage, year built and speed, and their total.

metadata.title: Torpedo-boat Destroyers
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese torpedo-boat destroyers in the fleet with their displacement and launch year, totalling 47 vessels, as part of the fleet survey.

metadata.title: Despatch-boats
metadata.description: Lists the five despatch-boats in service besides the destroyers, giving displacement and launch year for each.

metadata.title: Warships Built in Japan
metadata.description: The text notes that the first home-built warship was the gunboat Seiki and lists the twenty-eight warships built in Japan up to the end of 1906.

metadata.title: [Naval Vessels, Types, Names, Tonnage, Year and Port]
metadata.description: This continuation lists Japanese naval vessels by type, name, tonnage, year of completion and home port, completing the fleet list begun on the previous page.

metadata.title: Patents
metadata.description: Statistics of patent applications received and patents granted under the trade-mark, design and patent law, from its enforcement in 1885 onward.

metadata.title: Designs
metadata.description: Statistics of design applications and registrations filed at the Japanese Office since the enforcement of the law, shown alongside the patent figures.

metadata.title: Trade-Marks
metadata.description: Continuation of the annual trade-mark series, giving applications and registrations for 1896 to 1906.

metadata.title: Applications by Foreigners
metadata.description: Breakdown of patent, design and trade-mark applications and registrations filed by foreigners in Japan, by country, for the period November 1896 to December 1904.

metadata.title: [Patents, Designs and Trade-Marks by Country]
metadata.description: Shows the number of patents, designs, trade-marks and practical utility designs applied for or granted by country of origin, as the Patent Office recorded them for the year.

metadata.title: [Applications and Registrations by Foreigners Residing in Japan]
metadata.description: Gives the applications made and registrations granted to foreigners residing in Japan, broken down by patents, designs and trade-marks and by their country.

metadata.title: Revenue of the Patent Office
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Lists the yearly revenue collected by the Patent Office from 1886 to 1904, with the accounting period noted for the early years.

metadata.title: [Applications and Registrations of Designs of Practical Utility]
metadata.description: Shows the number of design applications and registrations under the July 1905 regulations, giving the figures for the first half-year of 1905 and for 1906.

metadata.title: [Postage Rates by Weight, Japan Proper and Adjacent Areas]
metadata.description: Gives the postage charged for parcels or packets by weight for mail within Japan proper and to Formosa, Korea or China, with a note that rates inside Korea or China match Japanese interior rates.

metadata.title: Money Orders Fees
metadata.description: Lists the fees charged for ordinary money orders according to the sum remitted, up to a maximum of 50 yen.

metadata.title: Telegraphic Money Orders Fees
metadata.description: Lists the fees charged for telegraphic money orders according to the sum remitted, up to a maximum of 50 yen.

metadata.title: Foreign Parcels
metadata.description: Lists the cheapest parcel post routes from Japan to each foreign country and region, with the maximum rate in yen for each route.

metadata.title: [Postal Charges to Europe, Canada and Hongkong by Route]
metadata.description: Lists the charges for sending items by direct or indirect exchange to Belgium, Denmark, Spain, Holland, Italy, Canada and Hongkong, by route and carrier.

metadata.title: The United States of America
metadata.description: Gives the direct exchange charge for sending items to the United States, including Hawaii and Porto Rico, by weight.

metadata.title: Maximum Amounts
metadata.description: Summarises the maximum amount of a foreign money order permitted for each country or group of orders, with the payment currency for Hongkong.

metadata.title: Number of Post and Telegraph Offices
metadata.description: Gives the yearly count of post and telegraph offices in Japan with the average area and population each office served, 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Number of Post and Telegraph Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Shows how many post and telegraph offices Japan maintained abroad at the end of each fiscal year from 1900 to 1905, the total being given in the last column.

metadata.title: Ordinary Mail Matter Transmitted
metadata.description: Records the yearly volume of ordinary mail, total and letters only, with the average number of items per head of population, from 1894 and 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Post-cards and Newspapers, Magazines, Etc.]
metadata.description: Post-card and newspaper/magazine figures for each fiscal year with per-capita averages, showing the growth of postal circulation from 1894 to 1905.

metadata.title: Parcel Post
metadata.description: Number of parcels handled by the post and the average per 100 population for each fiscal year, 1894 to 1905.

metadata.title: Mail Matter and Parcels Dealt With at Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Mail matter and parcels transmitted and delivered by post offices stationed abroad, by fiscal year, from 1894 to 1904.

metadata.title: Foreign Mail Matters and Parcels Dealt With
metadata.caption: (Exclusive of those dealt with by Offices stationed abroad.) (in thousand.)
metadata.description: Volume of foreign mail matters and parcels transmitted and arrived through the post, excluding those handled by offices abroad, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Mail Matters Exchanged with Principal Countries in 1905 Fiscal Year
metadata.caption: (in thousand.)
metadata.description: Shows the volume of mail sent and received by Japan with Asian, European, and American countries in fiscal 1905, illustrating the postal exchange with each region.

metadata.title: Postal Saving Deposits at Home
metadata.description: Gives the number of home postal savings depositors and amounts deposited from 1894 onward, showing the marked rise after the war as the text notes.

metadata.title: Saving Deposits at Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Records the number of depositors, amounts, and average deposit per depositor for postal savings handled by offices stationed abroad from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: International Rates
metadata.caption: The rates for telegrams to places abroad are as follows:—
metadata.description: Gives the telegraph charges to foreign and Chinese stations, all sent via Shanghai, in yen, with the Chinese stations grouped under a side label.

metadata.title: Korean Stations Telegraph Rates
metadata.description: Gives the telegraph rate in yen from the Korean stations, routed via Fusan, showing the charge for each station's telegrams.

metadata.title: Telegraph Rates to Foreign Countries by Route
metadata.description: Lists telegraph charges in yen from Japan to Europe, America, Asia and Oceania by the alternative routes via Vladivostock, Shanghai, Manila and Ogasawara Islands.

metadata.title: Extension of Telegraph
metadata.description: Shows the growth of the telegraph network from 1894 to 1905, recording aerial wire length in ri and submarine cable length in knots at each fiscal year end.

metadata.title: Number of Domestic Telegrams Transacted
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of domestic telegrams and messages per hundred population, alongside foreign telegrams transmitted and arrived, from 1894 to 1905.

metadata.title: Number of Telegrams Transacted by Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Shows the telegrams sent and received by Japanese telegraph offices stationed overseas in each fiscal year from 1894 to 1904.

metadata.title: Foreign Telegrams in 1905
metadata.description: Breaks down the foreign telegrams transmitted and received in 1905 by region, with Asia and its listed countries shown.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Subscribers
metadata.caption: At end of fiscal year.
metadata.description: Gives the number of telephone subscribers at the end of each fiscal year, showing growth of the telephone service from 1894 to 1905.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Apparatus
metadata.caption: At end of fiscal year.
metadata.description: Lists the number of telephone exchange, ordinary subscriber and automatic apparatus installed at the end of each fiscal year.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Receipts
metadata.caption: (in thousand yen.)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly receipts of the post and telegraph services by category, in thousand yen, from 1894 to 1905.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Service Expense
metadata.caption: (in thousand yen.)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly expense of the post and telegraph service, broken down by postal and telegraph branch, from 1894 to 1905, giving the state of service costs over time.

metadata.description: The table gives the number and gross tonnage of registered steamers and sailing vessels by size class at the end of March, 1901 to 1906, illustrating growth of Japan's mercantile marine.

metadata.description: Breaks down the registered steamers over 1,000 tons of March 1906 by hull material (wood, composite, iron, steel and combinations), with tonnage bands and gross tonnage.

metadata.title: Steamers Classified by Speed (March '06)
metadata.description: Classifies the registered steamers over 1,000 tons of March 1906 by their speed in knots, with tonnage bands and gross tonnage for each speed range.

metadata.title: Steamers Classified According to Nature of Service
metadata.description: Summarises the steamers in the mercantile marine by the nature of their service, giving number of steamers and gross tonnage for each class.

metadata.title: Built at Home

metadata.title: [Subsidised Steamship Services and Annual Grants]
metadata.description: Lists the government-subsidised steamship services with their contract terms and annual grants in yen, giving the total subsidy sum.

metadata.title: Ships Classified According to Service
metadata.description: Shows the number, total tonnage and average tonnage of Japanese steamers on regular and irregular services, introducing the carrying-trade survey.

metadata.title: Regular Service Ships Classified by Routes
metadata.description: Breaks down the regular-service steamers by route (foreign, China/Korea/Vladivostok, coasting trade), with counts, tonnage and average tonnage.

metadata.title: Foreign Lines
metadata.description: Lists the foreign shipping lines operated from Japan, with their routes, number of sailings, tonnage and the company running each, totalling 32 sailings.

metadata.title: Subsidized Ship-Owners in Regard to Foreign Services
metadata.description: Shows the shipping companies receiving government subsidies for foreign services, the lines each operates and the frequency of its sailings.

metadata.title: Seamen of Higher Grade
metadata.description: Gives the number of licensed captains and mates at successive dates from 1903 to 1906, with foreigners (f.) shown separately, to indicate the rate of increase since the Russo-Japanese War.

metadata.title: Shipwrecks
metadata.description: Gives the number of steamers, sailing-ships and junks destroyed, damaged or missing in shipwrecks each year from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: No. of Lives Lost and Injured
metadata.description: Lists deaths, injuries, missing persons and lives rescued in shipwrecks for each year from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: No. of Pilots
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese, foreign and total licensed pilots from 1900 to 1905, illustrating the effect of the Pilotage Law of 1899 that restricted pilotage to Japanese subjects.

metadata.title: [Financial Summary of the Company, 1901–1907]
metadata.description: The table gives the shipping company's vessels, capital, receipts, expenditures and profits year by year from 1901 to 1907, illustrating its growth alongside its expanded services.

metadata.title: [Shipping Company Statistics, 1900-1906]
metadata.description: Statistics of a shipping company with Osaka head office, showing vessels, capital, receipts, expenditures and profits for 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: [Toyo Kisen Kaisha Statistics, 1900-1905]
metadata.description: Annual figures for the Toyo Kisen Kaisha's fleet, capital, receipts, expenditures and profits from 1900 to 1905, given under its description.

metadata.title: [Mitsui Bussan Kaisha Shipping Department Statistics, 1903-1905]
metadata.description: Operating figures of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha shipping department, which runs mostly colliers on coasting trade and services to China and other Asiatic ports, for 1903 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Share of Components in the Japan-China Steamship Company]
metadata.description: Shows how the four constituent companies shared in the common enterprise of the Japan-China Steamship Company, whose capital was set at Yen 8,000,000 for the present.

metadata.title: Mileage Open to Traffic
metadata.description: Shows the growth of state, private and total railway mileage open to traffic at the end of each fiscal year from 1900 to 1905, opening the railways chapter.

metadata.title: Table I
metadata.description: Gives, for each main state railway line in 1905–6, its open mileage, construction expense, rolling stock numbers and average construction cost per mile.

metadata.title: [Open Railway Lines: Mileage, Construction Cost and Rolling Stock]
metadata.description: Gives mileage, construction cost, locomotive, car and wagon numbers, and average construction cost per mile for each state railway line, with totals, as of the period covered.

metadata.title: Table II
metadata.description: Shows net profit and average daily receipts, expenses and profit per mile for each state railway line, with the total, to compare the financial performance of the lines.

metadata.title: [Average Account of Railways per Day and per Mile, 1902–1904]
metadata.description: Shows the average daily and per-mile receipts, expenses and profit of the railways for 1902 to 1904.

metadata.title: Private Railways in 1905–6
metadata.description: Lists each private railway company with its open mileage, construction cost, locomotives, carriages, wagons and average construction cost per mile in 1905–6.

metadata.title: Table II
metadata.description: Table II compares total profit, daily receipts, expenses and profit per mile, and profit per cost of construction for each named railway line.

metadata.title: Table III
metadata.description: Lists the private railway companies of the period with their opening year, paid-up capital, president or general manager, and head office location.

metadata.title: Traffic of State and Private Railways. Volume of Passenger and Freight Service
metadata.description: Begins a table of railway traffic volume, giving passenger numbers and freight tonnage by year, starting with the 1874 figures shown here.

metadata.title: Net Profit of State and Private Railways
metadata.description: Gives the net profit of state and private railways in yen, and profit per Y. 100 of construction cost, for selected years from 1895 to 1904.

metadata.title: Railway Casualties
metadata.description: Lists railway casualties, deaths and wounded among railway staff, passengers and others, and in total, for 1899 to 1904.

metadata.title: Lines to be Nationalized
metadata.description: The table lists the private railway lines the government was to nationalize, giving each line's capital, share payments, construction cost, purchase price, loans, reserves and bonds offered.

metadata.title: [Railways Purchased by the Government and Dates of Purchase]
metadata.description: Lists the railway lines the Government purchased under the nationalization scheme, grouped by the date each purchase took effect in 1906–1907.

metadata.title: Redemption of the Railway Nationalization Loan
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows, year by year, the construction cost, profits, interest, and the distribution of surplus used for redeeming the loan and for investment, with the outstanding loan amount.

metadata.title: Passenger and Goods Tariff on the Government and Other Railways
metadata.caption: Passenger Tariff Rates per Mile
metadata.description: The page closes its discussion of railway materials and makers with a comparison of passenger fares per mile on Government and other railways, by class and distance band.

metadata.title: [Passenger Fares on Railways]
metadata.description: The first table gives passenger fare rates per railway company by class, expressed in sen and as multiples of the third-class fare for distance bands.

metadata.title: Goods Tariff Rate per Mile per Ton
metadata.description: This table lists the goods tariff rates per mile per ton for each railway group, by goods kind, treasure and terminal rate, in rin.

metadata.title: Luggage and Parcels
metadata.description: This table gives the free luggage limits by class and the delivery charge for railway luggage on the main lines.

metadata.title: Parcel Rate
metadata.description: This table gives the parcel rates by weight and distance band, with an additional charge for each further 5 kin.

metadata.title: Special Car-Load Rates on Government Lines
metadata.caption: (per Ton per Mile.)
metadata.description: The page gives the special reduced car-load freight rates charged on government railway lines for various goods, by distance band.

metadata.title: [Special Car-Load Rates on Government Lines: Raw Silk Cocoons]
metadata.description: This follows the special rate table and gives the ordinary and car-load freight rates for raw and dried silk cocoons.

metadata.title: [Electric Railway Companies in Tokyo]
metadata.description: The text introduces Japan's electric railway companies, noting that Tokyo has one such company, whose service, mileage and capital are listed here.

metadata.title: [Electric Railway Mileage at End of 1905]
metadata.description: The remaining electric railway companies, apart from those amalgamated or combined, are listed with their mileage as returned at the end of 1905.

metadata.title: Press Statistics
metadata.description: Gives the number of Japanese dailies and periodicals existing at the end of each of the five latest years available, illustrating the rapid growth of the press after 1900.

metadata.title: Leading Periodicals Published in Tokyo
metadata.description: A list of leading Tokyo periodicals giving each title's subject feature, frequency of publication, price per issue and publisher, introduced under the Press section.

metadata.title: Total Casualties During the Late War — Army
metadata.description: Gives the army's returned deaths from all causes during the late war, by division, separating killed or died of wounds, disease and accidents, and total deaths.

metadata.title: Total Casualties During the Late War — Navy
metadata.description: Shows the navy's casualties in the late war by rank, giving those killed or died of wounds, wounded, and the combined total.

metadata.title: Cost of Living
metadata.description: Shows the rising cost of household living in Tokyo for a family on about Y. 40 a month, comparing 1887, 1897 and 1906 prices.

metadata.title: Ladies' Wardrobe
metadata.description: Compares the yearly cost of fashionable wardrobe items for upper-class and middle-class ladies, to show how costly native dress is.

metadata.title: Servants' Wages per Month
metadata.description: Gives the latest official inquiries into monthly wages paid to male and female servants in various Japanese towns.

metadata.title: Revenues
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: The table gives Formosa's revenues by fiscal year from 1898 to 1907, showing how the subsidy from central government fell away while ordinary revenue rose, supporting the claim of colonial policy's success.

metadata.title: Chief Items of Ordinary Revenues
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: This table breaks down the principal components of Formosa's ordinary revenue for 1898 to 1901 into inland taxes, customs, and receipts from public undertakings and State property.

metadata.title: [Untitled Statistical Table, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top of this page continues a statistical table of yearly figures for 1902 to 1907, whose column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Expenditures
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: This table gives the Government's expenditures in Formosa by fiscal year from 1898 to 1907, broken down by civil administration, special undertakings and other items.

metadata.title: List of Governor-Generals
metadata.description: This list gives the successive Governor-Generals of the colony with the dates of their appointment and relief from office.

metadata.title: Population
metadata.description: This table gives the population of the colony at the end of each year from 1900 to 1905, by Japanese and native inhabitants, by sex, and by number of families.

metadata.title: Area of Tillage Land
metadata.description: Shows the area of tillage land in Formosa at the end of each year from 1902 to 1905, split between rice-paddy and upland field.

metadata.title: Agricultural Products
metadata.caption: (in 1,000.)
metadata.description: Lists the yearly output of Formosan agricultural products, 1901 to 1905, in koku or kin as indicated for each crop.

metadata.title: Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the quantity and value of raw and cured marine products in Formosa for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Mineral Products
metadata.description: Records Formosa's yearly output of gold, gold dust, coal and sulphur from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Textile Fabrics
metadata.description: Shows the number of weaving works, looms, output value and persons employed in the textile fabrics industry for 1904 and 1905.

metadata.title: Camphor and Camphor Oil
metadata.description: Gives annual quantities of camphor and camphor oil produced, in kin, for 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Amount of Opium Manufactured
metadata.description: Records the quantity of opium manufactured in momme for each fiscal year from 1900 to 1905.

metadata.title: Opium-smokers
metadata.description: Shows the number of male, female and total opium smokers in each period from 1900–1 to 1905–6, with the rate per 100 population.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Presents the value of Japan's exports, imports and total foreign trade in yen for each year from 1900 to 1903.

metadata.title: [Trade Totals, 1904–1906 (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a yearly trade-totals table for 1904–1906, whose column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Trade with Japan Proper
metadata.description: Shows Formosa's yearly exports and imports with Japan Proper from 1900 to 1906, with the balance of trade in the last column.

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Exported
metadata.caption: Value (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the value in thousands of yen of Formosan commodities exported each year from 1900 to 1906, such as tea, rice, sugar and camphor.

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Imported
metadata.caption: Value (Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Lists the value in thousands of yen of the main goods Formosa imported each year from 1900 to 1906, such as opium, petroleum, flour and hogs.

metadata.title: No. of Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of schools, teachers and students and pupils in Japan at the end of each year from 1901 to 1904.

metadata.title: Schools Classified
metadata.caption: (at end of 1904)
metadata.description: Breaks down the schools at the end of 1904 by type (State, Communal and Private), showing schools, teachers and pupils for each.

metadata.title: Railways
metadata.description: Shows Japanese railway mileage open, rolling stock and receipts for 1900 to October 1905, illustrating the rapid growth of the railway system.

metadata.title: [Estimated Expenditures and Revenues of Karafuto, 1907-8 Fiscal Year]
metadata.description: Sets out the estimated expenditures and revenues of the Karafuto administration for the 1907-8 fiscal year, in yen.

metadata.title: [Karafuto Population at End of 1905 and 1906]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of the Karafuto settler population between the end of 1905 and the end of 1906, broken down by sex.

metadata.title: [Settlers by Urban and Rural Districts at End of 1906]
metadata.description: Gives the distribution of settlers at the end of 1906 between the urban districts and the rural districts, as returned in the census.

metadata.title: Aliens
metadata.description: Lists the alien residents of Southern Saghalien by nationality, from the latest census, following the note on Russians and the aboriginal population.

metadata.title: Aborigines
metadata.description: Lists the five aboriginal tribes of Southern Saghalien by family, sex and total, from the latest census.

metadata.title: [Catch of Marine Products in Karafuto, 1906]
metadata.description: The text reports the 1906 fishery catch in Karafuto by species, giving the amount and value of each, as the figures for the year.

metadata.title: Temperature
metadata.caption: (C.)
metadata.description: Monthly and average temperatures recorded at Fusan, Ninsen, Gensan, Seoul, Chinnampo and Pingyang, based on consular meteorological records.

metadata.title: Rainfalls
metadata.caption: (milm.)
metadata.description: Monthly and total rainfall in millimetres at Fusan, Ninsen, Seoul and Gensan, showing the wet summer months.

metadata.title: No. of Days of Rainfalls and Snowfalls
metadata.description: Number of days with rainfall or snowfall per month at five Korean stations, continuing the meteorological records.

metadata.title: [Monthly Figures, Continued From Previous Page]
metadata.description: The continuation of a monthly figures table, March to December with totals, whose column headings appear on the previous page and are not printed here.

metadata.title: Expenditure of State
metadata.description: Shows Korea's state expenditure for 1907 compared with 1906, split into ordinary and extraordinary items by department, with the increase or decrease for each.

metadata.title: [Revenue Statement, 1907 and 1906]
metadata.description: The page gives the Korean government's revenue for 1907 compared with 1906, by ordinary and extraordinary items, showing the increase or decrease in each head.

metadata.title: Raising Funds for the Work
metadata.caption: Yen.
metadata.description: The Korean Government raised funds for the reform work through the Japan Industrial Bank, and this table itemises how the Yen 4,500,000 raised was allotted to each outlay.

metadata.title: The Japanese Population of Korea
metadata.caption: (Jan. 31st, 1907.)
metadata.description: The table gives the Japanese resident population of Korea by residency as of 31 January 1907, split by sex, showing the size of the Japanese community there.

metadata.title: Volume of Trade
metadata.description: The table lists the yearly value of Korean imports and exports in yen from 1902 to 1906, showing how the trade volume grew over these years.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows Korea's export trade by principal commodity from 1902 to 1906, with yearly totals, giving the reader a picture of the country's outward trade.

metadata.title: Imports
metadata.description: Lists Korea's import trade by commodity group from 1902 to 1905, with subtotals and the grand total including goods re-exported.

metadata.title: Export and Import of Specie and Bullions
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of gold and other specie exported and imported, with the resulting balance, for 1902 to 1905.

metadata.title: Trade with Different Countries
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Korea's trade with Japan and China, split into imports from and exports to each country, for each year 1902 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Table Continued From Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top rows continue a figures table from the previous page, giving country-wise amounts with totals; the column headings are not on this page.

metadata.title: Customs Receipts
metadata.description: Shows Korean customs receipts from import duties, export duties, tonnage dues and their total for 1902 to 1905, given as background to the banking discussion below.

metadata.title: Harvest
metadata.caption: (per tan, this unit holding good for other statistics)
metadata.description: The table gives the cotton harvest, in seed and ginned cotton, from experimental plots at Mokpho and Yongsampho, comparing upland and Korean varieties to show the native variety's relative performance.

metadata.title: Rate of Ginned Cotton and Staples
metadata.description: The table compares upland and Korean cotton by ginning rate and staple length and size, supporting the conclusion that the upland variety is superior in these respects.

metadata.title: [Ginned Cotton Yield and Value per Tan, Upland and Korean Varieties]
metadata.description: Shows, for a tan of cotton, the ginned yield and value of Upland versus Korean varieties under three manuring methods, supporting the case for planting Upland cotton in Korea.

metadata.title: [Gold Output of Korea, 1902-1905]
metadata.caption: (Unit: yen)
metadata.description: Lists Korea's annual gold output in yen for 1902 to 1905, illustrating the scale of gold mining that keeps the country's trade near balance.

metadata.title: Cost of Engineering Work etc.
metadata.description: Shows how the South Manchurian Railway's initial capital of 100,000,000 yen was allocated among engineering works, reserves and related items.

metadata.title: Valuation of the Government Property
metadata.description: Gives the valuation of the government property transferred to the South Manchurian system, itemised by railway, coal-mines and stations, totalling 100,000,000 yen.

metadata.title: Estimate of Investment and Profit of South Manchurian System
metadata.description: Estimates the aggregate investment, net profit and rate of profit of the South Manchurian System for each of the first ten years.

metadata.title: Construction and Working Expenses of the Tairen-Chungchun Section
metadata.description: Breaks down the first year's construction and working expenses on the Tairen-Chungchun section by improvement, doubling, rolling stock and total.

metadata.title: Manchuria
metadata.description: Shows the yearly amounts for the successive periods of the Manchurian railway development plan, with totals, in three unlabelled columns.

metadata.title: Gross Earnings and Operating Expenses of the Above Lines
metadata.description: Gives gross earnings, operating expenses and net profit by year for the lines listed above, showing the railway's financial results over ten years.

metadata.title: Exploiting Fushun and Yentai Mines
metadata.caption: Capital to be invested
metadata.description: Lists the capital to be invested in successive years for developing the Fushun and Yentai mines, with accumulated totals.

metadata.title: Mines
metadata.description: Shows gross earnings, disbursements and net profit of the mines in each successive year.

metadata.title: [Antung-Mukden Line Estimated Gross Earnings, Operating Expenses and Net Profit]
metadata.description: The estimated yearly gross earnings, operating expenses and net profit of the Antung-Mukden Line are set out for the first ten years after the line is built.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Chienkin-sai Coal]
metadata.description: The text describes the Chienkin-sai coal deposits and their quality, and this analysis of the three grades of that coal shows its water, ash, coke, volatile matter, sulphur and caloric content.

metadata.title: Weights, Measures and Moneys
metadata.description: This list gives the Japanese units of weight, measure and money with their British or American equivalents, so readers can convert figures used elsewhere in the Year Book.

metadata.title: [Area of Japan by Districts]
metadata.description: Gives the area in square ri of Japan's main islands and island groups, totalling the national territory cited in the preceding sentence.

metadata.title: [Principal Mountain Peaks Above 8,000 Feet]
metadata.description: Lists the principal mountain peaks above 8,000 feet in Japan, with heights, illustrating the mountainous character of the land described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Rivers Above 40 Ri in Length]
metadata.description: Lists the rivers of Japan longer than 40 ri, with their lengths, to illustrate that Japanese rivers are short and rapid because of the mountain chains and coastline.

metadata.title: Coast-Line of the Principal Islands
metadata.description: The text notes the coast is well indented, with about one ri of coast-line for every 3.64 surface ri, and this table gives the coast-line length of each principal island and its area per ri of coast.

metadata.title: [Ports Opened to Foreign Trade]
metadata.description: A list of treaty ports opened to foreign trade, giving the year each was opened and its island or territory, placed before the Atmospheric Pressure and Wind section.

metadata.title: Monthly Average Temperature (C°) in Japan
metadata.description: Monthly average temperatures at eight Japanese stations, with their observation periods, shown to illustrate the climate described in the surrounding geography text.

metadata.title: Average Monthly Rainfalls and Snowfalls in Japan from Beginning of Observation to 1906
metadata.description: The table gives average monthly and yearly rainfall in millimetres for eight observation stations, plus the number of rain and snow days per year, to illustrate the climate described above.

metadata.title: [Losses from the Flood of 1907]
metadata.description: The table gives the itemised human, property and agricultural losses of the 1907 flood in Yamanashi prefecture, summing the yen damage to show the scale of the disaster.

metadata.title: [Most Disastrous Seismic Calamities in the Pre-Tokugawa Period]
metadata.description: The Seismic Disaster Investigation Commission lists the most destructive earthquakes recorded before the Tokugawa period, from 684 A.D. onward.

metadata.title: [Principal Calamities during the Tokugawa Period]
metadata.description: The principal calamities that occurred during the Tokugawa period are listed with dates, places, houses destroyed and deaths.

metadata.title: [Seven Earthquakes in Recent Time]
metadata.description: Recent major earthquakes from 1891 to 1906 are listed with the houses destroyed and the numbers killed and injured.

metadata.title: [Principal Mineral Springs]
metadata.description: The section on mineral springs notes that Japan has many hot or cold springs, and lists the more popular ones with their location, quality and temperature.

metadata.title: Movement of Population
metadata.description: Shows the end-of-year population of Japan from 1900 to 1907 by sex, with annual increase and increase per 100 head, opening the chapter on population.

metadata.title: [Population Density and Population per Family by Region]
metadata.description: Gives the population density per square ri and population per family for each region of Japan proper, as at the end of 1904.

metadata.title: Distribution of Population in Rural and Urban Districts
metadata.description: Shows how the population was distributed among villages, towns and cities by population grade, with counts of towns and cities for 1895 to 1898.

metadata.title: [Number of Villages, Towns and Cities by Population Grade]
metadata.description: Shows the number of villages, towns and cities in each population grade, with towns and cities counted for 1895 to 1898, giving the urban structure of Japan.

metadata.title: Rate per 100 Population
metadata.description: Gives the rate per 100 population by city size grade for 1894 to 1903, alongside the number of cities in each grade in 1894. The 1897–1894 figures for the first four grades are printed as a single merged value.

metadata.title: Population by Ages and Sexes
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1903 population by five-year age group and sex, and gives the per-100 share of each age group for several census years.

metadata.title: Marriages and Divorces
metadata.description: Lists the number of marriages and divorces in Japan from 1900 to 1904, with each expressed per 1,000 of population.

metadata.title: Married or Unmarried, by Age
metadata.caption: (At end of 1903)
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese population at the end of 1903 broken down by age group, split into married and unmarried persons for each sex, with totals and the number of males per 100 females.

metadata.title: Birth-Rates
metadata.caption: (Exclu. Still-Births)
metadata.description: Gives yearly birth figures for 1900–1904, with males and females born, birth rate per 100 people, sex ratio at birth and still-births.

metadata.title: Births Classified
metadata.description: Breaks down births for 1900–1904 by legitimacy, giving sex ratios for legitimate and illegitimate births and the illegitimacy rate per 100 legitimate births.

metadata.title: Death-Rates
metadata.description: Shows yearly death totals for 1900–1904 by sex, the death rate per 100 people, and the male-to-female mortality ratio.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified (1902)
metadata.description: Lists the principal causes of death in 1902 with their death counts, noting only causes producing at least 10,000 deaths, together with the total deaths.

metadata.title: Stature
metadata.caption: Per cent.
metadata.description: Conscript examinations by an Army Surgeon over eleven years show the Japanese are gradually growing taller, as the share of men at each stature band shifts.

metadata.title: Population by Social Rank (at End of 1903.)

metadata.title: Number of Passports Issued to Japanese Going Abroad
metadata.description: Annual counts of passports issued to Japanese subjects going abroad, split by sex, from 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: Foreign Countries and Places Where Over 100 Japanese Are Living
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese living in foreign countries and places in 1904 and 1905, and by sex and total in 1906.

metadata.title: Foreigners Residing in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the number of foreigners residing in Japan at the end of each year from 1902 to 1906, by sex and total.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Japan by Districts
metadata.description: Official returns give the number of foreign residents in Japan by prefecture or district for 1904 to 1906.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Japan, by Nationality

metadata.title: Ainu in Hokkaido
metadata.description: Shows the Ainu population of Hokkaido at the end of 1905 and 1906, by sex and total.

metadata.description: Lists the 2,366 recipients of the Golden Kite decoration for the Japan-China War and North-China trouble, classified by grade from 2nd to 7th.

metadata.title: [Number of Peers by Rank, 1884–1907]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Japanese Peers in each rank from 1884 to November 1907, showing how the peerage grew over time, as the text introduces the five grades.

metadata.title: Precedent at Court
metadata.description: Shows how certain princes of the Imperial family are placed at court by the military or official posts they last held, following the statement about Count Matsukata's treatment.

metadata.description: A two-column list naming the Marquises of the peerage, with a cross-reference to the Who's Who chapter for biographical details on each member.

metadata.chapter_raw: Chapter XIII. Justice, Prisons, Police and Sanitation

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the Court of Cassation
metadata.chapter_raw: Chapter XIII. Justice, Prisons, Police and Sanitation
metadata.description: Breaks down the civil cases decided at the Court of Cassation from 1901 to 1905 by their subject matter, such as personal, land, money and rice matters.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Court of Cassation
metadata.chapter_raw: Chapter XIII. Justice, Prisons, Police and Sanitation

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Breaks down the appeal cases of 1901 to 1905 by subject matter, such as land, money and documents, for District and Local Court appeals.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Appeal Courts
metadata.caption: Appeals coming from the District Courts.

metadata.title: Appeals Coming from the Local Courts
metadata.description: Shows the number of appeals from the Local Courts for 1900 to 1904, in unlabelled columns; the page notes that no such case arose in 1905.

metadata.title: Civil Case at the District Courts
metadata.description: Gives the yearly civil case load at the District Courts from 1901 to 1905: cases heard, disposed of, carried forward, and new cases per population.

metadata.title: Cases Affecting Aliens by Nationality of Party
metadata.description: Breaks down the civil cases affecting aliens by nationality of party for 1905 and gives totals for 1901 to 1904.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the District Courts
metadata.description: Breaks down the District Court cases from 1901 to 1905 by their subject matter, such as personal, land, money and documents, with yearly totals.

metadata.title: Appeals Made to the Local Courts
metadata.description: Shows the number of appeals lodged at the local courts for 1901–1905 and the nature of the cases disposed of, grouped by subject matter.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Local Courts
metadata.description: Gives the yearly civil case load at the local courts, including cases disposed of, cases left pending, and new cases per 1,000 population.

metadata.title: Cases Affecting Aliens at the Local Courts
metadata.description: Lists civil cases in which aliens were parties, by nationality of party for 1905 and yearly totals for 1901–1904, with cases disposed of.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the Local Courts
metadata.description: Breaks down the civil cases disposed of at the local courts by nature of case for 1901–1905, with yearly totals.

metadata.title: Law Suits on Money Matters at the First Instance Classified
metadata.description: Shows the number of money-matter lawsuits at the first instance, grouped by the amount in dispute, with yearly totals for 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: Cases of Conciliation Dealt with at the District Courts
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for conciliation cases handled by the district courts, showing how many were settled, failed, withdrawn or still pending.

metadata.title: Nature of Conciliation Cases
metadata.description: Breaks down the conciliation cases of each year by their subject matter, such as personal, land, money and documents, with yearly totals.

metadata.title: Cases of Rehabilitation of Civil Rights
metadata.description: Reports yearly insolvency cases, debtors, creditors and credit amounts, along with the number of rehabilitations sanctioned and rejected, for 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: Criminal Defendants
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal defendants convicted and found not guilty by sex for 1901 to 1905, giving the yearly trend in criminal cases.

metadata.title: Sentences Carried Out
metadata.description: Lists the sentences actually carried out each year from 1901 to 1905 by type of punishment, with a yearly total.

metadata.title: No. of Major Criminal Cases and No. of Accused
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of major criminal cases and the number of persons accused in them, from 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: Nature of Accusations and No. of Conviction (in 1905)
metadata.description: Breaks down the major criminal accusations of 1905 by the category of accusation and by the outcome of the case.

metadata.title: [Offences by Type, 1905 (Column Headings Not Shown on This Page)]
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal offences in 1905 by type, with column headings not reproduced on this page. The text below gives the convictions breakdown.

metadata.title: [Criminal Cases Tried, 1901-1904 (Column Headings Not Shown on This Page)]
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for 1901-1904 in four unlabelled categories, shown for comparison with the 1905 totals above.

metadata.title: Aliens as Accused
metadata.description: Lists sentences passed on aliens accused of offences in Japan from 1901 to 1905, by punishment type and total.

metadata.title: Causes of Murders Classified
metadata.caption: (sentence in presence of accused.)
metadata.description: Breaks down murder cases by the motive behind them for each year from 1901 to 1905, with 1905 split by sex, and notes the number of murders consummated.

metadata.title: Personal Condition of Accused charged with Major Crimes
metadata.caption: (Cases sentenced in presence of accused.)
metadata.description: Shows the age and marital/consort condition of persons whose cases were sentenced in the accused's presence, for 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: Cases of Minor Crimes and No. of Persons Accused
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of minor-crime cases, persons accused, and judgments declared in the accused's presence, with the rate per 1000 population.

metadata.title: Offenders Charged with Police Offence and Conviction
metadata.description: Lists yearly numbers of offenders detained, fined, acquitted or rejected, and others under police offence charges, with totals, for 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: Appeals to the Court of Cassation and Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Shows the number of appeals before the Court of Cassation and the appeal courts, with cases dealt with, dropped or cancelled, and cases left pending, for 1905 and the preceding four years.

metadata.title: Appeals to Appeal Courts and District Courts
metadata.description: Gives the yearly figures for appeals lodged with appeal courts and district courts, cases dealt with, cases non-suited or cancelled, and cases still pending, for 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: Average Number of Prison Inmates at End of Year
metadata.description: Reports the number of prisons and the average daily count of inmates by category (convicts, correction, defendants, separate cells, infants) for 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: New Convictions and Population
metadata.description: Lists the number of persons convicted each year from 1901 to 1906 and the convictions per 1,000 of population.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified
metadata.description: Shows yearly counts of new convictions by felony type, larceny and police offences, their percentage shares, and capital punishment per 10,000 population, 1902–1906.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences by Convicts
metadata.description: Gives the number of convicts by how many times they had offended, with totals and the ratio of repeat offenders per 100 first offenders, 1902–1906.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified by Education
metadata.description: Breaks down new convictions each year into educated and illiterate offenders, with their percentage shares, 1902–1906.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified by Profession and Property
metadata.description: Classifies new convictions by whether offenders had property and by whether they had a profession, with counts and percentages, 1902–1906.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified by Age
metadata.description: Shows the number of new criminal convictions in 1902–1906 broken down by the age of the offenders, with the ratio of minors to adults.

metadata.title: Escape of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Lists the yearly number of prison inmates who escaped, by category of inmate, with the escape rate per 1000 and an average for 1887–1906.

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the sickness rate, average number of sick spells and sick days per inmate, and the mortality rate among prison inmates for 1902–1906.

metadata.title: No. of Days Work by Prison-inmates Earnings
metadata.description: Shows the number of days worked by prison inmates and their earnings and shares given, for government and contract work, from 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: Average Yearly Earnings and Receipts per One Worker
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Gives the average yearly earnings and receipts per one prison worker in yen for the years 1901 to 1906.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-officers and Prison-inmates
metadata.description: Shows the ratio of prison inmates to each warder, turnkey and female keeper for the years 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: Revenue of Prisons
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Lists the prison revenue for each fiscal year from 1903-4 to 1907-8, split into ordinary earnings, other receipts, extraordinary revenue and total.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prison
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows annual prison expenditure in yen, split into ordinary items (salaries, wages, inmate expenses, others), extraordinary outlay and total, for 1903–4 to 1907–8.

metadata.title: Prison Expense per 1 Inmate
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the prison expense per inmate in yen, split into ordinary, extraordinary and total amounts, for 1902–3 to 1906–7.

metadata.title: Prison Expense per 1 Inmate
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Repeats the per-inmate prison expense in yen for 1902–3 to 1906–7, restated in a second block with the same ordinary, extraordinary and total figures.

metadata.title: Police Offices and Police Force
metadata.description: Lists the number of police offices, police officers and men, and population per officer for 1901 to 1905, showing the police establishment's growth.

metadata.title: Epidemic Diseases and Mortality
metadata.description: Reports cases and deaths from enteric fever, dysentery, diphtheria, cholera, plague and other epidemics for 1902 to 1906, with mortality per 100 cases.

metadata.title: Suicides
metadata.description: A summary of suicide numbers by sex for 1901 to 1905, with totals and the ratio per 10,000 population, opening the section on suicides.

metadata.title: Acts of Suicides
metadata.description: Breaks down suicides by method (hanging, drowning, edged tools, fire arms, poison, others) and sex for 1901 to 1905, with totals.

metadata.title: Case of Suicides of Over 200 Classified
metadata.description: Shows suicides of over 200 cases, classified by the apparent cause such as mental derangement, illness, poverty, love, remorse and domestic discord, by sex.

metadata.title: Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.description: Gives the number of sufferers from robbery, larceny, peculation and fraud for 1901 to 1905, with totals and the rate per 1,000 population.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, total burned area and per-case averages, illustrating the fire losses recorded in these years.

metadata.title: Hospitals, Doctors and Mid-wives
metadata.description: Gives the number of hospitals, doctors (total and per 100 population) and mid-wives at the end of each year from 1901 to 1905.

metadata.title: Vaccination Cases
metadata.description: Records the total number of vaccinations performed each year from 1901 to 1905, as vaccination was compulsory in Japan.

metadata.title: Ratio of Successful Vaccination on Persons Tried for the First Time
metadata.description: Shows the share of first-time vaccinations that succeeded each year, supporting the text's claim that more than 85 in 100 first cases succeed.

metadata.title: [Convicts Under Age, November 1907]
metadata.description: Gives the census of convicts under 20 in November 1907, broken down by age group, to show the scale of juvenile offending.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Convicts Under 14, 1902–1906]
metadata.description: Lists the yearly number of convicts under 14 from 1902 to 1906, showing trends in juvenile crime over five years.

metadata.title: [Gross Area of Japan Proper]
metadata.caption: (Unit: cho)
metadata.description: Shows how the gross area of Japan proper (excluding Formosa and Saghalien) is distributed among Crown and government land, private land, and highways and waters.

metadata.title: [Arable Land by Classification]
metadata.caption: (Unit: cho)
metadata.description: Classifies the gross arable land of Japan proper, about 15.7 per cent of the whole area, into paddy fields, upland fields and others.

metadata.title: [Margin of Reclamation by Districts]
metadata.description: Compares whole area, land inclined under 15 degrees, area under tillage and not yet reclaimed land by district, to show the margin left for reclamation.

metadata.title: Progress of Reclamation of Forests and Wild Land
metadata.description: Shows the area of forests and wild land converted to arable land, dwelling-lots and other uses each year from 1900 to 1904, with totals, to illustrate the progress of reclamation.

metadata.title: Farming Population
metadata.description: Gives the number of farming families and their percentage of total householders in 1903 and 1904, distinguishing those farming only from those combining farming with other occupations.

metadata.title: Cultivated by Owners and Tenants
metadata.description: Compares the area of paddy-fields and upland farms cultivated by owners and by tenants, with their percentage shares, for 1903 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Cultivated Area and Value, 1901–1906]
metadata.description: The top of the page gives the cultivated area and its value for 1901 to 1906, a background figure set beside the Treasury investigation of dwelling-land values that follows.

metadata.title: Rate per "Tsubo (6×6ft.)" for Urban Dwelling-Land
metadata.description: This table gives the official value, annual rent and market value per tsubo of urban dwelling-land for each prefecture, from the Treasury investigation made public in early 1906.

metadata.title: Rate per "Tsubo" for Rural Dwelling-Land
metadata.description: This table gives the official value, annual rent and market value per tsubo of rural dwelling-land for each prefecture, from the same Treasury investigation of 1906.

metadata.title: [Average Yield per Tan of Paddy-fields]
metadata.description: Shows the average yield in koku per tan of paddy-fields in successive five-year periods and over twenty years, illustrating the gradual improvement in productive power.

metadata.title: Increase of Tillage Area in Old Japan
metadata.description: Compares the average tillage area of paddy-fields, upland farms and the total in two periods, with the rates of increase, showing upland farms grew faster than paddy-fields.

metadata.title: [Transfer Returns of Arable Land]
metadata.description: Lists the number of arable land transfers recorded by the Department of Finance for the last three available years, showing the frequency of ownership transfers.

metadata.title: [Ratio of One-crop and Two-crop Paddy Fields]
metadata.description: Gives the official figures of paddy fields under one crop and two crops in recent years, both in cho and as a percentage of the total.

metadata.title: Two-Crop Paddy-Fields, Green Manure for Second Crop
metadata.description: Shows the area of two-crop paddy-fields with green manure for the second crop in 1903–1905, in cho and as a percentage of the total, continuing from the previous page.

metadata.title: Human Labor and Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.description: Gives the approximate areas tilled with cattle or horse labor (1st kind) and exclusively with hands (2nd kind) for paddy-fields and upland farms, 1903–1905, in cho and percentages.

metadata.title: [Projects Sanctioned, Work Commenced and Completed, 1900–1907]

metadata.title: [Volume of Manure Consumption at End of 1905]
metadata.caption: (in 000 yen.)
metadata.description: Gives the estimated volume of manure consumption, by kind, as investigated at the end of 1905, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [Home Production and Imports of Manure, 1902–1906]
metadata.description: Compares yearly manure imports, home production and their totals, showing how domestic manufacture grew relative to imports.

metadata.title: [Artificial Fertilizer Output by Locality, 1903–1906]
metadata.description: Shows the value of artificial fertilizer returns in four localities for 1903 to 1906, illustrating the recent striking advance of the industry.

metadata.caption: (in 000)

metadata.caption: (in 000)

metadata.description: Records oat area, harvest and value for 1902 to 1905, introduced by a note that oats are chiefly grown in Hokkaido where cultivation is expanding.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (in 000)

metadata.caption: (in 000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly production figures for soja beans, red beans, sweet potatoes and potatoes from 1902 to 1906.

metadata.description: Records yearly output of leaf indigo and leaf tobacco, in thousand kwan, for 1902–1906.

metadata.title: Fibers
metadata.description: Shows cotton and hemp cultivated area and output for 1902–1906.

metadata.description: Lists area and output of other minor crops such as peas, beans, peanuts, maize, radish and carrot, with output in koku or kwan.

metadata.description: Lists the area under and output of minor crops such as burdock, ginger, chilies and sugar cane, showing the agricultural production of the year.

metadata.title: Mulberry Trees and Families Pursuing Sericulture
metadata.description: Gives the mulberry-tree area and number of households engaged in sericulture for 1901 to 1906, as background to Japan's silk industry.

metadata.description: Shows annual cocoon production by grade (good, double, pierced and waste cocoons) and total output for 1901 to 1907.

metadata.title: Cocoons Classified by Season
metadata.description: Breaks down cocoon production by season (spring, summer and autumn crops) for 1902 to 1907, in thousands of koku.

metadata.description: Shows the yearly quantity, value and highest Shinshiu filature price of raw silk exported from Japan, 1901 to 1906.

metadata.description: Classifies the 1907 output of raw silk, noshi, kibiso, waste silk and silk floss by establishments and families, in kwan and yen, from Department of Agriculture and Commerce returns.

metadata.description: Shows the volume and value of waste silk exported from Japan in 1905 to 1907, with a note on the main destinations.

metadata.description: Shows the bales of raw silk exported directly by Japanese and foreign exporters, split by Europe and the U.S.A., with the share handled by Japanese firms.

metadata.description: Gives the yearly area of tea plantations in cho and the number of tea-manufactories, illustrating the tea industry's scale in the early 1900s.

metadata.description: Lists annual tea output in kwan by grade and type (green, black, oolong), with totals, showing how production changed over these years.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1906)
metadata.description: Shows the leading tea-producing districts in 1906, with the number of families engaged in tea and the value of production in yen for each.

metadata.description: Gives the quantity and value of Japanese tea exports for 1902 to 1907, set against the competition from Ceylon and Chinese teas.

metadata.title: Destinations of Black Tea Exported
metadata.description: Shows black tea exports from 1901 to 1906 by destination (U.S.A., Canada and others), explaining the manufacturers' interest in black and brick tea.

metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of horses in Japan by native, cross and foreign breeds, with totals, births and deaths for 1901 to 1906.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of native, cross-bred and foreign cattle in Japan with totals, births and deaths for 1901 to 1906.

metadata.title: Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Gives the yearly numbers of sheep, goats and swine in Japan for 1901 to 1906, set out in two side-by-side panels.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Lists the number of cattle and calves, horses, sheep and goats, and swine slaughtered in Japan each year from 1901 to 1906.

metadata.title: Leading Stock Farms

metadata.title: Number of Households Keeping Poultry, (1906)
metadata.description: Gives the national count of households keeping poultry in 1906, with the number of fowls and ducks and the value of eggs produced.

metadata.title: Leading Poultry Districts in 1906
metadata.description: Lists the twelve leading prefectures for poultry in 1906, giving household numbers, fowl and duck counts, and egg prices.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Dairy in 1906.
metadata.description: Shows the number of dairies, milk cows, and milk output by value in the leading dairy prefectures in 1906, with a national total.

metadata.title: Fruits in 1905
metadata.description: Lists the number of fruit trees and yield in kwan for each main fruit kind in 1905, with the leading districts for each fruit noted below.

metadata.title: Exports of Fruits and Vegetables
metadata.caption: yen.

metadata.title: Area and Price of State Land Offered for Sale in Hokkaido
metadata.description: Lists the maximum lot areas and sale prices per cho for each category of State land an individual may purchase in Hokkaido.

metadata.title: Time Limit for Finishing Work on Purchased or Leased State Land
metadata.description: Gives the period within which work must be finished on State land bought or leased in Hokkaido, according to lot size.

metadata.description: The table gives the relative percentage of sedimentary and igneous strata existing in Japan proper, showing the share of each geological period and the totals.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Gold and Silver Mines (1907)
metadata.description: Lists the principal gold and silver mines in Japan in 1907 with their locations, owners and gold and silver output in momme, to show the scale of each mine's production.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Copper Mines
metadata.description: Lists the estimated 1907 copper output in kin of the principal copper mines, with the owner of each mine.

metadata.title: Output of Iron Mines in 1906

metadata.title: Production of Principal Sulphur Mines in 1906

metadata.title: Output of Principal Coal Mines in 1907

metadata.description: Gives the area and 1907 metric-ton output of the principal coal mines, with their owners, to show the scale of the coal industry.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Manganese Mines in 1905
metadata.description: Shows the area and 1905 output in kin of the principal manganese mines, listed at the foot of the page.

metadata.title: Wages (in Yen) at Metal-mines
metadata.description: Gives the daily maximum and minimum wages in yen for males and females in each occupation at metal mines.

metadata.title: Accident in the Mines

metadata.description: Shows the number of fishing boats accidentally wrecked, drifted, missing, upset or otherwise lost in 1906, and the resulting killed, wounded and missing crew, supporting the surrounding discussion of fishing-boat costs.

metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of fish catches and of marine products from 1901 to 1906, showing the trend in Japan's fisheries output.
