metadata.description: Lists the principal manufactured marine products (dried, boiled and manure goods) and their values, shown in two side-by-side columns.

metadata.title: Aquiculture

metadata.title: Pelagic Fishery in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Breaks down pelagic fishing in Japan proper by kind of fishery and vessel type for 1906 and 1905, with the value of catches.

metadata.title: Pelagig Fishery off Korean Coast
metadata.description: Shows the number of ships, crew and catch value of each pelagic fishing method off the Korean coast in 1906, with 1905 figures for comparison.

metadata.description: Gives the number of junks, sailing ships and European-style vessels and the value of catches in the pelagic fishery on the Saghalien coast in 1906.

metadata.title: Japanese Fishery on Siberian Coast
metadata.description: Shows the sailing ships, tonnage, crew and catch value of Japanese fishing off the Siberian coast in 1906.

metadata.title: [Salt Production Statistics, 1901–1906]
metadata.description: Annual salt production figures for 1901 to 1906, showing salt field area, furnace numbers, output, value and average price per koku.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Salt Production in 1905
metadata.description: Shows the leading salt-producing prefectures in 1905, with their salt field area, output and value.

metadata.title: Area of Forests
metadata.caption: (1 cho=2½ acres) (At end March, 1907)
metadata.description: The table gives the area of forests by ownership at the end of March 1907, showing protection, utilization and percentage forests, and totals, to illustrate the classification of forest proprietorship.

metadata.title: Distribution of Forests
metadata.description: Lists the prefectures of northeastern Honshu and Hokkaido that each contain at least 500,000 cho of forest, showing the forest area of each.

metadata.title: Forest Yield, 1906–1907
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of timber and fuel forest yield for 1906–1907, by kind of tree, excluding Hokkaido and Formosa, to illustrate the modest returns from forestry.

metadata.title: Financial Yield of Forests by Ownership, 1905
metadata.description: Gives the financial yield of forests of each ownership class in 1905, divided into timber, fagots and total, as the basis for the per-cho yield figures in the text.

metadata.title: [State Forest Receipts, Expenses and Balance]
metadata.description: Shows receipts, expenses and balance of State forest administration for each fiscal year from 1900-1 to 1906-7, illustrating the modest rate of profit noted in the text.

metadata.title: [Principal Items of Forest Products in Foreign Trade]
metadata.caption: (in 1000 yen)
metadata.description: Gives the principal forest products figuring in export and import trade for 1901 to 1906, showing timbers, tea-chest boards, match sticks, bamboos and total trade values.

metadata.title: [Forest Adjustment Works Estimates]
metadata.description: Summarises the planned forest adjustment works, giving the area disposed of, brought under work and the related planting and road items for each period up to 1907.

metadata.title: Regeneration of State Forests
metadata.description: Shows the annual area planted and naturally regenerated on State forests and the number of trees planted for 1906 to 1908.

metadata.title: State Sawing Pits
metadata.description: Lists the State sawing pits with their motive power, horsepower and output, the works run by the Government to convert timber from state forests.

metadata.title: [Conversion Plants: Motive Power, Output and Maximum Output]
metadata.description: Lists the conversion plants at named localities with their motive power, ordinary output and maximum output, shown before the three-year conversion results.

metadata.title: Total Volume of Felling (Shakjime) and Conversion (Tana)
metadata.description: Shows the total volume of timber felled and converted and faggots produced over three years, with 1908 as an estimate.

metadata.title: Sided Logs and Charcoals (Kwamme)
metadata.description: Gives the volumes of sided logs (timbers) and charcoal produced in the same three years, noting that faggots were also produced.

metadata.title: Hewn Boards Etc.
metadata.description: Records the output of hewn boards and other timber for the same three years, continuing the forestry production figures.

metadata.title: [Camphor Yield from Twigs and Leaves Analysis]
metadata.description: The results of the latest analysis at the Chemical Laboratory of Agricultural College, Imperial University, Tokyo, comparing water and camphor content of twigs and leaves.

metadata.title: Uses of Camphor
metadata.description: Camphor is used for making celluloid, gunpowder, perfume and other goods, and this short list gives the printed share of camphor used for each purpose.

metadata.title: [Shooting Licenses Issued, 1902-1906]
metadata.description: This table, introduced by the text on shooting licenses, shows how many License A and License B permits were issued each year from 1902 to 1906, and their totals, as fees were raised.

metadata.title: Progress of Industrial Investment
metadata.description: The table gives yearly figures for the number and capital of industrial companies from 1896 to 1906, showing the growth of industrial investment and the 1900 setback.

metadata.title: Industrial Establishments Classified by Amount of Investment
metadata.description: The table lists the forty kinds of industrial establishments whose paid-up capital reached yen 500,000 or more, showing company numbers and capital invested in 1905 and 1906.

metadata.title: Distribution of Industries
metadata.description: Shows the leading prefectures with companies each having over Y.3,000,000 paid-up capital, with company counts and paid-up capital for 1906.

metadata.title: Factories and Its Employees
metadata.description: Gives the number of factories by type of motive power and the number of male, female and total operatives employed, for the years 1896 to 1906.

metadata.title: Motive Powers Used in Factories, 1905
metadata.description: Lists the kinds of motive power used in factories in 1905, with the number of engines and horse power of each kind.

metadata.title: Kind of Factories
metadata.description: The table breaks down Japanese factories by industry, showing how many were run by motors, how many were not, and the daily average number of employees in each.

metadata.title: Weaving Establishments, Operatives and Value of Products (1895 to 1906)
metadata.description: Summarises the number of weaving establishments, looms, operatives and the value of woven products in Japan year by year from 1895 to 1906.

metadata.title: Leading Weaving Districts (1)
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures by number of weaving houses, machine and hand looms, and operatives, showing where the textile weaving industry was concentrated.

metadata.title: Leading Weaving Districts. (2)
metadata.caption: Value (in Y. 1,000).
metadata.description: Shows the value of silk, mixed, cotton, hempen and woolen fabrics woven in each leading prefecture, illustrating the regional distribution of textile weaving.

metadata.title: Production (Value).
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000).
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of production of silk, mixed, cotton, hemp and woolen fabrics from 1895 to 1906, showing the growth of the weaving industry over time.

metadata.title: Ceramics
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japanese ceramic production and exports for 1897 to 1906, giving the overall trend of the ceramic industry.

metadata.title: Leading Ceramic Districts (1906)
metadata.caption: (Above Y. 150,000)
metadata.description: Lists the leading ceramic-producing prefectures in 1906, with families engaged, employees and value of output, for districts above Y. 150,000.

metadata.title: Value of Lacquer Ware Production and Its Export
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of lacquer ware production and exports from 1897 to 1906, showing the lacquer industry's development over the decade.

metadata.title: Leading Lacquer Ware Districts (1906)
metadata.description: Lists the leading lacquer ware producing districts in 1906 with families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Production and Export of Matches
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly production and export of matches in quantity and value from 1897 to 1906, giving the trend of the match industry.

metadata.title: Leading Districts for Match Industry (1906)
metadata.description: Lists the seven leading prefectures for the match industry in 1906, with families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Value of Wax and Refined-Wax Products
metadata.description: Gives the number of wax-producing families and the value of wax and refined-wax output from 1897 to 1906.

metadata.title: Leading Wax Districts (1906)
metadata.description: Lists the six leading prefectures for wax production in 1906, with families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Mats and Matting
metadata.description: Shows the number of families engaged in mat and matting work and the values of floor mats and fancy matting for export, year by year from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: Leading Mat and Matting Districts
metadata.caption: (Above 200,000 yen in 1906)
metadata.description: Lists the leading mat and matting districts whose 1906 output exceeded 200,000 yen, with families, employees and values of mats and fancy matting.

metadata.title: Plaits of Straw and Wood Shaving
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of workshops, employees and value of straw and wood-shaving plaits production from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: Leading Straw-Plaits Districts
metadata.caption: (of above Y. 200,000 in 1906.)
metadata.description: Lists the leading straw-plait districts whose 1906 value exceeded 200,000 yen, with their workshops, employees and value.

metadata.title: Vegetable Oils
metadata.description: Gives the yearly figures for the vegetable oil industry from 1897 to 1906, covering families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Leading Vegetable Oils Districts
metadata.caption: (Places which produced above Y. 250,000 in 1906).
metadata.description: Lists the prefectures that produced more than Y. 250,000 of vegetable oils in 1906, with families, employees and value.

metadata.title: Japanese Paper
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for the Japanese paper industry from 1897 to 1906, covering families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Japanese Paper Districts
metadata.caption: (Places which produced above Y. 300,000 in 1906).
metadata.description: Lists the places that produced more than Y. 300,000 of Japanese paper in 1906, with families, employees and value.

metadata.description: The top of the page continues a prefectural statistics table whose column headings appear on the previous page, listing figures for nine prefectures.

metadata.title: Leading European Paper Manufacturing Companies
metadata.caption: (of above Y. 500,000 in 1906)
metadata.description: Lists the largest European paper manufacturing companies, those with capital above Y. 500,000 in 1906, with their capital, machines, horse power, staff and output.

metadata.title: Production and Import of European Paper
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Compares the annual value of European paper production with the total value of imports, for 1896 to 1906, shown in two side-by-side columns.

metadata.title: Indigo (Japanese.)
metadata.description: Gives the number of families, employees and value of Japanese indigo production from 1900 to 1907, showing the industry's trend over those years.

metadata.title: [Indigo Production in 1906-7, Tokushima-ken]
metadata.description: Shows that most of the 1906-7 indigo production came from Tokushima prefecture, with its families, employees and value figures.

metadata.title: Peppermint
metadata.description: Records families, employees and the value of crude peppermint, menthol crystal and oil production from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: [Peppermint Production in 1906, Kanagawa and Hyogo]
metadata.description: Shows that most of the 1906 peppermint production came from Kanagawa-ken, with Hyogo as the other producing prefecture, by factories, employees and value.

metadata.title: Leathers
metadata.description: Gives the number of families, employees and value of leather production from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: Leading Leathers Districts in 1906
metadata.caption: (Places producing above Y. 100,000)
metadata.description: Lists the leading leather-producing districts in 1906, showing families and employees engaged and the value of leather output by animal source.

metadata.title: Bricks and Tiles in 1906 — A. Bricks
metadata.description: Shows the number of brick factories, employees and value of output by prefecture in 1906, with 1905 figures for comparison.

metadata.title: Bricks and Tiles in 1906 — B. Tiles
metadata.description: Gives the tile-making figures by prefecture for 1906 and 1905, continuing the brick and tile statistics; column headings are inferred from the layout.

metadata.title: Milling Districts in 1906 (by Machine.)
metadata.description: Reports the number of milling factories, employees, output and value by district in 1906, using machine milling.

metadata.title: Canned Articles in 1906
metadata.description: Shows the number of canned-goods factories, employees and output value by prefecture for 1906, with 1905 totals for comparison.

metadata.title: Leading Silk Handkerchief Districts (1906)
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures for silk handkerchief making in 1906, with workshops, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Industries (in 1906)
metadata.description: Gives the number of workshops, employees and value of output for a range of miscellaneous industries in 1906.

metadata.title: Factories Conducted by Government (1906)
metadata.description: Shows the engines, horse power, employees, daily wages and coal use of the government-run printing bureau factories in 1906.

metadata.title: [Government Arsenals, Dockyards and Works]
metadata.description: A list of government arsenals, dockyards, shipyards and railway works with their figures, continued from the previous page, showing the state of these establishments.

metadata.title: [Monthly Figures, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a monthly figures table, with rows for March to June and a total, whose column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Cotton Tissues

metadata.description: Year-by-year statistics of Japanese cotton spinning mills, showing mill numbers, capital, spindles, yarn output, hands employed and working hours from 1895 to 1906.

metadata.title: Import of Sugar
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yen value of brown, refined and total sugar imports for selected years, shown in two side-by-side runs of years.

metadata.title: Export of Sugar from Formosa
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Lists Formosan sugar exports by year, split into white and brown sugar sent to Japan proper and to other countries, with totals.

metadata.title: Leading Sugar Refining Companies
metadata.description: Lists the leading sugar refining companies with their establishment years, paid-up capital and latest dividend rates.

metadata.title: [Japanese Sake, Shochu, Beer and Alcohol Production]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of sake, shochu, other spirits, beer and alcohol, illustrating the scale of Japan's liquor industry in the text on sake and beer.

metadata.title: [Soy Production in Recent Years]
metadata.description: Lists the recent annual output of soy, showing production by year for the Chiba prefecture-led industry described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Distances of Ports and Towns]
metadata.description: The page lists a set of places with figures in ri, cko and ken, apparently measured distances, though the table carries no printed title or explanation.

metadata.description: Shows yearly numbers of patent, design and trade-mark applications and grants or registrations at the Japanese Office from 1900 to 1907, as the text introduces them.

metadata.title: [Utility Model Designs: Applications and Registrations, 1905–1907]
metadata.description: Gives the number of utility model design applications and registrations after the July 1905 regulations took effect, for the second half of 1905 and each later year.

metadata.title: [Estimated Expenditure for the 1908-9 Year]
metadata.description: Shows how the estimated expenditure voted by the 24th Diet session for the 1908-9 financial year is divided between ordinary and extraordinary expenditures and the supplementary budget.

metadata.description: Lists the increased taxes by which the budget deficit of yen 4,915,291 is to be met, with their total.

metadata.title: Revenues and Expenditures
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Summarises the state's ordinary and extraordinary revenues and expenditures for 1908-9 against 1907-8, with the year-on-year increase or decrease.

metadata.title: Items of Ordinary and Extraordinary Revenues
metadata.caption: Ordinary Revenues (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Itemises the ordinary revenues by source for 1907-8 and 1908-9, showing the increase for each tax and state enterprise line.

metadata.description: This table gives the extraordinary revenue items of the national budget in thousands of yen, by source, comparing three sets of figures.

metadata.description: Shows government expenditure on industry, covering agricultural societies, experimental and technical stations, fisheries, sericulture and sugar, with a total.

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Shows the 1908-9 postponed government expenditure items, comparing original outlays, revised figures and the amounts postponed for each item.

metadata.description: Lists the fixed postponement amounts in yen for each item, with their periods and the overall total, as a companion to the postponement figures above.

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows how the post-bellum adjustment outlay, spread over years ending 1914-15, was rearranged from its original yearly allotments, with the resulting postponements and increases.

metadata.description: Shows the original and rearranged yearly allotments for warship building and other naval construction after the programme was extended by two years.

metadata.title: Maintenance of the Fleet
metadata.description: Shows the original and rearranged yearly allotments for fleet maintenance over the six-year programme, which was extended by two years.

metadata.title: Disbursements by Japan
metadata.caption: 1906, yen

metadata.title: [Foreign Loans Raised Since the Conclusion of Peace]
metadata.description: The table lists loans raised by Japanese companies from foreign capital after the Russo-Japanese war, showing amounts, interest rates, net proceeds and actual interest.

metadata.title: The Cost of the War
metadata.description: Summarises the settled receipts, disbursements and resulting balance of the war cost accounts at the end of 1907.

metadata.title: Chambers of Commerce at Principal Districts (1906)
metadata.description: Lists the chambers of commerce in the principal trading districts in 1906, showing their membership, numbers of electors by voting right, and expenses.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Agency Subscribers, Inquiries and Replies, 1902–1907]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly subscriber, inquiry and reply counts of the Tokyo foreign-communications agency, showing its growth from 1902 to 1907.

metadata.title: Osaka Mercantile Agency (Established 1901)
metadata.description: The table lists the subscribers and communications issued by the Osaka Mercantile Agency, established in 1901, by year from 1902 to 1907.

metadata.title: Number, Capital, Etc. of Exchanges
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: The table gives the number of exchanges in Japan and their capital, reserves, deposits, fees, expenses and profits for 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: Amount of Bonds and Shares Transacted at the Stock Exchanges
metadata.description: Shows the yearly volume of bonds and shares traded at the stock exchanges, given in the Home Trade section to illustrate the scale of securities dealing.

metadata.title: Amount of Rice Transacted at the Rice Exchanges
metadata.description: Gives the yearly quantity of rice dealt in at the rice exchanges and the average price per koku, showing the scale of rice trading from 1900 to 1906.

metadata.title: [Exchange Dues and Brokerage on National, Provincial and Municipal Loan Bonds]
metadata.caption: per Y. 100 ruling price

metadata.title: Number of Shares, etc. Transacted — Tokyo Stock Exchange
metadata.caption: No. of shares, etc.

metadata.caption: Yen 50.
metadata.description: Gives the highest, lowest and average monthly quotations of two leading shares, Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Co. and N.Y.K., at selected months from 1905 to 1908.

metadata.caption: Yen 50

metadata.caption: Yen 50
metadata.description: Monthly highest, lowest and average share prices of the Tokyo Stock Exchange and Tokyo Electric Light Company, giving comparative market figures for 1905 to 1907.

metadata.title: Average Daily Wages
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Average daily wages in yen for workers in clothing, food and drink, and house-building trades at several years from 1895 to 1906, shown to illustrate changes in labour income.

metadata.title: [Daily Wages by Occupation]
metadata.description: Shows daily and monthly wage rates for various artisans, agricultural workers, and servants; the column headings are not printed on this page, so the wage series cannot be identified from it.

metadata.title: Aver. Wages in Tokyo.
metadata.description: Gives average daily wages in Tokyo for five trades across three years, from the latest official return of wages.

metadata.title: Index Number of Prices.
metadata.description: Monthly index numbers of prices from 1904 to 1908, with yearly averages, showing the movement of price levels over the period.

metadata.description: The table tabulates Japan's section size, exhibit numbers, values, sales and expenses at the Chicago, Paris and St. Louis world fairs, showing its participation in international exhibitions.

metadata.title: Exports and Imports of Commodities
metadata.caption: (Value in Y. 1,000.)

metadata.title: Exports and Imports of Specie and Bullion
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly exports, imports and balance of specie and bullion for 1895 to 1907, showing when Japan's bullion trade ran to an import or export surplus.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade in the 1st Half Year of 1908
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Summarises Japan's foreign trade in the first half of 1908 against the same period of earlier years, for commodities and specie and bullion, to show the trade balance.

metadata.title: Monthly Trade of Merchandise
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000.)
metadata.description: Gives month-by-month values of Japan's merchandise exports and imports for 1908 with comparative figures for 1902 and 1904–1907, showing seasonal patterns in trade.

metadata.title: Monthly Exports and Imports of Specie and Bullion
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)

metadata.title: Trade Returns of Leading Ports
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000.)

metadata.title: Exports by Countries from Leading Ports
metadata.caption: (In Y. 1,000)

metadata.title: [Foreign Trade by Countries and Ports]

metadata.description: Shows the value of imports at the principal ports, broken down by country of origin, with totals for each region and for all imports.

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)

metadata.caption: Exports (in Y. 1,000)

metadata.title: [Distribution of Trade by Countries, 1906–1907]
metadata.description: Shows exports to and imports from Asian countries in 1906 and 1907, supporting the text's argument that Asia's share of Japan's foreign trade has grown relative to Europe and America.

metadata.title: Trade with China
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000); Exports to.

metadata.title: British India — Exports to
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's imports from British India in value (thousand yen) for 1901 to 1907, led by raw cotton and rice.

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)

metadata.description: Shows Japan's trade with Canada in selected articles, 1901–1907, in thousands of yen, listing exports to and imports from Canada.

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's trade with Australia in selected articles, 1901–1907, in thousands of yen, covering exports to and imports from Australia.

metadata.title: [Japanese Warships Listed with Tonnage and Date]
metadata.description: A continuation list of Japanese warships giving each vessel's tonnage and date, part of the fleet-strength survey that follows.

metadata.description: Compares the number and displacement of Japan's fleet classes before the late war with the present strength, as the text states.

metadata.title: Vessels Lost During the Hostilities
metadata.description: Lists the vessels Japan lost during the course of the hostilities, by class, with number and displacement.

metadata.title: Vessels Captured or Built

metadata.title: [Domestic Parcel Post Charges Outside Each Locality]
metadata.description: Gives the domestic parcel post charges for ordinary and registered parcels sent outside the locality of the post office, by weight band up to 800 momme.

metadata.title: Postal Money Orders Fees
metadata.caption: Postal Money Orders:—Maximum, 5 yen; Fee, 3 sen. Ordinary Money Orders:—Maximum, 50 yen. Fees:—

metadata.title: Telegraphic Money Orders Fees
metadata.caption: Telegraphic Money Orders:—Maximum, 50 yen. Fees:—
metadata.description: Lists the fees charged for telegraphic money orders according to the sum remitted, up to a maximum of 50 yen.

metadata.title: Foreign Parcels
metadata.description: Lists the cheapest parcel post routes from Japan to several European countries, British India and Dutch East India, with the maximum rate in yen for each.

metadata.title: [Postal Rates to Foreign Countries by Route]
metadata.description: The page lists postal rates for letters sent to various foreign countries, giving the routing and the rate charged for each service route.

metadata.title: Russia
metadata.description: Lists the postal rates for correspondence sent to Russia by the direct Siberian route and via Germany by German steamer.

metadata.title: Number of Post and Telegraph Offices
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of post and telegraph offices in Japan from 1901 to 1906, with the average area and population served by each office.

metadata.title: Number of Post and Telegraph Offices in Korea and China
metadata.caption: At end of fiscal year.
metadata.description: Shows how many post and telegraph offices Japan maintained in Korea and China at the end of each fiscal year from 1901 to 1906.

metadata.title: Ordinary Mail Matters Transmitted
metadata.description: Gives the annual volume of ordinary mail items (letters, post-cards, newspapers and magazines) transmitted, with per-capita averages, across the fiscal years shown.

metadata.title: Parcel Post
metadata.description: Records the total number of parcels handled by the post each fiscal year and the average per 100 people, showing growth of the parcel service.

metadata.title: Mail Matters and Parcels Dealt with at Offices Stationed Abroad
metadata.description: Shows the ordinary mail and parcels transmitted and delivered by Japanese post offices stationed abroad in selected years.

metadata.title: [Ordinary Mail Matters and Parcels Transmitted and Delivered by Fiscal Year]
metadata.description: Shows the volume of ordinary mail matters and parcels transmitted and delivered in 1903 and 1906, giving the scale of domestic postal business.

metadata.title: Foreign Ord. Mail Matters and Parcels Dealt With
metadata.caption: (Exclusive of those dealt with by Offices established abroad.) (in 1,000.)

metadata.title: Mail Matters Exchanged with Principal Countries in 1906 Fiscal Year
metadata.caption: (in 1,000.)
metadata.description: Breaks down mail matters transmitted and arrived in the 1906 fiscal year by region and by principal foreign country.

metadata.title: Postal Savings Deposits at Home
metadata.description: Tracks the growth of postal savings deposits at home, showing depositors, amounts and per-depositor averages, and notes the rise after the recent war.

metadata.title: Savings Deposits at Offices Stationed in China
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of depositors, total savings amounts and average deposit per depositor at post offices in China from 1901 to 1906.

metadata.caption: Via Shanghai

metadata.title: [Telegraph Rates from Japan to South America]
metadata.caption: Ordinary Telegrams
metadata.description: Gives ordinary telegram charges from Japan to South American countries, by the Vladivostock and Shanghai routes.

metadata.description: Shows the growth of the telegraph network from 1894 to 1906, giving aerial wire length in ri and submarine cable length in knots at the end of each fiscal year.

metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of domestic telegrams, foreign telegrams transmitted and arrived, and messages per 100 people from 1894 to 1906.

metadata.title: Foreign Telegrams in 1906
metadata.description: Breaks down foreign telegrams transmitted and arrived in 1906 by country and region, with Asia and Europe totals followed by individual countries.

metadata.description: Continuation of a comparison of telephone figures for several foreign countries, whose column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.description: Lists the number of telephone exchange, subscriber and automatic apparatus installed at the end of each fiscal year.

metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen.)

metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen.)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly expenses of the postal and telegraph services by branch, from 1894 and 1901 to 1906, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Registered Steamers of over 1,000 Tons Classified by Materials
metadata.caption: (Dec. '06.)

metadata.title: Steamers Classified by Speed
metadata.caption: (Dec. '06.)
metadata.description: Shows how the registered steamers over 1,000 tons at December 1906 were distributed by rated speed in knots, with tonnage.

metadata.title: Registered and Unregistered Steamers Classified According to Nature of Service (Dec. '06.)
metadata.description: Shows the number and gross tonnage of registered and unregistered steamers in Japan at December 1906, grouped by the nature of their service.

metadata.description: Shows the number and gross tonnage of home-built steamers by size class and hull material (wool/steel) in 1906, part of the mercantile marine statistics.

metadata.title: [Vessels Built or Launched at Leading Shipyards, Encouragement Law to May '08]
metadata.description: Lists the vessels built or launched at the leading shipyards since the Encouragement Law, up to May 1908, by yard.

metadata.title: [Dimensions of Docks and Shipyards by Locality]
metadata.description: The table gives the length, breadth, entrance width and water depth of the docks and shipyards at each port, showing the size of the facilities available for shipbuilding and repair.

metadata.title: Subsidized Routes
metadata.caption: Yen
metadata.description: Lists the annual government subsidies paid to each shipping company on subsidized routes, with the total.

metadata.description: Shows the navigation bounties paid to each shipping company, with the total for the bounty列.

metadata.title: Items Added to Navigation Bounties
metadata.description: Gives the two further items added to the navigation bounties and the grand total of government marine subsidies.

metadata.title: Subsidized Services: Service, Term of Contract and Annual Grant
metadata.description: Lists the subsidized steamship services with their contract periods and the annual government grant for each.

metadata.title: Ships Classified According to Service
metadata.description: Shows the number, total tonnage and average tonnage of Japanese steamers split between regular and irregular service.

metadata.title: Regular Service Ships Classified by Routes
metadata.description: Breaks down the regular service ships by route, giving the number, tonnage and average tonnage for each route group.

metadata.title: Foreign Lines
metadata.description: Lists the regular foreign shipping lines with their routes, number of ships, tonnage and operating company, with a total.

metadata.title: Subsidized Ship-Owners in Regard to Foreign Services
metadata.description: Lists the subsidized shipping companies, the lines each serves and the frequency of service required under their subsidies.

metadata.description: Shows the number of licensed mercantile marine officers and engineers by class of license over 1903–1906, with foreigners shown in brackets, explaining the qualifications of each class.

metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of shipwrecks for 1902–1906, split between steamers and sailing-ships and junks, with destroyed, damaged and missing vessels and totals.

metadata.description: Records the lives lost (deaths, injured, missing) in shipwrecks for 1902–1906, with the total and the number of lives rescued each year.

metadata.description: The table shows the number of Japanese and foreign pilots from 1902 to 1906, illustrating the effect of the Pilotage Law restricting pilotage to Japanese subjects.

metadata.description: Shows the share each of the four predecessor companies contributed to the common enterprise forming the Japan-China Steamship Company, totalling 8,140,000 yen.

metadata.description: A balance sheet of the mercantile marine company as at 31st March 1908, listing its liabilities and assets in yen, shown alongside the company's founding and management details.

metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of passengers and tonnage of freight carried by the railways from 1874 to 1906, showing the growth of rail traffic over the period.

metadata.description: Lists each state railway line with its open mileage, construction cost, and average construction cost per mile in 1906–7, with gross and net expense figures.

metadata.description: The table gives earnings, expenses, net profit and expense ratio for each railway group, showing the financial results of the lines by district.

metadata.description: The table breaks down each railway line's earnings from passenger cars and wagons, giving total receipts and receipts per day per mile.

metadata.description: Lists the railway lines taken over by the state, giving each line's paid-up capital, share values, construction cost, purchase price, loans, reserves and bond compensation per share.

metadata.title: Private Railways in 1906-7
metadata.description: Lists the private railway companies of Japan in 1906-7 with their open mileage, paid-up capital, construction cost and head office location.

metadata.title: Receipts and Expenses in 1906-7
metadata.description: Shows passenger and wagon receipts of each private railway company in 1906-7, both totals and receipts per day per mile.

metadata.description: Gives the Government railways' passenger fares per mile by distance band and class, in sen, as part of the note on railway tariffs.

metadata.title: Goods Tariff Rate per Mile per Ton
metadata.caption: (per ton)
metadata.description: Shows the Government and former private railways' goods freight rates per mile per ton, in rin, by goods grade, treasure and terminal charges.

metadata.description: Shows the free luggage allowance by class on Government and former Nippon railways, with delivery charges for luggage within about four miles of the station.

metadata.description: Gives the parcel charges in sen by weight and by distance band, with an extra charge for each additional 5 kin.

metadata.description: Lists the railway companies whose lines had recently been opened for service, with the paid-up capital of each and the combined total.

metadata.description: Compares the quantity and value of raw and cured marine products from 1901 to 1906, showing the fisheries output on which the country relied.

metadata.description: Records annual output of gold, gold dust, coal and sulphur from 1901 to 1906 as the principal mineral products of Japan.

metadata.description: Shows the number of male and female opium smokers in Formosa by year, with totals and the proportion per 100 population.

metadata.description: Gives the number of buildings and treasures designated as national treasures year by year from 1897 to 1910, with a grand total.

metadata.title: Expenditure for the Department of Education (1910-11)
metadata.description: Shows the annual expenses of the Department of Education and its attached committees and observatories for fiscal 1910-11, itemised from ordinary and extraordinary outlays down to the grand total.

metadata.title: General Statistics on Education
metadata.description: The table gives figures for schools, instructors, students and graduates of each kind of education in Japan over three school years, 1906-7 to 1908-9.

metadata.title: Foreign Instructors at the Institutions Under Direct Control of the Department of Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign instructors by nationality at government-controlled institutions and their annual salary totals for 1906-7 to 1908-9.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Lists the subjects taught in each of the four school years of the ordinary elementary course, with weekly hours for each subject.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools (Continued) and Higher Elementary Schools
metadata.description: The page gives the weekly hours allotted to each subject across the Fifth and Sixth years of ordinary elementary schools and the First and Second years of higher elementary schools.

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age
metadata.description: The table gives the number of children of school age by year, sex and whether they were receiving prescribed instruction, with school attendance ratios, showing the expansion of compulsory schooling.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers of Both Sexes in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: The table shows average, minimum and maximum monthly salaries of public elementary school teachers for five years, illustrating salary trends in the teaching profession.

metadata.title: [Primary School Fees, 1906–1909]
metadata.description: Shows how many primary schools charged fees and how many pupils paid, paid in part, or were exempt in 1906–1909, explaining the rise in fee-collecting schools.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens, 1906–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the number of kindergartens, their conductors and infants enrolled in 1906–1909, showing growth in early childhood education.

metadata.title: The Curriculum of the Middle School
metadata.description: Shows the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each of the five years of the middle school course, with totals.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Middle Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of public and private middle schools, their instructors, pupils and graduates for three successive school years, 1906–7 to 1908–9.

metadata.title: Graduates and Subsequent Careers
metadata.caption: Careers as reported within the year after the graduation are:—
metadata.description: Shows what graduates of the schools went on to do within a year of graduating, for three successive school years, with deaths included. It precedes the note on leaving school unfinished.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Girls' High Schools
metadata.description: Gives the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each of the four years of the girls' high school course, explaining the curriculum described in the text beside it.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Girl's High Schools
metadata.description: Statistics of public and private girls' high schools by school numbers, staff, pupils, graduates, unfinished-course leavers and admission rates for 1906-7 to 1908-9.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the First Section of the High School
metadata.description: The weekly teaching hours for each subject in the three years of the first section of the high school course, showing the curriculum structure described in the surrounding text.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Third Section of the High School
metadata.caption: Preparatory to the College of Medicine
metadata.description: This table sets out the weekly hours per subject for the third section of the High School, a preparatory course for the College of Medicine.

metadata.title: [Higher Schools: Instructors, Students, Graduates, Applicants and Enrolment, 1906-7 to 1908-9]
metadata.description: Shows the staff, student numbers, graduates, applicants and enrolment at the eight government higher schools for the last three school years.

metadata.title: [Applicants for Admission and Percentage of Admission by Section, 1907-8 and 1908-9]
metadata.description: Breaks down applicants for admission to the higher schools by section and the percentage admitted in each section for the two years.

metadata.title: Male Students Classified by Occupation of Parents (%)
metadata.description: Shows the occupational background of male students by parents' occupation for three academic years, followed by a sex breakdown of students and graduates.

metadata.title: [Male and Female Students and Graduates]
metadata.description: Gives the number of male and female students and graduates for three years, classified by sex, as a follow-on to the occupation figures.

metadata.title: Statistics of Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: Compares the staff, student numbers, graduates, applicants and admissions at the Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools over three years.

metadata.title: Statistics Relating to the Imperial University of Tokyo
metadata.description: Shows the faculty numbers, student body, graduates, applicants and matriculants of each hall and college of the Imperial University of Tokyo for 1906–7 to 1908–9.

metadata.title: [Average Age of Those Matriculated in 1908–9]
metadata.description: Gives the average age of students matriculated in 1908–9 in each college of the Imperial University of Tokyo, listed beside the description of the university's courses.

metadata.title: [Average Ages of Students Enrolled in 1908-9]
metadata.description: The text states that the average ages of students enrolled in 1908-9 are shown in the following table, one figure per college.

metadata.title: [Professors, Students, Graduates and Admissions at the University Hall and Colleges]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of professors, students, graduates, applicants and matriculants for each hall and college, with totals for three successive years.

metadata.title: [Sapporo Agricultural College Enrolment and Graduates]
metadata.description: The table gives yearly figures for Sapporo Agricultural College, the only college then existing for the Imperial North-Eastern University, covering professors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolments.

metadata.title: [Nautical School Students and Graduates]
metadata.description: Gives the number of students and graduates of the Nautical School at Tokyo for three years, split into navigation and marine engineering courses.

metadata.title: [Morioka Higher School of Agriculture and Forestry Staff, Students and Graduates]
metadata.description: Shows instructors, students, graduates, and admission applicants and admissions for the Morioka Higher School of Agriculture and Forestry over three years.

metadata.title: Statistic of the Higher Commercial Schools
metadata.description: Statistics of the higher commercial schools at Tokyo, Kobe, Yamaguchi and Nagasaki, giving staff, students, graduates, applicants and admissions over four academic years.

metadata.title: Professions Pursued by Graduates of Tokyo Higher Com. School
metadata.description: Shows where Tokyo Higher Commercial School graduates went after leaving school, by profession, for three academic years.

metadata.title: Statistics of the Higher Technical Schools
metadata.description: The table gives yearly statistics of teaching staff, students, graduates, applicants and admissions at the higher technical schools in Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, Nagoya and Kumamoto, as described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Number of Students in Fishery Schools]
metadata.description: Shows the number of students enrolled in the fishery course, marine industry and pisciculture at the fishery institution from 1906 to 1908, with totals, alongside a note on school accommodation.

metadata.title: Institutes for Training Teachers of Technical Education
metadata.description: Gives student, graduate, applicant and admission numbers for the three government teacher-training institutes for technical education over three school years.

metadata.title: Public and Private Technical Schools
metadata.description: Summarises the number of public and private technical schools, their instructors, pupils and graduates for three school years, covering industrial, agricultural, commercial and aquatic schools.

metadata.title: Special Schools of Medicine
metadata.description: Shows instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admissions for the special medical schools at Chiba, Sendai, Okayama, Kanazawa and Nagasaki, with totals for three years.

metadata.title: The Tokyo Foreign Language School
metadata.description: Gives instructor, student, graduate and admission figures for the Tokyo Foreign Language School over three years, after describing its courses of study.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Fine Art Academy: Instructors, Students and Graduates]
metadata.description: Shows the instructors, students, graduates and early leavers of the Tokyo Fine Art Academy over three academic years, illustrating the institution's size and attrition.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Academy of Music: Instructors, Students and Graduates]
metadata.description: Gives instructor, student and graduate numbers of the Tokyo Academy of Music for three years, together with the share of students leaving before graduation.

metadata.title: Blind and Deaf and Dumb School
metadata.description: Shows the number of blind and mute children of school age, by sex, and how many attended school, with the defectives per 1,000 normal children of the same age.

metadata.title: Public and Private Blind and Deaf and Dumb Schools
metadata.description: Summarises the numbers of schools, teachers, pupils and graduates for blind and deaf-and-dumb education, ordinary and professional, over three school years.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Blind and Deaf and Dumb School Statistics]
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for the Tokyo Blind and Deaf and Dumb School, covering staff, pupils, teacher-training course, graduates and admissions.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Collegiate Institutions
metadata.description: Summarises the enrolment and graduate numbers of public and private collegiate institutions by subject for three academic years, 1906–7 to 1908–9.

metadata.title: [Public and Private Collegiate Institutions: Name, Locality, Founding Year and Subjects Taught]
metadata.description: Lists the public and private collegiate institutions with their locality, founding year and subjects taught, as a companion to the statistics above.

metadata.title: [Statistics of the Meiji Gakuin, July 1910]
metadata.description: Statistics returned in July 1910 for the Meiji Gakuin, giving the number of students and alumni in each of its departments.

metadata.title: License for Secondary Schools
metadata.description: Shows teacher license applications and grants for secondary schools over three years, supplementing the staff of qualified teachers for secondary-grade schools, normal schools and middle schools.

metadata.title: License for Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows teacher license applications and grants for elementary schools over three years, with the ratio of licenses granted to applications.

metadata.title: [Existing Sum, Loans, Bonds and Deposits]
metadata.description: Shows the existing sum, loans, bonds and deposits of a fund for the three fiscal years 1906–9, continuing from the previous page's table.

metadata.title: Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers
metadata.description: Gives the receipts of the super-stipend fund for teachers by source for three years, from State aid, provincial contributions, interest and balances brought forward.

metadata.title: [Disbursements from the Super-Stipend Fund]
metadata.description: Shows how the super-stipend fund was disbursed each year, split between additional allowances to teachers and the amount carried to the next account.

metadata.title: State Aid for Promoting Technical Education
metadata.description: Lists the number of low-grade technical, agricultural, fishery, commercial and navigation schools aided by the State and the total aid given, for 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid Out of Provincial and Communal Treasuries
metadata.description: Shows educational expenses paid from provincial and communal treasuries by school type over four fiscal years, showing rising spending on schools from 1905–6 to 1908–9.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Gives the physical condition, including constitution and eyesight, of male students examined in government institutions over three years as part of school hygiene.

metadata.title: Health in Public and Private Schools of Secondary and Elementary Education
metadata.description: Gives the health returns (constitution and eyesight) for boys and girls in secondary and elementary schools, with yearly totals for 1906-7 to 1908-9.

metadata.title: [Ryugakusei Sent Abroad by the Department of Education, 1904-5 to 1908-9]
metadata.description: The table shows how many government-sponsored ryugakusei (students studying abroad) the Department of Education despatched each year, and what became of them, with females marked by asterisks.

metadata.title: Condition of Graduates of Higher Schools for Girls
metadata.description: Shows the classified condition after graduation of girls leaving higher schools for girls in three successive years, illustrating how few marry compared with those who continue study or work.

metadata.title: Subsequent Career of Graduates of the Japan Woman's University
metadata.description: Gives the subsequent careers of the 386 graduates of the Japan Woman's University (private) up to 1906, showing the largest share married.

metadata.title: [Imperial Library Statistics]
metadata.description: Shows the Imperial Library's holdings, opening days, and visitor numbers for three years, illustrating how small it is compared with Western national libraries.

metadata.title: [University Libraries Holdings]
metadata.description: Gives the volume counts of the Imperial University libraries at Tokyo and Kyoto in 1908-9, showing the university libraries surpassing the Imperial Library.

metadata.title: [Public and Private Libraries Statistics]
metadata.description: Summarises the number of public and private libraries, their volumes, opening days, and visitors for three years, showing a far poorer provision than the government libraries.

metadata.title: [Articles Displayed in the Museum at End of 1908]
metadata.description: The text states that the articles displayed in the museum were returned at the end of 1908, and this list gives the count of each class of exhibit.

metadata.title: [Output of Books, 1906–1908]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of books from 1906 to 1908, split into original works and translations, to illustrate the recent growth of publishing.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of publications from 1904 to 1908 by category, with totals and transfers, supporting the discussion of what kinds of books were published.

metadata.title: Censorship
metadata.description: Shows the number of publications whose sale was forbidden or copies seized, and plates seized, for public order and public morals reasons from 1904 to 1908, as censorship cases excluded from the prose discussion of press regulation.

metadata.title: Press Statistics
metadata.description: The returns give the number of dailies and periodicals existing at the end of each of the five latest years available, showing the growth of the press.

metadata.title: Shrines and Ministers
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of Shinto shrines by grade (Ise, state, national, provincial, communal, village, ungraded) and the number of shrine ministers, 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Buddhist Temples and Priests
metadata.caption: Sects possessing over 1,000 temples are as follows:
metadata.description: The table gives the number of temples held by the larger Buddhist sects from 1904 onward, illustrating the Buddhist temple establishment discussed in the surrounding text on sects.

metadata.title: [Priests Statistics, 1904–1908]
metadata.description: A multi-column statistical table of priests by year from 1904 to 1908, placed under the religious heading and preceding the account of Christianity in Japan.

metadata.title: Statistics of Churches in Japan (1909)
metadata.description: Gives 1909 counts of Protestant, Roman Catholic and Russo-Greek churches in Japan, covering churches, missionaries, ministers, membership, schools and welfare institutions.

metadata.title: Relief Fund
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly local apportionments, proceeds, State aids, disbursements and existing balance of the Relief Fund for 1903-4 to 1907-8.

metadata.title: Paupers and Foundlings Supported by the State
metadata.description: Gives the number of paupers supported at State expense and the amounts paid by the State, with foundling numbers and expenses, at the end of each year from 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Number of Members
metadata.description: Shows the growth of Red Cross Society membership in Japan from 1877 to 1909, illustrating the society's steady expansion described in the text.

metadata.title: [Membership, Expense, Receipt and Fund of the Women's Patriotic Society]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of the Women's Patriotic Society's membership, expenses, receipts and funds from 1907 to 1909, illustrating the success the author describes.

metadata.title: [Occupations of Boys Admitted to the Tokyo Reformatory]
metadata.description: The Tokyo Reformatory has reformed 440 boys since 1885, and this list gives the previous occupations of those boys.

metadata.title: List of Charity Institutions
metadata.description: The list names other principal charity institutions in Japan besides those described above, giving each one's religious affiliation and locality, with asterisked bodies receiving state gifts.

metadata.title: [Membership of Kodo-kwan, 1882–1910]
metadata.description: The table gives the growth in membership of the Kodo-kwan jujitsu training hall from 1882 to March 1910, shown alongside the text on the spread of the discipline.

metadata.title: [Physical Particulars of Tokyo Wrestlers by Camp]
metadata.description: The table lists the age, weight, height and chest measurements of the famous Tokyo wrestlers of the east and west camps, illustrating the physiques of professional sumo wrestlers.

metadata.title: Stamps in Civil Suits
metadata.description: Gives the stamp duty payable on civil suits according to the value of the object of the suit, shown in two side-by-side scales with notes on additions and appeals.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts, at End of 1909
metadata.description: Shows the number of courts, judges and procurators in each court tier at the end of 1909, with a 1908 comparison row.

metadata.title: No. of Cases during 1909
metadata.description: Gives the 1909 case numbers and monthly averages per court and per judge for the Supreme and Appeal Courts.

metadata.title: No. of Cases at District and Local Courts during 1909
metadata.description: Breaks down 1909 case numbers and monthly averages per court and per judge for the district and local courts under each Appeal Court jurisdiction.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Court of Cassation
metadata.description: Shows civil cases pending and disposed of at the Court of Cassation over the years 1904 to 1907.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Court of Cassation
metadata.description: Lists the number of cases involving foreign parties at the Court of Cassation by nationality of party and their outcomes, for 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Appeal Courts
metadata.caption: Of the two figures for each year the upper represent appeals from the District Courts and the lower those from the Local Courts for which the decision of the Appeal Courts is final.
metadata.description: Shows civil appeal cases at the Appeal Courts for 1904 to 1907, split between appeals from District Courts and from Local Courts, with cases in hand and disposed of.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Appeal Courts
metadata.caption: Appeals coming from the District Courts
metadata.description: Lists aliens' appeals decided at the Appeal Courts for 1904 to 1907 by nationality of appellant and by outcome: rejected, non-suited or quashed, or withdrawn.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the District Courts
metadata.description: Gives the civil case load of the District Courts for 1904 to 1907: total cases, cases disposed of, cases remaining, and new cases per 10,000 population.

metadata.title: [Cases Involving Aliens at the District Courts]
metadata.caption: Of the above cases those affecting aliens are as follows:—
metadata.description: Breaks down the District Court cases affecting aliens for 1904 to 1907 by nationality of the party, with the number of such cases disposed of.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the District Courts
metadata.description: Shows the number of cases heard at the district courts from 1904 to 1907, broken down by the nature of the dispute.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Local Courts
metadata.description: Gives the civil case totals at the local courts for 1904 to 1907, including cases disposed of, cases pending and new cases per 1,000 population.

metadata.title: [Civil Cases Affecting Aliens by Nationality of Party]
metadata.description: Lists the cases affecting foreigners at the local courts, by nationality of the party, with the number of cases disposed of in each year.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the Local Courts
metadata.description: Breaks down the local court cases for 1904 to 1907 by the nature of the dispute, with money matters the largest category.

metadata.title: Law Suits of Money Matters at the First Instance Classified
metadata.description: Classifies money lawsuits at the first instance by the amount claimed, with case counts and total sums in money for 1904 to 1907.

metadata.title: Cases of Conciliation Dealt with at the District Courts
metadata.description: Shows the number of conciliation cases handled at the district courts from 1904 to 1907 and how each case was resolved or left pending.

metadata.title: Nature of Conciliation Cases
metadata.description: Breaks down the conciliation cases of 1904 to 1907 by their subject matter, such as personal, land, money and goods.

metadata.title: Cases of Insolvency and No. of Persons Affected
metadata.caption: Cases of Rehabilitation of Civil Rights
metadata.description: Gives the number of insolvency cases with the debtors, creditors and credit involved, and the rehabilitation of civil rights cases sanctioned or rejected, for 1904 to 1907.

metadata.title: Criminal Defendants
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal defendants from 1903 to 1907 who were convicted or found not guilty, by sex, illustrating the effect of the new code on prosecutions.

metadata.title: Sentences Carried Out
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal sentences carried out in each year from 1904 to 1907, broken down by type of punishment.

metadata.title: No. of Major Criminal Cases and No. of Accused
metadata.description: Gives the total number of major criminal cases and of persons accused in them for the years 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Nature of Accusations and Number of Conviction (in 1907.)
metadata.description: Breaks down the accusations in major criminal cases of 1907 by nature of offence, showing convictions, acquittals and other outcomes.

metadata.title: [Convictions in Major Criminal Cases, 1904–1906]
metadata.description: Continues the convictions summary for earlier years, giving convicted, acquitted and other totals for 1904 to 1906.

metadata.title: Aliens as Accused
metadata.description: Lists the sentences and outcomes for foreign nationals accused in criminal cases from 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: Causes of Murder Classified
metadata.caption: (sentence in prefence of accused.)
metadata.description: Classifies murder cases by their causes, such as covetousness, adultery and enmity, for the years 1905 to 1908.

metadata.title: Personal Condition of Accused charged with Major Crimes
metadata.caption: (cases sentenced in presence of accused.)
metadata.description: The tables break down accused persons charged with major crimes by age, consort status and literacy for 1903–1907, showing the personal condition of those sentenced in the accused's presence.

metadata.title: Violation of Administrative and Taxation Rules Etc.
metadata.description: This table gives the average yearly number of prosecutions for violations of administrative and taxation rules, listing only offence categories with at least 1,000 cases.

metadata.title: Appeals to the Court of Cassation and Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Gives the number of appeals to the Court of Cassation and appeal courts in 1907, with comparative figures for 1903 to 1906 on cases dealt with, cancelled and outstanding.

metadata.title: Appeals to Appeal Courts and District Courts
metadata.description: Shows appeals to appeal courts and district courts for 1903 to 1907, with cases dealt with, non-suited or cancelled, and cases remaining in hand each year.

metadata.title: Average Number of Prison Inmates at End of Year
metadata.description: Shows the average daily number of prisoners by category each year, indicating how the prison population was composed and changed from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: New Convictions and Population
metadata.description: Gives the number of new convictions each year and their ratio to the population, showing how convictions relate to population size.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified
metadata.description: Breaks down new convictions by felony (capital and other), larceny and police offence, with percentage shares and capital punishment rate per 10,000 population.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences According to Convicts
metadata.description: Shows how many convicts were first-time, repeat and multiple offenders each year, with the ratio of repeat offenders per 100 first-time offenders.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified According to Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of new convictions from 1904 to 1908 split by whether the convicted person was educated or illiterate, with percentages.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified According to Profession and Property
metadata.description: Breaks down new convictions from 1904 to 1908 by whether offenders had property or a profession, with percentages of each group.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified According to Age
metadata.description: Gives the number of new convictions by age group from 1904 to 1908, with totals and the ratio of children and minors per 100 adults.

metadata.title: Escape of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Reports the number of prison inmates who escaped from 1902 to 1906, by convict category, with an average for 1887 to 1906.

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Shows annual sickness rates and mortality among prison inmates from 1904 to 1908, giving the state of health within the prison system.

metadata.title: No. of Days Work by Prison-Inmates and Earnings
metadata.description: Gives the number of days worked by prison inmates under government and contract systems, with their earnings and the shares given to them, 1904–1908.

metadata.title: Average Yearly Earnings and Receipts per One Worker
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Lists the average yearly earnings and receipts of each prison worker for 1903–1908, shown in yen.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-Officers and Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Shows how many prison inmates each warder, turnkey and female keeper had to supervise in each year from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Revenue of Prisons
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly revenue of the prisons from 1905–6 to 1909–10, split into ordinary earnings and receipts and extraordinary revenue, with totals.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prison
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Table 14 gives the yearly expenditure of Japanese prisons, split into ordinary items (salaries, wages, inmate expenses, others) and extraordinary outlay, with totals.

metadata.title: Prison Expense per 1 Inmate
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Table 15 shows the average prison expense per inmate in yen, divided into ordinary and extraordinary costs, for each fiscal year from 1904–5 to 1908–9.

metadata.title: [Summary Judgments at Police Offices, 1909]
metadata.description: Summary of cases judged in 1909 at police offices, showing acquittals and sentences by length of detention or size of fine, illustrating the summary judgement system described in the text.

metadata.title: Police Offices and Police Force
metadata.description: Number of police offices, police officers and men, and population served per officer for each year from 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Suicides and Acts Thereof
metadata.description: Suicides by method (hanging, drowning, edged tools, fire arms, poison, others) for males and females, with totals, for 1903 to 1908.

metadata.title: Cases of Suicides of Over 200 Classified
metadata.description: Suicide cases with over 200 cases are classified by cause and sex for the years 1904 to 1908, showing the motives behind self-destruction.

metadata.title: Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.description: Rates of sufferers from robbery, larceny, peculation and fraud per 10,000 houses and population for 1904 to 1908, shown with the five-year averages.

metadata.title: Arrests Police Offences Classified of Over 200 Cases
metadata.description: Numbers of arrests for various police offences and crimes over 200 cases from 1903 to 1907, showing trends in offences such as gambling, larceny and fraud.

metadata.title: [Regulation Offences (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: The top rows continue a table of regulation offences whose header lies on the previous page, giving yearly counts of offences by regulation type.

metadata.title: The Ratio of Arrests Per 100 Offences
metadata.description: Shows, for each category of offence, how many arrests were made per 100 offences committed in each year from 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Unnatural Deaths
metadata.description: Lists yearly cases of suicide and other unnatural deaths from 1904 to 1908, with totals, to show trends in such deaths.

metadata.title: No. of Foundlings
metadata.description: Gives the number of foundlings taken in each year from 1904 to 1908, divided into boys and girls.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Records the number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, total burnt area and average damage per fire for each year from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Casualties Concerning Police Affairs
metadata.description: Shows the number of people killed and wounded in incidents concerning police duties from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Rewards with Regard to Police Administration
metadata.description: Shows the number of men receiving police rewards and the total sums of money awarded, by amount category, for the years 1905 to 1908.

metadata.title: [Convicts Under 20 Years Old by Age, November 1907]
metadata.description: Gives the number of convicts under 20 by age group in November 1907, supporting the discussion of reform houses for refractory minors.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Convicts Under 20 by Year]
metadata.description: Lists the yearly number of convicts under 20 from 1905 to 1908, presented as statistics accompanying the reform houses article.

metadata.title: Hospitals, Doctors and Mid-wives
metadata.description: Shows the number of hospitals, doctors (total and per 10,000 population) and mid-wives at the end of each year from 1903 to 1907, illustrating the medical services discussed in the text.

metadata.title: Total Vaccinations
metadata.description: Gives the total number of vaccinations recorded each year from 1903 to 1907, since vaccination was compulsory in Japan.

metadata.title: Ratio of Successful Vaccination on Persons Tried for the First Time and Second Time or Over
metadata.description: Shows the percentage of successful vaccinations among persons vaccinated for the first time and among those tried a second time or more, for 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified
metadata.caption: (Total No. and relative ratio per 1,000 deaths)
metadata.description: Shows annual deaths from major diseases from 1903 to 1907, with each disease's share expressed as a relative ratio per 1,000 total deaths.

metadata.title: Eight Epidemic Diseases and Mortality
metadata.description: Lists cases and deaths from eight epidemic diseases for 1904 to 1908, with mortality per 100 cases for each year.

metadata.title: Gross Area
metadata.description: Gives the gross area of agricultural land in Japan proper, excluding Formosa and Saghalien, divided into private, crown and state land, in cho.

metadata.title: Arable Land Classified for 1908
metadata.description: Classifies the gross arable land of Japan for 1908 into paddy fields and upland fields, giving the total in cho.

metadata.title: Margin of Reclamation
metadata.description: Shows the land inclined less than 15 degrees, the area already under tillage, and the area not yet reclaimed, by region, to indicate the remaining margin of reclamation.

metadata.title: Forests and Wild Land Converted
metadata.description: The table shows the progress of land reclamation from 1902 to 1908, giving arable land, other land, totals and Hokkaido reclamation in cho.

metadata.title: Farming Population
metadata.description: The table gives the number of farming families in 1903 and 1908 by occupation, with each group's percentage of total farming households.

metadata.title: Independent Farmers and Tenant Farmers
metadata.description: The table compares cultivated land in cho and its percentage share, for owner-cultivated and tenant-cultivated paddy-fields and upland farms, 1903–1908.

metadata.title: [Paddy and Land Areas by Year]
metadata.description: Shows the areas of various land categories in the years 1901 to 1910, the continued portion of a table, to illustrate changes in cultivated and built land.

metadata.title: Rate per "Tsubo" (6×5 ft.) for Urban Dwelling-Land
metadata.description: Gives official value, annual rent and market value per tsubo of urban dwelling-land in selected prefectures and on average for Japan proper, from Treasury investigations.

metadata.title: Rate per "Tsubo" for Rural Dwelling-Land
metadata.description: Gives official value, annual rent and market value per tsubo of rural dwelling-land in selected prefectures and on average for Japan proper, from Treasury investigations.

metadata.title: Average Yield per Tan of Paddy-fields
metadata.description: Shows the average yield per tan of paddy-fields in five-year periods and over twenty years ending 1906, illustrating gradual improvement in productive power.

metadata.title: Increase of Tillage Area in Old Japan
metadata.description: Compares average annual increases in paddy-field, upland-farm and total tillage area for two periods, showing upland farms expanded faster than paddy-fields.

metadata.title: [Rate of Increase and Average Annual Rate]
metadata.description: The top of the page carries the closing rows of a continued table giving rates of increase and average annual rates; the column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Transfer of Ownership of Land
metadata.caption: Shewing Number of Items
metadata.description: Shows the number of land ownership transfers by purchase, pledge and mortgage, owing to petty subdivision of farming lots, from the latest Finance Department returns.

metadata.title: Average Area per One Farmer's Family
metadata.description: Gives the average farm area per farmer's family in several divisions, split into farmland, moors and total, following the statement about Main Island averages.

metadata.title: Ratio of One-Crop and Two-Crop Farms
metadata.description: The official returns show the ratio of one-crop and two-crop paddy fields in the recent years, given in cho and as percentages for 1903 and 1908.

metadata.title: Human Labor and Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.description: The area of land tilled by cattle or horse labor (1st kind) and that tilled exclusively by hands (2nd kind) is shown in cho and percentages for 1903 and 1908.

metadata.title: [Projects Sanctioned and Area Adjusted, 1900-1909]
metadata.description: Shows the number of land readjustment projects sanctioned and the area adjusted each year from 1900 to 1909, illustrating the progress of the work the Japan Hypothec Bank and authorities supported.

metadata.title: Export, Import and Sale of Home Production
metadata.description: Gives the export, import and domestic sale figures for fertilizer and manure from 1906 to 1908, set against the estimated yearly manure consumption described in the text.

metadata.title: Rice (in 1,000)
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows rice area, production, yield and export and import quantities and values for 1904–1909 with a normal-yield average, illustrating Japan's rice farming output and trade.

metadata.title: [Yield per Tan of Early, Middle and Late Rice Varieties]
metadata.description: Gives the average yield per tan at Government Experimental Farms for early, middle and late rice varieties, showing the middle variety is most productive.

metadata.title: Consumption and Price of Rice
metadata.caption: Per capita consumption is 1 koku. The average price of per koku is shown below:
metadata.description: Shows the average price per koku of clean rice in Tokyo and of rice exported and imported, from 1887–96 average through 1909.

metadata.title: [Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat Production, 1904-1909]
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: Barley, naked barley and wheat are the staple upland crops and are also grown as second crops after rice, so their annual output is shown here for 1904 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat Cultivation by Field Type, 1909]
metadata.description: The text explains that barley, naked barley and wheat are compared for 1909 between paddy-fields and upland farms, showing where each crop is grown.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: Millets and other miscellaneous grains are grown in mountainous districts and as rice substitutes, and this table gives their yearly production from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Beans, Sweet Potato and Potato
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: Shows annual production of soy beans, red beans, horse beans, peas, sweet potatoes, potatoes and peanuts, as part of the discussion of subsidiary farm crops.

metadata.title: Some Special Crops
metadata.caption: (in Kwan)
metadata.description: Lists yearly output of indigo, tobacco, cotton, hemp and rape seed, the special crops mentioned alongside the discussion of subsidiary farm produce.

metadata.title: Other Minor Crops
metadata.description: Gives the cultivated area and annual output of various minor crops, such as radish, ginger, lily and rush, following the discussion of leaf-tobacco and other crops.

metadata.title: Mulberry Fields and No. of Sericulturists in Japan
metadata.description: Shows mulberry field area and the number of households engaged in sericulture for 1903–1909, supporting the discussion of silk production.

metadata.title: Output of Cocoons
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly cocoon output by weight in koku, broken down into double, pierced and waste cocoons, with output per egg card, for 1905–1909.

metadata.title: Cocoons by Season
metadata.caption: (1000 koku)
metadata.description: Breaks down cocoon production by season (spring, summer, autumn) with totals and seasonal percentages for 1904–1909.

metadata.title: Output of Raw Silk
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of raw silk, waste silk, floss silk and silkworm eggs from 1900 to 1909, illustrating the growth of sericulture.

metadata.title: Production in 1909
metadata.description: Gives the 1909 production totals of raw silk and its by-products by quantity (kwan) and value (yen) across all establishments.

metadata.title: [Output of Filature, Frame and Tama Silk in 1909]
metadata.caption: (in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1909 output of filature, frame and tama (doupion) silk by raw silk, noshi, kibiso and waste, in quantity and value.

metadata.title: Export of Shinshu Filature No. 1 by Kind and Highest Quotation at Yokohama
metadata.caption: in 1,000 kin by kind and highest quotation (in Yen) of Shinshu Filature No. 1 per 100 kin at Yokohama
metadata.description: Shows the export volumes of Shinshu filature silk by grade and the highest Yokohama quotation for 1908 and 1909.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Raw Silk Production
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures for raw silk production with families engaged in 1908 and the value of production in 1907 and 1908.

metadata.title: Import (from China)
metadata.description: Shows Chinese imports of ordinary cocoons and tussah silk by quantity and value for 1904 to 1909, illustrating the trade flows behind the silk industry discussed on the page.

metadata.title: Silk Conditioning
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for silk conditioning at the Yokohama Silk Conditioning House, covering numbers of lots, weights, average loss, weighing, boil-off and quality tests, 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Japanese and Foreign Exporters of Raw Silk
metadata.description: Compares total raw silk bales exported by Japanese and foreign firms, with percentage shares, 1904 to 1909, to show the growing part played by Japanese exporters.
