metadata.title: Area of Tea Plantations and Number of Manufacturers
metadata.description: Shows the tea-growing area and the number of tea manufacturers in Japan for 1904 to 1909, supporting the discussion of tea production.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Tea
metadata.description: Gives the annual output in kwan of each grade of green tea, black tea and oolong, with the total, from 1904 to 1909.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1909)
metadata.description: Lists the six leading tea-producing districts in 1909 with their output in kwan and value in yen.

metadata.title: Export of Teas
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of Japanese tea exports for 1902–1909, illustrating the difficulty Japanese teas face in extending foreign markets after the export subsidy ended.

metadata.title: Destination of Green Tea Exported
metadata.description: Gives the annual value of green tea exports from Japan by destination (U.S.A., Canada, China and others) for 1904–1909, showing the main overseas markets.

metadata.title: [Castration Records of Horses, 1905-1907]
metadata.description: Castration records for horses, showing the number castrated, horses disabled or dead, grants paid and compensation, to illustrate the case for possible compulsory castration measures.

metadata.title: Number of Horses in Japan
metadata.description: Statistics of the horse population in Japan from 1904 to 1908, broken down by domestic, cross-bred and foreign horses, with totals, foalings and deaths.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of cattle in Japan by native, cross and foreign breeds, with totals, calvings and deaths, to show livestock trends in the period.

metadata.title: Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Lists the yearly numbers of sheep, goats and swine in Japan, presented alongside the cattle statistics in the agriculture section.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Shows yearly slaughter-house numbers and the animals slaughtered (cattle and calves, horses, sheep and goats, swine), illustrating the meat trade in Japan.

metadata.title: Leading Stock Farms
metadata.description: Listing the leading government and private stock farms in Japan, mainly in Hokkaido, with their location, kind of stock or farming, and ownership, following the introductory note on stock farming.

metadata.title: Number of Households Keeping Poultry
metadata.description: Gives the national totals of households keeping poultry and of fowls, ducks and eggs for 1907 and 1908, showing the poultry industry's scale.

metadata.title: Leading Poultry Districts in 1908
metadata.description: Lists the five leading prefectures for poultry keeping in 1908, with household numbers and the value of fowls and eggs.

metadata.title: Leading Dairy Districts in 1908
metadata.description: Shows the four leading dairy districts in 1908, with the number of dairies, milk cows, and milk output in koku and yen.

metadata.title: [Prefecture Figures, Continued From Previous Page]
metadata.description: Continuation of a prefectural statistics table giving four figure columns for several prefectures, the national total, and the figures for 1907 and 1906.

metadata.title: Animal Epidemics
metadata.description: Shows annual counts of glanders, anthrax and rinderpest cases and deaths or slaughter among horses and cattle in Japan from 1903 to 1909.

metadata.title: Fruits in 1906-8
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives the number of fruit trees and the yield of the main fruit kinds in Japan for 1906 to 1908, illustrating the growth of horticulture described in the text.

metadata.title: Output of Principal Fruit Districts
metadata.caption: (Output in Koku)
metadata.description: The page lists the output in koku of principal fruit districts, showing where each fruit is grown most heavily in Japan.

metadata.title: Exports of Fruits and Vegetables
metadata.caption: (Value in Yen)
metadata.description: The value of fruit and vegetable exports is shown year by year from 1903 to 1909, indicating the growth of this trade.

metadata.title: Sale of State Land in Hokkaido
metadata.description: The table gives the area limits and prices per cho at which an individual may buy State land in Hokkaido, by purpose.

metadata.title: Time Limit for Work on Land Purchased or Leased in Hokkaido
metadata.description: The table sets the time limits within which work must be finished on land bought or leased from the State, according to lot size.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.description: The strata existing in Japan are classified by relative percentage, separating sedimentary rocks (by geological era) from igneous rocks (old and young periods), with subtotals and a grand total of 100.

metadata.title: Mineral Productions: Gold, Silver, Copper and Lead
metadata.caption: Momme=2.411 drachms. Kin=1.607 lbs. (Troy). Kwan=10.047 lbs. (Troy). Koku=39.703 gallons.
metadata.description: Gives annual quantities and values of Japan's gold, silver, copper and lead output from 1902 to 1909, excluding Formosa.

metadata.title: Mineral Productions: Iron, Iron Pyrites, Antimony and Manganese
metadata.caption: Momme=2.411 drachms. Kin=1.607 lbs. (Troy). Kwan=10.047 lbs. (Troy). Koku=39.703 gallons.
metadata.description: Shows annual output quantities and values of iron, iron pyrites, antimony and manganese in Japan from 1902 to 1909.

metadata.title: Mineral Productions: Coal, Sulphur, Petroleum, Others and Total
metadata.caption: Momme=2.411 drachms. Kin=1.607 lbs. (Troy). Kwan=10.047 lbs. (Troy). Koku=39.703 gallons.
metadata.description: Shows annual output quantities and values of coal, sulphur and petroleum, plus other minerals and total mineral value in Japan from 1902 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Yamagano Gold Mine Production, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the annual gold and silver output of the Yamagano Gold Mine, described just above, for 1907 to 1909.

metadata.title: Ushio and Oguchi Gold Mines
metadata.description: Shows recent gold and silver production of the Ushio and Oguchi gold mines, which are located close together and both worked by companies.

metadata.title: [Sado Mine Gold, Silver and Copper Output, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: The table gives the annual gold, silver and copper output of the Sado mine for 1907 to 1909, supporting the description of this long-worked island mine.

metadata.title: Kosaka Copper Mine
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output of gold, silver and copper at the Kosaka copper mine for 1907 to 1909, following the description of the mine's situation and ore.

metadata.title: Ashio Copper Mine
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output of gold, silver and copper at the Ashio copper mine for 1907 to 1909, which is described as one of Japan's oldest and most important copper mines.

metadata.title: [Besshi Copper Mine Output, 1907-1909]
metadata.description: Gives the silver and copper output of the Besshi Copper Mine for 1907 to 1909, illustrating the mine's present prosperity described in the text.

metadata.title: [Iron and Iron Mines Copper Output, 1907-1909]
metadata.description: Lists copper output figures for 1907 to 1909 printed under the Iron and Iron Mines heading, accompanying the discussion of Japan's iron production.

metadata.title: Injurious Ingredients
metadata.caption: (per 100 ores.)
metadata.description: Chemical analysis of Kamaishi and Taiya ores and Hokkaido sand iron, showing the harmful phosphorus, sulphur and copper content that makes the sand iron suitable for melting.

metadata.title: [Gold, Copper and Iron Output, 1907-1909]
metadata.description: Annual output of gold, copper and iron at the Kamaishi mine for 1907 to 1909, illustrating the mine's production as the most important iron mine in Japan.

metadata.title: Other Metallic Mines
metadata.caption: (Figures for 1909)
metadata.description: Lists the principal other metallic mines with their gold, silver and copper output for 1909 and the firms working them.

metadata.title: Analysis of Coals from the Principal Coal-Fields
metadata.description: The table gives water, volatile matter, coke, ash, sulphur, caking behaviour, specific gravity and calorific power for coals from the principal Japanese coal-fields, as analysed.

metadata.title: [Coal Output of Hokkaido Collieries, 1908–1909]
metadata.description: Shows coal output of the principal Hokkaido collieries for 1909 and 1908, supporting the preceding survey of the island's coal-fields.

metadata.title: [Coal Output of Honshu, 1908–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the total coal output of Honshu for 1908 and 1909, following the description of the Iwaki-Hitachi coal-field and its collieries.

metadata.title: Other Principal Coal Mines in Chiku-Ho District and Saga and Nagasaki
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 metric tons.)
metadata.description: Lists the production of the other principal coal mines of the Chiku-Ho district and Saga and Nagasaki for 1909 and 1908, with their owners.

metadata.title: [Miike Coal Production]
metadata.description: Gives the annual coal output of the Miike coal-field for 1908 and 1909 in metric tons, following the description of the field.

metadata.title: [Baumé and Price of Crude Oil by Oil-Field]
metadata.description: Baumé gravity and price per koku of crude oil from the main Echigo oil-fields, given to show the quality difference between fields.

metadata.title: [Output of Principal Echigo Oil-Fields]
metadata.description: Output of the principal oil-fields in 1909 and 1908 and their share of Japan's total crude oil production, shown to indicate the fields' relative importance.

metadata.title: [Production of Echigo Fields by Classification]
metadata.caption: (in koku)
metadata.description: Annual Echigo crude-oil production split into volatile, lamp, solar and heavy-and-lubricant oil grades for 1908 and 1909.

metadata.title: [Relative Percentage of Crude Oil Productions]
metadata.description: Share of each oil grade in total crude oil output for 1907 and 1908, showing how the product mix shifted.

metadata.title: [Wells Existing at End of 1908]
metadata.description: Number of wells of each type working in the main Echigo oil-fields at the end of 1908.

metadata.title: Number of Mine-Workers at Principal Mines
metadata.caption: (At the end of June.)
metadata.description: Gives the number of mine-workers at principal mines by type of mine (metal, coal, non-metal) and alluvial diggers for 1903 to 1908, illustrating the growth of the mining labour force.

metadata.title: Work and Wages of Mine-Workers
metadata.description: Based on Mining Bureau research, this table sets out the monthly working days and average daily hours of various mine-worker groups in metal mines and collieries.

metadata.title: Wages (in Yen) at Metal-Mines
metadata.description: Shows the maximum and minimum daily wages in yen for male and female mine-workers in metal mines, as tabulated from Mining Bureau research.

metadata.title: [Wages at Mines (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top rows continue a wage table for mine workers whose column headings appear on the previous page; the paired figures give wage rates in yen.

metadata.title: Wages at Collieries (Yen)
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Gives maximum and minimum daily wages in yen for male and female workers of various grades at collieries.

metadata.title: Accidents in the Mines
metadata.description: Lists the number of mining accidents from 1903 to 1909 with their outcomes: deaths, severe injuries, other injuries and totals.

metadata.title: Imports and Export Mineral Productions
metadata.caption: Export (in 1,000): Copper (kin), Coal (ton), Sulphur (kin); Imports (in 1,000): Iron & Steel (Long ton), Petroleum (Gal.)
metadata.description: Shows yearly export quantities of copper, coal and sulphur and import quantities of iron and steel and petroleum, 1904 to 1909, with the total trade value for 1909 noted below.

metadata.title: [Fishing-Boats by Year, 1904–1908]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of fishing-boats in Japan from 1904 to 1908, split into total, newly built, worn-out and European-style boats, supporting the discussion of the fishing fleet.

metadata.title: Accidents to Fishing-Boats and Casualties to Fishermen
metadata.description: Gives the number of fishing boats accidentally wrecked, drifted, missing, upset or otherwise lost, with the resulting crew casualties, for 1908 and 1907.

metadata.title: The Value of Catches and of Marine Products
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of fish catches and of marine products from 1903 to 1908, indicating the growth of the fishing industry.

metadata.title: Value of Catch and Commercial Value of Principal Kinds of Fish, Shell-Fish, etc. in 1908
metadata.description: Lists the catch quantity and commercial value of the principal fish and shell-fish kinds in 1908.

metadata.title: Principal Kinds of Manufactured Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the quantity and value of the main kinds of manufactured marine products, such as dried and salted fish and fertilizers.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Catches and Marine Production (1908)
metadata.description: Ranks the leading prefectures by the value of their fish catches and marine production in 1908, showing where Japan's fishing wealth was concentrated.

metadata.title: Aquiculture
metadata.description: Gives the value of Japanese aquiculture products by species from 1904 to 1908, with the miscellaneous 'Others' category and totals, alongside a note on pearl-oyster culture.

metadata.title: [Deep-Sea Fishery Vessels, Crew and Value, 1905–1908]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of deep-sea fishery from 1905 to 1908 in junks, sailers, steamers, crew, tonnage and value, illustrating the development encouraged by State aid.

metadata.title: [Deep-Sea Fishery Returns by Branch, 1908]
metadata.description: Gives the 1908 deep-sea fishery returns for Japan proper, broken down by fishing branch, showing vessels, crew and value.

metadata.title: [Sealing Returns, 1908 and 1909]
metadata.description: Shows the number of seals and otters taken in the sealing enterprise in 1908 and 1909, illustrating the industry's development after state bounty was withdrawn.

metadata.title: [Salt Production, 1903-1908]
metadata.description: Salt production statistics for 1903 to 1908, giving salt fields area, furnace numbers, output, value and average price, illustrating the industry described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: Marine Products in Foreign Trade
metadata.description: Values of marine products in foreign trade, exports and imports in yen with totals for selected years, showing their importance relative to mineral products.

metadata.title: Area of Forests
metadata.caption: (1 cho = 2½ acres) (At the end of 1908)
metadata.description: The table gives the area of Japan's forests by ownership at the end of 1908, split into protection, utilization and percentage forests, with totals for each owner class.

metadata.title: Prefectures Containing Not Less Than 500,000 Cho of Forest
metadata.caption: (Area in cho; 1 cho = about 2.45 acres)
metadata.description: The page lists the prefectures of northeastern Honshu and Hokkaido whose forest area exceeds 500,000 cho, showing the areas of forest in each.

metadata.title: Forest Yield for 1908–1909
metadata.description: The page gives the forest yield for 1908–1909 (excluding Formosa and Saghalien), showing timber and fagot quantities and values by species, to illustrate the modest revenue from forestry.

metadata.title: [Financial Yield of Forests by Ownership, 1908-9]
metadata.description: Shows the 1908-9 financial yield of forests by ownership class (State, Crown, percentage, public and private), supporting the text's calculation of yield per cho.

metadata.title: [Receipts, Expenses and Balance of State Forests, 1902-3 to 1908-9]
metadata.description: Gives the receipts, expenses and balances of State forest management for the last few years, illustrating the profit rate discussed in the text.

metadata.title: Forest Products in Foreign Trade
metadata.caption: Principal items of forest products as figuring in export and import trade are given below (in 1,000 yen).
metadata.description: Lists principal forest products (timbers, tea-chest boards, match sticks, bamboos) with total export and import values, showing foreign trade in forest goods.

metadata.title: [Rotation System of Principal Trees]
metadata.description: Lists the rotation periods, in years, for the principal trees planted in State forests under the adjustment and working plan.

metadata.title: [Working Plan Classification of State Forests]
metadata.description: Shows the intended percentage division of State forest area among high forest, coppice, coppice-with-standard and barren classes under the working plan decided in 1909.

metadata.title: Total Volume of Felling (Shakujime) and Conversion
metadata.description: Shows the State's government conversion works' total felling and conversion volumes for 1907 to 1909, for timbers and faggots.

metadata.title: Sided Logs and Charcoals (Kwamme)
metadata.description: Gives the government yards' output of sided logs (timbers) and charcoals for 1907 to 1909, with the column years taken from the table above.

metadata.title: Hewn Boards etc.
metadata.description: Records the government yards' output of hewn boards and timbers for 1907 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Private Sawing Yards by District]
metadata.description: Lists the private sawing yards in the Akita and Osaka districts, the largest in the country, by number of yards, capital, wood converted and motive power.

metadata.title: [Shooting Licenses Issued, 1902–1909]
metadata.description: The table shows the number of shooting licenses of each class issued from 1902 to 1909, illustrating the sharp fall in sportsmen after the fees were raised.

metadata.title: Progress of Industrial Investment
metadata.description: Shows the number of companies and their gross capital, paid-up capital and reserves for industrial enterprises from 1898 to 1904, illustrating the growth of industrial investment in Japan.

metadata.title: [Industrial Companies, 1905–1908 (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a yearly series for 1905–1908 whose column headings are not printed on this page, shown alongside the text on the steady growth of industrial companies after 1900.

metadata.title: Industrial Establishments Classified by Amount of Investment
metadata.description: Introducing the section on industries by investment size, this table lists the number of companies and paid-up capital for each industry with capital of 500,000 yen and above in 1907 and 1908.

metadata.title: [Industries by Number of Companies and Paid-Up Capital (Continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a table of industries with company counts and paid-up capital, whose column headings fall on the previous page; it precedes the text on industrial activities.

metadata.title: Distribution of Industries
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures with companies each having paid-up capital over 3,000,000 yen in 1908, showing company numbers and total paid-up capital.

metadata.title: Factories and its Employees
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of factories by type of power and the number of male, female and total operatives employed from 1898 to 1908.

metadata.title: [Engines and Horse Power]
metadata.description: Shows the number of engines and their horse power by type (steam, gas, petroleum, water wheel, dynamo, motor) used in Japanese factories, with extra electrical output given in the notes.

metadata.title: Kind of Factories
metadata.description: Lists the number of factories run by motors and not run by motors, and the daily average employees, across the textile, machinery, chemical and food industries.

metadata.title: [Factory Industries by Branch, Continued]
metadata.description: This page lists the number of establishments and related figures for the minor and special manufacturing industries, ending with a grand total for all industries.

metadata.title: [Cotton Spinning Output and Trade, 1893–1909]
metadata.description: The top table gives the cotton-spinning industry's average daily spindles, bale output, and export and import bales at five dates from 1893 to 1909.

metadata.title: Capital, Reserves, Operatives, Etc.
metadata.description: This table gives the number of cotton mills, their capital, profit, reserves, spindles, male and female hands and working hours for each year from 1903 to 1908.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Cotton Spinning (1903)
metadata.description: This table compares the leading cotton-spinning districts by number of mills, capital, spindles, operatives and yarn production in the stated year.

metadata.title: Leading Cotton Spinning Companies (1910, 1st Half)
metadata.description: This table lists the leading cotton-spinning companies in 1910 (first half) with their locality, paid-up capital, spindles, reserves, looms and dividends.

metadata.title: [Weaving Companies with Figures, Continued]
metadata.description: Lists weaving companies with their figures, the starred ones being encumbered with loans as itemised in the table below.

metadata.title: Companies Encumbered with Loans
metadata.caption: (at the end of I half year, 1910)
metadata.description: Shows the amount of loans encumbering each starred company at the end of the first half of 1910.

metadata.title: [Silk Export Value by Districts]
metadata.caption: Value (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: The table gives the value of silk export through the Yokohama guild by prefectural district over 1904 to 1908, supporting the discussion of the growing weaving industry.

metadata.title: Weaving Establishments' Operatives and Value of Products
metadata.description: This table shows the yearly growth in weaving houses, looms, operatives and product value from 1903 to 1908, as factory weaving expanded.

metadata.title: Leading Weaving Districts (1)
metadata.description: This table lists the leading prefectures in weaving, giving weaving houses, machine and hand looms, and operatives for each district.

metadata.title: [Leading Weaving Districts (1), Continued]
metadata.description: Continuation of the prefectural table of weaving districts, giving figures for the remaining prefectures from Miye to Yamanashi; the column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Leading Weaving Districts (2)
metadata.caption: Value (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of fabric output from the leading weaving prefectures, broken down by fabric type, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Production
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the value of annual production of each fabric type from 1903 to 1908, showing growth in silk and cotton output over the period.

metadata.title: [Movement of Machine-Construction Imports, 1905–1909]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The table shows the value of machine-construction imports such as nails, rails, irons, machines and steamships over five years, to illustrate the trade movement described in the text.

metadata.title: [Value of Machine-Construction Exports, 1906–1909]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly value of Japan's machine-construction exports, showing the scale of the export trade discussed in the accompanying text.

metadata.title: [Paper Production in 1908 by Kind of Paper]
metadata.description: The table gives the amount and value of paper produced in Japan in 1908, broken down by kind of paper, as the paper industry section introduces it.

metadata.title: [Imports of Paper and Pulp]
metadata.description: Shows the yen value of paper and pulp imported in 1906 to 1908, supporting the text's discussion of rising paper imports and the growth of pulp imports.

metadata.title: Statistic of Japanese Paper
metadata.description: Gives the number of families engaged, employees and value of the Japanese paper industry from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Leading Japanese Paper Districts
metadata.description: Lists the eight leading paper-producing prefectures in 1908 by families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: European Paper
metadata.description: Summarises the number of factories, capital, machinery, horse power, employees and output of European-style paper mills from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Leading European Paper Manufacturing Companies
metadata.caption: (of above Y. 500,000 in 1908)
metadata.description: Lists the leading European-style paper manufacturing companies capitalised above Y. 500,000 in 1908, giving their capital, machines, horsepower, staff and output value.

metadata.title: Production and Import of European Paper
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of European paper produced in Japan and the total value of imports from 1902 to 1908, shown as a comparison of domestic output with foreign supply.

metadata.title: Mats and Matting
metadata.description: Shows the number of families engaged in mat-making and the values of floor mats and export mats from 1903 to 1908, illustrating the trade's scale alongside the description of the conditioning inspection.

metadata.title: Leading Export Mat Districts
metadata.description: Compares the three leading mat-producing prefectures by families engaged, employees, looms and export mats, supporting the text's account of where the export output is concentrated.

metadata.title: Statistics on Straw and Chip Braids
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for the number of workshops, employees, value of output and chip-braid output in the straw and chip braid industry from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Leading Straw and Chip Braid Districts
metadata.description: Compares the workshops, employees and value of output in the two leading straw and chip braid districts, Kagawa and Okayama.

metadata.title: Leading Markets for Japanese Porcelains
metadata.caption: (Value Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: The text notes that U.S.A. takes more than half of Japan's porcelain exports, and this table compares the value of exports to leading markets in two years.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Statistics of enamel (Shippo) ware production and export values from 1903 to 1908, showing the decline of the Shippo trade amid imitation cloisonné competition.

metadata.title: Leading Ceramic Districts
metadata.caption: (1908.) (Above Y. 250,000).
metadata.description: Lists the leading ceramic districts of Japan in 1908 with families engaged, employees and value of output, for districts above Y. 250,000.

metadata.title: Production and its Export
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives lacquer production and export values in thousand yen for 1902 to 1908, showing the trend of the lacquer industry over these years.

metadata.title: Leading Lacquer Ware Districts
metadata.description: Lists the leading lacquer ware districts with the number of families engaged, employees and value of output, showing where the industry was concentrated.

metadata.title: [Sugar Production in Japan Proper and Formosa, 1904–1909]
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000 kin)
metadata.description: The table gives sugar output in Japan Proper (Main island and Luchu, Oshima, Bonin) and Formosa from 1904 to 1909, showing Formosa's rapid growth that now exceeds domestic consumption.

metadata.title: Production
metadata.caption: Output
metadata.description: Gives the annual output of sake, beer and soy in koku for 1902 to 1908, showing the growth of Japan's brewing industry over those years.

metadata.title: [Principal Flour Mills and Their Working Capacity]
metadata.description: The text notes that the principal flour mills, with their paid-up capital and daily working capacity in barrels and sacks, are listed below.

metadata.title: Milling Districts in 1908 (By Machine)
metadata.description: After discussing flour consumption, imports of wheat and the tariff, the page gives the number of factories, employees, output and value of machine flour milling in four districts in 1908.

metadata.title: [Prefectural Industry Figures, Continued]
metadata.description: The top rows are the tail of a prefectural industry table, giving figures for several prefectures and a grand total including other districts.

metadata.title: Import of Flour
metadata.description: The flour import table shows the quantity in sacks and value in yen for each year from 1902 to 1909, with the two blocks side by side.

metadata.title: Matches
metadata.description: Shows Japan's match production and exports by year from 1903 to 1909, with export price per gross, illustrating the state of the match industry discussed beneath.

metadata.title: Leading Match Districts (1908)
metadata.description: Lists the three leading match-producing districts in 1908 with the number of families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: [Kilowatt in Operation by Motive Force, 1904–1909]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of electric power in operation in Japan, split between water and steam motive force, to illustrate the threefold increase over the last six years.

metadata.title: [Electric Power Utilized For, 1908]
metadata.description: Breaks down electric generating capacity for 1908 by purpose of use and by source (hydro, steam, others), with capacity in operation and not yet in operation.

metadata.title: Value of Wax and Refined-Wax
metadata.description: The table gives the number of families engaged in wax production and the values of wax, refined wax and their total for 1903 to 1908, illustrating the trade's trend.

metadata.title: Leading Wax Districts (1908)
metadata.description: Shows the families engaged, employees and value of wax production in the leading wax-producing prefectures in 1908.

metadata.title: Vegetable Oils
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for families, employees and value of the vegetable oil industry from 1903 to 1908.

metadata.title: Leading Vegetable Oils Districts
metadata.caption: (Places which produced above Y. 500,000 in 1908)
metadata.description: Lists the places whose vegetable oil output exceeded Y. 500,000 in 1908, with their families, employees and value.

metadata.title: Indigo (Japanese.)
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for families, employees and value of Japanese indigo production from 1903 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Indigo Production in Tokushima, 1908-9]
metadata.description: Shows that most indigo production in 1908-9 came from Tokushima Prefecture, with its families, employees and value.

metadata.title: Peppermint
metadata.description: Gives families, employees and the value of crude peppermint, menthol crystal and peppermint oil for 1903 to 1905.

metadata.title: [Peppermint Production in Previous Years, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuation of a yearly statistics table of peppermint production, whose headings appear on the previous page; the 1908 figures lead into the text on the 1908 output.

metadata.title: [Peppermint Production in 1908 by Prefecture]
metadata.description: Shows the 1908 peppermint production, mostly from Kanagawa-ken, with factories, employees and the value of menthol and oil for each prefecture.

metadata.title: Leathers
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of families, employees and value of the leather industry from 1903 to 1908.

metadata.title: Leading Leather Districts in 1908 (Places Producing Above Y. 300,000)
metadata.caption: (Places producing above Y. 300,000)
metadata.description: Lists the leading leather-producing districts in 1908, with families, employees and value by type of leather.

metadata.title: Bricks and Tiles in 1908 — A. Bricks
metadata.caption: (Value: Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the number of brick factories, employees and value of fireproof and ordinary bricks by prefecture for 1908, with totals and the 1907 comparison.

metadata.title: Bricks and Tiles in 1908 — B. Tiles
metadata.caption: (Value: Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of tile production by prefecture in 1908, split into fireproof and ordinary tiles, with totals and the 1907 comparison.

metadata.title: Canned Articles
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000) over the fish, fruit and other columns
metadata.description: Summarises the number of canned-food factories, employees and output value by product in three prefectures, with totals for 1908 and 1907 for comparison.

metadata.title: Leading Silk Handkerchief Districts (1908)
metadata.description: Lists the main districts producing silk handkerchiefs, giving workshop numbers, employees and output value for 1908.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Industries (in 1908)
metadata.description: Shows the number of workshops, employees and value for a range of minor manufactures in 1908, indicating where some were chiefly produced.

metadata.title: Factories Conducted by Government (1908)
metadata.description: Gives the engines, horsepower and coal consumption of government-run factories, arsenals and shipyards in 1908.

metadata.title: [Dockyards, Arsenals and Works (continued from previous page)]
metadata.description: This continued table lists government dockyards, arsenals and railway works with three figures for each, most likely the upper part of a statistical list whose headers appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Data at End of March '09
metadata.description: Financial data for the mine-workers' relief fund at the end of March 1909, showing funds received from the beginning and payments made, with totals.

metadata.title: [Percentage of Mine-workers According to Length of Service]
metadata.description: Shows the percentage of mine-workers in metal and coal mines grouped by length of service, below 1 to below 25 years, as part of the treatment of mine-workers.

metadata.title: [Days and Hours of Work by Class of Mine-Workers]
metadata.description: Shows how many days per month and hours per day different classes of mine-workers worked in metal and coal mines, supporting the discussion of working days.

metadata.title: [Average Wages Per Day in Big Mines, 1906]
metadata.description: Gives the average daily wages of each occupational class at six big mines during 1906, illustrating the wage differences the text describes.

metadata.title: [Savings at a Few Mines]
metadata.description: Shows how many workers at four mines save under employer schemes and the average sum each has saved, illustrating the savings encouragement described in section 10.

metadata.title: [Private Primary Schools Attached to Mines]
metadata.description: Gives the teachers, pupils, yearly expenditure and average cost per child for the private primary schools of two mines, as an example of miners' education provision.

metadata.title: [Mines Statistics (Continued)]
metadata.description: A continuation of a mines statistics table, listing three mines with figures in four numeric columns whose headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Service Over
metadata.description: Allowances the company grants retiring or dismissed employees, by rank and length of service, with a note on additional sums and injury payments.

metadata.title: [Special Funds for Operatives]
metadata.description: Listing the amounts of the special funds set aside by the Kanegafuchi Cotton Mill for employee and operative benefit, which are being rapidly increased.

metadata.title: [Estimated Number of Government Officials, Clerks and Employes]
metadata.description: The author estimates the number of brain-workers in officialdom and companies at 900,000, subdivided by grade with a 5% mortality figure, to show the scale of the candidate pool.

metadata.title: [Young Men Completing Schooling in 1908]
metadata.description: Figures for 1908 show how many young men finished secondary or higher schooling each year, compared with the 45,000 official vacancies, to illustrate the surplus of job seekers.

metadata.title: [Monthly Cost of Living of a Mechanic's Family]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: The author gives a monthly budget for a high-class mechanic's family of four, with the husband earning 30 yen, to illustrate the hardship of Japanese labourers' living costs.

metadata.title: [Female Workers at Factories by Age]
metadata.description: Shows the number and per-thousand rate of male and female factory workers by age group at 25 prefectures in September 1909, illustrating how female labor dominates factory employment.

metadata.title: Child Operatives
metadata.description: Gives the percentage of child operatives under 16 by age band in the factory industries where they form the largest share, such as match, glass and silk filature.

metadata.title: [Working Hours, Rest Hours and Monthly Holidays in Factories]
metadata.description: Shows ordinary, maximum and minimum working hours, rest hours, monthly holidays and yearly working days by industry, illustrating the conditions of child and female labour in factories.

metadata.title: Age Distribution of Operatives at Government Factories
metadata.description: Gives the number of child operatives under 10, 12, 14, 16 and 20 years by sex at each government factory, showing the age composition of the workforce.

metadata.title: [Working Hours, Rest Hours, Monthly Holidays and Yearly Work Days at Government Factories]
metadata.description: Shows the working hours, rest intervals, monthly holidays and yearly work days for men, women and children in several Government factory trades, illustrating the labour conditions the Factory Law debate addresses.

metadata.title: Causes of Poverty
metadata.description: Results of an investigation of 3,224 inmates over 41 years of age at the Tokyo Municipal Poor Asylum (April 1902 to March 1909), listing the causes of their poverty.

metadata.title: Average Daily Wages (Yen)
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Average daily wages of laborers in various trades, from 1895 to 1908, showing how pay rose over the period for clothing, food, drink and house-building workers.

metadata.title: [Wages by Occupation]
metadata.description: Shows daily wage rates for many artisan and labour occupations, grouped by trade; the column headings are not printed on this page and appear to be on the previous page.

metadata.title: Average Wages in Tokyo
metadata.description: Gives the latest return of average daily wages in Tokyo for five trades over 1906 to 1909.

metadata.title: Operatives Classified According to Employment (1908)
metadata.description: This table classifies the operatives in Japanese factories in 1908 by industry, giving male and female counts and average daily wages for workers above and below fourteen years of age.

metadata.title: [Factory Statistics by Industry]
metadata.description: Factory statistics by industry, showing counts and figures across several columns, with the grand total at the foot; the column headings are not legible in the scan.

metadata.title: Laborers in Various Government Factories (End of 1908)
metadata.description: Shows the number of operatives, apprentices and laborers employed at each government factory and naval yard at the end of 1908, with daily wages and working days.

metadata.title: [Applications and Registrations of Patents, Designs, Trade-marks and Utility Models, 1902-1903]
metadata.chapter: Patents, Designs, Trade-marks and Utility Models
metadata.chapter_raw: Patents, Designs, Trade-marks and Utility Models
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly numbers of applications filed with the Patent Office by Japanese and foreigners for patents, designs, trade-marks and utility models, plus patents and registrations granted for 1902 and 1903.

metadata.title: [Actions for Trials by Nationality, 1904–1909]
metadata.chapter: Patents, Designs, Trade-marks and Utility Models
metadata.description: The figures continue a series of annual statistics of actions for trials by nationality of the parties, covering 1904 to 1909, whose column headings appear on the preceding page.

metadata.title: No. of Actions for Trials, in 1908
metadata.chapter: Patents, Designs, Trade-marks and Utility Models
metadata.description: Shows the number of actions for trials in 1908 by class of industrial property, with outcomes upheld or rejected/withdrawn, and comparative totals for 1907 and 1908.

metadata.title: Transfer, Hypothecation, Exploitation
metadata.chapter: Patents, Designs, Trade-marks and Utility Models
metadata.description: Gives the number of patents, models, designs and trade-marks transferred, hypothecated or exploited in 1907 and 1908, with totals.

metadata.title: [Expenditure on River Works by Agency, 1902–1906]
metadata.description: The text explains that river works are funded by the Central Government and prefectures, and this table breaks down annual river-work expenditure by the agencies that undertook the works from 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: Principal Harbor-Works
metadata.description: Introducing the port improvement works, this table lists the leading harbour projects, with their works, start and completion dates, and expenditure.

metadata.title: [Harbour Works at Ports, with Work, Dates Commenced and Completed, and Cost]
metadata.description: The table lists harbour improvement works at several Japanese ports, giving the work done, its start and completion dates, and its cost, as part of the public works survey.

metadata.title: [Civil Engineering Expenses by Classification, 1902–1906]
metadata.description: Civil engineering expenses by category for the last five years, shown to illustrate how national and local spending on rivers, roads, harbours and water works was distributed from 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: Damage from Floods and Other Calamities
metadata.description: Shows yearly flood, tidal wave and typhoon damage in yen by item for 1904 to 1907 and the 1902-7 average, illustrating the calamity losses discussed in the text above.

metadata.title: [Water-Works of Principal Cities]
metadata.description: Listing the remarkable water-works of the principal cities, showing construction cost, pipe length, daily water supply, houses served and daily quantity per house.

metadata.title: Domestic Parcel Post Charges to a Locality under a Different Post Office
metadata.description: Gives the domestic parcel post charges by weight band for sending a parcel to a locality under a different post office, for ordinary and registered parcels.

metadata.title: [Charges for Postal Parcels Within Japan Proper]
metadata.description: This table gives the parcel postage charges by weight for ordinary and registered parcels within Japan proper, continuing the fee schedule from the preceding page.

metadata.title: Charges for Postal Parcels Exchanged Between Japan Proper, Formosa and Saghalien, and China and Korea
metadata.description: This table lists parcel postage charges by weight for parcels exchanged between Japan proper, Formosa, Saghalien, China and Korea, with ordinary and registered rates.

metadata.title: Foreign Parcels
metadata.description: The page lists the cheapest-rate routes for foreign parcels to several countries, giving the maximum rate in yen for parcels up to 1 and up to 5 kilograms.

metadata.title: [Parcel Post Rates to Foreign Countries by Route]
metadata.description: This page lists the postal parcel rates by weight for sending goods from Japan to various foreign countries, with the route used for each.

metadata.title: Russia in Asia
metadata.description: Gives the direct exchange rate for parcels by weight, printed as a short list above the foreign money order section.

metadata.title: Foreign Money Orders
metadata.description: Lists countries on which foreign money orders may be drawn, with maximum amounts, fees, and the money in which the amount is expressed.

metadata.title: [Telegraphic Money Orders to Foreign Countries]
metadata.description: Lists the countries to which telegraphic money orders can be sent, with the amount limits and charges, and notes which countries cannot be drawn upon.

metadata.title: Number of Post and Telegraph Offices
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of post and telegraph offices in Japan from 1902 to 1908 and the average area served by each office.

metadata.title: Number of Post and Telegraph Offices in Korea and China
metadata.description: Gives the number of Japanese post and telegraph offices abroad in China and Korea at the end of each fiscal year, 1903 to 1908.

metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Reports the number of domestic ordinary mail and parcel post items despatched each year from 1904 to 1908, with totals.

metadata.title: [Foreign Mail Despatched and Arrived]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly volume of foreign mail and parcel post despatched and arrived, with grand totals, percentage change and average per capita, continuing the communications statistics.

metadata.title: Parcel Post
metadata.description: Gives the annual number of parcels despatched and delivered, with the percentage and increase, for fiscal years 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Classification of Ordinary Mail Matters
metadata.description: Breaks down ordinary domestic mail by type, namely sealed letters, cards and return cards, for each fiscal year from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.description: Records the number of ordinary foreign mail items transmitted and arrived each fiscal year from 1903 to 1908, with the increase.

metadata.description: Summarises ordinary mail matters for the 1908 fiscal year by kind, showing the quantity and increase for each kind and the overall total.

metadata.title: Mail Matters Exchanged with Principal Countries in 1908 Fiscal Year
metadata.description: Shows the number of mail items sent to and received from each principal foreign country during the 1908 fiscal year, reflecting Japan's postal exchanges.

metadata.title: Postal Savings Deposits at Home
metadata.description: Records the growth of home postal savings deposits by fiscal year, noting the marked increase in deposits and depositors after the late war.

metadata.title: Savings Deposits at Offices Stationed in China
metadata.description: Shows savings deposits held at Japanese post offices stationed in China, by fiscal year, with number of depositors, amounts and average deposit per depositor.

metadata.description: Gives the telegram fees for messages exchanged between Formosa, Manchuria, Chefu, the Bonins, Saghalien, Korea and the offices in Japan proper, by Kana and Roman-letter type.

metadata.description: Telegraph rates from Japan to Asian destinations, ordinary and press telegrams sent via Shanghai, in yen.

metadata.description: Telegraph rates from Japan to European destinations by the Vladivostock and Shanghai routes, with a note on press telegram rates.

metadata.title: [Telegraph Rates to North America]
metadata.description: Telegraph rates from Japan to North American cities, ordinary and press telegrams sent via Bonin or Manila, in yen.

metadata.title: [Telegraph Rates to Oceania]
metadata.description: Telegraph rates from Japan to Oceanic destinations sent via Shanghai, ordinary and press telegrams, in yen.

metadata.title: [Telegraph Rates to South America]
metadata.description: Telegraph rates from Japan to South American destinations sent via Bonin or Manila, showing the press telegram rate.

metadata.title: Extension of Telegraph
metadata.description: Shows the yearly growth of the telegraph network from 1904 to 1908, with the lengths of underground, aerial and submarine cables at fiscal year end.

metadata.title: Number of Domestic Telegrams Transacted
metadata.description: Gives the annual volume of domestic telegrams and of foreign telegrams transmitted and received, with the yearly increase in domestic traffic, for 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Foreign Telegrams in 1908
metadata.description: Lists the number of foreign telegrams transmitted and arrived in 1908 by country, with Korea and South Manchuria at the head as the largest exchange.

metadata.description: The page sets out the wireless telegram charges for coast stations, ships, and land lines under the international regulations Japan adopted, in gold cents per word or per group of words.

metadata.description: Lists the five Japanese coast wireless stations with their geographical coordinates, given as the domestic wireless telegraph system was introduced in 1903.

metadata.description: Shows the yearly receipts of the postal and telegraph services by branch, from 1901 to 1908, with totals.

metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly service expenses of the postal and telegraph branches from 1901 to 1908, set beside the receipts table above.

metadata.description: Reports how many telephone subscribers existed at the close of each year from 1901 onward, with a March 1910 figure.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Apparatus
metadata.description: Breaks down the telephone apparatus in use at the end of each fiscal year from 1903 to 1908 by type of equipment.

metadata.title: Number of Registered Vessels Classified According to Tonnage
metadata.description: Shows the number and gross tonnage of registered Japanese steamers and sailers, grouped by tonnage class, at the end of each year from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Registered Steamers Classified by Age
metadata.caption: (End, Dec. '08.)
metadata.description: Breaks down the registered steamers at the end of December 1908 by age of vessel and hull material, giving counts, tonnage and gross tonnage for each age band.

metadata.title: Registered Steamers of Over 1,000 Tons Classified by Materials
metadata.caption: (Dec. '08.)
metadata.description: Shows the registered steamers over 1,000 tons at December 1908, counted and weighed by hull material, giving a picture of the mercantile fleet's construction.

metadata.title: Steamers Classified by Speed
metadata.caption: (Dec. '08.)
metadata.description: Gives the registered steamers over 1,000 tons at December 1908 grouped by their rated speed in knots, with number of vessels and tonnage in each speed band.

metadata.title: Steamers Used on the Lines

metadata.description: Shows roughly how tramp-boats carried various goods between Far Eastern ports, according to Mr. Nishikawa's investigation, in tonnage.

metadata.description: Shows the differentiated shipbuilding subsidy rates in yen for each grade of Class A and Class B vessels, as introduced under the amended law from January 1910.

metadata.title: [Merchant Vessels Built by the Four Leading Shipyards]
metadata.description: Gives the share of the four leading shipyards in the 137 merchant vessels, totalling 246,764 tons, built in Japan up to 1908.

metadata.title: Seamen of Higher Grade
metadata.description: Shows the number of licensed first-class captains for 1905 to 1908, with the f. figure given alongside each year, to illustrate growth since the Russo-Japanese War.

metadata.title: [Certificated Officers of the Merchant Marine by Class]
metadata.description: Shows the number of certificated merchant marine officers and engineers by class, with foreigners counted separately, and the scope of each class's navigation rights.

metadata.title: Shipwrecks
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of steamers and sailing-ships and junks destroyed or damaged in shipwrecks, with totals, for 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: No. of Lives Lost and Injured
metadata.description: Lists yearly deaths, injuries, missing persons and rescued lives in shipwrecks from 1904 to 1908, following the shipwreck table.

metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of Japanese and foreign pilots from 1904 to 1908, illustrating the effect of the 1899 Pilotage Law on licensing.

metadata.title: [Freight Rates on Principal Articles by Steamship and Railway]

metadata.description: A shipping company's business returns for 1907 to 1910, given in half-yearly columns, showing its capital, fleet, receipts, profit and dividend.

metadata.title: [Shares Taken by the Four Companies in the Common Enterprise]
metadata.description: Shows the share each of the four amalgamated companies (Hunan, Osaka, Yusen and Daito) took in the new Japan-China Steamship Company enterprise.

metadata.title: Business Returns for the Last Three Years
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Business returns of the constituent steamship company, giving capital, fleet, receipts, profit and dividends for each half-year of 1907 to 1909.

metadata.title: Volume of Business of the Three Steam-Ship Companies
metadata.caption: (Nihon Yusen Kaisha, Osaka Shosen Kaisha and Toyo Kisen Kaisha)
metadata.description: The table gives cargo tonnage, passenger numbers and receipts of the three steamship companies year by year from 1905 to 1909, showing the scale of their combined business.

metadata.description: Combines state and private traffic receipts by coaching, freight, sundry and total for each year from 1906 to 1909.

metadata.caption: (yen 1000)
metadata.description: Shows expenses and profit of state and private railways for each year from 1906 to 1909.

metadata.description: Compares average daily earnings, expenses and net profit per mile of state and private railway lines in 1908-9, with expenses per 100 yen of earnings.

metadata.title: [District Offices of the Railway Board]
metadata.description: Lists the Railway Board's district offices, their locations and the mileage of railway each controls, giving the organisation of the Imperial railways.

metadata.description: Shows the growth of electric tramway companies from 1900 to 1909, covering capital, reserves, mileage, construction and rolling stock.

metadata.description: Summary figures for the private railway companies over 1900 to 1909, shown before the list of leading establishments in 1909.

metadata.title: [Fixed Number of Members of the House of Representatives, 1894–1908]
metadata.description: Gives the fixed number of House of Representatives members at successive dates from 1894 to 1908, showing how the chamber's size grew over the period.

metadata.description: Breaks down the membership of the House of Peers by rank and category as it stood in December 1910, with the total of 364 at the foot.

metadata.description: The page lists the informal political groups or coteries of members of the House of Peers, with the number of members in each, explaining they have no regular leaders.

metadata.title: Sessions of the House (D.=Dissolution)
metadata.description: The table lists each session of the House with its sitting dates, president and vice-president, marking dissolutions and noting the extraordinary general elections held between sessions.

metadata.title: [Sessions of the House of Representatives, 14th to 26th, with Dates and Presidents]
metadata.description: Lists each Diet session of the House of Representatives from the 14th to the 26th with its dates and the Speaker before and after, noting the general elections held in between.

metadata.title: [Party Strength in the House of Representatives]
metadata.description: Shows the number of members of the House of Representatives held by each party, with the total, as the page discusses the composition of the Diet.

metadata.title: Number of Franchise-Holders
metadata.description: Gives the number of franchise-holders from 1890 to 1908, with the ratios per member and per 1,000 population, showing the effect of changes in the property qualification.

metadata.title: Violation of Election Rules
metadata.description: The table gives the number of cases and offenders for election rule violations at each general election from 1890 to 1908, showing the scale of electoral malpractice over time.

metadata.title: [Nature of Offences at the 2nd and 9th General Elections]
metadata.description: This breakdown classifies the offences committed at the 2nd and 9th elections by their nature, illustrating the two extreme instances cited in the preceding note.

metadata.title: Profession of the Members
metadata.description: Comparing the professions of members returned in the 1890 and 1908 elections, showing the decline of farmer members and the rise of members of other origins.

metadata.title: [Average Age of Members by Session]
metadata.description: Shows the average age of members in successive Diet sessions, illustrating the gradual increase in the age of members of the House.

metadata.title: Shin-nin Rank

metadata.title: Naval Officers

metadata.title: Military Officers

metadata.title: Military and Naval Attaches at Embassy or Legation
metadata.description: Shows the allowances paid to military and naval attachés at embassies or legations, by rank and by the country they are posted to.

metadata.description: Gives the salary and allowance of the top posts in the Residency-General in Korea, shown in yen.

metadata.title: [Budget for the 1910—'11 Year, Revenue and Expenditure in Yen]

metadata.title: Revenue
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: This table compares revenue for 1910–'11 with 1909–'10, showing increases and decreases in thousands of yen, to illustrate the budget changes.

metadata.title: Expenditure
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: This table compares expenditure for 1910–'11 with 1909–'10 in thousands of yen, showing the increase in each category of the budget.

metadata.title: Ordinary Revenue
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: The table lists the ordinary government revenue items by source for three fiscal years, showing how tax and state enterprise receipts changed around the 1910 financial adjustments described above.

metadata.title: Extraordinary Revenue
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the extraordinary government revenue items and totals for three fiscal years, reporting how the extra income was raised in each year.

metadata.title: Ordinary Expenditures
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the itemised ordinary expenditure of each government department and branch for three fiscal years, showing the main spending heads of the state budget.

metadata.title: Extraordinary Revenue
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists extraordinary revenue by department across three years, with totals and total expenditure, showing how special receipts were distributed among government offices.

metadata.title: Annual State Revenue and Expenditure Pertaining to the General Account
metadata.caption: (1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Gives the state's annual revenue and expenditure on the general account for each fiscal year from 1894-5 to 1910-11, set out in two side-by-side columns.

metadata.title: [Revenue Surpluses, 1904-5 to 1909-10]
metadata.description: Shows the revenue surpluses for the last six fiscal years, introduced by the text explaining the sudden 1907-8 rise and the lower bona fide surplus in later years.

metadata.title: [Special Account Items Classified by Kind, 1909-10]
metadata.description: Gives the number of Special Account items in 1909-10 by kind, following the statement that there were 60 such items that year.

metadata.description: Lists the largest Special Account items by kind with their amounts for 1908-9, illustrating the total of about 1,067,739,035 in such funds.

metadata.description: The table lists the amounts of government funds and the capital of state undertakings, including the total of other items, with the remainder of the Chinese indemnity account noted below.

metadata.title: Statistics on State Monopolies
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the annual amounts and values of the State tobacco, salt and camphor monopolies, which yielded considerable revenue to the Treasury.

metadata.title: Profit and Loss Account
metadata.caption: (Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the profit and loss accounts and consolidated capital of the principal State undertakings, which are not compiled like those of ordinary private enterprises.

metadata.title: [Receipts, Expenses and Profit of Government Factories and State Railway]
metadata.description: The table gives receipts, expenses and profit for several government arsenals, factories and the State Railway, with figures for two periods and a total column.

metadata.title: Collection Expense of Revenue
metadata.description: The table shows the tax revenue, collection expense and the expense ratio per Yen 100 of revenue for several fiscal periods, to show the cost of collecting taxes.

metadata.title: [Land Tax Rates]
metadata.description: Shows the land tax rates for urban, rural and other land, split into normal rate, war tax and combined total, as levied after the Russo-Japanese War.

metadata.title: [Value of Land by Category]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Shows the assessed value of land in yen by category, split into two columns with the national total, as part of the land-tax data.

metadata.title: Income Tax, 1st Kind (Income of Juridical Persons)
metadata.description: Gives the normal and war-tax rates of income tax on juridical persons, by company type and income bracket.

metadata.title: Income Tax, 2nd Kind (Income from Bonds and Shares)
metadata.description: States the single normal income-tax rate applied to income from bonds and shares.

metadata.title: Income Tax, 3rd Kind (Income of Other Descriptions)
metadata.description: Lists normal and war-tax rates of income tax on income from other sources, by income brackets.

metadata.description: Shows how the juridical persons of B class, with income of not less than 100,000 yen, were distributed by income band, as given by the Government Delegate at the 23rd Diet.

metadata.title: [Individuals Getting Income Above 100,000 Yen a Year]
metadata.description: Lists individuals whose yearly income exceeded 100,000 yen, grouped by income band, with total income and number of persons in each band.

metadata.description: Explains the business tax classification by kind of occupation and gives the data used for assessment and the normal rate applying to each kind.

metadata.title: [Business Tax Rates by Kind]
metadata.description: The page lists the rates of the business tax by kind, each kind giving a capital or proceeds basis and a per-person levy, as part of the account of Japan's war taxation.

metadata.title: [Registration Fees by Object]
metadata.description: The page gives the registration fee rates for taxable registrable objects, grouped into immovables, corporations, trade establishments and professional registration, based on value and including war taxation.

metadata.description: The page continues a list of fees payable for certificates and licences of mariners, marine engineers and pilots, with the amounts in yen.

metadata.title: Patent Right

metadata.title: Designs
metadata.description: Shows the fees for transferring or jointly owning a design right and for hypothecating it.

metadata.title: Trade-marks
metadata.description: States the fee for transferring or jointly owning a registered trade-mark.

metadata.title: Mining
metadata.description: Lists the government fees for mining licence matters, from prospecting and working through transfers, hypothecation and abandonment.

metadata.title: Medicine Tax
metadata.description: Lists the national tax rates on compounding, licensing and stamp duty for medicine, as set out under the Medicine Tax heading.

metadata.title: Sugar Excise Rates by Class
metadata.description: Gives the sugar excise rate in yen per picul for each of the four sugar classes.

metadata.title: Woolen and Silk Textile Taxes
metadata.description: States the tax rate on woollen and silk textiles or mixtures as a fraction of their value.

metadata.title: [Offenders and Fines for Tobacco, Salt, Camphor and Customs]
metadata.description: Shows the number of offenders and the fines imposed under the tobacco, salt, camphor and customs monopoly and revenue laws.

metadata.title: Arrears in National and Local Taxes in 1907-8
metadata.description: Gives the 1907-8 arrears in national and local taxes, counting writs, fines, distraints, auctions and deficits.

metadata.description: Lists the number of writs and fines under the principal national tax items for 1907-8.

metadata.title: Principal Items in Local Taxes
metadata.description: Lists the number of writs and fines under the principal local tax items for 1907-8.

metadata.title: Admirals on Active Service
metadata.description: Lists the admirals on active service with the date of each one's appointment.

metadata.title: Monetary Endowment on Communities

metadata.title: [Provincial Fund Amounts by Province]

metadata.description: The table breaks down Japan's disbursements on the Korean protectorate in 1910-11 by department and by ordinary and extraordinary account, showing the main items of expenditure.

metadata.title: Rainfall

metadata.title: No. of Days of Rainfall and Snowfall
metadata.description: Number of days with rainfall or snowfall at five stations, for February, July and the annual total, showing the climate of the peninsula.

metadata.title: The Foreign Residents in Korea

metadata.title: Revenues
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's government revenues for 1908 to 1910, split into ordinary and extraordinary items, giving the yearly totals of government income.

metadata.title: Expenditures
metadata.description: Lists Japan's ordinary and extraordinary government expenditures by department for 1908 to 1910, with totals, following the revenue figures.

metadata.title: National Debts
metadata.description: Lists Japan's national debt loans with interest rates, amounts, dates of contracting, redemption years and creditors, closing the finance section.

metadata.title: Volume of Trade
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly volume of Korea's merchandise and specie and bullion trade in imports and exports from 1903 to 1909.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the principal export articles of Korea and their values for each year from 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Imports
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the principal import articles into Korea, mainly textiles and manufactured goods, with values for 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Principal Commodities, 1905–1909]
metadata.description: A continuation of a list of commodity figures for 1905 to 1909, showing values for items such as porcelain, salt, coal and timber.

metadata.title: Trade in Leading Ports
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the export and import values of Korean treaty ports such as Ninsen, Fusan and Gensan for 1905 to 1908.

metadata.title: Trade with Different Countries
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the value of trade with Japan, China, Great Britain, the U.S.A. and Russia in 1904 and 1906 to 1909, by import and export.

metadata.title: [Korean Banks Established, Capital and Paid-Up Capital, 1909]
metadata.description: Lists the three Korean ordinary banks reported at end of 1909, with their establishment dates and capital figures.

metadata.title: [Korean Banks: Loans from Government, Deposits, Loans, Overdrafts and Bills Discounted, 1909]
metadata.description: Shows the business position of the three Korean banks at end of 1909, including government loans, deposits, loans, overdrafts and bills discounted.

metadata.title: [Japanese Banks in Korea: Deposits, Loans, Overdrafts and Bills Discounted]
metadata.description: Gives the deposits, loans, overdrafts and bills discounted of the three Japanese banks operating in Korea, which the text describes as the 1st, 18th and 58th Banks.

metadata.title: [Japanese Residents in Korea, December 1906 to December 1909]

metadata.title: [Property Held by Japanese in Korea]
metadata.description: Estimated land, buildings and value held by Japanese in the principal places of the Peninsula, showing the scale of Japanese property holdings in Korea.

metadata.title: [Fishing Boats, Fishermen and Catches in Korean Waters]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of fishing boats, fishermen and the value of catches for Korean and Japanese fishermen in Korean waters, illustrating the scale of Japanese fishing activity there.

metadata.title: Wages in Korea
metadata.caption: Returns made in April 1910
metadata.description: Wage rates for native coolies at seven Korean ports, comparing Japanese and Korean labourers, showing Korean wages are much cheaper than in Japan, which attracted demand for labour.

metadata.title: [Korean Railways Returns for 1908–9]
metadata.description: A small set of figures giving the Korean railway returns for the 1908–9 year: mileage, locomotives, carriages, wagons and construction cost.

metadata.title: Traffic Returns
metadata.description: Summarises the Korean railway traffic returns, giving receipts by passenger, goods and sundries, total receipts, expenses and the resulting balance or loss.

metadata.title: Revenues

metadata.title: Expenditures

metadata.title: [Foreign Residents in Japan, 1904-1908]

metadata.title: Forests and Plains
metadata.caption: (March, 1908)

metadata.description: Shows the number of state forest and plain items under promise of sale and their area for each year from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.caption: (in 1,000)

metadata.caption: (in 1,000)

metadata.title: Marine Products (in 1,000)
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Compares yearly quantity and value of raw and cured marine products in Formosa, showing fisheries output from 1903 to 1908.

metadata.title: Mineral Products
metadata.description: Gives yearly output of gold, gold dust, coal, sulphur and petroleum, showing Japan's mineral production from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade
metadata.caption: (in Y. 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows total foreign trade, exports and imports, and specie and bullion movements for 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Trade with Japan Proper

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Exported

metadata.title: Camphor and Camphor Oils
metadata.description: Shows the output of camphor and camphor oil, and the price paid for crude camphor by the Government, for the years 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Estimated Expenditures and Revenues of Karafuto, 1908-9 and 1909-10]

metadata.title: [Marine Products of Karafuto, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Shows the yield of marine products in Karafuto for 1907 to 1909, given to illustrate the fishery trade after the introduction of the experimental laboratory plans.

metadata.title: Finance

metadata.description: Gives the number of Japanese residents in each Manchurian centre at the end of 1907, broken down by sex and total.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade at Dairen (1909)

metadata.description: The South Manchuria Railway's rolling stock and open mileage at the end of the second half of 1909-10, shown separately for the main lines and the Antung-Mukden line.

metadata.title: Business Result for the First Half of 1910-11

metadata.description: The table gives the company's earnings and disbursements by business category, illustrating the scale of its harbor, mining, electricity and other operations in the Dairen railway zone.

metadata.title: Total Expenditures by the Company
metadata.caption: (Y. 1000)
metadata.description: Shows how the company's total spending of about Y. 65 million since its formation, up to the end of 1909, was distributed across its operating and administrative departments.

metadata.title: [Distribution of Land Along the Railway in Russian Control]
metadata.description: Shows how the land in Russian control along the Eastern Chinese Railway is distributed by province and category, in acres and square miles, with totals.

metadata.title: Weights (Japanese)
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese units of weight and their equivalents in Kwamme, Momme and avoirdupois pounds, for readers converting Japanese figures.

metadata.title: Avoirdupois, Troy and Metric Weights
metadata.description: Gives Western weight units (ounce, pound, stone, hundredweight, ton) expressed in Japanese momme and kwamme for comparison.

metadata.description: Gives the artisan's linear measure in shaku, sun and bu, with their English inch equivalents.

metadata.title: Dry Goods (Kujira)
metadata.description: Gives the dry-goods (cloth) measure of length in shaku, sun and bu, with English equivalents.

metadata.title: Distance
metadata.description: Gives the Japanese units of distance (ri, cho, ken, shaku) with their equivalents in miles and feet.

metadata.description: Explains the Japanese land units (cho, tan, se, tsubo) and how they relate to acres and square yards.

metadata.description: Lists Japanese dry and liquid capacity units (koku, to, sho, go) with equivalents in bushels, quarts, gallons and pecks.

metadata.description: A list of English-style length units with the number of each smaller unit that makes up the next larger one.

metadata.title: Moneys
metadata.description: Gives the value of the yen in sen, shillings and cents, and the U.S. dollar in francs, for currency comparison.

metadata.title: [Area of Japan by Islands]
metadata.description: The table gives the area in square ri of Japan's main islands and island groups, showing how the national total of territory is distributed, excluding Karafuto and Korea.

metadata.title: [Principal Mountain Peaks Above 8,000 Feet]
metadata.description: Listing the principal mountain peaks of Japan above 8,000 feet, with their heights, as an introduction to the geography section.

metadata.title: [Rivers Above 40 ri in Length]
metadata.description: Listing the rivers of Japan longer than 40 ri, showing that Japanese rivers are short and rapid because of the mountain relief.

metadata.title: Coast-Line of the Principal Islands
metadata.description: Gives the total coastline length of each principal island and the area per coast-line unit, showing how serrated each island's coast is.

metadata.title: Harbors Open to the Call of Foreign Steamers
metadata.description: Lists the thirty-six harbours open to foreign steamers, with the year each was opened and the island where it lies, in two columns.

metadata.title: Typhoons During the Last Seven Years
metadata.description: Following the description of wind and typhoons, this table lists notable typhoons since 1905 with their origin, disappearance point, places passed, minimum pressure and velocity.

metadata.title: [Average Dates and Last Occurrence by Locality]
metadata.description: A short list giving, for four localities, an average date and the date it last occurred, shown at the head of the page before the temperature table.

metadata.title: Monthly Average Temperature in Japan
metadata.description: Monthly average, average and extreme temperatures at ten Japanese meteorological observatories, showing the seasonal range of climate across the country.

metadata.title: Average Monthly Rainfalls and Snowfalls in Japan from Beginning of Observation to the End of 1908
metadata.description: The table gives average monthly and yearly rainfall and snowfall at eleven Japanese observatories, with the number of rain and snow days per year, to illustrate the country's climate.

metadata.title: Principal Calamities during the Tokugawa Period
metadata.description: The page lists the most destructive earthquakes and tidal-wave calamities of the Tokugawa period, giving date, place, houses destroyed and deaths, before the recent seismic record.

metadata.description: Recent major earthquakes, with houses destroyed, persons killed and injured, are listed to illustrate the seismic losses of modern times in Japan.

metadata.title: [Mineral Springs of Japan]
metadata.description: A list of Japanese hot springs giving each spring's name, distance from the nearest convenient place, prefecture, mineral quality and temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.

metadata.title: Movement of Population
metadata.description: Shows the yearly male, female and total population of Japan from 1903 to 1909 with annual increase and rate per 100 population, illustrating the growth discussed in the census introduction.

metadata.title: [Population Density and Family Size by Region, 1908]
metadata.description: Gives the relative population density per square ri and the average persons per family in each region of Japan proper in 1908, for comparison with foreign countries.

metadata.title: [Area and Population of Principal Countries]
metadata.description: Compares Japan's area, population and density per square mile with six major Western and Asian countries, placing Japan in international context.

metadata.description: Gives the 1908 census population of Japan by age group and sex, with each age group's share per 100 population compared across census years from 1888 to 1908.

metadata.title: Percentage Rate of Married and Unmarried per 100 People
metadata.description: Expresses the married and unmarried population as percentages per 100 people for each census year from 1888 to 1908.

metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of marriages and divorces in Japan from 1904 to 1908, with each expressed per 1,000 population.

metadata.description: Gives the population of Japan from 1894 to 1908 split between cities over 10,000 and villages under 10,000, with each group's share of the total.

metadata.description: Lists annual deaths by sex, with deaths per 100 people and the male-to-female mortality ratio, for 1904 to 1908.

metadata.description: Gives the number of foreign residents in Japan at the end of each year from 1905 to 1909, split by sex with totals.
