metadata.description: Shows the number of children of school age in 1905-10, split by sex and by whether they were under compulsory attendance, with the ratio attending school.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers of Both Sexes in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Gives average, minimum and maximum monthly teacher salaries in public elementary schools for each year from 1905 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Schools Collecting Fees]
metadata.description: Shows how many schools collected fees in each year, how many pupils paid in full, in part or were exempt, and the average fee, explaining the rise in fee-charging schools.

metadata.title: [Kindergarten Statistics]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of kindergartens, their conductors and infant pupils from 1906–7 to 1909–10, illustrating growth of kindergarten education.

metadata.title: The Curriculum of the Middle School
metadata.description: Lists the weekly teaching hours for each subject across the five years of the middle school course, showing the curriculum structure.

metadata.title: [Subjects and Hours of Instruction in Middle Schools]
metadata.description: Shows the weekly-lesson distribution of subjects in middle schools across the columns of years; the printed column headings are not visible in this crop.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Middle Schools
metadata.description: Gives yearly counts of public and private middle schools, their instructors, pupils and graduates, showing trends across the four school years listed.

metadata.title: Graduates and Subsequent Careers
metadata.caption: Careers as reported within the year after the graduation are:—
metadata.description: Shows where middle-school graduates went within the year after graduating, such as high schools, professional schools, military service, teaching or other work.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Girls' High Schools
metadata.description: The page gives the weekly hours of each subject across the four years of the girls' high school course; History and Geography share one bracketed figure in the original.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Girl's High Schools
metadata.description: This statistical table compares the number of public and private girls' high schools, their instructors, pupils, graduates, and dropout and admission rates for three school years.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the First Section of the High School
metadata.description: Shows the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each of the three years of the First Section of the High School, which the preceding text describes as a three-year course.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Second Section of the High School
metadata.description: Shows the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each of the three years of the Second Section of the High School, the companion to the First Section curriculum.

metadata.title: [Statistics of the Eight Higher Schools]
metadata.description: Lists, for each of the eight higher schools, the number of instructors, students, graduates, applicants for admission and those enrolled.

metadata.title: [Entrants and Applicants by Year (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top rows continue a yearly figures table whose column headings fall on the previous page; they give the enrolment and applicant counts for 1907-8 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: [Applicants and Admissions by Section]
metadata.description: Shows the number of applicants for admission to the normal schools in each of three sections, and the corresponding admission figures, for three school years.

metadata.title: Male Students Classified by Occupation of Parents
metadata.description: Gives the percentage breakdown of male normal school students by their parents' occupation for three school years.

metadata.title: [Students and Graduates by Sex]
metadata.description: Lists the numbers of male and female students and graduates of normal schools for three school years, introduced by the statement that they are classified by sex.

metadata.title: Statistics of Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: Gives instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admissions at the Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools for the three school years 1907-8 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: Average Age of Those Matriculated in 1909-10
metadata.description: Gives the average age, in years and months, of students matriculated in 1909-10 in each college of the Imperial University of Tokyo.

metadata.title: Statistics Relating to the Imperial University of Tokyo
metadata.description: Shows the professors, students, graduates, applicants and matriculants of each hall and college of the Imperial University of Tokyo, with yearly totals for 1907-8 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: [Average Ages of Students Enrolled in 1909-10]
metadata.description: Shows the average ages of students enrolled in 1909-10 at each college, as introduced by the preceding text on the organization of the universities.

metadata.title: Statistics Relating to the Kyoto University
metadata.description: Gives the professor numbers, students, graduates, applicants and matriculants for each hall and college of Kyoto University over 1907-8 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: Science College at Sendai
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for the Science College at Sendai, established in 1910, covering professors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolments for three academic years.

metadata.title: [Students and Graduates of the Naval and Engineering School]
metadata.description: Gives enrolment and graduate numbers of the naval and engineering school over four years, noting that 95 Chinese students were then in the school.

metadata.title: The Morioka Higher School of Agriculture and Forestry
metadata.description: Shows staff, students, graduates and admissions at the Morioka agricultural and forestry college, whose two sub-courses are listed separately for 1909-10.

metadata.title: Statistic of the Higher Commercial Schools
metadata.description: Compares teaching staff and student numbers at the five government higher commercial schools across 1905-6 to 1909-10, with Yamaguchi and Nagasaki newly opened in that period.

metadata.title: [Graduates, Applications for Admission and Admissions at Higher Commercial Schools: Tokyo, Kobe, Yamaguchi, Nagasaki]
metadata.description: Shows graduates, applicants and admissions at the higher commercial schools in Tokyo, Kobe, Yamaguchi and Nagasaki over five periods; the column years are not printed.

metadata.title: Professions Pursued by Graduates of Tokyo Higher Commercial School
metadata.description: Gives the careers taken up by graduates of the Tokyo Higher Commercial School in the three years 1907-8 to 1909-10, following the discussion of the school's reorganisation.

metadata.title: Statistics of the Higher Technical Schools
metadata.description: The page gives statistics of the higher technical schools (Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, Nagoya, Kumamoto, Sendai), comparing teaching staff, students, graduates, applicants and admissions over five years.

metadata.title: [No. of Students by Course, Fishery Institution]
metadata.description: Gives the number of students in each course of the fishery institution from 1906 to 1910, with yearly totals, alongside a note on its laboratories and training vessel.

metadata.title: [Students and Graduates of Institutes for Training Teachers of Technical Education]
metadata.description: Shows student numbers, graduates, applicants and admissions for the three Government institutes that train technical school teachers, for 1907-8 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: [Public and Private Technical Schools: Schools, Staff, Pupils and Graduates]
metadata.description: Summarises the number of schools, instructors, pupils and graduates of the public and private technical schools for 1907-8 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: [Special Schools of Medicine: Instructors, Students, Graduates and Admissions]
metadata.description: Shows the instructors, students, graduates and admission figures for the government special medical schools at Chiba, Sendai, Okayama, Kanazawa and Nagasaki over three school years.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Foreign Language School: Instructors, Students, Graduates and Admissions]
metadata.description: Gives the staffing, enrolment, graduate and admission figures of the Tokyo Foreign Language School for the last three years, following its description of the course.

metadata.title: [Instructors, Students and Graduates, Continued]
metadata.description: The top rows continue a table of instructors, students, graduates and early leavers for the preceding school years, ending the figures for the first institution described.

metadata.title: The Tokyo Academy of Music
metadata.description: Figures for instructors, students, graduates and early leavers at the Tokyo Academy of Music over three school years, described in the accompanying text on its course structure.

metadata.title: Blind and Deaf and Dumb School
metadata.description: Counts of blind and mute school-age children, with the defectives rate per 1,000 normal children of the same age, for several years.

metadata.title: Public and Private Blind and Deaf and Dumb Schools
metadata.description: Number of public and private blind and deaf and dumb schools, with their teachers, pupils and graduates, split into ordinary and professional education and totalled for three years.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Blind and Deaf School Statistics, 1907-8 to 1909-10]
metadata.description: Shows staff, pupil numbers, teachers' course, graduates, applicants and admissions at the Tokyo Blind and Deaf School for three school years, illustrating the school described above.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Collegiate Institutions
metadata.description: Summary of enrolment by faculty, total students and graduates at public and private collegiate institutions for three successive academic years, 1907-8 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: [List of Collegiate Institutions, with Locality, Foundation Date and Subjects Taught]
metadata.description: A list of the collegiate institutions with their locality, year of foundation and subjects taught, giving the scope of higher education in Japan at the time.

metadata.title: [Meiji Gakuin Students and Alumni, July 1910]
metadata.description: Statistics returned by the Meiji Gakuin in July 1910 give the number of students and alumni in its theological, higher and middle school departments.

metadata.title: License for Secondary Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of applicants, licences granted and the resulting ratio for secondary-school teachers' licence examinations over the last four years.

metadata.title: License for Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of license applications, licenses granted and the resulting license ratio for elementary school teachers over three school years.

metadata.title: [Educational Stock Fund Account]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly account of the Educational Stock Fund, showing its existing sum, loans, bonds and deposits, derived from the Chinese Indemnity appropriation.

metadata.title: Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers
metadata.description: Shows the receipts of the fund for giving super-stipends to teachers, including State aid, provincial contributions, interest and balances brought forward, for three years.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers]
metadata.description: Shows how the disbursements of the super-stipend fund were applied, to additional teacher allowances and to the amount carried to the next account, for three years.

metadata.title: State Aid for Promoting Technical Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of low-grade vocational schools receiving state aid and the total aid given in each school year from 1905-6 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid out of Provincial and Communal Treasurie
metadata.description: Lists the educational expenses paid from provincial and communal treasuries by type of institution for the years 1906-7 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Shows the constitution and eyesight condition of male students in government institutions over three school years, illustrating the state of student health.

metadata.title: Health of Female Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Shows the constitution and eyesight condition of female students in government institutions over three school years, placed alongside the male figures.

metadata.title: Health in Public and Private Schools of Secondary and Elementary Education: Health Returns for Boys
metadata.description: Gives the health returns for boys in various school types over recent years, showing constitution and eyesight by school category.

metadata.title: [Health Returns for Girls in Public and Private Schools]
metadata.description: Gives the health returns for girls in elementary, girls' higher and normal schools, presented after the boys' figures for comparison.

metadata.title: [Continued Table of Students by School Type, 1907-8 to 1909-10]
metadata.description: This is the continuation of a statistical table on school types and year totals, whose column headings appear on the previous page; the figures compare school categories across three years.

metadata.title: [Department of Education's Ryugakusei Staying Abroad at End of Year]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of the Department of Education's ryugakusei (foreign-going students) staying abroad at the end of each year, from 1904-5 to 1910-11, illustrating the scale of Japanese students overseas.

metadata.title: [Graduates of Girls' Higher Schools by Condition After Graduation]
metadata.description: Shows how graduates of girls' higher schools in each year from 1904-5 to 1909-10 were classified by their condition after graduation, illustrating the limited shift away from marriage among educated girls.

metadata.title: [Imperial Library Volumes, Opening Days and Visitors]
metadata.description: Gives volumes, opening days, visitors and average daily visitors for a national library over four fiscal years, illustrating the growth of library use before the university and private library figures.

metadata.title: [University Library Volumes, 1908-9]
metadata.description: Compares the book holdings of the Tokyo and Kyoto Imperial Universities, split into Japanese and Chinese, European and total volumes for 1908-9.

metadata.title: [Public and Private Libraries Statistics]
metadata.description: Shows the number of public and private libraries, their volumes, opening days, visitors and average daily visitors for three years, supporting the remark that these libraries were poorer than the university ones.

metadata.title: [Articles Displayed in the Museum Returned at the End of 1908]
metadata.description: Lists the museum's displayed articles returned at the end of 1908 by category, followed by zoo and museum visitor totals for the year.

metadata.title: [Output of Books, 1906-1909]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of books from 1906 to 1909, split into original works and translations, to illustrate the publishing trade's recent volume.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.description: Gives yearly copyright registrations from 1905 to 1909 by category, with totals and transfers, following the discussion of the revised copyright law.

metadata.title: Censorship
metadata.description: The table gives yearly counts, 1905–1909, of publications whose sale was forbidden, copies seized, or plates seized on public order or public morals grounds.

metadata.title: Press Statistics
metadata.description: The returns give the number of dailies and periodicals existing at the end of each of the five latest years available, showing the growth of the press.

metadata.title: Leading Periodicals Published in Tokyo
metadata.description: A list of leading Japanese-language periodicals published in Tokyo, giving each title's subject feature, frequency, price per issue and publisher.

metadata.title: [Japanese Magazines Published in Tokyo]
metadata.description: A list of Japanese magazines by title, class, publication frequency, price in sen and publisher, showing the press's periodical output in the period.

metadata.title: [News Agencies in Tokyo]
metadata.description: A short list of Tokyo news agencies giving each agency's founding year and office address, noted as the least developed branch of the press.

metadata.title: Shrines and Ministers
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly number of Shinto shrines of each grade from 1904 to 1908, showing how the total declined over those years.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Buddhist Ministers, 1904–1908]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a multi-year statistical table, bracketed as 'Ministers', giving annual figures for 1904 to 1908 on Buddhist clergy in Japan.

metadata.title: Buddhist Temples and Priests
metadata.caption: Sect possessing over 1,000 temples are as follows:
metadata.description: Shows the number of Buddhist temples and priests of the main sects from 1904 to 1908, giving the scale of Buddhist religious organization in Japan.

metadata.title: Statistics of Churches in Japan (1909)
metadata.description: The table gives 1909 statistics for Protestant, Roman Catholic and Russo-Greek churches in Japan, introducing the section on Christians not affiliated with any church.

metadata.title: Relief Fund
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly apportionments, proceeds, State aids, disbursements and remaining balance of the prefectural Relief Fund for 1904-5 to 1908-9.

metadata.title: [Paupers and Foundlings Supported by the State]
metadata.description: Gives the number of paupers supported at State expense and the amount the State paid, together with foundling numbers and expenses, at the end of each year from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: [Red Cross Society Membership, 1877–1910]
metadata.description: Membership growth of the Red Cross Society of Japan over the years from its founding in 1877 to 1910, shown in two side-by-side columns.

metadata.title: [Women's Patriotic Society Membership, Expenses, Receipts and Fund, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Annual figures for the Women's Patriotic Society's membership, expenses, receipts and fund from 1907 to 1909, illustrating its rapid growth.

metadata.title: [Occupations of Persons Listed Under the Institution]
metadata.description: This continued list gives the occupations of the persons concerned, with the largest group being those whose present occupation is not definitely known, before the text describing the institution's imperial patronage.

metadata.title: The Blind as Bread-Earners
metadata.description: The table classifies the 69,167 blind people in Japan proper, as returned in early 1910, by the profession they followed.

metadata.title: [Membership of Kodo-kwan]
metadata.description: Shows how the membership of the Kodo-kwan jujitsu training hall grew between 1882 and 1910, illustrating the rising popularity of the art.

metadata.title: [Famous Wrestlers of Tokyo]
metadata.description: The text describes professional wrestling's organisation and prestige in Tokyo, and this list gives the physical measurements of the famous wrestlers of the East and West camps.

metadata.title: Data at End of March '09
metadata.description: Summarises the Government Railways Mutual Relief Society's fund receipts and payments from its beginning to March 1909, showing the scale of the workmen's insurance scheme described above.

metadata.title: [Percentage of Workers According to Length of Service]
metadata.description: Following its discussion of change of workers, the text gives the percentage of workers in metal and coal mines by length of service, showing how long mineworkers have stayed.

metadata.title: [Days and Hours of Work by Class of Mine-Worker]
metadata.description: Under the heading on days and hours of work, the table compares the monthly working days and daily working hours of different classes of mineworkers in metal and coal mines.

metadata.title: [Average Wages Per Day in Big Mines, 1906]
metadata.description: Shows the average daily wages paid to different categories of workers at six large mines in 1906, illustrating pay levels across the mining industry as described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Savings at a Few Mines]
metadata.description: Some mines compel workers to save part of their earnings, and this table gives the number of savers and average sums held at four mines.

metadata.title: [Private Primary Schools of Mines]
metadata.description: The page gives the number of teachers, children, yearly expenditure and average cost per child at the private primary schools run by five mines.

metadata.title: [Allowances to Mechanics of the Mitsubishi Dockyards by Rank and Length of Service]
metadata.description: The table lists the allowance paid to dockyard mechanics of each of seven ranks, according to the number of years served, when they die, retire or are dismissed.

metadata.title: [Special Welfare Funds for Employees and Operatives]
metadata.description: Listing the funds set aside for employees and operatives, which the text says are rapidly increasing and being liberally expended for their welfare.

metadata.title: [Estimated Number of Government Officials, Company Officials and Employees by Grade]
metadata.description: Uemastsu's estimate of the 900,000 brain-workers divided by grade, with the expected mortality at 5 per cent, to illustrate the scale of the employment problem.

metadata.title: [Graduates of Schools Completing Study in 1908]
metadata.description: Number of young men finishing secondary or higher schooling in 1908, set against the 45,000 official vacancies to show the surplus of candidates.

metadata.title: [Estimated Monthly Cost of Living of a Mechanic's Family]
metadata.caption: yen
metadata.description: The estimate of monthly living costs for a high-class mechanic's family, with the husband earning 75 sen and wife 25 sen a day, shows the household budget against wages.

metadata.title: [Age Distribution of Factory Workers, 1909]
metadata.description: Results of the Department of Agriculture and Commerce inquiry at end of September 1909 into factory labor at 25 prefectures, showing workers by age and sex.

metadata.title: Child Operatives
metadata.description: Lists the factories employing the largest percentage of child operatives under 16, broken down by age group.

metadata.title: [Girl Workers by Industry and Age Group (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a table of worker proportions by industry; the text then argues that girl workers aged 13 to 20 form over half the labour force.

metadata.title: Working Hours and Days
metadata.description: Shows daily working hours, rest hours, monthly holidays and yearly working days in private factories of 25 prefectures in September 1909, by industry.

metadata.title: [Percentage of Minors by Age Group]
metadata.description: Shows the percentage of minors employed in the factories, split by age group, with the total, as a continuation of the preceding figures.

metadata.title: Age Distinction of Operatives at Government Works
metadata.description: Gives the number of male and female operatives at government works in each factory by age band, showing how many were minors under 20.

metadata.title: [Working Hours, Rest Intervals and Monthly Holidays at Government Works]
metadata.description: Summarises daily work hours, rest intervals, monthly holidays and yearly working days for each industry and sex at government works.

metadata.title: Causes of Poverty
metadata.description: Lists the causes of poverty found among 3,224 men over 41 years old examined in the Tokyo Municipal Poor Asylum between 1902 and 1909.

metadata.title: [Causes of Vagrancy and Number of Persons]
metadata.description: The list gives the number of persons recorded under each assigned cause of vagrancy, ending with a grand total of 3,224.

metadata.title: Wages of Laborers
metadata.caption: Average Daily Wages (yen)
metadata.description: The table gives average daily wages in yen for many trades and laborers in selected years from 1895 to 1909, showing the wage trend over time.

metadata.title: Operatives Classified According to Employment, Giving Only Those Employing Not Less Than 10,000
metadata.description: The table classifies factory operatives by industry for 1908 and 1909, covering only establishments employing at least 10,000 persons, showing male, female and total numbers.

metadata.title: Stamps in Civil Suits
metadata.description: Gives the stamp duty payable on civil suits according to the value of the object of the suit, with rules for surcharges, non-property suits and appeals.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts, at End of 1909
metadata.description: Shows the number of courts, judges and procurators at each court level at the end of 1909, with 1908 totals for comparison.

metadata.title: No. of Cases During 1909
metadata.description: Gives the number of civil, criminal and prosecution cases handled by the Supreme and Appeal Courts in 1909, with monthly averages per court and per judge.

metadata.title: No. of Cases at District and Local Courts During 1909
metadata.description: Lists case numbers at district and local courts in 1909 by appeal jurisdiction, with monthly averages per court and per judge and procurator.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Court of Cassation
metadata.description: Shows civil cases pending and disposed of at the Court of Cassation for the years 1905 to 1908.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Court of Cassation
metadata.description: Records the number of cases involving foreign parties at the Court of Cassation by nationality of appellant, with outcomes, for 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Shows the number of civil appeal cases in hand and disposed of by the Appeal Courts for 1905 to 1908, separately for appeals from the District Courts and from the Local Courts.

metadata.title: Cases Involving Aliens at the Appeal Courts
metadata.caption: Appeals coming from the District Courts
metadata.description: Lists appeals involving foreign parties at the District Courts that reached the Appeal Courts from 1905 to 1908, by nationality of appellant and how each case ended.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the District Courts
metadata.description: Gives the total civil cases handled by the District Courts from 1905 to 1908, with cases disposed of, remaining in hand, and new cases per 10,000 population.

metadata.title: [Civil Cases Affecting Aliens at the District Courts]
metadata.description: Breaks down the district court civil cases from the preceding table that affected aliens, by nationality of party, showing cases and cases disposed of for 1905 to 1908.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the District Courts
metadata.description: Shows the number of cases heard at the district courts by nature of case, for 1905 to 1908, as a yearly record.

metadata.title: Civil Cases at the Local Courts
metadata.description: Gives the civil case totals at the local courts for 1905 to 1908, including cases disposed of, cases in hand and the rate of new cases per population.

metadata.title: Of the above cases those affecting aliens are as follows:—
metadata.description: Breaks down the civil cases from the previous table that affected aliens, by nationality of party, with cases disposed of, for 1905 to 1908.

metadata.title: Nature of Cases at the Local Court
metadata.description: Shows the local court cases by nature of case for 1905 to 1908, with money matters forming the largest share.

metadata.title: Law Suits of Money Matters at the First Instance Classified
metadata.description: Classifies first-instance money lawsuits by the amount in dispute, with total cases and total money involved, for 1905 to 1908.

metadata.title: Cases of Conciliation Dealt with at the District Courts
metadata.description: Shows yearly figures for conciliation cases handled by the district courts from 1905 to 1908, including outcomes such as settlement, failure and withdrawal.

metadata.title: Nature of Conciliation Cases
metadata.description: Breaks down the conciliation cases of 1905 to 1908 by subject matter, such as personal, land, money and documents.

metadata.title: Cases of Insolvency and No. of Persons Affected
metadata.caption: Cases of Rehabilitation of Civil Rights
metadata.description: Gives yearly counts of insolvency cases with the debtors, creditors and credit involved, and of rehabilitation of civil rights cases sanctioned or rejected, 1905 to 1908.

metadata.title: Criminal Defendants
metadata.description: Gives the number of criminal defendants convicted or found not guilty, by sex, from 1904 to 1908, following the enforcement of the new penal code.

metadata.title: Sentences Carried Out
metadata.description: Shows the number of sentences of each kind actually carried out in 1904 to 1907, giving the penal and confinement punishments imposed.

metadata.title: No. of Major Criminal Cases and No. of Accused
metadata.description: Gives the yearly totals of major criminal cases and of persons accused in them from 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Nature of Accusation and Number of Conviction (in 1907)
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1907 major criminal accusations by offence type, showing convictions, acquittals and others, with the sex split of those convicted.

metadata.title: [Verdicts on Accused, 1904–1906]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly verdict breakdown for accused persons in 1904 to 1906, continuing the conviction analysis of the major criminal cases.

metadata.title: Aliens as Accused
metadata.description: Shows the outcomes of cases in which aliens were accused, by type of sentence, for 1902 to 1906.

metadata.title: Causes of Murder Classified
metadata.caption: (sentence in presence of accused)
metadata.description: Breaks down murder cases by motive (covetousness, adultery, domestic trouble and so on) for several years, showing the causes behind the offences sentenced.

metadata.title: Personal Condition of Accused Charged with Major Crimes
metadata.caption: (cases sentenced in presence of accused)
metadata.description: Shows the age, marital/consort status and literacy of persons whose major-crime cases were sentenced in the accused's presence, for 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Violation of Administrative and Taxation Rules Etc.
metadata.description: Gives the average annual number of cases for each administrative and taxation rule violation, including only categories with at least 1,000 cases, with the 1908 conviction ratio noted.

metadata.title: [Figures for Laws and Regulations Under Which Offences Were Recorded]
metadata.description: A list of figures under various laws and regulations, with a total, whose opening rows continue from the previous page; the printed heading is not visible.

metadata.title: Appeals to the Court of Cassation and Appeal Courts (1907)
metadata.description: Shows the number of appeals to the Court of Cassation and Appeal Courts in 1907, with comparative figures for 1903 to 1906, including cases dealt with and remaining.

metadata.title: Appeals to Appeal Courts and District Courts
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for appeals to appeal courts and district courts from 1903 to 1907, covering appeals received, cases dealt with, cases non-suited or cancelled, and cases remaining.

metadata.title: Average Number of Prison Inmates at End of Year
metadata.description: Shows the average daily number of prison inmates by category at year end, derived from days of confinement, illustrating how the prison population changed from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: New Convictions and Population
metadata.description: Gives the number of persons newly convicted each year and the ratio of convictions per 1,000 of population, 1902–1906.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified
metadata.description: Breaks down new convictions by felony (capital and other), larceny and police offences, with percentages of each and capital punishment per 10,000 population, 1902–1906.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences According to Convicts
metadata.description: Shows the number of convicts by how many times they had been convicted (first to fifth time) and the ratio of repeat offenders per 100 first-time offenders, 1904–1908.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified According to Education
metadata.description: Shows new criminal convictions in each year from 1904 to 1908 split by whether the offender was educated or illiterate, with percentages.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified According to Profession and Property
metadata.description: Gives new convictions for 1904 to 1908 broken down by whether offenders had property and whether they had a profession, with percentages.

metadata.title: New Convictions Classified According to Age
metadata.description: Breaks new convictions for 1904 to 1908 down by age group, with totals and the ratio of children and minors per 100 adults.

metadata.title: Escape of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Records the number of prison inmates who escaped each year from 1902 to 1906, by category, with the average for 1887–1906 and escapes per 1,000 inmates.

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the sickness rate and mortality among prison inmates from 1904 to 1908, illustrating health conditions in the prisons.

metadata.title: No. of Days Work by Prison-Inmates and Earnings
metadata.description: Gives the number of days worked by prison inmates for government and contractors, their earnings and shares given, plus average daily earnings, 1904–1908.

metadata.title: Average Yearly Earnings and Receipts per One Worker
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Lists the average yearly earnings and receipts per prison worker for 1903 to 1908 as a supplement to the days-work and earnings figures.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-Officers and Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the number of prison inmates per prison warder, per turnkey and per female keeper, for 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Revenue of Prisons
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly revenue of prisons, split into ordinary earnings from work, other ordinary receipts, extraordinary receipts and totals, for 1905-6 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prison
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Lists prison expenditure by year, broken into ordinary items (salaries, wages, inmate expenses, others), extraordinary expenditure and total, for 1905-6 to 1909-10.

metadata.title: Prison Expense per 1 Inmate
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the average prison expense per inmate in yen, split into ordinary and extraordinary costs and total, for 1904-5 to 1908-9.

metadata.title: [Summary Judgements at Police Offices, 1909]
metadata.description: Summary judgements at police offices in 1909, showing acquittals with warning and the sentences given, broken down by length of detention and fine size.

metadata.title: Police Offices and Police Force
metadata.description: Numbers of police offices, police officers and men, and population per police officer from 1903 to 1909, showing the growth of the police force.

metadata.title: Suicides and Acts Thereof
metadata.description: Suicides by method and sex from 1904 to 1909, counted by hanging, drowning, edged tools and fire arms.

metadata.title: Suicides by Poisons and Others
metadata.description: Continuation of the table of suicide numbers by means (poisons and other methods), with male and female totals and a grand total for the years shown; the year headings are on the previous page.

metadata.title: Cases of Suicides of Over 200 Classified
metadata.description: Shows the number of suicides of over 200 cases by assigned cause and sex for 1905 to 1909, supporting the classification discussed in the surrounding text.

metadata.title: Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.description: Gives yearly rates of sufferers from robbery, larceny, peculation and fraud from 1904 to 1908, illustrating the level of property crime.

metadata.title: Arrests Police Offences Classified of Over 200 Cases
metadata.description: Lists police arrests for selected offences over 200 cases, from 1903 to 1907, showing trends in surveillance, coining, gambling, homicide and injury.

metadata.title: [Offences and Police Regulation Cases]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of criminal offences and police or tax regulation violations recorded, with the continuing table running from the top of the page into the following section.

metadata.title: The Ratio of Arrests Per 100 Offences
metadata.description: Gives, for each main offence type, the number of arrests per 100 offences over the years '03 to '07, with an overall average row.

metadata.title: Unnatural Deaths
metadata.description: Lists yearly numbers of unnatural deaths by cause, from suicide and murder to accidents and natural calamities, with the yearly totals.

metadata.title: Number of Foundlings
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of foundlings taken in, divided into boys and girls, with yearly totals for 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, total burnt area and the average house and area damage per fire from 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Casualties Concerning Police Affairs
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of police-related casualties, killed and wounded, from 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Rewards with Regard to Police Administration
metadata.description: Gives the number of men receiving police rewards and the total sums of money awarded, by year, from 1906 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Convicts Under Age, November 1907]
metadata.description: Lists the number of convicts under age in November 1907 by age group, showing the census of this class of children at the time.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Convicts Under 20]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of convicts under 20 from 1905 to 1908, a trend the author uses to explain the need for reform houses.

metadata.title: Hospitals, Doctors and Mid-wives
metadata.description: Shows the number of hospitals, doctors (total and per 10,000 population) and mid-wives at the end of each year from 1904 to 1908, illustrating the medical provision available.

metadata.title: Vaccination
metadata.description: Gives the total number of vaccinations performed each year from 1905 to 1909, as vaccination is compulsory in Japan.

metadata.title: Ratio of Successful Vaccination of Persons Tried for the First Time and Second Time or Over
metadata.description: Shows the percentage of successful vaccinations for persons vaccinated for the first time versus those tried a second time or over, from 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified
metadata.caption: (Total No. and relative ratio per 1,000 deaths)
metadata.description: The table gives the number of deaths from each leading cause and its ratio per 1,000 deaths for the years 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Eight Epidemic Diseases and Mortality
metadata.description: The table lists yearly case and death counts for eight epidemic diseases, with the mortality rate per 100 cases, for selected years from 1904 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Cost of Works Undertaken by Different Agencies, 1903-1907]
metadata.description: The table gives the annual cost of river works in Japan from 1903 to 1907, broken down by the agencies that undertook them, showing the central government's and prefectures' shares.

metadata.title: Principal Harbor-Works
metadata.description: The table lists the leading harbours improved by construction works, with the works carried out, dates of beginning and completion, and expenditure in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [Harbour and Port Works, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: The table lists harbour and port works with their nature, start and completion dates and a final figure, continued from the previous page; the text then discusses classification of ports and harbour improvement costs.

metadata.title: [Classification of Civil Engineering Expenses, 1903–1907]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly classification of civil engineering expenditure by category, covering the last five years before the year book's publication, as described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Average Yearly Damage from Floods, Tidal Waves and Typhoons, 1905-1908]
metadata.description: The table gives yearly flood, tidal wave and typhoon damage in yen for 1905 to 1908 and the 1902-8 average, showing the scale of natural-disaster losses to public works.

metadata.title: [Water-Works in Principal Cities]
metadata.description: Listing the most remarkable water-works of the cities, with cost, pipe extension, daily supply, houses served and quantity per day, illustrating the spread of Western-style water supply.

metadata.title: Gross Area
metadata.description: Gives the distribution of the gross agricultural area of Japan proper (excluding Formosa and Saghalien) among private, crown and state land.

metadata.title: [Arable Land Classification, 1908]
metadata.description: Shows the 1908 division of Japan's arable land between paddy fields and upland fields, with the overall total.

metadata.title: [Margin of Reclamation by Region]
metadata.description: Gives, by region, the land inclined under 15 degrees, the area already under tillage, and the remaining unreclaimed area, to show the scope of reclamation.

metadata.title: Forests and Wild Land Converted
metadata.description: Records the yearly area of forest and wild land converted to arable use, with the Hokkaido reclamation figures, showing the progress of reclamation from 1902 to 1908.

metadata.title: [Householders and Farming Population]
metadata.description: Shows the number of farming families and their share of all households in 1903 and 1909, supporting the discussion of the farming population.

metadata.title: Independent Farmers and Tenant Farmers
metadata.caption: (Unit: cho; percentage)
metadata.description: Gives the cultivated area of paddy and upland farms held by owners and by tenants, with each category's share, for 1903, 1908 and 1909.

metadata.title: Taxable Land
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000 cho)
metadata.description: Shows taxable land by category in 1,000 cho for 1904, 1907, 1910 and 1911, as a basis for comparing land area over the years.

metadata.title: [Value of Paddy-fields and Upland Farms by Prefecture]
metadata.description: Shows the official and market values per unit of paddy fields and upland farms in six prefectures, illustrating the productive power of tilled land.

metadata.title: [Average Yield per Tan of Paddy Field]
metadata.description: Gives the average yield per tan of paddy field over successive periods, showing the twenty-year trend of productive power in rice cultivation.

metadata.title: Increase of Tillage Area in Old Japan
metadata.description: Compares average tillage area in old Japan for the periods 1884-93 and 1894-1905, with the rate of increase, to show that upland farms expanded faster than paddy fields.

metadata.title: [Average Farm Area per Farmer's Family by Division]
metadata.description: Gives the average farmland, moor and total area per farmer's family in Shikoku, Kyushu and Hokkaido, supplementing the figures for the Main Island.

metadata.title: Ratio of One-Crop and Two-Crop Farms
metadata.description: Official returns show how paddy fields divided between one-crop and two-crop farming in 1903 and 1909, in cho and as percentages of the total.

metadata.title: Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.description: Approximate areas of land tilled by cattle or horse labour in 1903 and 1909, shown in cho and as percentages, for paddy fields and upland farms.

metadata.title: [Projects Sanctioned and Area Adjusted, 1900–1909]
metadata.description: The table gives, year by year from 1900 to 1909, the number of farm-adjustment projects sanctioned and the area in cho actually adjusted, supporting the text's account of the programme's progress.

metadata.title: [Fertilizer Manufacturers and Importers, 1908–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the number of fertilizer manufacturers and importers for 1909 and 1908, showing the rapid growth in the fertilizer trade over that year.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows rice cultivated area, production, and export and import quantities and values for 1904 to 1906, illustrating the staple farm product's trade and output.

metadata.title: [Rice Yield, 1907-1910 and Normal Yield]
metadata.description: The continuing table gives yearly rice-crop figures for 1907 to 1910 and a normal yield, which the note explains was averaged from the preceding seven years.

metadata.title: [Yield per Tan by Variety of Rice Plant]
metadata.description: The list compares average rice output per tan across early, middle and late varieties at Government Experimental Farms, showing the middle variety to be most productive.

metadata.title: [Average Price of Clean Rice, Export and Import per Koku]
metadata.description: This table shows the average price per koku of clean rice in Tokyo and of rice exports and imports for periods from 1887 to 1909, following the statement on per capita consumption.

metadata.title: [Rice, Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat Output, 1905-1910]
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: The table gives annual barley, naked barley, wheat and total grain output in thousands of koku for 1905 to 1910, with a normal average yield per tan.

metadata.title: [Area of Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat Cultivation, 1910]
metadata.description: Shows the 1910 acreage of barley, naked barley and wheat, split between paddy-field and upland farms, to illustrate where these second crops are grown.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly production of miscellaneous grains such as millets, buckwheat and maize from 1905 to 1909, which are grown mainly in mountainous districts.

metadata.title: Beans, Sweet Potato and Potato
metadata.description: Gives yearly production of beans, sweet potatoes and potatoes from 1905 to 1909, showing the secondary food crops that supplement rice in the diet.

metadata.title: Some Special Crops
metadata.caption: (in Kwan)
metadata.description: Shows annual output of indigo, tobacco, cotton, hemp and rape seed over 1905–1909, supporting the text's remarks on tobacco's progress and the decline of cotton and indigo.

metadata.title: Other Minor Crops
metadata.description: Lists area under cultivation and output of several minor crops such as radish, carrot, burdock, konnyaku, ginger, chilies and lily, giving the main non-cereal crops of the country.

metadata.title: [Fibre and Other Minor Crops, Continued]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a table listing minor agricultural crops such as China grass, paper mulberry, matting rush and peppermint with their quantities and values.

metadata.title: Mulberry Trees Area
metadata.description: Shows the area under mulberry trees from 1904 to 1910, alongside a note on government funding to encourage mulberry planting for sericulture.

metadata.title: Output of Cocoons
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for silkworm egg cards hatched, cocoon output and cocoon grades, with output per card, from 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: Cocoons by Season
metadata.caption: (1000 koku)
metadata.description: Shows cocoon output by season (spring, summer, autumn) with totals and seasonal percentages for 1905 to 1910.

metadata.title: Output of Raw Silk
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly output of raw silk, waste silk, floss silk and silkworm eggs by method from 1907 to 1910.

metadata.title: Production in 1910
metadata.description: Summarises the 1910 silk production by number of establishments, product type (raw silk, tama, noshi, kibiso, waste) in kwan and yen, and total value.

metadata.title: [Raw Silk, Noshi, Kibiso and Waste Export by Kind]
metadata.description: The top rows give the value and quantity of the silk categories by kind (filature, frame, tama) that the surrounding export statistics for the year refer to.

metadata.title: [Export of Shinshu Filature Silk by Kind and Highest Quotation]
metadata.caption: Export in 1,000 kin by kind and highest quotation (in yen) of Shinshu Filature No. 1 per 100 kin at Yokohama.
metadata.description: Shows the Shinshu export of silk in 1,000 kin by grade for 1908 and 1909, with the highest Yokohama quotation for Shinshu Filature No. 1.

metadata.title: Leading District of Raw Silk Production
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures for raw silk production, with families engaged in 1909 and the value of production in 1908 and 1909.

metadata.title: Import (from China)
metadata.description: Shows annual Chinese imports of ordinary cocoons and tussah silk, in quantity and value, for 1905 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Silk Conditioning, Weighing and Testing Returns]
metadata.description: Returns of raw silk conditioning, weighing, boiling-off and quality tests at the government testing establishment, showing lots, weights and average loss for each year from 1904 to 1910.

metadata.title: Japanese and Foreign Exporters of Raw Silk
metadata.description: Shows the number of bales of raw silk exported annually from 1904 to 1910 by Japanese and foreign firms, with each group's share of the total as percentages.

metadata.title: Area of Tea Plantations and Number of Manufactures
metadata.description: Shows the acreage of tea plantations and the number of tea manufactories for 1904 to 1909, presented in two side-by-side blocks.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Tea
metadata.description: Gives the annual output in kwan of green, black and oolong teas, with totals, for 1905 to 1910.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production
metadata.description: Lists the three leading tea-producing districts on each side of the table, with their output and value of tea.

metadata.title: Export of Teas
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of tea exported from 1902 to 1909, the earliest year printed being hard to read.

metadata.title: Destination of Green Tea Exported
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of green tea exported from Japan, 1904 to 1909, by destination (U.S.A., Canada, China, others), supporting the trade statistics given in the year book.

metadata.title: [Colts of Improved Breed Reared, 1906–1910]
metadata.description: The text notes that the four kinds of establishments have produced many improved colts over the last five years, and this figure line gives the yearly numbers reared from 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Castration of Horses, 1905–1907]
metadata.description: Shows the number of horses castrated, animals disabled or dead, and the grants and compensation paid, which the author uses to argue that compulsory castration may be needed.

metadata.title: Number of Horses in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the yearly totals of horses in Japan by domestic, cross-bred and foreign types, with foaling and deaths, from 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Stallions for Service at End of 1910]
metadata.description: Lists the stallions available for service throughout the country at the end of 1910, by ownership and by native, cross and foreign breed.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the yearly national cattle count from 1904 to 1909, broken down by native, cross-bred and foreign stock, with calving and death figures.

metadata.title: Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of sheep, goats and swine in Japan from 1904 to 1909, supporting the discussion of stock farming.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Lists the yearly number of slaughter houses and animals slaughtered in Japan from 1904 to 1909.

metadata.title: Leading Stock Farms
metadata.description: A list of the leading stock farms in Japan, mainly in Hokkaido, with their location, kind of stock and ownership.

metadata.title: [Government and Private Pastures (continued)]
metadata.description: The continuing list gives the chapter's pastures and farms with their location, type of stock or farming, and owner, before the text on the Shimosa and Koiwai pastures.

metadata.title: Number of Households keeping Poultry
metadata.description: The table gives the numbers and values of fowls, ducks and eggs for 1907 and 1908, illustrating the modest state of poultry raising in Japan.

metadata.title: Leading Poultry Districts (1910)
metadata.description: Lists the five leading prefectures for poultry in 1910, giving household numbers and the value of fowls and eggs.

metadata.title: Leading Dairy Districts in 1909
metadata.description: Gives the leading dairy prefectures in 1909 with dairy and milk cow numbers and milk output and value, with totals and figures for 1907 and 1908.

metadata.title: [Animal Epidemics]
metadata.description: Records annual animal epidemic cases among horses and cattle, covering glanders, farcy, anthrax and rinderpest, for 1903 to 1909.

metadata.title: Fruits in 1907-9
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of trees and the yield of each principal fruit kind in Japan for 1907 to 1909, giving the national agricultural picture for fruit growing.

metadata.title: Exports of Fruits and Vegetables
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Gives the value in yen of Japan's exports of fruits and vegetables for each year from 1903 to 1909, showing the growth of this trade.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.caption: (Relative percentage)
metadata.description: The strata existing in Japan are classified by relative percentage into sedimentary and igneous rocks, showing how much of the country each geological formation covers.

metadata.caption: Momme=2.411 duts. Kin=1.607 lbs. (Troy). Kwan=10.047 lbs. (Troy). Koku=39.703 gallons.

metadata.title: [Mineral Output, 1904–1909 (Continued From Previous Page)]

metadata.title: [Output of Minerals, 1902–1909]
metadata.description: Annual output of iron, pyrites, antimony, manganese, coal, sulphur and petroleum with values, 1902–1909, shown before the Yamagano Gold Mine note.

metadata.title: [Gold and Silver Output, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the combined gold and silver output in momme for 1907 to 1909, shown at the head of the Mines and Mining section before the detailed mine accounts.

metadata.title: Ushio and Oguchi Gold Mines: Production
metadata.description: Shows recent annual gold and silver production of the Ushio and Oguchi mines, the two most important of the neighbouring gold mines described in the text.

metadata.title: [Sado Mine Production, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the annual output of gold, silver and copper from the Sado mine, following the description of its veins and ore quality.

metadata.title: [Ikuno Silver Mine Production, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of gold, silver and copper at the Ikuno silver mines in Tajima Province from 1907 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Gold, Silver and Copper Output, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Summarises the combined yearly gold, silver and copper output of the mines described in this part of the section, showing production for 1907 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Ashio Copper Mine Output, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the annual silver and copper output of the Ashio copper mine for 1907 to 1909, following the description of its lodes and ore.

metadata.title: [Copper Production, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the annual copper output in kin for 1907 to 1909, following the account of the Tachikawa copper mine and its ore.

metadata.title: Injurious Ingredients
metadata.caption: (per 100 ores.)
metadata.description: Compares the phosphorous, sulphur and copper content of Kamaishi ores, Taiya ores and sand iron, to show sand iron contains fewer injurious ingredients.

metadata.title: [Kamaishi Mine Output, 1907-1909]
metadata.description: The table gives annual output of gold, copper and iron from the Kamaishi mine for 1907 to 1909, illustrating the mine's production after Ichibei Tanaka's improvements.

metadata.title: [Gold, Silver and Copper Output of Principal Mines]
metadata.description: Lists the annual gold, silver and copper output of the principal Japanese mines and the companies or persons working them, introducing the section on minerals.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Coals from the Principal Coal-Fields]
metadata.description: Gives proximate analyses (water, volatile matter, coke, ash, sulphur), caking qualities, specific gravity and calorific power of coals from the main fields, as the coal section introduces them.

metadata.title: [Hokkaido Coal Output, 1908 and 1909]
metadata.description: Following the description of the Hokkaido coalfields, this table gives coal output by colliery for 1909 and 1908 in million tons.

metadata.title: [Honshu Coal Output, 1908 and 1909]
metadata.description: After describing the Iwaki-Hitachi coalfield, the text gives the total output of the Honshu coal mines for the last two years.

metadata.title: Other Principal Coal Mines in Chiku-Ho District and Saga and Nagasaki
metadata.caption: (in 1.000 metric tons)
metadata.description: Listing the other principal coal mines of the Chikuho district and Saga and Nagasaki, with their output for 1909 and 1908 and their owners.

metadata.title: [Miike Coal-Field Output]
metadata.description: Giving the annual output of the Miike coal-field in metric tons for 1908 and 1909, in the Miike section.

metadata.title: [Baumé and Price of Crude Oil by Oil-Field]
metadata.description: Shows the Baumé gravity and price per koku of crude oil from four fields, illustrating that Nishiyama and Higashiyama oil yields more lamp-oil than Niitsu.

metadata.title: [Output of Principal Oil-Fields, 1908 and 1909]
metadata.description: Gives the output of the principal oil-fields in 1908 and 1909 in koku and their percentage share of total Japanese crude oil output.

metadata.title: [Production of Echigo Oil-Fields by Product Classification]
metadata.caption: (in koku)
metadata.description: Classifies the Echigo oil production in 1908 and 1909 by product type (volatile, lamp, solar, heavy and lubricant oil), in koku.

metadata.title: [Relative Percentage of Oil Products to Total Crude Oil]
metadata.description: Shows the percentage share of each product type in total crude oil production for 1907 and 1908.

metadata.title: [Oil-Wells Existing at End of 1908]
metadata.description: Counts the wells in each Echigo oil-field at the end of 1908 by digging method: machine-bored, Kazusabori, and hand-dug.

metadata.title: Number of Mine-Workers at Principal Mines
metadata.caption: (At the end of June)
metadata.description: Gives the number of mine-workers at principal mines, by type of mine, at the end of June for 1904 to 1909, as part of the mining industry survey.

metadata.title: Work and Wages of Mine-Workers
metadata.description: Shows the monthly working days and average daily working hours of the main classes of mine-workers in metal mines and collieries, based on Mining Bureau research.

metadata.title: Wages (in Yen) at Metal-Mines
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Lists daily wages in yen at metal mines for each class of worker, separately for males and females, giving maximum and minimum rates.

metadata.title: Wages at Collieries (yen)
metadata.description: Gives the maximum and minimum daily wages in yen paid to various classes of male and female colliery workers.

metadata.title: Accidents in the Mines
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of mine accidents and the resulting deaths, severe injuries and other casualties from 1903 to 1909.

metadata.title: Imports and Export Mineral Production
metadata.caption: Exports (in 1,000); Imports (in 1,000
metadata.description: Lists yearly exports of copper, coal and sulphur and imports of iron and steel and petroleum from 1904 to 1909, with the trade total noted below.

metadata.title: [Fishing-Boats by Year, 1905–1909]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of fishing-boats in Japan from 1905 to 1909, split into total, newly built, worn-out and European boats, illustrating the fishing fleet's size.

metadata.title: Accidents to Fishing-Boats and Casualties to Fishermen
metadata.description: Shows the number of fishing boats lost by accident in each category and the resulting killed, wounded and missing crew, for 1909 with 1908 and 1907 for comparison.

metadata.title: The Value of Catches and of Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of fishery catches and of marine products from 1904 to 1909, showing the trend in the fishing industry.

metadata.title: Value of Catch and Commercial Value of Principal Kinds of Fish, Shellfish, etc.
metadata.description: Lists the catch quantity and commercial value of the main fish and shellfish kinds in 1909.

metadata.title: Principal Kinds of Manufactured Marine Products
metadata.description: Lists the quantities and values of the principal manufactured marine products, such as dried and salted fish and fertiliser, in the period covered.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Catches and Marine Production (1909)
metadata.description: Shows the value of catches and marine products for the leading fishing districts of Japan in 1909, as a basis for the discussion of fisheries output.

metadata.title: Aquiculture
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of aquaculture products from 1905 to 1909 by species, with a total, showing the growth of cultivated fisheries.

metadata.title: [Deep-Sea Fishery Development, 1906–1909]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of deep-sea fishing by junks, sailers and steamers, with crew, tonnage and value, including both aided and unaided vessels, from 1906 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Deep-Sea Fishery in Japan Proper, 1909]
metadata.description: Gives the 1909 returns for the various branches of deep-sea fishery in Japan proper, by junks, sailers, steamers, crew and value, to illustrate the situation of the industry.

metadata.title: [Sealing Vessels, Fur Seals and Others, 1907-1910]
metadata.description: Shown beneath the sealing discussion, this table gives the number of sealing vessels and the catches of fur seals and other animals for each year from 1907 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Salt Production, Area, Furnaces, Value and Price, 1904–1909]
metadata.description: The table gives annual salt field area, furnace numbers, production, value and average price per koku from 1904 to 1909, illustrating the salt industry after the state monopoly was adopted.

metadata.title: Area of Forests (1 cho=2½ acres)
metadata.caption: (At the end of 1909)
metadata.description: Shows the area of forests by ownership category at the end of 1909, split into protection, utilization and percentage forests, to introduce the forestry chapter.

metadata.title: [Forest Area of Prefectures Containing Not Less Than 500,000 Cho]
metadata.description: The page lists the prefectures of northern and central Japan proper that contain at least 500,000 cho of forest land, to show where the forests lie.

metadata.title: [Forest Yield by Species, 1909-1910]
metadata.description: The forest yield for 1909-1910, excluding Formosa and Saghalien, is returned by species, showing timber and fagot quantities and values to illustrate the low financial return from forestry.

metadata.title: [Value of Forest Products by Ownership]
metadata.description: Shows the value of timber, fagots and total forest products by ownership category (State, Crown, Percentage, public and private), illustrating the scale of forest output.

metadata.title: [State Forests Receipts and Expenses]
metadata.description: Gives the receipts, expenses and resulting profit of State forest administration for the years 1903-4 to 1909-10, supporting the discussion of the rate of profit.

metadata.title: [Principal Forest Products in Export and Import Trade]
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Lists the principal forest products figuring in Japan's export and import trade by year from 1903 to 1909, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [Working Plan Forest Systems and Barran Area]
metadata.description: Shows the percentage division of the working plan for State forests among forest management systems, plus the barren area and total.

metadata.title: [Rotation System for Principal Trees]
metadata.description: Lists the rotation periods in years adopted under the working plan for each principal tree species.

metadata.title: Total Volume of Felling (Shakujime) and Conversion
metadata.description: Gives the total volume of felling (shakujime) and conversion of timbers and fagots by the Government yards for 1907 to 1909.

metadata.title: Hewn Boards etc.
metadata.description: Shows the yearly production of hewn boards and similar timber from 1907 to 1909.

metadata.title: Private Sawing Yards
metadata.description: Lists the number of private sawing yards, capital, wood converted and motive power for Akita and Osaka, the leading districts, as returned by the Department of Agriculture and Commerce.

metadata.title: [Number of Shooting Licenses Issued, 1904–1910]
metadata.description: Shows the number of shooting licenses of classes A and B issued in selected years, illustrating the sharp fall in sportsmen after the fees were raised.

metadata.title: [Industrial Companies: Number, Paid-up Capital and Reserves, 1902–1903]
metadata.description: Under the heading on investment in industrial enterprises, this small table gives the number of companies with paid-up capital and reserves for 1902 and 1903.

metadata.title: [Number and Paid-Up Capital of Industrial Establishments, 1904–1909]

metadata.title: Industrial Establishments Classified by Amount of Investment
metadata.description: Shows, for 1908 and 1909, the number of companies and paid-up capital of each industry whose paid-up capital is ¥500,000 or more, with spinning absorbing the most capital.

metadata.title: [Industries Continued from Previous Page: Ice to Porcelains and Earthenware]
metadata.description: Continuation of a table listing the numbers of various industrial activities and their figures; the page's text then notes that most of the 40 industries started after the opening of the country.

metadata.title: [Districts Containing Companies with Over Yen 5,000,000 Paid-up Capital, 1909]

metadata.title: Factories and Employees
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of factories (by motive or manual power) and the number of male, female and total operatives employed in them from 1899 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Motive Powers, 1909]
metadata.description: A note giving the number of engines and horse power for each kind of motive power in 1909, with extra electrical or pounds figures recorded in footnotes.

metadata.title: Kind of Factories Classified
metadata.description: Classifies the factories by industry, showing how many run by motors, how many do not, and the daily average number of employees.

metadata.title: [Industrial Establishments by Industry, Continued]
metadata.description: The top of the page concludes a table of industrial workshops and their figures by industry, with a total row, before the article on the spinning industry begins.

metadata.title: [Silk Spinning Statistics, 1906-1910]
metadata.description: Statistics for the silk spinning industry over 1906-1910, showing companies, capital, output, yarn trade and cloth production, presented to illustrate recent development of the trade.

metadata.title: [Cotton Spinning Statistics, 1908–1910]
metadata.description: The top rows continue a multi-year table of cotton spinning figures whose column headings appear on the previous page; the headings are not visible here.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Cotton Spinning (1909)
metadata.description: This table lists the leading cotton-spinning districts in 1909 with their mills, capital, spindles, operators and yarn output, illustrating the industry's regional scale.

metadata.title: [Cotton Spinning Statistics, 1908-1910 (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page carries the final rows of a multi-year cotton spinning statistics table, whose column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Cotton Spinning (1909)

metadata.title: Imports by Countries

metadata.title: [Imports by Country, Continued]

metadata.title: Staple Items of Trade Classified
metadata.caption: Exports (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the values of the main export commodities for 1907 to 1910, under the heading Staple Items of Trade Classified, in yen thousands.

metadata.title: [Foreign Trade: Exports and Imports by Commodities]
metadata.description: The table gives the values of Japan's exports and imports by commodity group across four years, with totals, showing the overall structure of foreign trade.

metadata.title: Staple Articles of Over Yen 1,000,000
metadata.caption: Exports (In yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The table lists the export articles each worth over one million yen, with yearly values from 1907 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Exports, Principal Articles (continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a table of principal export articles, with year-by-year values for each commodity, the column year headings having appeared on the previous page.

metadata.title: Imports (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of principal imported articles for the years 1907 to 1910, given in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [Imports of Manufactured Goods and Raw Materials, Continued]
metadata.description: The page continues a list of imported goods, with figures for four columns of values or quantities whose headings appear on an earlier page.
