metadata.description: Custom returns comparing the share of Asia, Europe and America in Japan's trade, showing exports to and imports from each country for 1909 and 1910.

metadata.title: America
metadata.description: Foreign trade figures by American countries and regions, with the column years given on the previous page, showing values for the United States, British America, Australia and others.

metadata.title: Trade with China
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Values of Japan's trade with China from 1906 to 1910, listing exports to and imports from China by commodity in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Trade with British India
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Values of Japan's trade with British India from 1906 to 1910, listing exports to and imports from India by commodity in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Trade with Dutch India
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yen value of Japan's trade with Dutch India in exports and imports for 1906 to 1910, by commodity.

metadata.title: Trade with Dutch Philippines
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yen value of Japan's trade with the Dutch Philippines in exports and imports for 1906 to 1910, by commodity.

metadata.title: Trade with Great Britain
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yen value of Japan's exports to Great Britain for 1906 to 1910, by commodity.

metadata.title: [Imports by Commodity, Cotton Goods, Wool and Machinery, 1906–1910]
metadata.description: Shows the values of listed imports from a country in the years 1906 to 1910, continuing a table begun on the previous page.

metadata.title: Trade with France
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly values of trade between Japan and France, with exports to France and imports from France, for 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: Trade with Germany
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly values of trade between Japan and Germany, with exports to Germany and imports from Germany, for 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Trade Items Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: Continuation of a list of Japanese trade items (iron, rail, indigo, paper, sugar) with yearly values from 1906 to 1910 carried over from the previous page.

metadata.title: Trade with Italy
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's exports of raw silk and noshi silk to Italy, by year from 1906 to 1910, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Trade with Belgium
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's exports of fish-oil to Belgium and imports of wool, iron and paper from Belgium, 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: Trade with Austria Hungary
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's exports of noshi silk and rice to Austria-Hungary and imports of paper and sugar from it, 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: Trade with U. S. A.
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists Japan's exports to the United States by commodity, such as raw silk, tea, camphor and porcelain, with values for 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Imports of Principal Articles, 1906–1910]
metadata.description: Lists the chief articles imported in each year from 1906 to 1910, with values shown as dashes where none were recorded.

metadata.title: Trade with Canada
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's trade with Canada, listing exports to Canada and imports from Canada for 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: Trade with Australia
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's trade with Australia, listing exports to Australia and imports from Australia for 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: Japanese and Foreigners in Foreign Trade
metadata.description: Shows how the share of foreign trade at Kobe and Yokohama was divided between Japanese and foreign merchants at selected dates.

metadata.title: [Percentage Shares of Nationalities in Kobe Trade]
metadata.description: Shows the percentage share of each major nationality in the export and import trade of Kobe, as introduced by the sentence that the percentages are as follows.

metadata.title: Steam-Vessels That Entered From and Cleared to Foreign Countries
metadata.caption: (1,000 tons)
metadata.description: Gives the tonnage of steam-vessels entering from and clearing to foreign countries by nationality, showing the growing share of Japanese shipping over the years.

metadata.title: [Foreign Trade Statistics, 1897-1910]
metadata.description: The figures show Japan's total and dutiable imports, duty-free share, customs revenue and average tariff percentage from 1897 to 1910, given as background to the tariff revision discussed below.

metadata.title: [National Defence Expenditure, 1902-3 to 1911-12]
metadata.caption: (Figures in unit of yen 1000)
metadata.description: Showing how national defence appropriations for the Army, Navy and in total rose sharply after the War of 1904-5, illustrating the expansion of armaments described in the text.

metadata.title: Under Control of Brigade Headquarters at Yokosuka
metadata.description: Lists the Siege Artillery units stationed under Yokosuka Brigade Headquarters, with their strength and whether they have horses, under the reorganized system after the Russo-Japanese War.

metadata.title: Under Control of Brigade Headquarters at Shimonoseki
metadata.description: Lists the Siege Artillery units stationed under Shimonoseki Brigade Headquarters, with their strength and horse provision, as part of the new Siege Artillery organization.

metadata.title: Organization of the Field Artillery Brigades
metadata.description: The Field Artillery Brigade was reorganized from three regiments to two per brigade, with three brigades, and the printed list shows how the regiments are stationed.

metadata.title: Murata's Magazine-Rifle of 1905 Type
metadata.description: The article describes the latest improvement of Murata's rifle, and this table gives the specifications of the 1905 magazine-rifle for infantry and cavalry use.

metadata.title: Guns Now in Service
metadata.description: Guns were first cast in 1885 at the Osaka Arsenal, and this lettered list gives the seven kinds of guns in service.

metadata.title: Quick-Firing Field-Guns of '98 Type
metadata.description: Specifications of the quick-firing field-guns of the 1898 type, given as an epitome of the official particulars that follow the introductory sentence.

metadata.title: Quick-Firing Mountain-Guns of '98 Type
metadata.description: Particulars of the quick-firing mountain-guns of the 1898 type, noted as much like the field-guns above but somewhat smaller.

metadata.title: Field-Gun of '05 Type
metadata.description: Particulars of the 1905 model field-gun, listed as the last of the artillery specifications on this page.

metadata.title: [Field Gun Specifications (continued)]
metadata.description: Continuing the specifications of a field gun, this list gives its length, shell and shrapnel weights, explosive charges, fuses and bullet count.

metadata.title: 10 Centimetre Canet-Gun of '05 Type
metadata.description: This gives the technical specifications of the 10 centimetre Canet gun of the 1905 type, covering its dimensions, ranges, weights and shell types.

metadata.title: 15 (12) Centimetre Canet-Gun of '05 Type
metadata.description: This gives the technical specifications of the 15 (12) centimetre Canet gun of the 1905 type, with bracketed alternative figures, covering dimensions, velocities, ranges, weights and shell.

metadata.title: [Shot Specifications: Cast Iron Armored Shell and Shrapnel]
metadata.description: Continuation of the ordnance specification list, giving weights, explosives and fuses for the shot of the cast iron armored shell and shrapnel types.

metadata.title: 24 Centimetre Canet-Gun
metadata.description: Ordnance specifications for the 24 centimetre Canet gun, listing calibre, velocities, range, elevation, barrel length and shot details.

metadata.title: 28 Centimetre Howitzer
metadata.description: Ordnance specifications for the 28 centimetre howitzer, listing calibre, velocities, range, angles, barrel length and shot details.

metadata.title: Result of Conscription Service Examination
metadata.description: Shows the results of the conscription service examinations for 1909 and 1910, giving the number examined and how many were found able-bodied, evaded service, volunteered, or were otherwise exempted.

metadata.title: Distribution of the Standing Army
metadata.description: The page lists the distribution of the standing army by division, showing each unit's brigade, regiment, battalion and garrison locality.

metadata.title: Divisions and Garrison Towns
metadata.description: Lists the army divisions by number, each with its garrison towns and regiment numbers, as part of the Army and Navy section.

metadata.title: Division Garrisons and Regimental Numbers
metadata.description: Shows, for each division's garrison town, the sequence of regimental numbers printed in brace groups on the rotated lower part of the page.

metadata.title: [Garrison Units by Division, Lower Section]
metadata.description: The page shows a rotated table listing the garrison regiments of the 11th to 18th Divisions of the Japanese Army, with the division names printed at the foot of each column.

metadata.title: Age-Limit in the Active Service
metadata.description: Gives the maximum age at which officers of each rank may remain in active service, set out in two parallel columns from Sub-Lieutenant to Marshal, following the promotion rules.

metadata.title: Vessels About to Be Completed
metadata.description: Lists the warships in the cradle that are expected to be commissioned within a year or two, with their class, name, displacement and builder.

metadata.title: At Time of the Outbreak
metadata.description: Compares the strength of the Japanese Navy at the moment the war broke out, by class of vessel, number and tonnage.

metadata.title: Present Strength
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese Navy's present strength by class of vessel, number and tonnage, for comparison with the position at the outbreak of the war.

metadata.title: Main Force Available in 1910
metadata.description: Captain Oguri enumerates the warships of the Powers available in the Pacific in 1910, according to the programs they have adopted.

metadata.title: Main Force Available in 1917
metadata.description: Captain Oguri enumerates the warships of the Powers available in the Pacific in 1917, according to the programs they have adopted.

metadata.title: [Naval Cadet Academy Admissions and Applicants, 1906–1909]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly numbers admitted, examination results and applicant totals for the Naval Cadet Academy over the last four years, as the text introduces it.

metadata.title: [Candidates for Entrance Examination, 1906–1909]
metadata.description: Shows yearly admissions, examination results and applicant numbers for the military entrance examinations from 1906 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Conscripts and Volunteers, 1905–1909]
metadata.description: Explains that the navy relies more on volunteers than conscripts, and gives the yearly numbers of each entering service from 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Battleships
metadata.description: Lists the battleships of the Japanese fleet with their displacement, length, launch year, speed, torpedo tubes, armour and main armament.

metadata.title: [Japanese Navy Warships: Battleships, Armored Cruisers and Protected Cruisers]
metadata.description: A list of Japanese navy warships by class, giving tonnage, year, speed and armament figures for battleships, armored cruisers and protected cruisers; the printed column headings are not on this page.

metadata.title: [Principal Vessels of the Japanese Navy: Armoured Cruisers, Gun-Boats and Despatch-Boats]
metadata.description: A list of Japanese navy vessels giving tonnage, horse-power, build year, speed, gun counts and main armament; column headings are not printed in these crops, so the column meanings are inferred and marked as unlabelled.

metadata.title: Torpedo-Boat Destroyers
metadata.description: The list names Japan's torpedo-boat destroyers with their tonnage and year of completion, showing the navy's fleet of such vessels at the time.

metadata.title: Age Limit of Officer in Active Service
metadata.description: Lists the maximum age limits for officers of each rank or equivalent while still in active service in the navy.

metadata.title: Office and Bluejackets on Active Service
metadata.caption: (Compiled at the end of the year)
metadata.description: Gives the year-end strength of the navy by rank group, showing admirals, officers, warrant officers, bluejackets and cadets for 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: States Aid for Preservation on National Treasures
metadata.description: Shows state preservation aid for national treasures from 1897 to 1909, split into structural articles, treasures and totals, supporting the text on the Old Temples Preservation Commission.

metadata.title: Number of Treasures
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of buildings and treasures recorded, 1897 to 1911, with totals, giving a statistical background to the art and craft preservation discussion.

metadata.title: Exhibits Submitted to the Committee from the First
metadata.description: Gives the number of exhibits submitted to and selected by the Hanging Committee for each National Art Exhibition from 1907 to 1911, by Japanese painting, foreign painting and sculpture.

metadata.title: Recipients of 2nd Prizes
metadata.description: Lists the artists who received prizes in each National Art Exhibition from 1907 to 1911, under the Japanese painting, foreign painting and sculpture categories.

metadata.title: [Objects Exhibited at the Tokyo Museum, End of 1910]
metadata.description: Lists the art objects exhibited at the Tokyo Museum at the end of 1910, split into Fine Art and Applied Art sections, illustrating the museum's holdings described in the text.

metadata.title: [Provincial Grants to the Relief Fund]
metadata.caption: (Unit: yen, as printed above each column)
metadata.description: The table lists the yen amounts allocated to each provincial governor's fund, the grants whose use the text describes as work, education and relief in bad years.

metadata.title: Temperature
metadata.description: Monthly and average temperatures at Korean stations, drawn from Japanese or other consulate meteorological records, to describe Korea's climate.

metadata.title: Rainfalls
metadata.description: Rainfall amounts in millimetres for January, August and the year total at four Korean stations, showing the climate of the peninsula.

metadata.title: No. of Days of Rainfalls and Snowfalls
metadata.description: Number of days with rainfall or snowfall at five Korean stations, given for February, July and as a total, as part of the climate data.

metadata.title: The Foreign Residents in Korea
metadata.description: Number of Chinese, European and American residents in Korea at the end of 1909 compared with 1908, by nationality, with the 1909 total given in the text as 10,427.

metadata.title: Budget for 1911-12
metadata.caption: (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The budget figures for 1911-12 show ordinary and extraordinary revenue and expenditure of Chosen, giving the government's fiscal plan for the year.

metadata.description: This table lists Chosen's outstanding government loans with their interest rates, amounts, dates, redemption years and creditors.

metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: This table gives the annual value of Chosen's foreign trade from 1903 to 1910, separating merchandise and specie and bullion imports and exports.

metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: This table shows the yearly export values from 1906 to 1910 of three main articles: beans and peas, rice and live stock.

metadata.description: Continuation of the export list, showing values of principal export goods across five periods; the column headings appear on the preceding page.

metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Import values for leading goods across five periods, with sheeting entries printed in a split layout; the year headings are not printed on this page.

metadata.description: Export and import values at the three leading Korean ports (Ninsen, Fusan, Chinnampho) for 1905 to 1909.

metadata.description: The table gives trade figures for the individual Korean ports and towns, showing exports and imports for each place across five periods, as a continuation of the port statistics.

metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: This table shows Korea's trade with each foreign country, with imports and exports in yen for each year from 1906 to 1910, given to show the main trading partners.

metadata.title: [Peoples' Banks in Korea — Loans from Government, Deposits, Loans, Overdraft and Bills Discounted]
metadata.description: Shows the financial position of the three Peoples' Banks in Korea, covering government loans, deposits, loans, overdrafts and bills discounted.

metadata.title: [Industrial Banks in Korea — Deposits, Loans, Overdraft and Bills Discounted]
metadata.description: Gives the deposits, loans, overdrafts and bills discounted of the three Japanese banks in Korea, the Industrial Bank not undertaking ordinary banking.

metadata.title: [Japanese Immigrants in Korea, by Period]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Japanese houses, men, women and total immigrants in Korea at half-yearly dates from December 1906 to December 1909, illustrating the rapid growth of Japanese settlement.

metadata.title: [Property Held by Japanese in Korea]
metadata.description: Estimates of the property held by Japanese in the principal Korean places of importance, giving land, buildings and their value, as part of the Property section.

metadata.title: [Existing States of the Fishing Industry in Korea]
metadata.description: Introduced in the Fishery section, this table compares Korean and Japanese boats, fishermen and catch values to show how much the Korean fishing industry lags behind.

metadata.title: [Wages of Laborers at Various Places in Korea]
metadata.description: Gives the local wage rates for Japanese and Korean laborers at seven Korean places, explaining that Chinese laborers have increasingly settled there because of their lower wages.

metadata.title: Governmental School
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools, teachers and pupils in Korea's government schools at the end of October 1910, as part of the account of Korean education.

metadata.title: Semi-Public
metadata.description: Gives the schools, teachers and pupils of semi-public industrial and elementary schools in Korea at the end of October 1910.

metadata.title: Public Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of public elementary schools, teachers and pupils in Korea at the end of October 1910.

metadata.title: Private
metadata.description: Lists private schools in Korea by kind, with their teachers and pupils at the end of October 1910; religious schools are noted as largely missionary-run.

metadata.title: [Schools, Teachers and Pupils in Chosen]
metadata.description: Summarises the number of schools, teachers and pupils in each kind of educational institution in Chosen (Korea), with totals.

metadata.title: [Korean Railway Returns, 1910-11]
metadata.description: Following the account of the Korean railways, this small table gives the operating returns for the 1910-11 year: mileage, locomotives, carriages and wagons.

metadata.title: Revenue
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives Taiwan's revenue, ordinary and extraordinary, for each fiscal year from 1907-8 to 1911-12, showing the island's finances becoming self-supporting.

metadata.title: [Taiwan Ordinary Expenditure]
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The table lists Taiwan's ordinary government expenditure by department for the same fiscal years, from administration and courts to railway expenses.

metadata.title: [Taiwan Government Expenditure, Continued]
metadata.description: A continuation of the Taiwan government's ordinary and extraordinary expenditure figures, showing the yearly totals of each item; the column year headings appear on the preceding page.

metadata.title: Population
metadata.description: Shows the population of Taiwan at the end of each year from 1904 to 1908, split by sex and by Japanese, native and savage groups, with grand totals.

metadata.title: Forests and Plains
metadata.caption: (March, 1908)
metadata.description: Summarises the area of forests and plains in the island's administration and aborigines' districts as of March 1908, split by protection, utilization, exploration status.

metadata.title: State Forests and Plains Under Promise of Sale
metadata.description: Lists, year by year from 1904 to 1908, the number of state forest and plain parcels and their area offered under promise of sale.

metadata.title: Tree Planting
metadata.description: Shows the area planted with trees by government and private bodies in Taiwan at each year end, with totals, in cho, for 1903 to 1908.

metadata.title: List of Governor-Generals
metadata.description: Lists the Governors-General of Taiwan with their dates of appointment and relief from office, from 1895 to 1906.

metadata.title: Education
metadata.description: Gives the number of government, public and private schools in Taiwan, with their teachers and students, for 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Justice (Sentences Carried Out)
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal sentences carried out by court type and year, from 1904 to 1908, illustrating the justice administration.

metadata.title: Area of Tillage of Land
metadata.description: Gives the cultivated land area, split into rice paddy and upland field, at the end of each year from 1903 to 1907.

metadata.title: Agricultural Products
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists annual output of principal agricultural products, in thousands of the stated units, for 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Live Stock
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of buffalo, cattle, swine and goats kept in Japan for each year from 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Marine Products
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Taiwan's raw and cured marine product output by quantity and value for 1904 to 1909, illustrating the fishery side of the island's economy.

metadata.title: Mineral Products
metadata.description: Lists Taiwan's annual output of gold, gold dust, coal, sulphur and petroleum from 1904 to 1909, presented alongside the marine product figures to show the island's mineral production.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Summarises Japan's total foreign trade with exports, imports, totals and specie and bullion movements for 1905 to 1910.

metadata.title: Trade with Japan Proper
metadata.description: Shows trade between Japan and Japan Proper from 1902 to 1910, with the excess of imports or exports each year.

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Exported
metadata.caption: Value (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the value of Japan's chief export commodities, such as tea, rice, sugar and camphor, for 1905 to 1910.

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Imported
metadata.caption: Value (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the value of Japan's chief import commodities, such as opium, petroleum, flour and cotton goods, for 1905 to 1910.

metadata.title: Three Important Undertakings — Estimated Cost and Period
metadata.caption: (Unit: yen)
metadata.description: The Formosan Government's planned undertakings of 1908-9 onward, listing each project's estimated yen cost and its start and end years.

metadata.title: The Revenue From the Four Items for the Last Few Years
metadata.description: Shows government revenue from camphor, opium, tobacco and salt monopolies for the fiscal years ending March 1904 to 1908, introduced by the text on the revenue from these four items.

metadata.title: Opium
metadata.description: Gives the opium monopoly figures for fiscal years 1904 to 1908: raw material used, value, manufactured output, number of smokers and the rate per 100 natives.

metadata.title: [Camphor and Oil Production and Price Paid]
metadata.description: Shows annual camphor and oil output from 1905 to 1909 with the price paid, as the bulk of these is produced at private refineries.

metadata.title: Salt
metadata.description: Gives the salt field area, output and value for fiscal years 1906 to 1909, alongside the text on consumption and export of Formosan salt.

metadata.title: [Output of Gold in 1907]
metadata.description: Gold output of the three Taiwan gold mines in 1907, with the number of laborer-days worked at each, illustrating the mining paragraph on gold.

metadata.title: Estimates for the Island of Karafuto for Fiscal Years
metadata.description: The table gives the estimated expenditures and revenues of the island of Karafuto for fiscal years 1909-10 and 1911-12, showing the island's finances under civil administration.

metadata.title: Marine Products in the Last Few Years
metadata.description: The page gives recent annual catches of marine products in Karafuto, showing herring oil cake, salmon, trout and totals in koku for 1907 to 1910, to illustrate the fishery's importance.

metadata.title: Finance
metadata.caption: (Unit: yen)
metadata.description: Gives the Kwantung Government's ordinary and extraordinary revenue and expenditure for 1909-10 and 1910-11 under the FINANCE heading.

metadata.title: Japanese in Manchuria
metadata.description: Shows the number of male, female and total Japanese residents in four Manchurian centres such as Antung and Mukden.

metadata.title: [Japanese Residents in Manchurian Towns]
metadata.description: Figures for Japanese residents in inland South Manchurian towns; the column headings were printed above, on the previous page, and are not visible here.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade at Dairen (1909)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Dairen's foreign trade in 1909 by trading partner, with 1908 totals for comparison, as part of the South Manchuria chapter.

metadata.title: Business Report
metadata.caption: yen 1000
metadata.description: Summarises the Manchurian Railway Company's business result for 1910-'11, showing earnings and disbursements by department in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [Distances, Hours and Third-Class Fares to Manchuria via the Antung-Mukden Railway]
metadata.description: Showing how much the Antung-Mukden line shortens passenger travel distance, time and third-class fares between Japan and Manchuria via Fusan or Dairen.

metadata.title: [Distances, Shimbashi to Harbin]
metadata.description: Lists the stage distances of the sea-and-rail route from Shimbashi to Harbin, which the text compares with the overland Antung-Mukden alternative.

metadata.description: Compares freight charges per ton from Mukden to Kobe by the Antung-Mukden route and by the Dairen route, showing the Dairen route is much cheaper.

metadata.title: Weights (Japanese)
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese units of weight and their equivalents in Momme, Kwamme, pounds avoirdupois and picul.

metadata.title: Weights (Western)
metadata.description: Gives the conversion of Western weights such as the ounce, pound, stone, hundredweight and ton into Japanese Momme and Kwamme.

metadata.title: Land Measures (Tsubo)
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese land measures based on the tsubo and their equivalents in acres and square yards.

metadata.title: Capacity Measures
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese units of capacity with their equivalents in bushels and quarts.

metadata.title: Gallon, Peck and Bushel Equivalents
metadata.description: Converts English liquid and dry measures such as gallon, peck and bushel into Japanese Sho.

metadata.title: Artisan's Measure (Kane)
metadata.description: Gives the artisan's measure units of shaku and sun and their approximate equivalents in inches.

metadata.title: Dry Goods Measures (Kujira)
metadata.description: Lists the dry goods (kujira) measures of shaku, sun and jo with their approximate equivalents in feet and inches.

metadata.title: Distance Measures
metadata.description: Gives Japanese distance units ri, cho, ken and shaku with their equivalents in miles and feet.

metadata.title: Measures of Length
metadata.description: Lists English units of length from inch to degree, with the number of each smaller unit in the next larger one.

metadata.title: Moneys
metadata.description: Gives the value of the yen in sen and in English shillings and cents, and the U.S.A. dollar in francs.

metadata.title: [Area of Japan by Islands and Groups]
metadata.description: The text states Japan's area exclusive of Karafuto and Korea, and this table gives the square-ri area of each main island and island group.

metadata.title: Principal Mountain Peaks Above 8,000 Feet
metadata.description: The page lists the principal mountain peaks of Japan and Formosa exceeding 8,000 feet, with their heights, to show the country's high mountain ranges.

metadata.title: Rivers Above 40 Ri in Length
metadata.description: The text notes that Japanese rivers are short and rapid, and lists the rivers longer than 40 ri with their lengths in ri.

metadata.title: [Coast-Line of the Principal Islands]
metadata.description: The coast-line section gives the total coastal length of the main islands and the surface area per ri of coast, showing how well each island's coast is indented.

metadata.title: [Thirty-Six Harbors Open to Foreign Steamers]
metadata.description: The page lists the harbors open to the call of foreign steamers, with the year each was opened and the island where it lies, in two columns.

metadata.title: Typhoons During the Last Seven Years
metadata.description: After describing wind and typhoon seasons in Japan, the page lists notable typhoons since 1905, giving their dates, origins, dispersal points, paths, minimum pressure and velocity.

metadata.title: [Average Time and Last Occurrence by Place]
metadata.description: A short list giving the average date for an annual event at four inland places, and the date it last occurred there.

metadata.description: Compares the area, population and density per square mile of Japan with several leading Western countries and China.

metadata.title: Population by Ages and Sexes
metadata.description: Gives the 1908 census population of Japan by five-year age groups and sex, with age-group shares per 100 of the population compared across census years.

metadata.description: Gives the number of marriages and divorces, and their rates per 1,000 population, for each year from 1905 to 1909.

metadata.description: Shows the ratio of males to females and of illegitimate to legitimate births for 1904 to 1908.

metadata.description: Reports annual death figures by sex and total for 1904 to 1909, with deaths per 100 people and male mortality relative to females.

metadata.title: Ainu in Hokkaido

metadata.caption: In 1910 the birthrates and deathrates were as follows:—

metadata.title: Population and No. of Households in Principal Cities, with Names of Mayors
metadata.description: Lists principal Japanese cities alphabetically with the name of each city's mayor, its population and number of households.

metadata.title: Number of Passports Issued to Japanese Going Abroad
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of passports issued to Japanese going abroad, split by males and females, from 1904 to 1911, to illustrate emigration trends discussed in the text.

metadata.caption: (At end of 1911)
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese residents at the end of 1911 in Chinese cities, broken down by sex, supporting the discussion of Japanese emigrants abroad.

metadata.description: This continuation lists figures by destination country and region, with the column headings appearing on the previous page; the figures are shown for each place in turn, with a grand total at the foot.

metadata.title: [Population Figures by Year, 1904–1910]
metadata.description: Population figures by year from 1904 to 1910, with Formosan figures marked by asterisks, shown without printed column headings.

metadata.title: Foreigners Residing in Japan
metadata.description: Number of foreign residents in Japan at the end of each year from 1905 to 1910, broken down by males, females and total.

metadata.title: Foreigners Who Landed at Ports of Japan (1911)
metadata.description: Breakdown of foreigners who landed at Japanese ports in 1911 by nationality and port, with totals by port and nationality.

metadata.description: Official returns of foreign residents in Japan from 1906 to 1910, broken down by principal districts, with the 1910 figures split into males, females and totals.

metadata.caption: Nationality of foreigners numbering 100 or above is:—
metadata.description: Foreign residents in Japan from 1906 to 1910 listed by nationality, covering only nationalities numbering 100 or more, with 1910 figures split by sex.

metadata.title: Naturalization
metadata.description: The Home Office's list of foreigners who became Japanese subjects by marriage, adoption, naturalization or rehabilitation, showing yearly counts from 1906 to 1911.

metadata.description: Explains that foreigners' perpetual lease land is a relic of earlier diplomacy, and lists the number of entries, area and rents of such holdings by city.

metadata.title: [Areas Held by Foreigners, Classified by Nationality]
metadata.description: Listing the land area held by principal foreign entries in each nationality group, given with the exchange-rate note before the law on foreign land ownership.

metadata.title: Holders of Decoration
metadata.description: The table gives the number of persons holding each Imperial decoration class by year from 1904 to 1911, showing the growth of honours awarded.

metadata.title: Number of Peers and Its Movement, 1903-1911
metadata.description: The table gives the number of peers in each rank and their total from 1903 to 1911, showing how the peerage grew after the annexation-era creations.

metadata.title: [Imperial Grants to Kuge Peers, 1894]
metadata.description: The table lists the 1894 yen 2,000,000 imperial grants to kuge peers by rank, showing the number of recipients, the sum each received and the total for each rank.

metadata.title: General Statistics on Education
metadata.description: Gives the number of schools, instructors, students and graduates in each kind of school in Japan for the last three years, as a general survey of the education system.

metadata.title: Foreign Instructors at the Institutions Under Direct Control of the Department of Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign instructors by nationality at institutions under the Department of Education, with their total annual salaries, for three years.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Lists the subjects taught in each of the four school years of ordinary elementary schools, with weekly hours and totals for boys and girls.

metadata.description: The table gives the number of children of school age by sex for 1905-6 to 1910-11, distinguishing those receiving and not receiving the prescribed instruction and the school attendance ratios.

metadata.description: This table lists average monthly teacher salaries in public elementary schools, with minimum and maximum figures, for 1905-6 to 1910-11.

metadata.description: Shows the number of schools collecting fees and the paying, exempt and total pupils and average fee, explaining the rise in fee-charging schools after the compulsory education extension.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens, 1906-7 to 1910-11]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of kindergartens, their conductors and infants enrolled from 1906-7 to 1910-11, illustrating growth of this pre-elementary training.

metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for public and private middle schools: number of schools, instructors, pupils and graduates, for 1906-7 to 1910-11.

metadata.description: Shows the careers that middle school graduates from 1907-8 to 1910-11 took up within a year of graduating, such as high school, teaching or unemployment.

metadata.description: Shows the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each of the four years of the girls' high school course, with the yearly total of 28 hours.

metadata.description: Gives year-by-year figures for public and private girls' high schools: number of schools, instructors, pupils, graduates, leaving-school rate and admission percentage, 1907-8 to 1910-11.

metadata.description: The page describes the High School course, and this table sets out the weekly hours per subject for each year of the First Section.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Second Section of the High School
metadata.description: The page describes the High School course, and this table sets out the weekly hours per subject for each year of the Second Section.

metadata.title: [Statistics of the Eight Higher Schools, 1911]

metadata.description: Shows the number of applicants for normal school admission by section, alongside the admission rates, to illustrate how selective admission was across sections.

metadata.title: Students Classified by Occupation of Parents (%)
metadata.description: Gives the percentage of normal school students by sex according to their parents' occupation, showing the social background of the student body.

metadata.title: [Instructors, Students and Graduates Classified by Sex]
metadata.description: Presents the numbers of male and female instructors, students and graduates at normal schools for 1907-8 to 1910-11, as the text introduces.

metadata.title: Statistics of Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: The table gives yearly figures for instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admissions at the Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools, covering 1908 to 1911.

metadata.title: Average Age of Those Matriculated in 1910-11
metadata.description: Shows the average age at which students matriculated in 1910-11 in each college of the Imperial University of Tokyo, with an overall average.

metadata.description: Gives professor numbers, students, graduates, applicants and matriculants for each hall and college of the Imperial University of Tokyo for 1910-11, with figures for earlier years.

metadata.description: The graduates of the Imperial Universities from their foundation to 1910-11 are classified by their occupation or condition in life across three universities.

metadata.description: Gives the professors, students, graduates, applicants and enrolment of the college's course over four academic years, following the note on its farms and the Sendai Science College.

metadata.description: Accompanies the account of the naval engineering school, showing yearly numbers of students and graduates, with naval and engineering departments listed separately.

metadata.description: Shows instructors, students, graduates and admission figures for the agriculture and forestry higher schools, the Morioka school and the newer Kagoshima school, over several years.

metadata.description: Gives the teaching staff and student numbers at the five government higher commercial schools (Tokyo, Kobe, Yamaguchi, Nagasaki) for the years 1906-7 to 1910-11.

metadata.title: Professions Pursued by Graduates of Tokyo Higher Commercial School
metadata.description: Gives the careers taken up by graduates of the Tokyo Higher Commercial School in each of four successive years, by category of employment.

metadata.description: Shows yearly figures for teaching staff, students, graduates, applications and admissions at the higher technical schools in Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, Nagoya, Kumamoto, Sendai and Yonezawa, 1906-7 to 1910-11.

metadata.title: [Students of the Fishery School by Course]
metadata.description: Shows the number of students in each course of the fishery institution from 1906 to 1910, with totals, alongside a note on its laboratories and training vessel.

metadata.description: Gives yearly student numbers, graduates, applicants and admissions at the three Government institutes that train teachers for technical secondary schools.

metadata.description: Shows the physical constitution and eyesight condition of female students in government institutions over four school years, set beside the male returns.

metadata.description: Shows the corresponding health returns for girls in public and private schools of secondary and elementary education, by school type, with a total line.

metadata.description: Shows the number of books published each year from 1907 to 1910, divided into original works and translations, to illustrate the recent growth of the publishing trade.

metadata.description: Gives the number of copyright registrations for 1906 to 1910 by category of work, with totals and transfers, under the discussion of the revised copyright law.

metadata.description: A list of leading Tokyo periodicals giving each title's subject feature, frequency of publication, price per number and publisher, shown to illustrate the Japanese press.

metadata.description: A continuing run of yearly figures for 1906 to 1910, with the row group marked 'Ministers', giving religious personnel and establishment counts that lead into the Buddhism section.

metadata.description: Shows the number of temples and priests of the Buddhist sects that possess over 1,000 temples, for 1906 to 1910, illustrating the strength of Buddhism in Japan.

metadata.description: Shows the growth in membership of the Red Cross Society of Japan at selected years from 1877 to 1910, illustrating the society's steady progress described in the text.

metadata.description: Shows how the charity society's membership, expenses, receipts and fund grew or changed from 1907 to 1911, illustrating the society's phenomenal progress.
