metadata.title: General Account — Ordinary Expenditure
metadata.caption: (Unit: yen)
metadata.description: The table lists the ordinary expenditure savings under the administrative reform for each department of the General Account.

metadata.title: General Account — Extraordinary Expenditure
metadata.caption: (Unit: yen)
metadata.description: The table lists the extraordinary expenditure savings under the administrative reform for each department of the General Account.

metadata.title: Savings and Increase in Annual Revenue
metadata.description: This summarises the government's total savings in expenditure and increases in revenue, the figures being reported in yen across the General and Special accounts.

metadata.title: Special Account
metadata.description: This table itemises the special account savings and revenue increases, showing how the General and Special account totals were reached.

metadata.title: Revenue
metadata.description: This gives the ordinary revenue and its component items (taxes and revenue stamps) for three fiscal years, 1911-12 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: [Government Revenue Receipts (continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of the national revenue account, listing extraordinary receipts, transfers and loans across three years up to the grand total of revenue.

metadata.title: Expenditure
metadata.description: Shows government expenditure, split into ordinary and extraordinary items by ministry, for three years.

metadata.title: [Expenditure by Departments, continued]
metadata.description: Continues a departmental expenditure table, showing amounts for each department and the grand total of state expenditure across three fiscal years.

metadata.title: Annual State Revenue and Expenditure Pertaining to the General Account
metadata.caption: (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual state revenue and expenditure under the General Account for fiscal years 1894-5 to 1913-14, the basis for the surplus figures that follow.

metadata.title: Revenue Surplus
metadata.description: Lists the revenue surpluses for each fiscal year from 1904-5 to 1912-13, which the text then explains as arising largely from transferred war funds and prosperity.

metadata.title: Deposit Account
metadata.description: Shows the funds held by the Deposit Department of the Treasury at the end of the 1911-12 year, broken down by type of deposit.

metadata.title: Tobacco
metadata.description: Shows the area, cultivation, harvest, purchases and price paid for tobacco under the state monopoly for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: Salt
metadata.description: Gives the salt monopoly's area, refinery and refiner numbers, output, purchases and price for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: Camphor in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Presents the camphor monopoly's area, refiner and refinery figures, purchases with their price, and sales with their price for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: Estimated Profit and Loss Account
metadata.description: Gives estimated revenue and expense of the state monopolies for four fiscal years, from 1909-10 to 1912-13.

metadata.title: Profit and Loss Account of State Undertakings
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Shows receipts, expenses and profits of each state undertaking, such as the arsenals, mint and railway, for 1911-12 and 1912-13.

metadata.title: Collection Expenses of Revenue
metadata.description: The table gives the collection expense of revenue against tax receipts for recent fiscal years, to show the cost of collection relative to net proceeds.

metadata.title: Land Tax
metadata.description: Shows the land tax rates by class of land after the post-war revisions, summarising the reductions made in the 26th session of the Diet.

metadata.title: Income Tax — 1st Kind (Income of Juridical Persons)
metadata.description: Lists the income tax rates per 1000 for juridical persons, by income bracket for partnership companies and by type for joint stock companies and others.

metadata.title: Income Tax — 2nd Kind (Gov. Bonds Exempted)
metadata.description: Gives the single income tax rate applied to income from bonds and shares, with government bonds exempted.

metadata.title: Income Tax — 3rd Kind (Income of Other Descriptions)
metadata.description: Sets out the graduated income tax rates per 1000 for income from other descriptions, by income bracket.

metadata.title: [Juridical Persons of B Class with Income of Not Less Than Yen 100,000]
metadata.description: Shows the number of juridical persons of B class and their total income by income bracket, as given by the Government Delegate in the 23rd Diet session.

metadata.title: [Individuals with Income of Above Yen 100,000 a Year]
metadata.description: Gives the number of individuals and their total income for each bracket above Yen 100,000 a year, as presented to the Diet by the Government Delegate.

metadata.title: [Data and Rate of Business Tax Assessment]
metadata.description: Lists the data used for business tax assessment and the corresponding assessment rates for each of the four kinds of occupation, as revised on readjustment of taxes.

metadata.title: [Business Tax Rates by Kind]
metadata.description: Lists the national business tax rates for the fifth to twelfth kinds of business, showing the rate for each taxable item and for the per-person levy.

metadata.title: [Registration Fees]
metadata.description: Gives the registration fee rates for various kinds of registrable objects, with separate fees for corporations and trade establishments, as a general-interest summary.

metadata.title: Professional Registration
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Fees payable for professional registration of barristers, medical practitioners, mariners, marine engineers and pilots.

metadata.title: Copyright
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Fees for copyright registration of newspapers, periodicals, plays, other works and photographs, and for transfers or hypothecation of copyright.

metadata.title: Patent Right
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Fees for transfer or common ownership and for hypothecation of patent rights.

metadata.title: Designs
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Fees for transfer or common ownership and for hypothecation of design rights.

metadata.title: Trade-marks
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Fee for transfer or common ownership of trade-marks.

metadata.title: Mining
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Fees for mining rights, covering protection, working, alterations, transfer, hypothecation, amalgamation and abandonment.

metadata.title: Medicine Tax
metadata.description: Lists the national tax rates on compounding, licensing and stamp duty for medicines, as set out in the Medicine Tax section.

metadata.title: Sugar Excise
metadata.caption: Per picul yen
metadata.description: Gives the excise rate per picul for each class of sugar, with molasses and syrup, under the Sugar Excise section.

metadata.title: Woolen and Silk Textiles or Mixtures
metadata.description: States the tax rate, as a share of value, on woollen and silk textiles and their mixtures.

metadata.title: Travelling Tax
metadata.caption: Sen
metadata.description: Shows the travelling tax charged by distance band and by first to third class fares, with the sen rates given in each band.

metadata.title: Violation of Rules, Fines, Etc.
metadata.description: Shows the number of cases and amounts of fines for violations of domestic, customs, tobacco, salt and camphor regulations over several years.

metadata.title: Arrears in National and Local Taxes
metadata.description: Gives the amounts of national and local tax arrears served with writs and the amounts in default for the years shown.

metadata.title: Appropriations for the Departments of State (1)
metadata.caption: During the last ten years (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists annual appropriations for the civil list and the main departments of state over ten fiscal years, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Appropriations for the Departments of State (2)
metadata.caption: During the last ten years (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Continues the departmental appropriations, giving the figures for justice, education, agriculture and commerce, communication and the total for the early years.

metadata.title: [Annual Expenditure Figures, 1906-7 to 1913-14]
metadata.description: This top table continues from the previous page and gives yearly figures for the period 1906-7 to 1913-14, preceding the section on departmental allotment percentages.

metadata.title: Total Expenditures Classified
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: This table classifies total national expenditures by year into undertakings, defence, debts and administration, showing how spending shifted after the war.

metadata.title: Continuing Expenditures
metadata.description: This table gives the continuing expenditures for 1913-14 and 1914-15, split between the ordinary and special accounts, which the text says are mainly army and navy allotments.

metadata.title: [Annual Financial Figures, 1915-16 to 1920 to 30]
metadata.description: Figures for successive fiscal periods from 1915-16 onward, showing the government's finances; the text notes the Government and Diet avoid creating continuing expense.

metadata.title: State Aids and Bounties
metadata.description: Subsidies and bounties granted by the Government, broken down by purpose (colonial, shipping, floods, others) and total, for each fiscal year from 1903-4 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: National Debts Classified
metadata.caption: (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows how Japan's national debts, domestic and foreign, grew across the years 1904 to 1913, illustrating the effect of War expenditure on the debt account.

metadata.title: [Loans Classified by Object of Raising]
metadata.description: The loans are classified according to the object for which they were raised, showing amounts raised, amounts redeemed, and balances outstanding at March 1912.

metadata.title: National Debts Outstanding at the End of March 1912: Domestic Loans
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the domestic loans still outstanding at the end of March 1912, by kind, with issue amounts, interest rates, issue years, redemption terms, maturity years and balances.

metadata.title: [Domestic Loans and Debentures (Continued)]
metadata.description: This continued table lists the domestic government loans and debentures, with issue amounts, interest rates, redemption years and outstanding amounts, leading to the total of the domestic debt.

metadata.title: Foreign Loans
metadata.description: This table gives the foreign loans of the Japanese government by issue, with interest rates, dates and outstanding amounts, ending in a grand total.

metadata.title: National Debts, Raised, Redeemed and Outstanding
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: This table shows yearly movements in national debt, from amounts brought forward and newly issued through redemptions to year-end outstanding debt and debt per head of population.

metadata.title: [Fiscal Year Figures, 1908-09 to 1911-12]
metadata.description: Shows annual figures for four fiscal years from 1908-09 to 1911-12, part of the Treasury's debt redemption and adjustment account discussed in the surrounding text.

metadata.title: New Foreign Loans (in 1913)
metadata.description: Lists the terms of the three foreign loans raised in 1913, including redemption period, issue price, interest rates and month of issue.

metadata.title: Conditions of Foreign Loans
metadata.description: Gives the interest rate, issue price, commission and net proceeds in pounds, shillings and pence for recent Government loans raised abroad.

metadata.title: Sinking Fund Account
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the government's annual receipts into and payments out of the sinking fund for each fiscal year from 1907-08 to 1912-13, illustrating the debt-redemption programme described in the text.

metadata.title: Foreign Loans and Interest and Redemption
metadata.caption: (Existing in November 1911)
metadata.description: Gives the outstanding foreign loans, by class of security, and the annual interest payable on them as at November 1911.

metadata.title: [Foreign Loans Redeemable in the 15 Years to Come]
metadata.description: Lists the loans of about 697 million yen due for redemption within the next fifteen years, with their maturity dates and the yearly instalment required.

metadata.title: [Conversion of 5% Loans into 4% Loans]
metadata.description: Figures for the attempted conversion of 5% loans into 4% loans, both at home and abroad, showing the amounts paid in with bonds, paid in cash and realized.

metadata.title: Specie Hoarded Abroad by the Government
metadata.description: Year-end figures for specie the Government kept abroad from 1906 to 1912, shown to illustrate the apparent stationary condition of reserves.

metadata.title: Inflow and Exodus in 1912
metadata.description: Breakdown of the inflow of funds in 1912, listing loans, specie imports, gold output and other sources, to show the balance against heavy annual payments.

metadata.title: [Specie Exodus and Trade Balance, Estimated Payments]
metadata.description: Estimated items of Japan's international specie payments and receipts for the year, showing a net excess of payment, set against the trade balance discussed in the text below.

metadata.title: Finances of Prefectural Governments
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows prefectural revenue and expenditure by item for six fiscal years, the ordinary sources of prefectural income and the main expenditure heads.

metadata.title: Average and Legal Limit of Local Taxation
metadata.description: Compares the average local tax rates actually levied with the legal maximum rates and shows the excess above the limit for each tax.

metadata.title: Cities
metadata.description: Gives the revenue and expenses of Japanese cities for the latest available years, noting that civic corporations derive income from supplementary rates and subventions.

metadata.title: [Prefectural Finance — Revenue and Expenditure Items]
metadata.description: Shows the revenue and expenditure items of prefectural finance, with the column headings and the section heading appearing on the previous page.

metadata.title: Finance of Towns and Villages
metadata.description: Gives the revenue and expenses of towns and villages, broken down into revenue and expenditure items, for the years compared in this section.

metadata.title: Local Loans Existing at the End of the Year
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The table shows the year-end balances of local loans by prefectures, counties, cities, towns, villages and local associations from 1906 to 1912, introduced alongside the discussion of government loans to communal bodies.

metadata.title: Classification of Local Loans
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives the outstanding local loans of cities, towns and villages by purpose at the end of each year from 1906 to 1910, with totals.

metadata.title: Local and Municipal Loans Classified
metadata.caption: (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The table lists the local and municipal loans of Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka by object, with amount, issue price, interest rate and amount still outstanding.

metadata.title: [Water-works, Harbour-works and Gas Works of Yokohama and Nagoya]
metadata.description: Figures for municipal water-works, harbour-works and gas works at Yokohama and Nagoya, showing issues, prices and amounts, presented as part of the corporate and municipal enterprise statistics.

metadata.title: Property of Urban and Rural Corporations
metadata.caption: (Yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the property of urban and rural corporations at March of 1898, 1903 and 1907 by category, illustrating the growth of corporate holdings in Japan.

metadata.title: Foreign Investment in Japan
metadata.description: Summarises foreign investment in Japan in 1911, listing foreign loans and domestic loans held by foreigners, as set out according to the Investor's Magazine.

metadata.title: [Shares Possessed by Foreigners]
metadata.description: Summarises the classification of the roughly 20,000,000 yen of shares held by foreigners in Japanese enterprises, by industry, with the total.

metadata.title: [Companies with Shares Owned by Foreigners]
metadata.description: Lists the individual companies in which foreigners hold shares, with the amount of shares owned by foreigners in each.

metadata.title: Debenture Loans
metadata.description: Shows the amount of debenture bonds issued by economic corporations, redeemed, and outstanding by half-year from 1911 to 1912, compiled by the Industrial Bank of Japan.

metadata.title: [Expenditure on National Defence, 1902-3 to 1912-13]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen 1000)
metadata.description: Shows the rise in army, navy and total national defence expenditure from 1902-3 onward, illustrating how appropriations expanded rapidly after the War of 1904-5.

metadata.title: [Siege Artillery Units Under Brigade Headquarters at Yokosuka]
metadata.description: Shows how the new Siege Artillery Corps is distributed among coastal posts under the Yokosuka brigade headquarters, with its unit strength and whether horses are provided.

metadata.title: [Siege Artillery Units Under Brigade Headquarters at Shimonoseki]
metadata.description: Shows how the new Siege Artillery Corps is distributed among posts under the Shimonoseki brigade headquarters, with unit strength and whether horses are provided.

metadata.title: [Stationing of Field Artillery Brigades]
metadata.description: Lists the three reorganized field artillery brigades, each now of two regiments, and the garrison town where each brigade is stationed.

metadata.title: Murata's Magazine-Rifle of 1905 Type
metadata.description: Gives the specifications of Murata's 1905-type magazine rifle, separately for infantry and cavalry use, as the latest improvement in Japanese army small arms.

metadata.title: Quick-Firing Field-Guns of '98 Type
metadata.description: Specifications of the quick-firing field-guns of 1898 type, the first of seven kinds of guns now in Japanese service, listed under heading a.

metadata.title: Quick-Firing Mountain-Guns of '98 Type
metadata.description: Specifications of the quick-firing mountain-guns of 1898 type, given as a smaller version of the quick-firers listed above under heading b.

metadata.title: Field-Gun of '05 Type
metadata.description: Brief specification of the 1905 type field-gun, the third kind of gun listed, given under heading c.

metadata.title: [Specifications of a Gun (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: Lists the technical particulars of a gun whose heading is on the previous page, covering bore, range, carriage, weights, lengths and shot types.

metadata.title: 10 Centimetre Canet-Gun of '05 Type
metadata.description: Gives the technical specifications of the 10 cm Canet gun of the 1905 type, including dimensions, weights, range and shot.

metadata.title: 15 (12) Centimetre Canet-Gun of '05 Type
metadata.description: Gives the technical specifications of the 15 (12) cm Canet gun of the 1905 type, with figures for both calibres in parentheses.

metadata.title: [Specifications of Gun (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a list of technical specifications for a gun, giving range, weights, lengths and shot details for the piece described above.

metadata.title: 24 Centimetre Canet-Gun
metadata.description: Specifications of the 24 centimetre Canet gun, listing its dimensions, velocities, ranges, elevation limits and the weights and fuses of its shot.

metadata.title: 28 Centimetre Howitzer
metadata.description: Specifications of the 28 centimetre howitzer, giving its calibre, bore-line count, velocity, range, elevation limits and barrel dimensions.

metadata.title: [Specifications of Shot]
metadata.description: A bracketed diagram listing the two kinds of hard steel shot with their weight, explosive and fuse, shown alongside the army and navy material on this page.

metadata.title: Result of Conscription Service Examination
metadata.description: Summarises the outcome of conscription service examinations for 1909 and 1910, showing numbers examined, able-bodied rates, and reasons for evasion, volunteering and exemption.

metadata.title: Stature (in Japanese Ft.) of Eligible Lads Examined
metadata.description: Gives the stature distribution of eligible lads examined in selected years, by height band with totals and percentages, showing the trend in physique.

metadata.title: Officers and Non-Combatants on Active Service
metadata.description: The page closes the Army and Navy section by giving the numbers of officers, non-combatants and civilians on active service for 1908 to 1911.

metadata.title: Distribution of the Standing Army
metadata.description: The page gives the distribution of the standing army, listing each division's headquarters with its infantry, cavalry, field artillery, engineer and commissariat units and garrison localities.

metadata.title: Army Divisions, Brigades and Regiments by Garrison
metadata.description: The page lists the army's divisions with their headquarters, brigades, regiment numbers and garrison towns, set out in rotated columns on the page.

metadata.title: [Army Divisions and Their Garrison Towns]
metadata.description: The page lists the army divisions with their garrison towns and associated numbered units, shown in rotated columns across the page.

metadata.title: Age-Limit in the Active Service
metadata.description: Gives the maximum age at which officers of each rank may remain in active service, following the promotion rules described above.

metadata.title: Super-Dreadnought (1.)
metadata.description: Lists the one super-dreadnought under construction that the reduced naval expansion program would add to the fleet.

metadata.title: Four Cruisers of the Same Type
metadata.description: Lists the four battle-cruisers of the same type that would be added to the proposed naval expansion, with their builders.

metadata.title: Battleship (8)
metadata.description: Shows the planned strength of eight battleships in the reduced naval program, giving each ship's tonnage and year of build or construction status.

metadata.title: Cruisers (6)
metadata.description: Shows the planned strength of six cruisers in the reduced naval program, with tonnage and build year or construction status for each.

metadata.title: Main Force Available in 1910
metadata.description: Captain Oguri lists the battleships and armoured cruisers the Powers could bring to bear in the Pacific in 1910, according to their adopted programmes.

metadata.title: Main Force Available in 1917
metadata.description: The same comparison for 1917 shows the battleships and armoured cruisers available to each Power in the Pacific under their adopted programmes, with Japan's expansion programme excluded.

metadata.title: [Naval Cadet Academy: Applicants, Admissions and Examination Results, 1906-1909]
metadata.description: The table gives the numbers admitted, passing the examinations, and applicants to the Naval Cadet Academy at Edajima for the four years 1906 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Naval Engineering School: Applicants, Admissions and Examination Results, 1906-1909]
metadata.description: The table gives the numbers admitted, passing the examinations, and applicants to the Naval Engineering School at Yokosuka for the years 1906 to 1909, a school whose term matches the Naval Cadet Academy's.

metadata.title: Volunteer and Conscription Service
metadata.description: Shows the yearly numbers of conscripts, volunteers and their total entering the Japanese Navy from 1905 to 1911, illustrating the mix of volunteer and conscript service.

metadata.title: Battleships
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese battleships with their displacement, length, launch date, speed, torpedo tubes, waterline armor and principal armament, showing the fleet's main warships.

metadata.title: Armored Cruisers
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese armored cruisers with their tonnage, complement, build year, speed, armour and gun armament, as a reference of the fleet.

metadata.title: Protected Cruisers
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese protected cruisers with their tonnage, complement, build year, speed, armour and guns, as a reference of the fleet.

metadata.title: [Cruiser and Gunboat Particulars, Continued]
metadata.description: Lists the particulars of the older cruisers of the Japanese navy, with tonnage, horse-power, build year, speed and armament.

metadata.title: Torpedo-Boat Dépôt-Ships
metadata.description: Lists the torpedo-boat depot-ships of the navy with their tonnage, year built and speed.

metadata.title: Gun-Boats
metadata.description: Lists the gun-boats of the navy with their tonnage, horse-power, build year, speed and armament.

metadata.title: Despatch-Boats
metadata.description: Lists the despatch-boats of the navy with their tonnage, horse-power, build year, speed and armament.

metadata.title: Torpedo-Boat Destroyers
metadata.description: A list of the torpedo-boat destroyers of the Japanese navy with their tonnage and year of building, showing the size of the destroyer fleet.

metadata.title: Age Limit of Officer in Active Service
metadata.description: Lists the maximum age limits for officers of each rank in active naval service, showing the age at which each rank must retire.

metadata.title: Officers and Bluejackets on Active Service
metadata.caption: (Compiled at the end of the year)
metadata.description: Gives the year-end strength of naval officers, warrant officers, bluejackets and cadets on active service for 1906 to 1912, showing the growth of the fleet's personnel.

metadata.title: Scale of Salaries
metadata.chapter_raw: Chapter XXXIII Directory Civil and Military Service
metadata.description: The salary scale was raised by 29 per cent from April 1910, and these figures give the annual salaries for principal civil and military posts in the Shin-nin and Choku-nin ranks.

metadata.title: [Salaries of Senior Civil Officials and Local Governors]
metadata.description: Lists the printed annual salaries of the principal civil posts and local governors, with allowances for certain prefectural governors noted below.

metadata.title: Diplomatic and Consular Service
metadata.description: Gives the salaries and allowances of diplomatic and consular officials, with allowances varying by the country of posting.

metadata.title: Officials of the Imperial Household
metadata.description: Shows the salaries of the senior officials of the Imperial Household, with a note on the salary range of higher civil officials.

metadata.title: The Court of Cassation
metadata.description: Shows the annual salaries of the officers of the Court of Cassation, the highest judicial court in Japan.

metadata.title: Appeal Courts
metadata.description: Lists the annual salaries of presidents, chief procurators, and judges and procurators at the Appeal Courts, with higher rates for Tokyo and Osaka.

metadata.title: Districts Courts
metadata.description: Gives the annual salaries of presiding judges, chief procurators and ordinary judges and procurators at the District Courts.

metadata.title: University Professors
metadata.description: Shows the salary scales for the president, professors and assistant professors of the Imperial University, plus extra pay for holding a chair.

metadata.title: Naval Officers
metadata.description: Lists the annual salary for each naval officer rank, from admiral down to midshipman.

metadata.title: Military Officers
metadata.description: Lists the number of military officers by rank, with figures printed beside each rank, as part of the directory of the civil and military services.

metadata.title: Military and Naval Attachés at Embassy or Legation
metadata.description: Gives the figures for military and naval attachés at embassies or legations by rank and by the country where they serve.

metadata.title: Residency-General in Korea
metadata.description: Shows the salaries and allowances in yen of the principal officials of the Residency-General in Korea.

metadata.title: Pensions and Annuities
metadata.description: Shows the number of recipients and amounts of pensions and annuities paid to civil service, army and navy persons from 1904 to 1909, with grand totals.

metadata.title: One Time Grant of Money
metadata.description: Lists the one-time grants of money given to civil service, army and navy recipients by year from 1903 to 1909, with totals.

metadata.title: [Imperial Household Department Officials]
metadata.description: Lists the chief officials of the Imperial Household Department with their titles and the names of the holders at the time of publication.

metadata.title: [Foreign Affairs Department Officials]
metadata.description: Lists the principal officials of the Foreign Affairs Department with their titles and names.

metadata.title: [Home Department Officials]
metadata.description: Lists the principal officials of the Home Department with their titles and names.

metadata.title: [Finance Department Officials]
metadata.description: Lists the principal officials of the Finance Department with their titles and names.

metadata.title: [Bureau Directors, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: Continues the directory of officials, listing the directors of the bureaus under the agricultural, commercial and industrial department.

metadata.title: Communication Department
metadata.description: Lists the minister, vice-minister, bureau directors and divisional superintendents of the Communication Department with their holders.

metadata.title: Korean Government General
metadata.description: Shows the Governor-General of Korea and the heads of its general administration departments, bureaus and sections with their holders.

metadata.title: Formosan Government General
metadata.description: Lists the Governor-General of Formosa and the directors of its civil affairs, police, finance, communication and industrial bureaus, plus the army staff chief.

metadata.title: [Commanders of Schools, Garrisons and Central Boys' Institutions]
metadata.description: Lists the commanders of the Toyama school, the riding, artillery, infantry, cadet and central boys' establishments and the Tokyo Garrison, with their ranks; the numeric dot columns are not reproduced here.

metadata.title: List of Divisional and Brigade Commanders
metadata.description: Gives the Lieutenant-Generals commanding each numbered division of the army, from the Guards through the 18th Division.

metadata.title: Infantry
metadata.description: Names the Major-Generals commanding each infantry brigade and the division to which it belongs, arranged in two side-by-side columns.

metadata.title: Cavalry
metadata.description: Shows the cavalry brigades, their parent divisions and the Major-Generals commanding them.

metadata.title: Artillery
metadata.description: Lists the artillery units of the army and their commanding officers, two units per line.

metadata.title: Heavy Artillery and Communication
metadata.description: Lists the heavy artillery and communication units with their commanding officers.

metadata.title: Commanders of Garrisons and Forts
metadata.description: Lists the commanders of the army garrisons and forts with their ranks.

metadata.title: The Navy
metadata.description: Lists the principal naval posts with their holders and ranks.

metadata.title: [Naval Establishment Officials]
metadata.description: This list gives the names and ranks of the senior officers heading the naval training schools, arsenal and imperial aides-de-camp in the Japanese Navy.

metadata.title: Naval Staff Board
metadata.description: This list names the chief and vice-chief of the Naval Staff Board, the body that directed naval planning.

metadata.title: Admiralty
metadata.description: This table lists the senior officers of the Admiralty at the four naval stations of Yokosuka, Kure, Sasebo and Maizuru.

metadata.title: [Provincial Relief Fund Grants by Province]
metadata.description: Lists the amounts of the provincial relief fund granted to each province, which the provincial governors hold and whose interest is spent on work, education and relief.

metadata.title: Temperature
metadata.description: Monthly temperature figures from Japanese or other consulates' meteorological records in Korea, showing January, August and average temperatures at five stations.

metadata.title: Rainfalls
metadata.description: Rainfall totals at four Korean stations from consular meteorological records, giving January and August amounts with yearly totals.

metadata.title: No. of Days of Rainfalls and Snowfalls
metadata.description: Number of days with rainfall or snowfall at five Korean stations, shown for February and July with yearly totals, as part of the climate record.

metadata.title: Home Treasury's Burdens
metadata.description: Burdens falling on the Home Treasury because of Korea, listed by fund to meet deficit, loans, garrison and navy, with totals, for two sets of figures.

metadata.title: Budget for 1913-14
metadata.caption: (Before the retrenchment of July)
metadata.description: The budget for 1913-14 gives ordinary and extraordinary revenue for Chosen, before the July retrenchment, with the grand totals compared against the previous year.

metadata.title: Ordinary Expenditure
metadata.description: This table sets out the ordinary budget expenditure of Chosen by department for 1913-14 against the figures for 1912-13.

metadata.title: Extraordinary Expenditure
metadata.description: This table lists the extraordinary budget expenditure of Chosen for 1913-14, with comparative figures for 1912-13.

metadata.title: Debts
metadata.description: This table lists Chosen's outstanding government loans, showing interest rate, amount, date of loan, redemption date and creditor.

metadata.title: Loans Outstanding
metadata.description: Lists the government and enterprise loans with their rates, amounts, dates and negotiators, with a note of a further loan for currency adjustment.

metadata.title: Volume of Trade
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of Japan's merchandise and specie/bullion imports and exports from 1904 to 1912, giving the overall foreign trade volume.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of Japan's principal export articles from 1906 to 1912, such as beans, rice, live stock and cotton.

metadata.title: Imports
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly import values for principal textile and other goods such as sheeting, cotton yarn, kerosene and sake from 1906 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Principal Commodities, 1906–1912]
metadata.description: Shows values of the principal commodities in the Chosen trade for 1906–1912, listed by commodity and year.

metadata.title: Trade in Leading Ports
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives export and import values for the leading Korean treade ports, showing the trade of each port by year from 1905 to 1911.

metadata.title: Trade with Different Countries
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's import and export trade by country for 1907 to 1911, in thousands of yen, illustrating the trade with China, Britain, the USA, Manchuria and Russia.

metadata.title: [Korean Banks: Establishment, Capital and Paid-up Capital, 1909]
metadata.description: Lists the three ordinary Korean banks with their year of establishment, capital and paid-up capital as reported at the end of 1909.

metadata.title: [Korean Banks: Government Loans, Deposits, Loans, Overdrafts and Bills Discounted, 1909]
metadata.description: Gives the business position of the three ordinary Korean banks at the end of 1909, covering government loans, deposits, loans, overdrafts and bills discounted.

metadata.title: [Japanese Banking Organs in Korea: Deposits, Loans, Overdrafts and Bills Discounted]
metadata.description: Four Japanese banking organs operate in Korea; this table gives the deposits, loans, overdrafts and bills discounted of the three that are compared, the Industrial Bank not undertaking ordinary banking.

metadata.title: Business Results
metadata.caption: (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese-run bank's liabilities, assets, and profit and loss for 1910 to 1912 in thousands of yen, giving its business results over those years.

metadata.title: [Japanese Immigrants in Korea by Houses, Men and Women]
metadata.description: Gives the number of Japanese houses, men, women and total settlers in Korea at half-yearly dates from 1906 to 1910, illustrating the growth of Japanese settlement there.

metadata.title: [Property Held by Japanese in Places of Importance in Korea]
metadata.description: The table estimates the land, buildings and value owned by Japanese at the main places of importance in the Korean Peninsula, showing the scale of Japanese property holdings there.

metadata.title: [Fishing Boats, Fishermen and Value of Catches, 1910]
metadata.description: The table gives the 1910 number of boats, fishermen and value of catches for Korean and Japanese fishing, illustrating the existing state of the Korean fishing industry described in the text.

metadata.title: [Daily Wages of Laborers by Place]
metadata.description: Wages of Japanese and Korean laborers at seven Korean places, shown because new engineering works have raised demand and Chinese laborers have settled in Korea.

metadata.title: Governmental School
metadata.description: Official figures for government schools in Korea at the end of October 1910, showing the marked improvement in Korean education.

metadata.title: Semi-Public Schools
metadata.description: Official figures for semi-public schools in Korea at the end of October 1910, part of the statement on the state of Korean education.

metadata.title: Public Schools
metadata.description: Official figures for public elementary schools in Korea at the end of October 1910, part of the statement on the state of Korean education.

metadata.title: Private Schools
metadata.description: Official figures for private schools in Korea at the end of October 1910, including religious schools kept by foreign missionaries.

metadata.title: [Schools, Teachers and Pupils by Kind in Korea]
metadata.description: This table gives the number of schools, teachers and pupils in each kind of school in Korea, with totals, as a summary of the education statistics for the territory.

metadata.title: [Railway Returns for 1910-11]
metadata.description: The railway returns for the 1910-11 year give the mileage and the numbers of locomotives, carriages and wagons on the Korean railways.

metadata.title: Revenue
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The Formosan finance was made independent from 1897-8; this table shows the colony's ordinary and extraordinary revenue for each fiscal year from 1907-8 to 1912-13.

metadata.title: Expenditure
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Alongside the revenue figures, this table gives the colony's ordinary expenditure by department for the same fiscal years, from 1907-8 to 1912-13.

metadata.title: [Government Expenditure Table (Continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a table of government expenditure, ordinary and extraordinary, over six years; the year headings appear on the previous page and are not visible here.

metadata.title: Population
metadata.description: Population of Japan (Japanese, Natives and Savages) by sex and total at the end of each year from 1906 to 1910, with grand totals and foreigners resident.

metadata.title: Forests and Plains
metadata.caption: (March, 1908)
metadata.description: The table gives the forest and plains area of Taiwan in 1908, split between administration and aboriginal districts, and the yearly protection and other forest figures from 1907 to 1910.

metadata.title: State Forests and Plains Under Promise of Sale
metadata.description: Lists the number of state forest and plain items placed under promise of sale and their area by year, with a conversion note for the units used.

metadata.title: Tree Planting
metadata.description: Shows the area of trees planted each year to March, split between government and private planting, with totals, illustrating the forestry programme described nearby.

metadata.title: List of Governor-Generals
metadata.description: Gives the successive Governor-Generals of Formosa with their dates of appointment and relief, placed after the account of the Arisan forest project.

metadata.title: Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools, teachers and students by type of school in Taiwan for the years 1908 to 1910, illustrating the state of education in the colony.

metadata.title: Civil and Criminal Cases
metadata.description: Gives the number of civil and criminal actions entered, disposed of and remaining at year end in the Taiwan courts for fiscal years 1908 to 1910.

metadata.title: No. of Actions Entered Before Police Magistrate
metadata.description: Shows the number of actions entered before the Police Magistrate by offence type for 1908 to 1910.

metadata.title: Persons Subjected to Flogging
metadata.description: Gives the number of persons subjected to flogging, by age group, for 1908 to 1910 as a companion to the police statistics.

metadata.title: Area of Tillage of Land
metadata.caption: At end of year; area in ko
metadata.description: Gives the cultivated land area at the end of each year from 1903 to 1910, split between rice paddy and upland field.

metadata.title: Agricultural Products
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists annual output of principal agricultural products, such as rice, tea, sweet potatoes and indigo, for 1905 to 1909.

metadata.title: Live Stock
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the number of buffalo, cattle, swine and goats kept in Japan for each year from 1904 to 1910.

metadata.title: [Sugar Output, 1909–1911]
metadata.caption: (The output is as follows, in 1000 kin.)
metadata.description: Gives Taiwan's sugar output in 1000 kin for 1909 to 1911, split between total, shipments to Japan proper and shipments abroad.

metadata.title: Marine Products
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of raw and cured marine products in Taiwan for 1904 to 1910, with dashes where no quantity was recorded.

metadata.title: Mineral Products
metadata.description: Lists Taiwan's mineral output for 1904 and 1905: gold, gold dust, coal, sulphur and petroleum.

metadata.title: [Continuation Table of Annual Figures, 1906-1910]
metadata.description: A continuation of an annual statistical series from the previous page, with five years of figures whose column headings are not printed on this page.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's foreign trade by year in yen thousands, with exports, imports, totals and specie and bullion movements.

metadata.title: Trade with Japan Proper
metadata.description: Compares exports and imports of trade with Japan Proper for 1905-1911, showing the excess of imports or exports each year.

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Exported
metadata.caption: Value (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the value of the principal export commodities such as tea, rice, sugar, camphor, turmeric and fibres for each year from 1905 to 1911.

metadata.title: Chief Commodities Imported
metadata.caption: Value (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value in thousands of yen of chief commodities imported into Taiwan, by year from 1905 to 1911, placed before the section on emigration.

metadata.title: Three Important Undertakings
metadata.caption: yen
metadata.description: Lists the three major public works planned by the Formosan Government from 1908-9, with each estimated cost in yen and its start and end years.

metadata.title: Revenue From the Four Monopoly Items
metadata.description: Shows the yearly revenue from Formosa's four state monopolies (camphor, opium, tobacco and salt) from 1904 to 1912, illustrating the monopolies' growing importance to government income.

metadata.title: [Manufactured and Sold Quantities and Values of State Monopolies, Fiscal Years 1909–1911]
metadata.description: Gives the manufactured and sold quantities and values of opium, camphor, camphor oil, salt and tobacco for fiscal years 1909 to 1911, showing the monopoly output behind the revenue figures.

metadata.title: Salt
metadata.description: Shows Taiwan's salt field area, salt output and value for 1907 to 1911, illustrating the growth of the salt industry discussed in the text.

metadata.title: [Gold Output in 1907]
metadata.description: Lists the 1907 gold output of the three principal Taiwan gold mines together with the number of labourer-days worked at each.

metadata.title: Finance
metadata.caption: (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The page gives the estimated finance of the island of Karafuto for fiscal years 1913-14 and 1912-13, listing ordinary and extraordinary expenditures and revenues in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [Marine Products in Karafuto, 1907–1910]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly catch of marine products in Karafuto (Southern Sakhalin) from 1907 to 1910, showing the importance of fishery to the island's economy.

metadata.title: Home Treasury's Burdens
metadata.description: Shows the yearly charges on the home treasury for the Kwantung region, split into the home treasury grant, garrison and navy costs, with totals for 1909-14.

metadata.title: Finance
metadata.caption: (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Summarises the Kwantung Government's revenue and expenditure, ordinary and extraordinary, for 1912-13 and 1913-14, showing the Home Treasury grant's role in receipts.

metadata.title: Home Treasury's Burdens
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a financial table of the Home Treasury's burdens, listing land-sale adjustments, grants and totals for two columns of figures.

metadata.title: Japanese in Manchuria
metadata.description: This table gives the number of Japanese residents in each Manchurian locality, divided into male, female and total, showing the size of the Japanese community there.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade at Dairen (1910)
metadata.description: This table reports the value of Dairen's foreign trade in 1910 by partner country, with exports, imports and totals, compared with the 1909 totals.

metadata.title: Business Report, 1911-'12
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen 1000)
metadata.description: The page gives the South Manchuria Railway Company's business result for 1911-'12, showing earnings, disbursements and profit or loss by business branch in yen thousands.

metadata.title: [Railway Company Income and Expense Statement (continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a financial statement of the South Manchuria Railway Company, listing income and expense items and totals across three unlabelled columns.

metadata.title: To Manchuria via Fusan or Dairen
metadata.description: The passage explains that the Antung-Mukden line saves distance for travellers to Manchuria via Fusan, and this table compares mileage, travel hours and third-class fares by both routes.

metadata.title: To Harbin via Fusan or Tsuruga
metadata.description: The text compares the Tokyo-to-Harbin distance via Tsuruga and Vladivostock, giving the mileage of each leg of that route.

metadata.title: [Freight Rates by Antung-Mukden and Dairen Routes]
metadata.description: The author shows, with a short comparison, that freight from Mukden to Kobe by the Antung-Mukden route costs about fourfold the Dairen route, which matters because the line mainly carries passengers.

metadata.title: [Chien-kin-sai Coal Output, Sales and Profit, 1909-1912]
metadata.caption: (Metallic tons; Yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly output, sales, receipts, disbursements and profit of the Chien-kin-sai coal mine, supporting the preceding description of its large coal reserves.

metadata.title: Weights, Measures and Moneys
metadata.description: A reference table converting Japanese traditional units of money, length, land area, capacity and weight into English and metric equivalents for readers of the Year Book.

metadata.title: [Coast Line and Area of Japanese Territory by Districts]
metadata.description: The table gives the coast line, area in ri, and percentage of total area for each part of the Empire, showing how the Imperial realm is distributed.

metadata.title: Principal Mountain Peaks Measuring Above 8,000 Feet
metadata.description: Lists the principal mountain peaks of Japan (and Formosa) rising above 8,000 feet, with their heights, to illustrate the country's mountainous character.

metadata.title: Rivers Above 70 Ri in Navigable Length
metadata.description: Shows the navigable lengths in ri of Japan's major rivers, noting that rivers are generally short and swift because of the limited distance from watersheds to the coast.

metadata.title: Gales in 1912
metadata.description: The table lists, for each observatory, how many days gales visited in 1912, their average and maximum speed, and the date of the strongest visit, illustrating the wind discussion.

metadata.title: Average Time and Last Occurrence by Place
metadata.description: A short list giving, for four places, the average time of a recurring event and the date it last occurred, printed above the temperature table.

metadata.title: Monthly Average Temperature in Japan
metadata.caption: (From the establishment of the Observatory to 1912)
metadata.description: Monthly and annual average, absolute maximum and minimum temperatures for ten observatories across Japan, showing the climatic range from Taihoku to Nemuro.

metadata.title: Average Monthly Rainfalls and Snowfalls in Japan from the Beginning of Observation to the End of 1912
metadata.description: The table gives average monthly rainfall and snowfall at ten observatories across Japan, showing seasonal and regional variation to support the discussion of climate and floods.

metadata.title: Number of Species Found in Japan
metadata.description: Introduces the fauna of Japan by giving approximate counts of species in each animal group, and how many are peculiar to the country.

metadata.title: [Insect Species Counts]
metadata.description: Lists the number of known insect species in Japan for cicadas and butterflies, before the text on other marine and land animal groups.

metadata.title: Species Existing in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the approximate number of plant species in Japan, divided into flowering plants, ferns and flowerless plants, and seaweeds or algae.

metadata.title: List of Mikados in Alphabetical Order
metadata.description: An alphabetical list of the Mikados (emperors) giving each reign's start and end years, with B.C. dates for the earliest rulers, to serve as a reference index.

metadata.title: [Sovereigns and Dates of Their Reigns]
metadata.description: The list gives the reigns of the early Japanese sovereigns with their dates, with notes on female rulers, Northern Court sovereigns and pre-Christian reigns.

metadata.title: List of the Shōguns and the Regents (Shikken)
metadata.description: This list gives the periods of the shoguns and Hōjō regents by family, showing when each held office during the successive shogunates.

metadata.title: List of Japanese "Year-Names"
metadata.description: A list of Japanese year-names (nengō) with their approximate Western year spans, given to help readers convert dates in the historical narrative of the outline.

metadata.title: [Japanese Era Names with Western Years]
metadata.description: The page lists Japanese era names with their romanized and kanji forms, giving the Western calendar years in which each era began and ended, as a reference for dating events.

metadata.title: [Japanese Era Names (Nengō) with Year Figures]
metadata.description: A reference list of Japanese era names with their romanized and kanji forms, each paired with two year figures, presented to illustrate the historical chronology of the nengō system.

metadata.title: [Japanese Era Names with Year Spans]
metadata.description: A list of Japanese era names (nengō) with their year spans, arranged in four columns, presumably to give the chronology of the reigns for reference.

metadata.title: [Principal Calamities Occurring Since the Tokugawa Period]
metadata.description: Listing the most disastrous earthquakes and their tolls, the table shows the principal calamities after the pre-Tokugawa period, with houses destroyed and deaths for each event.

metadata.title: Mineral Springs by Type and Region
metadata.description: Introducing the Home Office investigations, this table counts Japan's mineral springs by chemical type and by region, showing how many of each kind occur in each district.

metadata.description: Under simple hot springs, the analysis of Dogo Spring gives the amounts of each positive ion per liter of water, in grams, milli-mols and milli-equivalents.

metadata.title: [Anions of Mineral Water Analysis, Continued]
metadata.description: This continues the anion figures of a mineral water analysis from the previous page, giving gram, milli-mol. and milli-equivalent values for each anion and their totals.

metadata.caption: Temperature 60°.6; In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:
metadata.description: This analysis gives the cation and anion composition of the Jizo-no-yu spring at Kusatsu, an acid alum-vitriol water, with per-liter weights and milli-equivalents.

metadata.title: Analysis of Shiobara Spring
metadata.caption: In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:

metadata.title: [Analysis of Mineral Spring (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a mineral spring analysis listing cation and anion constituents per liter, with grams, milli-mol and milli-equivalent values, the totals closing the analysis.

metadata.caption: Sp. W.: 1.0006 when 15 c.; In 1 liter of the mineral water are contained
metadata.description: Analysis of the Kawaura-mura hot spring, listing the cations and anions in one liter of water, given as weight, milli-mol and milli-equivalent, illustrating acid alum spring composition.

metadata.title: Analysis of "Furuyashiki," Cold Spring Nasu
metadata.description: Analysis of the cold Furuyashiki spring at Nasu, a vitriol spring, listing its cation contents per liter in grams, milli-mol and milli-equivalent.

metadata.title: [Cations and Anions of Unnamed Mineral Spring (Continued)]
metadata.description: The page continues a table of ion analysis for an unnamed spring, listing cations and anions in grams, milli-mol and milli-equivalents, with totals.

metadata.title: Analysis of Amidamine Mineral Springs
metadata.caption: Sp. W. 1.012 at 16°. In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:
metadata.description: Analysis of the Amidamine mineral spring, listing cation and anion contents per liter of water in grams, milli-mol and milli-equivalents, as an example of alum-vitriol springs.

metadata.title: Analysis of Furo-sen Spring, Beppu
metadata.caption: Temperature: 56°. In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:
metadata.description: Analysis of the Furo-sen spring at Beppu, an iron carbonate spring, giving cation contents per liter of mineral water.

metadata.title: Analysis of Kowakidani No. II Spring, Hakone
metadata.caption: In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:--
metadata.description: This analysis gives the mineral content of Kowakidani No. II spring in Hakone, listing cations, anions and free hydrogen sulphide per liter of water, as an example of sulphur springs.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Mineral Water Spring (Cations and Anions)]
metadata.description: The top of the page closes an analysis of a bitter spring's cations and anions, giving grams, milli-mol and milli-equivalent values per liter.

metadata.title: Analysis of Yamashiro Spring No. 1
metadata.caption: Sp. W. 1,0017 at 15.° temp. 64.7°; In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained
metadata.description: This analysis gives the mineral composition of Yamashiro spring in Kaga, listing the cations and anions of one liter of its water.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Nashiki-kosen Spring, Akagisan]
metadata.caption: In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:
metadata.description: Gives the chemical analysis of the Nashiki-kosen spring at Akagisan, an alkaline spring, listing cations and anions per liter of water in grams, milli-mol and milli-equivalents.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Oyu Spring, Atami]
metadata.caption: In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:
metadata.description: Gives the chemical analysis of the Oyu spring at Atami, a salt spring dominated by chlorine and sodium ions, with per-liter amounts in grams, milli-mol and milli-equivalents.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Mineral Spring Waters (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues an analysis of mineral spring waters, giving ion and silicate values whose column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Radio-Activity of the Mineral Springs in Japan
metadata.description: The results of testing radium emanation in several Japanese mineral springs, given to show their radio-activity.

metadata.title: Movement of Population
metadata.description: Shows the total and sex-divided population of Japan at the end of each year from 1903 to 1910, with annual increase and rate per 100 population.

metadata.title: Average Density and Families per Region
metadata.description: Gives the relative population density per square ri and the number of persons per family in each region of the country, illustrating regional differences noted in the text.

metadata.title: Distribution of Population in Rural and Urban Districts
metadata.description: Shows how the population was divided between cities of over 10,000 people and villages under 10,000 in selected years from 1894 to 1908, with ratios and totals.

metadata.title: Population by Ages and Sexes
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese population broken down by age group and sex in 1908, with each age group's share per 100 of the population compared across census years 1888 to 1908.

metadata.title: Married and Unmarried
metadata.description: Gives the quinquennial census counts of married and unmarried males and females in Japan proper, first compiled in 1886, to show changes in marital status.

metadata.title: [Percentage of Married and Unmarried Per 100 People]
metadata.description: Shows the percentage of married and unmarried males, females and totals per 100 people in each census year from 1888 to 1908.

metadata.title: Marriages and Divorces
metadata.description: Lists the annual number of marriages and divorces in Japan from 1905 to 1909, with each expressed per 1,000 of population.

metadata.title: Age of Marriage
metadata.description: Shows the number of men and women marrying in each age group in 1900 and 1909, illustrating the age distribution at marriage.

metadata.title: Birth-Rates
metadata.caption: (Excluding Still-Births)
metadata.description: Gives yearly totals of births by sex, births per 100 people, sex ratio at birth and still-births from 1904 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Sex Ratio and Illegitimacy of Births]
metadata.description: Shows the sex ratio of births (total, legitimate and illegitimate) and the illegitimate births per 100 legitimate births by sex, 1904 to 1908.

metadata.title: Death-Rates
metadata.description: Gives yearly death totals by sex, deaths per 100 people, and male mortality relative to female mortality from 1904 to 1909.

metadata.title: Ainus in Hokkaido
metadata.description: Reports the Ainu population in Hokkaido at the end of each year from 1906 to 1912, by sex and in total.

metadata.title: [Birth and Death Rates of Ainus, 1910]
metadata.description: The page gives the 1910 birth and death figures for the Ainu population, broken down by sex, as an introductory statistic.

metadata.title: Population and No. of Households in Principal Cities, with Names of Mayors
metadata.description: A list of principal Japanese cities giving each city's mayor, population and number of households, shown to illustrate urban population at the time.

metadata.title: Number of Passports Issued to Japanese Going Abroad
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of passports issued to Japanese subjects travelling abroad, split by sex, from 1904 to 1911.

metadata.title: Japanese Abroad
metadata.caption: (At the end of June 1913)
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese residing abroad by sex at the end of June 1913 for China, Amoy and Antung.

metadata.title: [Japanese Population Abroad by Locality]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Japanese residents abroad by locality in China, the South Seas, Asiatic Russia, Europe, the United States and Central and South America, split by sex.

metadata.title: [Japanese Emigrants by Sex, 1906–1911]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly number of Japanese emigrants by sex, 1906–1911, preceding the article on Japanese emigrants by Prof. Shigetaka Shiga.

metadata.title: Foreign Visitors to Japan (1913)
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign visitors to Japan in 1913 by nationality, given to indicate the scale of foreign arrivals in the period.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Japan by Districts
metadata.caption: Official returns put the number of foreign residents in Japan from the end of 1906 to 1910 as follows:—
metadata.description: Gives the official counts of foreign residents in Japan by district for 1906 to 1910, with a 1910 breakdown by sex.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Japan by Nationality
metadata.caption: Nationality of foreigners numbering 100 or above is:—
metadata.description: Lists foreign residents in Japan by nationality for 1906 to 1910, with the 1910 figures split by sex, covering nationalities of 100 or more.

metadata.title: [Persons Marrying into Family, Adopted, Naturalized and Rehabilitated, 1906-1911]
metadata.description: Annual counts of marriages into families, adoptions, naturalizations and rehabilitations, shown to illustrate the population statistics for these categories over 1906-1911.

metadata.title: [Area and Rents of Land Held Under Perpetual Lease by Place]
metadata.description: Number of entries, area in tsubo and annual rents in yen of perpetual lease holdings by foreigners in the principal treaty ports, given in round numbers.

metadata.title: [Area Held Under Perpetual Lease by Nationality]
metadata.description: Breakdown of the perpetual lease land area held by principal foreign entries, classified by nationality, in tsubo.

metadata.title: Decorations Granted Each Year
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese decorations of each order and class conferred in each year from 1908 to 1912, with a yearly total.

metadata.title: Holders of the Golden Kite (Military Honor)
metadata.description: Lists the number of holders of the Golden Kite military honor by class for 1907 to 1911, with cumulative totals and the annuities paid out.

metadata.title: [Number of Peers by Rank, 1904-1912]
metadata.description: The table lists the number of peers of each rank for 1904 to 1912, accompanying the discussion of the Japanese peerage and honours.

metadata.title: [Imperial Grants to Kuge Peers, 1894]
metadata.description: The table gives the 1894 Imperial grant of 2,000,000 yen to the Kuge peers, broken down by rank and amount per person.

metadata.title: [National Art Exhibition: Works Submitted, Selected and Exhibited, 1907–1913]
metadata.description: Explains the annual national art exhibition, its selection and prize system, and gives the number of works submitted and exhibited each year from 1907 to 1913.

metadata.title: Recipients of Prizes
metadata.description: Lists the artists who received first, second and third prizes in the national art exhibition, by category of painting and sculpture.

metadata.title: States Aid for Preservation of National Treasures
metadata.description: The page describes the National Treasure Commission and its state aid, and this table shows yearly government preservation grants for structural articles, treasures and their totals from 1897 to 1909.

metadata.title: [Annual Figures, 1910–1912, Continued From Previous Page]
metadata.description: This is the continuation of a multi-year statistical table, whose earlier rows and column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Number of Treasures
metadata.description: This table gives the number of buildings and treasures recorded year by year from 1897 to 1913, with totals, relating to the art collections described on this page.

metadata.title: Buddhist Temples and Priests
metadata.caption: Sects possessing over 1,000 temples are as follows:
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Buddhist temples and priests for the main sects with over 1,000 temples, from 1907 to 1911, illustrating the scale of Buddhist institutions in Japan.

metadata.title: Statistics of Christian Churches in Japan (1911)
metadata.description: Gives the number of churches, foreign and native missionaries, and total membership of the Protestant, Roman Catholic and Russo-Greek churches in Japan in 1911.

metadata.title: Church Expenses in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the income and expenses of native and foreign churches in Japan, by denomination, supporting the discussion of church finances on the page.

metadata.title: Relief Fund
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly state of the prefectural Relief Fund, including apportionments, proceeds, State aids, disbursements and the balance existing, for 1906-7 to 1910-11.

metadata.title: [Paupers and Foundlings Supported by the State]
metadata.description: Gives the number of paupers supported at State expense, the amounts the State paid for them, and the foundlings and their expenses for 1907 to 1911.

metadata.title: [Sums Granted by the Court for Calamities, May 1891 to May 1912]
metadata.description: Shows the total sums the Imperial Court granted at home for various calamities over May 1891 to May 1912, illustrating the Court's charitable benevolence described in the text.

metadata.title: [Red Cross Society Membership, 1877–1913]
metadata.description: The text describes the society's steady growth since 1877, and these figures give its membership at selected years from 1877 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Membership, Expense, Receipt and Fund of the Patriotic Women's Society, 1908–1912]
metadata.description: Shows the rapid growth of the Society's membership, expenses, receipts and fund from 1908 to 1912, offered as evidence of its phenomenal success.

metadata.title: [Inmates of Leper Hospitals at the End of 1912]
metadata.description: The text explains that five state leper hospitals and several private asylums held 1,230 inmates by the end of 1912, and this list gives their distribution.

metadata.title: [Blind People in Japan Proper Classified by Profession, 1910]
metadata.description: The table gives the 1910 breakdown of the 69,167 blind people in Japan proper by profession, showing how many earned a living through shampooing, acupuncture and other trades.

metadata.title: List of Charity Institutions
metadata.description: Shows the number of charity institutions by type, with their expenses and the number of persons rescued, according to the latest reports.

metadata.title: [Charity Institutions Granted State Aid in 1914]
metadata.description: Lists the 117 principal charity institutions that received State aid in 1914, giving each institution's name, religious affiliation and location.

metadata.title: [List of Charitable Institutions, Orphanages and Schools]
metadata.description: An alphabetical list of charitable institutions, orphanages and schools, giving each one's denomination (Buddhist or Christian) and its town or prefecture.

metadata.title: General Statistics on Education
metadata.description: The table gives, for the last three years, the number of schools, instructors, students and pupils, and graduates in each kind of school under government, public and private control.

metadata.title: Foreign Instructors at the Institutions under Direct Control of the Department of Education
metadata.description: Shows the nationalities, total number and annual salary bill of foreign instructors employed at institutions under the Department of Education for 1910-11 and 1911-12.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Lists the subjects taught in each of the four school years of ordinary elementary schools, with weekly hours and total hours for boys and girls.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools (Continued)
metadata.description: Shows the weekly subject timetable of the ordinary elementary schools for the fifth and sixth school years, with hours per week for each subject.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Higher Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the weekly subject timetable of the higher elementary schools for the first, second and sixth school years, with hours per week for each subject.

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age
metadata.description: Gives the number of children of school age by sex, showing those receiving and not receiving the prescribed instruction, those not yet under obligation, and the resulting school attendance ratios.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers of Both Sexes in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows average monthly teachers' salaries in public elementary schools for 1906-7 to 1911-12, with counts of teachers earning under 5 yen and 50 to 75 yen.

metadata.title: [School Fees in Public Elementary Schools]
metadata.description: Shows how many public elementary schools charged fees and how many pupils paid in full, in part, or were exempt, with the average fee, for recent years.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens: Number of Kindergartens, Conductors and Infants]
metadata.description: Gives the number of kindergartens, their conductors and infants enrolled over six years, from 1907-8 to 1911-12, to show growth of this pre-school training.

metadata.title: Blind and Deaf and Dumb Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of blind and mute children of school age, and those receiving instruction at school, with defectives per 1,000 normal children, for 1909-10 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: The Curriculum of the Middle School
metadata.description: Shows the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each year of the five-year middle school course, set out as the national curriculum.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Middle Schools
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for public and private middle schools, covering schools, instructors, pupils and graduates for 1907-8 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: Graduates and Subsequent Careers
metadata.caption: Careers as reported within the year after the graduation are:—
metadata.description: Shows how graduates of the year's schools were employed or otherwise placed within a year of graduating, with those who left school unfinished or died also counted.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Girls' High Schools
metadata.description: Gives the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each of the four years of the girls' high school course.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Girls' High Schools
metadata.description: Statistics of girls' high schools, public and private, giving school numbers, staff, pupils, graduates, leaving rate and admission percentage for 1908-9 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: List of the High Schools
metadata.description: A list of the eight government high schools in November 1913 with their directors, staff, students, graduates, admission rates and expenses, plus yearly totals for 1908-1912.

metadata.title: [Applicants and Admissions by Section]
metadata.description: Shows the number of applicants for admission to the boys' schools by section and the percentage admitted in each section, for 1908 to 1912, illustrating the average age and selection of new pupils.

metadata.title: [Students and Graduates of Normal Schools by Sex]
metadata.description: Gives the male and female instructors, students and graduates of the normal schools for four successive years, showing the classification of students and graduates by sex.

metadata.title: Statistics on Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: The table gives instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admissions for the Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools over three school years, 1909-10 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Tokyo (Dec. 1913)
metadata.caption: Est'd, April 1877; President, Dr. Yamagawa, Kenjiro
metadata.description: Lists the colleges of the Imperial University of Tokyo with place, dean, staff and student numbers as of December 1913.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Kyoto (Dec. 1913)
metadata.caption: Est'd, June 1897; President, Dr. Arai, Torajiro (acting)
metadata.description: Shows the four colleges of the Imperial University of Kyoto with their deans, staff and student numbers as of December 1913.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Tohoku (Dec. 1913)
metadata.caption: Est'd, June 1907; President, Dr. Hojo, Jikei
metadata.description: Gives the colleges of the Imperial University of Tohoku at Sendai and Sapporo with deans, staff and students as of December 1913.

metadata.title: Students in the University Hall
metadata.caption: (Sep. 1913)
metadata.description: Shows how many students attended each Imperial University in September 1913, broken down by faculty.

metadata.title: Average Age of Matriculation at Tokyo
metadata.caption: Average age of those matriculated recently is as follows:—
metadata.description: Lists the average age at which recent students matriculated at Tokyo University, by college, for three academic years.

metadata.title: Professions of the University Graduates
metadata.description: Records how the graduates of the Imperial Universities up to 1911-12 were distributed across different occupations and positions in life.

metadata.title: [Occupations of Graduates, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuation of a table of graduates by occupation or status, with the column headings cut off at the top of the page; the column labels are inferred from the college headings in the next table.

metadata.title: The Total Number of Graduates Classified by Colleges in 1911-'12
metadata.description: Shows how the graduates of 1911-'12 were distributed among the faculties of the Tokyo, Kyoto and Tohoku Imperial Universities.

metadata.title: List of the Government Technical Schools for 1913
metadata.description: The table lists the government technical schools of 1913 by type, with each school's director, instructors, students, admission percentage, graduates and expenses, illustrating the section's account of technical education.

metadata.title: [Special Schools: Principals, Teachers and Pupils]
metadata.description: Lists the special higher schools (mining, agricultural and forestry, sericultural, language, art, music, nautical and fishery) with their location, head and figures.

metadata.title: Public and Private Technical Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of technical schools, instructors, pupils and graduates for four school years, 1908-9 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: Public and Private Blind and Deaf and Dumb Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of blind and deaf and dumb schools, their teachers, public pupils and graduates for three school years.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Blind and Deaf Schools, 1911-12]
metadata.description: Gives staff, pupil, graduate and admission figures for the Tokyo Blind School and the Tokyo Deaf and Dumb School for 1911-12, illustrating the two schools described in the text.

metadata.title: Statistics on Public and Private Collegiate Institutions
metadata.description: Gives student enrolment by subject and graduate numbers at public and private colleges for three academic years, 1909-10 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: [Collegiate Institutions: Name, Location, Founding Date and Subject Taught]
metadata.description: Lists the private and public collegiate institutions with their location, year founded and subjects taught, supporting the preceding statistics on students.

metadata.title: Recipients of Prizes
metadata.description: The Academy's prizes, first awarded in 1911, are listed by year with the recipient, the subject of the work rewarded, and the body giving the prize.

metadata.title: The Educational Stock Fund
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly account of the Educational Stock Fund, created from the Chinese Indemnity, showing its existing sum, loans, bonds and deposits for 1908-09 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: [Receipts of the Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers]
metadata.description: Shows the receipts of the teachers' super-stipend fund by year, from State aid, provincial contributions, interest and balances brought forward.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of the Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers]
metadata.description: Shows how the super-stipend fund was disbursed each year, as additional allowances to teachers and sums carried to the next account.

metadata.title: [Schools Receiving State Aid for Technical Education]
metadata.description: Lists the number of low-grade agricultural, fishery, commercial, navigation and technical schools aided by the State, with the total aid for each year.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid out of Provincial and Communal Treasuries
metadata.description: Shows how much provincial and communal treasuries spent on various kinds of education over four fiscal years, from 1908-9 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Gives the physical condition, by constitution and eyesight, of male students examined in government institutions over four school years.

metadata.title: Health of Public and Private Schools of Secondary and Elementary Education
metadata.description: Gives the health returns for boys in public and private secondary and elementary schools for the 1911-12 year, by school type.

metadata.title: [Health of Girls in Public and Private Schools, 1911-12]
metadata.description: Gives the corresponding health returns for girls in public and private schools for the 1911-12 year, by school type.

metadata.title: [Health Data of Elementary School Children, 1907-1911]
metadata.description: Gives average height and weight of elementary school children by age and sex, drawn from national health data for 1907 to 1911.

metadata.title: The Imperial Library
metadata.description: Statistics of the Imperial Library's volumes, opening days, and visitor numbers over six years, showing its size and use relative to other institutions.

metadata.title: The University Library
metadata.caption: March 1912
metadata.description: Comparison of the volume holdings of the University of Tokyo and University of Kyoto libraries, the Tokyo library being the largest in Japan.

metadata.title: [Library Statistics, 1908-9 to 1911-12]
