metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for libraries: number of libraries, volumes, days open, visitors and average daily visitors, showing growth in library use across four years.

metadata.title: [Total Number of Museum Visitors, 1912]
metadata.description: Shows the total number of museum visitors in 1912 at the museums in Tokyo, Kyoto and Nara, and at the Zoo attached to the Tokyo museum.

metadata.title: [Ryugakusei of the Department of Education Staying Abroad at End of Year]
metadata.description: The page gives the number of the Department of Education's ryugakusei (foreign-going students) staying abroad at the end of each school year from 1904-5 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: License for Secondary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of applications and licenses granted for secondary school teachers over the last four years, with the resulting ratio of licenses, under the examination-free licence service.

metadata.title: License for Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Gives the yearly totals of applications and licenses granted for elementary school teachers, with the ratio of licenses, for the last four years.

metadata.title: Private School Graduates and License
metadata.description: Lists the private universities and institutions authorized to issue secondary school teachers' licenses to superior graduates, with the subject for each.

metadata.title: [Condition of Higher Girls' School Leavers After Leaving School]
metadata.description: Shows what happened to girls graduating from higher schools for girls after leaving school, by category, over six school years, illustrating that marriage was the common ideal.

metadata.title: Stamps in Civil Suits
metadata.description: Gives the schedule of court stamp fees for civil suits, scaled by the value of the object of suit, in the section on the civil law and courts.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts, at End of 1912
metadata.description: Shows how many courts of each grade existed at the end of 1912 and the number of judges and procurators attached to them.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases During 1912
metadata.description: Gives the number of civil cases handled in each court during 1912, with cases disposed of, left pending, and retrials withdrawn or quashed.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases Demanded for Revision
metadata.description: Shows the number of civil cases demanded for revision in 1908–1912 and how they were concluded, with the five-year average.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases Appealed
metadata.description: Shows yearly figures for civil cases appealed, how they were concluded, and cases left pending, with a five-year average.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases Complained
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for civil cases complained, showing how they were concluded and cases still pending, with an average.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases of First Instance
metadata.description: Shows yearly figures for civil cases of first instance, their conclusions, pending cases, and the loss of plaintiffs per 100 decisions.

metadata.title: Nature of the Above Cases
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of cases by the nature of the matter in dispute, with a five-year average, illustrating the composition of the civil litigation reported.

metadata.title: Cases of Bankruptcy and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of bankruptcy cases adjudicated by type of company, cases still pending, credit amounts, and rehabilitation outcomes, with averages.

metadata.title: Cases of Insolvency and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Reports yearly insolvency cases with the numbers of debtors and creditors, the credit involved, and the rehabilitation outcomes, with an average.

metadata.title: No. of Cases Involving Aliens (1912)
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1912 cases involving foreigners by whether the plaintiff was Japanese, foreign, or both foreign, across the three court stages.

metadata.title: No. of Criminal Cases
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal cases handled in 1910–1912 by stage, from searches and preliminary trials through first-instance and appeal proceedings, illustrating the workload under the new criminal code.

metadata.title: Grand Total of Cases
metadata.description: Summarises the total number of cases handled, disposed of and still pending in 1910-1912, as the opening figures for the justice statistics.

metadata.title: Sentence Carried Out
metadata.description: Shows, for 1910-1912, the number of offenders sentenced by case type, the penalties imposed, acquittals, and offenders per 100,000 population, with a note on foreign defendants.

metadata.title: Number of Prison Inmates at End of Year
metadata.description: Gives the number of prison inmates at the end of each year from 1908 to 1912, broken down by prisons, convicts, correction cases, defendants, separate cells, infants and totals.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified
metadata.description: Classifies the new convicts of 1912 by offence and gives the number of convicts per 100,000 population for each category.

metadata.title: [Minor Offences (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a list of minor offence categories with their number and proportion, ending in a total of offences recorded.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences According to Convicts
metadata.description: Convicts are classified by how many times they had offended and by age, showing the frequency of offences for 1910 to 1912 by sex.

metadata.title: [Amnesty Granted on the Occasion of the Imperial Funeral of the Late Emperor Meiji]
metadata.description: Amnesty granted in 1912 at the Imperial funeral of Emperor Meiji, broken down by type, with the share later reimprisoned.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Education
metadata.description: New convicts for 1910 to 1912 are grouped by their level of education, from higher and middle course down to illiterate, by sex.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Property
metadata.description: Shows new convicts for 1908 to 1912 by sex, grouped by their property status, to illustrate the poverty of incoming prisoners.

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Gives yearly sickness figures and mortality among prison inmates from 1908 to 1912, showing the health conditions in prisons.

metadata.title: Work by Prison Inmates and Earnings
metadata.description: Shows the work done by prison inmates and the earnings and shares given to them for 1910 to 1912, to compare convict wage rates with maintenance costs.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-officers and Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Shows how many prison inmates each warder, turnkey and female keeper was responsible for in each year from 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Entered and Left of Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Records the number of prison inmates entering and leaving prisons by sex for 1909 to 1912, broken down by reason for entry and exit.

metadata.title: Revenue of Prison
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the estimated and actual annual revenue of prisons from 1909-10 to 1913-14, split into ordinary and extraordinary receipts.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prison
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows the annual expenditure of Japanese prisons over five fiscal years, broken down into ordinary items and extraordinary outlay, with totals.

metadata.title: Prison Expense Per 1 Inmate
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the average yearly prison expense per inmate, split into ordinary and extraordinary costs with a total, for the same five fiscal years.

metadata.title: Police Offices and Police Force
metadata.description: Shows the number of police stations, police officers, policemen and the total police force for each year from 1907 to 1911, as part of the chapter on police administration.

metadata.title: Suicides and Acts Thereof
metadata.description: Breaks down suicides by method and sex for 1909 to 1911, with male and female totals and a grand total, showing the scale of self-destruction recorded.

metadata.title: Cases of Suicides of Over 200 Classified
metadata.description: Classifies suicides attributed to mental derangement by sex for 1909 to 1911, a category among the leading recorded causes.

metadata.title: [Suicides by Cause, 1909–1911]
metadata.description: The table lists suicide causes by sex for 1909 to 1911, showing the motives recorded for suicides, with the start of the table on the previous page.

metadata.title: Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.description: This table gives the numbers of persons and households suffering from robbery, peculation and fraud over three years, with robbery expressed per 1,000 of population.

metadata.title: Police Offences of Over 200 Cases Classified
metadata.description: The table counts police offences with more than 200 cases in each year from 1909 to 1911, classified by type of offence.

metadata.title: Unnatural Deaths
metadata.description: Records the number of unnatural deaths by cause, with deaths per 100,000 population, for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: Number of Foundlings
metadata.description: Gives the number of foundlings, by sex, for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Summarises the number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, and burned area, with per-case averages, for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: Casualties Concerning Police Affairs
metadata.description: Shows the number of people killed and wounded in police-related casualties from 1906 to 1911.

metadata.title: Rewards with Regard to Police Administration
metadata.description: Reports the number of people rewarded for police administration, by type of reward, and the total money awarded, for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: [Hospitals, Doctors and Mid-wives at End of Year]
metadata.description: Shows the number of hospitals, doctors and licensed mid-wives at the end of 1909 to 1911, illustrating medical provision in Japan alongside the discussion of hospital use.

metadata.title: Vaccination
metadata.description: Records the total number of vaccinations performed in 1909, 1910 and 1911, since vaccination was compulsory in Japan.

metadata.title: Ratio of Successful Vaccination
metadata.description: Shows the percentage of successful vaccinations among persons vaccinated for the first time and among those revaccinated, for selected years from 1905 to 1911.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified
metadata.caption: (Total No. and relative ratio per 1,000 deaths)
metadata.description: Lists the number of deaths and their relative ratio per 1,000 deaths for the main causes of death in 1908 to 1910, illustrating the mortality rate.

metadata.title: Eight Epidemic Diseases and Mortality
metadata.description: Gives annual case and death counts for eight epidemic diseases, plus the combined mortality per 100 cases, for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Labor Strikes by Year, 1908–1911]
metadata.description: Shows the number of labor strikes and laborers involved for 1908 to 1911, given as roughly half the actual figures, following the text on the rise of labor disputes since 1907.

metadata.title: Data at End of March 1913
metadata.description: Summarises the mutual relief insurance societies in some Government establishments at the end of March 1913, showing membership, receipts, disbursements and persons helped.

metadata.title: [Mutual Relief Society Members and Payments by Establishment]
metadata.description: Shows the Mutual Relief Society's membership, deaths, and benefit payments for each government establishment, which the text on Government Railways explains.

metadata.title: [Index Numbers of Mechanic, Output and Spindles in Operations]
metadata.description: Index numbers over 1887–1910 for mechanics, output and spindles in operation, illustrating Japanese labor efficiency growth in the spinning industry.

metadata.title: [Spinning Operatives per 1000 Spindles and Wages in the United States, England and Japan]
metadata.description: Compares, based on 1908 data, the number of operatives per 1000 spindles and the wages in the U.S.A., England and Japan to show Japanese spinning efficiency.

metadata.title: [Wages to Produce 10 Kwan of Yarn by Count in the United States, England and Japan]
metadata.description: Shows the cost in sen of producing 10 kwan of No. 16 and No. 32 count yarn in each country, supporting the claim that output per capita is cheapest in Japan.

metadata.title: Wages Per Week in Yen
metadata.caption: (Maximum ‡ Minimum †)
metadata.description: Gives maximum and minimum weekly wages in yen for five trades in England (1903) and Germany (1908), as comparison for Japanese artisan living expenses.

metadata.title: [International Wage Comparison, France, Belgium, U.S.A. and Japan]
metadata.description: This continued table gives comparative wage or living-cost figures for France, Belgium, the U.S.A. and Japan, the Japanese row showing single values against paired figures for the other countries.

metadata.title: Living Expense in 1903 per Day per Artisan
metadata.caption: (in sen)
metadata.description: This table shows the daily living expenses per artisan in 1903, broken down by category and by the monthly earnings of the principal wage-earner.

metadata.title: Earnings and Disbursements per Year per Artisan
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: This table compares the average yearly earnings, disbursements and resulting balance of an artisan in England, the U.S.A., Germany, France and Japan.

metadata.title: Percentage of Female Labor
metadata.description: This table gives the number of male and female factory workers by age at 25 prefectures in September 1909, with the rate per thousand for each age group.

metadata.title: Child Operatives
metadata.description: This table shows the percentage of child operatives under 16 in the factory types where they make up the largest share, by age band.

metadata.title: [Factory Statistics Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top of this page continues a table of industry figures whose column headings appear on the previous page; it is followed by the Female Operatives discussion.

metadata.title: [Working Hours, Rest Hours, Monthly Holidays and Yearly Working Days in Factories]
metadata.description: Gives typical daily working hours, rest hours, monthly holidays and yearly working days for six kinds of factories, showing ordinary, maximum and minimum figures.

metadata.title: [Operatives at Government Factories by Sex and Age, End of 1912]
metadata.description: Shows the number of male and female operatives over and under fourteen years at Government works at the end of 1912, with totals.

metadata.title: [Working Hours, Rest Hours and Holidays at Army Cloth Factory]
metadata.description: Gives work hours, rest intervals, monthly holidays and yearly work days for male, female and child operatives at Government army cloth works.

metadata.title: [Factory Labor Conditions by Industry]
metadata.description: A multi-column table of labor conditions across woolen, tobacco, paper and printing industries, split by male, female and child workers, shown under the Social Politics and Labor Problems heading.

metadata.title: Wages of Laborers
metadata.caption: Average Daily Wages (yen)
metadata.description: Average daily wages of various skilled and unskilled occupations in Japan for the years 1906, 1910, 1911 and 1912, showing labor pay trends under the Wages of Laborers heading.

metadata.title: Operatives Classified According to Employment, Giving Only Those Employing Not Less Than 10,000 Operatives
metadata.description: The table classifies operatives by type of employment in large factories employing at least 10,000 operatives, giving male, female and total figures for 1911 and 1912.

metadata.title: [Millionaire Families by Locality, End of 1912]
metadata.description: Shows how the 408 Japanese millionaire families at the end of 1912, reported by the Osaka Asahi, were distributed among prefectures and cities.

metadata.title: [Millionaire Families by Profession]
metadata.description: Shows the relative numbers of Japanese millionaire families by profession, as divided according to the same Osaka Asahi survey.

metadata.title: Causes of Poverty
metadata.description: The page lists the recorded causes of poverty with the number of cases attributed to each, in two side-by-side columns totalling 3,224.

metadata.title: [Number of Dailies and Periodicals Existing at End of Year]
metadata.description: The figures give the number of dailies and periodicals existing at the end of each of the latest years available, from 1904 to 1911.

metadata.title: [Japanese Periodicals Published in Tokyo]
metadata.description: A list of Japanese periodicals with their subject, frequency, price and publisher, continuing from the previous page, giving the press of the period.

metadata.title: [Output of Books, 1908-1911]
metadata.description: Shows the number of books published in recent years, split into original works and translations, to illustrate the growth of publishing.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of copyright registrations by category, with transfers, under the revised copyright law, showing the trend from 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: Censorship
metadata.description: The table gives yearly counts of publications banned for sale or seized, and of plates seized, on grounds of public order and public morals, from 1906 to 1911.

metadata.title: [Famous Wrestlers of Tokyo]
metadata.description: The page lists the famous wrestlers of Tokyo, grouped by Eastern and Western camp, with their birth years and physical measurements in kwan and shaku.

metadata.title: [Cost of River Works by Different Finances, 1905–1909]
metadata.chapter_raw: Chapter Xv — Constructions and Public Works
metadata.description: The table shows the annual cost of river works from 1905 to 1909, broken down by financing body, illustrating the split between central government, prefectures and local bodies.

metadata.title: Principal Harbor-Works
metadata.description: Among the leading harbor improvement works, this list gives each harbor's works, the dates they began and were completed, and their expenditure in thousand yen.

metadata.title: [Harbour Works at Ports Listed in the Opening Paragraph]
metadata.description: Listing of harbour improvement works at several ports, giving the work done, its start and completion dates, and its cost, illustrating the port-improvement programme described in the text.

metadata.title: [Civil Engineering Expenses by Classification, 1905–1909]
metadata.description: Breakdown of the national treasury's civil engineering expenditure by category (rivers, roads, harbours and so on) for each year from 1905 to 1909, shown to illustrate the text's account of spending.

metadata.title: Damage from Floods and Other Calamities
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly damage from floods, tidal waves and typhoons, by category, for 1908 to 1911 and the average of 1902 to 1911, in thousand yen.

metadata.title: [Waterworks of Principal Cities]
metadata.description: Lists the most important city waterworks, giving construction cost, pipe extension, daily water supply, houses supplied and daily quantity per house.

metadata.title: [Arable Land: Paddy and Upland Fields]
metadata.description: Shows the area of paddy and upland fields and their share of the whole national area, illustrating the steady rise in the proportion of arable land.

metadata.title: [Unreclaimed Land Inclined Less Than 15 Degrees]
metadata.description: Gives, by region, land inclined under 15 degrees, the area already under tillage, and the remaining unreclaimed area, to show the margin available for reclamation.

metadata.title: [Farming Population by Families, 1903 and 1912]
metadata.description: Gives the number of farming families in 1903 and 1912 and their percentage of all families, based on the central authorities' latest returns.

metadata.title: Independent Farmers and Tenant Farmers
metadata.caption: (Area in cho; percentage)
metadata.description: Shows the cultivated area of paddy-fields and upland farms worked by owners and by tenants in 1904, 1909 and 1912, with each category's percentage share, to illustrate the spread of tenant farming.

metadata.title: Taxable Land
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000 cho)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly taxable land area in 1,000 cho by category from 1908 to 1913, supporting the text's statement on the total taxable land at the end of 1912 and its comparison over recent years.

metadata.title: Highest Class
metadata.caption: (Official value and market value per tan, March 1912, in Yen)
metadata.description: Compares the market price (M.P.) and official valuation (O.V.) per tan of highest-class paddy fields and upland farms in four prefectures in March 1912, showing that market prices far exceed official values.

metadata.title: Lowest Prices
metadata.description: Shows the lowest recorded prices for two prefectures, Iwate-ken and Kochi-ken, though the column headings are not printed.

metadata.title: [Average Yield Per Tan of Paddy Field, 1892–1912]
metadata.description: Shows the average paddy yield per tan over successive periods and the twenty-year average, illustrating the rise in productive power of tilled land.

metadata.title: [Farmers' Families Classified by Cultivated Area, 1911 and 1912]
metadata.description: Classifies farmers' families by the average area they cultivate, giving family numbers and percentage shares for 1911 and 1912.

metadata.title: Ratio of One-Crop and Two-Crop Farms
metadata.description: Official returns showing the proportion of one-crop and two-crop paddy fields in recent years, in cho and as percentages of the total area.

metadata.title: Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.description: Approximate area of land tilled by cattle or horse labor in 1904 and 1912, in cho and as percentages, for paddy-fields and upland farms.

metadata.title: [Artificial Fertilizers Produced in 1912]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The text gives the value of artificial fertilizers produced in Japan in 1912 by principal kind, showing the total national output of manures.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives Japan's rice area, production, and export and import quantities and values for 1909-1913 and the normal yield, showing rice trade and output trends.

metadata.title: [Yield of Rice Plant per Tan at Government Experimental Farms]
metadata.description: The text compares average output per tan of early, middle and late rice varieties at Government Experimental Farms, showing the middle variety is most productive.

metadata.title: Barley and Wheat
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives yearly production of barley, naked barley and wheat from 1909 to 1913 against the normal crop, showing these upland staples as second crops after rice.

metadata.title: [Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat Area by Field Type, 1913]
metadata.caption: (cho)
metadata.description: Showing 1913 data, this table splits the cultivated area of barley, naked barley and wheat between paddy-fields and dry farms, illustrating which crops are grown in each field type.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: The table lists production of miscellaneous grains, including millets, buckwheat and maize, for 1908 to 1912, as minor food crops alongside rice, barley and wheat.

metadata.title: Beans, Sweet Potato and Potato
metadata.description: The table gives annual production figures for soy, red, horse and pea beans, sweet potatoes and potatoes from 1908 to 1912, illustrating the importance of these subsidiary farm crops.

metadata.title: Some Special Crops
metadata.caption: (in kwan)
metadata.description: Shows output of indigo, tobacco, cotton, hemp and rape seed for 1908-1912, illustrating how monopoly-protected tobacco grew while cotton and indigo declined against imports.

metadata.title: Other Minor Crops (1912)
metadata.description: Lists the cultivated area and output of minor crops in 1912, such as radish, ginger, lily, rush and peppermint, as a supplement to the special crops above.

metadata.title: [Mulberry Trees Area]
metadata.description: The mulberry tree acreage for 1908 to 1913 is given to show the growth of planting that supports the silk industry, which the Government encouraged with subsidies.

metadata.title: Output of Cocoons
metadata.caption: (in 1000)
metadata.description: Annual cocoon output figures, with egg-cards hatched and reeled silk grades, show the yield per egg-card as a measure of improving sericultural production.

metadata.title: Cocoons by Season
metadata.caption: (1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Shows annual cocoon production by season (spring, summer, autumn) with the seasonal percentage shares, giving the basis for raw silk output.

metadata.title: Output of Raw Silk
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly raw silk output in kwan, waste silk, floss silk, and the sheet and cellular (moth) rearing methods used for cocoons.

metadata.title: [Raw Silk Establishments and Output Value, 1912]
metadata.description: Summarises the number of silk-producing establishments and the quantities and values of each silk category in 1912.

metadata.title: [Output of Filature, Frame and Tama Silk, 1912]
metadata.caption: (in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1912 output of filature, frame and Tama (doupion) silk by product type, giving quantities and yen values.

metadata.title: Average Price of Raw Silk at Yokohama
metadata.caption: (Per 100 kin)
metadata.description: Records the average Yokohama price per 100 kin of filature steam raw silk in two denier grades for 1908 to 1913.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Raw Silk Production
metadata.description: Compares the number of families engaged in and the value of raw silk production in the four leading prefectures in 1911 and 1912.

metadata.title: [Prefectural Sericultural Figures, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuation of a prefectural table of sericulture figures, with rows for Nagano, Fukushima, Saitama, Gifu and Yamagata; its headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: [Silk Conditioning Statistics by Year]
metadata.description: Shows yearly silk conditioning house figures at Yokohama, covering conditioning, weighing, boil-off and quality tests, from 1909 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Direct Export of Raw Silk by Japanese and Foreign Firms]
metadata.description: Shows the total raw silk bales exported directly, split between Japanese and foreign firms with their percentage shares, 1908 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Raw Silk Export Quantity and Value by Destination]
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of raw silk exported by Japanese merchants to each destination country in 1912 and 1913.

metadata.title: Area of Tea Plantations and Number of Manufacturers
metadata.description: Shows the declining tea plantation area alongside the rising number of tea manufacturers from 1907 to 1912, illustrating the stagnation of the tea industry described in the text.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Tea
metadata.description: Gives the annual output of green, black and oolong tea by grade, with totals, for 1908 to 1912, supporting the discussion of the stagnant tea output.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1912)
metadata.description: Shows the leading tea-producing districts in 1912 with their output in kwan and value in yen, placed beside the surrounding text on tea production.

metadata.title: Export of Teas
metadata.description: Gives the quantity and value of tea exported from 1909 to 1913, following the note that manufacturers are turning to black and brick tea.

metadata.title: [Volume of Teas Exported through Various Ports]
metadata.description: Lists the volume of teas exported through the main ports, in kwan, pounds and boxes, as introduced by the sentence on exports through various ports.

metadata.title: Destination of Teas Exported
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Shows the value in thousand yen of tea exports by destination country or region from 1909 to 1913.

metadata.title: Number of Horses in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of native, cross-bred and foreign horses in Japan from 1908 to 1912, supporting the discussion of the decline of the native breed.

metadata.title: Number of Stallions in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the yearly count of native, cross-bred and foreign stallions in Japan from 1908 to 1912, shown alongside the horse figures under the agriculture heading.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of native, cross-bred and foreign cattle in Japan, with totals, calvings and deaths, 1907 to 1912, as part of the stock-farming section.

metadata.title: Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Gives the yearly head counts of sheep, goats and swine in Japan from 1907 to 1912.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Records the number of animals slaughtered at licensed slaughter houses by kind, from 1907 to 1912.

metadata.title: Leading Stock Farms
metadata.description: A list of leading stock farms in Japan, giving each farm's location, kind of stock and ownership, introduced by a note that Hokkaido is the most important area for stock farming.

metadata.title: [Government and Private Stock Farms]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a list of government and private stock farms, with their location, kind of stock and management, before the chapter on poultry begins.

metadata.title: Number of Families Keeping Poultry
metadata.description: Shows how many families kept poultry each year from 1909 to 1913, with fowl and egg numbers and values, illustrating the small scale of the poultry industry.

metadata.title: Leading Poultry Districts at the End of June (1913)
metadata.description: Lists the five prefectures with the largest poultry industry in mid-1913, giving family numbers and the value of fowl and eggs.

metadata.title: Leading Dairy Districts (1912)
metadata.description: Shows dairy farm numbers, milk cows and milk output in koku and yen for leading dairy prefectures in 1912, with national totals for three years, to illustrate the dairy trade.

metadata.title: [Animal Epidemics, 1908–1912]
metadata.description: Summarises annual cases of glanders, farcy, anthrax and rinderpest in horses and cattle from 1908 to 1912, introducing the discussion of rinderpest's damage to cattle owners.

metadata.title: Fruits
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Accompanying the text on fruit-culture's recent growth, this table gives the number of trees and the yield of the principal fruits for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Distribution of Strata by Rock Type]
metadata.description: The page classifies the rocks existing in Japan by relative percentage, separating sedimentary from igneous rocks and giving the grand total of all strata.

metadata.title: Mineral Production
metadata.caption: Momme = 2.411 dwts. Kin = 1.607 lbs. (Troy). Kwan = 10.047 lbs. (Troy). Koku = 39.703 gallons.
metadata.description: Table of annual mineral production in Japan from 1908 to 1912 by mineral, giving quantities and values, with a total value; it excludes Formosa.

metadata.title: Principal Metal-mines
metadata.caption: (figures in 1000)
metadata.description: The page's metal-mining survey lists yearly output of gold, silver and copper at the principal mines, illustrating the mining section's discussion of metals.

metadata.title: [Mine Output Figures, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuation of a table of individual mine output figures, the column headings of which fall on the previous page.

metadata.title: [Iron Output of Kamaishi and Senninyama]
metadata.caption: (Unit: m. tons)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly iron output of the two principal iron mines, Kamaishi and Senninyama, from 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Lead and Zinc Output of Kamioka]
metadata.description: Shows the lead and zinc output of the Kamioka mine for 1910 to 1912, as a further note on Japanese mining.

metadata.title: [Available Coal Resources by District]
metadata.caption: (Unit: million tons)
metadata.description: Shows the roughly estimated distribution of Japan's available coal resources among Kyushu, Hokkaido and other districts.

metadata.title: [Output of the Chief Coal-Fields of Japan, 1910–1912]
metadata.description: Gives annual output in million tons of the chief coal-fields of Japan, grouped by Hokkaido, Iwaki-Hitachi and Chikuho, for 1910 to 1912, following the discussion of available coal resources.

metadata.title: Analysis of Coals from the Principal Coal-Fields
metadata.description: Shows proximate and chemical analysis of coals from the principal coal-fields, including water, volatile matter, coke, ash, sulphur, caking quality, specific gravity and calorific power.

metadata.title: [Crude Oil Output in Echigo Fields, 1910-1913]
metadata.description: The page gives the recent annual output of crude oil from the Echigo oil fields by district, with total output and value, to show how production has developed.

metadata.title: [Echigo Production by Oil Classification, 1911-1912]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Koku)
metadata.description: The text states that production from the Echigo fields is classified by type of oil, and this table gives the 1911 and 1912 figures for each category.

metadata.title: [Wells in Echigo Fields by Digging Method]
metadata.description: The page describes the drilling methods used in Echigo, including the Kazusabori artesian method, and this table counts the wells in each main field by method.

metadata.title: Leading Concessionaires of Mines
metadata.description: Lists the mining concessionaires whose production in 1911 and 1912 exceeded or nearly reached two million yen, with the number of mines each worked.

metadata.title: Number of Mine-Workers at Principal Mines
metadata.caption: (At the end of June)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of mine workers at principal mines, by mine type, with alluvial diggers, from 1908 to 1912, taken at the end of June.

metadata.title: Work and Wages of Mine-Workers
metadata.description: Gives the monthly working days and average daily hours of miners and other mine-workers in metal mines and coal mines, from Mining Bureau research.

metadata.title: Average Wages at Principal Mines (in yen; 1912)
metadata.description: Shows average daily wages paid to each class of worker at metal mines and collieries in 1912, by sex and age, in yen.

metadata.title: Accidents at the Mines
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of accidents at mines from 1908 to 1912, broken down by fatal, severely wounded and other cases.

metadata.title: Imports and Exports of Mineral Production
metadata.description: Lists yearly exports of copper, coal and sulphur and imports of iron and steel and petroleum, 1908 to 1912, as a mineral trade summary.

metadata.title: Fishing-Boat
metadata.description: Shows the number of fishing boats in Japan from 1908 to 1912, total and by newly built, worn out and European boats, illustrating the fishery's scale.

metadata.title: Accidents to Fishing-Boats and Casualties to Fishermen
metadata.description: Shows the number of fishing boats wrecked, drifted, missing, upset or otherwise damaged, and the resulting killed, wounded and missing crew, for 1912 with 1911 and 1910 for comparison.

metadata.title: The Value of Catches and Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of fishing catches and of marine products in yen from 1908 to 1912, showing the growth of the fisheries.

metadata.title: Value of Catch and Commercial Value of Principal Kinds of Fish, Shellfish, Etc. in 1911 and 1912
metadata.description: Lists the quantity in thousand kwan and value in thousand yen of the principal kinds of fish and shellfish caught in 1912 and 1911, explaining the catch values summarised above.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Catches (in yen; 1912)
metadata.description: Shows the value of catches by leading prefectures and Hokkaido in 1912, split into fish, shell fish, aquatic animals and totals, to illustrate the regional distribution of fishery output.

metadata.title: [Custom Returns of Staple Marine Products, 1912]
metadata.description: Lists the quantities and values of the main marine products exported in 1912, according to customs returns, as an illustration of the export trade.

metadata.title: Aquaculture
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of aquaculture products from 1908 to 1912, by species, showing the growth of cultivated fisheries in Japan.

metadata.title: [Development of Pelagic Fishery, 1908–1912]
metadata.description: Shown after the text on the bounty, this table gives the growth of deep-sea and pelagic fishing vessels, including aided and unaided, by type, tonnage, crew and catches for 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Deep Sea Catches
metadata.description: Gives the 1912 returns of Japan proper's deep-sea fisheries by branch, showing vessels by type, crew and catch value to illustrate the situation of the industry.

metadata.title: [Salt Fields, Furnaces and Production, 1908–1912]
metadata.description: Shows the decline in salt fields, furnaces and output of Japan's salt industry from 1908 to 1912, illustrating the state-monopoly production described in the preceding prose.

metadata.title: Area of Forests
metadata.caption: (1 cho = 2.5 acres) (At the end of 1912)
metadata.description: This table gives the area of forests in Japan at the end of 1912, broken down by ownership and by forest category, showing the total forest area under each owner.

metadata.title: Distribution of Forests
metadata.description: Lists the prefectures containing not less than 600,000 cho of forest in 1912-13, showing the area of each in cho.

metadata.title: Forest Yield for 1912-13 (Exclusive of Formosa and Saghalien)
metadata.description: Shows the forest yield returned for 1912-13 by kind of tree, giving timber and fagot quantities and values, to illustrate that forestry yielded little revenue.

metadata.title: Average Output of Forest Products for Years (1908-12)
metadata.caption: (In ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the average annual output value of the principal forest products over 1908-12, listed in two columns by product.

metadata.title: Financial Yield of Forest Classified (1913)
metadata.description: Shows the 1913 financial yield of forests by ownership class (State, Crown, Public and private), split into timber, fagots and total values.

metadata.title: [Receipts, Expenses and Balance Surplus of State Forests]
metadata.description: Gives the receipts, expenses and balance surplus of State forest accounts for the years 1908-9 to 1912-13, to illustrate the modest rate of profit.

metadata.title: Principal Items of Forest Products in Foreign Trade
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Lists the main forest products (timber, tea-chest boards, matches, bamboos) and total forest-product exports and imports in foreign trade for 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Working Plan Forest Composition by Management System]
metadata.description: Gives the percentage breakdown of the 1,735,174 cho working plan area, by forest management system and barren land, as ascertained up to March 1912.

metadata.title: [Rotation Periods for Principal Trees]
metadata.description: Lists the rotation periods in years adopted for the principal trees to be preserved or planted in State forests under the working plan.

metadata.title: Total Volume of Felling (Shakujime) and Conversion
metadata.description: Shows the yearly volume of timber and fagots felled and converted, in shakujime, for 1911 to 1913, as part of the forestry statistics.

metadata.title: Sized Logs and Charcoals (Kwan)
metadata.description: Gives the quantities of sized logs (timber) and charcoal produced in kwan for 1907 to 1909, as part of the forestry returns.

metadata.title: Hewn Boards, Etc.
metadata.description: Shows the quantity of hewn timber boards produced for 1907 to 1909, reported alongside the other forestry production figures.

metadata.title: Private Sawing Yards
metadata.description: Lists the private sawing yards in the districts of Akita and Osaka, the leading districts, with their number, capital, wood converted and motive power.

metadata.title: Output and Value of Refined Camphor (Japan Proper)
metadata.description: Gives the annual output and value of refined camphor in Japan Proper for 1907 to 1912, following the text on experiments with camphor twigs.

metadata.title: [Shooting Licenses Issued, 1909-1913]
metadata.description: Shows the number of shooting licences of Classes A and B issued each year from 1909 to 1913, illustrating how the number of sportsmen changed after fees were raised.

metadata.title: [Joint Stock Companies, 1907–1912]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly growth from 1907 to 1912 in the number of companies, paid-up capital and reserves, as a background to the industry figures that follow.

metadata.title: Industrial Establishments Classified by Amount of Investment
metadata.caption: Paid up capital in (1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Lists industries whose paid-up capital is 500,000 yen or more, comparing the number of companies and capital invested in 1911 and 1912.

metadata.title: [Industrial Companies by Industry, Factories, Hands and Paid-up Capital]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues an industry table listing numbers of establishments and capital figures by industry, with the column headings lying on the previous page; the text then notes that most of these industries began after the port opening.

metadata.title: Leading Districts Containing Companies with Capital over Yen 10,000,000 (1912)
metadata.description: This table lists the leading prefectures by number of companies and paid-up capital for companies with capital over ten million yen in 1912, showing where large industrial enterprises were concentrated.

metadata.title: Factories and Employees
metadata.description: This table gives the yearly number of factories, split by type of power, and the number of male, female and total operatives employed from 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Motive Power Used in Factories, 1912
metadata.description: Following the factory figures, this small table gives the number of engines and horse power for each kind of motive power used in 1912.

metadata.title: [Motive Power Engines in Factories]
metadata.description: Gives the number of engines and horse power of the motive power used in factories, by type of water wheel, dynamo and motor.

metadata.title: Kind of Factories Classified
metadata.description: Lists the number of factories, those not worked by motive power, and employees in each industry group, showing the scale of factory industry by kind of enterprise.

metadata.title: Cotton Spinning
metadata.description: General statistics of the Japanese cotton spinning industry from 1908 to 1912, giving number of mills, paid-up capital, spindles and output.

metadata.title: Exports and Imports of Cotton Yarns
metadata.description: Shows the yearly quantities and values of cotton yarn exported and imported by Japan from 1908 to 1912, illustrating the growth of the export trade.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Cotton Spinning (1912)
metadata.description: Lists the number of mills, capital, spindles, operatives and output of cotton spinning mills in the leading prefectures in 1912.

metadata.title: Silk Spinning
metadata.description: Gives the number of silk spinning mills, their capital, spindles and output of silk yarn and tsumugi from 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Hempen Spinning
metadata.description: Gives the number of hempen spinning mills, paid-up capital, spindles and output for 1908 to 1912, showing the trend of the industry.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Hempen Spinning
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures for hempen spinning by number of mills and output, showing where the industry was concentrated.

metadata.title: Establishments, Operatives and Products
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for Japan's textile industry from 1908 to 1912: establishments, looms, operatives and value of output, illustrating the scale of the sector described above.

metadata.title: [Mousseline-de-Laine Producers and Looms]
metadata.description: Lists the four leading companies producing mousseline-de-laine and the number of stands (looms) each operates, in the text on the mousseline-de-laine industry.

metadata.title: Production (Value)
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of Japan's textile production, by fabric type, from 1908 to 1912, as a background to the industry's growth.

metadata.title: Exports (Value)
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly export values of silk, cotton and woolen goods and the total exports from 1908 to 1912, showing the trade side of the textile industry.

metadata.title: Leading Weaving Districts (1912)
metadata.caption: Value (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the value of silk, mixed, cotton, hempen and woolen fabrics produced in each leading weaving prefecture in 1912.

metadata.title: Principal Fabrics (1912)
metadata.description: Lists the principal silk, silk-and-cotton and cotton fabrics by output value in 1912, showing which textiles dominated Japanese weaving at the time.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Habutaye for Exports
metadata.description: Gives the number of establishments, looms, operatives and output of the four leading prefectures producing habutaye for export, with totals.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of ceramic and Shippo production and export from 1908 to 1911, illustrating the trade trend of the ceramic industry.

metadata.title: Leading Ceramic Districts (1912)
metadata.description: Lists the seven leading ceramic prefectures in 1912 with families engaged, operatives and value of output, supporting the discussion of the ceramic industry.

metadata.title: Production and Export
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of lacquer-ware production and exports from 1907 to 1912, illustrating the growth of the lacquer industry.

metadata.title: Leading Lacquer-ware Districts
metadata.description: Lists the six leading lacquer-ware districts in 1912 with the number of families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Output
metadata.description: Gives the annual output of sake, beer and soy in koku from 1908 to 1912, as the opening of the brewing industry section.

metadata.title: Matches
metadata.description: Shows Japan's matchmaking output and exports from 1908 to 1912 by quantity, value and price per gross, illustrating the match industry's development alongside the beer and soy notes.

metadata.title: Leading Match Districts (1912)
metadata.description: Shows the number of families, operatives and value of match manufacture in the three leading match districts in 1912.

metadata.title: [Japanese Match Exports by Destination (1912)]
metadata.description: Lists the destinations of Japanese matches exported from Kobe and Osaka in 1912, with box counts and the total.

metadata.title: [Cement Industry Statistics (1909-1912)]
metadata.description: Shows the number of cement factories, employees, output and value from 1909 to 1912, set against the over-production problem in the industry.

metadata.title: [Paper Produced in 1912]
metadata.description: Shows the amount and value of each kind of paper produced in Japan in 1912, with totals, following the comparison with mill numbers and capital from ten years earlier.

metadata.title: Statistics of Japanese Paper
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of paper mills, paid-up capital, quantity and value of Japanese paper production from 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Leading Japanese Paper Districts (1912)
metadata.description: Lists the main paper-producing prefectures in 1912 with the families engaged, operatives and output of each.

metadata.title: European Paper
metadata.description: Compares European-style paper establishments, capital, operatives, output and imported value for 1908 to 1912, noting that Japanese mills depend on imported pulp.

metadata.title: [Soap Industry Statistics, 1908-1912]
metadata.description: Shows the number of soap establishments, workers and soap output by type from 1908 to 1912, illustrating the growth of the Japanese soap industry mentioned in the text.

metadata.title: [Output of Sardine, Herring and Whale Oil, 1909–1912]
metadata.description: The page introduces the output of sardine, herring, whale and other oils for 1909 to 1912, showing quantities in koku and values in thousand yen.

metadata.title: [Gas Companies, 1908–1912]
metadata.description: Shows the rapid growth of the gas industry from 1908 to 1912 in number of companies, paid-up capital and length of pipes, illustrating the 'rapid growth' noted in the text.

metadata.title: Leading Gas Works
metadata.description: Lists the five leading gas works with their paid-up capital, length of pipes and coal consumption, giving a view of the largest companies in the gas industry.

metadata.title: [Electric Enterprises in Operation, 1908]
metadata.description: Gives the number and kilowatt capacity of electric enterprises in operation in 1908, broken down by type of works, to show the growth of electricity supply.

metadata.title: Electric Enterprises by Motive Power, 1909–1912
metadata.description: Shows the number and kilowatt capacity of electric enterprises by motive power and operator type from 1909 to 1912, plus projects awaiting official sanction.

metadata.title: Electric Industry Classified by Nature of Enterprise and Motor Force Employed, 1912
metadata.caption: (Kilowatt)
metadata.description: Breaks down 1912 electric industry kilowatt capacity by hydro, steam, gas and other power sources, separating sanctioned and not-yet-sanctioned projects by enterprise type.

metadata.title: Production
metadata.caption: (1,000 kin.)
metadata.description: Shows annual sugar production in Japan Proper, its Kagoshima and Okinawa prefectures, and Formosa's unrefined and refined output for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: Leading Sugar Refining Factories
metadata.description: Lists the leading sugar refining factories in 1912, showing their raw material sources and their output in quantity and value.

metadata.title: Leading Flour Districts (1912)
metadata.description: Shows the number of mills, output and value of flour production in the leading flour-producing prefectures in 1912, with the national total.

metadata.title: Imports and Exports of Wheat and Flour
metadata.description: Gives Japan's yearly imports and exports of wheat and flour from 1909 to 1912 in yen, showing the growing reliance on imported wheat for milling.

metadata.title: [Peppermint Plantation Area and Crop]
metadata.description: Peppermint cultivation, showing the area of plantations and the crop harvested for 1910 to 1912, with Hokkaido noted as the main producing region.

metadata.title: [Crude Menthol and Crystal Oil Production]
metadata.caption: (yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Values of crude peppermint, menthol crystal and peppermint oil for 1909 to 1912, given in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Output
metadata.description: Output of vegetable wax, split into crude and refined wax and total, for 1909 to 1912, after the industry began to recover.

metadata.title: [Vegetable Wax Value by Prefecture, 1912]
metadata.description: Value of vegetable wax produced in four prefectures in 1912, placed beside the wax output figures.

metadata.title: Total Output
metadata.description: Shows the yearly total output of the vegetable oils industry, with employees, value and the breakdown by oil-seed type from 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Leading Vegetable Oils Districts (1912)
metadata.description: Lists the five leading districts for vegetable oil production in 1912, with families engaged, employees and value of output.

metadata.title: Indigo (Japanese)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly figures for Japanese indigo production from 1908 to 1912: families engaged, employees and value.

metadata.title: Production
metadata.description: Production figures for the straw and chip braid industry from 1908 to 1912, with the leading prefectural districts, illustrating the trade's growth and its concentration in a few areas.

metadata.title: Output
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output value of ordinary and fancy mats and mattings, with the leading prefectures for mats, supporting the discussion of the mat industry on this page.

metadata.title: Output
metadata.description: Shows families engaged, operatives and value of hide and leather production, with leading districts and the 1912 value breakdown, illustrating the leather industry discussed on this page.

metadata.title: [Hosiery Exports, 1910–1913]
metadata.chapter_raw: The Japan Year Book — Vii. Sundry Industries
metadata.description: Shows the growth of Japanese hosiery exports, which rose steadily from 1910 to 1913 in both dozens and yen values.

metadata.title: [Canning Factories by Prefecture, 1912]
metadata.chapter_raw: The Japan Year Book — Vii. Sundry Industries
metadata.description: Lists canning factories, employees and output by product and prefecture in 1912, accompanying the discussion of Japan's growing canned fish industry.

metadata.title: [Umbrella Production and Exports, 1909–1913]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly production and export quantities and values of umbrellas from 1909 to 1913, supporting the industry description above it.

metadata.title: Bricks and Tiles in 1912
metadata.description: Shows the 1912 brick industry by prefecture: number of factories, employees and output value, split into fireproof, ordinary and total bricks.

metadata.title: B. Tiles
metadata.description: Lists the number of tile factories, employees and value in the leading tile-producing prefectures and the national total for 1912.

metadata.title: Leading Silk Handkerchief Districts (1912)
metadata.description: Shows the workshops, employees and value of silk handkerchief production in the three leading districts in 1912.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Industries (1912)
metadata.description: Gives the workshops, employees and value of bamboo ware and fan manufacturing as miscellaneous industries in 1912.

metadata.title: Leading Factories Conducted by Government (1912)
metadata.description: Lists the government-run factories with their steam, gas and oil engine horsepower, employees and coal consumed in 1912.

metadata.title: [Fee for Extension of Patent]
metadata.chapter: Patents, Designs, Trade-Marks and Utility Models
metadata.chapter_raw: Chapter XXI: Patents, Designs, Trade-Marks and Utility Models
metadata.description: The page explains Japanese patent fees and term, and this short list gives the fees payable for extending a patent in successive year-bands.

metadata.title: No. of Applications and Registrations
metadata.description: Shows yearly numbers of applications filed at the Patent Office and registrations or grants for patents, designs, trade-marks and utility models from 1909 onward.

metadata.title: No. of Actions for Trial and No. of Cases Upheld
metadata.description: Lists the number of actions brought for trial, appeal and appeal to the Supreme Court in each year, with the number of cases upheld, for each industrial property category.

metadata.title: No. Existing at the End of the Fiscal Years
metadata.description: Gives the number of patents, designs, trade-marks and utility models still existing at the close of each fiscal year from 1907-08 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: [Investment by Nature of Project]
metadata.description: Shows the amount of investment in each branch of enterprise over five years, and the text notes that most items show a marked decrease compared with preceding years.

metadata.title: Number and Capital Classified by Nature of Enterprise
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000) At the End of Year
metadata.description: Gives the number of enterprises, paid-up capital and reserves by nature of enterprise for 1907–1912, as compiled by the Department of Agriculture and Commerce.

metadata.title: [Bonus of Some Well-Known Banks and Companies, First Half of 1913 or Second Half of 1912]
metadata.description: The table shows paid-up capital, profit, bonus and dividend of several banks and companies, illustrating how bonus compares with profits, as the text explains bonus appropriation methods.

metadata.title: [Chambers of Commerce, 1908 to 1912]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Chambers of Commerce, their members and expenses for recent years, following the account of their legal position after the 1908-9 amendment.

metadata.title: Number, Capital, Etc. of Exchanges
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number, paid-up capital, reserve, brokers, deposits, receipts, expenses and profit of the Exchanges from 1908 to 1912, illustrating the growth of the exchange business.

metadata.title: Amount of Bonds and Shares Transacted at the Stock Exchanges
metadata.description: Shows the amounts of government bonds and bank, electric railway and navigation company shares transacted at the stock exchanges from 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Amount of Rice Transacted at the Rice Exchanges
metadata.description: Shows the yearly volume of rice traded at the Tokyo and Osaka rice exchanges from 1908 to 1912, with the average price per koku, illustrating the exchanges' growth.

metadata.title: Quotation of Leading Shares and Bonds at Tokyo (yen)
metadata.description: Gives the highest and lowest quotations in 1912 and 1913 of leading shares (time and spot delivery) and bonds on the Tokyo exchange, as a market reference.

metadata.title: [Number of Warehouses and Storage Value, March 1912 to February 1914]
metadata.description: Shows how many warehouses existed and the value stored in them each month, for 1912 and 1913 with the following January and February, to illustrate the trade in bonded storage.

metadata.title: [Principal Items of Goods Stored in Warehouses at the End of February]
metadata.description: Lists the principal goods held in bonded warehouses at the end of February 1913 and 1914, with the change in stored value, showing which commodities rose or fell.

metadata.title: [Storage and Charge Rates for Goods]
metadata.description: This list gives the storage charges and handling charges per day, in yen per 100, for various goods, shown as the rates warehousing businesses applied to each item.

metadata.title: Domestic Exhibitions
metadata.description: Summarises the results of the five domestic exhibitions held so far, showing days open, buildings, exhibitors, exhibits and sales for each exhibition from 1877 to 1908.

metadata.title: [Results of the Successive Osaka Exhibitions]
metadata.description: Figures for the five successive national exhibitions held at Osaka, showing prizes, jurors, visitors, ticket proceeds and expenses, with the 5th exhibition noted for foreign participation.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Industrial Exhibition and Tokyo Taisho Exhibition Compared]
metadata.description: Comparison of the Tokyo Industrial Exhibition (1907) and the Tokyo Taisho Exhibition (1914), showing their days open, buildings, exhibitors, exhibits and expenses to show their national scope.

metadata.title: Japan in World Fairs
metadata.description: Japan's participation in principal international exhibitions from Chicago 1893 to London 1910, giving the Japanese section area, exhibits, values, sales and expenses.

metadata.title: Principal Production Guilds
metadata.description: Lists the principal staple production guilds by commodity, with the number of guilds for each, as part of the account of guild organisation in Japan.

metadata.title: Prices of Principal Commodities in Japan
metadata.description: Gives average prices of principal commodities in Japan for the years 1907 and 1909 to 1912, showing the price movements of staples and foodstuffs.

metadata.title: [Average Prices of Principal Commodities, 1907–1912]
metadata.description: Shows average prices of principal commodities such as cotton yarn, raw silk, coal and sleepers for 1907 to 1912, with unit measures and a conversion key below.

metadata.title: New Schedule of Fees at the Tokyo Stock Exchange
metadata.description: Gives the new brokerage fee rates per share on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, effective from September 1914, by actual value band for duly entered and not entered transactions.

metadata.title: Exports and Imports of Commodities
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of Japan's exports, imports and total foreign trade from 1909 to 1913, with per capita trade and the excess of imports, to show the trend over five years.

metadata.title: Exports and Imports of Specie and Bullion
metadata.description: Shows Japan's yearly exports and imports of specie and bullion from 1909 to 1913, with the balance between them, as part of the five-year review of foreign trade.

metadata.title: Trade Returns at Leading Ports
metadata.description: Lists the export and import values of Japan's six leading ports for 1911 to 1913, showing where the country's foreign trade was concentrated.

metadata.title: Staple Items of Trade Classified — Exports
metadata.caption: Exports (¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the values of Japan's principal export commodities and totals for 1909–1913, giving the staple items of foreign trade in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Staple Items of Trade Classified — Imports
metadata.caption: Imports (¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the values of Japan's principal import commodities for 1909–1913, in thousands of yen, completing the staple-items statistics begun with the export table.

metadata.title: [Articles Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top rows continue a table of trade figures by article, with yearly totals for 1906 to 1913, before the staple exports table begins.

metadata.title: Staple Articles of Over ¥ 1,000,000
metadata.caption: Exports (In ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: The table lists the export articles each worth over one million yen, with their values in thousands of yen for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's rice exports by destination for 1911 to 1913, illustrating the country's main export markets.

metadata.title: Green Teas
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of green tea exports by destination for 1911 to 1913, mainly to the United States.

metadata.title: Sugar
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of sugar exports by destination for 1911 to 1913, with China as the dominant market.

metadata.title: Matches
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of match exports by destination for 1911 to 1913, sent mainly to China, Hongkong and India.

metadata.title: Waster Silk
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of waste silk exports by destination for 1911 to 1913, with France the largest buyer.

metadata.title: Raw Silk
metadata.description: Exports of raw silk by destination, showing the quantity sent to each country in 1911–1913 with totals.

metadata.title: Cotton Yarn
metadata.description: Exports of cotton yarn by destination for 1911–1913, listing each country's quantity and the overall total.

metadata.title: Habutaye
metadata.description: Exports of habutaye silk fabric by destination for 1911–1913, with country figures and totals.

metadata.title: Cotton Fabrics
metadata.description: Exports of cotton fabrics by destination for 1911–1913, showing each country's figures and the total.

metadata.title: Silk Handkerchief
metadata.description: Exports of silk handkerchiefs by destination for 1911–1913, with the quantity for each country and the total.

metadata.title: Knitted Shirts
metadata.description: Exports of knitted shirts by destination for 1911–1913, listing each country's figures and the overall total.

metadata.title: Coal
metadata.description: Shows the values of coal shipped from Japan to various countries and regions in 1911–1913.

metadata.title: Copper
metadata.description: Gives the value of copper exported from Japan by destination country for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Straw Plait
metadata.description: Lists the export of straw plait from Japan by destination country across 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Porcelain
metadata.description: Records the export of porcelain from Japan to principal countries for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.description: Shows the quantities of rice exported from Japan to the listed countries for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Soja Bean
metadata.description: Gives the export of soja beans from Japan by destination for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Staple Imports and Destinations
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's staple imports (sugar, petroleum, ammonia sulphate, cotton, flax, wool, worsted and woollen goods) for 1911–1913 by country of origin, with totals.

metadata.title: Iron (Bars, Wires, Plates and Belts)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's imports of iron bars, wires, plates and belts by country of origin for 1911 to 1913, illustrating the sources of supply.

metadata.title: Iron (Pipes and Tubes)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's imports of iron pipes and tubes by country of origin for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Oil Cakes
metadata.description: Shows the origin of oil cakes imported into Japan from 1911 to 1913, with Kwantung and China as the main sources.

metadata.title: Asia
metadata.description: Compares Japan's trade with Asian countries, exports to and imports from each, for 1912 and 1913, to show the growing weight of the Asiatic Continent in foreign trade.

metadata.title: Japanese and Foreigners in Foreign Trade
metadata.description: The text explains that Japanese merchants' share of foreign trade should grow, and this table shows the shares of Japanese and foreign merchants in Kobe and Yokohama trade.

metadata.title: [Percentage Shares of Nationalities in Kobe Trade]
metadata.description: Percentage shares of the more important nationalities in the entire trade of Kobe, for exports and imports, 1906 to 1909.

metadata.title: Steam-Vessels That Entered From and Cleared to Foreign Countries
metadata.caption: (1,000 tons)
metadata.description: Steam-vessel tonnage that entered from and cleared to foreign countries at the port, by nationality, for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: Custom Revenue
metadata.description: Movement of total imports, dutiable goods, and customs revenue from 1909 to 1913, showing how revenue rose after tariff revisions.

metadata.title: 1. Mirrors
metadata.description: This list gives the rates for manufactured mirror glass under the Foreign Trade inspection ordinance, with black-type headings marking manufactured articles.

metadata.title: 2. Umbrellas or Umbrella Ribs
metadata.description: This list gives the rates for manufactured umbrella ribs and related wire, ribbon and sheet articles under the same inspection ordinance.

metadata.title: 3. Clocks, Hanging or Standing
metadata.description: This list gives the rates for clock-related metal articles, such as iron wire, steel ribbons and zinc plates, under the manufactured-articles classification of the ordinance.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Rates on Manufactured Goods, Continued]
metadata.description: The page lists customs duty rates per unit on various manufactured goods, such as chemicals, tinned goods, matches, glass, iron ware and lamps, as the tariff schedule continues.

metadata.title: Class II. 1. Refined Sugar, Rock Candy Sugar, Cube Sugar, Loaf Sugar & Other Similar Articles, & Oil, etc.
metadata.description: This class of the tariff lists duty rates on refined sugars, soya beans, seeds, nuts and wheat flour, each per 100 kin.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Rates on Manufactured Articles, Nos. 8–12]
metadata.description: The page lists the import duty rates under the tariff for beer, soda, paper, clothing and cotton shirts and underclothing, shown against each article in yen per 100 kin.

metadata.title: [Duties on Iron, Pipes and Vessel Materials]
metadata.description: Customs duty rates on iron, pipes, rivets, timber and other materials for vessels not receiving ship-building bounties, shown per 100 kin or per cubic metre.

metadata.title: Life Insurance
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Life insurance statistics for 1908-9 to 1912-13, showing companies, capital, reserves, premiums, claims and contracts, with the asterisked companies that also write other insurance.

metadata.title: [Investment of Life Insurance Company Income, End of 1912]
metadata.description: Shows how insurance companies' income was invested at the end of 1912, in amounts and as index numbers, with reserve funds listed separately.

metadata.title: Leading Life Insurance Cos. (at the End of Sept., 1913)
metadata.description: Compares six leading life insurance companies on insurance amount, reserves, premiums, claims, expenses, capital, dividends and ratios at the end of September 1913.

metadata.title: Fire Insurance
metadata.description: Shows the yearly development of fire insurance companies in Japan from 1908–9 to 1912–13, with capital, reserves, policies, insured amounts, premiums and expenses.

metadata.title: Leading Fire Insurance Cos. (at the End of June, 1913)
metadata.description: Gives insurance amounts, reserves and premiums by class (ordinary, floating, marine, fidelity) for five leading fire insurance companies at the end of June 1913.

metadata.title: Marine Insurance
metadata.description: Lists the marine insurance business of companies from 1908–9 to 1912–13, giving company numbers, paid-up capital, premium fund, policies, amounts, revenue and expenses.

metadata.title: Carriage Insurance
metadata.description: Gives carriage insurance figures for 1908–9 to 1912–13, covering companies, paid-up capital, premium fund, insurance amount, revenue and expenses.

metadata.title: Fidelity Insurance
metadata.description: Gives fidelity insurance figures for 1911–12 and 1912–13, including capital, premium reserve, claims paid and assured numbers at year end.

metadata.title: Engine & Boiler Insurance
metadata.description: Gives engine and boiler insurance figures for 1911–12 and 1912–13, with one company, its capital, premium fund, claims and insured numbers.

metadata.title: G. Conscription Insurance
metadata.description: Shows the number of companies, capital, premium fund, claims paid and insured persons for conscription insurance business in the two fiscal years listed.

metadata.title: H. Sickness Insurance
metadata.description: Shows the company count, capital, premium fund, claims and insured numbers for sickness insurance in the two fiscal years listed.

metadata.title: I. Accident Insurance
metadata.description: Gives the company count, capital, premium fund, claims and insured numbers for accident insurance in the two fiscal years listed.

metadata.title: A. Life Insurance
metadata.description: Shows the yearly development of foreign life insurance companies operating in Japan, covering companies, capital, premium fund, claims and policies.

metadata.title: B. Fire Insurance
metadata.description: Shows yearly figures for foreign fire insurance companies in Japan, including company numbers, capital, premium fund, claims and insured contracts and policies.

metadata.title: C. Marine Insurance
metadata.description: Shows the number of marine insurance companies, their paid-up capital, premium fund, claims paid and insured contracts and policies for 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Rates in Tokyo, %
metadata.description: Gives the minimum agreed fire insurance premium rates in Tokyo by district class, for wooden and fire-proof buildings, under the 1911 conventional rate agreement.

metadata.title: Mortality Rate of Assured in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the mortality rate of assured persons by age in Japan compared with England, per 100,000, from the new mortality table prepared by Mr. S. Ebihara.

metadata.title: General Statistics at the End of 1912
metadata.description: Summarises the aggregate deposits, loans, bills discounted, net profits and dividend rates of Japanese banks for each year from 1906 to 1912, supporting the general statements on banking growth.

metadata.title: Special Banks
metadata.caption: (At the end of June 1913; in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the capital, reserves, note issue and debentures of Japan's special banks at June 1913, followed by their deposits, loans, bills, profits and dividends.

metadata.title: Ordinary Banks
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number, paid-up capital and reserves of ordinary banks by type of organization at the end of 1912, with totals and comparative figures for 1909–1911.

metadata.title: Incomes and Outgoes of Ordinary Banks
metadata.description: Gives the total incomes and outgoes of ordinary banks for 1912 and 1911, presented as the year's financial record.

metadata.title: Bills Discounted
metadata.description: Compares bills of exchange and promissory notes discounted by ordinary banks in 1912 and 1911, with the year-on-year increase.

metadata.title: Documentary Bills and Foreign Bills
metadata.description: Shows documentary and foreign bills payable and receivable handled by banks for several years, illustrating the bill discounting business discussed above.

metadata.title: [Foreign Bills Classified by Kind (1912)]
metadata.description: Introduces the 1912 breakdown of foreign bills payable and receivable by kind, such as bills of exchange, documentary bills and telegraphic orders.

metadata.title: Deposit Accounts Classified (1912)
metadata.description: Shows the bank deposit accounts by type for 1912, with totals and comparative figures for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: Loans Classified
metadata.description: Compares the bank loans by type of security, with amounts and percentage shares for 1912 and 1911.

metadata.title: [Foreign Bills Classified by Country (1912)]
metadata.description: Gives the 1912 foreign bills payable and receivable broken down by country or region, with a total.

metadata.title: [Government and Other Bonds Held by Banks]
metadata.description: Shows the face value and current price of the bonds and securities held by the banks, with a total including other holdings.

metadata.title: [Debentures and Shares Possessed by Banks]
metadata.description: Gives the face value and current price of debentures and shares held by the banks for 1909 to 1912, with the 1912 franc-denominated entry shown separately.

metadata.title: Cash Accounts (at the End of 1912)
metadata.description: Shows the cash holdings of the banks at the end of 1912 and the preceding three years, broken down by cash, bank notes, cheques and bank bills.

metadata.title: Statistics on Savings Banks
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Summarises the number of savings banks, their paid-up capital and reserves for 1909 to 1912.

metadata.title: Outgoes and Incomes
metadata.description: Compares the outgoes and incomes of the savings banks for 1911 and 1912.

metadata.title: Deposits
metadata.description: Shows the savings deposits and other deposits held by the savings banks for 1909 to 1912.

metadata.title: Loans Classified (1912)
metadata.description: Classifies the loans made by the savings banks in 1912 by the type of security in which they were invested, showing face value and amount.

metadata.title: [Investments Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top of the page carries the end of an investment table, giving face value and amounts for local bonds and the total invested.

metadata.title: [Number of Licensed Pawnbrokers in Japan Proper]
metadata.description: Shows the number of licensed pawnbrokers in Japan Proper from 1908 to 1912, based on Home Office inquiries.

metadata.title: Pawnbroking in Tokyo
metadata.description: Gives the yearly Tokyo pawnbroking business from 1908 to 1912: pawns accepted and redeemed, and money advanced and repaid, to illustrate the trade.

metadata.title: Ordinary Banks
metadata.caption: (At the end of Feb. 1914; in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the leading ordinary banks in Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto with their paid-up capital, reserves, deposits, loans and latest dividends, as at the end of February 1914.

metadata.title: Leading Banks in Yokohama
metadata.description: Lists the leading banks in Yokohama with their capital, reserves, deposits, loans and latest dividends.

metadata.title: Leading Banks in Kobe
metadata.description: Lists the leading banks in Kobe with their capital, reserves, deposits, loans and latest dividends, continuing onto the next printed fragment.

metadata.title: Rate of Interest at the Bank of Japan
metadata.description: Shows the Bank of Japan's interest rates on loans, bills, commercial bills, overdrafts and fixed deposits at the end of March for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: Rate of Interest at Tokyo
metadata.description: Gives high, low and average rates on loans, discounts, overdrafts and current and fixed-deposit interest at Tokyo at the end of March, 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: At Osaka
metadata.description: Shows the high, low and average rates on loans, discounts, overdrafts and deposit interest at Osaka at the end of March for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: Average Rate in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Gives the high, low and average loan, discount, overdraft and deposit interest rates for Japan Proper at the end of March, 1910 to 1913.

metadata.title: Bulletins of Nippon Ginko or the Bank of Japan
metadata.description: Presents the Bank of Japan's note issue, specie reserve, securities and total figures at the end of March, 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: Volume of Clearing House Business in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the annual volume of clearing-house business in Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto from 1908 to 1913, illustrating the growth of clearing-house activity described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Clearing House Totals by City, Continued]
metadata.description: The top rows are the continuation of a multi-year city table, with totals for Yokohama, Kobe, Nagoya, Hiroshima and Shimonoseki-Moji, whose column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Dishonoured Bills at the Clearing Houses
metadata.description: The table gives the sum and number of dishonoured bills handled at the clearing houses of six major cities for each year from 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Amount of Coins and Paper Currency in Circulation
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the amount of gold, silver, nickel and copper coins, bank notes and grand total in circulation at the end of February for 1912 to 1914, illustrating the currency supply.

metadata.title: Coins in Circulation in Japan
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000); (At the end of January, 1914)
