metadata.description: Gives the state of Japan's coinage at the end of January 1914, showing minted totals, cancellations, net exports, Nippon Ginko reserves and coins actually in circulation by type.

metadata.title: [Domestic Parcel Post Charges to a Locality under a Different Post Office]
metadata.description: Gives the domestic postal parcel charges for sending to a locality under a different post office or outside the city, by weight band for ordinary and registered parcels.

metadata.title: [Charges for Postal Parcels Exchanged with Formosa, Saghalien, China and Korea]
metadata.description: Lists the postage charges for parcels exchanged between Japan proper, Formosa, Saghalien, China (registered) and Korea, by weight band.

metadata.title: Foreign Parcels
metadata.caption: In the following list, the cheapest-rate routes are given.
metadata.description: The list gives the cheapest-rate routes and yen fees for foreign parcels sent to France, Germany, Austria-Hungary, British India, Siam and Great Britain by weight.

metadata.title: [Postal Rates to Foreign Countries by Route and Weight]
metadata.description: Lists the postal rates by route and weight limit for sending mail to Belgium, Holland, Italy, Canada, Hongkong, the Dutch East-Indies, Australia and Russia.

metadata.title: Statistics Relating to Post, Telegraph & Telephone
metadata.description: Gives the number of post offices, telegraph and telephone offices in 1912, with the area and population served per office, including colonies and China.

metadata.title: Ordinary Mail Matters (in 1,000)
metadata.caption: Excluding foreign mail matters
metadata.description: Shows annual volumes of ordinary domestic mail items despatched, excluding foreign mail, with totals and per-capita figures, for 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Ordinary Foreign Mail Matters (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of foreign-bound ordinary mail items transmitted and arrived from 1908 to 1912, by kind of matter.

metadata.title: Parcel Post (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists parcel post volumes, domestic and foreign, with totals and per-capita despatch, for the years 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Telegraphic Money Orders: Maximum Amounts and Fees]
metadata.description: The page lists the maximum amounts, fees and money denominations for telegraphic money orders sent from Japan to foreign countries, grouped by region, as the text introduces.

metadata.title: Postal Savings Deposits at Home
metadata.description: The text notes the marked increase in amount and number of postal savings depositors over these few years, and this table gives the figures for 1908 to 1912.

metadata.title: Rate to Formosa, Korea Etc.
metadata.description: Gives the telegram fees between Formosa, Manchuria, Chefu, the Bonins, Saghalien, Korea and offices in Japan proper, for Kana and Roman-letter telegrams.

metadata.title: International Rates
metadata.caption: The rates for telegrams per word to places abroad are as follows (subject to alteration):
metadata.description: Lists the per-word telegraph rates to places abroad in Asia, Europe, North America and South America, routed via Shanghai, Vladivostock, Europe, Bonin or Manila.

metadata.title: [Telegraph Rates to Oceania]
metadata.description: Gives the telegraph rates to Oceanic destinations, routed via Shanghai, for the reader's reference alongside the explanation of telegram charging rules.

metadata.title: Extension of Telegraph
metadata.caption: (in ri)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly growth of Japan's telegraph network from 1908 to 1912 by line type, with total length per area.

metadata.title: Number of Telegrams Transacted
metadata.description: Records the annual number of telegrams sent domestically and exchanged with foreign countries from 1908 to 1912, including wireless traffic.

metadata.title: [Wireless Stations Equipment]
metadata.description: Lists the seven wireless coast stations with the length of their pole, electric power and transmission distance, showing the equipment of each station.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Receipts
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly receipts of the postal and telegraph services by category, from 1908 to 1912, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Service Expenses
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly expenses of the postal and telegraph services by category, from 1908 to 1911, with no figures printed for 1912.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Apparatus
metadata.description: Shows the growth of telephone subscribers and exchange and automatic apparatus in Japan from 1908 to 1912, illustrating the expansion of the telephone service.

metadata.title: Inventions Relating to Wireless Telegraphy and Telephone
metadata.description: Lists some patents obtained by Japanese experts for wireless telegraphy and telephone devices, with the year each patent was issued and the patentee.

metadata.title: Statistics
metadata.caption: (April, 1910—March, '11)
metadata.description: Gives the staff, students, graduates and admissions for the Staff College and the Artillery and Engineering School over April 1910 to March 1911, under the army education outline.

metadata.title: [Military Training Schools: Staff, Students, Graduates and Admissions]
metadata.description: Lists the staff, students, graduates and admissions of the army's special training schools, continuing the preceding account of the military establishment.

metadata.title: [Siege Artillery Corps Deployment by Brigade Headquarters]
metadata.description: Shows how the reorganized Siege Artillery corps is distributed among coastal fortress stations under the two brigade headquarters at Yokosuka and Shimonoseki.

metadata.title: Murata's Magazine-Rifle of 1905 Type
metadata.description: Introduced in the Arms section, this table gives the specifications of Murata's 1905-style magazine rifle as issued to infantry and cavalry, as the text describes the weapon.

metadata.title: Result of Conscription Service Examination
metadata.description: Shows the outcome of the conscription service examinations in 1910 and 1911, with the numbers examined, enrolled, postponed, exempted and disabled.

metadata.title: Stature (in Japanese ft.) of Eligible Lads Examined
metadata.description: Gives the stature distribution of eligible lads examined in the conscription years, with totals and percentages for each height band.

metadata.title: Officers and Non-Combatants on Active Service
metadata.description: Gives the numbers of military officers and non-combatants on active service by rank for 1909 to 1912, with civilians listed separately, as a statistical summary following the Supreme Military Council entries.

metadata.title: Distribution of the Standing Army Is as Follows
metadata.description: The page lists how the standing army's cavalry, artillery, engineer and commissariat units were distributed and where their garrisons were located.

metadata.title: Distribution of the Standing Army (Divisions)
metadata.description: This part of the table gives each division's headquarters and the cavalry and infantry brigades and regiments assigned to it.

metadata.title: [Army Divisions and Their Garrison Units]
metadata.description: This rotated page lists the army divisions by number with their garrison towns and the unit numbers attached to each, showing how the army was organised across the country.

metadata.title: [Army Garrisons, Divisions and Regiment Numbers]
metadata.description: A rotated page listing army garrison towns with their division numbers and the infantry regiment and battalion numbers stationed there, under the heading on the Army and the Navy.

metadata.title: Age-Limit in the Active Service
metadata.description: Gives the maximum age at which officers of each rank may remain in active service, under the rules for promotion of military officers in peacetime.

metadata.title: Four Super-Dreadnaughts
metadata.description: Lists the four super-dreadnought battleships provided for in the Budget, with their building yards, completion dates and tonnage.

metadata.title: Three Super-Dreadnaught Cruisers
metadata.description: Lists the three super-dreadnought cruisers provided for in the Budget, with their building yards, launch years and tonnage.

metadata.title: Statistics (April, 1910—March, '11)
metadata.description: Gives staff, student, graduate and admission figures for the naval training institutions, including the Naval Engineering Academy, for the period April 1910 to March 1911.

metadata.title: [Conscripts and Volunteers in the Navy, 1908–1912]
metadata.description: Shows the annual numbers of conscripts and volunteers entering the Navy from 1908 to 1912, explaining that volunteers were preferred over conscripts.

metadata.title: The Japanese Fleet
metadata.description: The table lists the battleships, battleship cruisers and first class cruisers of the Japanese navy with their displacement, speed, armour and armament, showing the fleet's composition.

metadata.title: [Japanese Navy Warships: Displacement, Speed, Armour and Armament]
metadata.description: The page lists Japanese navy warships by class, giving each vessel's displacement, length, launch year, speed, torpedo tubes, armour and main guns.

metadata.title: Second Class Coast Defence Ships
metadata.description: Lists the specifications of the Japanese second-class coast defence ships, gun-boats and first-class torpedo-boat destroyers, giving tonnage, length, launch date, speed, torpedo tubes, armour and armament.

metadata.title: Third Class Torpedo-boat Destroyers
metadata.description: Gives the names, displacement and launch years of the third-class torpedo-boat destroyers in two columns, with a summary count of other torpedo-boat and submarine strength.

metadata.title: Age Limit of Officers in Active Service
metadata.description: Sets out the maximum age limits for each officer rank in the active navy, from fleet admiral down to sub-lieutenant.

metadata.title: Officers and Bluejackets on Active Service
metadata.caption: (Compiled at the end of the year)
metadata.description: Gives the number of naval personnel on active service at the end of 1911 and 1912, broken down by rank category and cadets.

metadata.title: [Interest Accruing from Railway Working, 1906–1915]
metadata.description: Shows the interest rate accruing from Government railway working over the last decade, offered to support the claim that the railways' financial results are successful.

metadata.title: General Statistics of State & Private Railways
metadata.description: The table gives state and private railway mileage, state rolling stock, and state and private railway investment, capital and reserves for 1909–1913, reflecting railway growth ahead of nationalization.

metadata.title: Redemption of the Railway Nationalization Loan
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: The page gives the year-by-year schedule for redeeming the Railway Nationalization Loan, showing construction cost, profit, interest, and the distribution of the balance of profit.

metadata.title: Imperial Railways District Offices and Open Mileage, April 1913
metadata.description: The page lists the four administrative districts of the Imperial Railways, where each district office is situated, and the open mileage in April 1913.

metadata.title: State in December, 1913
metadata.description: Lists the principal state railway lines and their open mileage in December 1913, with the national total, alongside notes on sections to be opened in the following years.

metadata.title: General Statistics of State Railway
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for the state railways from 1904 to 1914, covering mileage, passenger and freight traffic, receipts, expenses, profit, capital and profit ratio.

metadata.title: Railway Capital
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1000)
metadata.description: Shows the capital of the Imperial railways for 1908 to 1912, broken into capital and the construction, improvement and additional expenses settled each year, as the railway finance account was separated.

metadata.title: Revenue and Expenditure for 1912-13
metadata.description: Gives the receipts and expenditure of the Imperial railways for the fiscal year 1912-13, itemised under operation receipts and expenses, to illustrate the finances described in the text.

metadata.title: Traffic Receipts and Expenses
metadata.description: Traffic receipts, expenses and net profits of the railways for 1909 to 1913, with daily receipts, expenses and profits per mile.

metadata.title: Traffic Receipts Classified (¥ 1000)
