metadata.description: Sets out the Japanese government's ordinary and extraordinary revenues and expenditures for the fiscal years 1913-14 and 1914-15, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade at Dairen (1912)
metadata.description: Shows the value of foreign trade passing through Dairen in 1912 by trading partner, compared with the 1911 total.

metadata.title: Education
metadata.description: Gives the number of pupils in primary schools in Kwantung and in the leased region outside it, divided into Japanese and Chinese pupils, for 1912.

metadata.title: Public Schools for Chinese (1912)
metadata.description: Reports the number of boys, girls and teachers in the public schools for Chinese in 1912.

metadata.title: [Schools in South Manchuria, 1912]
metadata.description: The table gives staff and student numbers of the schools in South Manchuria for 1912, with a note on the higher schools and private Chinese schools.

metadata.title: [Fushun and Yentai Colliery Output, Sales and Receipts, 1911-1913]
metadata.description: Statistics of the Fushun and Yentai coal fields' output, sales and receipts from 1911 to 1913, given alongside the descriptions of the collieries.

metadata.title: Business Report for 1913-14
metadata.description: Shows the South Manchuria Railway's business results for 1913-14 by undertaking, with receipts, expenses and balances against the prior year's balance.

metadata.title: [Distribution of Net Profit]
metadata.description: Explains how the net profit of ¥9,318,491 for 1913-14 was distributed among reserves, dividends, bonus and carry-forward.

metadata.title: [Capital Invested Classified, 1907-08 to 1913-14]
metadata.description: Breaks down the total capital of ¥138,433,961 invested from 1907-08 to 1913-14 by enterprise type.

metadata.title: Weights, Measures and Moneys
metadata.description: A conversion table giving the Japanese units of money, distance, land, capacity and weight with their English and metric equivalents, to help readers interpret figures in the Year Book.

metadata.title: [Area and Coast Line of the Imperial Realm by Territory]
metadata.description: Gives the coast line, area and percentage share of each island group and territory of the Imperial realm, following the text on the expansion of Japanese territory.

metadata.title: [Principal Mountain Peaks Above 8,000 Feet]
metadata.description: Lists the principal mountain peaks in Japan rising above 8,000 feet, with their heights, as a geographical reference on the country's mountains.

metadata.title: Rivers Above 70 ri in Navigable Length
metadata.description: Gives the navigable lengths in ri of Japan's rivers exceeding 70 ri, noting that rivers are generally short and fast-flowing.

metadata.title: Gales in 1912
metadata.description: Gives, for each observatory, the number of days visited by gales in 1912, the average and maximum gale speeds, and when the strongest gale occurred, supporting the preceding account of Japan's winds.

metadata.title: [Average Time and Last Occurrence by Place]
metadata.description: A short list giving, for four places, the average time of a certain phenomenon and the date it last occurred, shown alongside the monthly temperature data.

metadata.title: Monthly Average Temperature in Japan
metadata.caption: (From the establishment of the Observatory to 1912)
metadata.description: Monthly and annual average, maximum and minimum temperatures for ten observatories in Japan, shown to illustrate the country's climate before the discussion of rainfall.

metadata.title: Average Monthly Rainfalls and Snowfalls in Japan from the Beginning of Observation to the End of 1912
metadata.description: The table gives average monthly and yearly rainfall and snowfall at eleven observatories, with the year each began observing and the number of wet days, illustrating Japan's climate.

metadata.title: [Number of Species Found in Japan]
metadata.description: The Fauna section gives approximate counts of animal species found in Japan, and of those peculiar to or especially conspicuous in the country, by group.

metadata.title: [Insects of Japan]
metadata.description: The list gives the number of known species of cicadas and butterflies, with a note that many other invertebrate groups are also found in Japan.

metadata.title: Species Existing in Japan
metadata.description: The Flora section lists how many species of flowering plants, ferns and sea-weeds exist in Japan.

metadata.title: List of Mikados in Alphabetical Order
metadata.description: An alphabetical index of the Mikados (emperors) of Japan, giving the years in which each reign began and ended, so readers can look up any sovereign and his dates.

metadata.title: [Mikados and Their Reign Dates]
metadata.description: A chronological list of the Mikados with their reign dates, showing the sovereigns' periods and which were female or Northern Court rulers.

metadata.title: List of the Shōguns and the Regents (Shikken)
metadata.description: A list of the Shoguns and Regents (Shikken) grouped by family, giving the years each held office, continuing onto the next page.

metadata.title: List of Japanese "Year-Names"
metadata.description: A reference list of Japanese year-names (nengō) with their corresponding Western year spans, given to help readers convert dates in Japanese history.

metadata.title: [Japanese Era Names and Their Years]
metadata.description: A chronological list of Japanese era names (nengō) in romanized form and characters, each with its first and last year in the Western calendar, given for reference across the four column groups.

metadata.title: [Japanese Era Names (Nengō) and Their Years]
metadata.description: A table of Japanese era names with their romanized and kanji forms and the years each era covered, set out as a chronological reference list for the reader of Japanese history.

metadata.title: [Japanese Era Names (Nengō) with Years A.D.]
metadata.description: This page lists Japanese era names (nengō) in romanized and Japanese characters, with the years they began and ended, as a reference for dating historical events.

metadata.title: Principal Calamities Occurring Since the Tokugawa Shogunate
metadata.description: Following a survey of the seismic history of Japan, the page lists the principal earthquake calamities after the Tokugawa period began, with houses destroyed and casualties.

metadata.title: [Mineral Springs by Kind and District]
metadata.description: Introducing the mineral springs section, this table gives the number of springs of each chemical kind across the mainland regions, Hokkaido and Kyushu, with totals.

metadata.title: Analysis of Dogo Spring
metadata.caption: Sp. W.: 1,00026 at 17.5°: temp.: 43°. In 1 liter of the mineral spring is held:—
metadata.description: Under simple hot springs, this analysis of the Dogo spring lists the cation content per liter of water in grams, milli-mols and milli-equivalents.

metadata.title: [Anions of Mineral Water, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuing from the previous page, this table lists the anion constituents of an acid mineral spring, with gramme, milli-mol. and milli-equivalent values and totals.

metadata.title: Analysis of "Jizo-no-yu," Kusatsu
metadata.caption: Temperature 60°.6; In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained
metadata.description: This analysis gives the cation and anion composition of the Jizo-no-yu spring at Kusatsu, expressed in grammes, milli-mols and milli-equivalents per litre.

metadata.title: Analysis of Shiobara Spring
metadata.caption: In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained
metadata.description: This table gives the cation composition of the Shiobara spring, one of the acid vitriol springs, per litre of mineral water.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Mineral Spring (Continued, Ferro-Ion to Silicate)]
metadata.description: This continuation table gives the ionic composition of an acid alum spring, listing the cations and anions per liter with their weights, molecular and equivalent values.

metadata.title: Analysis of Kawaura-mura Hot Spring
metadata.caption: Sp. W.: 1,0006 when 15 c. In 1 liter of the mineral water are contained:
metadata.description: This analysis of the Kawaura-mura hot spring lists the cations and anions in one liter of its water, showing the weight, milli-mol and milli-equivalent of each constituent.

metadata.title: Analysis of "Furuyashiki." Cold Spring Nasu.
metadata.description: This analysis gives the cation content per liter of the cold spring at Furuyashiki, Nasu, a vitriol spring containing more than .010 g. of ferro-ions.

metadata.title: [Analysis of Amidamine Mineral Springs (continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues an ion analysis of Amidamine mineral water, listing cations and anions with their gramme, milli-mol and milli-equivalent values and totals.

metadata.title: Analysis of Amidamine Mineral Springs
metadata.caption: Sp. W. 1.012 at 16°. In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:
metadata.description: Gives the full mineral analysis of Amidamine springs in Yamashiro, showing the cations and anions per liter of water in grammes, milli-mols and milli-equivalents.

metadata.title: Analysis of "Furo-sen Spring," Beppu
metadata.caption: Temperature: 56°. In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:
metadata.description: Shows the mineral analysis of the Furo-sen spring at Beppu, an iron carbonate spring, listing its cation contents per liter of water.

metadata.title: Analysis of Kowakidani No. II Spring, Hakone
metadata.caption: In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:—
metadata.description: This analysis gives the cation and anion composition of the Kowakidani No. II spring at Hakone, showing grams, milli-mols and milli-equivalents per liter of water.

metadata.title: Analysis of Yamashiro Spring No. 1
metadata.caption: In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:—
metadata.description: The section on bitter springs gives the full mineral analysis of Yamashiro spring No. 1, listing its cations and anions per liter of water.

metadata.title: Analysis of Oyu Spring, Atami
metadata.caption: In 1 liter of the mineral water is contained:
metadata.description: Gives the chemical analysis of the Oyu spring at Atami, one of the salt springs, listing dissolved constituents per liter of water.

metadata.title: [Mineral Water Ion Analysis (Continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of an ion analysis of mineral waters, with the printed sums for each sample; the column headings are not shown on this page.

metadata.title: Radio-Activity of the Mineral Springs in Japan
metadata.description: Results of radium emanation testing on several Japanese mineral springs, given to show their radio-activity, as the section introduction explains.

metadata.title: Population in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Shows legal and real population of Japan Proper for 1898, 1903 and 1908, with the tentative figure, to illustrate the gap between the two official counts.

metadata.title: Population
metadata.caption: The figures given below show legal population in Japan Proper.
metadata.description: Legal population of Japan Proper by sex, with annual increase and density per square ri, from 1885 to 1914, showing the growth that the preceding discussion of census data had found lacking.

metadata.title: Population in Rural and Urban Districts
metadata.description: Population split between cities of over 10,000 and villages under 10,000 inhabitants, with ratios, showing the steady shift toward urban districts between 1894 and 1908.

metadata.title: Population by Ages and Sexes
metadata.description: Gives the national population broken down by five-year age groups and sex for 1908, with each age group's share per 100 population compared across census years from 1888 to 1908.

metadata.title: [Married and Unmarried Census Returns, Japan Proper]
metadata.description: Shows the census counts of married and unmarried males and females in Japan proper from 1888 to 1908, the census returns being first compiled in 1886.

metadata.title: [Percentage of Married and Unmarried per 100 People]
metadata.description: Gives the share of married and unmarried people per 100 population, split by sex, for each census year from 1888 to 1908.

metadata.title: Marriages and Divorces
metadata.description: Lists the yearly number of marriages and divorces from 1905 to 1909 and their rates per 1,000 population.

metadata.title: Age of Marriage
metadata.description: Shows the number of men and women marrying in each age group in 1900 and 1909, illustrating the age distribution at marriage.

metadata.title: Birth-Rates (Excluding Still-Births)
metadata.caption: (Excluding Still-Births)
metadata.description: Gives yearly birth totals for 1904–1909, split by sex, with birth rate per 100 people, sex ratio at birth and still-birth rate.

metadata.title: [Birth-Rates: Sex Ratio and Illegitimacy]
metadata.description: Continues the birth statistics, giving the sex ratio of births and the ratio of illegitimate births for 1904–1908.

metadata.title: Death-Rates
metadata.description: Reports annual death totals by sex and the death rate per 100 people, with the male-to-female mortality ratio, for 1904–1909.

metadata.title: Age of Deaths
metadata.description: Breaks down deaths in 1908 by sex and age group, with 1903 totals and deaths per 1000 for comparison.

metadata.title: [Deaths by Age Group, 1908 and 1903]
metadata.description: Shows deaths by age group, sex and year for 1908 compared with 1903, with deaths per 1000 in each group, illustrating the age structure of mortality.

metadata.title: Population and Number of Households in Cities, with Names of Mayors
metadata.description: Lists each city with its mayor as of March 1915, its 1913 population and its 1908 number of households.

metadata.title: Japanese Abroad
metadata.caption: (At the end of June 1913)
metadata.description: Gives the number of Japanese residents abroad, by sex, in China and in two Chinese places (Amoy and Antung) at the end of June 1913.

metadata.title: [Japanese Residents Abroad by Locality, Males, Females and Total]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Japanese residents in each locality abroad, by sex and total, showing where the overseas Japanese population lived in the period.

metadata.title: Number of Passports Issued to Japanese Going Abroad
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of passports issued to Japanese going abroad from 1904 to 1913, by sex, introducing the section on Japanese emigrants.

metadata.title: Foreign Visitors to Japan (1913)
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign visitors to Japan in 1913 by nationality, with comparative totals for the two previous years and the ports of landing.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Japan by Districts
metadata.description: Gives official counts of foreign residents in Japan at the end of each year by district, 1907–1910, with 1911 split by sex.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Japan by Nationality
metadata.description: Lists foreign residents in Japan by nationality for nationalities numbering 100 or more, across 1907–1910 and by sex and total for 1911.

metadata.title: [Marriages into Family, Adoptions, Naturalizations and Rehabilitations, 1906-1911]
metadata.description: Shows yearly counts of foreigners marrying into families, adopted, naturalized and rehabilitated, supporting the population discussion of foreign residents' status.

metadata.title: Land Held Under Perpetual Lease by Places
metadata.description: Lists the number of perpetual lease entries, area and annual rents held by foreigners in each treaty port, showing the scale of the land question.

metadata.title: Principal Perpetual Lease Entries Classified by Nationality
metadata.description: Shows the area of perpetual lease land held by principal foreign nationalities, indicating which groups held the most land.

metadata.title: Decorations Granted Each Year
metadata.description: Shows the numbers of Japanese decorations conferred by class and kind in 1912 and 1913, with totals, illustrating the honours system.

metadata.title: Holders of the Golden Kite (Military Honor)
metadata.description: Lists the number of Golden Kite military honour holders by class for 1912 and 1913, with cumulative totals and annuities paid.

metadata.title: [Number of Peers]
metadata.description: Shows the number of Peers in each of the five grades in 1912 and 1913 and their total, illustrating the movement of the peerage.

metadata.title: [Imperial Grants to Kuge Courtiers, 1894]
metadata.description: The table shows the 1894 yen 2,000,000 Imperial grant to the Kuge courtiers, broken down by rank, illustrating the Court's generous protection of the Peers.

metadata.title: [Exhibits Submitted to the National Art Exhibition, 1st to 8th Displays]
metadata.description: Shows the works submitted, selected and exhibited for reference at each of the first eight national art exhibitions held in Tokyo from 1907, split by Japanese painting, Western painting and sculpture.

metadata.title: Recipients of 2nd Prizes
metadata.description: Lists the artists who received the 1st, 2nd and 3rd prizes in each category (Japanese painting, Western painting and sculpture) at the national art exhibition.

metadata.title: [Judges of Annual Art Exhibitions, 4th to 8th]
metadata.description: The page lists the judges of the successive annual art exhibitions, showing which names served on each group for each numbered exhibition.

metadata.title: States Aid for Preservation of National Treasures
metadata.description: This table gives the annual state aid, split into structural articles and treasures, for preserving national treasures from 1897 to 1909, as the Commission's funding is discussed.

metadata.title: [Continued Table: Figures for 1910–1912 and Total, Column Headings Not On This Page]
metadata.description: This continued table gives yearly figures for 1910 to 1912 with a total, the column headings of which appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Number of Treasures
metadata.description: This table gives the number of buildings and treasures of the Art Education section, year by year from 1897 to 1913, with totals, shown beside the art commissioners section.

metadata.title: Shrines and Ministers
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly numbers of Shinto shrines by class and of the ministers serving them, 1908 to 1912, showing a decline in total shrines.

metadata.title: Buddhist Temples and Priests
metadata.caption: Sects possessing over 1,000 temples are as follows:
metadata.description: Shows the number of temples and priests of the main Buddhist sects from 1908 to 1912, illustrating the scale of Buddhist institutions in Japan.

metadata.title: Statistics of Christian Churches in Japan (1913)
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Christian churches, preaching houses, believers and pastors in Japan in 1913, supporting the discussion of religious life and the growth of the churches.

metadata.title: Relief Fund
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Shows the annual figures for the local Relief Fund: local apportionments, proceeds, State aids, disbursements and the fund balance for two fiscal years.

metadata.title: [Paupers and Foundlings Supported by the State]
metadata.description: Gives the number of paupers supported at State expense with the amount the State paid, and the number of foundlings with their expenses, for two years.

metadata.title: [Relief Allowances for Persons Unable to Work]
metadata.description: Lists the rice allowances granted by the state to decrepit, disabled, infant and invalid persons, as part of the account of relief and charity measures.

metadata.title: [Inmates of Leper Hospitals at End of 1912]
metadata.description: The text describes the leper hospitals established by the State and private bodies, and gives the number of inmates at each at the end of 1912.

metadata.title: The Blind as Bread-Earners
metadata.description: Gives the 1910 count of blind people in Japan proper by profession, showing how many earned a living through shampooing, acupuncture and other trades.

metadata.title: [Charity Institutions and Their Work]
metadata.description: Summarises the number, expenses and persons rescued of charity institutions of each kind, according to the latest reports, introducing the list of institutions.

metadata.title: [Charity Institutions Granted State Aid in 1914]
metadata.description: Lists the principal charity institutions that received State aid in 1914, with their religious affiliation and location; the list continues beyond this page.

metadata.title: [List of Orphanages, Schools and Charitable Institutions]
metadata.description: A directory of charitable, orphanage and religious-education institutions in Japan, listed by name with denomination and location, as a reference index.

metadata.title: [List of Charitable and Welfare Institutions]
metadata.description: A continuing alphabetical list of charitable and welfare institutions, giving each institution's name and its location, with a Ch. mark for certain entries.

metadata.title: General Statistics on Education
metadata.description: The table gives the number of schools, instructors and teachers, students and pupils, and graduates by kind of school for the last three years, illustrating the state of education in Japan.

metadata.title: Foreign Instructors at the Institutions under Direct Control of the Department of Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign instructors by nationality at education-department institutions for 1911-12 and 1912-13, with their total annual salaries.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Lists the weekly subjects and teaching hours for each of the four years of ordinary elementary schools, introduced by a note on the compulsory curriculum changes of 1911.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Higher Elementary Schools
metadata.description: The Higher Elementary Schools' weekly timetable by school year, listing each subject's hours per week for boys and girls.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools (Continued)
metadata.description: The continued weekly timetable of the Ordinary Elementary Schools, showing subject hours for the Fifth and Sixth school years.

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age
metadata.description: Shows the number of children of school age, split by whether they attended school under compulsory obligation, with ratios of attendance, for the years 1907-08 to 1912-13.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers of Both Sexes in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Gives the monthly average salary of public elementary school teachers and the number of teachers in the lowest and a middle salary band over six years.

metadata.title: [Fee-Paying Elementary Schools and Pupils, 1908–9 to 1912–13]
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools collecting fees and the pupils paying full, partial or no fees for 1908–9 to 1912–13, placed before the Kindergartens section.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens, Schools, Conductors and Infants, 1910–11 to 1912–13]
metadata.description: Gives the number of kindergartens, conductors and male, female and total infants by type of establishment for 1912–13, with totals for 1911–12 and 1910–11.

metadata.title: [Blind and Deaf-Mute Children of School Age and Those Receiving Instruction, 1910–11 to 1911–12]
metadata.description: Compares blind and deaf-mute children of school age with those receiving instruction at school, with defectives per 1,000 normal children, for 1910–11 to 1911–12.

metadata.title: The Curriculum of the Middle School
metadata.description: The table gives the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each year of the middle school course, shown alongside notes on optional subjects.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Middle Schools
metadata.description: The table shows yearly counts of public and private middle schools, their instructors, pupils and graduates from 1908–09 to 1912–13.

metadata.title: Graduates and Subsequent Careers
metadata.caption: Careers as reported within the year after the graduation are:—
metadata.description: Shows what graduates were doing within a year of graduating, by year, and notes the ratio of those leaving school unfinished or dying.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Girls' High Schools
metadata.description: Lists the weekly teaching hours for each subject across the four years of the girls' high school course.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Girls' High Schools
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of public and private girls' high schools, their instructors, pupils, graduates, leaving rate and admission percentage, giving the trend over five years.

metadata.title: List of the High Schools
metadata.description: Lists the eight government high schools with their directors, staff, students, graduates, admission rates and expenses, followed by yearly totals for recent years.

metadata.title: [Applicants and Admissions by Section]
metadata.description: Shows the number of applicants for admission to the three sections and the admissions per 100 applicants, illustrating the average-age and selection figures discussed in the text.

metadata.title: Students and Graduates Classified by Sex
metadata.description: Gives the numbers of male and female instructors, students and graduates at normal schools for 1908-09 to 1912-13, as the text on normal schools introduces the sex breakdown.

metadata.title: Statistics of Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admissions at the Tokyo and Hiroshima Higher Normal Schools for 1910-11 to 1912-13.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Tokyo (Dec. 1913)
metadata.caption: Est'd, April 1877; President, Dr. Yamagawa, Kenjiro
metadata.description: Lists the colleges of the Imperial University of Tokyo, with place, dean, staff and student numbers as of December 1913, following the note on the four state universities.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Kyoto (Dec. 1913)
metadata.caption: Est'd, June 1897; President, Dr. Yamagawa, Kenjiro
metadata.description: Shows the colleges of the Imperial University of Kyoto in December 1913, with place, dean, staff and student numbers; the Science and Engineering staff and student figures are joined by a bracket.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Tohoku (Dec. 1913)
metadata.caption: Est'd, June 1907; President, Dr. Hojo, Jikei
metadata.description: Gives the colleges of the Imperial University of Tohoku in December 1913, with place, dean, staff and student numbers, as the last of the four state universities described.

metadata.title: Students in the University Hall
metadata.caption: (Sep. 1913)
metadata.description: Shows the number of students in each college of the Imperial Universities in the University Hall in September 1913.

metadata.title: Average Age of Matriculation at Tokyo
metadata.caption: Average age of those matriculated recently is as follows:—
metadata.description: Gives the average age at matriculation for students entering Tokyo Imperial University colleges over three academic years.

metadata.title: Professions of the University Graduates
metadata.caption: The graduates of the Imperial Universities since the foundation to 1912-13 make the following record, as classified according to their condition in life.
metadata.description: Classifies graduates of the Imperial Universities by their occupation or position in life, as recorded up to 1912-13.

metadata.title: [Occupations of Graduates, Continued]
metadata.description: This continued table gives the occupations or status of university graduates in three figure columns, with the column headings not reproduced on this page.

metadata.title: The Total Number of Graduates Classified by Colleges till 1911-12
metadata.description: This table gives the total number of graduates of the Tokyo, Kyoto and Tohoku Imperial Universities by faculty up to 1911-12.

metadata.title: List of the Government Technical and Special Schools for 1913
metadata.description: Lists the government technical and special schools (medical, higher commercial and higher technical) in 1913, giving each school's director, staff, students, admission rate, graduates and expenses.

metadata.title: [Higher Specialised Schools — Location, Principal and Statistics]
metadata.description: Lists the government higher specialised schools by location, with their principals and figures, grouped under each school type, as part of the education survey.

metadata.title: Public and Private Blind, Deaf and Dumb Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of blind, deaf and dumb schools, their teachers, pupils and graduates for four school years, introducing the description of the Tokyo schools below.

metadata.title: [Schools for the Blind and Deaf-Mutes, 1912-13]
metadata.description: Gives the 1912-13 teaching staff, pupils, graduates, applicants and admissions for the two Tokyo schools for the blind and for deaf-mutes described above.

metadata.title: [Peers' School Staff, Students and Graduates by Course, 1913]
metadata.description: Shows the Peers' School's staff split by boys' and girls' parts, and its students and graduates by course, for 1913; staff figures are printed once spanning all courses.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Collegiate Institutions
metadata.description: Shows yearly student numbers by faculty and the number of graduates at public and private collegiate institutions for 1910–11 to 1912–13, as a statistical overview of higher education.

metadata.title: [Collegiate Institutions: Names, Locations, Founding Dates and Subjects Taught]
metadata.description: Lists the public and private collegiate institutions with their location, founding year and subjects taught, followed by the author's remark on which universities are most important.

metadata.title: Recipients of Prizes
metadata.description: The Academy's prize recipients from 1911 to 1914 are listed by year, recipient, subject and the body (Emperor or Academy) that awarded the prize.

metadata.title: The Educational Stock Fund
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: The Educational Stock Fund, created from the Chinese Indemnity, is shown with its loans, bonds, deposits and total sum for four fiscal years, 1909–10 to 1912–13.

metadata.title: [Income of Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly income of the fund created in 1900-01 to give regular allowances to common school teachers, from State aid, provincial contributions and interest.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers]
metadata.description: Shows how the Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers was disbursed each year as additional allowances and amounts carried forward.

metadata.title: [Aid to Low-Grade Technical and Similar Schools]
metadata.description: Lists the number of low-grade agricultural, fishery, commercial and technical schools aided by the State and the total aid given each year from 1907-08 to 1911-12.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid Out of Provincial and Communal Treasuries
metadata.description: The table gives provincial and communal expenditure on education by item for four fiscal years, showing how education funds were spent across school types.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: The table shows the constitution and eyesight of male students examined in government institutions over four years, as part of the school hygiene section.

metadata.title: Health of Female Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Shows the constitution and eyesight condition of female students in government institutions over four school years, 1909-10 to 1912-13.

metadata.title: Health of Public and Private Schools of Secondary and Elementary Education
metadata.description: Gives the physical health returns of boys in various secondary and elementary schools for the year 1912-13, as lead-in text states.

metadata.title: Data for Girls, 1912-13
metadata.description: Presents the physical health returns of girls in elementary, higher and normal schools for 1912-13, as introduced by the preceding sentence.

metadata.title: [Health Data of Elementary School Children, 1907-1911]
metadata.description: Gives average height and weight by age for 925 elementary school children in Japan Proper, from 1907 to 1911, as the lead-in text announces.

metadata.title: The Imperial Library
metadata.description: Statistics of the Imperial Library's collection of volumes, days open, and visitors for the years 1910 to 1913, illustrating its size relative to European libraries.

metadata.title: [University Library Volumes, March 1913]
metadata.description: Volume counts of the Imperial universities' libraries at Tokyo, Kyoto and Tohoku as of March 1913, showing the Tokyo library as the largest.

metadata.title: Libraries Under the Department of Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of public libraries, their volumes, opening days and visitors for 1910 to 1913, illustrating the growth of library provision in Japan.

metadata.title: [Visitors to the Tokyo, Kyoto and Nara Museums and the Zoo]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of visitors to the Imperial museums at Tokyo, Kyoto and Nara and to the zoological garden attached to the Tokyo museum.

metadata.title: [Department of Education's Ryugakusei Staying Abroad at End of Year]
metadata.description: Shows how many of the Department of Education's ryugakusei (students abroad) were staying overseas at the end of each school year from 1905-6 to 1912-13.

metadata.title: License for Secondary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of applications, licences granted and the ratio of licences for secondary school teachers over the last four years, under the Examination Committee's licensing service.

metadata.title: License for Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Gives the applications, licences granted and licence ratios for elementary school teachers over the same four years, continuing the licensing statistics.

metadata.title: Private School Graduates and License
metadata.description: Lists the private universities and institutions authorized, subject to Education Department approval, to issue secondary school teachers' licences to superior graduates, with the subject for each.

metadata.title: [Condition of Girls Leaving Higher Schools After Graduation]
metadata.description: The table shows how female students of higher schools for girls were classified after leaving school in each year from 1904-5 to 1909-10, supporting the point that marriage remained the ideal.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts, at End of 1912
metadata.description: Shows the number of courts of each grade at the end of 1912 and the number of judges and procurators attached to them.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases During 1912
metadata.description: Gives the number of civil cases handled in each court during 1912, with cases disposed of, cases remaining, and retrial withdrawals and quashings.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases Demanded for Revision
metadata.description: Shows the number of civil cases demanded for revision in 1908–1912, how they were concluded (quashed, rejected, withdrawn), and the cases left in hand, with averages.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases Appealed
metadata.description: Shows yearly figures for civil cases brought on appeal, how they were concluded, and cases still pending, with a five-year average.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases Complained
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for civil cases complained against, with how each was concluded and the number left pending, plus an average.

metadata.title: No. of Civil Cases of First Instance
metadata.description: Presents yearly figures for first-instance civil cases: number heard, how they were concluded, cases pending, and the rate of plaintiff losses per 100 decisions.

metadata.title: Nature of the Above Cases
metadata.description: Breaks down the above cases by the nature of the property or matter involved, year by year with an average, showing the kinds of cases handled.

metadata.title: Cases of Bankruptcy and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Shows yearly counts of bankruptcy adjudications by type of business organisation, cases remaining in hand, credit amounts, and rehabilitation outcomes.

metadata.title: Cases of Insolvency and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for insolvency cases, including debtors, creditors, credit involved, and rehabilitation outcomes, with averages.

metadata.title: No. of Cases Involving Aliens (1912)
metadata.description: Classifies the 1912 court cases involving foreigners by the nationality of the plaintiff and the stage of trial reached.

metadata.title: No. of Criminal Cases
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal cases handled in 1910–1912 across search, preliminary trial, first instance and appeal stages, illustrating the workload under the new criminal code.

metadata.title: [Grand Total of Criminal Cases, 1910-1912]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly totals of cases handled, disposed of and still pending in 1910-1912, the counts shown being for violations of administrative and taxation rules.

metadata.title: Sentence Carried Out
metadata.description: Shows the number of offenders sentenced and the penalties imposed by category of case for 1910-1912, with the grand totals and offenders per 100,000 population.

metadata.title: Number of Prison Inmates at End of Year
metadata.description: Gives the number of prisons and the inmates held in them at year end from 1908 to 1912, broken down by convicts, correction cases, defendants, cell type and infants.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified
metadata.description: Breaks down the new convicts of 1912 by type of offence, giving the number for each offence and the rate per 100,000 population.

metadata.title: [Offences by Category, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a table of offence categories, with case numbers and percentages, ending in a total for the year.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences According to Convicts
metadata.description: This table shows offences by convicts broken down by number of previous offences and by age under or above 18, for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Amnesty Granted on the Occasion of the Imperial Funeral of Emperor Meiji, 1912]
metadata.description: Lists the numbers of persons granted each kind of amnesty at the 1912 Imperial funeral of Emperor Meiji, with the total.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Education
metadata.description: Shows the education level of newly admitted convicts by sex for 1910 to 1912, with illiterate convicts and totals.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Property
metadata.description: Shows the number of new convicts each year, by sex, classified by their property status (with property, small property, without property, or indigence).

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the sick rate and mortality among prison inmates for 1908 to 1912, including average daily sick numbers and mortality counts.

metadata.title: Work by Prison Inmates and Earnings
metadata.description: Shows the work done by prison inmates by sex, their total earnings, and the average share paid to each inmate per head for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-Officers and Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the number of inmates per prison warder, turnkey and female keeper for 1908 to 1912, indicating staffing ratios in prisons.

metadata.title: Entered and Left of Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the yearly numbers of male and female prison inmates entered and released, by reason, for 1909 to 1912.

metadata.title: Revenue of Prison (in yen)
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Lists the prison's revenue in yen by ordinary and extraordinary receipts for fiscal years 1909-10 to 1913-14, the last being an estimate.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prison
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows annual prison expenditure in yen for 1908-9 to 1912-13, split into ordinary items (salaries, wages, inmate expenses, others) and extraordinary outlays, with totals.

metadata.title: Prison Expense Per 1 Inmate
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the average yearly prison expense per inmate in yen, separated into ordinary and extraordinary costs and total, for 1908-9 to 1912-13.

metadata.title: Police Offices and Police Force
metadata.description: Shows the number of police stations, officers, policemen and the total police force for 1907 to 1911, illustrating the growth of the police establishment that handled police court offences.

metadata.title: Suicides and Acts Thereof
metadata.description: Breaks down suicides by method and sex for 1909 to 1911, with male and female totals and a grand total, showing the methods most used.

metadata.title: Cases of Suicides of Over 200 Classified
metadata.description: Gives the number of suicide cases attributed to mental derangement, by sex, for 1909 to 1911, as a classified subset of the suicide statistics.

metadata.title: Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.description: Shows the number of people and houses affected by robbery, peculation and fraud over 1909 to 1911, with robbery rates per 1000 population.

metadata.title: Police Offences of Over 200 Cases Classified
metadata.description: Lists the number of police-recorded offences of each category with over 200 cases, for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: Unnatural Deaths
metadata.description: Shows the number of unnatural deaths by cause and the death rate per 100,000 population for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: Number of Foundlings
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of foundlings, divided into boys and girls, for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Summarises the number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, and burnt area for 1909 to 1911, with per-case averages and a three-year average.

metadata.title: Casualties Concerning Police Affairs
metadata.description: Shows the numbers killed and wounded in casualties connected with police affairs from 1906 to 1911.

metadata.title: Rewards with Regard to Police Administration
metadata.description: Gives the number of persons rewarded in money and by certificates of merit for police administration, and the total money awarded, for 1909 to 1911.

metadata.title: [Hospitals, Doctors and Mid-wives at the End of Year]
metadata.description: Shows the number of hospitals, doctors (total and per 10,000 population) and mid-wives at the end of 1909 to 1911, illustrating the medical provision discussed in the section text.

metadata.title: [Vaccination Cases Recorded, 1909–1911]
metadata.description: Gives the total number of vaccinations recorded in 1909, 1910 and 1911, as the text notes that vaccination is compulsory and recorded in recent years.

metadata.title: Ratio of Successful Vaccination of Persons Tried for the First Time and Second Time or Over
metadata.description: Gives the percentage of successful vaccinations for persons vaccinated for the first time and for those vaccinated a second time or later, for the years 1905 to 1911.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified
metadata.caption: (Total No. and relative ratio per 1,000 deaths)
metadata.description: Lists the number of deaths from major diseases and their ratio per 1,000 deaths for 1908 to 1910, illustrating the leading causes of death under the mortality discussion.

metadata.title: Eight Epidemic Diseases and Mortality
metadata.description: Shows annual case and death counts for eight epidemic diseases in 1910 to 1912, with mortality per 100 cases, as evidence of the disease burden preceding the tuberculosis discussion.

metadata.title: [Strikes and Laborers Involved, 1908-1911]
metadata.description: Following a discussion of labor disputes from 1897 to 1902, the Department of Agriculture and Commerce's figures for strikes and the laborers involved in each year from 1908 to 1911 are given.

metadata.title: Data at End of March 1913
metadata.description: Shows the data of the mutual relief insurance arrangement in force in some Government establishments, illustrating the workmen's insurance system described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Members and Payments of the Mutual Relief Society by Government Establishment]
metadata.description: The table gives the membership, deaths and benefit payments of the Mutual Relief Society for each government establishment, illustrating how the scheme operated, with the Government Railway discussed below.

metadata.title: [Index Numbers of Mechanics, Output and Spindles in Operation, 1887–1910]
metadata.description: Index numbers for mechanics, output and spindles in operation over 1887–1910 illustrate the growth of Japanese spinning labour efficiency that the following data then examine.

metadata.title: [Wages and Operatives per 1000 Spindles in Spinning, 1908]
metadata.description: Based on 1908 data, this table compares the number of operatives per 1000 spindles and the wages in the U.S.A., England and Japan to show Japanese spinning efficiency.

metadata.title: [Cost of Labour for Producing 10 Kwan of Yarn by Count]
metadata.description: Assuming the same cotton, this table gives the wages needed to produce 10 kwan of yarn in each country, showing Japan's lower labour cost per unit.

metadata.title: Wages Per Week in Yen
metadata.caption: (Maximum ‡ Minimum †)
metadata.description: Weekly wages of skilled trades in England and Germany are given as the comparison with Japanese living expense figures, drawn from the British Board of Trade report.

metadata.title: [Wages and Earnings by Country, 1907–1909]
metadata.description: Comparison of wage figures for France, Belgium, the United States and Japan in 1907–1909, showing Japan's much lower earnings relative to Western countries.

metadata.title: Living Expense in 1903 per Day per Artisan
metadata.caption: (in sen)
metadata.description: Daily living costs in sen for an artisan's household, broken down by category and by the monthly earnings of the main wage-earner.

metadata.title: Earnings and Disbursements per Year per Artisan
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Annual earnings, disbursements and balance per artisan in several countries, showing Japan's small surplus compared with Western nations.

metadata.title: [Factory Workers by Age at 25 Prefectures, 1909]
metadata.description: Results of the September 1909 inquiry into factory labor at 25 prefectures, giving the number of male and female workers by age, with the rate per 1,000 workers.

metadata.title: Child Operatives
metadata.description: Percentages of child operatives under 16 by age band in the match, glass and filature industries, which employ the largest shares of such children.

metadata.title: [Spinning, Weaving and Printing Figures (Continued Table)]
metadata.description: The top of the page carries the tail of a table giving figures for spinning, weaving and printing, whose opening header is on the previous page.

metadata.title: [Working Hours, Rest Hours and Monthly Holidays in Factories by Kind]
metadata.description: Compares working hours, rest hours, monthly holidays and yearly working days across several factory kinds, showing the conditions of filatures, spinning, weaving, match, printing and paper workers.

metadata.title: [Working Hours and Holidays of Operatives at Army Cloth Works]
metadata.description: Shows working hours, rest hours, monthly holidays and yearly work days for male, female and child operatives at army cloth works, illustrating the better treatment at Government factories.

metadata.title: [Operatives at Government Works by Sex and Age, End of 1912]
metadata.description: Gives the number of male and female operatives over and under 14 years of age at Government works at the end of 1912, showing the small share of child workers.

metadata.title: [Factory Workers by Industry and Sex, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuing figures for several factory industries, giving male, female and child workers with wage and employment-related columns; the column headings are not printed on this page.

metadata.title: Average Daily Wages
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Average daily wages of various artisans, labourers and servants in the years 1906, 1910, 1911 and 1913, shown to show wage trends for the working population.

metadata.title: Operatives Classified According to Employment, Giving Only Those Employing Not Less Than 10,000 Operatives
metadata.description: Shows the number of operatives in each industry employing at least 10,000 workers, by sex and year, for 1911 and 1912, illustrating the labor force in major factory industries.

metadata.title: [Millionaire Families by Locality, 1912]
metadata.description: Shows how the 408 millionaire families at the end of 1912 were distributed among localities, according to the Osaka Asahi, as the article on plutocracy opens.

metadata.title: [Millionaire Families by Profession]
metadata.description: Gives the relative numbers of the 408 millionaire families divided by profession, showing merchants and manufacturers as the largest group.

metadata.title: [Causes of Poverty]
metadata.description: The table counts the number of persons classed by cause of poverty, listing causes such as intemperance, gambling, indolence and natural misfortune, with a grand total.

metadata.title: Press Statistics
metadata.description: Police Bureau returns giving the number of dailies and periodicals with and without deposit existing at the end of 1913 and 1914.

metadata.title: [Periodicals Listed by Title, Subject, Frequency and Price]
metadata.description: A classified list of Japanese periodicals giving each journal's subject, frequency, price and publisher, continuing the alphabetical press listing before the News Agencies section.

metadata.title: [Books Published, 1911-1913]
metadata.description: The page gives the recent output of books, showing original works, translations and totals published in each year from 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Prohibitions of Publications and Sales of Newspapers and Periodicals]
metadata.description: Introduced by the sentence about cases of prohibition, this table lists censorship actions against newspapers and periodicals in 1913 and 1914.

metadata.title: [Cases of Other Publications Forbidden, Suppressed, Warned or Tried]
metadata.description: Introduced by 'Cases of other publications are as follows', the table gives yearly counts of publications suppressed, banned, warned or taken to court in 1912 and 1913.

metadata.title: [Foreign Books Prohibited for Sale, by Grounds]
metadata.description: Introduced by 'There were also some cases of prohibition of sale of foreign books imported', the table shows volumes banned for public order or public morals in 1912 and 1913.

metadata.title: [Famous Wrestlers of Tokyo]
metadata.description: The page introduces the sumo wrestlers of the two opposing camps and lists the famous Tokyo wrestlers with their birth years, weights and heights.

metadata.title: [Cost of River Works Undertaken by Different Finances, 1905–1909]
metadata.description: The table shows how river works costs were met by the Central Government, prefectures, districts, cities, villages and other bodies over 1905–1909, illustrating the financing of river control.

metadata.title: Principal Harbor-Works
metadata.description: Lists the leading harbours improved by harbour works or dredging, with the works carried out, dates of beginning and completion, and expenditure.

metadata.title: [Harbour Works Completed or Under Construction (Continued)]
metadata.description: The table lists minor port works, giving the type of work, start and completion dates and cost for each port, as a continuation of the preceding table.

metadata.title: [Civil Engineering Expenses by Classification, 1905-1909]
metadata.description: The table classifies civil engineering expenditure by type of work for the years 1905 to 1909, showing how the national treasury's spending was distributed.

metadata.title: [Average Yearly Damage from Floods, Tidal Waves and Typhoons]
metadata.description: Shows yearly flood, tidal wave and typhoon damage for 1908 to 1911 and the average for 1902-1911, illustrating the scale of natural-disaster losses the text describes.

metadata.title: [Waterworks of Principal Cities]
metadata.description: Lists the main waterworks of Japanese cities, giving construction cost, pipe length, daily water supply and houses served, illustrating the spread of Western-style waterworks.

metadata.title: Arable Land and Farming Population
metadata.description: Shows the gross area of arable land in Japan Proper, split into land-owners' and tenanted paddy and upland, for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Farming Families by Category of Holding, 1911–1913]
metadata.description: Classifies the farming families into land-owners, tenants and both combined, giving the total farming families for each year from 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Farming Families Rearranged by Occupation, 1911–1913]
metadata.description: Rearranges the farming families into those farming solely and those with subsidiary occupations, with totals, for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Farmer's Family Classified as to Area of Cultivation
metadata.description: Distributes farmers' families by the area of land each cultivates, with numbers and percentages for 1912 and 1913.

metadata.title: [Taxable Land, 1912–1914]
metadata.caption: (In 1,000 cho)
metadata.description: Shows the area of taxable land by category at the end of December for 1912 to 1914, compared with the farming area, to illustrate recent land trends.

metadata.title: [Market Price of Farm Land, 1914]
metadata.description: Gives the latest market value of paddy and upland farms in 1914 by region and quality, as found by the Hypothec Bank of Japan, to show how far prices exceed the official 1875 values.

metadata.title: [Average Yield per Tan of Paddy Field]
metadata.caption: (In koku)
metadata.description: Shows the average paddy yield per tan over successive five-year periods and the twenty-year average ending 1912, illustrating the rise in productive power.

metadata.title: [Cultivated Area by Crop System, 1912 and 1913]
metadata.description: The table shows the division of cultivated land by cropping system, with areas in cho and percentages for 1912 and 1913, as part of the agriculture statistics.

metadata.title: Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.caption: Cattle and horses employed in tillage are returned as follows:—
metadata.description: The table gives the numbers of cattle and horses used in tillage and the area tilled by animal labor on paddy and upland farms for 1912 and 1913.

metadata.title: [Fertilizers Consumed]
metadata.description: The table lists the principal fertilizers consumed in the year, and the text that follows gives the main fertilizers imported and the estimated total manure consumption in Japan.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.description: The table gives the area, production, average yield, and export and import figures for rice in 1912 to 1914, with the normal yield for comparison.

metadata.title: Yield per Tan of Rice Varieties
metadata.description: The table compares the average output per tan of early, middle and late rice varieties at Government Experimental Farms, showing the middle variety is most productive.

metadata.title: Barley and Wheat
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Shows annual production of barley, naked barley and wheat from 1911 to 1914 against a normal yield, supporting the discussion of these upland staple crops.

metadata.title: [Barley and Wheat Cultivation by Field Type, 1914]
metadata.description: Gives the 1914 area sown to barley, naked barley and wheat in paddy-fields versus dry farms, illustrating where each crop is grown.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Lists production of minor grains such as millets, buckwheat and maize from 1911 to 1913, which are grown in mountainous districts and as rice substitutes.

metadata.title: Beans, Sweet Potatoes and Potatoes
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual output of beans, sweet potatoes and potatoes, illustrating the importance of these subsidiary farm crops in Japanese food supply.

metadata.title: Some Special Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives output of special crops such as indigo, tobacco, cotton, hemp and rape seed for 1911–1913, with commentary on the trends in each.

metadata.title: Other Minor Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kwan)
metadata.description: Gives the production of various minor vegetables, roots and other crops in Japan for 1912 and 1913, in thousands of kwan.

metadata.title: [Sericultural Families, Mulberry Plantation and Cocoon Output]
metadata.description: Shows the number of sericultural families by rearing season, the mulberry plantation area and the total value of cocoon output for 1911–1913, supporting the discussion of sericulture and government encouragement of mulberry planting.

metadata.title: No. of Egg-Cards Hatched
metadata.description: Gives the number of egg-cards hatched and the cocoons yielded per card for each rearing season and in total, for 1910–1912.

metadata.title: Output of Cocoons
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Reports spring and summer cocoon output in koku and value by quality grade (normal, double, pierced, waste) with percentage shares, for 1911–1913.

metadata.title: Output of Cocoons (in 1,000) Continued
metadata.description: Shows the autumn and total silk cocoon output, by grade and by value, with percentage shares of each cocoon grade, continuing the cocoon output table from the previous page.

metadata.title: Output of Raw Silk (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the annual output of raw silk and of waste silk, with combined totals, in kwan and yen for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Silk Conditioning at Yokohama]
metadata.description: Records the number of silk lots conditioned, weighed, boiled off and quality-tested at the Yokohama conditioning house, with weights and average loss, for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Tea Exports by Year and Firm Nationality]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly volume of tea exported from Japan, split between Japanese and foreign firms, with percentage shares, illustrating the tea trade's stagnation.

metadata.title: [Tea Exports by Destination, 1912 and 1913]
metadata.description: Lists the quantity and value of Japanese tea exports to each destination country in 1912 and 1913, introduced by the statement that the destinations are as follows.

metadata.title: Area of Tea Plantations and Number of Manufacturers
metadata.description: Shows the area of tea plantations in cho and the number of tea manufacturers for 1910 to 1913, illustrating the state of the tea industry in those years.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Teas
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output of each grade of tea (green, black and oolong) from 1912 to 1914, with the note explaining the 1914 decrease.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1913)
metadata.description: Lists the three leading tea-producing districts in each of two groups, with output and value for 1913.

metadata.title: [Quantity and Value of Tea Exported, 1909–1914]
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of tea exported each year from 1909 to 1914, set out to support the discussion of the export trade.

metadata.title: [Volume of Teas Exported in 1913 from Various Ports]
metadata.description: Gives the volume of teas exported in 1913 from four ports, in kwan, pounds and boxes, with totals, as introduced by the preceding text.

metadata.title: Principal Destinations of Teas Exported
metadata.caption: (Unit: yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of tea exports from Japan, in thousands of yen, to each principal destination for 1912 to 1914, introduced as a supporting figure in the Agriculture section.

metadata.title: Number of Horses in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the number of horses in Japan from 1911 to 1913, divided into native, cross-bred and foreign animals, in support of the discussion of horse breeding.

metadata.title: Number of Stallions in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the number of stallions in Japan from 1911 to 1913 by native, cross-bred and foreign breed, set beneath the horse figures as part of the horse-breeding survey.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the yearly head counts of native, cross-bred and foreign cattle, with totals, calving and deaths, showing the decline of the native breed.

metadata.title: Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Lists the numbers of sheep, goats and swine in Japan for three successive years.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Reports the number of slaughter-houses and the animals slaughtered each year, by kind of animal, for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Leading Stock Farms
metadata.description: Lists leading stock farms in Japan, mainly in Hokkaido, giving each farm's place, kind of stock and ownership.

metadata.title: [Principal Stock Farms and Pastures]
metadata.description: Lists the principal government and private stock farms, pastures and sheep farm, with their location, kind of stock and ownership.

metadata.title: Number of Families Keeping Poultry (in 1,000)
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of families keeping poultry, the fowl stock and the egg production with their values for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: Leading Poultry Districts at the End of June, 1914
metadata.description: Ranks the leading poultry prefectures by number of poultry-keeping families and by value of fowl and eggs at mid-1914.

metadata.title: Leading Dairy Districts (1913)
metadata.description: The table gives the number of dairy farms, milk cows, and milk output in yen and koku for the leading dairy prefectures in 1913, with yearly totals for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Animal Epidemics
metadata.description: The table lists numbers of horses and cattle affected or died from glanders, farcy, anthrax and rinderpest from 1911 to 1913, illustrating the disease losses discussed in the text.

metadata.title: Output of Fruits
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Fruit-culture has grown in importance, and this table gives the number of trees and the yield of each main fruit for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.description: The page classifies the strata existing in Japan, by relative percentage, into sedimentary and igneous rocks, giving each era's share and the overall grand total.

metadata.title: Mineral Production: Gold, Silver, Copper and Lead
metadata.description: Gives the latest figures for Japan Proper's output and value of gold, silver, copper and lead for 1909 to 1913, as an introduction to the mineral statistics.

metadata.title: Mineral Production: Iron, Iron Pyrites, Antimony and Manganese
metadata.description: Continues the statistics of principal mineral output in Japan Proper, giving iron, iron pyrites, antimony and manganese quantities and values for 1909 to 1913.

metadata.title: Mineral Production: Coal, Sulphur, Petroleum and Total Value
metadata.description: Completes the table of Japan Proper's principal mineral production, giving coal, sulphur and petroleum output with the total value of all minerals for 1909 to 1913.

metadata.title: Principal Metal-Mines
metadata.caption: (figures in 1000)
metadata.description: Listing the principal metal mines and their gold, silver and copper output for 1910 to 1912, illustrating the scale of Japan's non-ferrous metal production under the preceding paragraphs on sulphur.

metadata.title: [Iron Output by Mines, 1910–1912]
metadata.description: Iron output from the various mines, with figures in unlabelled groups, shown as the continuation of a table begun on the previous page.

metadata.title: [Iron Output of Kamaishi and Senninyama Mines]
metadata.description: The full iron output of the two principal iron mines, Kamaishi and Senninyama, is given for 1910 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Lead and Zinc Output of Kamioka]
metadata.description: Kamioka is noted for lead and zinc, and its output of both metals for 1910 to 1912 is listed here.

metadata.title: [Available Coal Resources by District]
metadata.description: The available coal resources, estimated at 1,738 million tons, are roughly distributed among the main coal districts of Japan.

metadata.title: Chief Coal-Fields of Japan
metadata.description: Lists the annual output of the chief coal-fields of Japan by district (Hokkaido, Iwaki-Hitachi, Chikuho) for 1910 to 1912, illustrating the scale of production.

metadata.title: Analysis of Coals from the Principal Coal-Fields
metadata.description: Gives the proximate analysis, sulphur content, caking quality, specific gravity and calorific power of coals from the principal coal-fields.

metadata.title: [Output of Crude Oil in Echigo Fields, 1910–1913]
metadata.description: Introduces the yearly crude oil output of the Echigo oil-fields from 1910 to 1913, with total value, as reported by the Petroleum Association at Nagaoka.

metadata.title: [Echigo Oil Production by Classification, 1911 and 1912]
metadata.caption: (Unit: koku)
metadata.description: Shows how the Echigo field production was divided among volatile, lamp, solar and heavy lubricant oils in 1911 and 1912.

metadata.title: [Number of Wells by Type in Echigo Fields]
metadata.description: Lists the number of machine wells, Kazusabori wells and hand wells in the main Echigo oil-fields, explaining the drilling methods used.

metadata.title: Leading Concessionaires of Mines
metadata.description: Lists the concessionaires whose mine production in 1912 and 1911 exceeded two million yen in value or nearly so, with mine counts by type.

metadata.title: Number of Mine-Workers at Principal Mines
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of mine-workers at principal metal, coal, and non-metal mines, with totals and alluvial-diggers, from 1909 to 1913.

metadata.title: Condition of Work and Wages of Mine-Workers
metadata.description: Compares the monthly working days and average daily hours of various mine-worker classes in metal mines and collieries.

metadata.title: Average Wages at Principal Mines
metadata.caption: (in yen; 1912)
metadata.description: Shows average daily wages in yen for male, female and child workers in metal mines and collieries in 1912, by occupation, giving a wage comparison across mining work.

metadata.title: Accidents at the Mines
metadata.description: Gives the number of mine accidents and the resulting casualties (deaths, severe and slight injuries) for each year from 1909 to 1913, showing the trend in mining accidents.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.description: Shows the quantities (in 1,000 kin) and values (¥1,000) of copper, coal and sulphur exported from Japan each year from 1909 to 1913.

metadata.title: Imports
metadata.description: Lists the quantities and values of iron and steel and petroleum imported into Japan each year from 1909 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Fishing-Boats by Type, 1911-1913]
metadata.description: Gives the number of fishing-boats in use from 1911 to 1913, broken down by sailing boats of Japanese and European type and steamers, to show the size of the fishing fleet.

metadata.title: Accidents to Fishing Boats and Casualties to Fishermen (1913)
metadata.description: Shows how many fishing boats were wrecked, drifted, lost, upset or otherwise damaged, and the resulting killed, wounded and missing crew, for 1913 with comparative totals for 1912 and 1911.

metadata.title: Catches and Marine Production
metadata.description: Gives the annual value of catches and of marine production for 1911 to 1913, as the opening summary of the fisheries statistics.

metadata.title: Principal Catches
metadata.caption: (1000 kwan; 1000 yen)
metadata.description: Lists the principal catches by species, with quantities and values for 1912 and 1913, showing the leading fish taken by Japanese fisheries.

metadata.title: Marine Products
metadata.caption: (1000 kwan; 1000 yen)
metadata.description: Shows the quantities and values of processed marine products such as dried, boiled, salted and manure fish for 1912 and 1913.

metadata.title: Export of Fresh Fish and Marine Products
metadata.caption: Exports (¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the export values of fresh fish and marine products, with totals and imports, for 1910 to 1912, illustrating the growth of the trade.

metadata.title: [Marine Products Quantity and Value]
metadata.description: Summarises the quantity and value of the principal dried and oil marine products of Japan's fisheries.

metadata.title: Aquiculture

metadata.title: Forests in Japan Proper by Proprietorship

metadata.title: [Prefectures Containing Not Less Than 500,000 Cho of Forest]

metadata.title: Forest Yield in Japan Proper, 1913-14
metadata.description: Gives the 1913-14 forest yield of Japan Proper by kind of tree, with timber and fagots each shown by quantity and value, as the basis for the forestry revenue discussion.

metadata.title: Financial Yield of Forest Classified (1913-14)
metadata.description: Shows the financial yield from timber and fagots for State, Crown, and public and private forests in 1913-14, as a basis for the forestry revenue discussion.

metadata.title: [Receipts, Expenses and Balance of State Forests]
metadata.description: Shows the receipts, expenses and resulting profit of the State forests over three fiscal years, illustrating why the rate of profit is comparatively small.

metadata.title: [Forest Products in Foreign Trade]
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 yen)
metadata.description: Lists the principal forest product items in export and import trade for 1912 to 1914, showing timber, tea-chest boards, match sticks, bamboos, teak and other timber.

metadata.title: [Working Plan Classification of State Forests]
metadata.description: Gives the percentage division of the 1,735,174 cho of State forests under the working plan decided up to March 1912, by forest system and barren area.

metadata.title: [Rotation System for Principal Trees]
metadata.description: Lists the rotation periods, in years, adopted for principal forest trees under the planting programme described in the surrounding text.

metadata.title: Total Value of Felling and Conversion
metadata.description: Shows the total value of timber and fagot felling and conversion for three successive years, as background to the discussion of the sawing business.

metadata.title: Principal Forest Products
metadata.description: The table gives the value in yen of principal subsidiary forest products such as timber, charcoal and mushrooms for 1912 and 1913, supporting the note that these products form a large share of total forestry output.

metadata.title: Output of Refined Camphor (Japan Proper)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly quantity and value of refined camphor output in Japan Proper, illustrating the revival of domestic production after the monopoly rules were extended there.

metadata.title: Number of Licenses Granted
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Class A (firearm) and Class B (other methods) hunting licences issued in each of three grades for 1912-13 and 1913-14, under the game law.

metadata.title: [Industrial Companies and Capital at the End of Year]
metadata.description: Summarises the number of organized companies, their paid up capital and reserves at year end 1911 to 1913, showing the growth of investment in industrial enterprises.

metadata.title: Industrial Companies Classified by Amount of Investment
metadata.description: Lists the industries whose companies have paid up capital of yen 500,000 or more, with company numbers, capital and reserves at the end of 1913.

metadata.title: Distribution of Industries
metadata.caption: To mention leading districts containing companies with total capital of over yen 10,000,000 p.u. each we have at the end of 1913 :—
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectural districts whose companies together held more than ten million yen of paid-up capital at the end of 1913, with their company counts and capital.

metadata.title: Factories and Employees
metadata.description: Gives the number of factories by type of motive power and the number of operatives by sex for 1911 to 1913, the Note below it explaining the 1913 motive powers.

metadata.title: [Motive Powers Used in 1913]
metadata.description: Breaks down the motive power in use in 1913 by kind of engine or motor, giving the number of engines and total horse power for each.

metadata.title: Kind of Factories Classified
metadata.description: Classifies the factories and their horse power, kilowatt capacity and employees by industry group, covering textile, machinery, chemical, food and miscellaneous enterprises.

metadata.title: Cotton Spinning
metadata.description: Shows the yearly development of the cotton spinning industry in Japan, covering mills, capital, spindles, cotton consumed and output for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Exports and Imports of Cotton Yarns
metadata.description: Gives the quantity and value of cotton yarn exported and imported by Japan for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: Leading Cotton Mills
metadata.caption: (At the end of 2nd half, 1914)
metadata.description: Lists the leading cotton spinning companies with their capital, reserves, debts, spindles and dividends at the end of the second half of 1914.

metadata.title: Silk Spinning
metadata.description: Presents the latest statistics on silk spinning mills, spindles and output of silk yarn and tsumugi for 1911 to 1913, as the text below introduces.

metadata.title: Hempen Spinning
metadata.description: Gives the statistics of hempen (hemp) spinning mills for 1911 to 1913, presented after the note that hemp spinning began in Shiga-ken and spread to other areas.

metadata.title: [Leading Mousseline-de-Laine Companies and Their Stands]
metadata.description: Lists the four leading companies producing mousseline-de-laine, a light woollen fabric, with the number of looms (stands) each operates.

metadata.title: Statistics of Textile Industry
metadata.description: Gives the number of textile factories, looms, operatives and the total output for 1911 to 1913, summarising the industry before the detailed fabric figures.

metadata.title: Output of Fabrics
metadata.caption: (Output in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Breaks down the year's textile output by fabric kind, grouped under silk, silk-and-cotton mixed, cotton and woollen headings, with totals.

metadata.title: Returns of Export Fabrics
metadata.caption: (Unit: ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of exported silk, cotton and woollen fabrics for 1911 to 1913, with totals, as a supplement to the output figures.

metadata.title: Production (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows yearly production of potteries, Shippo ware, fireproof bricks, ordinary bricks and tiles, illustrating the over-production that has depressed the brick and tile trade since 1913.

metadata.title: Exports (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the export values of potteries and Shippo ware for 1912 to 1914, showing the trade in these ceramic goods during the period of over-production.

metadata.title: [Cement Production and Exports]
metadata.description: Summarises cement production in barrels and yen alongside exports in kin and yen for 1912 to 1914, set against the text on the industry's over-production and the European war's revival.

metadata.title: Production and Export
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of lacquer-ware production and export in Japan for 1912 to 1914, following the description of the lacquer industry's regional centres.

metadata.title: [Production of Sake, Beer and Soy]
metadata.description: Gives annual production of sake, beer and soy in koku for the March-to-February years 1912–13 to 1914–15, illustrating the scale of these industries.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows export quantities of sake, beer (by pint, quart and cask) and soy from 1912 to 1914, with the export destinations listed beneath.

metadata.title: Leading Breweries
metadata.description: Gives the latest financial conditions of the leading breweries, here the Dai Nippon Beer company, as a summary of the industry's main firms.

metadata.title: Matches
metadata.description: The table shows Japan's match production and exports over 1912 to 1914, set out to show the trade in matches in those years.

metadata.title: [Match Exports from Kobe and Osaka to Places, 1914]
