metadata.title: [Paper Production, Exports and Imports, 1913]
metadata.description: The table gives the amount and value of printing paper, cardboard and renshi produced, exported and imported in 1913.

metadata.title: [Paper Production, Exports and Imports]
metadata.description: Shows Japanese paper production, exports and imports by type, with pulp imports listed separately, illustrating the paper industry's scale.

metadata.title: Leading Paper-Making Companies in Japan, 1913
metadata.description: Lists the leading Japanese paper-making companies with their capital, receipts, expenditure and dividends for 1913, to show the industry's condition.

metadata.title: General Statistics of Soaps
metadata.caption: (Unit: ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly soap output, exports and imports for toilet and other soaps from 1911 to 1913, showing the rapid growth of soap exports.

metadata.title: [Production, Imports and Estimated Consumption of Artificial Fertilizers]
metadata.description: Shows latest figures for artificial fertilizer production, imports and estimated home consumption, illustrating how rapidly the industry has grown in recent years.

metadata.title: Output of Fish Oil
metadata.description: The output of sardine, herring and whale oil (with others and total) for 1911 to 1913 is given to illustrate the fish-oil industry's production, following the description of refining methods.

metadata.title: [Representative Machine Construction Companies]
metadata.description: Given as examples of representative machine construction companies, showing their paid-up capital, receipts, expenditure and dividends.

metadata.title: [Number of Gas Lamps and Installations, 1910–1912]
metadata.description: Shows how gas use for lighting, heating and motive power changed from 1910 to 1912, as electricity increasingly encroached on the gas industry.

metadata.title: [Electric Industry Classified by Nature of Enterprise and Motor Force, End of 1913]
metadata.caption: (Kilowatt)
metadata.description: Shows electric undertakings at the end of 1913 by nature of enterprise and motor force, in kilowatts, sanctioned and not yet sanctioned, which the page introduces as the classification obtained for that year.

metadata.title: Leading Electric Companies (at the End of 2nd Half, 1914)
metadata.description: Lists the leading electric companies with capital paid up, receipts, expenditure and dividend rate at the end of the second half of 1914, giving the scale of the principal undertakings.

metadata.title: Production and Consumption
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kin)
metadata.description: Gives Japan's sugar production, imports from abroad and Formosa, exports and resulting domestic consumption for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: Leading Sugar Companies in Japan
metadata.description: Shows capital, receipts, expenditure and productive capacity of the three leading sugar refining companies in Japan.

metadata.title: [Japanese Flour Milling Companies: Capital, Receipts, Expenditure and Productive Power]
metadata.description: The table gives capital, receipts, expenditure and productive power of the listed flour-milling companies, with the note explaining which reports cover the second half of 1914.

metadata.title: Production
metadata.description: The table shows annual output of native and imported wheat used as stuff, and the resulting flour production in koku and yen for 1911 to 1913, illustrating the milling industry discussed above.

metadata.title: Imports of Wheat and Flour
metadata.description: Shows the quantities and values of wheat and flour imported from 1911 to 1913, with totals, illustrating the growth of this import trade.

metadata.title: Leading Flour Mills (1914)
metadata.description: Lists five leading flour milling companies with their capital, receipts, expenditure and annual dividends, to indicate their size and profitability.

metadata.title: [Peppermint Production and Exports]
metadata.description: Gives the value of peppermint produced (crude, menthol, crystal oil) and the value exported for 1912 to 1914 in Hokkaido's peppermint industry.

metadata.title: Vegetable Wax
metadata.description: Shows the decline and partial recovery of Japan's vegetable wax output, in crude and refined form, alongside exports for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: Vegetable Oils
metadata.caption: (Outputs in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the annual output of vegetable oils from rape seed, sesame, yemola, cotton seed and other plants, with the grand total, for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Hemp Braid Production and Exports, 1912–1914]
metadata.description: Shows hemp braid output and export values by material (straw, chip, mixed) for 1912–1914, illustrating the rapid growth of the industry mentioned in the text.

metadata.title: [Matting Production and Exports]
metadata.description: Shows Japan's production and export values of floor mats and mattings for 1912 to 1914, given as background to the trade in matting goods.

metadata.title: [Leather Output]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output of leather from 1911 to 1913, split by cow and calf leather, horse leather and other kinds, as the text introduces leather statistics.

metadata.title: [Hosiery Exports]
metadata.caption: (Value in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the rising value of Japan's hosiery exports by item from 1911 to 1913, illustrating the progress the industry has made since 1903.

metadata.title: Production
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's canned goods output by category, including beef, fish and shellfish, and fruit, for 1911 to 1913, illustrating the growing canning industry.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's canned article exports by category, such as abalones, crabs, fish and vegetables, for 1912 to 1914, as part of the canning trade discussion.

metadata.title: Isinglass Production and Exports
metadata.description: Gives Japanese isinglass (kanten) production and export quantities and values for 1912 to 1914, a product exported mainly to Europe and America for jam making.

metadata.title: [Patent Fee for Extension of Period]
metadata.description: The page explains the patent fee schedule, giving the fee for extending the patent period by year range, with the fee amounts in yen listed alongside each period.

metadata.title: No. of Applications and Registrations
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of applications filed and patents, designs, trade-marks and utility models registered at the Patent Office since 1909.

metadata.title: No. of Actions for Trial and No. of Cases Upheld
metadata.description: Lists, for each fiscal year, the trials, appeals and appeals to the Supreme Court and how many actions were upheld across the four categories.

metadata.title: No. Existing at the End of the Fiscal Years
metadata.description: Gives the number of patents, designs, trade-marks and utility models still in force at the end of each fiscal year from 1907-08 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: Paid Up Capital of Sales Companies in 1913

metadata.title: [Companies by Industry, with Increase Compared with 1913]
metadata.description: Shows the number of companies, paid-up capital, and changes from 1913 for each branch of economic enterprise, with totals split by organization type.

metadata.description: Gives the yearly volume of rice dealt in at the exchanges, split by Tokyo and Osaka, with the average price per koku, as background to the rice market discussion.

metadata.title: Buddhist Temples and Priests
metadata.caption: Sects possessing over 1,000 temples are as follows:—

metadata.title: Statistics of Christian Churches in Japan
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Christian churches, tabernacles, believers and missionaries in Japan by denomination, illustrating the church-by-church picture discussed in the preceding text on the Orthodox Church.

metadata.title: Relief Fund
metadata.description: The table gives the annual local apportionments, proceeds, State aids, disbursements and balances of the prefectural Relief Fund for 1912 to 1914, illustrating the relief regulations described in the text.

metadata.title: [Paupers and Foundlings Supported by the State]
metadata.description: The table shows the number of paupers and foundlings the State supported, and the outlay on them, for calendar years 1911 to 1913, as part of the State's charity measures.

metadata.title: [Relief Allowances for Destitute Classes]
metadata.description: Lists the yearly or daily rice allowances granted under the relief system to decrepit or disabled persons, infants under fifteen, and invalids.

metadata.title: [Leper Hospitals and Inmates, End of 1912]
metadata.description: The page describes leper hospitals founded or established by the Government and private bodies, and lists the number of inmates at each at the end of 1912.

metadata.title: The Blind as Bread-Earners
metadata.description: The table gives the 69,167 blind people in Japan in 1910 classified by their profession, showing how many earned a living through shampooing, acupuncture and similar work.

metadata.title: List of Charity Institutions
metadata.caption: According to the latest reports compiled at the end of 1913 charity institutions and their works are as follows
metadata.description: Shows the number of charity institutions of each kind at the end of 1913, with the numbers cared for and expenses, as compiled from the latest reports.

metadata.title: Principal Institutions Granted State Aid in 1914
metadata.description: Lists the charity institutions that received State aid in 1914, giving each one's name, religious affiliation and location.

metadata.title: General Statistics on Educational Institutions in Japan Proper for 1913-4 Year
metadata.description: Gives the number of schools, instructors, students and graduates for each kind of educational institution in Japan Proper in 1913-14, with notes on how certain schools are taught and excluded.

metadata.title: Foreign Instructors at the Institutions under Direct Control of the Department of Education
metadata.description: Gives the number of foreign instructors by nationality, with total and annual salary cost, at institutions directly controlled by the Department of Education for 1912-13 and 1913-14.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the weekly hours allotted to each subject in each of the four school years of the ordinary elementary course, which the text describes as tabulated below.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Ordinary Elementary Schools—(Continued)

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age under Obligation to Attend School
metadata.description: Shows the number of school-age children obliged to attend school, split by sex and by whether they were receiving the prescribed course of instruction, for 1908-09 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: [Children under Obligation and Ratio Attending School]
metadata.description: Gives the total number of children under the compulsory education obligation by sex, and the per-100 ratio of those attending school, for 1908-09 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers of Both Sexes in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of public elementary school teachers of both sexes and their monthly salary distribution for 1908-09 to 1913-14, preceding the text on text-books and fees.

metadata.title: [Pupils Paying Fees and Exemptions in Schools]
metadata.description: Shows, for 1909–1914, how many schools collected tuition fees and how their pupils were divided between full payers, partial payers and those wholly exempted.

metadata.title: Blind, Deaf and Dumb of School-Age
metadata.description: Gives the number of blind and deaf-mute children of school age and those receiving instruction, with defectives per 1,000 normal children, for 1911–1914.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens, Conductors and Infants]
metadata.description: Lists the government, public and private kindergartens with their conductors and infant pupils by sex for 1913–14, with totals for 1912–13 and 1911–12.

metadata.title: The Curriculum of the Middle School
metadata.description: The table sets out the weekly hours for each subject in the five years of the Middle School curriculum, illustrating the course described in the preceding text on entrance and the division of the fourth year.

metadata.title: Careers of Public and Private School Graduates
metadata.description: Shows where public and private school graduates went in the year after graduation over three school years, by business, higher schools, conscription or volunteering, and other outcomes.

metadata.title: Curriculum of the Girls' High Schools
metadata.caption: hrs per week
metadata.description: Lists the weekly teaching hours per subject for each of the four years of the girls' high school course, showing the fixed total of 28 hours per week.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Girls' High Schools
metadata.caption: Number of girls attending the Girls' High Schools or Girls' Domestic High Schools are as follows for the year 1913-14 :—
metadata.description: Shows the number of girls attending public and private girls' high schools by course in 1913-14, with the share leaving or unfinished, as part of the chapter on high schools.

metadata.title: List of the High Schools for 1915-16 Year
metadata.description: Lists the eight government high schools for 1915-16 with their staff, students, graduates, applicants and admissions, followed by totals and figures for earlier years.

metadata.title: [Applicants and Admissions by Section]
metadata.description: Shows the number of applicants for admission to the three sections and the admissions per 100 applicants for each section, 1910-11 to 1913-14, with the average age of new boys.

metadata.title: [Instructors, Students and Graduates of Normal Schools by Sex]
metadata.description: Gives the number of normal schools by type and the male and female instructors, students and graduates in each year from 1909-10 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: Statistics of the Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: The table gives yearly figures for instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admissions at the Higher Normal Schools in Tokyo, Hiroshima, and the Tokyo and Nara women's schools, 1910-11 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Tokyo (1914-15)
metadata.caption: Est'd, April 1877. President, Yamakawa, Kenjiro, D. Sc.
metadata.description: Introduces the four state universities and gives the 1914-15 staff, student and graduate figures for the Tokyo university by college.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Kyoto (1914-15)
metadata.caption: Est'd, June 1897. President, Araki, Torasaburo, D.M.
metadata.description: Gives the 1914-15 staff, student and graduate figures for the Kyoto university, whose Science and Engineering rows share one bracketed set of figures.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Tohoku (1914-15)
metadata.caption: Est'd, June 1907. President, Hojo, Jikei
metadata.description: Shows the 1914-15 staff, student and graduate figures for the Tohoku university, the only one admitting students free from examination to science teachers' courses.

metadata.title: Students in the University Hall (Sep. 1914)
metadata.description: Shows the number of students from each imperial university enrolled in the various colleges at the University Hall in September 1914.

metadata.title: Average Age of Matriculation at Tokyo
metadata.caption: Average age of those matriculated recently is as follows:—
metadata.description: Gives the average age at which students were recently matriculated at Tokyo Imperial University, by college, for each year from 1909-10 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: Professions of the University Graduates
metadata.caption: Graduates of the Imperial Universities since the foundation to 1913-14, classified by their condition in life
metadata.description: Shows how graduates of each imperial university since its foundation to 1913-14 were employed, by profession.

metadata.title: [Employment and Status of Graduates by Imperial University, Continued]
metadata.description: This continued table gives the subsequent occupations and status of graduates of the four Imperial Universities, with a total for each university.

metadata.title: Total Number of Graduates from Inauguration till 1913-14 Classified by Colleges
metadata.description: This table counts the cumulative graduates of each Imperial University by college up to 1913-14, explaining the Kyoto decrease through the detachment of Kyushu University.

metadata.title: [Doctorates Conferred by Subject, March 1915]
metadata.description: Shows how many doctoral degrees were held by living and deceased recipients in each faculty, explaining the categories of doctors recognised under the regulations described above.

metadata.title: List of Government Technical and Special Schools for 1915–16
metadata.description: Lists the government technical and special schools of 1915–16 by type, giving each school's director, staff, students, applicants and admissions, as a guide to practical education.

metadata.title: [Special Schools: Principals and Figures]
metadata.description: Lists the government special schools (mining, agriculture and forestry, sericulture, foreign languages, art, music, nautical and fishery) with their location, principal and figures; the column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Public and Private Blind, Deaf and Dumb Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of blind, deaf and dumb schools, their teachers, pupils and graduates for each school year from 1910 to 1914.

metadata.title: [Schools for the Blind and Deaf-Mutes, 1913-14]
metadata.description: The page gives 1913-14 figures for the Tokyo blind and deaf-and-dumb schools, comparing staff, pupils, graduates and admissions, as a companion to the description of the schools' courses.

metadata.title: [The Peers' School Staff, Students and Graduates, 1914]
metadata.description: The page presents the Peers' School's 1914 breakdown by course, showing staff by department and students and graduates by sex, illustrating the school's boys' and girls' departments.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Collegiate Institutions
metadata.description: Gives yearly enrolment of students by subject, total students and graduates at public and private collegiate institutions over three academic years, 1911 to 1914.

metadata.title: Names, Locations, Founding Dates and Subjects of Collegiate Institutions
metadata.description: Lists the private and public collegiate institutions covered by the statistics, with each school's location, founding year and subjects taught.

metadata.title: [Recipients of Academy Prizes, 1911–1915]
metadata.description: Lists the recipients and subjects of the Imperial Academy's prizes from their beginning in 1911 through 1915, showing which prize each award came from.

metadata.title: The Educational Stock Fund
metadata.description: Shows the yearly account of the Educational Stock Fund, split into loans, bonds, deposits and total sum existing, for 1910-11 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: [Receipts of the Super-Stipend Fund]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly receipts of the fund that financed super-stipends for teachers, from state aid, provincial contributions, interest and carried-over balances, with totals.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of the Super-Stipend Fund]
metadata.description: Shows how the super-stipend fund's disbursements were split each year between additional teacher allowances and the balance carried forward, with totals.

metadata.title: [Aid to Technical and Vocational Schools]
metadata.description: Lists the number of low-grade technical, agricultural, fishery and commercial schools aided by the state each year and the total aid given.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid out of Provincial and Communal Treasuries
metadata.description: Shows educational expenses paid from provincial and communal treasuries by school type for four fiscal years, giving the national totals for each year.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Presents the physical condition of male students in government institutions over five school years, covering constitution and eyesight, as part of the schools hygiene section.

metadata.title: Health of Female Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Shows the physical health (constitution and eyesight) of female students in government institutions for each year from 1909-10 to 1913-14.

metadata.title: Health of Public and Private Schools of Secondary and Elementary Education
metadata.caption: Health returns of boys for 1913-14
metadata.description: Gives the 1913-14 health returns for boys in public and private secondary and elementary schools, by school type, with totals.

metadata.title: [Health of Girls in Public and Private Schools, 1913-14]
metadata.caption: Data for girls for 1913-14
metadata.description: Gives the 1913-14 health returns for girls in public and private schools by school type, with totals, continuing the boys' figures above.

metadata.title: [Height and Weight of Elementary School Children, 1913-14]
metadata.description: Gives the height and weight of elementary school boys and girls aged 7 to 16 in 1913-14, with the number examined at each age.

metadata.title: The Imperial Library
metadata.description: The Imperial Library's annual volume counts, days open, and visitor numbers from 1910 to 1914, showing its modest size relative to Western institutions.

metadata.title: The Imperial University Libraries (At the End of March, 1914)
metadata.description: The number of volumes stored in each Imperial University library at the end of March 1914, split into Japanese and Chinese, European and total works.

metadata.title: [Libraries and Their Attendance, 1911–1914]
metadata.description: Summarises the growth of public libraries from 1911 to 1914, showing number of libraries, volumes, opening days and visitors as an indicator of educational expansion.

metadata.title: [Total Number of Visitors to Museums, 1913–1914]
metadata.description: Gives the total visitor numbers for the Imperial museums at Tokyo, Kyoto and Nara, and the Zoo, for the years ended March 1913 and 1914.

metadata.title: [Department of Education's Ryugakusei Staying Abroad]
metadata.description: Shows how many of the Department of Education's ryugakusei (students sent abroad) were staying overseas at the end of each year from 1907 to 1914.

metadata.description: Gives the yearly applications, grants and percentages for teachers' licenses for secondary schools, by examination and without examination, over four years.

metadata.title: License for Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows yearly applications, grants and percentages for teachers' licenses for elementary schools, both by examination and without examination, over four years.

metadata.title: Private School Graduates and License
metadata.description: Lists the private universities and institutions authorized to issue secondary school teachers' licenses to superior graduates, with the subject for each.

metadata.description: Shows how girls who finished higher schools at seventeen or over were classified by their situation after leaving school, year by year from 1904-5 to 1909-10, to illustrate that marriage remained the ideal.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts, at End of 1914

metadata.description: Gives the number of civil cases handled in 1914 by each court level and kind of case, with the cases disposed of and those remaining in hand.

metadata.description: Shows, year by year from 1910 to 1914 with an average, how many first-instance civil cases were decided, withdrawn, reconciled or otherwise closed, and how many remained pending.

metadata.description: This table shows the number and kinds of civil cases settled at first instance each year from 1910 to 1914, with an average, broken down by subject matter.

metadata.description: This table reports bankruptcy cases each year from 1910 to 1914, separating individual, partnership and company cases, with amounts of credit and rehabilitation outcomes.

metadata.description: This table gives insolvency cases each year from 1910 to 1914, with numbers of debtors and creditors, amounts of credit and rehabilitation outcomes, plus averages.

metadata.description: Explains that criminal cases handled in the last three years are tabulated, showing cases received, disposed of and remaining in hand at each trial stage, 1912 to 1914.

metadata.description: The table gives the number of offenders whose sentences were carried out in 1912–1914, broken down by type of decision and sentence, showing the rate per 100,000 population.

metadata.description: Shows the number of prison inmates at year end from 1910 to 1914, broken down by category of inmate, to illustrate the trend in the prison population.

metadata.description: Shows the educational attainment of new convicts by sex for 1912 to 1914, from higher course education down to illiterate.

metadata.description: Shows the number of new convicts in 1912-1914, by sex and by the property status of each convict, to illustrate the economic condition of those entering prison.

metadata.description: Gives the sickness and death figures among prison inmates for 1912-1914, showing how often inmates fell ill and how many died per thousand.

metadata.description: Shows the number of prison inmates entering and leaving custody by sex for 1912 to 1914, illustrating the flow of prisoners through the prison system.

metadata.description: Shows the number of prison inmates entered and left by sex for 1912 to 1914, giving the background to prison administration figures in Japan.

metadata.description: Lists the prison's revenue by year to March 1916, showing earnings from works, rental income, other receipts and extraordinary receipts.

metadata.description: Gives the ordinary expenditure of prisons by year to March 1915, covering officers' salaries, wages, inmates' expenses and totals.

metadata.description: Gives the number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, total area burnt and damage amount for 1911 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Total Numbers of Licensed Patent Medicines and Receipts, 1911–1913]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly totals of licensed patent medicines and receipts, illustrating the Toyama patent medicine trade discussed in the text.

metadata.title: [First and Second Time Figures, 1911–1913]
metadata.description: Shows first-time and second-time figures for 1911–1913, printed just before the section on the rate of mortality.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified
metadata.description: Lists the number of deaths from major diseases and their ratio per 1,000 deaths for 1908 to 1911, given to illustrate the mortality picture.

metadata.description: Gives yearly case and death counts for nine epidemic diseases, with the total for the remaining diseases, for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.description: Gives representative daily working hours, rest hours, monthly holidays and yearly working days for filature and spinning factories, as compiled by the Department of Agriculture and Commerce.

metadata.title: [Operatives at Government Works by Sex and Age, End of 1914]
metadata.description: Shows the number of male and female operatives at Government works at the end of 1914, split by age group, to support the discussion of treatment at Government factories.

metadata.title: Output of Books, 1911-1914
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of books in Japan from 1911 to 1914, split into original works, periodicals and translations, to illustrate the growth of publishing.

metadata.title: [Annual Average Sale of Books, 1910-14]
metadata.description: Gives the annual average value of book sales in each category for 1910-14, the figures used to compare per-capita book consumption with alcohol.

metadata.title: [Cases of Prohibition of Newspapers and Periodicals]
metadata.description: Cases of prohibition of publications or sales of newspapers and periodicals in 1913 and 1914, showing how often the censors acted against the press.

metadata.title: [Cases of Other Publications]

metadata.title: [Waterworks of Principal Cities]

metadata.title: [Gross Area of Arable Land in Japan Proper]

metadata.title: [Value of Manures Used in 1912]
metadata.description: The author lists the value of the various manures used in Japan in 1912, the figures being given in thousands of yen, after describing the shift in fertilizer use.

metadata.title: Barley and Wheat
metadata.caption: (Production in 1,000 oku)

metadata.title: [Cultivated Area of Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat, 1915]
metadata.description: Shows the 1915 cultivated area of barley, naked barley and wheat in paddy-field and upland farms, illustrating that the staple second crops are grown mainly on upland farms.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (Production in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Gives annual production of miscellaneous grains such as millets, buckwheat and maize for 1911 to 1914, discussed in the text on these crops grown in mountainous districts.

metadata.title: Beans, Sweet Potatoes and Potatoes
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000)

metadata.title: Other Minor Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kwan)
metadata.description: Production of other minor crops such as radish, carrot, burdock, konnyaku and ginger over 1912 to 1914, given in thousand kwan.

metadata.title: [Miscellaneous Agricultural Products, Continued]
metadata.description: A continued table listing yields of various minor crops and vegetables for 1912 to 1914, supplementing the agricultural statistics before the sericulture section.

metadata.title: [Sericultural Families, Mulberry Area and Cocoon Value]
metadata.description: Shows yearly sericultural families by rearing season, mulberry plantation area and total cocoon output value, illustrating the sericulture trends discussed in the surrounding text.

metadata.title: Number of Egg-Cards Hatched
metadata.description: Gives the number of silkworm egg-cards hatched each year by season and the resulting cocoon yield per card, with totals and averages.

metadata.title: Output of Cocoons
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Shows the annual output of normal, double, pierced and waste cocoons by season, with value and percentage shares of each grade.

metadata.title: Output of Raw Silk
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the annual output of raw silk and waste silk in kwan and yen, with totals, for 1911 to 1914.

metadata.title: [Silk Conditioning Returns]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly silk conditioning house returns at Yokohama for weighing, conditioning, boil-off and quality tests, 1912 to 1915.

metadata.title: [Direct Export of Raw Silk by Japanese and Foreign Merchants]
metadata.description: Compares bales of raw silk exported directly by Japanese and foreign firms, with the percentage share of each, for 1912 to 1915.

metadata.title: [Raw Silk Export Destinations]
metadata.description: Lists the destinations of Japanese direct raw silk exports, with quantity and value for 1913 to 1915.

metadata.title: Area of Tea Plantations and Number of Tea Manufacturers
metadata.description: Shows that tea plantation area and the number of tea manufacturers stayed roughly stationary from 1911 to 1914, illustrating the article's point that the industry has remained stagnant.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Teas (kwan)
metadata.description: Gives the annual output in kwan of the different grades of green, black and oolong tea from 1912 to 1915, showing the trend in tea production described in the text.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1914)
metadata.description: Shows the leading tea-producing prefectures in 1914, with their output in kwan and value in yen.

metadata.title: [Tea Exports by Quantity and Value, 1910–1915]
metadata.description: Gives the quantity and value of Japanese tea exported each year from 1910 to 1915.

metadata.title: [Destinations of Tea Exported]
metadata.description: Shows the value of tea exports from 1912 to 1915 by destination country or region, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Number of Horses in Japan
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly number of horses in Japan from 1912 to 1914, split into native, cross-bred and foreign stock, following the discussion of horse breeding and improvement.

metadata.title: Number of Stallions in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the number of stallions in Japan by breed type (native, cross, foreign) and total for 1912 to 1914, under the horse heading.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the number of cattle in Japan by native, cross and foreign breeds, with totals, calving and deaths for 1912 to 1914, as the native breed declines.

metadata.title: Number of Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Gives the number of sheep, goats and swine in Japan for 1912 to 1914, showing livestock numbers for the stock-farming section.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Shows the number of animals slaughtered in Japan by kind (horses, cattle, horses, sheep and goats, swine) for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: Leading Stock Farms
metadata.description: Lists the leading government and private stock farms in Japan with their location, kinds of stock and ownership.

metadata.title: Number of Families Keeping Poultry (in 1,000)
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of families keeping poultry and the fowls, chickens and eggs produced with their values, for each year from 1912 to 1915.

metadata.title: Leading Dairy Districts (1914)
metadata.description: Lists the number of dairy farms, milk cows, and milk output in koku and yen for leading dairy districts in 1914, with yearly totals, in the dairy section.

metadata.title: Output of Fruits (in 1,000)
metadata.description: The horticulture section notes the growing importance of fruit-culture, and this table gives the number of fruit trees and the yield of each fruit for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.description: The table gives the relative percentage of sedimentary and igneous rock strata existing in Japan, classified by geological period, as introduced by the sentence on strata classification.

metadata.title: Mineral Production
metadata.description: The table gives Japan Proper's principal mineral production by quantity and value for 1911–1914, introducing the detailed notes on gold that follow.

metadata.title: Principal Metal Mines and the Production
metadata.caption: (figures in unit of 1,000)

metadata.title: [Output of Principal Mines by Metal, 1914]
metadata.description: Shows the 1914 output of gold, silver, copper and total metals and ores at Japan's principal mines, grouped by island and district.

metadata.title: [Iron Mines Output, 1914]
metadata.description: Gives the 1914 output of pig iron, steel and iron ore from Kamaishi and Senninyama, the two principal iron mines.

metadata.description: The petroleum output of the district is classified by oil type for the years 1912 to 1914, showing the growth of each class.

metadata.title: [Output of Principal Mining Companies]

metadata.title: [Mine-Workers Classified by Mines, Age and Sex, End of June 1914]

metadata.description: Records the number of mine accidents and the resulting deaths and casualties (severely and slightly wounded) for each year from 1911 to 1914.

metadata.title: [Applications for Prospecting, Extraction and Sand-Mineral Digging, 1913-1915]

metadata.title: [Fishing-Boats by Type, 1913 and 1914]

metadata.description: Lists the six leading gas companies in 1915 with their paid-up capital, receipts, expenditure and latest dividend, to show the industry's leading works.

metadata.description: Shows how the national population was divided between towns of different sizes and rural areas in the 1913 and 1912 counts, by number of towns, population and percentage.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Summarises the number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, building area affected and the amount of damage for 1912 to 1914.

metadata.title: [Hospitals, Practitioners, Dispensers, Midwives and Nurses, 1911-1914]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of hospitals, medical practitioners, dispensers, midwives and nurses from 1911 to 1914, supporting the text's point that dispensers still fall short of requirement.

metadata.title: [Licensed Patent Medicines and Receipts, 1912-1914]
metadata.description: Gives statistics of licensed patent medicines and receipts, with medicine tax and revenue stamps, for Japan from 1912 to 1914, illustrating the Toyama patent medicine trade.

metadata.title: Vaccination
metadata.description: Shows the number of vaccination cases dealt with for first and second time in 1912 to 1914, under Japan's compulsory vaccination system.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified
metadata.description: Gives the total number of cases and the relative ratio per 1,000 deaths for the principal diseases, from 1908 to 1912, the latest figures obtainable.

metadata.title: Nine Epidemic Diseases and Mortality
metadata.description: Presents cases and deaths from nine epidemic diseases for 1912 to 1914, with a combined total for the other three diseases, illustrating epidemic mortality.

metadata.title: [Number of Co-operative Societies in Japan by Type, 1913–1914]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of co-operative societies in Japan by type at December 1913 and 1914, showing steady growth in the movement since the 1900 law.

metadata.title: [Strikes Reported in Newspapers Since the Beginning of the Current Year]
metadata.description: The table lists notable labor disputes reported by newspapers since the start of the year, showing each strike's demanded wage increase, how it was settled, and its dates.

metadata.title: Data at the End of March 1915
metadata.description: Shows the mutual relief insurance data at the end of March 1915 for five Government establishments, covering societies, members, receipts, disbursements and persons helped.

metadata.title: [Mutual Relief Societies by Institution]
metadata.description: The table gives membership, persons helped and payments by type for each mutual relief society, such as the Printing, Monopoly, Government Railway, Naval Yard and Postal Savings societies.

metadata.title: [Index Numbers of Mechanics, Output and Spindles in Operation]
metadata.description: Index numbers over 1887–1910 show growth in mechanics, output and spindles, illustrating labor and productivity trends that support the discussion of spinning efficiency.

metadata.title: [Spinning Labor and Wages per 1000 Spindles, 1908]
metadata.description: Comparison of operatives needed per 1000 spindles and weekly wages in the U.S.A., England and Japan, showing Japanese spinning labor efficiency.

metadata.title: [Wages for Producing 10 Kwan of Yarn by Count]
metadata.caption: (1 kwan = 8.28 lb)
metadata.description: Shows the wage cost of producing 10 kwan of yarn for No. 16 and No. 32 counts in each country, supporting the claim that Japan's output is cheapest per capita.

metadata.title: Wages Per Week in Yen
metadata.caption: (Maximum ‡ Minimum †)
metadata.description: Weekly wages of bricklayers, carpenters, painters, smiths and compositors in England and Germany, giving minimum and maximum rates for comparison with Japanese living-expense data.

metadata.title: [Wage and Living Cost Comparison by Country, continued]
metadata.description: A continuation table comparing wage and living-cost figures for France, Belgium, the U.S.A. and Japan, with its headers on the previous page.

metadata.title: Living Expense in 1903 per Day per Artisan
metadata.caption: (in sen)
metadata.description: Shows the daily living expenses in sen per artisan, broken down by category, for four monthly earnings brackets of the principal wage-earner in 1903.

metadata.title: Earning and Disbursement per Year per Artisan
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Compares the yearly earnings, disbursements and resulting balance per artisan in England, the U.S.A., Germany, France and Japan.

metadata.title: [Workers in Factories by Age and Sex]
metadata.description: Gives the number of male, female and total factory workers in Japan Proper by age group, from the 1914 inquiry of the Department of Agriculture and Commerce into factories employing five or more operatives.

metadata.title: [Child Operatives under 16 in Factories]
metadata.description: Shows how child operatives under 16 are distributed by sex and age group across the match, glass and filature factories, which employ the largest shares of them.

metadata.title: Working Hours and Days
metadata.description: Gives representative working hours, rest hours, monthly holidays and yearly working days for filature and spinning factories, compiled by the Department of Agriculture and Commerce.

metadata.title: [Male and Female Operatives at Government Works, End of 1914]
metadata.description: Gives the number of male and female operatives over and under 14 years of age at Government works at the end of 1914, illustrating the proportion of child workers.

metadata.title: Wages of Laborers
metadata.caption: Average Daily Wages (yen)
metadata.description: Lists average daily wages in yen for various laborers in 1913 and 1914, with a monthly figure for sake-brewers, to show labour remuneration.

metadata.title: Number of Operatives
metadata.description: Number of male and female operatives in factories employing not less than 10,000 people, classified by industry, as recorded for 1914.

metadata.title: Factories (Continued)
metadata.description: Continuation of the factory employment table, giving male, female and total workers in tea, miscellaneous and special-works factories with the grand total.

metadata.title: Families Owning More Than ¥500,000 Worth of Property by Locality, 1916
metadata.description: Distribution of the 2,201 Japanese plutocratic families owning over ¥500,000 in property, by locality, according to the Jiji.

metadata.title: Plutocratic Families Divided According to Profession
metadata.description: Breakdown of the 2,201 plutocratic families by profession, giving the relative numbers of peers, merchants, bankers, ship-owners and others.

metadata.title: Causes of Poverty
metadata.description: The Tokyo Municipal Poor Asylum examined 3,224 men over 41 years of age, from 1902 to 1909, and this table gives the number attributed to each cause of poverty.

metadata.title: Press Statistics
metadata.description: Police Bureau returns giving the number of dailies and periodicals existing at the end of each year, split by whether a deposit was made, for 1913 and 1914.

metadata.title: [Japanese Magazines and Periodicals with Prices and Publishers]
metadata.description: A list of Japanese periodicals in English and Japanese, giving each magazine's subject, price in sen and publisher, with a note on war-time price surcharges.

metadata.title: [Output of Books, 1911–1915]
metadata.description: Shows the number of books published each year from 1911 to 1915 by category, illustrating the growth of publishing output in Japan.

metadata.title: [Average Annual Sale of Textbooks, Magazines and General Publications, 1910–14]
metadata.description: Gives the annual average sales value of textbooks, magazines and general publications for 1910–14, showing the publishing business side.

metadata.title: Cases of Prohibition of Publication or Sale of Newspapers and Periodicals
metadata.description: Shows yearly counts of newspaper and periodical cases: prohibitions of sale and publication, suspensions, warnings and court cases, illustrating how closely the censors watched the press.

metadata.title: Cases of Other Publications
metadata.description: Lists censorship actions against books, magazines and almanacs in 1912–1915, including prohibitions on public order and morals grounds, showing the scope of non-newspaper censorship.

metadata.title: Prohibition of Sale of Foreign Books Imported
metadata.description: Gives the number of foreign books, by volume, whose sale was prohibited on public order or morals grounds in 1912–1915.

metadata.title: [Famous Wrestlers of Tokyo]
metadata.description: The text describes the sumo wrestling ranks and then lists the famous Tokyo wrestlers of the Western and Eastern camps with their birth years, weights and heights.

metadata.title: [Japanese Athletic Records Up to 1915]
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese athletic champions and their best records up to the 3rd grand meet held in Tokyo in 1915, as the text introduces.

metadata.title: [North Alps Peaks of the Japan Alps]
metadata.description: The list gives the heights in feet and nearest railway stations of the North Alps peaks, part of the Japan Alps described as a mountaineering region.

metadata.title: [Cost of River Works by Different Finances]
metadata.description: Shows how river control expenditure was funded, by Central Government, prefectures, districts, cities, villages and other bodies, over 1907–8 to 1911–12.

metadata.title: [Expenses on Roads and Bridges, 1906-7 to 1910-11]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly expenses on roads and bridges, by national treasury, prefectures, districts, cities, towns and villages and other bodies, for the last five fiscal years.

metadata.title: Principal Harbor-Works
metadata.description: The table lists the leading harbour improvement works, with their type of work, dates of beginning and completion, and expenditure, for the principal ports in Japan.

metadata.title: [Public Works Continued: Ports, Works and Expenditure]
metadata.description: Continuation of a list of public works at several ports, giving the works undertaken, their start and completion dates, and expenditure in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [Civil Engineering Expenses by Classification, 1906–1910]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly civil engineering expenditure by the national treasury on rivers, roads and bridges, and ports and harbours for the last five years, 1906 to 1910.

metadata.title: Damage from Floods and Other Calamities
metadata.description: The table shows damage over 1909–1913 from floods, tidal waves and typhoons, by devastated area, casualties, buildings, ships, damages and repair costs, as the text introduces.

metadata.title: [Waterworks of Principal Cities]
metadata.description: The table gives the waterworks statistics of the principal cities, covering construction cost, pipe length, houses supplied by private and public stopcocks, and receipts.

metadata.title: [Length of Telegraph and Telephone Lines, End of March 1913–1916]
metadata.description: The table gives the latest lengths of Japan's aerial, underground and submarine telegraph and telephone lines for 1913 to 1916, illustrating the growth of the country's communications network.

metadata.title: [Wireless Shore Stations Equipment]
metadata.description: Describes the nine shore wireless stations Japan operated besides Funabashi, listing each station's vibration metre settings, electric power and transmission range by day and night.

metadata.title: [Wireless Shore Stations (Continued)]
metadata.description: Continues the list of government wireless shore stations, giving vibration metre readings, electric power, spark type and transmission range in daytime and at night.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Apparatus
metadata.description: Shows the yearly growth of telephone subscribers and exchange and telephone apparatus, with the automatic exchange count, from 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: Inventions Relating to Wireless Telegraphy and Telephone
metadata.description: Lists Japanese patents for wireless telegraphy and telephone inventions, with the date each patent was issued and the inventor, illustrating the experts' work described in the preceding prose.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Offices
metadata.description: Gives the number of post and telegraph offices, post offices and totals at each end of March from 1913 to 1916, with the ratio of offices to area and population.

metadata.title: Ordinary Mail Matters
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of ordinary mail items by class, including frank and registered matter, for each year from 1912–13 to 1915–16, with the per-10,000-population rate.

metadata.title: Foreign Ordinary Mail Matters
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the volume of foreign ordinary mail matters sent and received by Japan each year, with growth rates and per-capita figures, for four fiscal years.

metadata.title: Telegrams
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the number of domestic, foreign despatched and foreign received telegrams, including those sent by wireless, with annual change and per-capita rates.

metadata.title: Parcels Transmitted
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of domestic and foreign parcels sent through the postal service each year, with the overall growth rate and per-capita figures.

metadata.title: Postal Savings Deposits
metadata.description: Shows the growth of postal savings accounts, depositors and deposit amounts at each year-end March, illustrating the steady rise in deposits noted in the text.

metadata.title: Domestic Money Orders
metadata.description: Gives the number and value of domestic money orders issued and paid in each year ended March, covering both postal and telegraphic money orders.

metadata.title: International Money Orders
metadata.description: Records the number and amount of international money orders issued and paid at each year-end March.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Receipts
metadata.description: Shows post and telegraph revenue by service (mails, parcels, orders, savings, telegrams, telephone) for each year ended March, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Service Expenses
metadata.description: Shows the annual operating expenses of the postal and telegraph services by branch, in thousands of yen, for each year ended March.

metadata.title: Parcel Post Rates
metadata.description: Gives the postage for parcels by weight band, inland and territorial, ordinary and registered, as the postal rates applied to parcel post within Japan and to Formosa, Saghalien, Korea and China.

metadata.title: [Postal Petty Orders Charges]
metadata.description: Shows the fees for Postal Petty Orders by amount band and the maximum remittance, as set out in the postal information on this page.

metadata.title: [Money Order Charges]
metadata.description: Lists the fees for Ordinary and Telegraphic money orders by remittance amount, with the maximum remittance each allows.

metadata.title: International Telegraph Rates
metadata.caption: The rates for telegrams per word to places abroad are as follows (subject to alteration):
metadata.description: Gives the per-word telegram rates via Shanghai to Asian destinations, shown as the foreign telegraph tariff for places abroad.

metadata.title: [Telegram Rates to Foreign Countries]
metadata.description: Gives the telegraph charges to foreign regions by route, Via Vladivostok, Via Europe or Via Shanghai, for the destinations listed in each region.

metadata.title: Foreign Parcels
metadata.caption: Cheapest-rate routes are given :—
metadata.description: Lists the cheapest parcel post routes and rates by weight to France and Germany, Austria-Hungary and British East Indies.

metadata.title: [International Money Orders — Asia]
metadata.description: Gives the maximum amounts and fees for international money orders payable in Asian places, showing ordinary, express and notice-for-payment charges.

metadata.title: [Telegraphic Money Order Rates by Country]
metadata.description: The table lists telegraphic money order limits, fees and related charges for countries in Asia, Oceania, the Americas and Africa, showing which destinations accept such orders.

metadata.title: [Rate of Profit from Railway Working, 1906–1916]
metadata.description: Introduced by the text on the rising profitability of government railways, this gives the annual rate of profit from railway working over the decade from 1906 to 1916.

metadata.title: General Statistics on Railways
metadata.description: Shows the growth of railway mileage by ownership and the state and private railway capital and reserves, 1911 to 1915, as background to the nationalization of private lines.

metadata.title: Financial Result of Nationalization
metadata.caption: (data fractions omitted)
metadata.description: Compares operating data of the nationalized railways between 1907–8, when nationalization was completed, and 1914–5, showing the increase in mileage, stock and capacity.

metadata.title: [Passenger Mileage and Goods Tonnage]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of railway passenger mileage and goods tonnage between 1907–8 and 1914–15, the background to the fare and receipts figures that follow.

metadata.title: [Passenger and Goods Receipts with Average Fare per Mile]
metadata.description: Gives passenger and goods receipts and the average fare per mile for the two periods, showing the fall in passenger fares and the goods rate.

metadata.title: [Railway Receipts and Disbursements, 1916–7 and 1908–9]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Compares the total receipts and disbursements of the railways in 1916–7 with those of 1908–9, the later figures being estimates.

metadata.title: [Consolidated Capital, Loans, Reserves and Profit]
metadata.description: Shows the consolidated capital, loans, reserves and net earnings of the railways over four periods, with the rate of profit on the consolidated fund minus loans.

metadata.title: [Imperial Railway Districts and Open Mileage]
metadata.description: Lists the five district offices of the Imperial Railways, where each is situated, and the open mileage in 1916 and 1915.

metadata.title: Main Lines and Mileage under Traffic at End of Mar. 1915
metadata.description: Gives the principal Japanese railway lines and their open mileage at the end of March 1915, with a note on mileage newly opened in the preceding years.

metadata.title: Railway Capital
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the Imperial railway capital and the construction, improvement and additional expenses settled in each fiscal year from 1913 to 1916, illustrating the railway finance account.

metadata.title: Traffic Mileage
metadata.description: Shows the average working mileage and the passenger and ton mileage of the railways for each year ended March, 1911 to 1915.

metadata.title: Traffic Receipts and Expenses
metadata.description: Gives yearly receipts, expenses and net profits of the railways in thousands of yen, with the same figures expressed per day per mile.

metadata.title: Traffic Receipts Classified
metadata.description: Breaks down the total railway traffic receipts for each year into passenger, goods and sundries receipts.

metadata.title: Operating Expenses Classified
metadata.description: Shows the railway operating expenses split into general, maintenance and transportation costs for the years 1911 to 1914.

metadata.title: Average Traffic Receipts and Working Expenses per Mile per Day
metadata.description: Gives average daily receipts and working expenses per mile of railway for 1913 and 1914, broken down by source and expense type.

metadata.title: Number of Passenger Cars
metadata.description: Lists the number of bogie and four-wheeled passenger cars in service, with totals and average seating capacity, for 1910–1914.

metadata.title: Passenger Traffic Fares
metadata.description: Shows total passenger fare receipts by class of accommodation for 1910–1914, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Ratio of Passenger Traffic Fares per 1,000
metadata.description: Gives the share of passenger fare receipts contributed by each class, expressed per 1,000 of total fares, for 1910–1914.

metadata.title: Number of Passengers
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the number of passengers carried in each class and in total for 1910–1914, in thousands.

metadata.title: Ratio of Passengers per 1,000
metadata.description: Gives the share of passengers per 1,000 travelling in each class on the railways for each year ended March.

metadata.title: Principal Goods Hauled by State Lines
metadata.description: Lists the tonnage of the principal goods items hauled by the State lines during the year ended March 1914, as examples of goods traffic.

metadata.title: Goods Traffic Rates
metadata.description: Shows the revenue from goods traffic rates by service type (ordinary, express, carload) for each year ended March.

metadata.title: Number of Goods Wagons
metadata.description: Counts the goods wagons in service by type each year, with total wagons and the loading capacity per mile of line.

metadata.title: Tonnage of Goods
metadata.description: Records the tonnage of goods carried by ordinary, express and carload service for each year ended March, with totals.

metadata.title: Number of Locomotives at the End of Jan. 1914
metadata.description: The table gives the number and proportion of locomotives in service by builder country and by type (saturated, superheater, electric), noting that home-made engines came from Kawasaki Dockyard or Osaka Railway Car Co.

metadata.title: Weight of Locomotives in Working Order at the End of Jan. 1914
metadata.description: Shows the weight of locomotives in working order at the end of January 1914, by country of build and by boiler type, with proportions of each.

metadata.title: Domestic and Foreign Orders and Their Percentage
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the estimated value of materials bought by the Government Railways from 1906 to 1913, split between domestic supply and foreign supply, with the foreign share as a percentage.

metadata.title: [Freight Schedule for Through Transportation of Raw Silk]
metadata.caption: (Per 100 kgrms)
metadata.description: Shows the freight charges per 100 kilograms for raw silk shipped by the through transportation service from Yokohama, Kyoto and Tsuruga to Moscow, from June 1914.

metadata.title: [Private Railways in Operation]
metadata.description: Lists the private railway companies in operation with their offices, line lengths, track mileage, gauge and paid-up capital.

metadata.title: Passenger and Goods Traffic of Private Railways
metadata.description: Shows yearly passenger and goods traffic figures (numbers, mileage, fares, tonnage, freights) of private railways for the years ended March 1911 to 1915.

metadata.title: Finance of Private Railways
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly financial position of private railways for the years ended March 1911 to 1915: capital, reserves, receipts, expenses and profit.

metadata.title: Leading Light Railways in Japan
metadata.description: A list of the leading light railway companies in Japan, giving each line's office, length, track mileage, gauge and paid-up capital.

metadata.title: [Electric Tramways Financial Summary, Year Ended March 1915]
metadata.description: Summarises the electric tramway companies and municipalities in Japan at March 1915, by type of operation, with capital, receipts, expenditure and profit.

metadata.title: Leading Electric Tramway Enterprises
metadata.description: Lists the leading electric tramway enterprises with their paid-up capital, railway and track mileage and gauge, following the national summary.

metadata.title: [Electric Railways and Tramways in Japan]
metadata.description: This list gives each electric railway and tramway company with its paid-up capital, railway and track mileage, and gauge, showing the scale of urban and interurban lines in Japan.

metadata.title: Number of Registered Vessels Classified by Tonnage
metadata.description: Shows the number and gross tonnage of registered steamers and sailing vessels by size class for each December from 1912 to 1916, illustrating growth of Japan's mercantile marine.

metadata.title: Registered Steamers Classified by Age (1914)
metadata.description: Gives the number and tonnage of registered steamers in 1914 broken down by age of vessel and by construction material (steel or iron, steel-wood or iron-wood, wood), with home-built and foreign totals.

metadata.title: Registered Steamers Classified by Materials (1914)
metadata.description: The table shows the registered steamers in 1914 broken down by hull material and tonnage class, with number and gross tonnage for each category.

metadata.title: Steamers Classified by Speed (1914)
metadata.description: The table gives the 1914 steamer fleet by speed in knots, with number of vessels and tonnage for each speed band.

metadata.title: Purchase and Sale of Second-Hand Boats
metadata.caption: (Ships of over 1000 tons gross)
metadata.description: The table shows the number and gross tonnage of second-hand foreign steamers imported and exported by Japan from 1912 to 1916, reflecting the reversal after the war.

metadata.title: [Oversea Services Run and Steamers Used Under the Law]
metadata.description: The table lists the subsidised oversea services, their steamer numbers, tonnage, speeds and yearly sailings under the Navigation Encouragement law.

metadata.title: [Subsidy Amounts Under the New Contracts, 1915–1920]
metadata.description: The table gives the subsidy amounts payable to each oversea service under the new five-year contracts approved by the Diet in May 1915.

metadata.title: Coasting and Near-Sea Service Subsidy
metadata.description: Lists the coasting and near-sea service subsidies for 1916, showing each route, its termini, the company operating it and the amount granted.

metadata.title: [Vessels of Non-Subsidized Owners above 1000 Gross Tons by Route, End of November 1916]
metadata.description: The table compares the 127 non-subsidized vessels above 1000 gross tons by trade route at the end of November 1916, showing how far their sphere of activity has extended.

metadata.title: [More Influential Tramp Owners at End of November 1916]
metadata.description: The page lists the approximate fleets of the more influential tramp owners at the end of November 1916, giving vessel numbers and gross tonnage for each.

metadata.title: Freight Market, Near-Sea Service
metadata.description: Monthly average freight per ton of coal from Moji (or Wakamatsu) to Yokohama, and near-sea and open-sea charter rates, for 1915 and 1916, illustrating the wartime freight boom.

metadata.title: Average Rates Between Moji and Yokohama Since 1909
metadata.description: Yearly average freight rates between Moji and Yokohama from 1909 to 1916, given as a summary after the monthly figures.

metadata.title: [Freight Rates on Exports to Europe]
metadata.description: Shows the freight rates the subsidized N.Y.K. and other Japanese companies charge against foreign companies for major export commodities shipped to Europe, to illustrate that Japanese rates are lower.

metadata.title: America (Export)
metadata.description: Lists the freight rates charged by Japanese and foreign companies for export cargoes shipped to America, showing the comparison of rates per unit.

metadata.title: America (Import)
metadata.description: Lists the freight rates charged by Japanese and foreign companies for import cargoes carried from America, continuing the comparison of oversea freight rates.

metadata.title: Vessels under Charter to Foreigners
metadata.description: Shows the monthly number of Japanese steamers and their gross tonnage chartered to foreign shipping services in 1916, illustrating a remarkable increase.

metadata.title: [Result of Shipbuilding Industry, 1912–1916]
metadata.description: The table records the annual tonnage built by private shipyards over five years, with the share of vessels above 100 tons gross, showing industry growth since the War.

metadata.title: [Orders with Anticipated Completion in the Current Year]
metadata.description: The table lists the shipbuilding orders by yard, with number of vessels and gross tonnage, expected to be completed in the current year, according to the Department of Communications.

metadata.title: [Rates of Shipbuilding Bounty by Grade and Class]
metadata.description: The table gives the shipbuilding bounty amounts per grade for Class A and Class B vessels under the law amended to take effect in January 1910.

metadata.title: [Annual Values, 1912–1917]
metadata.description: Estimated annual figures for 1912 to 1917 are given at the head of the page, before the account of the principal shipyards.

metadata.title: [Licensed Captains and Mates at End of Year]
metadata.description: The numbers of licensed captains, mates and engineers, Japanese and foreign, at the end of each year from 1912 to 1914 are listed.

metadata.title: Shipwrecks
metadata.description: Shows the number of steamers, sailing ships and junks wrecked or damaged, and lives lost or injured in Japanese shipwrecks for 1912 to 1914, illustrating maritime safety.

metadata.title: Condition of Lights and Signals at the End of 1914
metadata.description: The table gives the number of lights, daymarks, fog signals and signal stations under government and public control at the end of 1914, as the text introduces the planned new lighthouses.

metadata.title: Business Returns of the Four Navigation Companies
metadata.caption: (Cargoes in 1,000 tons for N.Y.K., in 1,000 pieces for O.S.K.; Fleet in tons gross; capital, reserve and money items in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The table compares business returns of four shipping companies (N.Y.K., O.S.K., T.K.K., N.K.K.) for half-year periods in 1915-16, covering cargoes, fleet, capital, receipts, expenditure, profit and dividends.

metadata.title: Fee for Extension of the Period
metadata.description: Under the Patent Fee rules, this list gives the extra fees payable to extend the patent period over the first ten years.

metadata.title: Registration of Patent Right
metadata.description: The table gives the number of patent applications filed and patents granted over six fiscal years, 1911-12 to 1916-17, as introduced by the Patent Office statistics.

metadata.title: Registration of Designs
metadata.description: The table gives the number of design applications filed and designs registered over six fiscal years, 1911-12 to 1916-17, at the Patent Office.

metadata.title: Registration of Trade-Marks
metadata.description: The table gives the number of trade-mark applications filed and trade-marks registered over six fiscal years, 1911-12 to 1916-17, at the Patent Office.

metadata.title: Registration of Utility Models
metadata.description: The table gives the number of utility model applications filed and utility models registered over six fiscal years, 1911-12 to 1916-17, at the Patent Office.

metadata.title: [Life Insurance Policy Amounts, New Contracts, Dissolutions and Net Increase, 1912–1915]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows life insurance policy amounts and contract movements for 1912–1915, illustrating the growing share of dissolved contracts relative to new business.

metadata.title: [Ratios of New Contracts, Net Increase and Dissolved Contracts to Existing Policy Amount, 1912–1915]
metadata.description: Expresses the new contracts, net increase and dissolved contracts for 1912–1915 as percentages of policy amount at the beginning of each year, showing the declining trend.

metadata.title: [Mortality Rate of Assured in Japan and England per 100,000]
metadata.description: The text introduces Japanese and English mortality of assured persons, comparing per-100,000 case and death counts by age to show Japan's mortality differs from England's.

metadata.title: Rates in Tokyo, %
metadata.description: After the 1911 agreement among Tokyo and Kobe fire insurers, this table gives the minimum fire insurance premium rates in Tokyo by district class for wooden and fire-proof buildings.

metadata.title: Statistics on Domestic Insurance
metadata.description: Statistics of domestic insurance business by type (life, fire, marine, carriage, fidelity, engine and boiler, consumption), showing companies, capital, reserves, premiums, claims and policies for 1912–1916, accompanying the introductory note on fire companies entering marine insurance.

metadata.title: [Sickness, Accident and Automobile Insurance]
metadata.description: Shows the paid-up capital, reserves, premiums, claims and policies of sickness, accident and automobile insurance businesses for the years ended March 1915 and 1916.

metadata.title: Leading Insurance Companies
metadata.caption: Year ended March, 1916
metadata.description: Lists the leading insurance companies with their paid-up capital, reserves, policies and amounts for the year ended March 1916, by class of business.

metadata.title: Foreign Insurance in Japan
metadata.description: The table gives the number of foreign insurance companies, deposits with the Government, premiums, claims and policies for life, fire and marine business in Japan, 1913 to 1915.

metadata.title: [Deposit Account of the Tokyo Union Bankers at Middle March]
metadata.caption: (Figures in ¥1000)
metadata.description: The author notes that bankers have excess funds and little profitable lending, illustrated by the Tokyo Union Bankers' deposits, loans and cash on hand from 1913 to 1917.

metadata.title: [Average Rates of Interest in Tokyo]
metadata.description: Shows the average interest rates ruling in Tokyo for 1913–1917, illustrating that current rates were the lowest of these few years.

metadata.title: Banking Statistics
metadata.caption: (Amount of money in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of banks, branches, capital, reserves, deposits and debentures of each class of bank in Japan Proper for 1911 and 1912, illustrating the many small banks in the country.

metadata.title: [Bank Statistics by Class of Bank, 1913–1915]
metadata.description: The upper part of the table gives yearly figures for the Bank of Japan, special, ordinary and savings banks from 1913 to 1915, with totals for each year.

metadata.title: [Bank Loans, Bills Discounted, Deposits and Cash Account, 1911–1915]
metadata.description: The continued part gives balance of loans, bills discounted, deposits, bonds and shares owned, and cash account for each class of bank in 1911–1915.

metadata.title: Liabilities of Banks
metadata.caption: (Dec. 31st 1916; in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the liabilities side of the balance sheets of the Japanese banks at the end of 1916, with the 1915 totals for comparison.

metadata.title: Assets of Banks
metadata.caption: (Dec. 31st 1916; in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Presents the asset side of the balance sheets of the principal Japanese banks at the end of 1916, showing specie, loans, bills and securities held.

metadata.title: [Bank Balance Sheets of Banks by Type, Continued]
