metadata.description: Shows the average yield per tan of paddy field over successive five-year periods and in 1914, indicating rising productive power.

metadata.title: [Cropping Area of Paddy and Upland Fields, 1914-1915]
metadata.description: Shows how the cultivated paddy and upland area was divided between one-crop and two-crop systems in 1914 and 1915, in cho and as percentages.

metadata.title: Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.caption: Cattle and horses employed in tillage are returned as follows:—
metadata.description: Gives the number of draught horses and horned cattle used in tillage, and the area tilled by animal labor on paddy and upland fields, for 1912 to 1915.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.description: The table gives Japan's rice area, production, average yield, and export and import quantities and values for 1912 to 1916, with a normal yield for comparison.

metadata.title: [Yield per Tan of Rice Varieties]
metadata.description: The average output per tan at Government Experimental Farms shows the middle rice variety to be the most productive of the three main types.

metadata.title: [Area and Output of Rice by Kind, 1916]
metadata.description: The table shows the 1916 area, output and value of rice, split into ordinary, glutinous and upland kinds, as the text describes their respective output.

metadata.title: Barley and Wheat
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: The table gives annual production of barley, naked barley and wheat with totals and average yield per tan, for 1912 to 1916 against a normal yield.

metadata.title: [Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat Cultivation, 1916]
metadata.description: Shows the 1916 area under barley, naked barley and wheat, split between paddy-field and upland farms, to illustrate how these staple crops are grown.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Gives annual production of miscellaneous grains, such as millets, buckwheat and maize, from 1911 to 1915, which were grown in mountainous districts and used as food by poorer folk.

metadata.title: Beans, Potatoes and Sweet Potatoes
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000)
metadata.description: Records annual production of soy beans, red beans, horse beans, peas, sweet potatoes and potatoes from 1911 to 1915, showing the minor food crops grown in Japan.

metadata.title: Productions of Some Special Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual output of several special crops, such as leaf indigo, tobacco, cotton, hemp and rape-seed, for 1911 to 1915, with commentary on which crops are growing or declining.

metadata.title: Productions of Other Minor Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kwan)
metadata.description: Lists output of minor vegetables and other crops such as radish, carrot, burdock, konnyaku and ginger for 1912 to 1915, placed after the discussion of special crops.

metadata.title: Sericultural Households and Mulberry Plantation
metadata.description: Shows the number of sericultural households by rearing season and the area of mulberry plantation, 1911–1915, illustrating the state of silk-raising support.

metadata.title: Output of Cocoons
metadata.description: Gives the number of egg-cards hatched, cocoon output by grade and variety, and cocoons per egg-card with value, for 1911–1915, to show sericulture production.

metadata.title: Output of Raw Silk
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual output of raw silk, waste silk and their totals in kwan and yen, from 1912 to 1915, under the output heading.

metadata.title: [Silk Conditioning Returns at Yokohama]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly volume of silk weighed and conditioned at the Yokohama house, with boil-off and quality test counts, from 1913 to 1916.

metadata.title: [Direct Export of Raw Silk by Japanese and Foreign Firms]
metadata.description: Shows how many bales of raw silk were exported directly, split between Japanese and foreign firms, with percentage shares, for 1913 to 1916.

metadata.title: [Raw Silk Exports by Destination]
metadata.description: Lists raw silk export quantities and values by destination country for 1914 to 1916, showing where Japanese silk was shipped.

metadata.title: Area of Tea Plantations and Number of Tea Manufacturers
metadata.description: Shows the cultivated tea area and the number of tea manufacturers in 1912–1915, illustrating that the tea industry had remained largely stationary.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Teas (Kwan)
metadata.caption: (Kwan)
metadata.description: Gives annual output in kwan of each grade of green tea, black tea and oolong tea, with total output, for 1913–1916 to show the trend of the tea crop.

metadata.title: Number of Horses in Japan
metadata.description: Following its discussion of native horse breeds and breeding establishments, the text gives the number of horses in Japan for 1913 to 1915, by native, cross and foreign stock.

metadata.title: Number of Stallions in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of native, cross-bred, foreign and total stallions in Japan for 1913 to 1915, alongside the horse-breeding discussion.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle in Japan
metadata.description: Shows yearly cattle numbers in Japan by native, cross-bred and foreign breed, with totals, calvings and deaths for 1913 to 1915, as the text discusses the decline of native cattle.

metadata.title: Number of Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Gives the number of sheep, goats and swine in Japan for 1913 to 1915, showing livestock numbers over these years.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Shows the number of slaughterhouses and animals slaughtered in Japan from 1913 to 1915, by kind of animal.

metadata.title: Leading Stock Farms
metadata.description: Lists the leading stock farms in Japan, with their location, kinds of stock kept and ownership, mainly Hokkaido farms.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1915)
metadata.description: Shows the leading tea-producing districts in 1915 with their output in kwan and value in yen, listing six prefectures in two side-by-side columns.

metadata.title: Export of Tea
metadata.caption: (in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the quantities and values of tea exported, by kind, for 1914 to 1916, reported by the Customs Office as shipped mainly to North America.

metadata.title: Families Keeping Poultry and Output
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of families keeping poultry, the number of fowl and chickens, and the egg output and value for each year from 1913 to 1916.

metadata.title: Leading Dairy Districts
metadata.description: Lists the number of dairy farms, milk cows and milk output in koku and yen for the leading dairy districts in 1905, with yearly totals from 1912 to 1915.

metadata.title: [Outbreaks of Glanders, Farcy, Anthrax and Hydrophobia]
metadata.description: Records of outbreaks of animal diseases such as glanders, farcy, anthrax and hydrophobia, with animals affected and destroyed, shown to illustrate the losses to cattle owners and authorities.

metadata.title: Output of Fruits (in 1,000 kan)
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kan)
metadata.description: Shows the annual output of major fruits in Japan from 1912 to 1915, illustrating the growing importance of fruit-culture described in the text.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.caption: (Relative percentage)
metadata.description: Shows the relative percentage of Japan's sedimentary and igneous strata by geological age, introduced as the classification of the strata existing in Japan.

metadata.title: [Mineral Production, 1912–1915]
metadata.description: A summary of Japan's annual output and value of gold, silver, copper, lead, iron, sulphur, coal and other minerals for 1912–1915, given to introduce the mining section.

metadata.title: Demand of Pig Iron and Steel
metadata.description: Shows past and prospective consumption of pig-iron and steel in Japan, as estimated by the Economic Investigation Commission under the Okuma Ministry.

metadata.title: Production at Present and Prospective of Pig-iron and Steel Materials in Japan and China
metadata.description: Gives the present and expected output of pig-iron and steel materials in Japan Proper, Korea, Manchuria and China, by year, to show the growth in prospective production.

metadata.title: Annual Output at Leading Foundries in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Shows present and planned future annual output of pig-iron and steel materials at the leading foundries in Japan proper, given as a comparison after the note on Chinese works.

metadata.title: Principal Metal Mines
metadata.caption: (figures in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives 1915 production of the leading metal mines, each producing over ¥500,000 a year, by gold, silver and copper output and total value including other metals and ores.

metadata.title: [Iron Output of Kamaishi and Senninyama, 1915]
metadata.description: The text names Kamaishi and Senninyama in Iwate-ken as the two principal iron mines and gives their 1915 output of pig iron, steel and iron ores.

metadata.title: [Available Coal Resources by Districts]
metadata.description: Gives the roughly estimated available coal resources, in million tons, for Kyushu, Hokkaido and the other districts, from the Mining Bureau's investigation.

metadata.title: Output of the Chief Coal-Fields in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Lists the annual coal output in metric tons for 1915 and 1914 from the chief coal-fields of Japan Proper, with the operating company of each field, following the discussion of available resources.

metadata.title: Analysis of Coals from the Principal Coal-fields
metadata.description: The page gives chemical analyses of coals from the principal coal-fields, covering moisture, volatile matter, ash, sulphur, caking quality, specific gravity and calorific power.

metadata.title: [Oil Output in Echigo and Akita, 1914 and 1915]
metadata.description: Following the text on oil-field development, this table gives the crude oil output of the principal Echigo and Akita oil-fields for 1915 and 1914, with their leasing companies.

metadata.title: [Oil Production by Kind, 1912–1914]
metadata.caption: (Unit: koku)
metadata.description: The page gives the annual output of the various grades of petroleum in koku for 1912 to 1914, showing the growth of the domestic oil industry.

metadata.title: [Mining Companies and Paid-up Capital by Group, 1912–1915]
metadata.caption: (Capital paid up in ¥1000; groups: I Metal, II Coal, III Both combined, IV Petroleum, V All others)
metadata.description: The table traces the number of mining companies and their paid-up capital by business group over 1912 to 1915, with coal taking the largest share of investment.

metadata.title: Leading Concessionaires of Mines
metadata.caption: (Production in 1914 exceeding ¥1,000,000 in value or nearly so)
metadata.description: The page lists the concessionaires whose 1914 mine production was worth about ¥1,000,000 or more, broken down by metal, coal and petroleum.

metadata.title: [Output of Mining Companies, Continued]
metadata.description: This continued list gives the output of the largest mining companies by metal, coal, petroleum and total, ranking them from highest to lowest total.

metadata.title: [Mine-Workers by Type of Mine, Age and Sex, End of June 1915]
metadata.description: This table breaks down mine-workers at the end of June 1915 by the type of mine they work at, their age, and whether they work underground or above ground, by sex.

metadata.title: Accidents at the Mines
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of mine accidents and the resulting deaths and injuries (severe and slight) with totals, from 1911 to 1915.

metadata.title: Import and Export of Mineral Production
metadata.description: Shows Japan's exports of copper, coal and sulphur and imports of iron and steel and petroleum in mineral production, 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: [Mining Concessions Granted by Type]
metadata.description: Compares the number of mining concessions of each type granted in 1915 and 1916, with the percentage increase in 1916, to illustrate the mining boom during the war.

metadata.title: [Fishing-boats in Japan, 1915]
metadata.description: The page notes that fishing-boats number a little above 400,000, mostly Japanese open boats, and gives their 1915 breakdown by type of propulsion.

metadata.title: [Fishing Population, 1915]
metadata.description: The page gives the male, female and total fishing population for 1915, alongside the fishing-boat figures.

metadata.title: Accidents to Fishing Boats and Casualties to Fishermen (1915)
metadata.description: The page reports accidents to fishing boats in 1915, by fate of the boat, with the resulting killed, wounded and missing crew, compared with 1914 and 1913.

metadata.title: Catches and Marine Production
metadata.description: Shows the annual value of fish and sea-product catches and of marine products in yen for 1912 to 1915, giving the national totals for the chapter.

metadata.title: Principal Catches
metadata.description: Lists the quantity and value of the principal fish caught in 1914 and 1915, such as herring, sardine, bonito and tunny.

metadata.title: Principal Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the quantities and values of processed marine products such as dried squid, boiled prawns, dried bonito and manure fish in 1914 and 1915.

metadata.title: Marine Products, Canned Goods and Whale Oil
metadata.description: Summarises the principal marine products, canned goods and whale oil for 1914 to 1916, introduced with a note that canned crabs are especially prominent.

metadata.title: Aquiculture
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of aquaculture products, such as snapping-turtle, oyster, carp, eel and porphyra, for 1912 to 1915, alongside the Japanese pearl-oyster hatchery discussion.

metadata.title: Deep Sea Catches
metadata.description: The table gives the 1915 returns for deep-sea fishing in Japan Proper by gear type, showing vessels, crew and catch value, illustrating the sector's growth under the bounty arrangement.

metadata.title: Coral Collection by Prefecture, 1913
metadata.description: Lists the 1913 coral collection in the seas around Kyushu by prefecture, in thousands of yen, as the opening figures of the coral fishery account.

metadata.title: Coral Collection by Colours, 1913
metadata.description: Classifies the 1913 coral collection by colour (pink, red, white and others), giving the total value, and notes how much was exported.

metadata.title: [Area of Forests in Japan Proper by Class of Ownership]
metadata.description: Shows the forest area of Japan Proper at each end of March from 1912 to 1915 and at December 1915, split by ownership category, illustrating the decline in State forests.

metadata.title: [Prefectures Containing Not Less Than 500,000 Cho of Forests]
metadata.description: Lists the prefectures of Japan Proper, and Hokkaido, holding not less than 500,000 cho of forest at the end of December 1915, to show where the forests are concentrated.

metadata.title: [Forest Yield of Principal Timbers, Japan Proper, 1915]
metadata.description: The table gives the 1915 forest yield of principal timbers in Japan Proper, by quantity in koku and value in yen, showing forestry's still modest returns.

metadata.title: Financial Yield of Forests (Dec. 1915)
metadata.description: This table sets out the December 1915 financial yield of forests, split between timber and fagots by State, Crown, and public and private ownership.

metadata.title: [State Forests Receipts, Expenses and Balance, 1912-1916]
metadata.caption: (Excluding Hokkaido and the Bonin, in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives recent years' receipts, expenses and balance for State forests, showing profit is comparatively small because of accessibility and planting costs.

metadata.title: [Timber Progress in the Last Four Years]
metadata.description: Timber is the main forest export, and this table shows its yearly progress over 1913–1916 across four categories of timber products.

metadata.title: [Import Trade in Teak and Other Timber]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1000)
metadata.description: Teak imports have been gradually replaced by other timber such as pine, fir and cedar, and this table compares teak with other timber imports for 1913–1916.

metadata.title: [Working Plan Area Distribution of State Forests]
metadata.description: Up to March 1912 the working plan for 260 divisions was decided, and this shows the percentage breakdown of forest types and barren area based on data so far ascertained.

metadata.title: [Lifespan of Principal Trees]
metadata.description: Lists the approximate rotation periods in years for principal tree species, shown in the context of forest planting that is largely neglected on civic community land.

metadata.title: [Planting Effected in Forests]
metadata.description: Shows the area and number of trees planted by state, crown and other forests, with totals, for the years ended March 1913 to 1915, illustrating forest-planting progress.

metadata.title: Total Volume of Felling
metadata.caption: (in 1,000; koku)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly volume of timber and fagots felled from 1912 to 1915, showing the trend in forestry output discussed in the surrounding text.

metadata.title: Principal Bye Products
metadata.caption: (1915; in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the value in 1915 of the principal by-products of forestry, such as fungi, galls, fruits, barks and camphor leaves.

metadata.title: Output of Refined Camphor (Japan Proper)
metadata.description: Shows the annual output of refined camphor in Japan Proper for two years, illustrating the camphor supply discussed in the preceding text.

metadata.title: Number of Licenses Granted
metadata.description: Shows how many hunting licences of Class A (firearms) and Class B (other methods) were granted in each grade for 1914-15 and 1915-16, illustrating the shooting regulations discussed.

metadata.title: [Number of Companies, Paid-up Capital and Reserves of Industrial Enterprises, 1911-1915]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly growth from 1911 to 1915 in the number of industrial companies, their paid-up capital and reserves, introducing the discussion of investment in industrial enterprises.

metadata.title: [Industrial Companies by Kind]
metadata.description: The table lists the number of companies, paid-up capital and reserves for each kind of industrial activity, showing the scale of Japan's modern industries before the section on distribution of industries.

metadata.title: [Number of Companies and Capital by District]
metadata.description: Shows the number of companies and paid-up capital in each prefecture or district, with the largest concentrations in Tokyo, Osaka and Hyogo, as a regional survey of industry.

metadata.title: Factories and Employees
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of factories by type of power and the number of male and female operatives employed, from 1911 to 1915.

metadata.title: [Motive Powers Used in Factories, 1915]
metadata.description: Breaks down the factory motive power for 1915 by engine type, giving the number of engines and horse power for steam, gas, oil, motor and water wheels.

metadata.title: Principal Factories (at the End of 1915)
metadata.description: Lists the principal factories at the end of 1915 by industry, giving the number run by steam or manual power, horse power and employees for textile and machinery enterprises.

metadata.title: [Cotton Spinning Companies, Dec. 1910–1916]
metadata.description: Introduced as evidence of the industry's recent progress, the table gives the Spinner's Association's figures for companies, mills, capital, reserves, spindles and looms from 1910 to 1916.

metadata.title: [Output of Yarns, Export and Consumption]
metadata.description: Following the spinning statistics, this table shows yarn output, the portions exported and consumed at home, yarn turned to textile, and resulting textile output for successive years.

metadata.title: [Leading Cotton Spinning Companies, End of 1916]
metadata.description: Stating that the mills numbered 161 at the end of 1916, this table lists the leading companies with their mills, paid-up capital, reserve funds and spindle and loom counts.

metadata.title: [Hempen Spinning Statistics, 1911-1915]
metadata.description: Gives annual statistics for the hempen spinning industry from 1911 to 1915, covering mills, capital, spindles, raw material consumed and output.

metadata.title: Statistics of Textile Industry
metadata.description: Summarises the number of textile factories or families, looms, operatives and output of the textile industry for 1912 to 1915.

metadata.title: Output of Fabrics by Kind
metadata.description: Breaks down the annual output of textile fabrics by kind, from silk and cotton to woollen and miscellaneous fabrics, for 1912 to 1915.

metadata.title: Returns of Exported Fabrics
metadata.description: Shows the value of exported silk, cotton and woollen fabrics, with totals, for 1912 to 1915, and refers readers to the foreign trade chapter.

metadata.title: Production
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of production of potteries, shippo (enamel ware), fireproof and ordinary bricks, and tiles, 1912 to 1915, supporting the text on the ceramic and brick industries.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the export values of potteries and shippo for 1913 to 1916, showing the trade side of the ceramic industries described in the text.

metadata.title: [Portland Cement Production and Exports]
metadata.description: Presents Portland cement production and export figures for 1913 to 1916, illustrating the over-production problem and the revival of demand from the European war.

metadata.title: Production of Lacquer-Juice and Lacquered Wares
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output of lacquer-juice and lacquered wares from 1913 to 1915, following the text on the lacquer industry's centres and uses.

metadata.title: [Sake, Beer and Soy Production, Years Ended March 1913–1916]
metadata.description: Following the discussion of soy brewing, this table gives the output of sake, beer and soy in koku for the years ended March 1913 to 1916.

metadata.title: [Untitled Statistics Table (Companies and Production)]
metadata.description: A small statistical table at the top of the page, under a heading that is too degraded to read, presumably giving annual figures for a commodity.

metadata.title: [Leading Companies: Capital, Reserves, Expenditure and Dividends]
metadata.description: The text states the chief financial conditions of the companies mentioned, listed with capital, reserves, expenditure and dividend rates for comparison.

metadata.title: [Matches: Production, Sales, Exports and Value]
metadata.description: Shows annual production, value, exports and export value of Japanese matches, illustrating the sharp rise in value in 1915 due to higher prices.

metadata.title: [Match Exports by Destination in 1916]
metadata.caption: (1,000 gross)
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1916 match exports, totalling 41,321,000 gross, by the destinations to which they were distributed.

metadata.title: Paper Produced, Exported and Imported in 1915
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the 1915 production, export and import quantities and values of Japanese paper grades and pulp, illustrating the scale of the paper industry discussed in the text.

metadata.title: Export
metadata.description: Shows Japan's exports of sake, beer and soy from 1913 to 1916, the destinations of which are described in the note below.

metadata.title: [Latest Conditions of Leading Breweries]
metadata.description: Gives the latest paid-up capital, receipts, expenditure and dividend rate of the six leading breweries and sake companies named in the text.

metadata.title: [Match Production, Value and Exports, 1912–1915]
metadata.description: Shows Japanese match production and exports with their values for 1912 to 1915, illustrating the sudden rise in value in 1915.

metadata.title: [Match Exports by Destination, 1916]
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 gross)
metadata.description: Lists the 1916 match exports, totalling 41,321,000 gross, by the countries and places that received them.

metadata.title: Paper Production, Exports and Imports in 1915
metadata.caption: (in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives the 1915 output, exports and imports of paper types, showing the scale of the domestic paper trade and the role of pulp imports in the industry.

metadata.title: Soap Output and Foreign Trade, 1912–1915
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the output of toilet soaps and other soaps, plus foreign trade in soap, for 1912 to 1915, illustrating the growth of the Japanese soap industry.

metadata.title: [Artificial Fertilizers: Production by Origin]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of artificial fertilizers by origin, supporting the note that demand for chemical manures has grown markedly in Japan.

metadata.title: Fish-Oil Output
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output of sardine, herring and whale oil in koku and yen, with other oils and totals, shown after the note on the fish-oil industry.

metadata.title: [Representative Companies of Machine Construction]
metadata.description: Representative machine-construction companies are listed with their paid-up capital, receipts, expenditure and dividend rates, following the author's survey of the industry.

metadata.title: [Gas Lamps, Installations and Production]
metadata.description: Shows the relative proportion of gas used for lighting, heating and motor purposes, with gas volume produced, as electricity encroaches on the gas industry's lighting business.

metadata.title: [Gas Works, Paid-Up Capital and Pipe Extension]
metadata.description: Gives the number of gas works, paid-up capital and length of pipes laid, showing the situation of the gas industry, mostly under private enterprise, over four periods.

metadata.title: [Gas Companies in Japan]
metadata.description: Shows capital, receipts, expenditure and latest dividend of the major gas companies, illustrating the scale of the gas industry alongside the electric enterprises discussed below.

metadata.title: [Kilowatt in Operation of Electric Enterprises, 1910–1915]
metadata.description: Shows the growing kilowatt capacity in operation of electric enterprises by type of plant from 1910 to 1915, illustrating the rapid development of electric industry.

metadata.title: [Plants Under Construction, 1915]
metadata.description: Lists the electric plants still under construction at the end of 1915, by type, as a sequel to the operating figures.

metadata.title: [Hydro-electric Kilowatt Capacity by Status, End of 1915]
metadata.description: Breaks down the hydro-electric kilowatt capacity by supplying, railway, combined, isolated and government plants, distinguishing plants in operation from those in preparation at the end of 1915.

metadata.title: [Electric Power Undertakings by Kind of Power Supplied (Continued)]
metadata.description: Shows the installed electric power capacity of Japanese undertakings by kind of power source (steam, gas, other) and by type of supply, continuing the preceding table.

metadata.title: Latest Situation of the Leading Electric Companies
metadata.caption: (second half, 1916)
metadata.description: Lists the capital, receipts, expenditure and latest dividend of the leading electric companies in the second half of 1916.

metadata.title: [Sugar Production, Imports, Exports and Consumption in Japan Proper, 1911-1915]
metadata.description: Shows annual sugar production in Japan Proper, imports from abroad and Formosa, exports and consumption, illustrating the refining trade described in the surrounding text.

metadata.title: [Native and Imported Wheat as Stuff, and Production of Flour, 1911–1915]
metadata.description: Shows annual quantities and values of native and imported wheat used as stuff and the flour produced, giving background to the milling industry for 1911–1915.

metadata.title: [Peppermint Produced and Exported, 1912–1915]
metadata.caption: (Value ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of peppermint produced as crude, menthol and crystal oil, and the value exported, for 1912–1915, illustrating the growth of the peppermint trade in Hokkaido.

metadata.title: [Production and Exports, 1912–1915]
metadata.description: Shows the output of crude and refined product and the exports of this industry for 1912–1915, illustrating its recovery after an earlier decline.

metadata.title: Vegetable Oils Output
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the annual output value of various vegetable oils, from rape seed, sesame, yemola and cotton seed, with totals, for 1912–1915.

metadata.title: Dye-stuffs Import Returns
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kin)
metadata.description: Shows the falling imports of various dye-stuffs into Japan from 1914 to 1916, as domestic production of dyes grew after the European War began.

metadata.title: [Productions of Straw, Chip and Hemp Braid]
metadata.description: Shows yearly production values of straw, chip, mixed and hemp braid, presented to illustrate how the braid industry developed after the Russo-Japanese war.

metadata.title: [Exports of Straw, Chip and Hemp Braid]
metadata.description: Shows yearly export values of straw, chip and hemp braid, illustrating the marked progress of exports in a short time.

metadata.title: [Fancy Matting Production and Exports]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of fancy and ordinary matting and the export values of fancy and floor mats, illustrating the trade after the Kobe mat conditioning inspection was introduced.

metadata.title: [Leather Output Statistics]
metadata.description: Gives the annual value of leather output by source (cows and calves, horses, others) from 1912 to 1915, presented as statistics of leather output in the hides and leathers discussion.

metadata.title: [Hosiery Production]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Osaka-centred hosiery output by product for 1912 to 1915, illustrating the wartime boom in the industry.

metadata.title: Production (¥1.0000)
metadata.description: Gives the value of Japan's canned goods production by type for 1913 to 1915, to show the growing canning industry.

metadata.title: Exports (¥1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the export value of canned abalones, crabs, fish and vegetables for 1914 to 1916, showing the market expansion.

metadata.title: [Isinglass Production]
metadata.caption: Quantity in 1000 kin; Value in ¥1000
metadata.description: Gives the yearly quantity and value of Japanese isinglass (kanten) production for the years ended March 1913 to 1916.

metadata.title: [Working Budget Revenue and Expenditure]
metadata.description: Shows the working budget revenue and expenditure split into ordinary, extraordinary and total amounts, with the resulting surplus transferred to the reserve account.

metadata.title: Budget at 38th Session
metadata.description: Gives the budget as passed at the 38th session of the Diet, with revenue and expenditure in ordinary, extraordinary and total columns.

metadata.title: [Ordinary Revenue Items Cut Down]
metadata.description: Lists the principal ordinary revenue items reduced, which together account for the curtailment of ordinary revenue by ¥10,564,340.

metadata.title: [Principal Extraordinary Revenue Decreases]
metadata.description: Lists the main extraordinary revenue items that decreased, accounting for the drop of ¥51,158,480 in extraordinary revenues.

metadata.title: [Principal Ordinary Expenditure Reductions]
metadata.description: Lists the larger ordinary expenditure items cut, which together form the reduction of ¥44,505,561 in ordinary expenditure.

metadata.title: [Principal Extraordinary Expenditure Reductions]
metadata.description: Lists the main extraordinary expenditure reductions, which make up the reduction of ¥74,595,291 in extraordinary expenditure.

metadata.title: [New Outlays in the Working Budget]
metadata.description: Gives the new outlays in the working budget, split into ordinary and extraordinary amounts and their total, after the expenditure curtailment of ¥119,146,852.

metadata.title: The Working Budget and the Original Estimate — Revenues
metadata.caption: (In ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The page gives the working budget and original estimate of government revenues for 1916-17 and 1917-18, listing ordinary and extraordinary revenue items in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [Extraordinary Revenue (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues the revenue accounts, giving the closing extraordinary revenue items and grand total for the two years.

metadata.title: Expenditures
metadata.caption: (In ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows state expenditure for 1916–17 and 1917–18, split into ordinary and extraordinary items by department, with totals.

metadata.title: Growth of National Expenses
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Quinquennial returns showing State Expenditure (General Account) by main divisions, illustrating how national expenses grew from 1898 to 1917.

metadata.title: [Special Account Totals: Total, Disbursed, Allotment and Remaining]

metadata.title: [Schools, Instructors, Students and Graduates by Sex]

metadata.description: Gives yearly instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admission rates for the Tokyo, Hiroshima, Tokyo Women's and Nara Women's higher normal schools, 1912-13 to 1915-16.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Kyoto (Sept., '16-June, '17)

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Tohoku (Sept., '16-June, '17)
metadata.caption: Est'd, June 1607; President, Fukuhara, Ryojiro

metadata.caption: (Sept. '15–Jun. '16)

metadata.title: Average Age of Matriculation at Tokyo
metadata.description: Gives the average age of new students matriculated recently in each college of Tokyo University, for 1915–16 and 1914–15.

metadata.title: Profession of the University Graduates
metadata.description: Classifies the graduates of the Imperial Universities from their foundation to 1915–16 by their occupation or condition in life, for each university.

metadata.title: [Occupations and Status of Former Students of the Imperial Universities]
metadata.description: This continued table shows what former students of the Tokyo, Kyoto, Tohoku and Kyushu universities were doing by occupation or status, including those who died.

metadata.title: Total Number of Graduates from Inauguration till the Year 1915-6, Classified by Colleges
metadata.description: This table gives the cumulative number of graduates of each imperial university, from its founding to 1915-6, broken down by college.

metadata.title: [Doctors Living and Deceased by Faculty, October 1917]
metadata.description: Shows the number of doctorate titles conferred up to October 1917, living and deceased, by academic faculty, illustrating the nine kinds of title described above.

metadata.title: List Government Technical Schools (1916-17)
metadata.description: Lists the government technical schools in 1916-17 by type and place, with their directors and numbers of instructors, students and graduates.

metadata.title: A, B & C Grade Schools
metadata.description: Summarises the number of A, B and C grade technical and business schools, their teachers, pupils and graduates, public and private, for 1915 and 1916.

metadata.title: Kind of Schools (Including Branches) and Pupils in March 1916
metadata.description: Breaks down the A, B and C grade technical and business schools and their pupils in March 1916 by type of school.

metadata.description: The top of the page continues a table of enrolment by type of special school, with rows labelled A & B and C, from the preceding page.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Blind and Deaf-Mute Schools, 1916–17]
metadata.description: Gives the staff, pupil and graduate numbers of the two Tokyo government schools for the blind and for the deaf and dumb in 1916–17.

metadata.title: Public and Private B.D.D. Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of public and private blind, deaf and dumb schools with their teachers, pupils and graduates for 1914–15 and 1915–16.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Collegiate Institutions (1914-15)
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools, staff, students, graduates, applicants and admission rates of public and private collegiate institutions by subject, 1914-15, with a brace grouping agriculture, technical and commerce.

metadata.title: [Public and Private Collegiate Institutions: Name, Location, Founding Year and Subject Taught]
metadata.description: A list of public and private collegiate institutions giving each school's name, location, year founded and subject taught, complementing the statistics above.

metadata.title: [Number of Prize Recipients of the Imperial Academy, 1911-1917]
metadata.description: The Imperial Academy's prize recipients are listed year by year, split between the Emperor's prizes and the Academy's own prizes, to show how many were awarded.

metadata.title: [Loans, Bonds and Deposits at End of March]
metadata.description: Shows the loans, bonds, deposits and total sum existing for the education fund at the end of each March from 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: Fund for Giving Super-Stipends to Teachers
metadata.description: Describes the fund created in 1900-01 to pay additional allowances to common school teachers, showing State, provincial and interest contributions and totals by year.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of the Super-Stipend Fund]
metadata.description: Shows how the Super-Stipend Fund was disbursed each year, split between additional allowances to teachers and the amount carried forward to the next account.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid Out of Provincial and Communal Treasuries
metadata.description: Lists educational expenditure paid from provincial and communal treasuries by type of institution for the four years 1912-13 to 1915-16.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Health data of students in the Imperial Universities, High Schools and professional schools for three school years, covering constitution and eyesight, are given to illustrate school hygiene.

metadata.title: Health of Public and Private Schools of Secondary and Elementary Education — Boys, 1915-16
metadata.caption: The health returns of boys for 1915-16 year stand thus:—
metadata.description: Gives the 1915-16 health returns for boys across elementary, middle, normal, technical and special schools, with constitution and eyesight percentages.

metadata.title: Health of Public and Private Schools of Secondary and Elementary Education — Girls, 1915-16
metadata.caption: The data for girls for 1915-16 year are as follows:—
metadata.description: Gives the 1915-16 health returns for girls across elementary, girls' high, normal and special schools, with constitution and eyesight percentages.

metadata.title: [Height and Weight of Elementary School Children, 1915-16]
metadata.caption: The health data as regards height and weight of elementary school children for 1915-16 year are given below:—
metadata.description: Shows average height and weight by age for elementary school boys and girls in 1915-16, with numbers examined at each age.

metadata.title: The Imperial Library
metadata.description: Shows the volumes, opening days, and visitor numbers of the Imperial Library in Ueno Park for 1915 and 1916, illustrating its modest scale.

metadata.title: The Imperial University Libraries
metadata.description: Lists the number of Japanese, Chinese and European books stored at the end of March 1916 in each imperial university library.

metadata.title: Reading Record
metadata.description: Reading record of the libraries for the years ended March 1915 and 1916, showing library numbers, volumes, days open, visitors and daily visitors.

metadata.title: [Visitors to Museums and Zoological Garden]

metadata.title: [Ryugakusei Staying Abroad, 1913–1916]
metadata.description: The table gives yearly totals of Japanese ryugakusei (privately or officially funded students) staying abroad, with the subset sponsored by the Department of Education, to illustrate the scale of Japanese study overseas.

metadata.title: License for Secondary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of applications, licenses granted and percentage success for secondary school teachers' licenses, on examination and without examination, over five years.

metadata.title: License for Elementary School
metadata.description: Gives applications, licenses granted and success percentages for elementary school teachers' licenses, both on examination and without examination, for the years 1911-12 to 1915-16.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts at End of 1915
metadata.description: Shows the number of courts, judges and procurators at each level of the Japanese judicial system at the end of 1915.

metadata.title: Number of Civil Cases during 1915
metadata.description: Gives the number of civil cases handled in 1915 by each court level and kind of case, with the cases disposed of and remaining in hand.

metadata.title: Civil Cases Disposed Of
metadata.description: Shows, for each year from 1911 to 1915 and as an average, how first-instance civil cases were decided, withdrawn, reconciled or otherwise disposed of.

metadata.title: [Civil Cases Appealed, Complained Of and Demanding Revision]
metadata.description: Continuation of the statistics of civil appeals, complaints and cases demanding revision, showing yearly outcomes and remaining cases from 1911 to 1915.

metadata.title: Nature of Civil Cases Settled at 1st Instance
metadata.description: Shows the number and subject matter of civil cases settled at first instance each year from 1911 to 1915, with an average.

metadata.description: Gives yearly bankruptcy adjudications by type of business, cases remaining, credit amounts and rehabilitation outcomes from 1911 to 1915.

metadata.description: Reports yearly insolvency cases with numbers of debtors and creditors, credit amounts and rehabilitation outcomes from 1911 to 1915.

metadata.title: [Condition of Criminal Cases Handled, 1913–1915]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of criminal cases handled by each stage of procedure from 1913 to 1915, illustrating the court workload the author describes after the new code.

metadata.title: Sentence Carried Out
metadata.description: Shows the number of offenders sentenced in 1913–1915 by type of decision and punishment, with totals and rates per 100,000 population.

metadata.title: Number of Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of inmates held in Japanese prisons, police lock-ups and related places from 1911 to 1915, by category.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified, 1914
metadata.description: Lists the number of new convicts in 1914 by type of crime, with the total number of convicts sentenced.

metadata.title: Capital Punishment Classified
metadata.description: Gives the number of persons executed for murder, burglary and offences against the Imperial Court in each year from 1910 to 1915.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Ages
metadata.description: Shows the age distribution of new convicts for 1913 to 1915, grouped in age bands from under 18 to over 60.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Education
metadata.description: Breaks down new convicts for 1912 to 1915 by level of education, separately for men and women, with illiterate and unknown cases.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Property
metadata.description: Shows the number of new convicts each year, sorted by their property circumstances and by sex, which indicates the economic background of offenders.

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the yearly sickness and death figures among prison inmates, including sick rates and mortality per thousand inmates.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences and Ages
metadata.description: Breaks down prison admissions by number of previous offences, age group (juvenile or adult) and sex for 1913 to 1915.

metadata.title: Number of Prison-Inmates Entered
metadata.description: Records how many inmates entered prisons each year by new conviction, cancelled provisional release, recapture, and totals.

metadata.title: Number of Prison-Inmates Left
metadata.description: Shows how many inmates left prison each year by serving their term, amnesty, provisional release, death or escape.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-Officers and Prison-Inmates
metadata.caption: Dec. 31
metadata.description: Compares the number of prison officers with the inmate population, giving inmates per officer, male inmates per turnkey and female inmates per female keeper at year end.

metadata.title: Work of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the number of days worked by prison inmates, their wages and daily wage per head under government, contract and trust work, illustrating how little convicts earn.

metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly receipts of the prisons, split into ordinary receipts (labour earnings, property rental, other receipts) and extraordinary receipts, for 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prison (in yen)
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Lists the annual expenditure of prisons on officers' salaries, wages, inmate expenses and extraordinary items, with totals, for 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: Annual Earnings and Expenses per Prison-Inmate (in yen)
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows the average yearly income earned by each prison inmate and the ordinary, extraordinary and total expenses charged per inmate, for 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: Suicides and Acts Thereof
metadata.description: Shows the number of suicides by method for 1913 to 1915, split by male and female, with the totals for each year.

metadata.title: Principal Causes of Suicides
metadata.description: Lists the principal causes attributed to suicides, broken down by male and female for 1913 to 1915.

metadata.title: Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud

metadata.title: Principal Police Offences
metadata.description: Shows the number of principal police offences recorded in Japan for 1913 to 1915.

metadata.description: Breaks down the foundlings of 1915 by age, whether living or found dead and by sex, with totals compared to 1914 and 1913.

metadata.description: Shows yearly counts of hospitals, licensed practitioners, dispensers, midwives and nurses in Japan, illustrating that dispensers still fall far short of requirement.

metadata.title: [Licensed Patent Medicines and Receipts, 1913–1915]
metadata.description: Gives statistics of licensed patent medicines and receipts, including recipe counts, medicine tax and revenue stamps, presented to illustrate the Toyama patent medicine trade.

metadata.caption: Total number of cases and relative ratio per 1,000 deaths are as follows, these representing the latest figures obtainable

metadata.description: The table lists cases and deaths from nine epidemic diseases for 1913 to 1915, highlighting the most prominent infectious causes of mortality in Japan.

metadata.description: A Government delegate's answer in the 40th Diet session gave recent figures on the number of strikes, strikers and their outcomes, illustrating the rising labor disputes of the War period.

metadata.title: [Prohibition of Sale of Foreign Books Imported]
metadata.description: Gives the number of foreign books imported and prohibited for sale each year, by grounds of public order and public morals, with total volumes.

metadata.description: Summarises the financial position of private railways for 1912 to 1916: paid-up capital, reserves, receipts, expenses and profit.
