metadata.description: Summarises the company's business receipts and expenses by undertaking for the 1916-7 year, showing the profit earned overall.

metadata.title: Assets and Liabilities
metadata.description: Lists the principal asset and liability items of the company according to the same 1916-7 report, as given in the text.

metadata.title: [Disbursements by Japan to the Allies]
metadata.description: Recapitulates, in round figures, the financial support Japan extended to the Allies, giving the disbursements for Britain, Russia and France and the British account particulars.

metadata.title: Distance and Length
metadata.description: This page gives the Japanese units of distance and length with their English and metric equivalents, as a reference for readers of the Year Book.

metadata.title: Land Measures
metadata.description: This section lists Japanese land measures, from the square ri down to the tsubo and the Formosan ko, with English and metric equivalents.

metadata.title: Quantity, Capacity and Cubic Measures
metadata.description: This part gives the Japanese units of capacity and cubic measure, such as the koku, with their American and metric equivalents.

metadata.title: Weights
metadata.description: This section sets out the Japanese units of weight (kwan, kin, momme) with their avoirdupois, troy and metric equivalents.

metadata.title: Moneys
metadata.description: This final section gives the value of the yen in sterling, United States dollars, French francs and German marks.

metadata.title: [Coast Line, Area and Percentage of Area of Japanese Territory by Districts]
metadata.description: The table gives the coast line, area and share of total area for each part of the Japanese Empire, showing how the territory expanded after the wars with China and Russia.

metadata.title: [Principal Mountain Peaks Measuring above 8,000 Feet]
metadata.description: Lists the principal mountain peaks of Japan above 8,000 feet, with their heights, as part of the geographical description of the country.

metadata.title: [Principal Rivers with Navigable Length above 70 ri]
metadata.description: Gives the navigable lengths in ri of Japan's main rivers longer than 70 ri, under the description of the rivers of the country.

metadata.title: Harbors Open to Foreign Steamers
metadata.description: The page introduces the list of sixty harbours open to the call of foreign steamers, grouped by island or territory, following the discussion of coasts and bays.

metadata.title: Gales in 1917
metadata.description: The table lists, for fourteen observatories, the number of days gales visited each place in 1917 along with average and maximum gale speeds, illustrating the wind conditions described in the text.

metadata.title: Monthly Average Temperature in 1917
metadata.description: The monthly average temperatures for ten localities in 1917, with yearly averages and absolute maxima and minima, illustrate Japan's climatic range from subtropical Taihoku to cold Sapporo and Dairen.

metadata.title: Average Monthly Rainfalls and Snowfalls in 1917
metadata.description: Monthly and annual rainfall and snowfall figures for ten Japanese and Formosan-Manchurian stations in 1917, illustrating the climate discussed in the preceding geography notes on wet days.

metadata.title: [Number of Species Found in Japan]
metadata.description: The Fauna section gives approximate species counts for Japan's animal groups, with the species peculiar to or especially conspicuous in the country noted for mammals.

metadata.title: Species Existing in Japan
metadata.description: Under the Flora heading, the page gives approximate counts of Japan's flowering plants, ferns and seaweeds before describing the principal plants by zone.

metadata.title: List of Mikados in Alphabetical Order
metadata.description: An alphabetical list of the Mikados (emperors) with the years each reign began and ended, giving a quick reference to the sovereigns named in the outline of Japanese history.

metadata.title: [List of the Mikados and Their Reigns]
metadata.description: The list gives the reign dates of each Mikado in order, so readers can follow the succession of sovereigns from the legendary period onward.

metadata.title: List of the Shoguns and the Regents (Shikken)
metadata.description: This list gives the years of office of the Shoguns and of the Hōjō Regents (Shikken) grouped by family, showing the succession of military rulers in Japan.

metadata.title: List of Japanese "Year-Names"
metadata.description: A chronological list of Japanese year-names (nengō) with their Japanese characters and the Western years in which each was in use, arranged alphabetically by romanized name.

metadata.title: [Table of Japanese Era Names (Nengō) with Years]
metadata.description: A reference list of Japanese era names (nengō) with their Romanized and kanji forms and the years each era covered, given for chronological lookup.

metadata.title: [Japanese Era Names with Characters and Years]
metadata.description: This page lists Japanese era names (nengō) in romanization and characters with their starting and ending Christian years, arranged in four columns for reference in the historical outline.

metadata.title: [Japanese Era Names (Nengō) with Years]
metadata.description: A list of Japanese era names (nengō) with their Romanized and kanji forms and the years each period covered, given to show the chronology of reign periods.

metadata.title: [Principal Calamities Since the Tokugawa Shogunate]
metadata.description: The page lists the principal Japanese earthquakes and related disasters after the Tokugawa period began, giving date, place, houses damaged or destroyed, and deaths or injuries.

metadata.title: [Mineral Springs in Japan by Kind and Region]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of mineral springs by type and by region of Japan, based on Home Office investigations, showing how widely such springs occur across the country.

metadata.title: Population in Japan Proper — Returns "Legal" Population
metadata.description: Shows the legal population of Japan Proper by sex and total from 1908 to 1916, with annual increase and density per square ri, illustrating population growth.

metadata.title: Population by Ages and Sexes
metadata.caption: (Dec. 31, 1913)
metadata.description: Gives the population of Japan Proper in five-year age groups by sex at December 31, 1913, both as real numbers and as ratios per 100 population.

metadata.title: Married and Unmarried
metadata.description: Census returns of married and unmarried persons in Japan proper, compiled quinquennially from 1888, giving numbers by sex.

metadata.title: [Ratios of Married and Unmarried Numbers]
metadata.description: Ratios of the married and unmarried numbers per 100 population at each census date from 1888 to 1913.

metadata.title: [Births, Still-births, Deaths, Marriages and Divorces, Five-Year Averages]
metadata.description: Gives the number of births, still-births, deaths, marriages and divorces in Japan as averages for each five-year period from 1889 to 1913.

metadata.title: Ratios of These Numbers per 1,000 Population
metadata.description: Expresses the vital statistics of the preceding table as ratios per 1,000 of population for each five-year period.

metadata.title: Age of Marriages
metadata.description: Shows the number of men and women marrying in 1914 and 1916 by age group, with the 1914 ratios per 1,000 of each sex.

metadata.title: Birth-Rates
metadata.description: Gives the annual number of births by sex and the legitimate and illegitimate proportions from 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: Rates of Still-Births
metadata.description: Reports the total number of still-births from 1912 to 1916, with the sex ratio and legitimate/illegitimate and live/still-birth proportions.

metadata.title: Death-Rates (1916)
metadata.description: Shows deaths in 1916 by age group and sex, with the rate per 1,000 of each age group.

metadata.title: Population of the Prefectures
metadata.caption: (Dec. 31, 1916)
metadata.description: Lists each prefecture with its area in square ri and its population at 31 December 1916, split across two columns of the page.

metadata.title: Population in the Cities (Dec. 31, 1917)
metadata.description: Lists the population, number of households and average persons per household for each city as of 31 December 1917, showing city sizes across Japan.

metadata.title: Distribution of Urban and Rural Population
metadata.description: Shows the distribution of Japan's population between urban and rural areas in 1913 and 1912, by town size, giving the number of towns, population and percentage in each size class.

metadata.title: Japanese Residing Abroad
metadata.caption: Data at the end of June, 1917, classified in North America according to consular jurisdiction
metadata.description: A two-column return giving the number of Japanese residents abroad by district (males, females, total) at the end of June 1917, arranged by region under the Foreign Department's data.

metadata.title: [Japanese in Other Districts, Tsingtao and German Pacific Islands]
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese population in other districts, including the Tsingtao neighbourhood and occupied German Pacific islands, with a total figure for the districts.

metadata.title: Number of Passports Issued in 1916
metadata.description: Lists the number of passports issued to Japanese going abroad in 1916, by destination and sex, showing the scale of emigration by region.

metadata.title: Foreign Visitors to Japan
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign visitors to Japan by nationality in 1917 and 1918, set alongside the totals for the two years and the figures for 1915 and 1916.

metadata.title: [Persons Entering the Special Class by Marriage, Adoption, Naturalization and Rehabilitation, 1913–1916]
metadata.description: Shown at the head of the article, these small figures record how many people entered or left the special class each year through marriage, adoption, naturalization and rehabilitation, 1913–1916.

metadata.title: Holders of Decorations Granted (Dec. 31, 1916)
metadata.description: Shows the number of holders of each Japanese decoration order at the end of 1916, by order grade, with totals for each decoration.

metadata.title: Number of Peers, 1915–1916
metadata.description: Gives the number of Japanese peers of each rank at the end of 1915 and 1916, excluding Korean peers, as the section on the peerage is introduced.

metadata.title: [National Art Exhibition Submissions, Committee Exhibits and Selections]
metadata.description: Shows the works submitted to the national art exhibition from the 9th to 12th exhibitions, with the numbers chosen by the committee and by second-prize recipients, and the final selection.

metadata.title: Shrines and Priests
metadata.description: Gives the number of Shinto shrines by rank and of priests for 1916 and 1917, showing the organisation of the Shinto shrine system.

metadata.title: Buddhist Temples and Priests
metadata.caption: Based on the report of the Department of Education:—
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Buddhist temples by sect in 1915 and 1916, based on Department of Education returns, illustrating the scale of the Buddhist establishment described in the text.

metadata.title: [Priests by Sect, 1915–1916]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Buddhist priests in each sect for 1915 and 1916, illustrating the scale of the clergy alongside the discussion of Buddhist contribution collections.

metadata.title: Statistics of Christian Churches in Japan for 1917
metadata.description: Shows the 1917 membership, clergy, Sunday school and enrolment figures for each Christian body in Japan, with the Protestant Principal Creeds listed under Protestant and a grand total.

metadata.title: Relief Fund
metadata.description: Shows the yearly state of the prefectural Relief Fund, including local apportionments, proceeds, State aids, disbursements and the balance remaining, to illustrate the administration of charity.

metadata.title: [Outlay for Paupers, Foundlings and Sick Travellers]
metadata.description: Gives the number of recipients and the State and communal disbursements for paupers, foundlings and sick travellers in each year ended December, as outlay under the relief arrangements.

metadata.title: [Charitable Institutions and Relief Works at End of 1916]
metadata.description: The table gives the number, expenses, funds and persons received by charitable and relief institutions in Japan at the end of 1916, with the explanatory note on overlapping establishments.

metadata.title: [Inmates of Government and Private Leper Hospitals, 1919]
metadata.description: Lists the inmates of the five Government leper hospitals in 1919 by district, the total, and the private leper hospitals with their approximate inmate count.

metadata.title: General Statistics on Educational Institutions in Japan Proper for the Year 1916-7
metadata.description: The page's discussion of national education is followed by a statistical summary of elementary schools in Japan Proper for 1916-7, giving school numbers, staff, enrolment and graduates.

metadata.title: Foreign Instructors at the Institutions under Direct Control of the Department of Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign instructors by nationality at institutions under the Department of Education for 1915-16 and 1916-17, with their annual salary totals.

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age under Obligation to Attend School
metadata.description: Gives the number of school-age children obliged to attend school, split by whether they received the prescribed instruction, for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Percentage Attending School
metadata.description: Shows the percentage of children attending school in cities, towns, villages and on average, for 1912 and 1917.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers on Both Sexes in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of public elementary school teachers of both sexes, their monthly average salary and the numbers in the lowest and higher salary bands, 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: [School Fees Collected and Pupils Paying, 1914-15 to 1916-17]
metadata.description: Shows how many lower-grade schools collected fees and how their pupils were classed as paying, partly exempt or fully exempt in three successive school years.

metadata.title: Blind, Deaf and Dumb of School-Age
metadata.description: Gives the number of blind and deaf-mute children of school age, how many receive instruction at school, and the defective rate per 1,000 normal children.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens, End of March 1917]
metadata.description: Shows the number of kindergartens, conductors and children at the end of March 1917, with a comparison to March 1916 and the average children per conductor.

metadata.title: Graduates and Subsequent Careers
metadata.description: Reports the subsequent careers of public and private middle school graduates in the year after graduation, for 1915-16 and 1916-17.

metadata.title: Salaries and Official Status of Intermediate School Teachers
metadata.caption: Average salaries for teachers of intermediate grade schools
metadata.description: Gives average annual salaries of teachers at intermediate grade schools of several types in 1914 and 1915.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public and Private Girls' High Schools
metadata.caption: Number of girls attending the Girls' High Schools or Girls' Domestic High Schools for the year 1916-17
metadata.description: The table gives the number of girls attending public and private girls' high schools by course in 1916-17, along with the percentages leaving or unfinished.

metadata.title: List of the High Schools for the Year 1916-17
metadata.description: Shows the eight government high schools for 1916-17 with their directors, staff, students, graduates, applicants and admissions.

metadata.title: [Applicants and Admission to High Schools by Department]
metadata.description: Gives the number of applicants and the percentage admitted in each department of the high schools for three school years.

metadata.title: [Normal Schools by Type, Instructors, Students and Graduates]
metadata.description: Shows the number of normal schools by type and their male and female instructors, students and graduates for three school years.

metadata.title: Statistics of the Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: The page closes the Higher Normal Schools article with figures on instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admission rates for each school over 1914-15 to 1916-17.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Tokyo (Sept. '16-June '17)
metadata.caption: Est'ed April 1877; President, Yamakawa, Kenjiro, Baron, D. Sc.
metadata.description: Lists the colleges of the Imperial University of Tokyo with their deans, staff, student numbers and graduates for the 1916-17 academic year.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Kyoto (Sept. '16-June '17)
metadata.caption: Est'd, June 1897; President, Araki, Torasaburo, D.M.
metadata.description: Lists the colleges of the Imperial University of Kyoto with their deans, staff, student numbers and graduates for the 1916-17 academic year.

metadata.title: The Imperial University of Kyushu
metadata.caption: (Sept. '16-Jun. '17)
metadata.description: Lists the colleges of the Imperial University of Kyushu with their place, dean, staff, students and graduates for the academic year 1916-17.

metadata.title: Students in the University Halls
metadata.caption: (Sept. '16-Jun. '17)
metadata.description: Shows the number of students living in university halls at each Imperial University, broken down by subject of study, for the academic year 1916-17.

metadata.title: Average Age of Matriculation at Tokyo
metadata.description: Gives the average age of new students matriculated at the colleges of Tokyo Imperial University in 1915-16 and 1916-17, by college.

metadata.title: [Occupations of Graduates by University]
metadata.description: Shows the occupations of graduates of the Tokyo, Kyoto, Tohoku and Kyushu universities, giving only the relatively numerous occupations in life.

metadata.title: Total Number of Graduates from Foundation till the Year 1916-7, Classified by Colleges
metadata.description: Gives the cumulative number of graduates of each university by college from the foundation of the universities to 1916-7.

metadata.title: Academic Titles
metadata.description: Shows the number of living and deceased holders of the special academic title Hakase, granted by private and state universities, by field, as of October 1918.

metadata.title: List of Government Technical Schools (1916-17)
metadata.description: The page introduces government technical and special schools and lists the technical schools of 1916-17 by type, giving place, director, instructors, students and graduates.

metadata.title: Other Government Schools of Equal Standing (Sep., 1917)
metadata.description: Lists the other government schools of equal standing as of September 1917, giving each school's location, head, and three further figures, though the column headings are not printed.

metadata.title: A, B & C Grade Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of A, B and C grade technical and business schools, their teachers, pupils and graduates, public and private, for March 1915 and March 1916.

metadata.title: Kind of Schools (including Branches) and Pupils in March 1916
metadata.description: Gives the number of schools (including branches) and their pupils by type of school in March 1916, in categories A & B, C, A & C and C.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Blind School and Tokyo Deaf and Dumb School Staff, Pupils and Graduates, 1916-17]
metadata.description: Shows the staff, pupil numbers and graduates of the Tokyo Blind School and the Tokyo Deaf and Dumb School for the 1916-17 year.

metadata.title: Public and Private B.D.D. Schools
metadata.description: Compares the number of public and private blind, deaf and dumb schools, with their teachers, pupils and graduates, for 1915-16 and 1916-17.

metadata.title: Statistics of Govt., Public and Private Collegiate Institutions (1915-16)
metadata.description: Statistics of government, public and private collegiate institutions by specialty, showing schools, staff and students, offered as the first part of a list continued on the next page.

metadata.title: [Collegiate Institutions: Name, Location, Year Founded and Subject Taught]
metadata.description: A list of the collegiate institutions named in the text, giving each school's location, year of founding and subject taught.

metadata.title: [Private Schools and Universities: Location, Founding Date and Subjects Taught]
metadata.description: The list gives the private schools and universities of the period with their locations, founding years and subjects taught, followed by notes on several institutions.

metadata.title: The Educational Stock Fund
metadata.description: The table shows the year-end loans, bonds, deposits and total sum of the Educational Stock Fund, created from the Chinese indemnity to promote national education, for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: [Provincial and Communal Education Fund Receipts]
metadata.description: Receipts of the special education fund for each year from 1914-15 to 1916-17, showing the State, provincial, and interest sources with carried-over balances.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of the Special Education Fund]
metadata.description: Disbursements from the special education fund for 1914-15 to 1916-17, showing the additional teacher allowance and the amount carried forward.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid out of Provincial and Communal Treasuries
metadata.description: Annual educational expenditure paid from provincial and communal treasuries, broken down by type of school, from 1913-14 to 1916-17.

metadata.title: [Endowments by Single Donors, 1918-1919]
metadata.description: The page lists notable endowments by single donors announced in 1918 and 1919, showing each donor, the sum given, and its purpose.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: The page gives health data of male students in the Imperial Universities, High Schools and professional schools, by constitution and eyesight, for two school years.

metadata.title: Health Returns of Boys for the 1916-17 Year
metadata.description: Gives the health returns of boys in each type of school for 1916-17, covering pupil numbers, constitution and eyesight.

metadata.title: Health Returns of Girls for the 1916-17 Year
metadata.description: Gives the health returns of girls in each type of school for 1916-17, covering pupil numbers, constitution and eyesight.

metadata.title: Height and Weight of Elementary School Children, 1916-17
metadata.caption: Height in shaku, weight in kwan
metadata.description: Presents average height and weight of boys and girls in elementary schools by age for 1916-17, as the health data supplement to the school returns.

metadata.title: [Imperial Library Volumes, Days Open, and Visitors, 1916–1917]
metadata.description: The Ueno Park Imperial Library's holdings, opening days, and visitor numbers for 1916 and 1917 are given to show its modest scale compared with Western institutions.

metadata.title: [Volumes Stored in Imperial University Libraries at End of March 1917]
metadata.description: The number of volumes held by each Imperial University library at the end of March 1917 is listed, showing that the Tokyo library is the largest.

metadata.title: [Libraries — Number, Volumes, Days Open and Visitors]
metadata.description: Shows the number of libraries, their volumes, days open and visitors for the years ended March 1915 to 1917, as part of the education statistics.

metadata.title: [Visitors to Imperial Museums and Zoological Garden]
metadata.description: Gives the number of visitors to the Imperial museums at Tokyo, Kyoto and Nara, the zoological garden and the Tokyo Educational Museum for two periods.

metadata.title: Number of Ryugakusei Staying Abroad
metadata.description: Shows how many Japanese ryugakusei (students sent abroad, mostly to Europe and America) were staying overseas each year from 1913 to 1917, with the Education Department's share.

metadata.title: License for Secondary School Teachers
metadata.description: Shows applications, grants and success percentages for secondary school teacher licences, by examination and without examination, over three recent years, in a section on teacher and medical licensing.

metadata.title: [Costs of First Instance in Civil Procedure]
metadata.description: Shows the stamp duty payable on petitions in first-instance civil suits according to the value of the subject-matter, as the text explains costs are paid by adhesive stamps.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts at End of 1917
metadata.description: Shows how many courts of each grade existed and how many judges and procurators staffed them at the end of 1917.

metadata.title: Number of Civil Cases During 1917
metadata.description: Gives the number of civil cases handled in each court grade during 1917, with cases disposed of and cases still pending at year end.

metadata.title: Civil Cases Disposed Of
metadata.description: The table shows how civil cases were disposed of in each category (first instance, appeal, complaint, revision) for 1913–1917 with averages, indicating the volume and outcomes of the courts' civil work.

metadata.title: Natures of Civil Cases Settled at 1st Instance
metadata.description: The table breaks down civil cases settled at first instance by their nature (personal, buildings, money, cereals, goods, documents, others) for 1913–1917.

metadata.title: Cases of Bankruptcy and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: The table gives the number of bankruptcy cases adjudicated by type of business, cases remaining, credit amounts, and rehabilitation outcomes for 1913–1917.

metadata.title: Cases of Bankruptcy and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Yearly figures for bankruptcy cases, debtors, creditors, credit amounts and rehabilitation decisions from 1913 to 1917, with averages, showing the trend in insolvency proceedings.

metadata.title: [Criminal Cases Handled, 1915–1917]
metadata.description: Introduced by the text on the condition of criminal cases over three years, this table gives case numbers at each judicial stage for 1915 to 1917, with cases disposed of and cases still pending.

metadata.title: [Criminal Cases Tried and Disposed Of]
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal cases for complaint and trial, with cases disposed of and cases still in hand, for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Sentence Carried Out
metadata.description: Gives the number of offenders sentenced and the sentences carried out (capital punishment, imprisonment, fines) by type of decision, 1915 to 1917, with rate per 100,000 population.

metadata.title: Number of Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the number of prison inmates at December 31 for 1915 to 1917, broken down by prisons, police lock-ups, convicts, defendants, cells and infants.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified, 1917
metadata.description: Lists the 1917 new convicts by type of crime, with the total number of convicts at the foot of the right column.

metadata.title: Capital Punishment Classified
metadata.description: Gives the number of persons executed by capital punishment each year from 1912 to 1917, classified by the crime for which they were condemned.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Ages
metadata.description: Shows the age distribution of new convicts for 1915 to 1917, in age bands from under 18 to over 60, with yearly totals.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Education
metadata.description: Shows the educational attainment of new convicts by year and sex, from high school level down to illiterate, with unknown cases and totals.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified According to Property
metadata.description: Classifies new convicts by economic circumstances (property, small property, none, indigence) and sex for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the number of sick prison inmates, daily average of sick inmates, sick rate, and mortality figures for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences and Ages
metadata.caption: (New convicts for 1917)
metadata.description: Breaks down new convicts for 1917 by number of previous offences (first, second, third, sixth-plus time) and by age under or over 18.

metadata.title: Number of Prison-Inmates Entered
metadata.description: Shows the number of prison inmates admitted each year by reason of entry (new conviction, cancelled provisional release, recapture) and totals, by sex.

metadata.title: Number of Prison-Inmates Left
metadata.description: Shows how prison inmates left custody each year, by serving out the term, amnesty, provisional release, death, or escape, by sex.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-Officers and Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the staffing ratios in Japanese prisons, comparing officers and inmates, and inmates per turnkey and female keeper, for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Work of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the number of convict workers, their wages in yen, and daily wages per capita under government, contract and trust work for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Revenue of Prisons (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows annual prison revenue for the years ended March 1916 to 1918, split into ordinary receipts (labour earnings, property rental, other receipts) and extraordinary receipts.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prisons (in yen)
metadata.description: Records prison expenditure for the years ended March 1916 to 1918, covering ordinary items (officers' salaries, wages, inmate expenses) and extraordinary outlays.

metadata.title: Annual Earnings and Expenses per Prison-Inmate (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows the average annual income and expenses for each prison inmate, in yen, for the years ended March 1916 to 1918.

metadata.title: Suicides and Suicidal Acts
metadata.description: Shows the number of suicides and suicidal acts by method, male and female, for 1914 to 1916, illustrating the police statistics discussed in the surrounding text.

metadata.title: Principal Causes of Suicides
metadata.description: Lists the principal motives behind suicides by sex for 1914 to 1916, showing which causes were most frequent among men and women.

metadata.title: Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of houses, boats or persons that suffered from robbery, fraud and related offences in 1914 to 1916, as introduced by the preceding sentence.

metadata.title: Principal Police Offences
metadata.description: Lists the number of principal police offences recorded in each of the years 1914 to 1916, showing the scale of different crimes and violations handled by the police.

metadata.title: Unnatural Deaths
metadata.description: Gives the number of unnatural deaths by cause for 1914 to 1916, with accidental deaths (floods, shipwrecks, fires, mines, railways and similar) listed under the total.

metadata.title: Number of Foundlings
metadata.description: Shows the number of foundlings recorded each year from 1914 to 1916, divided into living and found dead, by sex, with overall totals.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of fires, houses destroyed or damaged, building area affected and the resulting damage amount from 1914 to 1916.

metadata.title: [Hospitals, Practitioners, Dispensers, Midwives and Nurses in Japan]
metadata.description: Gives the numbers of hospitals, licensed practitioners, dispensers, midwives and nurses at December of each year from 1914 to 1916, illustrating the shortage of dispensers.

metadata.title: [Licensed Patent Medicines and Receipts]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly totals of licensed patent medicine recipes, the medicine tax and the revenue stamps levied on them, to illustrate the regulation of patent medicines.

metadata.title: Deaths Classified
metadata.caption: Total number of cases and relative ratio per 10,000 population
metadata.description: Gives the number of deaths and the ratio per 10,000 population for the main causes of death in Japan for 1912, 1914 and 1916, the latest figures obtainable.

metadata.title: Nine Epidemic Mortality
metadata.description: The table gives annual case and death counts for nine epidemic diseases in Japan from 1915 to 1917, part of the public health discussion on this page.

metadata.title: [Co-operative Societies by Kind, 1916–1917]
metadata.description: Shows the number of co-operative societies of each kind in Japan at December 1916 and 1917, to illustrate the good progress the societies were making.

metadata.title: Mutual Aid Associations of Workmen in Five Government Establishments
metadata.description: Summarises the combined mutual aid figures for five Government establishments: membership, receipts, disbursements and persons helped.

metadata.title: Data of Mutual Aid Societies of the Five Establishments
metadata.description: Gives the membership, persons helped and payments by type for each of the five establishments' mutual aid societies, following the summary figures.

metadata.title: Living Expenses of Workpeople and Petty Salary Men
metadata.description: Prof. Iwano's 1916 survey of twenty labor families gives monthly living-expense figures by category, showing that no accurate Japanese data comparable to Europe and America exists.

metadata.title: [Cost of Living Compared, Feb. 1918 and June 1914]
metadata.description: Shows how the monthly cost of living for a family of four in Tokyo rose between June 1914 and February 1918, item by item, to illustrate the pinch on lower-paid officials.

metadata.title: [Workers at Factories by Age and Sex]
metadata.description: Gives the number of male and female factory workers in Japan Proper by age group, from the Department of Agriculture and Commerce inquiry at the end of 1917, supporting the discussion of female labour.

metadata.title: Child Operatives
metadata.description: Shows the number of child operatives under 15 in the main industries, by sex and by age group, illustrating where child labour was concentrated.

metadata.title: Working Hours and Days
metadata.description: Gives the working hours, rest hours, monthly holidays and yearly working days for representative lines of factory business, as compiled by the Department of Agriculture and Commerce.

metadata.title: [Workers at Tobacco Factories by Age and Sex at End of 1917]
metadata.description: Shows the number of child and adult workers by sex at the 63 tobacco factories, which employ the largest share of child workers, at the end of 1917.

metadata.title: Wages of Laborers
metadata.caption: Average Daily Wages (yen)
metadata.description: Lists average daily wages in yen for various skilled and unskilled occupations from 1914 to 1917, showing the wage level of laborers during the period.

metadata.title: Number of Operatives
metadata.description: Operatives in 1917 classified by their employments, based on the Department of Agriculture and Commerce factory statistics, showing male, female and total workers by factory type.

metadata.title: Families Owning Over ¥500,000 Worth of Property by Locality
metadata.description: Shows how the 2,201 plutocratic families of 1916, each owning over ¥500,000 in property, were distributed among prefectures, with the leading localities listed.

metadata.title: Families Owning Over ¥500,000 Worth of Property by Profession
metadata.description: Gives the relative numbers of the plutocratic families divided according to their profession.

metadata.title: Causes of Poverty
metadata.description: The Tokyo Municipal Poor Asylum's inquiry examined 3,224 men over 41 years of age to classify the causes of their poverty, listed by number of cases.

metadata.title: Data for Strikes
metadata.description: Summarises strike data for 1914 to 1918, giving cases, strikers, average strikers per case and strikers counted by days, to illustrate the wartime rise in labour disputes.

metadata.title: Average Number of Strikers Per Case, Classified by Occupations
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1914–1918 strikes by industry, showing the number of cases, strikers and average strikers per case for each occupation.

metadata.title: Strikes Classified by Result
metadata.description: Shows how the strikes of 1914–1918 ended, giving cases and strikers by outcome (compromise, demand accepted, withdrawn or refused) with yearly and grand totals.

metadata.title: Strikers Arrested Under the Peace Regulation
metadata.description: Shows how many strikers and strike cases were arrested under the Peace Regulation from 1914 to 1918, with outcomes, and explains the sharp rise in 1918 linked to the rice riots.

metadata.title: Female Teachers in Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of female teachers in elementary schools compared with male teachers for 1915–1917, illustrating women's role in the teaching profession.

metadata.title: Female Teachers in Girls, High Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of female teachers in girls' high schools for 1915–1917 with male teachers alongside, showing the much lower male proportion in these schools.

metadata.title: [Marriage Record of Alumni of the Tokyo Higher Women's School]
metadata.description: The table gives the marriage record of Tokyo Higher Women's School alumni by graduation period, showing that many graduates remained unmarried, supporting the argument that higher education affects women's marriage.

metadata.title: Press Statistics
metadata.description: The Police Bureau's returns give the number of dailies and periodicals existing at the end of 1916 and 1917, split by whether a deposit was paid.

metadata.title: Periodicals Published in Tokyo
metadata.caption: (Title in Italics = in English. m = monthly. w = weekly. f = fortnightly.)
metadata.description: This list gives the English-titled and Japanese periodicals published in Tokyo, with their subject, price per copy and publisher, as a guide to the city's press.

metadata.title: [Output of Books, 1913-1917]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of books in Japan from 1913 to 1917, split into original works, periodicals and translations, given to illustrate the publishing trade.

metadata.title: [Annual Average Sale of Publications, 1910-14]
metadata.description: The page reports the annual average sale of textbooks, magazines and general publications for 1910-14 and the resulting per capita figure compared with alcohol consumption.

metadata.title: Cases of Prohibition of Publication or Sale of Newspapers and Periodicals
metadata.description: The table lists yearly counts of censorship actions against newspapers and periodicals, including forbidden sales, suspensions, court cases and warnings, from 1913 to 1917.

metadata.title: Cases of Prohibition of Other Publications
metadata.description: The table gives yearly counts of censorship cases against books, magazines and almanacs, covering public order and morals grounds, from 1914 to 1917.

metadata.title: [Publications Forbidden Sale or Suppression, 1913-1916]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly number of publications banned or suppressed on public order and public morals grounds, with total volumes, illustrating the censors' work described in the text.

metadata.title: [Famous Wrestlers of Tokyo]
metadata.description: Lists the famous wrestlers of Tokyo in the eastern and western camps, with their birth year, weight in kwan and height in shaku.

metadata.title: The Athletic Record in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the best athletic records in Japan up to 1915, when the third grand meet was held in Tokyo, with the holder of each event.

metadata.title: [Japan Alps Peaks, Heights and Nearest Railway Stations]
metadata.description: The table lists the principal peaks of the Japan Alps grouped into North, Central and South Alps, with their heights in feet and the nearest railway stations for access.

metadata.title: [Cost of Works Undertaken by Different Finances, 1909–10 to 1913–14]
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Shows how the cost of river control works was borne by central government, prefectures, districts, cities, towns, villages and other bodies over five fiscal years.

metadata.title: Principal Harbor-Works
metadata.description: The text notes that many harbours have been improved since the 1890s; this table lists two leading harbour works under way, with their dates and costs.

metadata.title: [Classification of Flood Prevention Expenses, 1911–1913]
metadata.description: The table gives the classification of the flood-related public works expenses, by category, for the three years 1911 to 1913, introducing the figures for the total outlay mentioned in the preceding text.

metadata.title: Damage from Floods, Tidal Waves and Typhoons, 1912–1916
metadata.description: The table shows the area devastated, casualties, property damage and repair costs from floods, tidal waves and typhoons over the five years 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: Waterworks
metadata.description: Shows the cost, pipe length, houses served by private and public stopcocks, and total receipts of the principal municipal waterworks in Japan's major cities.

metadata.title: [Length of Telegraph and Telephone Lines at End of March]
metadata.description: Shows the latest lengths of aerial, underground and submarine telegraph and telephone lines in Japan for 1915 to 1918, given to illustrate the growth of the communications network.

metadata.title: [Wireless Shore Stations of Japan]
metadata.description: Lists the nine shore wireless stations of Japan with their vibration metre settings, electric power and transmission ranges, of which three are shown here.

metadata.title: [Wireless Shore Stations (Continued)]
metadata.description: Lists the wireless shore stations with their vibration metre, electric power, spark type and transmission distances in daytime and at night, with a note on planned expansion.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Apparatus
metadata.description: Shows the growth from 1914 to 1918 in telephone subscribers, exchange and telephone apparatus, and automatic apparatus, reflecting the excess demand for connections described in the text.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Offices
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of post and telegraph offices, with the area and population served per office, for 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: Ordinary Mail Matters (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the annual volume of ordinary domestic mail by class, total items, registered items and items per ten of population.

metadata.title: Foreign Ordinary Mail Matters (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Reports the number of foreign ordinary mail items transmitted and arrived, the growth rate and the per-100-population figure for 1914 to 1918.

metadata.title: Telegrams (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists domestic telegrams, charged and frank, with totals for each year and the portion sent by wireless.

metadata.title: Parcels Transmitted
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of domestic and foreign parcels transmitted through the postal service, with totals, increase rates and rates per ten of population.

metadata.title: Postal Savings Deposit
metadata.description: Shows the number of postal savings depositors, total deposit amounts, average deposit per depositor and refunded amounts at each end of March from 1916 to 1918.

metadata.title: [Postal Savings Deposits Classified by Occupation]
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Breaks down the postal savings depositors and their amounts in 1917 and 1918 by occupation: agriculturists, schoolchildren, tradepeople, and laborers and employers.

metadata.title: Domestic Money Orders
metadata.description: Shows the number and value of domestic postal money orders issued and paid at the end of March for three fiscal years, 1916 to 1918.

metadata.title: International Money Orders
metadata.description: Gives the number and amount of international money orders issued and paid at the end of March for 1916 to 1918.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Receipts
metadata.description: Shows the yearly receipts from ordinary mail, parcels, money orders, savings, telegrams and telephones, with totals, for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Service Expenses
metadata.description: Lists the yearly cost of running each postal and telegraph service, with totals, for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Parcel Post Rates
metadata.description: Gives the parcel post charges by weight for domestic and colonial parcels, ordinary and registered, under the rates revised from 15 April 1919.

metadata.title: Fees for Domestic Money Orders
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Lists the fees charged for postal petty, ordinary and telegraphic domestic money orders in force since January 1915, by amount remitted.

metadata.title: International Telegraph Rates
metadata.caption: Rates per word to places abroad (subject to alteration)
metadata.description: The table gives the international telegraph rates per word in yen for sending telegrams from Japan to places in Asia, Europe and North America, by route.

metadata.title: South America
metadata.description: Gives the telegraph rates to South American countries, by route, showing the cost per word via Europe or via Shanghai or Manila.

metadata.title: Oceania
metadata.description: Lists telegraph rates to Oceanian destinations, all routed via Shanghai, following the South America rates.

metadata.title: Cheapest-Rate Routes for Foreign Parcels
metadata.caption: Cheapest-rate routes are given:
metadata.description: Shows the cheapest-rate parcel post routes from Japan to various countries, with the rate in yen for each weight band.

metadata.title: [Parcel Post Rates to Foreign Countries]
metadata.description: Lists parcel post destinations abroad with the direct exchange routes and the postage rates by weight, in yen, for each country.

metadata.title: [Principal Countries for International Money Orders]
metadata.description: A summary list of principal countries on which money orders can be drawn, giving maximum amounts, fees, and the currency for the amount sent.

metadata.title: [Telegraphic Money Order Fees by Country]
metadata.description: The table lists the maximum amount and the fees for telegraphic money orders by country, with notes on express delivery and payment notice, and which countries cannot be drawn upon.

metadata.title: [Rates of Profit from Railway Working, 1913–14 to 1917–18]
metadata.description: The author gives the rate of profit from railway working for the last five fiscal years to show the returns on the nationalized railway system.

metadata.title: General Statistics on Railways
metadata.description: Shows the growth of Japan's open railway mileage by state, private and light railways from 1914 to 1918, with mileage per 100 square ri.

metadata.title: [State and Private Railway Capital and Profit, Years Ended March]
metadata.description: Gives the capital invested in state railways, their percentage profit on capital, and the capital and reserves of private railways open to traffic, by year ended March.

metadata.title: The Ten Year Result of the Nationalization
metadata.description: Compares railway operating figures in 1907-8, when nationalization was completed, with those of 1916-7 to review its results.

metadata.title: [Railway Operating Statistics, Year Ending March (Continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of the railway operating statistics for the years ending March 1906 and 1817, covering wagon, car and engine performance figures under state-run railways.

metadata.title: [Coaching and Goods Receipts Proportion, 1907-8 to 1916-17]
metadata.description: Shows that the proportion of coaching and goods receipts on the railways was reversed for the first time in 1916-1917, with goods overtaking passengers.

metadata.title: [Imperial Railways Districts and Open Mileage]
metadata.description: Lists the five administrative districts of the Imperial Railways with their district offices, locations and open mileage, showing the Board's organisation.

metadata.title: Main Lines and Mileage Under Traffic at End of Mar. 1918
metadata.description: Gives the principal lines of the Imperial Railways with their open mileage at the end of March 1918, which the text summarises as about 150 miles newly opened in 1917–18.

metadata.title: Disposition of Net Earnings
metadata.caption: (in ₮1,000)
metadata.description: Shows how net railway earnings for each year ended March from 1914 to 1918 were disposed of, across addition works, surveys, interest, subsidies and net profit.

metadata.title: Traffic Mileage
metadata.description: Shows average working mileage, passenger mileage and ton mileage of the railways for each year ended March from 1914 to 1918.

metadata.title: Traffic Receipts and Expenses
metadata.description: Gives yearly railway receipts, expenses and net profits in yen thousands, with receipts, expenses and profits per train mile, for the years ended March 1913 to 1918.

metadata.title: Traffic Receipts Classified
metadata.description: Breaks down railway traffic receipts into coaching and goods, with totals including sundries, for each year ended March 1914 to 1918.

metadata.title: Operating Expenses Classified
metadata.description: Itemises railway operating expenses (general, maintenance, coaching and transportation) in yen thousands for 1916 to 1918.

metadata.title: Ratio between Coaching & Goods Receipts
metadata.description: Shows the percentage share of coaching and goods in railway receipts for each year ended March from 1914 to 1918.

metadata.title: Railway Working and Shipping Receipts
metadata.description: Shows railway working and shipping receipts for 1915 to 1918, following the note on passenger fare increases.

metadata.title: Number of Passenger Cars
metadata.description: Gives the number and seating capacity of railway passenger cars by type, with average capacity per vehicle, for 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: Passenger Traffic Fares
metadata.description: Shows passenger fare receipts by class for 1915 to 1918, rising after the July 1918 fare increase.

metadata.title: Passenger Traffic
metadata.description: Gives the number of passengers carried, passenger-miles, year-on-year change and average journey lengths for 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: Ratio of Passengers per 1,000 by Class
metadata.description: Shows how many passengers per 1,000 travelled in each class of railway accommodation for 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: [Tonnage of Principal Commodities Carried]
metadata.description: A short list giving the tonnage of principal commodities carried by the railways, with the unit noted beside the first figure.

metadata.title: Goods Traffic Freight
metadata.description: Shows railway goods traffic freight receipts by category (ordinary, express, carload) and total for four fiscal years, 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: Number of Goods Wagons
metadata.description: Gives the number of covered and open goods wagons, their capacity and average figures per vehicle and per open mile for the years ending March 1914 to 1918.

metadata.title: Tonnage of Goods
metadata.caption: (1,000 tons)
metadata.description: Shows the tonnage of goods carried by piece, express and carload consignments and the total, for the years ended March 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: Aggregate Ton-mileage of Goods Hauled
metadata.caption: (1,000 m.)
metadata.description: Gives the aggregate ton-mileage of goods hauled by express consignment, piece, carload and total for 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: Locomotives
metadata.description: The table summarises the number and weight of new locomotives added to stock in the five years ending March 31, 1918, by type and average weight.

metadata.title: Number of Locomotives at the End of January 1914
metadata.description: The table shows the number and share of home-made and foreign-built locomotives by type, counted at the end of January 1914, to illustrate the locomotive stock's origins.

metadata.title: Weight of Locomotives in Working Order at the End of Jan. 1914
metadata.description: Shows the weight of locomotives in working order at the end of January 1914 by country of build and by engine type, with proportions, following the note on locomotives built in Japan.

metadata.title: Materials Purchased by the Government Railways
metadata.caption: (in yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows estimated materials purchased by the Government Railways from 1906 to 1913, split into domestic and foreign supply, to show the share of foreign supply each year.

metadata.title: [Private Railways in Japan, 1916]
metadata.description: Lists the eight private railways of Japan, with their offices, mileage, gauge and paid-up capital, as they stood when they were being converted to light railways.

metadata.title: Leading Light Railways in Japan
metadata.description: Gives the principal light railways operating in Japan, listing their offices, mileage, gauge and paid-up capital, following the account of the Light Railways Law of 1911.

metadata.title: [Electric Tramway Companies Summary, 1916]
metadata.description: Summarises the 1916 position of Japan's electric tramway enterprises by type, showing companies, capital, debentures, reserves, receipts, expenditure and net profit.

metadata.title: Leading Electric Tramway Enterprises
metadata.description: Lists the leading electric tramway enterprises with their capital, railway and track mileage and gauge.

metadata.title: Number of Registered Vessels Classified by Tonnage
metadata.description: Shows the number and gross tonnage of registered steamers and sailing vessels by size class from 1913 to 1917, illustrating the growth of Japan's mercantile fleet.

metadata.title: Registered Steamers Classified by Age (Dec. 1917)
metadata.description: Breaks down the registered steamers at December 1917 by age and by construction material, with totals and the split between home-built and foreign-built ships.

metadata.title: Registered Steamers Classified by Materials (Dec. 1918)
metadata.description: Classifies the registered steamers at December 1918 by construction material within each tonnage band, giving counts and tonnage for steel or iron, steel-wood or iron-wood, wood and in total.

metadata.title: Steamers Classified by Speed (1918)
metadata.description: Gives the number of steamers and their tonnage grouped by speed in knots for 1918, showing how the fleet was distributed by speed.

metadata.title: Tonnage Registered at Kwantung, Korea and Formosa
metadata.caption: (1,000 gross tons)
metadata.description: Shows how the registered tonnage in the three jurisdictions declined between 1914 and 1918, attributed to wartime submarine losses of Dairen steamers.

metadata.title: Export and Import of Steamers
metadata.description: Shows the number and gross tonnage of steamers, second-hand or new, imported and exported (sold abroad) during the war years 1915–1918.

metadata.title: Market of Second-Hand Boats
metadata.caption: (Yen per Dead Ton)
metadata.description: Gives the minimum and maximum market price per dead ton of medium-sized 15 to 30-year-old cargo boats for the four years to 1918.

metadata.title: Increase of Tonnage During the War
metadata.description: Shows the vessels added to the mercantile fleet from 1915 to the end of 1918, by source, supporting the statement that wartime tonnage growth was record-breaking.

metadata.title: [Decrease of Tonnage During the War]
metadata.description: Lists the vessels removed from the fleet during the war (wrecked, exported, missing, struck off, other), offset against the gains to give the net change.

metadata.title: Subsidised Oversea Service
metadata.description: Lists the oversea subsidised steamship services, their number of steamers, tonnage, speed and yearly sailings under the subsidy law.

metadata.title: [Subsidy Payments to Oversea Services, 1915-1920]
metadata.description: Shows the subsidy amounts paid to each oversea service under the new contract approved by the Diet in May 1915, year by year.

metadata.title: Near Sea and South Seas Service Now Run
metadata.description: Lists the near sea and South Seas steamship services run after the 1919 regulation amendment, with their sailing frequency and operating company.

metadata.title: Open Sea Service by Tramp-boats
metadata.description: Lists the open sea services run by tramp-boats to America, Europe and Australia, with frequency and operating company for each route.

metadata.description: The coal freight rates from Moji to Yokohama, the standard near-sea rate, are shown for selected months of 1915 and 1918 to illustrate the market's movement.

metadata.title: Average Rates Between Moji and Yokohama Since 1910
metadata.description: Shows the average freight rate between Moji and Yokohama for each year from 1910 to 1918.

metadata.title: North American Line (Beans)
metadata.description: Freight rates on the North American line for beans, for subsidized and unsubsidized vessels, with the dates of change.

metadata.title: Vessels Chartered to Foreigners
metadata.description: Number and gross tonnage of vessels chartered to foreigners from May 1918 to April 1919.

metadata.title: Seamen of Higher Grade
metadata.description: Gives the numbers of licensed captains, mates and engineers of Japanese and foreign nationality at the end of 1916, 1915 and September 1917, with the navigation limits of each class.

metadata.title: Shipwrecks
metadata.description: Shows the number of steamers and sailing ships and junks destroyed or damaged in shipwrecks, and the lives lost or injured, for 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: [Lighthouses and Other Navigational Signals at End of 1916]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of lights, daymarks and fog signals maintained by Government and public bodies at the end of 1916, built by native experts after Japan dispensed with foreign engineers.

metadata.title: Business Returns of the Three Navigation Companies
metadata.description: The table compares the business returns of the N.Y.K., O.S.K. and T.K.K. shipping companies for half-year periods in 1917–1918, covering cargo, passengers, fleet, capital, receipts, expenditure and dividends.

metadata.title: [Steel Shipbuilding, 1914–1918, Of Over 1,000 Tons Gross]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of steel shipbuilding by private yards over five years, illustrating the progress made since the outbreak of the War.

metadata.title: [Shipyards Capable of Building Steamers of Over 1,000 Tons Dead Weight]
metadata.description: Gives the number of shipyards able to build steamers over 1,000 tons dead weight, with their capital and workforce, at the end of 1913 and in March 1918.

metadata.title: [Tonnage Built at Leading Dockyards, Four Years Ending 1918]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of steamers and gross tonnage built at the leading dockyards during the four years ending 1918, as background to the shipbuilding discussion.

metadata.title: Registration of Patent Right
metadata.description: Shows the number of patent applications filed and patents registered at the Patent Office over six years, given to illustrate the state of invention protection.

metadata.title: Registration of Designs
metadata.description: Gives the applications and registrations of designs at the Patent Office for six years, part of the Office's annual figures for industrial property.

metadata.title: Registration of Trade-Marks
metadata.description: Records trade-mark applications and registrations at the Patent Office over six years, showing the Office's work alongside patents and designs.

metadata.title: Registration of Utility Models
metadata.description: Lists utility model applications and registrations at the Patent Office for six years, completing the set of industrial property figures on the page.

metadata.description: Shows the mortality rate of assured persons in Japan and England per 100,000 by age, supporting the claim that Japanese mortality differs from the English 17 Offices' table and resembles France's.

metadata.description: The continued fire-insurance tariff gives rate ranges by building class for wooden and fire-proof buildings, shown before the discussion of rebates.

metadata.title: Statistics of Insurance Companies

metadata.title: Foreign Insurance in Japan
metadata.description: Shows the business of foreign life, fire and marine insurance companies in Japan for 1914-1916, placed under the heading Foreign Insurance in Japan.

metadata.title: 5. Crystal Soda
