metadata.title: [Import Duty Rates on Miscellaneous Articles, Items 6 to 13]
metadata.description: This page lists specific customs duty rates per 100 kin or per gross on various manufactured goods, set out under numbered item headings in the tariff schedule.

metadata.title: [Class II: Refined Sugar, Rock Candy, Cube and Loaf Sugar, Oil, Etc.]
metadata.description: This page gives the specific duty rates for Class II goods, including sugars, oils, seeds, beer and paper, as set out in the tariff.

metadata.title: Import Duties on Tissues (Continued)
metadata.description: Continuation of a list of import duty rates on textile tissues, giving the yen rate per 100 kin for each weight and fibre category.

metadata.title: Shirts, Collars and Cuffs, and Ladies' Underclothing
metadata.description: Customs duty rates on cotton and flax tissues used for shirts, collars and cuffs, by weight, thread count and dyeing, under the Import Tariff.

metadata.title: Import Duty on Chains
metadata.description: Customs duty rate on gold-coated metal wire, listed as item 13 of the import duty schedule.

metadata.title: Import Duties on Iron and Steel Vessels Not Receiving Ship-Building Bounties
metadata.description: Customs duty rates on iron and steel products used in vessels not receiving ship-building bounties, by product type and thickness.

metadata.title: [Import Duties on Metal Pipes, Vessel Materials and Timber]
metadata.description: The list gives the import duty rates under the Customs Tariff Law on metal pipes, iron rivets, vessel materials and various woods, continuing from the previous page.

metadata.title: Tariff A. Import Duties in Japan
metadata.description: The page sets out the conventional import duties in Japan under the Japanese-Italian treaty tariff, listing each article with its duty and unit of measure.

metadata.title: [Import Duties Continued from Previous Tariff]
metadata.description: Continuation of a customs duty schedule listing Japanese export goods and their import duties, with rates and units printed in columns.

metadata.title: Tariff B. Import Duties in Italy
metadata.description: Italian import duty schedule (Tariff B) listing duties on Japanese textiles, furniture, basketwork, braids and fans, with rates and units.

metadata.title: Partial Revision of the Tariff
metadata.description: The page lists the items whose import duties were reduced or made duty free in the March 1916 partial revision of the tariff, with their new rates.

metadata.title: [Machinery Import Duties (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a list of machinery import duty rates, with the altered tariff wording for some items noted beneath.

metadata.title: Comparison of Statutory and Conventional Tariffs on Articles Affected by the Annulment of the German Tariff
metadata.caption: Statutory Tariffs and Conventional Tariffs; rates for chemicals and cloth rows printed per 100 kin
metadata.description: The annulment of the German tariff took effect in April 1915, so this table compares the statutory and conventional duty rates on the affected goods.

metadata.title: [Gas Engines, Petroleum Engines and Hot Air Engines, and Dynamos Connected with Above Engines]
metadata.description: Customs duty rates on gas, petroleum and hot air engines and on dynamos connected with them, listed by weight class, with two rate figures per item.

metadata.title: Gross Area of Arable Land in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Shows the gross arable land of Japan proper, split into landed farmers', tenanted and total paddy field and upland areas at the end of each December, 1914–1917.

metadata.title: Numbers of Families Engaged in Farming
metadata.description: Gives the number of families engaged in farming by category (landed farmers, tenants, combining tenantry) and their total at each December, 1914–1917.

metadata.title: [Farming Families Rearranged by Subsidiary Occupation]
metadata.description: Rearranges the farming families by whether they farm solely or also have a subsidiary occupation, for 1914–1916.

metadata.title: [Farming Families Classified by Area Cultivated per Family]
metadata.description: Classifies farming families by the area of cultivated land each family works, comparing the numbers and percentages for 1917 and 1916.

metadata.title: [Taxable Land Area by Category, 1914–1918]
metadata.caption: (In 1,000 cho)
metadata.description: Shows the taxable land area by category for 1914 to 1918, set beside the farming area, to illustrate the land base for tenant farming.

metadata.title: [Market Value of Farm Land per Tan, 1917]
metadata.caption: (Market value in Yen per tan, according to inquiries of the Hypothec Bank of Japan)
metadata.description: Gives the market value per tan of good, bad and ordinary paddy and upland farm land by region in 1917, showing regional differences in land prices.

metadata.title: [Average Yield of Paddy Field per Tan]
metadata.description: Shows the average paddy-field yield per tan over successive periods from 1894 to 1917, giving the historical trend in yields.

metadata.title: Ratio of One-Crop and Two-Crop Farms
metadata.description: Gives the official returns on the area and share of one-crop and two-crop paddy fields for 1915 and 1916.

metadata.title: Animal Labor in Tillage
metadata.description: Returns the number of horses and horned cattle used in tillage and the area tilled by animal labor for 1912 to 1916.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.description: Shows rice area, production, average yield and export and import quantities and values for 1914 to 1918 and the normal yield, as staple farm products.

metadata.title: [Rice Output by Kind of Rice, 1917]
metadata.description: Gives the 1917 rice area, output and value broken down by ordinary, glutinous and upland rice, as the text describes the output of each kind.

metadata.title: [Yield per Tan of Rice Varieties]
metadata.description: Compares average output per tan of early, middle and late rice varieties at Government Experimental Farms, showing the middle variety is most productive.

metadata.title: Barley and Wheat
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Gives barley, naked barley and wheat production for 1914 and 1915 with totals and average yield per tan.

metadata.title: [Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat by Paddy-field and Upland Farm, 1918]
metadata.description: The text notes that these grains are grown mainly in upland farms and as second crops, and gives the 1918 area figures in cho for paddy-field and upland farms.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: This table gives annual production of millets, buckwheat and maize from 1913 to 1917, illustrating the role of these grains in mountainous districts and as food where rice is scarce.

metadata.title: Beans, Potatoes and Sweet Potatoes
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual production of soy beans, red beans, horse beans, peas, sweet potatoes and potatoes, which the surrounding prose describes as important subsidiary farm crops.

metadata.title: Productions of Some Special Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly production of leaf indigo, leaf tobacco, cotton, hemp and rape-seed, listed as special crops alongside the foodstuff crops discussed above.

metadata.title: Productions of Other Minor Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kwan)
metadata.description: Lists the annual output of minor crops such as radish, taro, onion and peppermint over 1914 to 1917, illustrating the trends the text describes for these crops.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of cattle in Japan, broken down into cows, bulls, total, calvings and deaths, as part of the stock-farming statistics.

metadata.title: Number of Horses
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of horses in Japan, split into native, cross-bred and foreign breeds, with totals, for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Number of Stallions
metadata.description: Gives the number of stallions by breed category (native, cross, foreign) and total for 1916 to 1918.

metadata.title: Number of Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Lists the number of sheep, goats and swine in Japan for each year from 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Reports the number of slaughterhouses and animals slaughtered (cattle and calves, horses, sheep and goats, swine) for 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Families Keeping Poultry and Output
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of households keeping poultry and the resulting fowl stock, chickens, value and egg output from 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: Leading Dairy Districts (1917)
metadata.description: Lists the number of dairy farms, milk cows and milk output by leading prefectures in 1917, with national totals for 1914 to 1917.

metadata.title: [Glanders, Anthrax and Hydrophobia Records, 1913-1917]
metadata.description: The table gives yearly records of glanders, anthrax and hydrophobia cases and animals destroyed, illustrating the losses from cattle disease discussed in the preceding text.

metadata.title: Output of Fruits
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kwan)
metadata.description: The table gives annual fruit output in Japan for 1913 to 1917, showing the yield of several fruit kinds in thousand kwan, before the discussion of sericulture.

metadata.title: Sericultural Households and Mulberry Plantation
metadata.description: Shows the number of sericultural families by rearing season and the area of mulberry plantation for 1913 to 1917, illustrating growth in silk-raising.

metadata.title: Output of Cocoons
metadata.description: Gives, by spring, summer and autumn silkworm varieties, the number of egg-cards hatched, cocoon output by grade, output per egg-card and value for 1914 to 1918.

metadata.title: Output of Raw Silk in 1,000
metadata.description: Shows the annual output of raw silk, waste silk and the combined total, in kwan and yen, for 1914 to 1917, illustrating growth in silk production.

metadata.title: [Direct Export of Raw Silk by Japanese and Foreign Firms]
metadata.description: Compares the number of raw silk bales exported directly by Japanese and foreign firms each season, with the percentage share of each, to show the growing role of Japanese exporters.

metadata.title: Area of Tea Plantations and Number of Tea Manufacturers
metadata.description: Shows the area of tea plantations and the number of tea manufacturers for 1914 to 1917, supporting the discussion that tea production has stagnated.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Teas
metadata.caption: (Kwan)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output in kwan of green, black and oolong teas from 1913 to 1917, illustrating the stagnant tea trade discussed in the text.

metadata.title: Leading Districts of Tea Production (1917)
metadata.description: Lists the leading tea-producing districts in 1917 with their output in kwan and value in yen, showing the main tea-growing prefectures.

metadata.title: Export of Tea
metadata.caption: (in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the quantities and values of tea types exported in 1917 and 1918, mainly shipped to North America, as reported by the Customs Office.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.caption: Relative percentage
metadata.description: The page classifies the strata existing in Japan, as relative percentages, into sedimentary rocks by geological age and igneous rocks by period, preceding the discussion of metal-veins and strata.

metadata.title: [Output of Metals and Minerals, 1913–1917]
metadata.description: The table gives Japan's annual mineral output by quantity and value for gold, silver, copper, lead, iron, sulphur, coal and other minerals from 1913 to 1917, introducing the section on gold.

metadata.title: Demand of Pig Iron and Steel
metadata.description: Shows the estimated consumption of pig iron and steel in Japan, past averages and prospective figures, from the Economic Investigation Commission's study of iron demand and supply.

metadata.title: Production at Present and Prospective of Pig-Iron and Steel Materials in Japan and China
metadata.caption: Pig-iron (unit of 100 tons)
metadata.description: Gives the pig-iron output at present and the prospective output in Japan Proper, Korea, Manchuria and China, by year, to show expected supply growth.

metadata.title: Steel Materials
metadata.caption: (unit of 100 tons)
metadata.description: Gives the steel materials figures by period from 1915 onward, with later periods expected to rise; the text then notes foreign and Japanese foundry sources.

metadata.title: Annual Output at Leading Foundries in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Compares present and future annual output of pig-iron and steel materials at the leading government and private foundries in Japan proper.

metadata.title: Principal Metal Mines
metadata.caption: (figures in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: The table lists the leading metal mines producing at least ¥500,000 a year, with gold, silver and copper output and total value for 1917, grouped by district.

metadata.title: [Pig Iron, Steel and Iron Ores Output]
metadata.description: Shows the 1917 output of pig iron, steel and iron ore at the Kamaishi and Senninyama works, introducing the mining survey of Japan's metal industries.

metadata.title: [Available Coal Resources by Region]
metadata.description: Gives the rough distribution of Japan's available coal resources among Kyushu, Hokkaido and other fields, as estimated by the Mining Bureau.

metadata.title: Output of the Chief Coal-Fields in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Lists the annual coal output of Japan's chief coal-fields for 1917 and 1916, with the operating company of each, preceding the analysis of coals.

metadata.title: Analysis of Coals from the Principal Coal-Fields
metadata.description: Gives proximate analysis, sulphur content, caking quality, specific gravity and calorific power of coals from the principal coal-fields, introduced by the lead-in sentence before the petroleum section.

metadata.title: [Output of Oil in Echigo and Akita, 1916 and 1917]
metadata.description: The page gives the official oil output of the Echigo and Akita fields for the last two years, with the lessee companies of each field.

metadata.title: [Classified Production of Oil, 1915–1917]
metadata.description: The table classifies the annual oil production of 1915 to 1917 by product type, namely volatile, lamp, solar, heavy and machine oil.

metadata.title: Investment in Mining Business
metadata.caption: (Capital paid up in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The table shows the rising number of mining companies and their paid-up capital from 1914 to 1917, grouped by metal, coal, combined, petroleum and other businesses.

metadata.title: Leading Concessionaires of Mines
metadata.caption: Production in 1917
metadata.description: The list names the leading mine concessionaires with their 1917 production values, showing the largest mining firms of the year.

metadata.title: Condition of Mine-Workers
metadata.caption: At the end of June, 1917
metadata.description: The table gives the number of metal mine workers by age and sex, split between underground and above-ground work, at the end of June 1917.

metadata.title: [Persons Employed at Mines by Age and Sex, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuation of the table of workers at mines by age and sex, with the underground and above-ground figures for coal, petroleum and other non-metal mines and grand totals.

metadata.title: Accidents at the Mines
metadata.description: Yearly figures for mine accidents from 1912 to 1917, giving the number of accidents and the resulting deaths and wounded casualties.

metadata.title: Import and Export of Mineral Production
metadata.description: The table gives yearly exports of copper, coal and sulphur and imports of iron and steel and petroleum, showing the rapid growth of mineral trade during the mining boom.

metadata.title: Promotion of New Mining Companies
metadata.description: The table compares the number of newly promoted kerosene and mining and refining companies and their authorised capital in 1917 and 1916.

metadata.title: Increase in the Capital of Existing Mining Companies
metadata.description: The table shows how many existing kerosene and mining companies increased their capital in 1917 and 1916, and by how much.

metadata.title: Accidents to Fishing Boats and Casualties of Fishermen (1917)
metadata.description: Shows the number of fishing boats wrecked or otherwise lost and the resulting crew casualties for 1917, with comparative figures for 1914–1916.

metadata.title: Catches and Marine Production
metadata.description: Gives the value of fishery catches and marine products, in thousand yen, for each year from 1914 to 1917.

metadata.title: Principal Catches
metadata.description: Lists the principal fish and marine catches by quantity in thousand kwan and value in thousand yen for 1915 and 1917.

metadata.title: Principal Marine Products
metadata.description: Shows the principal marine products, such as dried squid, boiled prawns and salted fish, by quantity and value for 1916 and 1917.

metadata.title: Export of Fish and Marine Products
metadata.caption: (in value of ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japanese marine product exports, canned goods and fish and whale oil for 1916–1918, as recorded in the customs report.

metadata.title: Aquiculture
metadata.description: Gives the value of aquiculture output (snapping turtle, oyster, carp, eel, porphyra) for 1913–1917, illustrating the growth of fish and shellfish culture in Japan.

metadata.title: Deep Sea Catches in 1916
metadata.description: Returns for 1916 showing the situation of deep-sea fishery in Japan proper by fishing method, with sailors, steamers, motor boats, crew and catches.

metadata.title: Coral Fishery
metadata.caption: (in ₮ 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the value of pink, red and white coral collected in the seas around Kyushu and Shikoku in 1917, by prefecture, with the total.

metadata.title: [Forest Area of Japan Proper by Ownership, End of March 1913–1915]
metadata.description: Shows the area of forests in Japan proper at the end of March for 1913 to 1915, broken down by ownership class, illustrating the broad classification of forests described in the text.

metadata.title: [Forest Area by Prefecture]
metadata.description: Lists forest area in cho for the prefectures, introducing the discussion that forestry has not yet made marked progress as a source of revenue.

metadata.title: [Forest Yield of Principal Timbers in Japan Proper, 1917]
metadata.description: Shows the 1917 forest yield of principal timber species in Japan proper, by quantity in koku and value in yen, as returned by the authorities.

metadata.title: Financial Yield of Forests (Dec. 1917)
metadata.description: Gives the financial yield of forests by ownership category for December 1917, split into timber, fagots and total, as a basis for the discussion of forestry revenue.

metadata.title: [State Forest Receipts, Expenses and Balance]
metadata.description: Receipts, expenses and balance of the State forests for 1914-15 to 1917-18, shown to illustrate that the rate of profit is comparatively small.

metadata.title: Coniferous Timber Trees
metadata.description: Volume in koku and value in yen of the six principal coniferous timber trees felled in 1917.

metadata.title: Broad-Leaved Timber Trees
metadata.description: Volume in koku and value in yen of the four broad-leaved timber trees of economic importance felled in 1917.

metadata.title: [Rotation Periods of Principal Forest Species]
metadata.description: Lists the approximate rotation periods in years for principal tree species managed in State forests, shown as two parallel columns of species.

metadata.title: [Forest Area and Number of Trees by Ownership, Years Ended March 1915–1917]
metadata.description: Shows the area and number of trees in State, Crown, and other forests, with totals, for the three years ended March 1915 to 1917.

metadata.title: Total Volume of Felling
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly volume and value of timber and firewood felled from 1915 to 1917, illustrating the growth of the forestry business.

metadata.title: Principal By-Products
metadata.caption: (1917 in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the principal wood by-products of 1917, such as galls, mushrooms, resin and acetate of calcium, with their values, to show the scale of this subsidiary forest output.

metadata.title: [Products from State Forests and Wild Lands]
metadata.description: Shows the by-products obtained from State forests and wild lands, itemised by type, with a total, as a companion to the principal by-products figures.

metadata.title: Chief Articles Exported
metadata.description: Lists the chief forest products exported in 1918 with their values in yen, shown in two side-by-side columns in the original.

metadata.title: [Timber Exports by Category, 1916–1918]
metadata.description: Shows the progress of timber exports over the last four years, broken down by railway sleepers, tea-chest boards, matchsticks and other timber.

metadata.title: [Teak, Pine, Fir and Cedar, and Ebony and Sandal Wood Imports, 1916–1918]
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1000)
metadata.description: Shows that imports of teak and other forest woods rose sharply over 1916–1918, as stated in the text on import trade.

metadata.title: Number of Licenses Granted
metadata.description: Shows the number of hunting licences granted by grade and class in 1915-16 and 1916-17, illustrating the scale of shooting permits under the game law.

metadata.title: [Manufacturing Companies, 1913–1917]
metadata.description: Shows the number of manufacturing companies in Japan and their paid-up capital and reserves for each year from 1913 to 1917, illustrating the growth of industrial enterprise.

metadata.title: [Principal Kinds of Industries and Capital Invested at End of Dec. 1917]
metadata.description: Lists the main kinds of manufacturing industry with company counts, paid-up capital and reserves at the end of December 1917, showing where capital was concentrated.

metadata.title: Distribution of Industries
metadata.caption: To mention leading districts containing companies with total capital of over yen 50,000,000 p.u. each we have at the end of 1917:—
metadata.description: Lists the leading prefectures or districts with companies of large total capital at the end of 1917, with company counts and capital figures.

metadata.title: Factories and Employees
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of factories by type of power and the number of male and female operatives employed from 1913 to 1917.

metadata.title: [Motive Powers Used in Factories, 1917]
metadata.caption: Note.—For the year 1917 the kind of motive powers was as follows:—
metadata.description: Gives the number of engines and horse power of each kind of motive power used in factories in 1917, with water wheels subdivided by type.

metadata.title: Principal Factories (at the End of 1917)
metadata.description: Lists the principal textile factories at the end of 1917 by type of enterprise, with power sources, horse power and employee numbers.

metadata.title: [Factories by Kind of Enterprise, Continued]
metadata.description: This continued table lists the number of factories by kind of enterprise, with steam and manual power units, horsepower and employees, including government factories.

metadata.title: [Expansion of Cotton Mills Since 1914]
metadata.description: Figures show how the war boosted older cotton mills, with paid-up capital, net profit, dividends and their ratios to paid-up capital rising from the second half of 1915 to 1918.

metadata.title: [Spindles in Work by Yarn Count, July 1918 and March 1919]
metadata.caption: (Spindles in 1,000 at work)
metadata.description: The table shows that finer yarn counts were gaining ground over coarser ones in spindles at work between July 1918 and March 1919, due to Chinese customs duties.

metadata.title: [Cotton Spinning Companies, Mills and Equipment]
metadata.description: Figures compiled by the Spinner's Association of Japan show the growth of cotton spinning companies, capital, reserves and machinery from 1914 onward, as evidence of progress under the labor problem.

metadata.title: [Yarn Output Exported and Consumed at Home]
metadata.description: The table records the yarn output, the quantities exported and consumed at home, and textile output for 1914 to 1918, illustrating the trade balance of the spinning industry.

metadata.title: [Hempen Spinning Statistics, 1913-1917]
metadata.description: Statistics of the hempen spinning industry from 1913 to 1917, giving number of mills, capital, spindles, raw material consumed and output, following the introduction of the industry.

metadata.title: Statistics on Textile Industry
metadata.description: Gives factories, looms, operatives and output of the textile industry for 1913 to 1917, illustrating the wartime expansion described in the preceding text on woollen and hemp fabrics.

metadata.title: [Output of Textile Fabrics, 1913–1917]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of various textile fabrics in Japan from 1913 to 1917, illustrating the wartime growth of the industry.

metadata.title: [Silk, Cotton and Woolen Figures, 1913–1917]
metadata.description: Gives yearly figures for silk, cotton and woolen goods from 1913 to 1917, with totals, and refers readers to the foreign trade chapter for details.

metadata.title: [Factories and Operatives in the Chemical Industry]
metadata.description: Gives the number of chemical-industry factories and their operatives, by branch, according to the Agriculture and Commerce Department report, to show the industry's classification.

metadata.title: Production
metadata.caption: (in ₸1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual production values of potteries, shippo ware, fire-proof bricks, ordinary bricks and tiles, illustrating the state of these ceramic and building industries during the war years.

metadata.title: Exports
metadata.caption: (in ₸1,000)
metadata.description: Gives export values for potteries and shippo ware for 1915 to 1918, showing how exports of these enamel and pottery goods changed over those years.

metadata.title: [Portland Cement Production and Exports]
metadata.description: Presents Portland cement production and export quantities and values for 1915 to 1917, supporting the discussion of the industry's over-production and the export decline.

metadata.title: Production of Lacquer-Juice and Lacquered Wares
metadata.description: Shows yearly production of lacquer-juice and lacquered wares from 1915 to 1917, introduced in the text on the lacquer industry; the printed text also notes lacquered-ware exports exceeding a million yen.

metadata.title: [Output of Sake, Beer and Soy, 1914–1917]
metadata.description: Gives the annual output of sake, beer and soy for 1914 to 1917, illustrating the production figures for the brewing industries described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Production of Sake, Beer and Soy]
metadata.description: Gives yearly output figures for pure sake, beer (by pint, quart and cask) and soy, showing the scale of these brewing industries from 1916 to 1918.

metadata.title: Leading Breweries
metadata.caption: Latest condition of the above-mentioned companies is as follows:—
metadata.description: Summarises the latest capital, receipts, expenditure and dividend of the four leading Japanese breweries.

metadata.title: [Matches Production and Exports, 1913–1917]
metadata.description: Shows annual match production and exports with their values from 1913 to 1917, illustrating the trade's growth and the price rise of 1915.

metadata.title: [Match Exports by Destination, 1918]
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 gross)
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1918 match exports, totalling about 39.5 million gross, by destination country or region.

metadata.title: [Production, Exports and Imports of Papers, 1917]
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the amount and value of papers produced, exported and imported in 1917, showing the wartime boom in the paper industry.

metadata.title: Shime
metadata.description: Shows production, exports and imports of shime (sheets of paper, Mino and Hanshi types) for 1917, as a second part of the paper statistics.

metadata.title: [Soap Output by Type, 1915–1917]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the output of soaps by toilet, industrial, and laundry categories over three years, supporting the text's claim that output roughly doubled between 1915 and 1917.

metadata.title: [Production of Artificial Fertilizers by Origin]
metadata.description: Official statistics showing the value of artificial fertilizer production by origin, 1915 to 1917, illustrating the rapid growth of the industry.

metadata.title: [Output of Sardine, Herring and Whale Oil]
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly output of sardine, herring and whale oil with other fish oils and totals, 1914 to 1917, shown to illustrate the fish-oil industry.

metadata.title: [Engineering Works and Electric Companies: Paid-up Capital, Receipts, Expenditure and Dividend]
metadata.description: Figures for several engineering and electric companies, shown at the head of the page as the close of a preceding list of enterprises before the watch and clock industry is described.

metadata.title: [Gas Lamps, Heating and Motor Installations, and Volume of Production]
metadata.description: Shows the growth of gas lamps, heating and motor installations and gas production, illustrating the relative proportion of gas used for different purposes.

metadata.title: [Number of Gas Works, Paid-up Capital and Length of Pipes]
metadata.description: Gives the situation of the gas industry through the number of works, paid-up capital and extent of pipes, showing the industry's growth from 1911 to 1915.

metadata.title: [Capital, Receipts, Expenditure and Latest Dividend of Gas Companies, Second Half 1918]
metadata.description: Shows the capital, receipts, expenditure and latest dividend of the leading gas works in Japan for the second half of 1918, as an example of the gas industry.

metadata.title: [Electric Power Plants in Operation, 1915–1917]
metadata.description: Shows the number and kilowatt capacity of electric plants by type of enterprise in operation at December of each year from 1915 to 1917, showing the rapid growth of the industry.

metadata.title: [Electric Plants Under Construction, 1917]
metadata.description: Gives the number and kilowatt capacity of electric plants still under construction at the end of 1917, by type of enterprise.

metadata.title: [Kilowatt Capacity Classified by Nature of Enterprise and Generation, End of 1916]
metadata.description: Classifies kilowatt capacity of electric enterprises as hydro or steam, in operation or in preparation, at the end of 1916.

metadata.title: [Electric Power Enterprises by Kind of Undertaking, Continued]
metadata.description: The table shows the status of gas, total and other electric power undertakings by type of supply at the end of 1917, continuing the list from the previous page.

metadata.title: [Chief Items of Electro-Chemical Output]
metadata.caption: (Value in ¥1000)
metadata.description: The page lists the main items of Japan's new electro-chemical industry and their output values at the latest returns, which were about ¥155 millions.

metadata.title: [Sugar Production, Imports, Exports and Consumption in Japan]
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000 kin)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's sugar production, imports from abroad and Formosa, total supply, exports and domestic consumption for 1913–1917, presented after the discussion of sugar refining and Formosa's growing role.

metadata.title: [Native and Imported Wheat and Flour Production, 1913-1917]
metadata.description: Shows annual quantities and values of native wheat, imported wheat and flour produced, 1913-1917, illustrating the growth of the grain and flour trades.

metadata.title: [Peppermint Produced and Exported, 1913-1917]
metadata.caption: (Unit: ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly value of peppermint produced (crude, menthol, crystal oil) and exported, 1913-1917, showing the growth of the Hokkaido peppermint trade.

metadata.title: [Production and Exports, 1914–1917]
metadata.description: The page shows production of crude and refined material and exports for 1914–1917, illustrating how the industry declined and then revived after the European War.

metadata.title: Vegetable Oils
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives the output of vegetable oils from rape seed, sesame, yemola, cotton seed and other seeds for 1914–1917.

metadata.title: Dye-stuffs Consumed in 1918
metadata.caption: (unit in 1,000)
metadata.description: The table lists the chief dye-stuffs consumed in 1918 with quantities, values and the amounts imported, showing how far domestic production covered demand.

metadata.title: [Productions of Straw, Chip and Hemp Braids]
metadata.description: Shows annual domestic production of straw, chip, mixed and hemp braids from 1915 to 1917, giving the growth of the industry before the export figures that follow.

metadata.title: [Exports of Straw, Chip and Hemp Braids]
metadata.description: Shows exports of straw, chip, mixed and hemp braids for 1915–1918, illustrating the rapid progress of braid exports in a short time.

metadata.title: [Production and Exports of Mats, 1914–1918]

metadata.title: Military Service

metadata.title: Naval Service
metadata.caption: (Amounts in Yen)
metadata.description: Completes the pension record with the naval service figures of pensioners, family annuitants and retiring grants for 1919 and 1920.

metadata.title: Annuity Attached to the Orders of Golden Kite (Military Honor) and Rising Sun
metadata.description: Shows the number of recipients and total annuity amounts for the Golden Kite and Rising Sun orders in 1918 and 1919, noting that these annuities are a form of state pension.

metadata.title: Divisional Commanders
metadata.description: Lists the commanders, by rank of Lieutenant-General, of the fifteen divisions of the Standing Army, along with the Guards Division.

metadata.title: [Army Divisions and Their Commanders]
metadata.description: Lists the army divisions and the lieutenant-generals commanding each one, given before the Navy Department listing.

metadata.title: Department of the Navy
metadata.description: Lists the principal officials of the Navy Department, with their bureaus, schools and aides-de-camp, and their ranks and names.

metadata.title: Naval Staff Board
metadata.description: Names the chief and vice-chief of the Naval Staff Board, with their ranks.

metadata.title: Admiralties
metadata.description: Gives the commanders-in-chief of the naval admiralties at Yokosuka, Kure and Sasebo.

metadata.title: [Foreign Legations in Tokyo: Staff and Addresses]
metadata.description: This page lists the foreign legations in Tokyo with their diplomatic staff, posts, and addresses with telephone numbers, arranged alphabetically by country.

metadata.title: [Foreign Legations in Japan]
metadata.description: Lists the foreign diplomatic legations in Tokyo with their addresses, telephone numbers and staff, as a reference for the diplomatic corps.

metadata.title: Foreign Consulates in Japan
metadata.description: Lists the foreign consulates in Japan by country and port, with the names and ranks of the consular officers.

metadata.title: [Foreign Consular Representatives in Japan and Korea]
metadata.description: Lists the foreign consular offices in Japan and Korea, by country and port, with the name of each consul, continuing the directory from the previous page.

metadata.title: [Foreign Consular Officials in Japan]
metadata.description: Lists the foreign consular officials stationed at Japanese ports and cities, with their places and ranks, as recorded in the Diplomacy section.

metadata.title: Japanese Embassies Abroad
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese diplomatic staff posted at the embassies in Brussels and Paris, with their official ranks.

metadata.title: [Legation Staff, Continued]
metadata.description: The top rows continue the staff list of a legation whose heading falls on the previous page, naming its secretaries and naval attaché.

metadata.title: Switzerland (Legation at Berne)
metadata.description: Lists the Japanese legation staff at Berne, Switzerland, by post and name.

metadata.title: Japanese Consulates Abroad
metadata.description: Lists Japanese consulates abroad by country, with the consular officer at each post, marking Consulate-Generals and vice-consulates.

metadata.title: [Japanese Consulates Abroad (Continued)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues the list of Japanese consular posts abroad, giving the city and the officer in charge at each South American, European and Asiatic Russian post.

metadata.title: Japanese Honorary Consulates Abroad
metadata.description: This list gives the honorary Japanese consulates abroad, arranged by country, with the city and the honorary consul or vice-consul in charge of each.

metadata.title: [Consular Representatives Abroad]
metadata.description: This page lists the foreign consular posts in various countries and the officers in charge of each, as a reference for Japan's diplomatic and consular network.

metadata.title: [Eyesight, Trachoma and Venereal Disease Among Conscripts]
metadata.description: Yearly figures for conscripts by eyesight grade in shaku, with trachoma and venereal disease rates, shown alongside the text on falling illiteracy among conscripts.

metadata.title: No. of Officers on Active List
metadata.description: Shows the number of active-list officers by rank at December 1920, with the 1918 total given for comparison, illustrating the size of the Army officer corps.

metadata.title: Statistics (Dec. 1919)
metadata.description: Gives staff, student, graduate and admission figures for the special Army schools as of December 1919, following the description of the schools connected with the Army.

metadata.title: [Special Corps Schools Figures]
metadata.description: Shows figures for the various special corps schools (heavy artillery, cadets, preparatory, engineering, surgery, aviation and others), whose column headings are not printed on this page.

metadata.title: [Field Heavy Artillery Brigades and Regiments]
metadata.description: Lists the four brigades of field heavy artillery, each of two regiments, with their headquarters locations and regiment numbers.

metadata.title: [Bounty Rates for Subsidized Motor-cars]
metadata.description: Shows the bounty rates set by the 1918 law encouraging motor-cars strong enough for military transport, by capacity class, for construction, extra allowance, purchase and yearly maintenance.

metadata.title: [Results of the Military Arsenals for the Year Ended March 1919]
metadata.description: Gives the expenses and revenues of the two Military Arsenals at Tokyo and Osaka for the year ended March 1919, with totals.

metadata.title: Distribution
metadata.caption: (As revised in August 1922)
metadata.description: The Distribution chart shows how the Imperial Body Guard Division at Tokyo and its attached units are allotted to garrisons, as revised in August 1922.

metadata.title: [Army Divisions, Brigades, Regiments and Garrisons]
metadata.description: The page lists the army divisions of Japan with their divisional headquarters, the infantry brigades, regiments and other units under each, and the garrison or corps location of each unit.

metadata.title: [Army Divisions and Their Brigades, Regiments and Garrisons]
metadata.description: This table lists the army divisions, their infantry brigades, regiments, cavalry, artillery, engineer and other units, and the garrison towns or corps where each is stationed.

metadata.title: [Standing Army as Reorganized, by Arm]
metadata.description: The table gives the standing army by arm as reorganized under the retrenchment plan, showing each arm's new strength and the increase or decrease in units compared with before.

metadata.title: [Programme of Ships to be Completed by 1927]
metadata.description: After the Washington Conference abandoned the original 8-8 fleet plan, this table gives the announced programme of cruisers, destroyers and submarines to be completed by 1927.

metadata.title: Volunteers and Conscripts
metadata.description: Shows the annual Navy enlistment of conscripts and volunteers, with totals, for the five years ending December 1919, illustrating how volunteer service was supplemented by conscription.

metadata.title: [Naval Personnel by Rank]
metadata.description: The figures give the numerical strength of the Japanese Navy by rank, placed at the head of the page before the account of naval officers' promotion.

metadata.title: Age Limit of Officers in Active Service
metadata.description: Lists the maximum age limits for officers of each rank in active naval service, the final column headed 'No. limit.'

metadata.title: Statistics for 1919 (Dec.)
metadata.description: Shows staff, students, graduates and admissions at each of the naval educational institutions as of December 1919.

metadata.title: Battleships
metadata.description: The list of warships gives the battleships of the Imperial Navy with their displacement, dimensions, launch dates, speeds, torpedo tubes, armour and main armament.

metadata.title: [Battleships, Battle Cruisers and Cruisers]
metadata.description: Lists the principal Japanese battleships, battle cruisers and cruisers with their displacement, dimensions, launch dates, speeds, torpedo tubes and armour.

metadata.title: First Class Coast Defence Ships
metadata.description: Lists the first class coast defence ships with their displacement, launch dates, speeds and armament.

metadata.title: Second Class Coast Defence Ships
metadata.description: Gives the displacement, launch year, speed and armament of the second-class coast defence ships, arranged in two blocks.

metadata.title: First Class Gunboats
metadata.description: Lists the first-class gunboats with their displacement, launch year, speed and armament.

metadata.title: Second Class Gunboats
metadata.description: Lists the second-class gunboats with their displacement, launch year, speed and armament.

metadata.title: First Class Torpedo-Boat Destroyers
metadata.description: Lists the first-class torpedo-boat destroyers by name, displacement and year of launch, in two blocks.

metadata.title: Second Class Torpedo-Boat Destroyers
metadata.description: Lists the second-class torpedo-boat destroyers with their displacement and year of launch, in two blocks.

metadata.title: [Second Class Torpedo-Boat Destroyers]
metadata.description: Lists the Navy's second-class torpedo-boat destroyers with their displacement and year of launch, giving the fleet's composition in two columns.

metadata.title: Third Class Torpedo-Boat Destroyers
metadata.description: Lists the Navy's third-class torpedo-boat destroyers with their displacement, launch year, speed and armament, in two columns.

metadata.title: [Tokorozawa-Changchun Flight Results]
metadata.description: Lieutenant Higuchi's flight results for the long-distance Tokorozawa-Changchun flight, listing each section's distance, date and departure and arrival times.

metadata.title: Shrines and Priests
metadata.description: Gives the number of Shinto shrines by class and the number of priests in 1919-1920, showing the scale of the Shinto establishment that the preceding text describes.

metadata.title: Buddhist Temples and Priests
metadata.caption: Based on the report of the Department of Education:—
metadata.description: Shows the number of Buddhist temples and priests by sect in 1918 and 1919, illustrating the strength of the various Buddhist denominations in Japan.

metadata.title: Statistics of Some Leading Churches in Japan for 1919
metadata.description: Gives 1919 figures for foreign and Japanese workers, communicants, Japanese church contributions and organised and self-supporting churches of the main Christian denominations in Japan.

metadata.title: [Rice Relief Rates for Decrepit, Infant and Invalid Persons]
metadata.description: The 1874 Relief rules set out the amounts of rice granted to decrepit or disabled persons, infants and invalids who have no relatives to care for them.

metadata.title: [Paupers, Foundlings and Sick Travellers Relieved by State and Communes]
metadata.description: Figures show the paupers and foundlings relieved at state and communal expense, and sick travellers attended to by local authorities, for the years ended December 1917 to 1919.

metadata.title: [Relief Work Given, Years Ended March 1917–1919]
metadata.description: This table gives the yearly figures of relief in shelter, food, clothing and other forms for the three years ended March 1917 to 1919, preceding the summary of charitable work.

metadata.title: [Eleemosynary Work Summarised, Year Ending March 1920]
metadata.description: This table summarises the establishments under State, communal or private management and their funds, expenses and persons received at the end of the year ending March 1920.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Ex-Convicts' Homes, March 1920 and 1921]
metadata.description: Gives the number of ex-convicts' homes, their funds, inmates cared for and those discharged as reformed in 1920 and 1921, under Hoseikai's guidance.

metadata.title: [Charity Hospitals: Statistics at End of March 1919]
metadata.description: Statistics for charity hospitals at the end of March 1919, comparing public and private institutions by number, beds, and in- and out-patient numbers and days of sickness.

metadata.title: [Leper Hospitals in Japan, Inmates as of March 1920]
metadata.description: The text explains that leper inmates in 1920 were housed in five government hospitals, with about 300 more in private ones, and lists each hospital's number of inmates.

metadata.title: General Statistics of Educational Institutions in Japan Proper for the Year 1919-20
metadata.description: Gives the number of educational institutions in Japan Proper for 1919-20, with instructors, enrolment and graduates by type and by government, public or private control.

metadata.title: Foreign Instructors at the Institutions under Direct Control of the Department of Education
metadata.description: Shows the nationalities and number of foreign instructors employed at institutions under the Department of Education, with their total annual salaries, for 1918-19 and 1919-20.

metadata.title: General Statistics of Elementary Schools (Mar. 1920)
metadata.description: Gives the number of ordinary, higher and combined elementary schools by control type in March 1920, compared with March 1919.

metadata.title: [Teachers, Pupils and Graduates of Schools]
metadata.description: Summarises the number of teachers, pupils and graduates in government, public and private ordinary and higher schools, with comparison to March 1919.

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age Under Obligation to Attend School
metadata.description: Shows how many school-age children were under obligation to attend school, how many did or did not receive the prescribed instruction, and the percentage attending school, for 1918–1920.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers of Both Sexes in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Gives the number of public elementary school teachers and their monthly average salary, with how many earned under ¥50 and ¥50 to ¥120, for 1918–1920.

metadata.title: [Schools Collecting Fees and Number of Pupils Paying Them]
metadata.description: Shows, for lower-grade primary schools, how many charged fees and how many pupils paid full, partial or no fees in two successive years, reflecting the fee rules described above.

metadata.title: Blind, Deaf and Dumb of School-Age
metadata.description: Gives the number of blind and deaf-mute children of school age, how many of them receive instruction at schools, and the defective rate per 1,000 normal children.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens by Establishment, End of March 1920]
metadata.description: Summarises the number of kindergartens, conductors and children by type of establishment in 1920, with a 1919 comparison, showing the average children per conductor.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Blind School and Tokyo Deaf & Dumb School, 1919-20]
metadata.description: Gives staff, pupil and graduate numbers for the two Tokyo schools for the blind and deaf-mutes in 1919-20, as a sample of special education.

metadata.title: Public and Private B.D.D. Schools.—(End, March 1920)
metadata.description: Shows the number of B.D.D. (blind, deaf and dumb) schools, with their teachers, pupils and graduates by type of disability for the years ending March 1918 and 1920.

metadata.title: Graduates and Subsequent Careers
metadata.description: Shows the subsequent careers of public and private school graduates in the year after graduation, as reported for the two end-March years, by occupation category.

metadata.title: [Students in Higher Courses by Type and Course, Government, Public and Private Schools]
metadata.description: This table gives the course-wise student figures, leavers and unfinished percentages for government, public and private institutions, showing the numbers in each course category.

metadata.title: List the Gov't High Schools for the Year 1919-20
metadata.description: This list gives, for each of the seven government high schools, the director, number of instructors, students, graduates and admissions for the academic year 1919-20.

metadata.title: [Government High Schools, Staff and Students (continued)]
metadata.description: Lists the directors, instructors, students, graduates and admissions of the 8th to 12th Government High Schools, continuing from the previous page's table.

metadata.title: [Applicants and Admission by Department, 1919-20]
metadata.description: Gives the number of applicants for admission to the high schools in 1919-20 by department (Literature and Science), with the percentage admitted in each.

metadata.title: The Tokyo Imperial University (Sept. '19—June '20)
metadata.caption: Est'ed April 1877; President, Kozni, Yoshinao, D.Sc.
metadata.description: Lists the seven colleges of the Tokyo Imperial University with their place, dean, and staff, student and graduate numbers for the 1919–20 session.

metadata.title: The Kyoto Imperial University (Sept. '19—June '20)
metadata.caption: Est'ed June 1897; President, Araki, Torasaburo, D.M.
metadata.description: Shows the two colleges of the Kyoto Imperial University with their dean, staff, student and graduate numbers for the 1919–20 session.

metadata.title: The Tohoku Imperial University (Sept. '19 - June '20)
metadata.caption: Est'd June 1907; President, Ogawa, Masataka, D. Sc.
metadata.description: Shows staff, students and graduates of each college of Tohoku Imperial University, with its founding date and president.

metadata.title: The Kyushu Imperial University (Sept. 19—June '20)
metadata.caption: Est'd Dec. 1910; President, Mano, Bunji, D. Eng.
metadata.description: Staff, student and graduate figures for the medical and engineering colleges of Kyushu Imperial University, with its founding date and president.

metadata.title: The Hokkaido Imperial University
metadata.description: Explains that the Agricultural Department of Tohoku University became an independent university in 1918, and gives its colleges' statistics.

metadata.title: Average Age of Matriculation at Tokyo
metadata.description: Gives the average age of new students matriculated in each college of Tokyo Imperial University in 1918-19 and 1919-20.

metadata.title: Profession of the University Graduates
metadata.description: Shows how graduates of each Imperial University, from foundation to 1919-20, were distributed by their occupation or condition in life.

metadata.title: Total Number of Graduates from Foundation till the Year 1919-20, Classified by Colleges
metadata.description: Gives the cumulative number of graduates from each Imperial University since foundation to 1919-20, broken down by college faculty.

metadata.title: [Staff and Student Roll of the Tokyo University of Commerce, April 1921]
metadata.description: Gives the number of staff and students in each department of the Tokyo University of Commerce as of April 1921.

metadata.title: [Universities of Medicine: Name, Location, Teaching Staff and Students]
metadata.description: Two Government medical schools at Okayama and Niigata were made universities in April 1922, and their latest statistics are given here.
