metadata.caption: Est'd 1880, made univ. Nov. 1919: Pres., Dr. A. Sata.
metadata.description: Staff and student numbers of the departments of Osaka University of Medicine, which the bracketed staff figure covers the first four departments together.

metadata.title: Aichi University of Medicine (July 1921)
metadata.caption: Est'd 1876, made univ. June 1920: Pres., Dr. S. Yamasaki.
metadata.description: Staff and student numbers at Aichi University of Medicine, a public university whose staff figure is bracketed across both departments.

metadata.title: Kumamoto University of Medicine (July 1922)
metadata.caption: Est'd 1906, made univ. May 1922.
metadata.description: Teaching staff and students of the Kumamoto University of Medicine, which was raised to university rank in May 1922.

metadata.title: [Waseda University Students by College]
metadata.description: Listing the Waseda University student numbers by college, the table gives the detail behind the roll of about 11,000 students in July 1922.

metadata.title: Other Private Universities
metadata.caption: (With latest available figures)
metadata.description: This list of other private universities, with latest available figures, gives each institution's location, founding year, faculties, teaching staff and student numbers.

metadata.title: [Doctorates Conferred, March 1921]
metadata.description: Shows the number of doctoral degrees conferred by subject in March 1921, split between living and deceased recipients, illustrating the scope of the new doctorate title.

metadata.title: List of Government Technical Schools
metadata.caption: (Figures are for 1919-20)
metadata.description: Lists the government higher agricultural, forestry and sericultural schools with their directors, instructors, students and graduates, showing the state technical institutions described in the text.

metadata.title: Higher Technical Schools
metadata.description: Shows the higher technical schools, giving instructors, students and graduates for each, with newly opened schools marked by their opening dates.

metadata.title: Mining School
metadata.description: Gives the staff, enrolment and graduate figures for the government mining school at Akita.

metadata.title: List of Government Special Schools
metadata.caption: (Figures are for 1919-20)
metadata.description: Lists the government special schools (medical, pharmaceutical, foreign language and fine art), with staff, student and graduate figures for 1919-20.

metadata.title: Higher Mercantile Marine School
metadata.description: Gives the location and director of the Higher Mercantile Marine School, which opened in August 1920.

metadata.title: A, B & C Grade Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools, teachers, pupils and graduates of the A, B and C grade secondary-level technical and business schools, public and private, for March 1919 and 1920.

metadata.title: Kind of Schools (Including Branches) and Pupils in March 1920
metadata.description: Breaks down the A, B and C grade secondary technical and business schools and their pupils by type of school in March 1920.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public & Private Collegiate Institutions
metadata.caption: (March 1920)
metadata.description: Summarises the number of public and private collegiate institutions, their staff, students and graduates as of March 1920, with a note on which institutions are included.

metadata.title: Public Collegiate Institutions (1919-20)
metadata.description: Lists the six public collegiate institutions with their location, founding year, subjects taught, staff and student numbers for 1919-20.

metadata.title: Principal Private Collegiate Institutions (1919-20)
metadata.description: Lists the principal private collegiate institutions with location, founding year, subjects taught, staff and student numbers for 1919-20.

metadata.title: [Prefectural Normal Schools: Schools, Instructors, Students and Graduates by Sex]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of prefectural normal schools by type and the male and female instructors, students and graduates for 1917-18 to 1919-20.

metadata.title: Statistics of the Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: The table gives yearly statistics for the Tokyo, Hiroshima, and Nara higher normal schools, including Women's branches, showing instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admission rates for 1917-1920.

metadata.title: [Nautical College Statistics, 1920-21]
metadata.description: Gives the instructors, students and graduates of the Nautical College's Navigation and Engineering departments for 1920-21.

metadata.title: [Fishery Institute Statistics, May 1921]
metadata.description: Shows instructors, students and graduates of each course at the Fishery Institute as of May 1921, with cumulative graduates since its founding.

metadata.title: The Educational Stock Fund
metadata.description: Shows the loans, bonds, deposits and total sum of the Educational Stock Fund, which was created from the Chinese Indemnity to promote national education.

metadata.title: [Income of the Fund for Giving Additional Stipends to Teachers]
metadata.description: Shows the annual income of the fund for additional teachers' stipends from the State, provincial contributions, interest and balances brought over, for three fiscal years.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of the Fund for Giving Additional Stipends to Teachers]
metadata.description: Shows how the disbursements of the teachers' additional stipend fund were split between additional allowances and the amount carried forward to the next account.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid Out of Provincial and Communal Treasuries
metadata.description: Shows the educational expenses paid from provincial and communal treasuries for each school type over four years, from 1916–17 to 1919–20, illustrating the rising cost of education.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Gives health data of male students in the Imperial Universities, High Schools and various professional schools, covering constitution and eyesight over three school years.

metadata.title: [Constitution and Eye-sight of Students, 1917-18 to 1919-20]
metadata.description: Shows the constitution and eye-sight condition of examined students over three school years, as a continuation of the health statistics for schools.

metadata.title: Health Returns of Boys for the 1919-20 Year
metadata.description: Gives the health returns of boys in each type of school for 1919-20, covering constitution and eye-sight.

metadata.title: Health Returns of Girls for the 1919-20 Year
metadata.description: Gives the health returns of girls in each type of school for 1919-20, covering constitution and eye-sight.

metadata.title: [Height and Weight of Elementary School Children, 1919-20]
metadata.description: Gives the average height and weight of elementary school boys and girls at ages 7, 10, 13 and 16 for 1919-20.

metadata.title: The Imperial Library
metadata.description: Recent annual statistics of the Imperial Library in Uyeno Park, Tokyo, the largest library in Japan, covering volumes held, days open, and visitor numbers.

metadata.title: The Imperial University Libraries
metadata.description: Number of volumes stored at the imperial university libraries at the end of March, 1920, broken down into Japanese and Chinese books, European books, and totals.

metadata.title: [Libraries, 1918-1920]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly growth of libraries, their holdings, opening days and visitor numbers for 1918 to 1920, presented before the section on museums.

metadata.title: License for Higher School Teachers
metadata.description: Shows the number of higher school teacher licences granted in 1919-20, split between those won by examination and those granted without examination.

metadata.title: License for Secondary School Teachers
metadata.description: Gives three years of secondary school teacher licences by method of grant (without or with examination) and by sex, with yearly totals.

metadata.title: License for Elementary School Teachers
metadata.description: Lists elementary school teacher licences for three years by category: regular, special and assistant teachers, with totals.

metadata.title: [Labor Unions by Occupation, January 1921]
metadata.description: Following the text on the growth of unions after the War, this table gives the number of labor unions and their members by occupation, per the Police authority of the Home Office, January 1921.

metadata.title: [Mutual Aid Associations of Workmen: Membership and Receipts]
metadata.description: Shows the membership and annual receipts of workmen's mutual aid associations in government establishments such as the Printing Bureau, Monopoly Bureau, Railways and Postal Savings Bureau.

metadata.title: [Relief Payments of Mutual Aid Associations]
metadata.description: This continued list gives the amounts paid out in relief by the police and Communication Department mutual aid associations, by category of payment.

metadata.title: [Factory Workers by Age and Sex, 1920]
metadata.description: Shows the 1920 official statistics of factory operatives under the Factory Law by age group and sex, with percentages, illustrating the declining share of female labor and the concentration of women in child labor.

metadata.title: [Workers in Factories by Industry and Sex]
metadata.description: The figures give the total, male and female workers employed in each factory industry, continuing the survey of conditions of workers that the page goes on to describe.

metadata.title: [Government Works Operatives by Age and Sex, End of 1920]
metadata.description: Shows the number of operatives at government tobacco factories by age and sex at the end of 1920, illustrating the high number of child workers in these works.

metadata.title: Average Daily Wages
metadata.caption: (yen)
metadata.description: Gives average daily wages of various craftsmen and laborers in 1919, the first and second halves of 1920, and the first half of 1921, showing the wage trend.

metadata.title: Number of Operatives
metadata.description: Operatives classified by their employment in factories, shown by total, male and female numbers for 1920, from the Department of Agriculture and Commerce factory statistics.

metadata.title: The Family Account
metadata.description: Household account data for 497 slum families in Tokyo, showing the distribution of monthly income bands with average income, expense and excess of expenditure over income.

metadata.title: Sources of Income
metadata.description: Breakdown of the average slum family income by source, comparing the master's earnings with the wife's contribution and the share of families with each income source.

metadata.title: Income and Outgo of Families (Continued)
metadata.description: Continuation of the family income table, showing monthly income by source and its percentage share of income and outgo, with the deficit explained in the note below.

metadata.title: Percentages of Expenditure
metadata.description: Shows how the percentage of family expenditure on food, rent, clothing, fuel and sundries varies with income, supporting the observed trends that follow in the text.

metadata.title: Sundries
metadata.description: Analyses the 'Sundries' item of the expenditure table into its component headings, giving monthly amounts per family and their share of total outgo.

metadata.title: [Monthly Family Outgo on Business Expense, Insurance and Savings (Continued)]
metadata.description: The continued table gives the monthly business expense, insurance and savings outlays per family, with their share of total household outgo.

metadata.title: Data for Strikes
metadata.description: Shows the number of labour disputes, participants, average participants per case, and disputes counted by duration for 1918–1921, illustrating the rise and fall of strikes.

metadata.title: Average Number of Strikers Per Case Classified by Occupations (1914-1920)
metadata.description: Breaks down the 1914–1920 strikes by industry, giving cases, strikers and average strikers per case, to show which occupations had the largest disputes.

metadata.title: Strikes Classified by Causes
metadata.description: Shows the causes of strikes in each year from 1918 to 1921, in real numbers and percentages of the yearly total, explaining what workers were striking for.

metadata.title: Strike: Classified by Result
metadata.description: Shows the number of strike cases and participants for 1918–1921 classified by how each dispute was settled, as part of the labor and social problems survey.

metadata.title: Strikers Arrested Under the Peace Regulation
metadata.description: Gives the number of strikes and strikers, and the arrests, verdicts and dropped cases under the Peace Regulation in 1918–1920.

metadata.title: [Factory Workers Discharged and Engaged by Industry, 1920-1921]
metadata.description: The table, compiled by the Department of Agriculture and Commerce, summarizes discharged and engaged factory workers by industry for 1920 and 1921, illustrating labor conditions before the Labor Exchange Law discussion.

metadata.title: Female Teachers in Elementary & Girls' High Schools
metadata.description: Shows the number of female and male teachers in elementary and girls' high schools, illustrating that women's professional work as teachers is still comparatively limited.

metadata.title: Monthly Earnings of Occupational Women in Tokyo
metadata.description: The Tokyo Bureau of Social Works investigated the monthly earnings of occupational women in Tokyo, listing maximum, minimum and average pay for five professions.

metadata.title: Alumnae Marriage Record of the Tokyo Women's Higher Normal School
metadata.description: The table gives the marriage record of Tokyo Women's Higher Normal School graduates by period, showing that the share of unmarried alumnae rose in later years, illustrating higher education's effect on marriage.

metadata.title: Costs of First Instance
metadata.description: The table gives the stamp duty payable on original petitions in civil cases at first instance, by the value of the subject-matter of the suit, as set out under Costs in Civil Procedure.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts at End of 1921
metadata.description: Shows how many courts of each grade existed at the end of 1921, with their judges and procurators, illustrating the scale of the judicial system that handled the civil cases discussed.

metadata.title: Number of Civil Cases in 1920
metadata.description: Gives the number of civil cases handled in 1920 by each court level, with cases disposed of and cases remaining in hand at year end.

metadata.title: Civil Cases Disposed Of
metadata.description: Shows how civil cases were disposed of by year from 1916 to 1920, covering first-instance cases and those appealed, complained against, or demanding revision.

metadata.title: Nature of Civil Cases Settled at 1st Instance
metadata.description: Breaks down civil cases settled at first instance from 1916 to 1920 by the nature of the dispute, such as personal, land, money, cereals, goods and documents.

metadata.title: Cases of Bankruptcy and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Statistics of bankruptcy cases, adjudicated and rehabilitated, over 1916 to 1920 with yearly averages, shown under the heading Cases of Bankruptcy and Rehabilitation.

metadata.title: Cases of Insolvency and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Figures for insolvency cases, debtors, creditors, credit and rehabilitation outcomes for 1916 to 1920 with averages, presented as a companion to the bankruptcy statistics.

metadata.title: Criminal Cases
metadata.description: Handling of criminal cases over three years, 1918 to 1920, by search, preliminary trial and summary judgment, showing cases received, disposed of and left in hand.

metadata.title: [Criminal Cases Disposed Of, Continued]
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal cases handled by courts in 1918–1920 by class of trial, with cases disposed of and cases remaining in hand.

metadata.title: Sentence Carried Out
metadata.description: Gives the number of offenders whose sentences were carried out in 1918–1920, broken down by type of penalty and by rate per 100,000 population.

metadata.title: Number of Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of prisons and the inmates held in them, by category, at 31 December 1918 to 1920, as background to the prison system described above.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified, 1920
metadata.description: Breaks down the new convicts received in 1920 by the offence they were convicted of, listing the number of convicts for each category of crime.

metadata.title: Capital Punishment Classified
metadata.description: Shows the number of persons under capital punishment classified by the offence committed, for several years, with the offence categories set side by side.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified by Ages
metadata.description: Gives the age distribution of newly admitted convicts for three years, from under 18 up to over 60, with yearly totals.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified by Education
metadata.description: Shows newly admitted convicts for three years by level of education and sex, with unknown cases and totals.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified by Property
metadata.description: Classifies newly admitted convicts for three years by property status (with, small, without property, indigence) and sex, with unknowns and totals.

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Reports the number of sick prison inmates, average daily sick numbers, sick rate and mortality per 1,000 inmates for three years.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences and Ages
metadata.caption: (New convicts for 1920)
metadata.description: Cross-tabulates new convicts of 1920 by number of previous convictions (first to over sixth time), sex and whether under or over 18.

metadata.title: Number of Prison-Inmates Entered
metadata.description: Shows the number of male and female prison inmates entered each year 1918–1920, by type of entry, including new convictions, cancelled provisional releases and recaptures.

metadata.title: Number of Prison-Inmates Whose Names Are Cancelled
metadata.description: Gives the number of prison inmates whose names were removed from the prison registers each year 1918–1920, by reason such as serving out the term, amnesty, death or escape.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-Officers and Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Compares the number of prison officers with the number of inmates, giving inmates per officer and per turnkey and female inmates per female keeper for 1918–1920.

metadata.title: Work of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the number of days worked, wages earned in thousand yen, and daily wages per capita in sen for government, contract and trust convict labour, 1918–1920.

metadata.title: Revenue of Prisons
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Reports the prison revenue in yen for the fiscal years ended March 1919–1921, split into ordinary receipts (labour earnings, rentals, other receipts) and extraordinary receipts.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prisons
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows annual prison expenditure in yen over 1918 to 1920, split into ordinary and extraordinary items, as part of the justice and prisons statistics.

metadata.title: Annual Earnings and Expenses per Prison-Inmate
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly earnings from inmate labour and the per-inmate expenses of prisons, showing how much of prison costs was offset by inmate work.

metadata.title: Suicides and Suicidal Acts
metadata.description: Shows the number of suicides and suicidal acts by method, male and female, for 1918 to 1920, as part of the police statistics section.

metadata.title: Principal Causes of Suicides
metadata.description: Lists the principal causes attributed to suicides, broken down by sex, for 1918 to 1920, following the table of suicidal acts.

metadata.title: No. of Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.caption: Numbers of houses, boats or persons that suffered from robbery, fraud, etc. are as follows:—
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of houses, boats or persons that suffered from robbery, larceny, pickpocketing and fraud in 1919 and 1920.

metadata.title: Number of Arrests Made by Police Officers
metadata.description: Lists the number of arrests made by police officers for each category of offence in 1918, 1919 and 1920.

metadata.title: Unnatural Deaths
metadata.description: Shows deaths by unnatural causes for 1918 to 1920, with accidental deaths grouped under a bracket and a total including other causes.

metadata.title: Number of Foundlings
metadata.description: Gives the number of foundlings found in 1917 to 1920, split into living and found dead, by sex, with totals.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Summarises fires for 1917 to 1920 by number of cases, houses destroyed or damaged, building area burnt and amount of damage.

metadata.title: [Medical Practitioners, Dentists, Pharmacists and Others, 1920]
metadata.description: Gives the number of dentists, pharmacists, midwives, nurses and acupuncturists in Japan, following the statistics for medical practitioners.

metadata.title: [Public Hospitals, 1920]
metadata.description: Shows the number of public hospitals in 1920, their bed capacity and average daily in- and out-patients, as part of the account of hospitals.

metadata.title: [Refuse Collected in Six Cities]
metadata.description: Shows the quantities of rubbish, dirt and night-soil handled in six large cities, placed under the Medicine and Sanitation chapter as a sanitation statistic.

metadata.title: Epidemic Mortality
metadata.description: Shows annual cases and deaths from enteric fever, dysentery, diphtheria, small pox, cholera and plague over 1917-1919, illustrating the infectious disease burden discussed in the section.

metadata.title: Number of Dailies and Periodicals
metadata.description: Police Bureau returns giving the number of newspapers and periodicals existing at the end of each year, split by whether a deposit was lodged, for 1920 and 1921.

metadata.title: Periodicals Published in Tokyo
metadata.caption: (Title in Italics = in English. m. = monthly. w = weekly. f = fortnightly △ = thrice a month)
metadata.description: A list of monthly, weekly and other periodicals published in Tokyo, giving each title with its interest or subject and its publisher.

metadata.title: [Publication Statistics, 1917–1921]
metadata.description: Gives the number of books published in Japan from 1917 to 1921 by category, showing the trend in original works, periodicals and translations.

metadata.title: Western Books in Customs Returns
metadata.description: Shows the value of foreign books imported into Japan by country of origin for 1913, 1921 and the first nine months of 1922, illustrating the rapid post-war growth in book imports.

metadata.title: Epochs in Japanese Art
metadata.description: The page introduces the division of Japanese art history into six main epochs and twelve periods, tabulating each epoch's characteristic, its periods, Christian-era dates and durations.

metadata.title: [Number of Works Submitted and Exhibits Selected, Art Exhibition]
metadata.description: Gives the number of works submitted to the art exhibition and the number selected, by category (Japanese painting, Western painting, sculpture).

metadata.title: [Famous Wrestlers of Tokyo]
metadata.description: The table lists the best-known Tokyo wrestlers of the eastern and western camps, with their birth years, weights in kwan and heights in shaku, illustrating the sport's leading figures.

metadata.title: All Subscription Australian Races
metadata.description: Gives the fastest recorded times at the Negishi Race Course for All Subscription Australian races, with weights carried, from 1900 to spring 1922.

metadata.title: N.R.C. Subscription Country Bred Griffin Races
metadata.description: Records of the fastest N.R.C. Subscription Country Bred Griffin races at the Negishi Race Course, from 1900 to spring 1922.

metadata.title: All Subscription Country-Bred Races
metadata.description: Fastest records of All Subscription Country-Bred races at the Negishi Race Course, listed with weights carried, from 1900 to spring 1922.

metadata.title: All Country-Bred Races
metadata.description: Results of the country-bred horse races, listing season, distance, horse, weight and winning time, placed at the head of the swimming section on the page.

metadata.title: Speed Swimming
metadata.description: Winners and times of the chief speed swimming events at the 1922 national championship contests, listed by distance.

metadata.title: 2nd Inter-collegiate Swimming Contest
metadata.description: Shows the points scored by the leading universities and schools in the 2nd Inter-collegiate Swimming Contest held at the Tama River pool in September.

metadata.title: Tokyo Y. M. C. A. Indoor Pool Championship Contest
metadata.description: Reports the new records and winners at the Tokyo Y.M.C.A. indoor pool championship, first held in November 1922.

metadata.title: Records at Y.M.C.A. Compared with Far Eastern Olympic Games Records
metadata.description: Compares the swimming records made at the Y.M.C.A. pool with the corresponding records made at the Far Eastern Olympic Games.

metadata.title: [Principal Peaks of the Japan Alps, with Heights and Railway Stations]
metadata.description: A list of the principal peaks of the Japan Alps, grouped into Northern, Central and Southern Alps, giving each peak's height in feet and the railway station from which it is approached.

metadata.title: Autumn Inter-collegiate Record (Keio v. Waseda no match) 1922
metadata.description: The page reports baseball prosperity and then gives the batting and fielding statistics of the 1922 autumn Keio versus Waseda intercollegiate record, comparing five university teams.

metadata.title: [Records Broken at the Athletic Meeting Held at Komaba]
metadata.description: Eight events at the national championship meeting in which records were broken, with the athlete or team and the new record for each.

metadata.title: J. A. A. A. Official Records for 1922
metadata.description: Official Japanese national athletics records as of 1922, listing each event with its record holder, the record, the place and the year it was set.

metadata.title: Records of 7th Inter-scholastic Championship Games
metadata.description: The records set at the 7th spring tournament of the Kanto secondary-school championship games held at Komaba, comparing middle and normal school winners in each event.

metadata.title: [Notable Marathon Race Records, 1922]
metadata.description: Introduces the notable marathon race records of 1922, listing the sponsor, date, distance, winner and time of each race to show the growing popularity of long-distance running.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Students Marathon Union Records]
metadata.description: Lists the records set at the first meeting of the Tokyo Students Marathon Union in November, which was organized to promote this special race.

metadata.title: [Girls' Championship Athletic Records]
metadata.description: Shows the best performances of the 1st Girls' Championship athletic matches held at Ochanomizu in November, the strongest results across the three girls' athletic functions of that year.

metadata.title: [Athletic Records (Continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of a table of women's athletic records, listing each event with its holder and the record set.

metadata.title: Higher Course Pupils
metadata.description: Records set at the Hochi primary school pupils' competition at Komaba in May, for higher course pupils, shown alongside the elementary course results.

metadata.title: Elementary Course Pupils
metadata.description: Records set at the Hochi primary school pupils' competition at Komaba in May, for elementary course pupils, shown beside the higher course results.

metadata.title: Championship Records
metadata.description: The table gives the placings and points of Japan, the Philippines and China at the 5th Far Eastern meeting held at Shanghai.

metadata.title: Far Eastern Athletic Records
metadata.description: A list of Far Eastern athletic records, giving event, holder, record and year made, with the Philippine, Japanese and Chinese holders.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Theatres: Days Open and Tickets Sold]
metadata.description: The page gives the latest figures for the Tokyo theatres, showing the number of days they were open and the number of tickets sold.

metadata.title: [Cinema-hall Statistics, Latest Available Figures]
metadata.description: Following the discussion of business concerns and cinema-halls, the page gives the latest available national figures for days open, tickets sold and revenue of picture-halls.

metadata.title: [Public Works Expenditure by Works, 1915 and 1916]
metadata.description: The introductory text states that public works expenditure rose well above the average in recent years, and this table compares the totals for each category of work in 1915 and 1916.

metadata.title: [Public Works Expenditure by Administrative Body, 1915 and 1916]
metadata.description: This table divides the public works expenditure not borne by the Central Government among prefectures, districts, cities, towns and villages, and local unions for 1915 and 1916.

metadata.title: [Annual Expenditure on Roads and Bridges, 1907–'17 Average by Source]
metadata.description: Shows how the average yearly expenditure of about ¥25,264,195 on roads and bridges during 1907–'17 was defrayed by each source of funds.

metadata.title: [Flood Damage and Repair Costs, 1916-1919]
metadata.description: Statistics of flood damage and river-work repair costs for 1916 to 1919, shown to illustrate the importance of river works in protecting against inundations.

metadata.title: [Cost of River Works and Source of Funds, Fiscal Years 1913-1916]
metadata.description: The table gives the cost of river works and the sources of the funds disposed of in fiscal years 1913 to 1916, showing contributions from State, prefectures, districts and other bodies.

metadata.title: [New River Work Program Disbursements, 1923-1935]
metadata.description: The revised consecutive river work disbursements over twelve years, with the State's share, were officially published in December 1922 to show the burden on State coffers.

metadata.title: [Harbor Works Costing Over ¥1,000,000]
metadata.description: A list of harbor works whose total cost or estimate exceeded ¥1,000,000, arranged chronologically, with the works carried out and the periods of construction.

metadata.title: [Waterworks of Principal Cities]
metadata.description: The table gives construction cost, pipe length, private cocks, posts and yearly receipts for the more important city waterworks, according to the latest returns.

metadata.title: [Damage Caused by Tidal Waves and Cost of Repair, 1916–1919]
metadata.description: Coast protection expenditure is partly driven by repairing tidal-wave damage, so this table gives the yearly amount of damage and the cost of repair from 1916 to 1919.

metadata.title: Telegraph and Telephone Service
metadata.description: The table gives the latest lengths of telegraph and telephone aerial, underground and submarine lines in Japan for 1917 to 1921, showing steady growth in the network.

metadata.title: Number of Telephone Apparatuses
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly growth of telephone subscribers and of exchange and telephone apparatus, with the automatic share, from 1916 to 1921, illustrating the expansion described in the text.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Offices
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of post and telegraph offices in Japan from 1918 to 1921, with the ratio of offices to area and population.

metadata.title: Ordinary Mail Matters
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly volume of domestic ordinary mail matters by class, including registered items and a per-population rate, for 1916–17 to 1920–21.

metadata.title: Foreign Ordinary Mail Matters
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly number of foreign ordinary mail items transmitted by type, with totals, arrivals, growth rate and per-population figures, 1916–17 to 1920–21.

metadata.title: Telegrams (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of telegrams handled by the Post and Telegraph service, split into domestic, foreign despatched and received, with wireless share, over three years.

metadata.title: Parcels Transmitted (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of domestic and foreign parcels transmitted by the postal service, with growth rates and parcels per ten of population.

metadata.title: Postal Savings Deposits
metadata.description: Shows the growth of postal savings depositors and deposit amounts from 1918 to 1921, noting that deposits rose steadily after a 1914 dip and that interest stands at 4.8%.

metadata.title: [Persons Classified by Occupation]
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the numbers of persons and yen amounts in each occupational group, classified as agriculturists, school children, tradespeople and laborers and employees, for 1919 to 1921.

metadata.title: Domestic Money Orders
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the number and value of domestic money orders issued and paid in each fiscal year ending March, 1919 to 1921.

metadata.title: International Money Orders
metadata.description: Records the number and value of international money orders issued and paid in each December year from 1918 to 1920.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Receipts
metadata.description: Shows the yearly receipts from ordinary mail, parcels, money orders, savings deposits, telegrams and telephones, with totals, for fiscal years ending March 1915 to 1920.

metadata.title: Post and Telegraph Service Expenses
metadata.description: Lists the yearly expenses of the postal and telegraph services by branch, with totals, for fiscal years ending March 1915 to 1920.

metadata.title: [Parcel Post Rates, Domestic and Colonial]
metadata.description: Gives the parcel post charges by weight band for domestic parcels and for parcels exchanged with Formosa, Saghalien and other colonial territories, as revised in April 1919.

metadata.title: [Fees for Postal Petty Orders, Ordinary Money Orders and Telegraphic Money Orders]
metadata.caption: (Rates of fee in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the current fees, in yen, for postal petty orders, ordinary money orders and telegraphic money orders at graded amount limits, as described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: Foreign Parcel Rates
metadata.description: Lists the foreign parcel postage rates, in yen, for parcels sent to Argentina by direct Japanese boat at two weight bands.

metadata.title: [Parcel Post Rates to Foreign Countries]
metadata.description: The page lists postal parcel rates from Japan to foreign destinations, giving the route, weight band and yen rate for each country.

metadata.title: [Postal Rates to Foreign Countries by Destination]
metadata.description: Lists postal rates for letters and parcels sent from Japan to each foreign destination, by route and weight, with the charge in yen.

metadata.title: [Telegraphic Money Orders: Maximum Amounts and Fees by Country]
metadata.description: The table lists the maximum amounts and fees for telegraphic money orders payable to each foreign country, grouped by continent, showing which countries are excluded from express or payment-notice service.

metadata.title: International Telegraph Rates
metadata.caption: The rates for telegrams per word to places abroad are as follows (subject to alteration):
metadata.description: The page gives the charges per word for international telegrams from Japan, by region, showing whether each route runs via Shanghai, Europe or Manila.

metadata.title: [Rate of Profit from Railway Working, 1916-17 to 1920-21]
metadata.description: Introductory remarks on the railway nationalization give the rate of profit from railway working for the last five years, listed in two columns.

metadata.title: Railway Mileage Open to Traffic
metadata.description: Shows the growth of State and private railway mileage open to traffic at the end of each March from 1917 to 1921, supporting the discussion of railway expansion.

metadata.title: Capital, Profit and Reserves of State and Private Railways
metadata.description: Gives the capital invested in State railways with their profit rate, and the capital and reserves of private railways open to traffic, for the years ended March 1917 to 1921.

metadata.title: Staff of the Government Railways on March 31st, 1921
metadata.description: Breaks down the 163,822 officers and employees of the Government Railways on March 31st, 1921 by class.

metadata.title: [Railway Employees, Continued from Previous Page]
metadata.description: The top of the page carries the closing rows of a staff-number table, giving subordinate employees, the total staff and the year-on-year increase.

metadata.title: [Mileage of Lines Worked and Length of Tracks, March 31st, 1921]
metadata.description: The page gives the mileage of lines worked and track length by division on March 31st, 1921, compared with the total for the preceding year.

metadata.title: Main Lines and Mileage Under Traffic, End of Mar., 1921
metadata.description: A two-column list of the principal railway lines under traffic at the end of March 1921, with the open mileage of each.

metadata.title: Disposition of Net Earnings
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual disposition of net earnings of the railways across 1917 to 1921, broken down by additional works, inspection, interest, subsidy and net profit.

metadata.title: Traffic Mileage
metadata.description: Gives the average working mileage, passenger mileage and ton mileage of the railways for each year from 1917 to 1921, illustrating the growth of traffic.

metadata.title: Working Revenue and Expenses
metadata.description: Summarises working revenue, expenses and net profit of the railways for 1919 to 1921, both in total and per mile worked, with the expense-to-revenue ratio.

metadata.title: Working Revenue Classified
metadata.description: Breaks down working revenue for 1919 to 1921 into coaching and goods receipts, with the total including sundries.

metadata.title: Working Expenses Classified
metadata.description: Shows the railways' working expenses broken down by category for three years, indicating how operating costs rose over the period.

metadata.title: Railway Working and Shipping Receipts
metadata.description: Gives the receipts from railway working and shipping, with totals, for the years 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Passenger Earnings
metadata.description: Following the fare-revision remarks, this gives passenger earnings by class and in total for the years 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Passengers Carried, etc.
metadata.description: Records the number of passengers carried, passenger-miles, average journey length and passengers per day and per train mile for 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Ratio of Passengers per 1,000 by Class
metadata.description: Shows how passengers per 1,000 were divided among the first, second and third classes in each year from 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: [Principal Items Hauled by State Lines]
metadata.description: Lists the principal goods hauled by the State lines during the year ended March 1921, giving tonnage for the main items.

metadata.title: Goods Earnings
metadata.description: Shows goods traffic earnings on the State railways by class of goods (ordinary, express, carload) for the years 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Tonnage of Goods
metadata.caption: (1,000 tons)
metadata.description: Gives the tonnage of goods carried on the State lines by class (ordinary, express, carload) for each year from 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Aggregate Ton-mileage of Goods Hauled
metadata.caption: (1,000 m.)
metadata.description: Gives the aggregate ton-mileage of goods hauled on the State lines by class of goods for 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Locomotives
metadata.description: Summarises the number and weight of locomotives in use on the State lines at the end of March for 1919 to 1921.

metadata.title: [Locomotives by Division]
metadata.description: Shows the number and weight of steam and electric locomotives held by each railway division, with lines under construction and totals.

metadata.title: Number of Passenger Carriages
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of passenger carriages by type, with seating capacity and average seats per car and per open mile of track.

metadata.title: Number of Goods Wagons
metadata.description: Records the yearly number and carrying capacity of covered and open goods wagons, with average capacity per vehicle and per open mile.

metadata.title: [Railway Purchases of Home and Foreign Make, Years Ended March 1917-1921]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly split between home and foreign purchases of railway equipment for the years ended March 1917 to 1921, with the foreign share as a percentage.

metadata.title: [Working of Local Railways in Japan Proper]
metadata.description: Gives the working results of Local railways in Japan proper for the year ended March 1921, compared with the two preceding years.

metadata.title: Leading Local Railways in Japan (March, 1921)
metadata.description: A list of the leading private local railway companies in Japan as of March 1921, giving office location, line length, motive power, gauge and paid-up capital.

metadata.title: Railways
metadata.caption: Continued
metadata.description: This continued table lists further railway companies with their office location, length of line open, motive power, gauge and paid-up capital.

metadata.title: [Results of Working of Tramways, Years Ending March 1917 to 1921]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly results of working Japan's tramways over the five years to March 1921, including mileage, capital, passengers, goods, revenue, expenses and profit.

metadata.title: Leading Tramways
metadata.caption: (As existing at the end of March 1921)
metadata.description: Lists the leading tramway companies and municipal systems in Japan at the end of March 1921, with their open mileage, motive power, gauge and capital.

metadata.title: [Working Results of Municipal Tramways in Tokyo and Osaka, Year Ended December 1921]
metadata.description: Gives the year's working results for the Tokyo and Osaka municipal tramways, totals and daily averages for cars run, mileage, passengers and receipts.

metadata.title: Number of Registered Vessels Classified by Tonnage
metadata.description: Gives the number of registered Japanese steamers and sailing vessels by size class and total gross tonnage at each December from 1918 to June 1922, illustrating the wartime and post-war growth of the fleet.

metadata.title: Tonnage Registered in Kwantung, Korea and Formosa
metadata.caption: Ships over 20 tons registered in the three jurisdictions and their tonnage were as follows, in 1,000 gross tons:—
metadata.description: Shows the number and gross tonnage of ships over 20 tons registered in Korea, Formosa and Kwantung at the end of 1919, 1920 and 1921, supplementing the national fleet statistics above.

metadata.title: Licensed Seamen of Higher Grade
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese and foreign licensed seamen of higher grade (captains, mates and engineers) holding each licence class in 1920 and 1921.

metadata.title: Pilots
metadata.description: Gives the number of Japanese and foreign licensed pilots for 1919 to 1921, under the Pilotage Law restricting pilotage to Japanese subjects.

metadata.title: Leading Shipowners
metadata.description: Lists the leading Japanese shipowners owning more than 15,000 gross tons in May 1922, with head office, number of ships and gross tonnage.

metadata.title: [Largest Steamship Owners and Their Fleets]
metadata.description: This ranked list of the largest steamship owners, with their fleet numbers and gross tonnage, precedes the article on leading steamship companies.

metadata.title: Business Returns of the Three Leading Companies
metadata.description: Shows the half-yearly business results of the N.Y.K., O.S.K. and T.K.K. shipping companies, covering capital, fleet, receipts, expenditure, profit and dividends.

metadata.title: Near Sea and Ocean Service Now Run
metadata.description: Gives the number of steamers and gross tonnage of vessels over 1,000 tons in the near sea and ocean services, as investigated by the Department of Communications in August 1922.

metadata.title: [Steamers Qualified for the Overseas Mail Subsidy Services]
metadata.description: Lists the steamers and services run under the 1909 Overseas Navigation Subsidy Law, giving steamer numbers, tonnage limits, speeds and annual sailings by route.

metadata.title: Regular Overseas Mail Service
metadata.description: Shows the regular mail lines the Nippon Yusen Kaisha runs under government contract to foreign countries, with their ports of call and service frequency.

metadata.title: [Principal Subsidized Lines and Subsidy for 1922]
metadata.description: Shows the maximum annual subsidy approved by the Diet for 1922 for each principal subsidized navigation line on near sea, South Sea and other routes.

metadata.title: [Subsidised Lines and Subsidy for 1922]
metadata.description: Lists the shipping lines receiving government subsidies and the amount granted for 1922 on each route.

metadata.title: [Coal Freight Between Wakamatsu and Yokohama, 1917-1921]
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Shows the monthly and average coal freight rate between Wakamatsu and Yokohama, the standard rate in Japan's near-sea service, for 1917 to 1921.

metadata.title: Freight Rate of Open Sea Lines
metadata.caption: (Per ton of General Cargo)
metadata.description: Gives the freight rates per ton of general cargo charged by open sea lines (European, American, Australian and Bombay) by year, with the wartime peak rates.

metadata.title: Freight Rate of Staple Commodities
metadata.caption: On European Line (per ton)
metadata.description: Shows freight rates per ton on European Line for staple commodities such as barley, oats, fish oil and silk, for selected years.

metadata.title: On N. American Line (Per Ton)
metadata.description: Shows freight rates on the North American line for tea, raw silk and peanuts, comparing subsidized and unsubsidized vessels, from 1914 to 1921, illustrating wartime and postwar movements.

metadata.title: [Recent Movements of Charterage (Per Ton)]
metadata.description: Gives the minimum and maximum charter rates per ton for June and December steamers of three sizes, 1919 to 1922, showing how charterage moved after the wartime boom.

metadata.title: [Lighthouses, Marks and Signals, End of September 1920]
metadata.description: Gives the number of lights, daymarks, land-marks and fog signals in Japan at the end of September 1920, split between Government and Public ownership.

metadata.title: Shipwrecks
metadata.description: Shows yearly shipwreck losses for 1918 to 1920, covering steamers and sailing ships and junks, and the lives lost or injured.

metadata.title: Number of Ships Launched
metadata.description: Shows the number and tonnage of steamships and sailing vessels launched by Japanese shipyards each year from 1918 to 1921, illustrating the postwar decline in shipbuilding.

metadata.title: Price of Newly Built Ships
metadata.caption: (per ton)
metadata.description: Gives the price per ton of newly built ships in January, June and December of each year from 1918 to 1921, showing the sharp price fall after the war boom.

metadata.title: [Number of Shipbuilding Yards and Docks, 1917–1921]
metadata.description: Gives the number of shipbuilding yards, docks and floating docks in Japan for each of the past five years, introducing a comparison of yard numbers and capacity.

metadata.title: [Shipbuilding Yards, Berths and Employees, 1913, 1918 and 1921]
metadata.description: Introduces the comparison of shipbuilding yards, berths and employees in Japan before and after the War, using figures for 1913, 1918 and 1921.

metadata.title: Principal Shipbuilding Yards (Aug. 1922)
metadata.description: Lists the principal shipbuilding yards in Japan as of August 1922, with their number of berths, year established and location.

metadata.title: Charterage Per Ton
metadata.caption: (Figures in sen)
metadata.description: Shows 1922 charter rates per ton in sen for coasting and overseas trade, illustrating how far the freight market had fallen for shipowners.

metadata.title: [Idle Ships Tonnage Tied Up]
metadata.description: Gives the number of idle ships and their tonnage tied up in Japanese ports at several dates, showing the peak in March 1921 and later decline.

metadata.chapter_raw: Patents, Designs, Trade-marks and Utility Models
metadata.description: The text lists the annual fees payable for an extended patent term, by period of years, following the note on the ordinary patent fee schedule.
