metadata.description: The table summarises the benevolent enterprises under State, communal or private management, with their number, funds, expenses and persons received, at the end of the year ending March 1920.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Ex-Convicts' Homes, 1920–1921]
metadata.description: Gives the number of ex-convicts' homes, their funds, inmates cared for and those discharged as reformed in 1920 and 1921, showing the statistics of homes under the Hoseikai.

metadata.title: Charity Hospitals at the End of March 1919
metadata.description: Gives the number of public and private charity hospitals at the end of March 1919, with their beds, in-patients and out-patients, as the chapter's opening statistics.

metadata.title: [Inmates of Leper Hospitals, March 1920]
metadata.description: Shows how the roughly 1,344 inmates in March 1920 were spread across the five government leper hospitals, plus about 300 at private institutions.

metadata.title: General Statistics of Educational Institutions in Japan Proper for the Year 1920-21
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools, instructors, enrolment and graduates for each type of educational institution in Japan Proper in 1920-21, with totals.

metadata.title: Foreign Instructors at the Institutions under Direct Control of the Department of Education
metadata.description: Shows the number of foreign instructors by nationality employed at institutions under direct Department of Education control, with their total and annual salary cost, for 1918-19 and 1919-20.

metadata.title: General Statistics of Elementary Schools (Mar. 1921)
metadata.description: Gives the number of ordinary, higher and combined elementary schools by government, public and private management, with totals and comparison figures for March 1920.

metadata.title: [Teachers, Pupils and Graduates in Schools]
metadata.description: Shows the number of teachers, pupils and graduates in ordinary and higher schools by school type (Government, public, private) and as at March 1920, for the education statistics.

metadata.title: Number of Children of School Age under Obligation to Attend School
metadata.description: Gives the number of school-age children under obligation to attend school, split by sex, whether they received the prescribed instruction, and the percentage attending school by area.

metadata.title: Salaries of Teachers of Both Sexes in Public Elementary Schools
metadata.description: Shows how many public elementary school teachers, both sexes, received monthly salaries of various sizes, with the average monthly salary, for 1918 to 1920.

metadata.title: [Primary Schools Collecting Fees and Pupils Paying Them]
metadata.description: Shows how many lower-grade schools collected fees and how many pupils paid full, partial or no fees in two school years, under the fee rules described.

metadata.title: [Blind, Deaf and Dumb Children of School-Age]
metadata.description: Gives the number of blind and deaf-mute children of school age, how many receive instruction at schools, and the defective ratio per 1,000 normal children.

metadata.title: [Kindergartens by Management]
metadata.description: Summarises government, public and private kindergartens with their conductors and children for March 1920, with the 1919 comparison and average children per conductor.

metadata.title: [Blind and Deaf-Mute Schools, 1919-20]
metadata.description: Gives the staff, pupil and graduate numbers for the two Tokyo schools for the blind and deaf-mute in 1919-20, as the education section describes these institutions.

metadata.title: Public and Private B.D.D. Schools (End March 1920)
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools, teachers, pupils and graduates of public and private blind, deaf and dumb (B.D.D.) schools at the end of March in two successive years.

metadata.title: Graduates and Subsequent Careers
metadata.description: Shows the subsequent careers of public and private school graduates, as reported within the year after graduation, for two successive years ending March.

metadata.title: [Students by Course and Type of Institution]
metadata.description: Shows the number of students in each course of the institutions, split into government, public and private, with totals, as a continuation of the chapter's statistics.

metadata.title: List of the Gov't High Schools for the Year 1920-21
metadata.description: Lists the seven government high schools with their directors and figures for instructors, students, graduates and admissions in the year 1920-21.

metadata.title: [Applicants and Admissions by Department, 1921-22 and 1922-23]
metadata.description: The text reports the number of applicants for admission by department and the admission rate for the two years, showing how selective entrance to the higher schools had become.

metadata.title: The Tokyo Imperial University (Oct. 1923)
metadata.caption: Est'd April 1877; President, Kozni, Yoshinao, D.Sc.
metadata.description: The page describes the five Imperial Universities, and this table gives the colleges, deans, staff, students and graduates of Tokyo Imperial University as of October 1923.

metadata.title: The Kyoto Imperial University (Oct. 1923)
metadata.caption: Est'd June 1897; President, Araki, Torasaburo, D.M.
metadata.description: This table gives the colleges, deans, staff, students and graduates of Kyoto Imperial University as of October 1923, as one of the five Imperial Universities.

metadata.title: The Tohoku Imperial University (Oct. 1923)
metadata.caption: Est'd June 1907; President, Ogawa, Masataka, D. Sc.
metadata.description: Lists the colleges of the Tohoku Imperial University in October 1923 with their deans, staff, students and graduates.

metadata.title: The Kyushu Imperial University
metadata.caption: Est'd Dec. 1910; President, Mano, Bunji, D. Eng.
metadata.description: Shows the colleges of the Kyushu Imperial University, founded December 1910, with their deans, staff, students and graduates.

metadata.title: The Hokkaido Imperial University
metadata.description: Gives the departments of the Hokkaido Imperial University, which was made independent in 1918 from the Tohoku University, with staff, students and graduates.

metadata.title: Average Age of Matriculation at Tokyo
metadata.description: Shows the average age in years and months of new students matriculated at the colleges of Tokyo University in 1918-19 and 1919-20.

metadata.title: Profession of the University Graduates
metadata.description: Shows how graduates of each Imperial University, since foundation to 1919-20, were distributed by their occupation or condition in life.

metadata.title: Total Number of Graduates from Foundation till the Year 1919-20, Classified by Colleges
metadata.description: Gives the cumulative number of graduates of each Imperial University since foundation to 1919-20, broken down by college.

metadata.title: [Staff and Students of the Tokyo University of Commerce, April 1923]
metadata.description: Lists the staff and student numbers of each department of the Tokyo University of Commerce as they stood in April 1923.

metadata.title: Universities of Medicine
metadata.description: Lists the five former Government medical schools, made universities in 1922–23, with their location, teaching staff and student numbers.

metadata.title: Osaka University of Medicine (April 1923)
metadata.caption: Est'd 1880, made univ. Nov. 1919: Pres., Dr. A. Sata.
metadata.description: Shows the staff and student numbers of the Osaka University of Medicine's departments, one of the public universities, as of April 1923.

metadata.title: Aichi University of Medicine (April 1923)
metadata.caption: Est'd 1876, made univ. June 1920: Pres., Dr. S. Yamasaki.
metadata.description: Gives the staff and student numbers of the Aichi University of Medicine at Nagoya, a public university, as of April 1923.

metadata.title: Kyoto University of Medicine (April 1923)
metadata.caption: Est'd 1879, made univ. May 1922: Pres., Dr. S. Ogawa.
metadata.description: Gives the teaching staff and students of the Preparatory Department of the Kyoto University of Medicine as of April 1923.

metadata.title: Kumamoto University of Medicine (April 1923)
metadata.caption: Est'd 1896, made univ. May 1922.
metadata.description: Gives the teaching staff and students of the Preparatory Department of the Kumamoto University of Medicine as of April 1923.

metadata.title: [Students of Waseda University by College]
metadata.description: Following the Waseda University description, this table gives the student numbers in each of its colleges and schools as of July 1922.

metadata.title: Other Private Universities
metadata.caption: (With latest available figures)
metadata.description: Lists the other private universities with their location, founding year, college or school, teaching staff and student numbers, the latest figures available.

metadata.title: [Doctorate Degrees Conferred by Subject, March 1922]
metadata.description: Shows the number of doctorate titles held by living and deceased recipients, by academic field, as of March 1922, illustrating how the title was conferred after the reform.

metadata.title: List of Government Technical Schools
metadata.caption: (Figures for 1921–22)
metadata.description: Lists the government technical schools of higher grade, their directors, instructors, students and graduates for 1921–22, grouped into agricultural/forestry and sericultural schools.

metadata.title: Higher Technical Schools
metadata.description: Gives the higher technical schools with directors, staff, student and graduate figures, including newer schools marked by their opening dates.

metadata.title: Mining School
metadata.description: Shows the single mining school, with its director, instructor, student and graduate numbers.

metadata.title: List of Government Special Schools (Figures for 1921–22)
metadata.caption: (Figures for 1921–22)
metadata.description: Lists the government special schools (pharmaceutical, foreign language and fine art) with their directors and figures for 1921–22.

metadata.title: Higher Mercantile Marine School
metadata.description: Gives the location, director, staff numbers, students and graduates of the Higher Mercantile Marine School at Kobe.

metadata.title: Public and Private Technical and Business Schools of Secondary Grade
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools, teachers, pupils and graduates in each of the three grades of technical and business schools of secondary grade, by type of school, as of March 1921.

metadata.title: Statistics of Public & Private Collegiate Institutions
metadata.caption: (March 1920)
metadata.description: Summarises the number of schools, staff, students and graduates of public and private collegiate institutions in March 1920, with a note on which institutions are included.

metadata.title: Public Collegiate Institutions
metadata.description: Lists the public collegiate institutions of 1919-20 with their location, founding year, subjects taught, staff and student numbers.

metadata.title: Principal Private Collegiate Institutions
metadata.description: Lists the principal private collegiate institutions of 1919-20 with their location, founding year, subjects taught, staff and student numbers.

metadata.title: [Instructors, Students and Graduates of Prefectural Normal Schools by Sex]
metadata.description: Shows the number of prefectural normal schools by type and the male and female instructors, students and graduates for three school years, illustrating the sex composition of teacher training.

metadata.title: Statistics of the Higher Normal Schools
metadata.description: Shows instructors, students, graduates, applicants and admissions for the Tokyo, Hiroshima and Nara higher normal schools, including the women's institutions, over 1918–19 to 1920–21.

metadata.title: [Nautical College Statistics, 1920-21]
metadata.description: Gives the instructors, students and graduates of the Navigation and Engineering Departments of the Nautical College for 1920-21.

metadata.title: [Fishery Institute Statistics, May 1921]
metadata.description: Shows the instructors, students and cumulative graduates of each course at the Fishery Institute for May 1921.

metadata.title: The Educational Stock Fund
metadata.description: Shows the balance of the Educational Stock Fund, created from the Chinese Indemnity, at the end of March for 1918 to 1920, broken down into loans, bonds and deposits.

metadata.title: Fund for Giving Additional Stipends to Teachers
metadata.description: Gives the receipts of the fund created in 1900-01 to pay additional allowances to common school teachers, showing State and provincial contributions, interest and balances brought forward.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of the Fund for Giving Additional Stipends to Teachers]
metadata.description: Shows how the stipend fund was disbursed each year, split between additional allowances to teachers and the amount carried to the next account.

metadata.title: Educational Expenses Paid Out of Provincial and Communal Treasuries
metadata.description: Shows how much education expenditure from prefectural and communal treasuries went to each type of school and institution over four fiscal years, accompanying the discussion of State grants to compulsory education.

metadata.title: Health of Male Students in Government Institutions
metadata.description: Gives health data for male students in the Imperial Universities, High Schools and professional schools, covering constitution and eyesight over three school years.

metadata.title: Health Returns of Boys, 1919-20
metadata.description: Gives the 1919-20 health returns for boys in public and private secondary and elementary schools, by school type, covering constitution and eyesight.

metadata.title: Health Returns of Girls, 1919-20
metadata.description: Gives the 1919-20 health returns for girls in public and private schools, by school type, for comparison with the boys' figures.

metadata.title: Height and Weight of Elementary School Children, 1919-20
metadata.description: Shows average height and weight by age for boys and girls in elementary schools in 1919-20, noting the health data as regards physique.

metadata.title: The Imperial Library
metadata.description: Recent annual statistics of the Imperial Library in Uyeno Park, Tokyo, the largest library in Japan, showing volumes, opening days and visitor numbers.

metadata.title: The Imperial University Libraries
metadata.caption: The number of volumes stored at the end of March, 1920 was as follows
metadata.description: Number of volumes held at the end of March 1920 by the imperial universities' libraries, split into Japanese and Chinese books, European books and totals.

metadata.title: [Libraries: Number, Volumes, Days Open, Visitors, 1918–1920]
metadata.description: Gives the number of public libraries, their volumes, days open, visitors and daily visitors for the years 1918 to 1920, showing growth in library provision before the museum section.

metadata.title: [Licenses Granted to Higher School Teachers, 1919-20]
metadata.description: Shows the number of higher school teacher licences granted in 1919-20, after the first higher-grade licence examination was held in spring 1920.

metadata.title: [Licenses Granted to Secondary School Teachers, 1917-18 to 1919-20]
metadata.description: Gives three years of figures for secondary school teacher licences, granted with or without examination, broken down by sex, to supplement qualified teaching staff.

metadata.title: [Representative Labor Unions With More Than 1,000 Members]
metadata.description: The page lists the representative labor unions in Japan at the time that had more than 1,000 members, with their membership figures.

metadata.title: Mutual Aid Associations of Workmen
metadata.description: Summarises membership and receipts of mutual aid associations of workmen in the Government Printing Bureau, Monopoly Bureau, Government Railways, naval and military workshops, and Postal Savings Bureau.

metadata.title: [Mutual Aid Society Payments by Category]
metadata.description: This continuation lists the yen amounts paid out by a relief fund under headings such as deaths, injuries, long service and medical costs, before the text on mutual aid schemes.

metadata.title: [Factory Workers by Age Group and Sex, 1920]
metadata.description: Shows the 1920 male and female factory operatives by age group, with percentages, illustrating that men dominate adult labor while women predominate among child workers.

metadata.title: [Number of Factory Workers by Industry and Sex]
metadata.description: The figures give the number of workers in each factory industry, split into male and female, and lead into the discussion of workers' living and working conditions.

metadata.title: [Child and Female Operatives at Government Factories, End of 1921]
metadata.description: Shows the number of child and female operatives at Government factories at the end of 1921, by age group, to illustrate the high share of young workers at tobacco factories.

metadata.title: Average Daily Wages (Yen)
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Lists average daily wages in yen for various craftsmen and factory workers in 1920, both halves of 1921 and 1922, showing that craftsmen's wages fell while factory wages held up.

metadata.title: [Wages of Workmen and Servants, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuing the wage table, it gives average wage rates for various trades and servants in the years 1921 and 1922, with monthly salaries marked by an asterisk.

metadata.title: Number of Operatives
metadata.description: Operatives in factories are classified by employment and sex, giving the 1921 totals from the factory statistics compiled by the Department of Agriculture and Commerce.

metadata.title: The Family Account
metadata.description: Family account of 497 Tokyo slum families, showing how many families fell into each monthly income band and their average income, expense and surplus or deficit.

metadata.title: Sources of Income
metadata.description: Breakdown of average monthly income of slum families by source, comparing the master's earnings with the wife's, as shares of income and outgo.

metadata.title: [Monthly Income and Outgo of Families (Continued)]
metadata.description: Shows monthly family income and outgo by source, including the share of income from other family members and other sources, and the deficit explained in the accompanying note.

metadata.title: Percentages of Expenditure
metadata.description: Gives the percentage of family expenditure spent on food, rent, clothing, fuel and lighting, and sundries at each income level, showing how the shares shift as income rises.

metadata.title: Sundries
metadata.description: Breaks down the sundries item of family expenditure into its component heads, with monthly amounts per family and their share of total outgo.

metadata.title: [Monthly Family Outgo Items (Continued)]
metadata.description: The continued table lists the monthly family spending on business expense, petty insurance, and savings and insurance, with their share of total household outgo.

metadata.title: Data for Strikes
metadata.description: Summarises labour disputes in Japan from 1919 to the first half of 1922, giving cases, participants, participants per case and strike days, to support the surrounding discussion of labour troubles.

metadata.title: Average Number of Strikers Per Case Classified by Occupations (1914-1920)
metadata.description: Shows the average number of strikers per strike case in each occupational group during 1914-1920, indicating which industries had the largest disputes.

metadata.title: Strikes Classified by Causes
metadata.description: Breaks down the yearly strikes from 1919 to the first half of 1922 by their causes, showing the real number and percentage for each cause such as higher wages or against dismissal.

metadata.title: Strikes Classified by Result
metadata.description: Shows the yearly strikes from 1919 to 1922 classified by their outcome, in cases and participants, illustrating how the labor disputes were settled.

metadata.title: Strikers Arrested Under the Peace Regulation
metadata.description: Gives the number of strikers and arrests under the Peace Preservation Regulation for 1918 to 1920, with the outcomes of the prosecutions.

metadata.title: [Factories: Discharged and Engaged]
metadata.description: Figures for workers discharged and engaged in several factory industries, shown at the top of the page, apparently continuing an earlier table.

metadata.title: [Labor Exchange: Vacancies, Registrations and Engagements, 1921–1922]
metadata.description: Statistics from the official report on the Labor Exchange offices, comparing vacancies, registrations and engagements for general and day laborers in 1921 and 1922.

metadata.title: Female Teachers in Elementary & Girls' High Schools
metadata.description: Shows how many women teachers, compared with men, served in elementary and girls' high schools in 1918–1920, illustrating women's role as professional bread-winners.

metadata.title: Monthly Earnings of Occupational Women in Tokyo
metadata.description: The Tokyo Bureau of Social Works investigated monthly earnings of occupational women in Tokyo, and this table lists maximum, minimum and average earnings for five professions.

metadata.title: [Alumnae Marriage Record of the Tokyo Women's Higher Normal School]
metadata.description: The alumnae marriage record of the Tokyo Women's Higher Normal School, by decade of graduation, showing how many graduates married, stayed unmarried, or died.

metadata.title: Costs of First Instance in Civil Procedure
metadata.description: Lists the stamp duty payable on civil petitions at first instance, by the value of the subject-matter, illustrating how court costs are paid by adhesive stamps.

metadata.title: Composition of Courts at End of 1921
metadata.description: Shows the number of courts, judges and procurators in each court tier at the end of 1921, illustrating the structure of the judicial system described in the surrounding discussion of legal costs.

metadata.title: Number of Civil Cases in 1920
metadata.description: Gives the number of civil cases handled in 1920 by each court level, with cases disposed of and cases remaining in hand, supporting the discussion of the costly and slow civil litigation process.

metadata.title: Civil Cases Disposed Of
metadata.description: Shows how civil cases were disposed of in the courts from 1916 to 1920, by first-instance cases and by cases appealed, complained of and demanding revision.

metadata.title: Nature of Civil Cases Settled at 1st Instance
metadata.description: Breaks down the civil cases settled at first instance from 1916 to 1920 by the nature of the dispute, such as personal, land, money and goods matters.

metadata.title: Cases of Bankruptcy and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Shows yearly bankruptcy cases adjudicated by type of debtor, cases remaining, credit amounts, and rehabilitation outcomes, giving annual figures and an average.

metadata.title: Cases of Insolvency and Rehabilitation
metadata.description: Shows yearly insolvency cases with numbers of debtors and creditors, credit amounts, and rehabilitation results, with an average, illustrating the insolvency trend.

metadata.title: [Criminal Cases Handled, 1918–1920]
metadata.description: Shows the number of criminal cases handled under search, preliminary trial and summary judgment for 1918–1920, illustrating how many were disposed of and left in hand.

metadata.title: [Court Cases Disposed Of, Continued]
metadata.description: Continuing the court statistics, this table gives first instance, appeal, complaint and retrial case numbers, disposals and cases in hand for 1918–1920.

metadata.title: Sentence Carried Out
metadata.description: Shows the number of offenders sentenced and how sentences were carried out (capital punishment, imprisonment, fines) for 1918–1920, with offenders per 100,000 population.

metadata.title: Number of Prison Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the number of prisons and of prison inmates at December 31 in 1918, 1919 and 1920, showing how the prison population was declining over those years.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified, 1920
metadata.description: Lists the number of new convicts received in 1920 by type of crime, with the crimes split across two columns of the printed page and a grand total.

metadata.title: Capital Punishment Classified
metadata.description: Shows the number of persons sentenced to capital punishment for each offence in 1914–1919, giving the grounds for the death sentences.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified by Ages
metadata.description: Gives the age distribution of newly admitted convicts in 1918–1920, showing how the prison intake was spread across age groups.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified by Education
metadata.description: Shows the educational background of newly admitted convicts in 1918–1920, broken down by sex and level of schooling.

metadata.title: New Convicts Classified by Property
metadata.description: Shows the property status of newly admitted convicts in 1918–1920, by sex, indicating the economic circumstances of offenders.

metadata.title: Sick Rate and Mortality of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the sickness and death figures among prison inmates for 1918–1920, showing sick rates and mortality per thousand inmates.

metadata.title: Frequency of Offences and Ages
metadata.caption: (New convicts for 1920)
metadata.description: Cross-tabulates newly admitted convicts of 1920 by sex, number of previous convictions and age, showing the frequency of repeat offending.

metadata.title: Number of Prison-Inmates Entered
metadata.description: Shows the number of male and female prison inmates newly entered in 1918-1920, by type of admission, with totals.

metadata.title: Number of Prison-Inmates Whose Names Are Cancelled
metadata.description: Shows the number of male and female prison inmates whose names were removed from prison registers in 1918-1920, by reason of cancellation.

metadata.title: Ratio of Prison-Officers and Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Gives the number of prison officers and the ratios of inmates per officer, per turnkey and per female keeper for 1918-1920.

metadata.title: Work of Prison-Inmates
metadata.description: Shows the number of working days, total wages and daily wage per capita of convicts in government, contract and trust work for 1918-1920.

metadata.title: Revenue of Prisons (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly revenue of prisons for fiscal years ended March 1919-1921, split into ordinary (labour earnings, rentals, other receipts) and extraordinary income.

metadata.title: Expenditure of Prisons
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Shows annual prison expenditure in yen, split into ordinary and extraordinary items, for the three years ended March 1918 to 1920.

metadata.title: Annual Earnings and Expenses per Prison-Inmate
metadata.caption: (in yen)
metadata.description: Gives the average yearly income from inmates' labour and the ordinary, extraordinary and total expenses per prison inmate for 1917 to 1919.

metadata.title: Suicides and Suicidal Acts
metadata.description: The table gives the number of suicides and suicidal acts by method for men and women in 1918, 1919 and 1920, showing how people ended their lives.

metadata.title: Principal Causes of Suicides
metadata.description: The table lists the principal recorded causes of suicide, by sex, for 1918 to 1920, showing which motives were most common.

metadata.title: Causes of Suicide (Continued)
metadata.description: Continuation of a table of suicide causes, giving male and female counts for 1918 to 1920 to show motives behind the deaths.

metadata.title: No. of Sufferers from Robbery, Peculation and Fraud
metadata.caption: Numbers of houses, boats or persons that suffered from robbery, fraud, etc.
metadata.description: Shows how many houses, boats or persons suffered from various kinds of robbery and fraud in 1919 and 1920.

metadata.title: Number of Arrests Made by Police Officers
metadata.description: Lists the number of arrests made by police officers for each category of offence in 1918, 1919 and 1920.

metadata.title: Unnatural Deaths
metadata.description: Shows the number of deaths by cause, murder and accidental causes, over 1918 to 1920, illustrating the scale of unnatural deaths in Japan.

metadata.title: Number of Foundlings
metadata.description: Gives the yearly number of foundlings, split by sex and whether they were living or found dead, for 1917 to 1920.

metadata.title: Fires
metadata.description: Summarises the number of fire cases, houses destroyed or damaged, building area burnt and damage amount for each year from 1917 to 1920.

metadata.title: [Cases Handled by Juvenile Courts in 1923]
metadata.description: Juvenile courts opened in Tokyo and Osaka in January 1923; this table gives the number of cases they handled that year, by sex and how each case was disposed of.

metadata.title: [Dentists, Pharmacists, Midwives, Nurses and Acupuncturists, 1920]
metadata.description: Gives the 1920 numbers of dentists, pharmacists, midwives, nurses and acupuncturists in Japan, as statistics for professional classes beyond medical practitioners.

metadata.title: [Hospitals in Japan, 1920]
metadata.description: Shows the 1920 count of public hospitals, their beds, and average in- and outpatients per hospital, illustrating hospitals' role in the welfare of the Japanese people.

metadata.title: [Refuse Collected in Six Cities]
metadata.description: Shows the amounts of rubbish, dirt and night-soil handled in six major cities, part of a section on public sanitation measures.

metadata.title: Epidemic Mortality
metadata.description: The table gives yearly case and death counts for enteric fever, dysentery, diphtheria, small-pox, cholera and plague, with totals, for 1917 to 1919.

metadata.title: [Number of Dailies and Periodicals Existing at End of Year]
metadata.description: The Police Bureau's returns give the number of dailies and periodicals existing at the end of 1920 and 1921, divided by whether a deposit was made.

metadata.title: Periodicals Published in Tokyo
metadata.caption: (Title in Italics = in English. m. = monthly. w = weekly. f = fortnightly. △ = thrice a month)
metadata.description: A list of periodicals published in Tokyo, giving each title's frequency, its subject or interest, and its publisher, as an aid to readers seeking Japanese and English journals.

metadata.title: [Number of Books Published, 1917–1921]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of original works, periodicals and translations published each year from 1917 to 1921, with totals, as the latest available statistics on book publishing.

metadata.title: [Imports of Foreign Books by Country, 1913–1922]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The text notes that foreign book imports rose sharply after the war, and gives recent-year figures by country to show England, the U.S.A., Germany and France's shares.

metadata.description: The table summarises the six main epochs and twelve sub-periods of Japanese art, giving each period's characteristic, Christian-era dates and duration, as a convenient framework for the history of art.

metadata.title: [Works Submitted and Exhibits Selected]
metadata.description: Gives the number of works submitted and exhibits selected in each category (Japanese painting, Western painting, sculpture) at the art exhibition described on this page.

metadata.title: [Famous Wrestlers of Tokyo]
metadata.description: The page describes the sumo wrestling profession and its ranks, and lists the famous Tokyo wrestlers of the eastern and western camps with their birth years, weights and heights.

metadata.title: All Subscription Australian Races
metadata.description: Gives the fastest records at Negishi Race Course for All Subscription Australian Races from 1900 to spring 1922, with weights and times.

metadata.title: N.R.C. Subscription Country Bred Griffin Races
metadata.description: Gives the fastest records at Negishi Race Course for N.R.C. Subscription Country Bred Griffin Races from 1900 to spring 1922, with weights and times.

metadata.title: All Subscription Country-Bred Races
metadata.description: Gives the fastest records at Negishi Race Course for All Subscription Country-Bred Races from 1900 to spring 1922, with weights and times.

metadata.title: Speed Swimming
metadata.description: Chief speed swimming results of 1922 at the Tama River pool and other events, giving the winner and time for each distance.

metadata.title: 2nd Inter-collegiate Swimming Contest

metadata.title: Tokyo Y.M.C.A. Indoor Pool Championship Contest
metadata.description: Lists the new senior swimming records set at the Y.M.C.A. indoor pool championship held in November 1922.

metadata.title: [Y.M.C.A. Pool Records Compared with Far Eastern Olympic Games Records]
metadata.description: Compares the swimming records made at the Y.M.C.A. pool with the corresponding records at the Far Eastern Olympic Games.

metadata.title: [Principal Peaks of the Japan Alps]
metadata.description: The page lists the principal peaks of the Japan Alps, grouped into Northern, Central and Southern Alps, with their heights in feet and nearest railway stations for climbers.

metadata.description: The page reports the 1923 autumn inter-collegiate baseball batting and fielding statistics for five Tokyo university teams, Waseda, Keio, Meiji, Hosei and Rikkyo.

metadata.title: [Records Broken at the National Championship Games]
metadata.description: Lists the eight events in which records were broken at the national championship games, with each record-maker and the new mark.

metadata.title: J. A. A. A. Official Records for 1923
metadata.description: Lists the official track and field records for 1923, giving each event's winner, time or distance, venue and year.

metadata.title: Records of the 7th Inter-scholastic Championship Tournament
metadata.description: Gives the event-by-event results of the 7th spring tournament, comparing middle school and normal school competitors.

metadata.title: [Notable Marathon Race Records, 1922]
metadata.description: The table lists notable marathon race records set during 1922, showing the organiser, date, distance, winner and time of each race.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Students Marathon Union Records]
metadata.description: The table gives the records made at the first meeting of the Tokyo Students Marathon Union at Komaba in November, by event, winner and time.

metadata.title: [Girls' Athletic Records, 1922]
metadata.description: The table gives the best records of the girls' athletic contests held in 1922 across the three functions, by event, winner and time.

metadata.title: [Women's Athletic Records]

metadata.caption: (in ¥ million)
metadata.description: The text notes that the revenue surplus has declined recently, and these figures show the annual surplus in yen million from 1917-18 to 1921-22.

metadata.title: Government Disbursements at End of March 1923
metadata.description: The table gives government disbursements by department and special account as they stood at the end of March 1923, with allotments for the following two fiscal years.

metadata.title: Deposit Account
metadata.caption: (Unit: ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The table shows the amount held by the Deposit Department of the Treasury in 1921-22, showing balances brought over, receipts, payments and closing balances by deposit type.

metadata.title: Statistics of National Wealth
metadata.description: The table compares Japan's national wealth in lands and mines at the end of 1913 with the end of 1919, split into government and private holdings, before the September earthquake.

metadata.title: Yield of Leaf
metadata.description: The page introduces the monopoly figures for Japan proper, and this table gives tobacco leaf plantation area, yield and value for 1917-18 to 1921-22.

metadata.title: Manufacture
metadata.description: This table gives the quantities manufactured and sold, with sales value, of cigarettes, cigars and cut tobacco in 1920-21 and 1921-22.

metadata.title: Foreign Leaf Tobacco Bought
metadata.caption: (Unit: ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The text notes that foreign tobacco purchases are recorded in ¥1,000, showing leaf bought from various countries for 1919-20 to 1921-22.

metadata.title: Foreign Manufactured Tobacco Bought
metadata.description: Continuation of the table of foreign manufactured tobacco bought by the monopoly for the three periods shown, listing cigarettes, cigars and cut tobacco.

metadata.title: Salt
metadata.description: Shows the salt field area, annual salt production and value for five fiscal years, part of the monopoly's salt operations.

metadata.title: [Salt Grades by Sodium Chloride Content]
metadata.description: Lists the five grades of purchased salt according to their percentage of sodium chloride content, as set by the Monopoly Bureau.

metadata.title: Camphor
metadata.description: Shows production quantity and value of crude camphor and camphor oil for five fiscal years.

metadata.title: Acreage and Manufacture of Crude Camphor and Oil
metadata.description: Gives the available figures for camphor tree acreage by ownership (state, communal, individual) and for refineries over five years.

metadata.title: Land Tax
metadata.description: Shows the national land tax rates on dwelling and cultivated land, with separate rates for Hokkaido, as part of the discussion of national and local taxes.

metadata.title: Income Tax
metadata.caption: (As revised in 1920 and enforced from Aug. 1 of the year)
metadata.description: Lists the rates of the income tax on juridical persons, covering excess, reserve, dividend and liquidation incomes under the 1920 revision.

metadata.title: [Income Tax Rates for Third Kind Incomes of Individuals]
metadata.description: The revised graduated income tax rates for individuals, shown by income band, illustrate how the heaviest burden falls on large incomes.

metadata.title: [Number of Juridical and Individual Income Tax Payers, Income and Tax, 1920-21]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of juridical and individual income tax payers, their income and the tax collected in 1920-21, by class.

metadata.title: [Income Tax Payers, Income and Tax by Kind, 1919-20]
metadata.description: Continuation of the income tax statistics, showing numbers of payers, income and tax by income kind and totals for 1919-20.

metadata.title: [Foreign Corporations Tax Rates]
metadata.description: Explains how foreign corporations in Japan are taxed on profits exceeding 10 per cent of invested capital, with a rate on income from Japanese business.

metadata.title: [Business Tax Rates by Occupation]
metadata.description: Lists the amended 1914 business tax assessment bases and rates for the main occupation groups.

metadata.title: [Registration Fee Rates Examples]
metadata.description: Gives a few example registration fee rates, which are based on value, as illustrations of the complicated registration fee system.

metadata.title: [Fees for Registration Changes]
metadata.description: The top of the page lists government fees for company registration changes, continuing a fee schedule from the previous page.

metadata.title: Rates of Tax on Sake
metadata.caption: (Assessed by koku, ab. 40 imp. gal.)
metadata.description: This schedule gives the tax rates on sake by class and alcohol strength, levied per koku, with a glossary of the sake terms used.

metadata.title: Sugar Excise
metadata.description: The page gives the sugar excise rates by class and by product, with the tax per picul in yen, as one of several indirect taxes described.

metadata.title: Excise on Woollen and Silk Textiles or Mixtures
metadata.description: The rate of excise charged on woollen and silk textiles and their mixtures, expressed as a share of value, is set out for both fabric types.

metadata.title: Travelling Tax
metadata.description: The travelling tax rates in sen are listed by journey distance and passenger class, showing how the charge rises with distance.

metadata.title: [Succession Duty Rates on Estates]
metadata.description: Shows the graded succession duty rates per 1000 by estate value and by the heir's relation to the deceased family head, as applied to estates.

metadata.title: [Inheritance Duty Rates on Bequests]
metadata.description: Gives the graded inheritance duty rates per 1000 by value of the property bequeathed and by the beneficiary's relation to the testator.

metadata.title: Collection Expenses
metadata.description: Shows the collection expenses of national taxes over the last few years, with tax yield, expense and the expense percentage, since collection costs must be weighed in determining net revenue.

metadata.title: Arrears in National and Local Taxes
metadata.description: Shows the number of defaulters, the arrears amount and the loss to the Treasury for national and local taxes in the years ended March 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Average Amount of Taxes per Capita
metadata.description: Gives the average tax paid per person, split into national, prefectural and communal taxes, with the total and rate on national tax for 1917 to 1921.

metadata.title: National Debts, Raised, Redeemed, Outstanding and Interest Thereof; Ratio per Capita
metadata.description: Shows national debt figures for 1918 to 1923: amounts redeemed and issued, outstanding debt, debt and interest per capita, to illustrate growth of the national debt.

metadata.title: National Loans Outstanding
metadata.caption: Domestic Loans (March 31, 1923)
metadata.description: Lists the domestic national loans with years of issue and redemption, amounts issued and outstanding as of March 31, 1923, with totals.

metadata.title: Foreign Loans
metadata.caption: (July 1, 1924)
metadata.description: Lists the foreign (sterling) loans outstanding as of July 1, 1924, with years of issue, redemption dates, and amounts.

metadata.title: Condition of Loans Raised Abroad
metadata.description: Shows the issue price, commission and net proceeds per £100-type unit for Government and other loans raised abroad, to illustrate the terms of recent overseas borrowing.

metadata.title: [Loans Issued to France, Russia and China]
metadata.description: Lists the government loans issued to France, Russia and China, with issue price, interest, redemption date and amounts, showing totals for each country and a grand total.

metadata.title: Loans to China
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows how Japan's loans to China are classified by central government, local government and private borrowers, and whether they have been advanced or not yet advanced.

metadata.title: [Special Undertaking Expenditure by Fiscal Year, 1920-21 to 1928-29]
metadata.description: The table gives annual expenditure figures for the public undertakings (telephone, telegraph, education, roadmaking, railways and colonial undertakings) by fiscal year, with the note explaining carried-over items.

metadata.title: [Japanese Government Securities Held at Home and Abroad]
metadata.description: The table shows how the total amount and its holdings at home and abroad changed from 1916 to 1923, as the balance of trade turned against Japan and the amount diminished.

metadata.title: Finance of Hokkaido, Prefectures & Civic Corporations
metadata.caption: (In ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives revenue and expenses of Hokkaido, the prefectures, cities, towns and villages, with totals, for four fiscal years, introducing the discussion of prefectural finance.

metadata.title: Revenue Items
metadata.description: Shows national government revenue items by source for three fiscal years, with the 1920–21 figures actual and the later two years estimated.

metadata.title: Expenditure Items
metadata.description: Shows national government expenditure by item for the same three fiscal years, following the revenue items, with the 1920–21 figures actual and later years estimated.

metadata.title: Cities — Revenue Items
metadata.description: Shows municipal revenue of cities for four fiscal years, split into taxes and rates and other sources, illustrating local finance growth.

metadata.title: Cities — Expenditure Items
metadata.description: Lists city expenditure by category over four fiscal years, showing how spending on offices, public works, education and other items changed.

metadata.title: Towns and Villages — Revenue Items
metadata.description: Shows revenue of towns and villages for four fiscal years, comparing taxes and rates with other sources of income.

metadata.title: Towns and Villages — Expenditure Items
metadata.description: Lists expenditure of towns and villages by category over four fiscal years, showing the weight of education and offices in local budgets.

metadata.title: Local Loans Outstanding
metadata.description: Shows the amount of local loans outstanding at each March 31st from 1918 to 1922, by prefectures, counties, cities, towns and villages, and local associations.

metadata.title: Classification of Local Loans Outstanding
metadata.description: Breaks down the local loans outstanding at each March 31st from 1918 to 1922 by purpose, such as education, sanitation, industry and public works.

metadata.title: [Bonds and Debentures Issued by Banks and Companies, 1916-1921]
metadata.description: The figures show the annual totals of bonds and debentures issued by banks and companies from 1916 to 1921, illustrating the growth of capital raising before the discussion of typical issues.

metadata.title: [Typical Bond Issues of 1921 and 1922]
metadata.description: Typical debenture issues of 1921 and 1922 with issue price, term and yield, illustrating the high yields in the money market that the text discusses.

metadata.title: Taxable & Private Owned Land
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000 cho)
metadata.description: The table gives the total area of taxable land by category for January 1 in 1919 to 1921, showing the scale of cultivated and forest land in private ownership.

metadata.title: [Percentage of Taxable Land and Per Capita Rate of Tax]
metadata.description: The page gives the share of taxable land in gross area by category, with per capita tax rates on taxable land, for 1919 to 1921.

metadata.title: Area of Arable Land in Japan Proper
metadata.description: The table classifies Japan proper's arable land by landed farmers' area, tenanted area and totals, split into paddy field and upland, for 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Number of Families Engaged in Farming
metadata.description: The table gives the number of farming families by category (landed farmers, tenants, combining tenantry) and their total, for 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: Landed Farmers Classified by Area Cultivated per Farmer's Family
metadata.description: The table shows how landed farmers' families are distributed by the area of land they cultivate, comparing 1920 and 1921.

metadata.title: [Assessed Value of Land and Buildings: Average, Maximum and Minimum per Tan]
metadata.description: Shows the average, maximum and minimum assessed values of paddy, upland and building land, continuing a table from the previous page on land tax valuation.

metadata.title: [Total Assessed Value of Paddy, Upland, Building and Forest Land]
metadata.caption: (Unit: ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the total assessed value of land and buildings in 1888, 1909 and 1921, showing that the land tax base fell while building value rose.

metadata.title: [Average Market Price per Tan of Paddy and Upland Fields]
metadata.description: Shows the average per tan price of paddy and upland fields as computed by the Hypothec Bank of Japan, illustrating the wartime price boom and its partial fall.

metadata.title: [Average Yield per Tan of Paddy Field, 1904–1920]
metadata.caption: (Unit: koku)
metadata.description: Gives the average yield per tan of paddy field over successive periods, illustrating the gradual rise in productive power of tilled land.

metadata.title: Ratio of One-Crop and Two-Crop Farms
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000 cho)
metadata.description: Official returns compare the area of one-crop and two-crop paddy-fields in 1917, 1913 and 1921, showing the recent trend in cropping practice.

metadata.title: Cattle and Horses Employed in Tillage
metadata.description: Returns of the number of horned cattle and horses used for tillage in each year from 1916 to 1920, showing the draught animal labour on Japanese farms.

metadata.title: Rice
metadata.description: Shows rice area, production, average yield, and export and import quantities and values for 1917–1921 with a normal-yield average, illustrating the staple crop's output and trade.

metadata.title: Varieties of Rice Plant
metadata.description: Average yields per tan of the early, middle and late rice varieties at Government Experimental Farms, showing the middle variety to be the most productive.

metadata.title: Consumption and Home Supply
metadata.description: Estimated total home consumption of rice in mil. koku and per capita, by five-year periods, balancing domestic yield against imports and exports.

metadata.title: Barley and Wheat
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Gives the national production of barley, naked barley and wheat for 1919 to 1921, with totals and yield per tan, to show the importance of these staple crops.

metadata.title: [Barley, Naked Barley and Wheat by Field Type, 1921]
metadata.description: Shows how the 1921 barley, naked barley and wheat crops were divided between paddy-field and upland farms, since these crops are mainly grown in upland farms.

metadata.title: Miscellaneous Grains
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Records production of minor grains such as millets, buckwheat and maize for 1918 to 1920, grown mainly in mountainous districts and used as ordinary food by poorer folk.

metadata.title: Beans, Potatoes and Sweet Potatoes
metadata.caption: (Production, in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual production of beans, sweet potatoes and potatoes, illustrating the importance of these subsidiary farm crops in Japanese diet and industry.

metadata.title: Productions of Some Special Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives yearly output of special crops such as indigo, leaf tobacco, cotton, hemp and rape-seed, whose trends the accompanying text comments on.

metadata.title: Productions of Other Minor Crops
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kan)
metadata.description: Lists production of radish, carrot and burdock for 1917 to 1920, showing minor root crops grown alongside the main special crops.

metadata.title: [Minor Crops Production, Konnyaku to Welsh Onion]
metadata.description: This table lists yields of minor vegetables, fibre and industrial crops across several years, showing the agricultural output discussed in the Agriculture chapter before the Stock-Breeding section.

metadata.title: Number of Cattle
metadata.description: Shows the number of cattle in Japan from 1918 to 1920, broken down by cows, bulls, total, calving and deaths, as part of the stock-farming statistics.

metadata.title: Number of Horses
metadata.description: Shows the number of horses in Japan from 1918 to 1920 by native, cross-bred and foreign breeds, with totals, following the cattle figures in the stock-farming statistics.

metadata.title: Number of Sheep, Goats and Swine
metadata.description: Gives the numbers of sheep, goats and swine in Japan for 1917 to 1920, showing the growth of these animal stocks.

metadata.title: Slaughtering Returns
metadata.description: Reports the number of slaughter houses and animals slaughtered by kind (cattle and calves, horses, sheep and goats, swine) for 1918 to 1920.

metadata.title: Statistics on Poultry
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Presents the number of poultry-keeping families, fowls, chickens and eggs produced, with their values, for 1918 to 1920, illustrating the small scale of Japanese poultry farming.

metadata.title: Leading Dairy Districts (1920)
metadata.description: Shows the number of dairies, milk cows and milk output in the leading dairy districts for 1920, and national totals for 1916–1920, as the dairy section surveys production.

metadata.title: [Animal Epidemics by Kind and Year, 1918–1920]
metadata.description: Lists the numbers of animals affected by anthrax, blackleg, cholera, erysipelas and hydrophobia in 1918–1920, illustrating the damage from animal epidemics described in the text.

metadata.title: Output of Fruits
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kan)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of major fruits in Japan from 1916 to 1920, illustrating the growth of fruit culture described in the Horticulture introduction.

metadata.title: Sericultural Families by Season
metadata.description: Gives the number of sericultural families by season for 1919 to 1923, showing the household base of silk production, with the 1921–1923 summer and autumn figures printed under a combined brace.

metadata.title: [Cocoon Output, Egg-Cards Hatched and Total Value]
metadata.description: Gives the number of egg-cards hatched, cocoon output by grade and total value for spring and summer/autumn silkworm varieties from 1918 to 1922.

metadata.title: No. of Establishments and Reeling Basins
metadata.description: Shows the number of silk reeling establishments by basin-count size class, with total establishments and reeling basins, from 1918 to 1922.

metadata.title: Output of Raw Silk
metadata.caption: (In 1,000: 1 kan = lb. 8267)
metadata.description: Gives annual raw silk and waste silk output in kwan with values in yen, plus total value, from 1918 to 1922.

metadata.title: [Yearly Values, 1918-1923]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a yearly series of yen values from 1918 onward; the column headings are not visible on this page.

metadata.title: Silkworm Eggs — Amount Produced (in No. of Moths)
metadata.caption: (in No. of moths)
metadata.description: Shows the number of silkworm egg producers and the number of moths' eggs produced, reproductive and industrial, with totals, for 1918 to 1920.

metadata.title: Mulberry Plantations
metadata.description: Gives the area of mulberry fields in cho for each year ending June, 1916 to 1921, to show the growth of mulberry cultivation.

metadata.title: Japanese and Foreign Exporters of Raw Silk
metadata.description: Compares the number of raw silk bales exported by Japanese and foreign firms each season, with the percentage share of each, to show the growing role of Japanese exporters.

metadata.title: Statistics on Tea
metadata.description: Shows the cultivated tea area and number of tea manufacturers in Japan for 1915 to 1920, illustrating the stagnation of the industry described in the text.

metadata.title: Output of Various Kinds of Tea
metadata.caption: (kwan)
metadata.description: Shows the annual output in kwan of each grade of green, black and oolong tea from 1917 to 1920, illustrating the declining tea production of the period.

metadata.title: Leading Tea Producing Districts (1920)
metadata.description: Lists the output and value in 1920 of the leading tea-producing prefectures, showing which districts dominated Japan's tea production.

metadata.title: [Tea Export by Kinds, 1917 and 1920]
metadata.description: Gives the quantity in kin and value in yen of each kind of tea exported in 1917 and 1920, showing the sharp fall in the export trade.

metadata.title: [Area of Forests by Ownership, 1915–1920]
metadata.caption: (in cho)
metadata.description: Forests in Japan proper are classified by usage and ownership, and this table gives the area of each ownership class at the end of 1915, 1918 and 1920.

metadata.title: Yield of Forests in Yen (Dec. 1920)
metadata.description: Shows the annual yield of forests by ownership category in December 1920, split into timber, fagots and totals, to illustrate the value of forest produce.

metadata.title: [State Forests Receipts, Expenses and Balance, 1917–1920]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000), excluding Hokkaido and the Bonin
metadata.description: Gives the receipts, expenses and balance of State forests for recent years, showing the profit trend the text discusses as modest.

metadata.title: Forest Yield of Principal Timbers in Japan Proper, 1920
metadata.caption: (1 koku = 10 cubic ft.)
metadata.description: Reports the 1920 forest yield, in koku and yen, of the principal timber species in Japan proper.

metadata.title: Principal By-Products
metadata.caption: (1920 in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the main forest by-products of 1920 with their values in thousand yen, with a total for the group.

metadata.title: [By-Products from State Forests and Wild Lands]
metadata.description: Gives the by-products obtained from State forests and wild lands in 1920, with a total including other items.

metadata.title: [Foreign Timber Arrivals by Kind, 1914–1921]
metadata.description: The table, taken from the Oriental Economist, shows yearly arrivals of American and other foreign timber, mainly cedar, pine and fir, supporting the text on the rising inflow of foreign timbers.

metadata.title: Catches and Marine Production
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's fishery catches and marine products by category over 1918 to 1921, illustrating the economic weight of the fishing industry.

metadata.title: Principal Catches
metadata.description: Lists the principal fish catches by quantity (kan) and value (¥1,000) for 1919 and 1920, with a total including other catches.

metadata.title: Principal Marine Products
metadata.description: Gives the value of two principal dried marine products, dried bonito and dried cuttle-fish, for 1920 and 1921.

metadata.title: [Fishery Products Output, 1920–1921]
metadata.description: Values of dried and salted fishery products (herring, sardine, trout, prawn, laver, isinglass) for 1920 and 1921, continuing the fishery statistics from the previous page.

metadata.title: Export of Fish and Marine Products
metadata.caption: Marine products, fishes cured in cans or bottles, and fish and whale-oils, figure on the customs report as follows (in value of ¥1,000):
metadata.description: Customs-reported export values of marine products, canned or bottled fish, and fish and whale oils for 1919 to 1921, with totals.

metadata.title: Aquiculture
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Output values of aquaculture products (oyster, carp, eel, laver and total) for 1918 to 1920, presented alongside the note on pearl fishery.

metadata.title: Deep Sea Catches
metadata.caption: (In Japan proper for 1921).
metadata.description: Shows the 1921 deep-sea catches in Japan proper by fishing method, with boat numbers, tonnage and total catch value, illustrating the growth of pelagic fishing under state bounty.

metadata.title: [Coral Fishing Figures by Prefecture]
metadata.description: This is the closing part of a prefectural list of coral fishing figures, followed by a note that a new coral bed has been found near Ogasawara and its exports go mainly to Italy.

metadata.title: Distribution of Strata
metadata.description: The table gives the relative percentage of sedimentary and igneous strata existing in Japan, classified by geological period, as an overview of the country's geology.

metadata.title: [Gold, Silver, Copper and Lead Production]
metadata.description: Shows Japan's annual mine output of gold, silver, copper and lead, quantities and values, for 1917 to 1921, as a statistical overview of the mining industry.

metadata.title: [Iron, Iron Pyrite, Antimony and Manganese Production]
metadata.description: Gives Japan's annual output of iron ore, iron pyrite, antimony and manganese, quantities and values, for 1917 to 1921.

metadata.title: [Coal, Sulphur, Petroleum and Total Mining Value]
metadata.description: Presents Japan's annual output of coal, sulphur and crude petroleum with values, plus the total mining value including other minerals, for 1917 to 1921.

metadata.title: [Copper Production, Import, Export, Consumption and Stock, 1914–1921]
metadata.description: Gives Japan's copper production, imports, exports, domestic consumption and stocks for 1914–1921 to show the post-war decline in output and rising reliance on imported metal.

metadata.title: Principal Metal Mines (in 1920)
metadata.caption: (Figures in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the leading metal mines producing over ¥500,000 a year in 1920, by district, with their gold, silver and copper output and total value.

metadata.title: [Coal Reserves by Region]
metadata.caption: (in 1000 tons)
metadata.description: Gives the estimated hidden and workable coal stores of the three main coal-producing regions of Japan, as set out in the Mining Bureau's investigation.

metadata.title: Investment
metadata.description: Shows the growth of the coal-mining companies in Japan from 1914 to 1921, by number of companies and capital figures, quoted from the Oriental Economist.

metadata.title: Output, Import & Export
metadata.caption: (in 1000 tons)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's coal output, imports, exports and export balance in selected years from 1914 to 1921, quoted from the Oriental Economist.

metadata.title: Rate of Increase of Output
metadata.description: Shows the increase of coal output and its rate, both total and average per year, across successive periods from 1877 to 1921.

metadata.title: Principal Uses of Coal (in 1000 tons)
metadata.description: Shows how Japanese coal output was consumed by ship, railway, factory and salt-refining uses from 1914 to 1921, illustrating the decline the text describes.

metadata.title: Output of the Chief Coal-Fields in Japan Proper
metadata.description: Lists the output of the principal Japanese coal-fields in 1919 and 1921 together with the company working each field, supporting the discussion of the coal industry.

metadata.title: Analysis of Coals from the Principal Coal-Fields
metadata.description: Shows the proximate analysis, caking quality, specific gravity and calorific power of coals from the principal coal-fields.

metadata.title: Crude Oil Output, 1913-1921
metadata.caption: (In 1000 koku)
metadata.description: Shows annual crude oil yield in thousand koku from 1913 to 1921, illustrating the rise after the rotary system and the later steady decline.

metadata.title: Output of Refined Oil
metadata.caption: (In 1,000 koku)
metadata.description: Gives the output of refined oil by type (volatile, lamp, solar, heavy, machine) in selected years to show the position of refined oil production.

metadata.title: Foreign Oil Arrivals in Japan
metadata.caption: (In 1000 koku; exclusive of the import by the Navy)
metadata.description: Lists recorded arrivals of refined and crude foreign oil in Japan during the five years from 1917, showing growing reliance on imports.

metadata.title: [Mining Investment by Group, 1917-1921]
metadata.caption: Capital paid up being in ¥1,000
metadata.description: The text introduces this table as showing the steady growth of mining investment from 1917 to 1921, split into metal, coal, combined, petroleum and other groups.

metadata.title: [Mining Companies by Number and Paid-Up Capital, 1917–1921]
metadata.description: Shows the number of mining companies and their paid-up capital in groups IV and V and in total for 1917 to 1921, as background to the mining industry.

metadata.title: Condition of Mine-Workers
metadata.caption: Mine-workers as classified by the mines they are working at and by the age and sex, at the end of June, 1920
metadata.description: Gives the number of male and female mine-workers by age group, mine type and above or below ground at the end of June 1920, with totals.

metadata.title: Accidents at the Mines
metadata.description: Shows the number of mine accidents and the resulting casualties (deaths and injuries by severity) for each year from 1916 to 1920, illustrating the safety record of Japanese mining.

metadata.title: [Factories Employing Over 5 Operatives, 1914-1921]
metadata.description: Official statistics of factories employing over five operatives, comparing motive-power and manual-power factories and male and female workers for 1914, 1919, 1920 and 1921.

metadata.title: [Factories Run by Motive and Manual Power and Employees by Industry, 1921]
metadata.description: For 1921, factories are classified by nature of industry, showing motive-power and manual-power factories, horse power and number of employees.

metadata.title: [Motive Powers Classified by Kind of Engine, 1921]
metadata.description: Shows the number of engines and horse power by kind of engine used in factories in 1921, reflecting the growth of motive power since 1914.

metadata.title: [Yarn Output by Count Grade]
metadata.description: Shows the average annual yarn output in bales by coarse, medium and fine count grades, with each grade's percentage share, illustrating the shift toward finer yarns.

metadata.title: Cotton Yarns in Customs Returns
metadata.caption: (in bales)
metadata.description: Summarises the supply and demand balance of cotton yarn from 1918 to 1922, comparing output, imports, exports, home consumption and balance.

metadata.title: Raw Materials Imported
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 piculs)
metadata.description: Gives the imports of raw cotton, including cotton in the seed and cotton ginned, by country of origin for 1921 and 1922, explaining where Japan's supply came from.

metadata.title: [Paid-up Capital, Reserves and Average Dividend of Spinning Companies]
metadata.description: Shows the paid-up capital, reserves and average dividend of spinning companies from 1913 to 1921, illustrating financial growth after the war boom.

metadata.title: Average Working Spindles Per Day
metadata.description: Gives the average number of working spindles per day in the cotton spinning industry by type, with looms and spindles per loom, for 1913 to 1921.

metadata.title: Data on Leading Companies (1921)
metadata.description: Lists the capital, factories, spindles and looms of the four leading hempen spinning companies in 1921, the largest establishments in that industry.

metadata.title: Statistics on Textile Industry
metadata.description: Gives the official figures for factories, looms, operatives and output of the textile industry for 1919 to 1921, introduced by a discussion of width and length defects in cloth.

metadata.title: [Output of Fabrics Classified]
metadata.caption: (Yen 1,000)
metadata.description: Classifies the yearly output of fabrics by type (silk, mixed, cotton, hempen and miscellaneous) for 1919 to 1921, with a note that woollen data appear elsewhere.

metadata.title: Cotton Fabrics Statistics
metadata.description: Shows the development of cotton factories, motive-power use, operatives, output, imports and exports from 1913 to 1920, marking the peak of prosperity in 1919.

metadata.title: Staple Products
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists output of principal staple cotton products, such as white cloth, striped stuff, flannel, crape and towels, with a total value, for 1913 and 1918 to 1921.

metadata.title: [Silk Factories, 1920]
metadata.description: Official data on the silk and silk-and-cotton fabric industry give the number of factories, those run by motive power, and operatives for 1920.

metadata.title: Staple Exports
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Staple silk exports for 1920 and 1921 by fabric type, giving quantity and value, with notes on the main customer countries for each fabric.

metadata.title: Data on Woolen Fabrics
metadata.description: The table gives yearly figures for Japan's woollen fabric industry from 1917 to 1921, covering factories, looms, operatives and output values by fabric type, supporting the discussion of the muslin-de-laine trade.

metadata.title: Import of Raw Materials
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows Japan's imports of tops and wool, in kin and yen, for 1913 and 1919–1921, as part of the industry statistics.

metadata.title: Staple Import and Export of Fabrics
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the main imports and exports of woven fabrics (serges, cloth, mixed fabrics, blankets) for 1913 and 1919–1921.

metadata.title: Statistics of Muslin
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
