metadata.title: Conventional Tariff Between Japan and Great Britain
metadata.description: Lists the conventional tariff duty rates applying between Japan and Great Britain on paints, linen yarns and cotton tissues, under the most-favored-nation arrangements described above.

metadata.title: [Import Duty Rates on Cotton Tissues by Thread Count and Weight]
metadata.description: The page lists the import duty schedule for cotton tissues, graded by weight and thread count, with rates per 100 kin for gray, bleached and other grades.

metadata.title: [Customs Duties on Tissues of Wool and Mixed Tissues]
metadata.description: The page lists customs duties on woollen and mixed woollen tissues, by weight per square metre and fibre content, with rates per 100 kin.

metadata.title: [Customs Duties on Iron]
metadata.description: The page gives customs duties on iron, beginning with pig iron in lumps and ingots at a rate per 100 kin, followed by the heading for plates and sheets.

metadata.title: Tarif Conventionnel Entre le Japon et la France
metadata.description: The French-language conventional tariff between Japan and France gives, for each wine and food product, the percentage of the Japanese national tariff and the resulting duty on French goods.

metadata.title: Tarif Conventionnel Entre Le Japon Et L'Italie
metadata.description: The table lists the conventional Japan–Italy tariff, giving the units and duties on preserved foods, pasta, vermouth, marsala and wines.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Municipal Revenue and Expenditure, Years Ending March 1922-1924]
metadata.description: The text notes that Tokyo's municipal finances expanded sharply after the Russo-Japanese War, and this table gives revenue and expenditure for the years ending March 1922 to 1924.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Municipal Taxes, 1921-1923]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The text explains that Tokyo citizens bear very heavy taxation, and this table breaks down municipal tax receipts by type for 1921 to 1923.

metadata.title: Revenue and Expenditure of the General Account and 14 Special Accounts of the Municipality Budget, 1923-24
metadata.description: The text introduces the Tokyo municipality's 1923-24 budget, and this table lists revenue and expenditure for the general account and each special account.

metadata.title: [Allotments of Road Improvement Funds, 1920-1926]
metadata.description: Shows how the seven-year road improvement fund of ¥39,468 thousand is allotted year by year from 1920 to 1926 in Tokyo.

metadata.title: [Water Supply Condition at End of March 1923]
metadata.description: Gives the state of Tokyo's water supply at the end of March 1923, showing meters, population and houses supplied.

metadata.title: [Electric Tramway Service Data, 1919-1921]
metadata.description: Summarises the municipal electric tramway service after the 1911 municipalization, showing mileage, working mileage, passengers and receipts for the years ended March 1919-1921.

metadata.title: Municipal Assets & Liabilities
metadata.description: The page gives the Municipality of Tokyo's assets at the end of November for 1920 to 1922, split into general and electricity department holdings.

metadata.title: [Osaka Settled Accounts, 1921–1923]
metadata.description: The settled accounts of Osaka city, general and special, for the past two years and the estimate for 1923, are set out to show the city's finances.

metadata.title: [Osaka City Revenue and Expenditure Estimate, 1923–24]
metadata.description: Details of Osaka's 1923–24 estimate, by item, showing revenue and expenditure at the end of August.

metadata.title: [Working Mileage and Passengers of Electric Tramways]
metadata.description: Shows the working mileage, passenger numbers and passenger receipts of the city's tramway service for successive years, illustrating its growth.

metadata.title: [Kyoto Ordinary Finance]
metadata.description: Gives the ordinary revenue and expenditure of the city of Kyoto for the two fiscal years 1921-22 and 1922-23.

metadata.title: [Special Account Estimates for 1923-24]
metadata.description: Lists the estimated revenue and expenditure of Kyoto's special accounts for canal and water-power works and waterworks for 1923-24.

metadata.title: [Municipal Undertakings — Revenue and Expenditure (continued)]
metadata.description: Continuation of the table of municipal undertakings, listing each undertaking's revenue and expenditure before the text describes the three leading undertakings.

metadata.title: [Electric Tramway Working Results]
metadata.description: Shows the number of passengers and passenger receipts for the municipal tramway and three private tramway companies, the results of their working.

metadata.title: [Yokohama Annual Revenue and Estimated Expenditure]
metadata.description: Gives Yokohama's annual revenue and estimated expenditure for the fiscal years 1921-22 and 1922-23.

metadata.title: [Annual Finance of Kobe City, 1919-20 to 1922-23]
metadata.description: Shows how Kobe City's annual revenue and expenditure, including special accounts, grew across the given fiscal years, illustrating the marked increase in its municipal finance.

metadata.title: [Working Results of Hanshin Railways, 1922]
metadata.description: The text gives the 1922 working results of the Hanshin and Hyogo electric railway and tramway companies, showing passengers carried and receipts for each line.

metadata.title: [Tax Burdens in the Five Larger Cities, Fiscal Year 1922-23]
metadata.caption: (Unit: ¥)
metadata.description: Based on Tokyo Municipality's investigation, this table compares national, prefectural and municipal tax burdens in the five larger cities as shown in the 1922-23 budgets.

metadata.title: [Six Premier Cities: Wards, Totals, Per Capita Rates and Population]
metadata.description: Compares the six premier cities by ward area figures, total figures, per capita rates and estimated population, as a background to the social-works discussion.

metadata.title: [Municipal Social Work Expenditure, 1922-23]
metadata.description: Shows the Home Office figures for total municipal expenditure and social work fund in six cities for the 1922-23 fiscal year, illustrating municipal social work.

metadata.title: Temperature
metadata.description: Following the geography description of Chosen, this table gives the average highest and lowest temperatures recorded at five stations, Fusan, Ninsen, Gensan, Seoul and Pyengyang.

metadata.title: Weather Condition in the Year
metadata.description: Summarises the year's weather at five Korean stations, giving clear or cloudy and rainy days and the dates of early and late frost and snow.

metadata.title: Native Population
metadata.caption: (Dec. 31)
metadata.description: Gives the native (Korean) population and households at year-end for 1910, 1920 and 1922, showing growth under Japanese rule.

metadata.title: Births and Still-births
metadata.description: Lists the number of live births and still-births by sex for 1911, 1920 and 1922.

metadata.title: Deaths, Marriages and Divorces
metadata.description: Gives the numbers of deaths by sex, and of marriages and divorces, for 1911, 1920 and 1922.

metadata.title: Ratio per 1000 Population of Births, Still-births, Deaths, Marriages and Divorces
metadata.description: Expresses the vital statistics of the native population as annual ratios per 1,000 population for 1910, 1920 and 1922.

metadata.title: Japanese in Korea
metadata.description: Shows the Japanese settler population in Korea by household and sex for 1910, 1920 and 1922, following the introductory note on their growth.

metadata.title: Population in Principal Cities, End 1922
metadata.description: Gives the population of Seoul at the end of 1922, divided into Japanese and Korean residents with the total including others.

metadata.title: [Japanese and Korean Residents at Open Ports (continued)]
metadata.description: Continuing the table of Japanese and Korean residents by open port in Korea, showing counts for each locality and the total including others.

metadata.title: Foreigners in Korea
metadata.description: Shows the number of male, female and total foreign residents in Korea for selected years from 1911 to 1922, with a nationality breakdown for 1922.

metadata.title: Prefectures or Provinces of Korea and Their Seats of Office
metadata.description: The thirteen provinces of Korea, listed in two columns with the seat of office of each, under the heading of local administration.

metadata.title: Budget
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: The page gives the Korean (Chosen) government budget for fiscal 1922–23 and 1923–24, setting out revenue and expenditure by ordinary and extraordinary heads in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: Continuing Expenditure
metadata.description: Shows government continuing expenditure on public works and enterprises, by item, split into amounts spent up to 1923 and planned for 1923-1933.

metadata.title: [Yearly Allotment of Continuing Expenditure After 1923-24]
metadata.description: Lists the yearly allotments of continuing expenditure after 1923-24, given in two columns of fiscal years.

metadata.title: Debts (End March, 1923)
metadata.description: Lists the national debts outstanding at the end of March 1923, with amounts, interest rates, years floated and redemption dates.

metadata.title: Volume of Trade
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: Summarises Korea's foreign trade from 1919 to 1923, giving merchandise imports, exports and totals, and specie and bullion movements in yen.

metadata.title: Staple Exports
metadata.description: Lists the value of Korea's principal staple exports in 1922 against 1913 and 1923 figures, showing changes in agricultural and mineral or manufactured goods.

metadata.title: Banking Statistics at End of September 1923
metadata.description: The banking statistics for Korea at the end of September 1923 show the capital, reserves, notes, deposits and loans of the Bank of Chosen, the Chosen Industrial Bank and ordinary banks.

metadata.title: [Cotton Cultivation in Korea, Area and Harvest, 1920–1922]
metadata.caption: (Unit: 1,000)
metadata.description: The Cotton section reports experimental and planned cotton cultivation in Korea, giving the area planted and the harvest of upland and native varieties for 1920 to 1922.

metadata.title: Principal Mineral Production (in unit of 1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly output of gold, Takō (a sealed quartz vein ore), iron ore, pig-iron and coal in Chosen for 1920–1922, in quantity and value.

metadata.title: [Fishery Business Summary, End of 1922]
metadata.description: The fishery industry's existing state, excluding whaling, is summarised by number of Korean and Japanese fishermen, annual catch value and marine products for 1922.

metadata.title: [Development of Manufacturing Industry in Korea, 1911-1921]
metadata.description: The table, taken from official reports, shows the rapid growth of manufacturing industry in Korea from annexation in 1910 up to 1921, comparing factories, capital, workers, power and output.

metadata.title: [Daily Wages of Artisans and Labourers in Korea]
metadata.description: Daily wages paid in Korea to skilled artisans and labourers, given separately for Japanese and Korean workers in yen.

metadata.title: [Schools and Pupils in Korea, March 1922]
metadata.description: Number of schools, staff and public pupils (boys and girls) in Korean common, higher, special and technical schools in March 1922, following the account of the education system.

metadata.title: [New Cases of Civil, Criminal and Preliminary Affairs]
metadata.description: Gives the latest figures for new civil, criminal, preliminary and other legal cases, introduced by the statement that the latest statistics are as follows.

metadata.title: [Prison Inmates at Year End]
metadata.description: Shows the number of prison inmates at the year end, by sex and total, with the 1922 figures further broken down by Japanese, Korean and foreign inmates.

metadata.title: [Traffic Results of the Chosen Government Railways]
metadata.caption: (Traffic results are shown below in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the annual traffic results of the Chosen Government Railways for the years ended March 1920 to 1922, giving passengers, luggage, goods and receipts.

metadata.title: [Average Figures Per Mile Per Day of Chosen Government Railways]
metadata.description: Gives the average daily passengers, goods and receipts per mile of Chosen Government Railways line for 1920 to 1922, showing the per-mile productivity of the system.

metadata.title: [Financial Position at End of March 1923]
metadata.description: Shows the company's paid-up capital, loans, available funds and borrowings as at the end of March 1923, given as the statistics for the settlement scheme.

metadata.title: [Land Owned and Leased by the Company and Settlers, March 1923]
metadata.description: Gives the land the company owned and leased to settlers, and the number of settlers, at the end of March 1923, as part of the settlement scheme described on this page.

metadata.title: Temperature (1923)
metadata.description: Monthly, average, maximum and minimum temperatures for two stations in Taiwan in 1923, given to illustrate the island's warm, tropical climate.

metadata.title: Rainfall (1923)
metadata.description: Gives monthly, total and maximum rainfall for six Taiwan stations in 1923, illustrating the island's rainfall pattern.

metadata.title: Number of Days of Rainfall
metadata.description: Lists the number of rainy days at six Taiwan stations for each year from 1917 to 1922.

metadata.title: Population
metadata.description: Gives the male, female and total population of Japanese, natives and foreigners in Taiwan for 1921 and 1922.

metadata.title: [Births, Stillbirths, Deaths, Marriages and Divorces, 1918–1922]
metadata.description: Gives yearly vital statistics of births, stillbirths, deaths, marriages and divorces in Taiwan from 1918 to 1922.

metadata.title: [Vital Statistics, 1918-1922]
metadata.description: Shows Japan's annual birth, death, marriage and divorce rates per 1,000 population, plus sex ratio at birth and deaths per 100 births, for 1918 to 1922.

metadata.title: Principal Cities at the End of 1922
metadata.description: Lists the population of the principal cities of Formosa (Taiwan) at the end of 1922, as the book turns to the island's aborigines.

metadata.title: Revenue and Expenditure
metadata.caption: Budget for 1922-23 & 1923-24; Revenue (¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: The budget table gives estimated national revenue, ordinary and extraordinary, for fiscal years 1922-23 and 1923-24, accompanying the note on the new local administration.

metadata.title: Education (March, 1923)
metadata.description: Number of schools, teachers and students in each type of educational institution in Japan's territories as of March 1923.

metadata.title: [Law Court Cases, Civil and Criminal]
metadata.description: Shows the number of civil and criminal cases brought, disposed of and remaining at first-instance and appeal courts in Taiwan, illustrating the working of the law courts.

metadata.title: Area of Afforestation (Ko)
metadata.description: Gives the area afforested in Ko by government and private bodies, by camphor and other trees, for the three years ended March 1920–1922, reflecting forestry efforts.

metadata.title: [Forest Stamps and Shakujime by Species]
metadata.description: Gives the number of stamps and the shakujime volume of the main conifer and broad-leaf species, showing the timber resources underlying the Government utilization and felling programme described in the text.

metadata.title: Area of Cultivation (in 1,000 cho)
metadata.description: Shows the cultivated area of paddy and upland fields and the area planted to rice, sweet potato, beans, sugar cane and ground nut in Formosa for 1920 to 1922, illustrating the agricultural section's text.

metadata.title: Principal Crops (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly output of Taiwan's principal crops, such as rice, rush, groundnut, sweet potato, beans, jute and ramie, for 1920 to 1922.

metadata.title: Fruits (in 1,000 kin)
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 kin)
metadata.description: Gives the quantities of fruits (oranges, longan, banana and pine-apple) produced in Taiwan in the years shown.

metadata.title: Live Stock
metadata.caption: No. of live stock (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the number of buffalo, cattle, swine and goats kept in Taiwan from 1920 to 1922, counted in thousands.

metadata.title: Value of Catches and Products (¥1,000)
metadata.description: Gives the value in yen of Taiwan's fishery catches (fish, shell fish, seaweed), marine products and aquiculture for 1920 to 1922.

metadata.title: [Mineral Production by Year, Gold to Petroleum]
metadata.description: The table gives recent annual output of gold, gold-copper, alluvial gold, copper, coal and petroleum at the mines, shown in the text as mainly Japanese-run except coal and alluvial gold.

metadata.title: [Mineral Production of Gold, Silver, Copper, Coal, Petroleum and Sulphur, 1920-1922]
metadata.description: The table shows the annual production of the principal mines near Keelung over 1920 to 1922, with gold, silver, copper, coal, petroleum and sulphur output.

metadata.title: [Sugar Plantations and Yield]
metadata.description: Shows the sugar plantation area and total cane yield in Taiwan for each year ended June, with the portion used for sugar.

metadata.title: [Output of Sugar]
metadata.caption: (in 1000 kin)
metadata.description: Records the yearly output of sugar in Taiwan by type, introduced by the statement that the output makes the following record.

metadata.title: Production at the Modern-style Refineries
metadata.caption: (1000 Kin)
metadata.description: Gives the 1920 and 1921–1922 production of each modern-style sugar refinery in Taiwan, with company totals.

metadata.title: [Tea Production by Season and Value, 1918–1920]
metadata.description: Shows Formosan tea output by season and its value for 1918 to 1920, illustrating the sharp fall in 1920 after the post-war market reaction.

metadata.title: Production of Opium, Salt, Camphor and Tobacco
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)
metadata.description: Shows annual output of opium, salt, camphor, camphor-oil and tobacco in Taiwan for 1918 to 1920, illustrating the island's production under government monopolies.

metadata.title: Trade
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Compares Taiwan's commodity trade and specie and bullion movements with Japan Proper and with foreign countries for 1919 to 1922.

metadata.title: Chief Exports
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Lists the main commodities Taiwan exported in value terms, such as tea, sugar, camphor and coal, for 1920 to 1922.

metadata.title: Chief Imports
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the chief goods Taiwan imported, such as opium, petroleum, tobacco leaf and beans, over 1920 to 1922.

metadata.title: Distribution of Exports
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Taiwan's exports sent to each main destination, including China, Hongkong, the Dutch Indies, Great Britain, the U.S.A. and the Philippines, for 1919 to 1922.

metadata.title: Distribution of Imports
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the value of Japan's imports from China, British India, the Dutch Indies, Great Britain, the U.S.A. and Persia for 1919 to 1922, illustrating the trade distribution by country.

metadata.title: Budget
metadata.description: The budget estimates for Karafuto for fiscal years 1922–23 and 1923–24 are set out in thousands of yen, showing ordinary and extraordinary revenue sources.

metadata.title: [Karafuto Government Expenditure, 1922–'23 and 1923–'24]
metadata.description: Shows Karafuto's government ordinary and extraordinary expenditure items for the fiscal years 1922–'23 and 1923–'24, with a grand total for each year.

metadata.title: [Catches and Manufactures of Karafuto, 1920–1922]
metadata.description: The text introduces a short table giving fishery catches and manufactures of Karafuto for the last few years, showing the yearly value of the island's fishing output.

metadata.title: [Light Railway Traffic and Working Results, Years Ended March]
metadata.description: Gives the train mileage, passengers, goods hauled, revenue, expenses and profit or loss of the light railway for the three years ended March 1921 to 1923.

metadata.title: [Population of South Manchuria, 1921]
metadata.description: Gives the 1921 population of South Manchuria by nationality and sex, the main census figures for the territory described in this section.

metadata.title: [Inhabitants of the Railway Zone at End of 1921]
metadata.description: Records the inhabitants living in the railway zone at the end of 1921, supplementing the main population figures given above.

metadata.title: Three Principal Cities at the End of 1921
metadata.description: Shows the population of the three principal cities of South Manchuria, Dairen, Port Arthur and Kinobou, at the end of 1921, by sex.

metadata.title: Budget for 1922-23 and 1923-24
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Sets out the government budget for the two fiscal years 1922-23 and 1923-24, covering ordinary and extraordinary revenue and expenditure of the territory.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade for 1921
metadata.caption: (at Dairen, Yinkow, Antung & Daitoko)
metadata.description: Shows the value of foreign trade handled at the Kwantung leased-territory ports in 1921, by trading country, in Haikwan taels.

metadata.title: [Educational Institutions Under the Administration Office and South Manchuria Railway, 1922]
metadata.description: Lists the schools maintained in the Kwantung territory and along the South Manchuria Railway zone, with their staff and pupil numbers for 1922.

metadata.title: [Coal Output and Equipment at Fushun and Yentai Mines]
metadata.description: Gives the coal output of the Fushun and Yentai mines for the years ended March 1920–1922, with the equipment in use at Fushun and Yentai at March 31, 1922.

metadata.title: Business Report for 1923-24 Year
metadata.description: The table reports the South Manchuria Railway's business receipts and expenses by undertaking for the 1923-24 year, showing overall operating results.

metadata.title: Principal Assets and Liabilities
metadata.caption: (¥1,000) (March 31st 1922)
metadata.description: The table gives the company's principal assets and liabilities as of March 31, 1922, showing the financial position of the South Manchuria Railway.

metadata.title: Principal Crops in 1000 Chinese Koku
metadata.description: Shows yearly output of the main crops in the Leased Territory for 1919 to 1921, illustrating the farming products of the region around the Kirin-Changchun railway zone.

metadata.title: Workshops
metadata.description: Shows the number of workshops, Japanese and Chinese employees, and capital in South Manchuria's Leased Territory and railway zone for 1920, with comparative totals for 1919 and 1918.

metadata.title: Principal Manufactures
metadata.caption: (in 1,000)*
metadata.description: Gives yearly output and value of the main South Manchurian manufactures (flour, iron, bricks, leather and soap) for 1918 to 1920.

metadata.title: [Area, Population and Position of the Mariana, Caroline and Marshall Islands]
metadata.description: The table gives the area, population and geographic position of the principal islands of the Japanese-administered South Sea groups, Mariana, Caroline and Marshall, preceding the description of their climate and natives.

metadata.title: [Number of After-Shocks Felt in Tokyo, September–October]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of after-shocks felt in Tokyo in each ten-day period, showing how rapidly their frequency declined after the great earthquake.

metadata.title: [Noted Fatal Earthquakes of the Past]
metadata.chapter: The Destruction of Life and Property
metadata.chapter_raw: The Destruction of Life and Property
metadata.description: Lists noted catastrophic earthquakes of the past two and a half centuries, with their places, dates and death tolls, to illustrate the loss of life caused by such shocks.

metadata.title: [Casualties of the September 1 Earthquake by Place]
metadata.description: Relief Bureau figures giving the killed, injured, missing and total casualties of the September 1 disaster for the affected districts, Tokyo and Yokohama.

metadata.title: [Foreign Sufferers in Tokyo and Yokohama]
metadata.description: Department of Education investigation showing the number of Chinese and other foreign inhabitants affected by the disaster in Tokyo and Yokohama, and their casualties.

metadata.title: [Estimated Material Losses of Private Property in the Stricken Districts]
metadata.description: Gives the Industrial Bank's estimate of damage to private property in the earthquake-stricken prefectures, broken down by district and by buildings, fixtures and merchandise.

metadata.title: [Amount of Damage to Public Works in the Devastated Area]
metadata.chapter_raw: Chapter IV: Damage to Public Works
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The table summarizes the yen amounts of damage to rivers, roads, harbors and other public works in the devastated area, by the Home Department, Navy, prefectures and cities.

metadata.title: [Values of K in Tokyo and Adjoining Places]
metadata.description: The author lists the value of K, the lateral-force factor for buildings, for several districts in Tokyo and nearby places, based on the hypothesis that the force is proportional to weight.

metadata.title: Relief Funds Received by June 30th, 1924
metadata.description: Statistics of the funds received by the Emergency Relief Bureau up to the end of June 1924, split into domestic and foreign subscriptions and actual receipts.

metadata.title: Foreign Donations in Cash Classified according to Nationality of Donors
metadata.caption: (Figures in brackets show the proportion donated by resident Japanese.)
metadata.description: Foreign cash donations to the relief effort, shown by donor country, with the portion given by resident Japanese in brackets.

metadata.title: [Foreign Relief Contributions by Country]
metadata.description: A country-by-country list of foreign contributions towards relief, with a grand total including other countries, which the text says passed through relief organizations.

metadata.title: [Disbursements of Relief Funds Up to the End of June 1924]
metadata.description: The page lists the sums disbursed from the relief funds up to June 1924, grouped by purpose, showing how the money was spent after the earthquake.

metadata.title: [Relief Disbursements (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: This continued table lists the remaining relief disbursement items and the grand total, which the page's text then sets against the contributions received by the end of June 1924.

metadata.title: [Temporary Hospitals and Consulting Rooms in Tokyo, Kanagawa and Chiba Prefectures]
metadata.description: Shows the temporary hospitals and consulting rooms set up after the earthquake in the three affected prefectures, with beds and totals.

metadata.title: Results of Requisition Enforced by the End of December 1923
metadata.description: Lists the value of foodstuffs, fuel, houses, building materials and other articles requisitioned and transported to the stricken areas by the end of December 1923.

metadata.title: [Relief Recipients in Tokyo City and Tokyo Prefecture, 1923-1924]
metadata.description: Relief recipients in Tokyo City and Tokyo Prefecture are tabulated by date, showing the steady decline in the number of sufferers after the earthquake disaster.

metadata.title: [Relief Given by Kanagawa Prefecture, 1923-1924]
metadata.description: Kanagawa Prefecture's relief operations are shown by date, with figures for Yokohama City, Yokosuka City and the prefecture, as the earlier relief was being wound down.

metadata.title: Distributions (Dec. 20th, 1923)
metadata.description: Shows the relief clothing, cloth, blankets, bedding and cotton received and distributed by district after the 1923 earthquake, with the remainder held in stock on December 20.

metadata.title: Purchases (Dec. 20, 1923)
metadata.description: Lists the relief goods bought by the authorities, with quantities and values, and those taken over from the Army and Navy, following the distribution figures.

metadata.title: Foreign Relief Articles Received and Distributed
metadata.caption: (Figures on Dec. 20, 1923)
metadata.description: The table lists foreign relief articles received by Japan after the earthquake and how many were distributed in Tokyo, Kanagawa and elsewhere, with the remainder left, as of December 20, 1923.

metadata.title: [Materials Supplied to Devastated Districts for Barracks]
metadata.description: Lists the materials commandeered or supplied to the devastated districts for building temporary barracks for refugees after the September 1923 earthquake.

metadata.title: [Temporary Barracks Built by End of December]
metadata.description: Summarises the total floor area of the temporary barracks and the number of people they housed at the end of December 1923.

metadata.title: [Barracks Constructed After the Earthquake]
metadata.description: Lists the barracks built after the earthquake by the government and by public and private bodies, giving their area and the number of people each could accommodate.

metadata.title: Relief Organs and Results of Their Work
metadata.description: The table gives the number of relief organs set up by Tokyo and Kanagawa prefectures after the earthquake and the number of cases each treated, illustrating the results of the relief work described in the text.

metadata.title: [Results of Employment Agency Work, September to June]
metadata.description: The table gives monthly vacancies filled and the ratio to registrations at the employment agencies for ordinary and labor work after the earthquake, showing their results.

metadata.title: [Summary of Work Done by Travelling Exchanges, Nov. to Jun.]
metadata.description: The travelling exchanges set up after the 1923 earthquake to create provincial employment reported monthly vacancies notified, vacancies filled and men given work until their closure in July 1924.

metadata.title: [Roads Cleared and Bridges Repaired after the Earthquake]
metadata.description: The table summarises the road clearing and bridge repair work carried out by the military units in Tokyo, Yokohama, Odawara and Kamakura after the earthquake.

metadata.title: [Railway Lines Reconstructed After the Earthquake]
metadata.description: Lists the railway lines that military railway forces reconstructed after the disaster, with each line's length and the date it reopened.

metadata.title: [Staff of the City Planning Bureau]
metadata.description: The list gives the functionaries who carry out the Bureau's business in place of the Minister President of State, with the number of staff in each grade.

metadata.title: Roads in the City of Tokyo
metadata.caption: (1 ken = 1.8+ metres)
metadata.description: Gives the length and area of Tokyo's roads before 1 September, those to be newly laid out, and those on completion of the reconstruction plan, with their share of total area.

metadata.title: Public Parks in the City of Tokyo
metadata.description: Shows the number and total area of public parks in Tokyo before the earthquake, planned as new, and on completion of the reconstruction plan, by size.

metadata.title: Bridges in the City of Tokyo
metadata.description: Lists the number and total area of Tokyo's bridges before the earthquake, those to be newly built or rebuilt, and those on completion of the reconstruction plan, by width.

metadata.title: [Estimate of Reconstruction Work by Tokyo Municipality]
metadata.description: The page gives the classified estimate of the reconstruction work to be carried out by the Tokyo Municipality, listing the cost of each category of roads, water works, sewerage, parks and rubbish disposal.

metadata.title: [Tokyo Reconstruction Project Costs by Facility]
metadata.description: This page lists the estimated costs of the Tokyo reconstruction works by project and component, showing how the funds were allocated across markets, schools, hospitals, social works and electricity.

metadata.title: [Restoration Works Expenditure Estimates (Continued)]
metadata.description: The table lists the estimated costs of the Tokyo restoration works, continued from the previous page, with a grand total for the main restoration items.

metadata.title: [Restoration Works Undertaken Independently by Tokyo Municipality, Estimated at ¥23,000,000]
metadata.description: The Tokyo Municipality's own restoration works, estimated at about ¥23,000,000 over three years from 1924, to be carried out without State aid.

metadata.title: [Area of Roads Destroyed]
metadata.description: The author lists the area in tsubo of each road type destroyed in the great fire, showing how many paved and other roads were damaged.

metadata.title: Restoration of Municipal Tramway System
metadata.description: Shows the month-by-month restoration of Tokyo's municipal tramway mileage worked and rolling stock after the earthquake, from August 1923 to May 1924.

metadata.title: Cost of Restoration
metadata.description: Gives the money spent in 1923 on restoring the tramway system and the estimated outlay planned for 1924.

metadata.description: Summarises the planned completion and monthly progress of restoring the destroyed electric lighting in Tokyo after the earthquake, showing lights restored by each month-end.

metadata.title: Restoration of Electric Lighting Equipment, Tokyo (continued)
metadata.description: Continues the monthly record of lights restored in Tokyo from January to May 1924 for the municipal and Tokyo Electric Light Company systems.

metadata.title: Cost of Restoration of Electric Lighting
metadata.description: Gives the money spent in 1923 and the estimated cost for 1924 of restoring the electric lighting systems of the Tokyo municipality and the Tokyo Electric Light Company.

metadata.title: No. of Houses Supplied
metadata.caption: (No. of Metres)
metadata.description: Shows the number of houses supplied with water, month by month from August 1923 to May 1924, as part of the Tokyo reconstruction program's utility work.

metadata.title: Quantity Supplied
metadata.caption: (In 1,000 Cubic ft.)
metadata.description: Gives the monthly quantity of supply, in thousands of cubic feet, from August 1923 to May 1924, accompanying the figures on houses supplied during reconstruction.

metadata.title: [Planned Road Widths and Lengths]
metadata.description: Lists the twelve planned roads of Yokohama by width in ken and metres, with their total lengths, and the road-making expenditure estimate.

metadata.title: [Existing and Projected Streets of Yokohama]
metadata.description: Shows the street length and area of Yokohama before and after the planned reconstruction, which will widen streets and lengthen and enlarge the network by about 7 and 25 per cent.

metadata.title: [Existing and Projected Parks of Yokohama]
metadata.description: Compares the existing municipal and private parks of Yokohama with the area planned after reconstruction, as a share of the city and per inhabitant.

metadata.title: Estimate of Expenditure for 18 Months' Supply
metadata.description: The estimate gives the projected expenditure for eighteen months of reconstruction supply, covering salaries, office costs, purchases, and timber and fuel, following the Ordinance on supply.

metadata.title: [Summary of Reconstruction Materials Estimate]
metadata.description: The top of the page gives a summary of the estimated reconstruction material costs by category, with a grand total, continuing the figures from the preceding page.

metadata.title: Estimate for the Purchase of Goods and Materials
metadata.description: This estimate lists the quantities and values of timber, fuel, iron and steel, clothing, fish and other goods to be purchased for reconstruction.

metadata.title: Estimate of the Sale of Goods and Materials
metadata.description: This estimate lists the quantities and values of goods and materials, such as timber, iron, clothing and fish, expected to be sold or needed after the conflagration.

metadata.title: [Iron and Steel Materials Required for Reconstruction]
metadata.description: The Government calculated the iron and steel supplies needed to rebuild temporary buildings, based on estimated numbers of special and ordinary buildings and the sheets per tsubo.

metadata.title: Arrivals
metadata.description: Shows the building materials that arrived for the Reconstruction Bureau, with contract quantities and values alongside the quantities and values actually received.

metadata.title: Sales
metadata.description: Lists the government's building materials sold off by the consignment firms, giving quantity and value for each material.

metadata.title: For the Whole Country
metadata.description: Gives the Government's figures for fire policies and insured amounts across the whole country in 1923, the baseline before the earthquake losses.

metadata.title: For the Affected Districts
metadata.description: Breaks down the policies and insured amounts in the affected prefectures, and then the portion of those reported as actually damaged by the earthquake fire.

metadata.title: Later Figures of Earthquake Loss and Percentage of Loss
metadata.description: The table gives the later government-verified figures for insurance policies and amounts covered by the 33 aided and 5 unaided Japanese companies affected by the earthquake.

metadata.title: [Percentage of Damage by Prefecture]
metadata.description: The table shows the percentage of damage to insured policies and insurance amounts in the affected prefectures, as a share of the total.

metadata.title: Scale of Sympathy Payments of (A) Group Companies
metadata.description: Shows the graded sympathy-payment scale used by the (A) group of insurance companies, by amount of cover, with the rate applied to any excess above the limit.

metadata.title: [Sympathy Payments and Loan Position of Tokyo & Yokohama Companies]
metadata.description: The table shows how the Tokyo and Yokohama companies' sympathy payments, loans advanced and premium returns compared with their total covered amounts after the September earthquake.

metadata.title: List of Estimated Sympathy Payments
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The list shows, for each insurance company, the loan advanced, its repayment term, and the estimated sympathy payments, illustrating how widely repayment terms differ between companies.

metadata.title: [Emergency Earthquake Expenditure]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The table breaks down the emergency earthquake expenditure by purpose, showing the sums allotted to relief, temporary construction, and telegraph and telephone services after the disaster.

metadata.title: [Estimated Revenue Shortfall for Fiscal Year 1924–1925]
metadata.description: The Financial Department estimated the revenue shortfall for 1924–1925 from lost tax receipts and failed loans, which the Treasury had to offset against the earthquake's effects.

metadata.title: Revised Budget for Fiscal Year 1923-24
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows the revised Budget for fiscal 1923-24 as published on December 7th, comparing existing and revised ordinary, extraordinary and total revenue and expenditure.

metadata.title: Budget for the Year 1924–25
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Compares the Budget for 1924–25, informally disclosed to the Lower House, with the previous year's Budget, showing revenue and expenditure in ordinary, extraordinary and total amounts.

metadata.title: Items of Revenue for the Year 1924-25 with Estimated Decreases and Increases
metadata.description: The author's estimates of revenue decreases caused by the earthquake and fire, and of the offsetting recovery, for fiscal 1924-25, are listed to show the disaster's effect on the national treasury.

metadata.title: Deferred Taxes Collected and Anticipated Natural Increments From Past Experience
metadata.description: Estimated recovery of revenue from deferred tax collection and expected natural increases, based on past experience, showing how much of the earthquake loss was offset.

metadata.title: [Final Adjustment of Revenue Decreases]
metadata.description: After the final adjustment of the increases and decreases, the revenue results show the following decreases, split into ordinary, extraordinary and total.

metadata.title: Curtailments or Postponements of Expenditure in the 1924-25 Budget
metadata.description: The table lists the curtailments and postponements of expenditure made in the 1924-25 Budget, with totals for ordinary and extraordinary items.

metadata.title: [Reconstruction Project Expenditure Allotments, 1923-24 to 1928-29]
metadata.description: The Reconstruction project placed before the extraordinary Diet session in December 1923 showed planned expenditure allotments over six years, to be financed by public loans.

metadata.title: [Earthquake Reconstruction Allotments by Item]
metadata.description: Lists the six categories of earthquake reconstruction funds and their amounts, with the total, to show how the state allocation was divided.

metadata.title: [Reconstruction Allotments for 1923-24 and Subsequent Fiscal Years]
metadata.description: Gives the reconstruction allotments for fiscal 1923-24 and the five following fiscal years, showing the planned annual spending.

metadata.title: [Reconstruction Work Expenses of Tokyo and Yokohama]
metadata.description: Breaks down the reconstruction work expenses of Tokyo and Yokohama by item, in thousands of yen, with totals for each city.

metadata.title: [Loans for District Reconstruction by Prefecture]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows how the district reconstruction loans are distributed between Tokyo and Kanagawa prefectures, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [State Contributions for Reconstruction by Recipient]
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows how state contributions for reconstruction are distributed among the prefectures, cities and fire-proof zone construction, in thousands of yen.

metadata.title: [State and Cities Share of Reconstruction Cost]
metadata.description: Shows the reconstruction work cost split between the State, the cities, and the two cities and two prefectures, with the State and local bodies bearing the cost in set proportions.

metadata.title: [Breakdown of Reconstruction Cost Borne by State and Cities]
metadata.description: Resolves the preceding cost figures into their components, including estimated interest payable by the State and State subsidies for fire-proof housing.

metadata.title: [Final Division of Reconstruction Cost Between State and Cities]
metadata.description: Summarises the final proportion of reconstruction cost to be borne by the State and by the cities, with the combined total.

metadata.title: [Working Budget Revenue and Expenditure, 1924-25]
metadata.description: The working budget for 1924-25, drawn up by the Kiyoura Cabinet on existing estimates, is set out as revenue and expenditure totals balancing at the same sum.

metadata.title: [Supplementary Budgets Adopted for 1924-25]
metadata.description: The supplementary budgets approved by the extraordinary Diet of June 1924 under the Kato Ministry are listed with their amounts.

metadata.title: [Ways and Means Adopted Against the 1924-25 Estimates]
metadata.description: Against the total government estimates of about 1,615 million yen for 1924-25, the ways and means adopted are listed, including additional revenue and loans.

metadata.title: [Budget Transfers and Supplementary Budget Allotments]
metadata.description: Two lists of budget items show the surplus transfer and the supplementary budget allotments for Tokyo reconstruction and restoration, which the author says cover continuing and Treasury-advanced expenses.

metadata.title: [Imports Admitted Duty Free under the Special Emergency Ordinance]
metadata.description: The text states that this table gives the total value of imports that arrived in Japan under the special emergency enactment, which admitted these goods duty free.

metadata.title: [Imports of Principal Commodities]
metadata.description: The page lists the values of various imported commodities, ending with a grand total, illustrating the composition of foreign trade in the period discussed.

metadata.title: Luxurious Tariff List
metadata.description: The list specifies the articles under the Luxury Law of 1924 on which a 100% ad valorem duty is imposed, identified by their tariff item numbers.

metadata.title: [Tariff Classification Items: Paper, Stones and Pottery]
metadata.description: This list of tariff item numbers and descriptions names the paper, stone and pottery goods covered by the duty classification, with explanatory notes on the 100 per cent. paper duty.

metadata.title: [Sheds, Warehouses and Exposed Space Before and After the Earthquake]
metadata.description: Shows the sheds, warehouses and exposed storage space at the port before the earthquake, after it, and at the end of April 1924, with the amount still under construction.

metadata.title: [Foreign Residents Before and After the Earthquake, by Nationality]
metadata.description: Compares the number of foreign families and residents by nationality before the 1 September earthquake with the figures computed at the end of June 1924.

metadata.title: Export of Raw Silk
metadata.description: Shows raw silk exports from Yokohama and Kobe over Sept. 1923 to April 1924, illustrating the shift of raw silk export toward Yokohama after the earthquake.

metadata.title: Export of Silk Fabrics
metadata.description: Shows silk fabric exports from Yokohama and Kobe for the same periods, comparing the two ports in the wake of the disaster.

metadata.title: Comparative Trade Returns
metadata.description: Compares export and import trade values of Yokohama and Kobe for Sept. 1923 to April 1924, showing how the two ports' trade stood against each other.

metadata.title: No. of Ocean-Going Vessels in Yokohama
metadata.caption: (1,000 tons)
metadata.description: Shows the number and tonnage of ocean-going vessels entering and leaving Yokohama monthly from September to April, comparing the two seasons to illustrate post-earthquake trade recovery.

metadata.title: In Kobe
metadata.description: Gives the number and tonnage of Japanese and foreign vessels entering and clearing the port of Kobe in the first halves of 1923 and 1924, for comparison of shipping activity.

metadata.title: Loans as Shown in the Bank of Japan's Weekly Bulletin
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: The table gives the Bank of Japan's loans by category at three dates in 1923, showing the central bank's increased lending to bankers after the earthquake disrupted normal operations.

metadata.title: Volume of Convertible Notes Issued
metadata.description: The author shows that the note circulation rose sharply after the September disaster, giving monthly maximum, minimum and average issue volumes for 1922 and 1923 to support the argument.

metadata.title: Loan Account
metadata.caption: (in ¥1,000)
metadata.description: Shows how the loans of the 43 Tokyo clearing banks by class changed between August 25 and January 12 after the earthquake, with Special banks rising sharply.

metadata.title: Rates of Interest on Debentures
metadata.caption: (Based on the investigation of the Hypothec Bank of Japan)
metadata.description: The table gives monthly rates of interest on debentures and average commercial bill prices in 1923-24, showing the money-market stringency after the earthquake that the text describes.

metadata.title: [Profit Percentage by Kind of Enterprise]
metadata.chapter_raw: Chapter XVI — The Earthquake and Economic Restoration
metadata.caption: (*indicating loss)
metadata.description: Comparing the profit percentages of the last three second-half terms across enterprise types, showing which kinds of business made losses after the earthquake.

metadata.title: [Loans of Government Funds Advanced by the Hypothec Bank, End of June 1924]
metadata.description: Shows the reconstruction loans the Hypothec Bank had outstanding at the end of June 1924, split into direct and agency loans of Government funds.

metadata.title: [Hypothec Bank Debentures, Loans and Reconstruction Funds]
metadata.description: Lists the financial measures the Hypothec Bank took for earthquake reconstruction, including debenture acceptances, capital loans, and low-interest reconstruction funds.

metadata.title: [Spinning Companies: Pre-quake and Restored Equipment]
metadata.description: Shows how far the spinning companies' pre-earthquake equipment has been restored, with the Kwanto mills at varying percentages of their former capacity.

metadata.title: [Muslin Companies: Pre-quake Equipment and Restoration]
metadata.description: Shows that the three Kwanto muslin companies, with eleven mills in all, have fully restored their pre-earthquake spinning and weaving equipment.

metadata.title: [Chemical Works Damaged by the Earthquake]
metadata.description: Shows the chemical works damaged by the earthquake, with pre-quake monthly output, loss amounts, and how much capacity had been restored, as a companion to the chemical industry text.

metadata.title: [Ceramic and Cement Works Damaged by the Earthquake]
metadata.description: Lists the cement, ceramic and brick works damaged in the quake, with pre-quake monthly output and the percentage of each works' capacity already restored.

metadata.title: [Shipbuilding Yards Damaged by the Earthquake]
metadata.description: Gives the damage to the Ishikawajima, Uraga and Yokohama shipyards, with their pre-quake yearly capacity and how much had been restored, explaining the shipbuilding losses described in the text.

metadata.title: [Electric Lighting Companies: Number of Lights Before Quake and Restored]
metadata.description: Shows how many electric lights the two main lighting companies had before the earthquake and after restoration, illustrating the recovery of electric lighting services.

metadata.title: [Goods Destroyed in Warehouses of Tokyo and Yokohama, Items Valued at Y 2 Millions or Over]
metadata.description: The table lists the principal goods destroyed in the Tokyo and Yokohama warehouses by the earthquake fires, with values, for items valued at two million yen or more.

metadata.title: [Warehouse Area Restored or Surviving on July 1st 1924 Compared with Before the Quake]
metadata.description: The table gives the warehouse floor area, in tsubo, in Tokyo and Yokohama on July 1st 1924 compared with the area before the earthquake.

metadata.title: [Relative Strength of Parties after the May Election]
metadata.description: After the May election, the list gives the number of seats each party won, showing the Kensei-kai as the largest party and explaining the subsequent change of Ministry.

metadata.title: Consulting Dispensaries
metadata.description: Following the disaster, consulting dispensaries and hospitals were set up as temporary medical provision, and this table lists the dispensaries by managing body, location and number in Tokyo and Kanagawa Prefectures.

metadata.title: Hospital Accommodation in Tokyo Prefecture
metadata.description: Lists the hospital beds for general, maternity and children's, and infectious-disease patients in Tokyo Prefecture at the end of December 1923, by managing body.

metadata.title: [Epidemic Cases in Tokyo and Kanagawa Prefectures to December 31, 1923]
metadata.description: Figures of epidemic cases in Tokyo and Kanagawa prefectures after the earthquake, brought down to December 31, 1923. The single Kanagawa figure 211 is bracketed against the last four diseases.

metadata.title: [Epidemic Cases Among Inmates of Temporary Sheds and Barracks, Tokyo Prefecture]
metadata.description: Shows the epidemic cases among occupants of temporary sheds and barracks, compared with ordinary houses, illustrating the poor sanitation of barrack life.

metadata.title: [Milk Supplied for Infant Feeding by Locality and Kind]
metadata.description: Shows the quantities of natural and condensed or pulverized milk supplied by the Relief Bureau in Tokyo and Kanagawa prefectures after the earthquake, with recipient numbers.

metadata.title: [Progress of Telephone Restoration in Tokyo]
metadata.description: Shows the progress of telephone restoration in Tokyo after the earthquake, with connections in operation and new connections added through March 1926.

metadata.title: [Progress of Telephone Restoration in Yokohama]
metadata.description: Shows the progress of telephone restoration in Yokohama, giving connections in operation in June 1924 and new connections added up to March 1926.

metadata.title: Tracks and Structures
metadata.description: Shows the progress of restoration works on Government Railways lines, stations and structures as of August 20th, 1924, by line, section, work, and completion date.

metadata.title: Rolling Stock
metadata.description: Summarises locomotives repaired, newly constructed and rebuilt on old trucks in government and private shops, as part of the railway restoration progress.

metadata.title: [Electric Cars and Passenger and Goods Wagons Repaired, Newly Constructed and Rebuilt]
metadata.description: This table gives the number of electric, passenger and goods railway vehicles repaired, newly built or rebuilt at private and government shops, supporting the discussion of railway rolling stock.

metadata.title: Railway Receipts for April 1923–March 1924
metadata.caption: (in ¥ 1,000)
metadata.description: The table shows monthly and total railway receipts (passenger, goods, total) of the Government Railways for April 1923–March 1924, with increases or decreases against the previous year, illustrating the post-earthquake revenue recovery.

metadata.title: The Circulation on January 1
metadata.description: Shows the yearly January 1 circulation of the Nichi-Nichi newspaper from 1913 to 1924, illustrating its growth to 709,000 in 1924 before the quake.

metadata.title: [Direct Telephone Communications between the Tokyo Nichi-Nichi and the Osaka Mainichi, September 6-16]
metadata.description: Shows the daily count of direct telephone calls between the Tokyo Nichi-Nichi and Osaka Mainichi newspapers after restoration, illustrating how communication recovered following the earthquake.

metadata.title: [Schedule of Articles Listed by Tariff Item Number]
metadata.description: A numbered list of tariff-classified articles (cotton, wool, footwear, paper, slate, cement, glass, iron and nails) printed under the Imperial Edicts and Emergency Legislation heading, giving the item numbers covered by the legislation.

metadata.title: [Tariff Items Exempted or Reduced Under Imperial Ordinance]

metadata.title: [Income Tax Remission for Damage to Residence or Household Property, Paragraph (B)]

metadata.title: [Income Tax Remission for Damage to Residence or Household Property, Paragraph (C)]

metadata.description: Lists the claims made under the Regulations for restoring deposits after the 1923 earthquake, by type, with counts and amounts in yen, as of the end of 1923.
