metadata.description: Because Chinese surveys do not give an exact area for Manchuria, this table gives a computed figure for each province and the total, drawn from various Japanese investigations.

metadata.title: Population in Manchuria
metadata.caption: (in thousands)
metadata.description: Following a note that population figures are hard to obtain, this table gives the estimated population of Manchuria by province and total, with annual increase and growth index, from 1907 to 1912.

metadata.title: [Population Growth in Manchuria, 1913–1930]
metadata.description: The table gives year-by-year population figures for Manchuria from 1913 to 1930, the 1930 row matching the provincial figures in the density table below.

metadata.title: Density of Population in Manchuria (1930)
metadata.description: The table shows the 1930 population, density per square kilometre and growth index for Manchuria's three provinces and total, with the text explaining why density is highest in South Manchuria.

metadata.title: [Population of Eight Important Cities in Manchuria at the End of 1930 by Nationality]
metadata.description: Gives the 1930 population of eight important Manchurian cities broken down by nationality, with totals for Manchuria, to illustrate population distribution in the region.

metadata.title: Chronological Table
metadata.caption: (After the Ching Dynasty)
metadata.description: A chronological list of key events in Manchurian and Russian relations from 1636 to 1722, placed under section 3 to give historical background.

metadata.title: [Organization Chart of the Kwantung Government Police and Finance Departments]
metadata.description: A bracketed organizational diagram showing the subordinate sections of the Police Administration Bureau and Finance Department of the Kwantung Government.

metadata.title: Organization of Courts of All Grades
metadata.description: The text describes the four-grade, three-instance judicial system under the National Government, and this diagram sets out which courts hear first-grade and local cases at each instance.

metadata.title: [Distribution of New Courts in the Manchurian Provinces and Tungsheng Special District]
metadata.description: The text explains that the new courts are distributed unevenly across the Manchurian provinces and the Tungsheng Special District, with Liaoning having the most courts.

metadata.title: [Prisons in Manchuria by District]
metadata.description: Based on the Commission on Extraterritoriality's report, this table gives the number of new and old prisons in each Manchurian district, showing Liaoning holds about a fifth of new prisons in China.

metadata.title: [Revenue and Expenditure of Liaoning Province, 1916-1929]
metadata.description: Gives the revenue and expenditure of Liaoning Province for selected years, showing the budget trend that led to the 1929 figures discussed in the text.

metadata.title: Ordinary Revenue
metadata.caption: (Yuan, Silver Tayang)
metadata.description: Lists the estimated ordinary revenue items of the Liaoning Province budget for 1929, with the total.

metadata.title: Extraordinary Revenue
metadata.caption: (Yuan, Silver Tayang)
metadata.description: Lists the estimated extraordinary revenue items of the Liaoning Province budget for 1929, leading to the grand total of revenue.

metadata.title: [Revenue and Expenditure of Kirin Province, 1916–1929]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly revenue and expenditure of Kirin Province from 1916 to 1929, illustrating how the province's finances improved after Jung Hou's reforms.

metadata.title: [Estimated Budget Revenue of Kirin Province, 1929]
metadata.description: Breaks down the estimated 1929 budget revenue of Kirin Province by tax and miscellaneous items, with the total matching the 1929 revenue figure.

metadata.title: [Revenue and Expenditure of Heilungkiang Province, 1916–1929]
metadata.description: The figures give only a vague indication of Heilungkiang Province's finances, showing its revenue and expenditure in selected years from 1916 to 1929.

metadata.title: [Chief Taxes of Heilungkiang Province, 1929]
metadata.caption: (Yuan, Harbin Tayang)
metadata.description: Taxes were the main source of Heilungkiang's revenue in 1929, and this list gives the chief tax items for that year.

metadata.title: Revenue and Expenditure of the Special Account for the Kwantung Government
metadata.caption: (Unit: Yen)
metadata.description: Shows revenue and expenditure of the Kwantung Government's special account from 1907 to 1930, with ordinary and extraordinary totals for each year.

metadata.title: Annual Expenditure Accounts of the Cities of Dairen and Port Arthur
metadata.caption: (the figures for 1930 are the budget estimates)
metadata.description: Gives the annual expenditure accounts of the cities of Dairen and Port Arthur from 1915 to 1930, showing municipal finance under the self-government bodies.

metadata.title: Revenue and Expenditure under Jurisdiction of Port Arthur Civil Administration Office, 1927–1930
metadata.caption: (in thousands of yen; the 1930 figure is the budget estimate)
metadata.description: Shows the revenue and expenditure of the Kai (Hui) under the Port Arthur Civil Administration Office for past years, with the 1930 budget revenue estimate.

metadata.title: [Civil Administration Offices Under the Kwantung Leased Territory]
metadata.description: Figures for the civil administration offices in the Kwantung area, whose column headings are printed on the previous page; the Railway Zone accounts follow below.

metadata.title: [Annual Account of the South Manchuria Railway Zone]
metadata.description: The annual accounts of the Railway Zone, run by the South Manchuria Railway Company, are listed by year from 1907 to 1929.

metadata.title: Revenue
metadata.caption: (in thousands of Yen)
metadata.description: Revenue of the Railway Zone for 1925 to 1929, showing taxes, fees, other revenues and the company's subsidy that makes up the deficit.

metadata.title: Expenditure
metadata.caption: (in thousands of Yen)
metadata.description: Shows annual expenditure by category from 1925 to 1929, giving the financial background to the administration's spending before the section on Customs.

metadata.title: Total Maritime Customs Revenue of Each Port of Manchuria (in thousands of Haikwan Tael)
metadata.description: Shows the maritime customs revenue of each Manchurian port from 1910 to 1929, with totals for the three provinces and for China, to indicate Manchuria's share of national customs income.

metadata.title: Area Under Cultivation in Manchuria (1929)
metadata.caption: (in square kilometre)
metadata.description: Shows the area under cultivation in Manchuria by province in 1929, split into cultivable and not arable land, supporting the discussion of cultivated land.

metadata.title: [Percentage of Cultivated Area to Total and Cultivable Land]
metadata.description: Gives the cultivated and uncultivated shares of each province's area, with 1928 comparison figures in parentheses, showing the extent of cultivation.

metadata.title: [Bean Production: Planted Area and Production, 1926-1929]
metadata.description: The page introduces bean production in Manchuria, giving planted area and output of soya beans and other pulse for 1926 to 1929.

metadata.title: Export Through Three Ports of South Manchuria
metadata.caption: (in metric tons)
metadata.description: The text notes that soya bean exports from South Manchurian ports were large, and this table gives export quantities of pulse, bean cake and bean oil for 1924 to 1929.

metadata.title: [Soybean Varieties: Crop per Hectare, Increase and Oil Content]
metadata.description: Compares yields and oil content of three soybean varieties, showing the crop per hectare and the percentage increase relative to the native variety.

metadata.title: Kaoliang
metadata.description: Gives planted area, production and three-port export of kaoliang, the main food of Manchurian farmers, for 1926 to 1929.

metadata.title: Millet
metadata.description: Shows planted area, production and three-port export of millet, a staple food also used for spirits and exported to Chosen, for 1926 to 1929.

metadata.title: Maize
metadata.description: Presents planted area, production and three-port export of maize, mainly grown in southern South Manchuria, for 1926 to 1929.

metadata.title: Upland and Paddy-Field Rice
metadata.description: Compares planted area and production of paddy-field and upland rice for 1926–1929, supporting the text on rising rice consumption and paddy-field reclamation in Manchuria.

metadata.title: [Tobacco Production in Manchuria, 1929]
metadata.description: Gives the 1929 tobacco planted area and production by province, illustrating the tobacco cultivation described in the preceding paragraph.

metadata.title: Live-Stock (1929)
metadata.description: Gives the number of cattle, horses, donkeys, mules, sheep and pigs in each district of South and North Manchuria in 1929, with 1928 comparison totals.

metadata.title: Export of Principal Pasture Products
metadata.caption: (In 1929 through the three ports of South Manchuria and the Harbin Customs District)
metadata.description: Lists the value in Haikwan taels of the principal animal and pasture products exported in 1929 through South Manchurian ports and the Harbin customs district, following the discussion of livestock.

metadata.title: [Wool Production in Manchuria, 1926]
metadata.description: Gives figures from a 1926 investigation of wool production in Manchuria, showing quantities transported, assembled and shipped by each railway and port.

metadata.title: Wool Carried by South Manchuria Railway
metadata.caption: (Including bristles and other animal hairs)
metadata.description: Shows annual volumes of wool carried by the South Manchuria Railway from 1922 to 1929, supporting the estimate of Manchurian wool exports.

metadata.title: [Annual Fur Export of Manchuria, 1926]
metadata.description: An approximate 1926 investigation of the annual fur export of Manchuria, showing values by parcel-post office and other sources, with the port of shipment and destination.

metadata.title: Forest Areas and Standing Timber in Manchuria
metadata.description: The table gives forest area and estimated standing timber for each forest region of Manchuria, introducing the account of the Yalu River valley forests and the lumber trade.

metadata.title: [Forest Areas and Standing Timber along the Kihui Railway Line]
metadata.description: Shows the forest area and standing timber volume at varying distances from the Kihui Railway line, illustrating the timber resources of the Kirin lumber region.

metadata.title: [Estimated Annual Lumber Supply in Manchuria]
metadata.description: Gives the estimated annual lumber supply in Manchuria by region, since exact figures were difficult to obtain, to describe the state of the forestry industry.

metadata.title: [Value of Lumber Exported, 1925–1929]
metadata.description: Shows the value of lumber exported through the main Manchurian customs ports and the Harbin district over the past four years, 1925 to 1929.

metadata.title: [Sea-coast and River Fisheries of Manchuria]
metadata.description: The table surveys Manchuria's sea-coast and river fisheries by district, showing fishing population, boats, species caught, annual catch and remarks on development.

metadata.title: Fishing Trade at the Three Ports of South Manchuria and Harbin Customs District
metadata.description: Shows the volume and value of fishing trade (imports, exports and import surplus) at the three South Manchurian ports and Harbin, 1915–1929, supporting the point that fish imports exceed exports.

metadata.title: Comparative Analysis of Sun Evaporated Salts
metadata.caption: (Conducted by the Salt Monopoly Bureau, Japanese Government, in 1927)
metadata.description: The Kwantung Government is improving salt quality, and this table compares the moisture, impurity and sodium chloride content and appraised quality of local and foreign sun-evaporated salts.

metadata.title: Salt Field Area in Kwantung Leased Territory
metadata.description: The authorities are expanding salt fields, and this table shows the yearly area of salt fields in the Kwantung Leased Territory operated by Japanese and Chinese, with totals.

metadata.title: Salt Production in Kwantung Leased Territory
metadata.description: Showing the results of the government's efforts, this table gives salt output in the Kwantung Leased Territory by Japanese and Chinese producers and the combined total for 1921 and 1923.

metadata.title: [Manufactured Salt Output, 1925–1929]
metadata.description: The table gives annual salt output figures for 1925 to 1929, shown to illustrate the sharp recent fall in manufactured salt, which the text attributes partly to economic depression.

metadata.title: Salt Production in 1929 According to Districts
metadata.description: This table breaks down the 1929 salt production by district, separating Japanese and Chinese fields, to explain the 1929 national statistics given in the text.

metadata.title: Export of Kwantung Salt
metadata.caption: (in kilograms)
metadata.description: The table shows kilograms of Kwantung salt exported by destination, supporting the text's statement that a large share of Manchurian salt output is exported.

metadata.title: Mineral Production in South Manchuria
metadata.caption: (in metric tons)
metadata.description: The table gives annual mineral output of South Manchuria from 1918 to 1929, showing how production of iron, coal, coke and various industrial minerals changed over that period.

metadata.title: [Pig-Iron Production at the Anshan Iron Works Since Its Establishment]
metadata.description: The text introduces a year-by-year record of pig-iron output at the Anshan Iron Works since its establishment, giving castings, annual and average daily production.

metadata.title: [Annual Figures, 1925–1929 (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: Continuation of an earlier statistical table of yearly figures; its column headings appear on the previous page and are not printed here.

metadata.title: Varieties of Pig-iron Produced at the Anshan Iron Works and Their Standard Analysis
metadata.description: Standard chemical analysis of each grade of pig-iron made at the Anshan Iron Works, given as a reference for the product.

metadata.title: Annual Quantities of By-products Produced at the Anshan Coke Ovens
metadata.description: Annual output of coke by-products and related materials at the Anshan works, whose coke production capacity is 800 metric tons a day.

metadata.title: [Present and Projected Annual Production of Mining and Metallurgical Products]
metadata.description: Shows the present annual output of several mining and chemical products and the expected output after new equipment is completed, set beside the South Manchuria Railway's steel project.

metadata.title: [Pig-iron Production of the Penhsihu Iron Works, 1921-1926]
metadata.description: Gives the year-by-year pig-iron output of the Penhsihu Iron Works since 1921, illustrating the restricted and fluctuating production described in the text.

metadata.title: [Annual Figures, 1927-1929 (continued from previous page)]
metadata.description: These final lines give three yearly figures, apparently the end of an earlier table whose heading is on the previous page.

metadata.title: [Standard Analysis of Pig-iron Produced at the Penshihu Iron Works]
metadata.description: The standard chemical analysis of the pig-iron produced at the Penshihu Iron Works, by quality grade, is given for carbon, silicon, manganese, phosphorus, sulphur and copper.

metadata.title: Export of Iron from Manchuria (1925-1929)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly export of iron ore from Manchuria from 1925 to 1929 in piculs, metric tons and Haikwan taels.

metadata.title: [Coal Production by Province and District of Manchuria]
metadata.caption: (Metric tons)
metadata.description: Gives the coal output of Manchuria's provinces and their principal districts, with a total, to show where the region's coal was mined.

metadata.title: [Coal Production at Fushun, 1910–1920]
metadata.caption: (Metric tons)
metadata.description: Shows how coal production at the Fushun field grew over the twenty years before the text was written, following the discussion of the field.

metadata.title: [Fushun Coal Production, 1925–1929]
metadata.description: The table gives Fushun coal output for 1925–1929, illustrating the scale of the field described in the text above it.

metadata.title: [Penhsihu Coal Production, 1924–1928]
metadata.description: The Penhsihu coal field's production over the past five years is listed year by year, as the text announces.

metadata.title: Export of Coal and Cokes from Manchuria (1925-1929)
metadata.description: Shows the volume and value of coal and coke exported from Manchuria in each year from 1925 to 1929, illustrating recent coal export trends.

metadata.title: [Number and Capital of Japanese Manufacturing Firms in Manchuria, 1926–1929]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Japanese firms, workers, capital and output in Manchurian manufacturing industries for 1926 to 1929, offered as a general survey of industrial enterprise.

metadata.title: [Export of Tussah Silk through the Three South Manchurian Ports, 1924–1928]
metadata.caption: (in Hk. Tls.)
metadata.description: Introduced by the text on the export of tussah silk, this table gives the value of tussah silk exported through the three South Manchurian ports over the past few years.

metadata.title: Raw Silk Production
metadata.description: Under the silk reeling discussion, this table shows the total value of South Manchurian silk production for 1927 to 1929, following the growth of sericulture.

metadata.title: [Principal Spinning Mills in Manchuria, 1928]
metadata.description: Introduces the more important spinning mills in Manchuria, giving their capital, spindles, weaving machines, and 1928 yarn and goods output, with totals for Japanese-managed firms.

metadata.title: [Value of Cotton Yarn Production in South Manchuria, 1925–1929]
metadata.description: Shows how the value of cotton yarn production in South Manchuria changed each year from 1925 to 1929.

metadata.title: [Production of Hemp Yarn, Gunny Bags and Hemp Cloth at Two Factories, 1929]
metadata.description: Given after a description of the Mukden hemp companies, this table shows the capital, yarn, gunny bag and cloth output of the two factories and their combined total for 1929.

metadata.title: [Hemp Yarn and Gunny Bag Production in South Manchuria, 1925–1929]
metadata.description: Introduced by the text on South Manchurian hemp yarn and gunny bag output, this table gives annual values and quantities from 1925 to 1929.

metadata.title: [Production of Cast Iron in South Manchuria]
metadata.description: Shows the yearly value of cast iron production in South Manchuria from 1925 to 1929, illustrating the output of the iron-casting trade described in the Casting section.

metadata.title: [Principal Mechanical Equipment at Shahokou Works, March 31, 1930]
metadata.description: The text describes the mechanical equipment installed and in active use at the Shahokou Works on March 31, 1930, listed by type with its count.

metadata.title: [Rolling-Stock Constructed or Assembled at the Shahokou and Liaoyang Works, 1907-1929]
metadata.description: The text gives the number of locomotives, coaches and trucks built or assembled at the works in selected years from 1907 to 1929.

metadata.title: [Repairing and Rebuilding at the Shahokou and Liaoyang Works, 1929]
metadata.description: The text reports the locomotives, passenger coaches and trucks repaired or rebuilt at the two works during 1929.

metadata.title: [Production of Furniture in South Manchuria]
metadata.description: The text introduces this short series to show the yearly value of furniture produced in South Manchuria from 1925 to 1928, as part of the utensil manufacturing discussion.

metadata.title: Bean Oil Mills in South Manchuria
metadata.caption: (at the end of 1929)
metadata.description: Shows the number, estimated capital and daily production capacity of the bean oil mills in South Manchuria at the end of 1929, by location.

metadata.title: Development of the Bean Oil Milling Industry in South Manchuria
metadata.description: Traces the number of bean oil mills and the quantity and value of bean oil and bean cake produced in South Manchuria from 1910 to 1929, showing the industry's growth.

metadata.title: [Bean Oil Mills in North Manchuria, by District, 1929]
metadata.description: The text notes that North Manchuria had 68 bean oil mills at the end of 1929 and gives their district breakdown of capital and daily production capacity.

metadata.title: [Bean Oil Industry in North Manchuria, Mills, Pressing Machines and Daily Capacity by District]
metadata.description: The table shows how the bean oil industry in North Manchuria grew from 1923 to 1929, by mill count, pressing machines and daily capacity in Harbin and the C.E.R. district.

metadata.title: Cement Production in South Manchuria
metadata.description: The table gives annual cement output in South Manchuria from 1924 to 1929, in metric tons and value in yen, illustrating the cement industry described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: Glass Production in South Manchuria
metadata.description: Shows the value of glass production in South Manchuria from 1915 to 1929, supporting the text's account of the glass industry's growth and of the Shoko and Antung companies.

metadata.title: Brick Production in South Manchuria
metadata.description: The table gives annual brick output and value in South Manchuria from 1915 to 1929, illustrating the brick industry discussed in the preceding text, which cites the 1929 figures.

metadata.title: Paper Production in South Manchuria
metadata.description: Following the discussion of paper mills and pulp manufacture, this table gives the value of paper production in South Manchuria for 1925 to 1929.

metadata.title: Paint Production in South Manchuria
metadata.description: Accompanying the text on paint manufacture at Dairen and Port Arthur, this table shows the value of paint production in South Manchuria from 1915 to 1929.

metadata.title: [Medicinal Factories and Their Value in South Manchuria]
metadata.description: Gives the number of medicinal production factories and their value in South Manchuria for 1920 to 1927, supporting the text on the medicine industry.

metadata.title: [Statistics Continued from Previous Page (Year, Count and Value)]
metadata.description: The top of the page carries the final rows of a statistical table whose earlier rows appear on the previous page; the text below then turns to the match industry in Manchuria.

metadata.title: Wheat Flour Production in South Manchuria
metadata.description: Shows the yearly quantity and value of wheat flour produced by the modern mechanical mills of South Manchuria, from 1910 to 1929, illustrating the flour milling industry's development described above.

metadata.title: [Production of the Tiehling Beet-Sugar Company, 1917–1927]
metadata.description: Shows the sugar output and value of the Tiehling beet-sugar company from its founding until operations were suspended in 1927.

metadata.title: [Sugar-Beet Consumption and Sugar Production by Factory, 1928–1929]
metadata.description: Lists sugar-beet consumption and sugar production at the Ashiho and Hulan sugar factories for 1928 and 1929, as a supplement to the sugar-industry discussion.

metadata.title: [Production of Kaoliang-Chiu, 1915–1929]
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of kaoliang-chiu produced in selected years from 1915 to 1929, in the South Manchuria areas covered by the statistics.

metadata.title: [Cigarette Factories in South Manchuria and Their Annual Production]
metadata.description: Following the text on cigarette manufacture, the table gives the number of cigarette factories in South Manchuria and their annual production in yen for 1920 to 1929, as investigated by the Kwantung Government.

metadata.title: Timber Production in South Manchuria
metadata.description: Shows the rising yen value of timber production in South Manchuria from 1925 to 1928, illustrating the industry's recovery described in the text.

metadata.title: [Leather and Skin Output in Mongolia]
metadata.description: A short list giving quantities of leather and skins for Mongolia, introduced by the words 'Mongolia is as follows', ahead of the section on special industries.

metadata.title: Electricity Supplied
metadata.description: Shows the growth from 1924 to 1928 of electric lighting, power and electric train supply in Manchuria, as background to the discussion of electric enterprises.

metadata.title: [Gas Industry: Production, Households and Factories Supplied, and Receipts, 1925–1929]
metadata.description: The gas industry's annual output, households and factories supplied, gas used and receipts for 1925 to 1929, given to detail the industry described in the text above.

metadata.title: Growth of Traffic on the South Manchuria Railway
metadata.description: Shows how goods carried and passenger numbers on the South Manchuria Railway grew from 1908 to 1922, illustrating the railway's role in Manchuria's economic development.

metadata.title: [South Manchuria Railway Goods and Passenger Traffic, 1924–1930]
metadata.description: The figures continue a yearly series of South Manchuria Railway goods and passenger traffic, shown graphically below, to support the text on the railway's goods-transport focus.

metadata.title: Receipts and Expenditures of South Manchuria Railway
metadata.caption: (in Gold Yen)
metadata.description: Business returns of the South Manchuria Railway since its establishment, presented to reflect the Company's efforts to improve its traffic service.

metadata.title: The Growth of Traffic on the Chinese Eastern Railway
metadata.description: Introduces the traffic returns of the Chinese Eastern Railway, showing goods carried and passengers carried year by year from 1922 to 1930, with a chart of the same figures below.

metadata.title: Receipts and Operating Expenditure of C.E.R.
metadata.caption: (in Gold Roubles)
metadata.description: Gives the Chinese Eastern Railway's total receipts, operating expenditure and reserve for extension in gold roubles for 1922 to 1927, as part of the railway's finances.

metadata.title: [Annual Figures for 1928–1930, Peining Railway]
metadata.description: Three years of figures for the Peining (Peking-Mukden) Railway, with the column headings printed on the previous page; they sit above the chart of receipts and expenditure.

metadata.title: Growth of Traffic on the Peining Railway
metadata.description: Recent traffic returns of the Peining Railway, shown as goods carried and passengers carried for 1921 to 1928, with a line graph of the same figures printed below.

metadata.title: Receipts and Expenditure of the Peining Railway
metadata.caption: (in Silver Dollars)
metadata.description: Annual receipts, expenditure and net profit of the Peining Railway from 1921 to 1928, given in silver dollars as part of the railway's recent business returns.

metadata.title: [Ssutao or Ssupingkai-Taonan Railway: Business Returns]
metadata.description: The recent returns of the Ssutao Railway, showing goods carried, passengers, receipts, expenditure and net profit for 1922 to 1930, given to illustrate the line's traffic.

metadata.title: [Kichang or Kirin-Changchun Railway: Business Returns]
metadata.description: The business returns of the Kichang (Kirin-Changchun) Railway in recent years, shown for goods, passengers, receipts, expenditure and net profit, following the description of the line's loan and management.

metadata.title: Business Returns of the Taoang Railway, 1926–1930
metadata.description: The table gives the yearly business returns of the Taoang Railway since its opening, showing goods, passengers, receipts, expenditure and net profit to illustrate the line's early development.

metadata.title: [Business Returns of the Mukden-Huipei Line of the Shenhai or Shenyang (Mukden)—Hailung Railway, 1929 and 1930]
metadata.description: A second set of business returns for 1929 and 1930, printed after the account of the Mukden-Huipei extension, giving the line's traffic and receipts.

metadata.title: [Business Returns of the Line Described Above, 1929–1930]
metadata.description: Shows the traffic and financial returns for the North Manchurian railway described in the preceding paragraph for 1929 and 1930, noting that expenditure figures were unknown.

metadata.title: [Uncompleted Railways Under Loan Agreements]
metadata.description: The text introduces five important uncompleted railways built under loan agreements between the Chinese Government and foreign creditors, listing their loan dates, creditor nation, length and termini.

metadata.title: Distance from Dairen to Ports of the World
metadata.caption: (Nautical miles)
metadata.description: The table gives the sea distances in nautical miles from Dairen to Japanese, Chinese, Asian, European and American ports, shown alongside the port's history and the harbour works.

metadata.title: Steamers Entering and Leaving Dairen
metadata.description: Shows the number of steamers and their registered tonnage by nationality entering and leaving Dairen for 1927 to 1929, illustrating the port's growing trade.

metadata.title: [Postal Managing Offices and First-Class Post Offices in the North-Eastern Provinces]
metadata.description: Lists the Chinese postal managing offices and first-class post offices by postal district in the North-Eastern Provinces, under the Chinese postal service described above.

metadata.title: [Postal Districts (Continued from Previous Page)]
metadata.description: A fragment of a list of postal districts, showing which offices fall under Harbin, with the Kirin district's independence proposal described in the prose below.

metadata.title: Railways of Manchuria
metadata.description: Lists the railways of Manchuria with their gauge, route lines, lengths and dates of opening to traffic.

metadata.title: Manchuria — Capital and Management of Railways
metadata.description: Shows the capital subscribed to each Manchurian railway and the type of management under which it was run.

metadata.title: Japanese Companies in Manchuria, 1925–1929
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese companies in Manchuria and their paid-up capital or invested amounts by year, for the Kwantung Leased Territory, Railway Zone and total, 1925–1929.

metadata.title: Number of Companies and Paid-up Capital or Invested Amount by Industry, End of 1929
metadata.description: Gives the number of companies and their paid-up capital or invested amounts by industry in the Kwantung Leased Territory, Railway Zone and total at the end of 1929.

metadata.title: [Condition of the Associations at the End of 1929]
metadata.description: The table gives the number of Import Associations, their Chinese and Japanese members, and annual expenditure in Kwantung Territory and the Railway Zone at the end of 1929.

metadata.title: [Markets at the End of 1929]
metadata.description: The text describes the markets in the Kwantung Leased Territory and Railway Zone and gives end-1929 statistics on their number, booths and sales.

metadata.title: [Foreign Nationals in Manchuria by Nationality and Locality]
metadata.description: The table breaks down foreign nationals resident in Manchuria by nationality across the principal cities and towns, with totals, showing the distribution of the foreign population.

metadata.title: [Sino-Japanese Joint Enterprises With a Capital of More Than ¥1,000,000]

metadata.title: [Banking, Exchange and Trust Companies, and Other Companies in Manchuria]
metadata.description: The page lists financial and other companies in Manchuria by classification (banking, exchange and trust companies, others), with their location and capital figures.

metadata.title: [Sino-Japanese Joint Enterprises: Companies, Locations and Capital]
metadata.description: Lists the Sino-Japanese joint enterprises with their location and capital, and introduces other joint enterprises that follow in the text.

metadata.title: Government Exchanges
metadata.description: Shows business security and broker figures for the government exchanges at the end of 1929, with totals and comparative year-end figures for 1925–1928.

metadata.title: Trust Companies
metadata.description: Lists the paid-up capital, reserve fund, and annual income and expenditure of the trust companies attached to the Dairen, Mukden, Kaiyuan and other exchanges at the end of 1929.

metadata.title: [Year-End Figures, 1925–1928 (continued from previous page)]
metadata.description: The top of the page continues a year-end series for 1925–1928 whose column headings appear on the previous page; the figures are not labelled here.

metadata.title: [Commodity Transaction Units and Quotation Standards at Mukden]
metadata.description: Continuation of a list giving, for Mukden commodities, the transaction unit, quotation unit and quotation standard used in domestic trade dealings.

metadata.title: Currency Deals
metadata.description: Shows, for each exchange town, the currency commodities dealt in, their transaction units, price quotation units and the standard notes used for quotation.

metadata.title: [Financial Returns of the Dairen and Antung Private Exchanges]
metadata.description: Shows the year-end 1929 financial returns of the two private exchanges at Dairen and Antung, with comparative figures for 1925–1928, as stated in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Transaction and Quotation Units of Domestic Trade]
metadata.description: Lists the standard transaction and quotation units for various goods and securities traded in domestic markets of Manchuria.

metadata.title: Transaction and Quotation Units
metadata.description: Shows the transaction and quotation units used on the Antung Stock and Merchandise Exchange for each listed commodity and security.

metadata.title: [Business Returns of South Manchuria Railway Warehouses]
metadata.description: Gives the yearly business returns of the South Manchuria Railway warehouses since their opening, showing goods received, stored and warehouse revenue.

metadata.title: Quantity Received and Delivered at South Manchuria Railway Warehouses
metadata.description: Shows the quantities of goods brought forward, received, delivered and left in South Manchuria Railway warehouses by storage category for 1928 and 1927, introducing the Chinese warehousing discussion.

metadata.title: [Wholesale Price Index Numbers at Dairen, 1925-1929]
metadata.description: Index numbers of wholesale prices at Dairen by commodity group, showing June, December and annual averages for 1925-1929 against a 1921-1922 base of 100.

metadata.title: Wholesale Price Index Number in Dairen and in Various Cities
metadata.description: The table compares wholesale price index numbers for Dairen with those of Tokyo, London, New York and China, plus the silver quotation, from 1912 to 1930, with 1914 as the base.

metadata.title: [Trade Ports of Manchuria and Dates of Their Opening]
metadata.description: The list gives the trade ports of Manchuria with their opening dates, introduced as the start of the chapter on foreign trade before the trade development table.

metadata.title: Foreign Trade of Manchuria by Ports, 1915–1929
metadata.description: Shows the value of Manchuria's foreign trade for each year from 1915 to 1929, broken down by port and by imports, exports and re-exports, and totals.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Exports
metadata.caption: Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports

metadata.title: Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports in 1929
metadata.caption: (Value H.K. Tael)
metadata.description: Shows the value of exports from Manchurian ports in 1929, by destination (foreign countries and China), giving the trade pattern by port group.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports, 1927–1929, and Value of Exports in 1929 by Destination
Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports
Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports
Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.description: Shows quantity and value of exports from Manchurian ports in 1927–1929 by commodity and port, with 1929 exports by destination (foreign countries and China), explaining the trade flows.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of silk products, bristles, wool, hairs and feathers, leather and horns exported through each Manchurian port in 1927–1929, with Japan and destination breakdowns for 1929.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.caption: (Quantity: Metric ton, except Cattle and Poultry in No.; Value in Yen as printed)
metadata.description: Gives the quantity and value of exports of bones, cattle, poultry, animal tallow, timber and firewood from each Manchurian port for 1927–1929, with the 1929 export destinations by country alongside.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.caption: Ginseng quantities are in kilograms. 1929 value by destination is printed on the facing page as 'Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports in 1929'.
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of exports from each Manchurian port by commodity for 1927–1929, with 1929 value by Japan, foreign countries and China, in the trade section of the year book.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.caption: Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports in 1929 (right-hand columns, from page 209)

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Exports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of re-exports and total exports leaving each Manchurian port for 1927–1929, with Japan's share, continued by the 1929 value breakdown by destination country.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.caption: Quantity in Metric ton; 1929 country breakdown in Value H.K. Tael.
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of imports of piece goods, thread and yarn at each Manchurian port for 1927–1929, with Japan's share and the 1929 breakdown by country of origin.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of Manchurian imports by goods and port for 1927–1929, with 1929 values by country of origin continued on the facing page.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.caption: Right-hand columns: Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports in 1929, by country of origin
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of wheat flour, vegetables, fruits, sugars, marine products and other provisions imported through each Manchurian port in 1927–1929, with Japan's share and the 1929 value by country of origin.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of imports at Manchurian ports by goods and port for 1927–1929, with the 1929 value broken down by country of origin and Japan.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.caption: Quantity in Metric ton, except Kerosene Oil and Machine Oil, which are in Litre. Right-hand columns: Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports in 1929, Foreign Goods and Chinese Goods.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of imports at Manchurian ports for 1927–1929 by commodity and port, with Japan's share and the 1929 foreign and Chinese goods breakdown by country of origin.

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.caption: Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports in 1929 (Foreign Goods / Chinese Goods)

metadata.title: Quantity and Value of Imports at Manchurian Ports
metadata.caption: Quantity in Metric ton (Bags, Gunny quantity in Pieces); 1929 value by country of origin printed on the facing page
metadata.description: Shows the quantity and value of imports at each Manchurian port by commodity for 1927–1929 with Japan's share, and the 1929 value broken down by country of origin.

metadata.title: [Principal Chinese Banks at the End of 1929]
metadata.description: The page lists the principal Chinese banks operating in Manchuria at the end of 1929, giving their name, founding year, paid-up capital, head office and branches.

metadata.title: [Provincial and Commercial Banks in Manchuria: Year, Capital, Head Office and Branches]
metadata.description: The page describes provincial and commercial banks operating in Manchuria, giving each bank's founding year, authorized and paid-up capital, head office and branch locations.

metadata.title: [Banks Operating in Manchuria: The Bank of Communications]
metadata.description: Gives the founding year, capital, head office and branch network of the Bank of Communications, one of the banks operating in Manchuria, alongside the preceding account of the Taching Bank.

metadata.title: [Banks Issuing Currency Notes in Manchuria]
metadata.description: Lists the banks that issued currency notes in Manchuria, giving each bank's founding year, capital, head office and branch locations.

metadata.title: Japanese Banks in Manchuria at the End of 1929
metadata.description: The page notes that Japanese banks in Manchuria were eliminated and reduced after the War, and lists the main Japanese banks there at the end of 1929 with their capital and offices.

metadata.title: [Currency Circulation by Locality and Currency Type]
metadata.description: The table gives currency circulation figures by locality in Manchuria, broken down by gold yen, silver yen, silver yuan, tayang yuan and yangpiao yuan, under the banking and currency section.

metadata.title: [Deposits and Loans by City]
metadata.description: Shows year-end deposits and loans of banks in each Manchurian city, by currency, with totals, for the four years covered by the page's table.

metadata.title: Clearing Amounts
metadata.caption: (in thousands of Yen)
metadata.description: Gives the number of bills and the amounts cleared through the Dairen Clearing House under its gold and silver accounts for 1925 to 1929.

metadata.title: Mukden Clearing House: Gold Account
metadata.description: Shows the Gold Account of the Mukden Clearing House, giving the number of bills and the amount cleared across five successive periods, with no column headings printed.

metadata.title: Drafts Accepted and Paid by Japanese Banks
metadata.caption: (Yen, Yuan or Taels ,000 ommitted)
metadata.description: Gives the yearly amounts of drafts accepted and paid by Japanese banks in gold yen, silver yen and Chinese currencies, showing the scale of this business.

metadata.title: Bar Silver and Exchange Quotations
metadata.description: Lists highest, lowest and average London and New York bar silver prices and Shanghai gold quotations for June, December and the yearly average of 1928 and 1929.

metadata.title: Dairen-Japan T.T. (Yokohama Specie Bank Quotation)
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Monthly Dairen exchange rates against the yen (T.T.) by Yokohama Specie Bank quotation, for June, December and the yearly average; column headers are not printed on this page.

metadata.title: Dairen-Japan 15 Days (Y.S.B. Quotation)
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Dairen exchange rates against the yen for 15-day transactions by Y.S.B. quotation, shown for June, December and the average, with column headers not printed on this page.

metadata.title: Dairen-Shanghai T.T. (Y.S.B. Quotation)
metadata.caption: (Taels)
metadata.description: Dairen exchange rates against the Shanghai tael by Y.S.B. quotation for June, December and the average, shown without column headers on this page.

metadata.title: Dairen-Tientsin T.T. (Y.S.B. Quotation)
metadata.caption: (Taels)
metadata.description: Dairen exchange rates against the Tientsin tael by Y.S.B. quotation for June, December and the average, without column headers on this page.

metadata.title: Dairen-London T.T. (Y.S.B. Quotation)
metadata.caption: (Shillings and pence per dollar, as printed)
metadata.description: Dairen exchange rates against sterling (London T.T.) by Y.S.B. quotation, expressed in shillings and pence, for June, December and the average.

metadata.title: Dairen-U.S. T.T. (Y.S.B. Quotation)
metadata.description: Dairen exchange rates against the US dollar by Y.S.B. quotation for June, December and the average, in fractional units, without column headers on this page.

metadata.title: Dairen-France T.T. (Y.S.B. Quotation)
metadata.caption: (Franc)
metadata.description: Dairen exchange rates against the franc by Y.S.B. quotation for June, December and the average, without column headers on this page.

metadata.title: Dairen-Germany T.T. (Y.S.B. Quotation)
metadata.caption: (Mark)
metadata.description: Dairen exchange rates against the mark by Y.S.B. quotation for June, December and the average, without column headers on this page.

metadata.title: Dairen-India T.T. (Y.S.B. Quotation)
metadata.caption: (Rupee)
metadata.description: Dairen exchange rates against the Indian rupee by Y.S.B. quotation for June, December and the average, without column headers on this page.

metadata.title: [Telegraphic Transfer Exchange Rates: Dairen and Shanghai against Singapore, Manila, Java, Japan, London and U.S.]
metadata.description: The page gives telegraphic transfer exchange rates between Dairen and several centres, and between Shanghai and Japan, London and the U.S., for June, December and the average, as background to banking and currency.

metadata.title: Postal Savings Accounts
metadata.caption: (in Yen)
metadata.description: Shows yearly postal savings deposits, refunds, and depositor and balance totals in Manchuria from 1925 to 1929, illustrating the growth of postal savings.

metadata.title: Postal Transfer Accounts
metadata.caption: (in Yen)
metadata.description: Gives yearly amounts paid in and paid out through postal transfer accounts in Manchuria from 1925 to 1929.

metadata.title: Loans Made by Money-Lenders
metadata.caption: (in Yen)
metadata.description: Reports yearly money-lender activity in Manchuria, including number of lenders, new loans, collections, losses and outstanding loans, 1925 to 1929.

metadata.title: Loans Made by Pawnshops
metadata.caption: (in Yen)
metadata.description: Shows yearly pawnshop numbers, new loans, redemptions, forfeitures and outstanding loans in Manchuria, 1925 to 1929, alongside the note on Oriental Development Company lending.

metadata.title: Loans Made by Manchuria Branches of the Oriental Development Company
metadata.caption: (in Yen)
metadata.description: Shows yearly loan numbers and amounts made by the Dairen, Mukden and Harbin branches of the Oriental Development Company in Manchuria, with totals, from 1925 to 1929.

metadata.title: [Chief Foreign Banks Operating in Manchuria]
metadata.description: Lists the chief foreign banks operating in Manchuria, with their founding dates, capital, head offices and branches, introducing the notes on the Russo-Asiatic and Dali banks.

metadata.title: [Estimated Circulation of Currencies at the End, Manchuria]
metadata.description: Lists the estimated circulation of each Manchurian currency at the end of the year, with its estimated value in Tayangchien yuan, followed by Chinese and Japanese currency totals.

metadata.title: [Rates of Conversion of Currencies Into Tayangchien and Hsientayan Yuan, 1927, and Estimated Circulation at the End of 1929]
metadata.description: Gives the 1927 conversion rates of each currency into Tayangchien and Hsientayan yuan, alongside estimated circulation and value at the end of 1929.

metadata.title: Market Value of Currencies
metadata.description: Shows the highest, lowest and average market values of silver and gold currencies in Dairen and Mukden against local currencies for June, December and the year, 1928–1929.

metadata.title: [Yingkow Prices of Gold, Luyin and Huishuei Currency Items, June, December and Yearly Average]
metadata.description: Shows June, December and yearly average market rates of Gold and Luyin items at Yingkow, expressed in yuan and tael, to illustrate local currency price movements.

metadata.title: [Exchange Rates at Antung]
metadata.description: Exchange rates at Antung, showing each local currency's price in the listed units for June, December and the yearly average, with units printed above each block's figures.

metadata.title: [Exchange Rates of Local Currencies in Kuantieh, Changehun, by Month and Year Average]
metadata.description: Shows the Tiao values of local currency notes (piao) and yuan in Kuantieh at Changehun, for June, December and the yearly average, across six reporting columns.

metadata.title: [Exchange Rates of Yuan and Yen at Kirin and Harbin, June, December and Average of the Year]
metadata.description: The table gives June, December and yearly average exchange rates for yuan and yen currencies quoted at Kirin and Harbin, showing local currency fluctuations in the banking and currency section.

metadata.title: [Insurance Business in Manchuria, 1925–1929]
metadata.description: Summarises the number of insurance firms and the premiums, claims, contracts, cancellations and total policies in force for life, loss and other insurance in Manchuria, 1925–1929.

metadata.title: Investments by Foreign Countries in Manchuria
metadata.caption: (in thousands of Yen)
metadata.description: Shows the amount invested in Manchuria by each foreign country by economic sector, illustrating that Japanese investment far exceeds that of the Soviet Union, Britain, the U.S. and others.

metadata.title: Classified Japanese Investments
metadata.description: Classifies Japanese investments in Manchuria at the end of the period by enterprise, with amounts and percentage shares, to illustrate how the total of over ¥1,510,000,000 was distributed.

metadata.title: Investments Made by South Manchuria Railway Co.
metadata.description: Shows the South Manchuria Railway Company's direct investments by field of enterprise at two dates in 1929 and 1930, supporting the statement that the company holds over half of Japanese investment in Manchuria.

metadata.title: [Indirect Investment (Continued)]
metadata.description: This continues the investment statistics, listing Japanese indirect investment in bonds, stocks and loans, with a grand total, before the page introduces a classification of Japanese investments by form.

metadata.title: According to the Form of Investment
metadata.description: Shows how Japanese foreign investment in Manchuria was divided by form of investment (railway, mining, manufacturing, banking and so on), with each category's share of the total.

metadata.title: Investments in the Form of Loans
metadata.description: The table shows the historical development of Japanese loan investments in Manchuria by sector from 1909 to 1927, illustrating how such loans grew over time.

metadata.title: Capital of Japanese Companies in Manchuria
metadata.description: The table shows the number of Japanese companies in Manchuria and their paid-up capital by industry, 1923–1928, with each sector's share of the total, illustrating Japanese investment there.

metadata.title: Earnings of Companies in Manchuria Formed under the Japanese Commercial Code
metadata.caption: (Average dividend, %)
metadata.description: The table gives average dividends of Japanese Commercial Code companies in Manchuria by industry and half-year, compared with companies in Japan proper, supporting the page's point that Manchurian enterprises earn poorer returns.

metadata.title: Investments of Various Countries in Manchuria
metadata.caption: (in thousands of Yen)
metadata.description: The table shows foreign investments in Manchuria by country and enterprise type as they stood in 1928, introduced as the next largest group after Japanese investment.

metadata.title: Census of Liaoning Province
metadata.caption: (Published by the provincial government in February, 1930).
metadata.description: The provincial census of Liaoning gives rough figures for households, population and employment, offered as a reference since no statistics cover all of Manchuria.

metadata.title: [Workers and Dependents by Industry, 1924–1928]
metadata.description: Shows the number of Japanese, Chinese and other workers and their dependents in each industry, 1924–1928, illustrating the composition of the labour force by nationality and industry.

metadata.title: [Working Hours of Japanese and Chinese Factory Workers]
metadata.description: Based on a South Manchuria Railway Company investigation, this table compares average daily working hours of Chinese and Japanese factory workers across industry types.

metadata.title: Wages in the Principal Cities of South Manchuria
metadata.caption: (April, 1929) (In Gold Yen)
metadata.description: The table gives daily wages of Japanese and Chinese craftsmen in several South Manchurian cities in April 1929, showing highest and lowest rates and a Manchuria-wide average.

metadata.title: [Daily Wages of Labourers and Workers by Occupation and Nationality]
metadata.description: Shows daily wage rates of various Japanese and Chinese workers and transport operators in Manchuria; column headings are not on this page and the table continues from the previous page.

metadata.title: Agricultural Labour
metadata.description: Shows daily, monthly and yearly agricultural wages for Korean and Chinese labourers, illustrating how cheap labour was in Manchuria before the discussion of Chinese workers' living costs.

metadata.title: [Average Monthly Living Expenses of Employees of South Manchuria Railway Company Factories, 1925-1926]
metadata.description: Gives an example of the average monthly living expenses of Chinese workers employed by the South Manchuria Railway Company, for single men and for families of four, in 1925-1926.

metadata.title: [Labour Disputes, 1916–1928]
metadata.description: Statistics of labour disputes, giving the number of strikes and the participants by nationality, shown to illustrate the labour disputes described in the preceding text.

metadata.title: [Chinese Labourers Entering and Leaving Manchuria, 1923–1926]
metadata.description: Shows the number of Chinese labourers entering and leaving Manchuria by sea and by rail, with the balance and the share of settlers among immigrants, illustrating the unusually large immigration of recent years.

metadata.title: [Immigration and Emigration Figures, 1927–1929 and Total]
metadata.caption: (in Thousands) appears as a chart caption below the table, not as a headnote to it
metadata.description: This table gives yearly totals of immigrants entering and leaving Manchuria, with the balance, for 1927–1929, supporting the chart and the discussion of immigration trends.

metadata.title: [Distribution of Korean Settlers in Manchuria at the End of 1927]
metadata.description: Korean settlers in Manchuria, by province, as investigated at the end of 1927, showing total settlers and naturalized settlers by households and population.

metadata.title: [Educational Expenditure and Number of Schools and Students in the Manchurian Provinces, 1929]
metadata.description: Shows the 1929 educational expenditure and the number of higher, secondary, normal and primary schools, with students attending, in each Manchurian province.

metadata.title: Educational Institutions Maintained by the Chinese Eastern Railway for the Education of Russians in 1929
metadata.description: Shows the number of schools and students of the educational institutions the Chinese Eastern Railway maintained for Russians in 1929, at Harbin and along the railway.

metadata.title: [Educational Institutions for the Chinese Maintained by Europeans, 1923]
metadata.description: Shows the number of educational institutions for Chinese run by British, French, German, Danish and Russian missions in each province in 1923, introduced as part of the section on Western-run schools.

metadata.title: [Temples, Shrines, Missionaries and Believers in Manchuria, April 1929]
metadata.description: Shows the number of Chinese temples and shrines, missionaries and believers in Manchuria by religion and district in April 1929, supporting the discussion of religious distribution.

metadata.title: [Haikwan Tael Equivalents in Foreign Money, 1912–1931]
metadata.description: Note 3 explains that the Haikwan Tael equivalents of monetary values were calculated at average sight exchange rates in London, New York, Paris, Berlin, Calcutta and Yokohama for 1912 to 1928, and this table gives them year by year.

metadata.title: The Rates Used in Converting Chinese and Foreign Standards of Weight and Measure into the Metric System Are as Follows
metadata.description: Gives the conversion rates used to express Chinese, Japanese and foreign units of length, area, capacity and weight in metric units.

metadata.title: Area of Manchuria
metadata.caption: (Square Kilometres)
metadata.description: Table 1 gives the area of Manchuria's provinces from two sources, along with the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone, to support the geographical discussion.

metadata.title: Climatic Conditions of Manchuria
metadata.description: This table gives the climatic figures for seven Manchurian stations, covering temperature, sunshine, rainfall, evaporation, humidity and frost, to describe the region's climate.

metadata.title: Population Growth in Manchuria*
metadata.caption: (in thousands)
metadata.description: The table gives estimated population growth in the former three eastern provinces of Manchuria from 1907 to 1930, supporting the preceding discussion of population distribution based on South Manchuria Railway Research Office estimates.

metadata.title: Density of Population
metadata.description: Shows the 1930 population of each province, the Kwantung Leased Territory and the SMR Zone, with density per square kilometre and population growth index since 1907.

metadata.title: Population of Important Cities in Manchuria Classified by Nationality, 1931*
metadata.description: Gives the 1931 population of Dairen, Port Arthur and other important Manchurian cities by Chinese, Japanese (excluding Korean), Korean and other nationalities, with 1930 comparative figures in parentheses.

metadata.title: [Number and Location of Courts in the Tungsheng Special District]
metadata.description: The page lists the courts of the Tungsheng Special District and their locations, according to the 'North-Eastern Year Book' (1931), to illustrate the district's judicial structure.

metadata.title: [Old and New Prisons in the Four North-Eastern Provinces, 1931]
metadata.description: Shows the number of new and old prisons in each of the Four North-Eastern Provinces before the recent Manchurian development, according to the Commission on Extraterritoriality and a 1931 Chinese year book.

metadata.title: Total Expenditure of the Three Eastern Provinces in 1930
metadata.caption: (Silver Yuan)
metadata.description: Table 1 sets out the total expenditure of the Three Eastern Provinces in 1930 by department, to illustrate the financial condition before the incident.

metadata.title: Total Revenue of the Three Eastern Provinces in 1930
metadata.caption: (Silver Yuan)
metadata.description: Table 2 lists the revenue of the Three Eastern Provinces in 1930, showing direct taxes, indirect taxes and current taxes with their share of the total.

metadata.title: [Revenue Items Continued From Previous Page]
metadata.description: Continues the list of provincial revenue items from the previous page, giving the final sources of income before the text turns to expenditure.

metadata.title: Revenue and Expenditure of Fengtien, Kirin, Heilungkiang and Jehol Provinces*
metadata.caption: (in 1,000 Silver Yuan)
metadata.description: Shows revenue and expenditure of four northeastern provinces, with military defence spending dominating, supporting the text's point about small general administration and large military outlays in Fengtien and Jehol.

metadata.title: Abolition and Reduction of Taxes
metadata.caption: (Silver Yuan)
metadata.description: The table shows the effect of the taxation reform on provincial revenue, listing the silver yuan value of abolished and reduced taxes in Fengtien, Kirin and Heilungkiang.

metadata.title: Estimated Revenue of the First Year of Tatung
metadata.caption: (In 1,000 Silver Yen)
metadata.description: The text introduces the estimated budget for Tatung's first fiscal year (July 1932 to June 1933), and this table itemises the projected revenue under ordinary and extraordinary heads.

metadata.title: Estimated Expenditure of the First Year of Tatung
metadata.caption: (In 1,000 Silver Yen)
metadata.description: The table gives the estimated ordinary and extraordinary expenditure for the first year of the Tatung government, by office and department, preceding the discussion of Manchoukuo's new financial system.

metadata.title: Salt Gabelle Revenue of the Three Eastern Provinces
metadata.description: Shows salt gabelle revenue in the Three Eastern Provinces from 1913 to 1931 against revenue and production indices, illustrating how revenue grew faster than production after 1927 due to higher tax rates.

metadata.title: Total Maritime Customs Revenue at Each Port of Manchuria
metadata.caption: (Haikwan Taels)
metadata.description: Shows the maritime customs revenue collected at each Manchurian port from 1910 to 1931, with totals for China and the Manchurian share of national revenue.

metadata.title: Revenue and Expenditure of the Special Account for the Kwantung Government
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: The table gives the revenue and expenditure of the Kwantung Government's special account from 1907 to 1931, showing how taxes and enterprise income grew over the period.

metadata.title: Income and Disbursement of Local Expenses of the Kwantung Leased Territory
metadata.caption: (Yen)
metadata.description: Shows the ordinary and extraordinary income and local expenditure of the Kwantung Leased Territory across selected years from 1907 to 1931, with 1930 and 1931 as estimates.

metadata.title: Annual Accounts of the City of Dairen and Port Arthur
metadata.description: Shows the annual revenue and expenditure of the cities of Dairen and Port Arthur, 1925 to 1931, with 1931 figures being budget estimates.

metadata.title: Annual Accounts of the South Manchuria Railway Zone
metadata.description: Gives the annual accounts (income/expenditure totals) of the South Manchuria Railway Zone from 1907 to 1931, as a background to the revenue and expenditure figures that follow.

metadata.title: Revenue and Expenditure of the Railway Zone
metadata.caption: Revenue (in thousands of Yen); Expenditure (in thousands of Yen)
metadata.description: Shows the yearly revenue and expenditure of the South Manchuria Railway Zone from 1925 to 1931, with the railway company's subsidy making up the deficit.

metadata.title: Land Utilization in Manchuria
metadata.description: The table shows land area, cultivable and uncultivated land, and cultivation shares for each province and the Kwantung Leased Territory, supporting the text's point that much arable land in North Manchuria remains uncultivated.

metadata.title: Agricultural Production in 1930
metadata.caption: (Metric Tons)
metadata.description: The author notes that the main crops are listed and then gives a table of agricultural production in 1930 by province and crop, in metric tons.

metadata.title: Cultivated Area Classified by Crops, 1930
metadata.caption: (Hectares)
metadata.description: Table 3 breaks down the cultivated area of Fengtien, Kirin, Heilungkiang and the Kwantung Leased Territory by crop type in 1930, giving hectares and percentage shares.

metadata.title: PRODUCTION OF ORDINARY CROPS †
metadata.caption: (Metric Tons)
metadata.description: Shows the annual production of ordinary crops in the Three Eastern Provinces and the Kwantung Leased Territory with S.M.R. Zone, by crop type, for 1924 to 1927.

metadata.title: [Agricultural Production of Manchuria, 1928–1930]
metadata.description: Year-by-year figures for Manchurian agricultural production in three regions (Three Eastern Provinces, Kwantung Leased Territory and S.M.R. Zone, and totals) for 1928–1930, with the column headings printed on the preceding page.

metadata.title: Cultivated Area of Ordinary Crops
metadata.caption: (Hectares)
metadata.description: This table gives the cultivated area of each ordinary crop in the Three Eastern Provinces and the Kwantung Leased Territory with S.M.R. Zone for 1924 to 1926.

metadata.title: [Statistics of Three Eastern Provinces, Kwantung Leased Territory and S.M.R. Zone, 1927–1930]
metadata.description: The table gives figures for the Three Eastern Provinces, the Kwantung Leased Territory and S.M.R. Zone, and their totals for 1927–1930; its column headings appear on the previous page.

metadata.title: Production Index Number of Ordinary Crops
metadata.description: Shows how production index numbers for each ordinary crop changed from 1924 to 1930, with 1924 taken as 100, illustrating the growth in harvests discussed in the text.

metadata.title: Index Number of Cultivated Area of Ordinary Crops
metadata.description: Gives index numbers of the cultivated area under each ordinary crop from 1924 to 1930, with 1924 as 100, supporting the text on planted area trends.

metadata.title: [Comparison of Original and Improved Soya Bean Varieties]
metadata.description: The table compares the original variety with two improved varieties, produced from Ssulihuang, by crop per hectare, crop index and oil percentage.

metadata.title: Production and Cultivated Areas of Ordinary Crops Classified by Districts, 1930
metadata.description: Gives the production and cultivated areas of the main ordinary crops (soya beans, kaoliang, millet, maize, wheat and rice) for each district of South and North Manchuria in 1930.

metadata.title: Value of Exports of Agricultural Products
metadata.caption: (Haikwan Taels)
metadata.description: The table gives the value of Manchurian agricultural exports, raw and manufactured, for 1926–1930, with each group's share of total exports shown beneath.

metadata.title: Exports of Principal

metadata.title: Connecting Steamer Services
metadata.caption: Undermentioned liners are thoroughly equipped with the latest facilities for the comfort and safety of passengers. Wireless telegraphy is installed on each steamer, and a qualified doctor is also on board. 1. Dairen-Tsingtao-Shanghai Line: The Dairen Kisen Kaisha's mail and passenger boats (3,749-4,018 G. Tons) sail every two days and arrive at the terminal port on the third day. 2. Dairen-Tientsin Line. This line is also maintained by the Dairen Kisen Kaisha. The passenger boats (1,270-2,352 tons) sail every one or two days covering the distance in 24 hours. 3. Dairen-Moji-Kobe Line. The Osaka Shosen Kaisha's mail and passenger boats (5,167-8,188 G. Tons) sail almost every day, covering the distance from Dairen to Moji in 43 hours. 4. Yuki-Seishin-Tsuruga Line. The Kita-Nippon Kisen Kaisha's mail and passenger boat (3,054 G. Tons) sail three times per month, covering the distance in 47 hours. 5. Yuki-Seishin-Niigata Line. The Nippon-kai Kisen Kaisha's mail and passenger boats (2,130-2,346 G. Tons) sail three times per month, covering the distance in 54 hours.
